english_verse: Even before I had finished praying, Rebekah came by with a water jar on her shoulder. When she had filled the jar, I asked her for a drink.
translation_verse: Yɛtɔɣa maa di na kul bela n suhu ni, ka Ribɛka paana, ka o koyuli tam o bɔɣusapiŋ zuɣu, ka o gari siɣi kɔbiliga maa ni ti ŋɔŋ kom na. Ka n yɛl’ o, ‘N suhir’ a, tim ma kom ka n nyu.’

english_verse: She quickly lowered the jar from her shoulder and said, “Have a drink. Then I'll get water for your camels.” So I drank, and after that she got some water for my camels.
translation_verse: Ka o dii suug’ o koyuli maa o bɔɣusapiŋ zuɣu na ti ma ka yɛli, ‘Nyuma, ka chɛ ka n ŋɔŋ shɛli ti a laakumnim’ ŋɔ gba ka bɛ nyu.’ Ka n di nyu ka chɛ ka o ŋɔŋ na ti ti n laakumnim’ maa gba ka bɛ nyu.

english_verse: I asked her who her father was, and she answered, “My father is Bethuel the son of Nahor and Milcah.” At once I put the ring in her nose and the bracelets on her arms.
translation_verse: Di saha ka m bɔh’ o, ‘Ŋun’ bia n-lee nyɛ a?’ Ka o yɛli ma, ‘N nyɛla Bɛtuɛl bipuɣiŋga. Bɛtuɛl mi daa nyɛla Nahɔr mini Milika bidibiga.’ Ka n zaŋ nintua m-pir’ o, ka zaŋ bansi pir’ o.

english_verse: Then I bowed my head and gave thanks to the God my master Abraham worships. The Lord had led me straight to my master's relatives, and I had found a wife for his son.
translation_verse: Di saha ka n di zaŋ n zuɣu silim tiŋa n-jɛm Yawɛ, ka paɣi ŋun’ Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ n dan’ Ibrahimma Naawuni ŋun wuhi yɛlimaŋli so’ shɛli n ni yɛn doli kpuɣi ŋuna n dan’ maa dɔɣim bipuɣiŋga nti ti o bia maa.

english_verse: Now please tell me if you are willing to do the right thing for my master. Will you treat him fairly, or do I have to look for another young woman?

english_verse: Take Rebekah with you; she can marry your master's son, just as the Lord has said.”

english_verse: Then he gave clothing, as well as silver and gold jewelry, to Rebekah. He also gave expensive gifts to her brother and her mother.

english_verse: Abraham's servant and the men with him ate and drank, then spent the night there. The next morning they got up, and the servant told Rebekah's mother and brother, “I would like to go back to my master now.”
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka o mini ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn daa dol’ o la daa naanyi di ka nyu, ka gbe nimaani. Ka biɛɣu daa neei ka o yiɣisi ka yɛli ba, “N suhiri soli ni n labi n dan’ sani.”

english_verse: “Let Rebekah stay with us for a week or ten days,” they answered. “Then she may go.”
translation_verse: Ka Ribɛka tizɔdoo maa min’ o ma daa yɛli, “Chɛ ka paɣisarili maa na kpalim be ti sani daba ayi kaman biɛɣu pia pahi ka naanyi chaŋ.”

english_verse: But he said, “Don't make me stay any longer. The Lord has already helped me find a wife for my master's son. Now let us return.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka nachin’ kpɛm’ maa yɛli ba, “Yawɛ ni ti ma nasara shɛm ŋɔ zuɣu, di bi simdi ni yi chɛ ka n lan kpalim be kpe, timiya ma soli ka n labi n dan’ sani.”

english_verse: They answered, “Let's ask Rebekah what she wants to do.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ yɛl’ o, “Chɛ ka ti boli paɣisarili maa na nti bɔh’ o nya.”

english_verse: They called her and asked, “Are you willing to leave with this man at once?” “Yes,” she answered.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa boli Ribɛka na nti bɔh’ o, “A ni doli doo ŋɔ chaŋ?” Ka o garigi yɛli, “N ni dol’ o chaŋ.”

english_verse: So they agreed to let Rebekah and an old family servant woman leave immediately with Abraham's servant and his men.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa chɛ ka bɛ tizɔpaɣ’ Ribɛka min’ o yiŋ’ dab’ paɣa doli Ibrahimma nachin’ kpɛm’ maa mini ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn daa dol’ o maa.

english_verse: They gave Rebekah their blessing and said, “We pray that God will give you many children and grandchildren and that he will help them defeat their enemies.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa suhi alibarika suhigu ti Ribɛka n-yɛli: “Ti tizɔpaɣa, Naawuni chɛ ka a leei niriba tusatusa ni tuhi’ piapia ma! Naawuni chɛ ka a zuliya ti nyaŋ bɛ dimnima.”

english_verse: Afterwards, Rebekah and the young women who were to travel with her prepared to leave. Then they got on camels and left with Abraham's servant and his men.
translation_verse: Ka Ribɛka min’ o dab’ bipuɣinsi daa yiɣisi m-ba laakumnima n-doli nachin’ kpɛm’ maa ka o zaŋ o lu yiŋ’ soli.

english_verse: One evening he was walking out in the fields, when suddenly he saw a group of people approaching on camels. So he started toward them. Rebekah saw him coming; she got down from her camel, and asked, “Who is that man?” “He is my master Isaac,” the servant answered. Then Rebekah covered her face with her veil.
translation_verse: ka bɔhi Ibrahimma nachin’ kpɛm’ maa, “Ka ŋuni n-lee be kpe ha palo ni n-chani tuhiri ti soli ŋɔ na?” Ka nachin’ kpɛm’ maa yɛl’ o, “N dana m-bala.” Ka Ribɛka daa zaŋ sariga pa n-lims’ o ninni.

english_verse: The servant told Isaac everything that had happened.
translation_verse: Ka Ibrahimma nachin’ kpɛm’ maa daa yɛli Yisahaku o ni niŋ shɛlikam zaa.

english_verse: Isaac took Rebekah into the tent where his mother had lived before she died, and Rebekah became his wife. He loved her and was comforted over the loss of his mother.

english_verse: Before Rebekah gave birth, she knew she was going to have twins, because she could feel them inside her, fighting each other. She thought, “Why is this happening to me?” Finally, she asked the Lord why her twins were fighting,
translation_verse: Ka bihi daa ti var’ o pul’ ni ka o yɛli, “Di yi yɛn nyɛ ŋ-ŋɔ n ni be?” Ka o daa chaŋ ni o ti bɔhi Yawɛ nya.

english_verse: the first baby was covered with red hair, so he was named Esau.

english_verse: As Jacob and Esau grew older, Esau liked the outdoors and became a good hunter, while Jacob lived the quiet life of a shepherd.
translation_verse: Bihi maa ni daa ti zooi, Iso daa niŋla tɔha biiŋa ŋun daa kul be mɔɣu ni; ka Yaakubu mi be baalim m-be yiŋa.

english_verse: Esau would take the meat of wild animals to his father Isaac, so Isaac loved him more, but Jacob was his mother's favorite son.
translation_verse: Yisahaku daa yurila Iso, dama o daa yuri mɔɣu ni nimdi pam, ka Ribɛka mi daa yuri Yaakubu.

english_verse: One day, when Jacob was cooking some stew, Esau came home hungry
translation_verse: Dahin shɛli ka Yaakubu daa ti duɣi ʒiɛri, ka Iso yi mɔɣu ni na ka kum wum o pam,

english_verse: Jacob replied, “Sell me your rights as the first-born son.”
translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu daa yɛl’ o, “Zaŋm’ a kpamdi ti ma pɔi.”

english_verse: “I'm about to die,” Esau answered. “What good will those rights do me?”
translation_verse: Ka Iso yɛl’ o, “M mini kum kul chɛ tab’ la kpe ni kpe, ka buchi bɔ ka kpamdi lan yɛn ku ma?”

english_verse: But Jacob said, “Promise me your birthrights, here and now!” And that's what Esau did.
translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu yɛl’ o, “Faashee ka a po.” Ka Iso daa shiri po, ka zaŋ o kpamdi maa ti Yaakubu.

english_verse: Jacob then gave Esau some bread and some of the bean stew, and when Esau had finished eating and drinking, he just got up and left, showing how little he thought of his rights as the first-born.
translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu daa zaŋ bɔrɔbɔro mini tuya ʒiɛri maa ti Iso ka o di ka nyu, ka yiɣisi chaŋ o chandi shee. Lala ka Iso daa niŋ ʒiɛm o kpamdi maa.

english_verse: because the Lord had appeared to Isaac and said: Isaac, stay away from Egypt! I will show you where I want you to go.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa ka Yisahaku sanna ti yɛl’ o, “Di chaŋ Ijipti, kpalim be tiŋgban’ shɛli ni n ni yɛn wuh’ a.

english_verse: You will live there as a foreigner, but I will be with you and bless you. I will keep my promise to your father Abraham by giving this land to you and your descendants.
translation_verse: Kul be tiŋgbani ŋɔ ni, ka m be a sani, ka niŋ alibarika niŋ a ni, ka zaŋ tiŋgbana ŋɔ zaa ti a min’ a zuliya, ka chɛ ka n ni daa lo a ba Ibrahimma alikauli shɛl’ la pali.

english_verse: I will give you as many descendants as there are stars in the sky, and I will give your descendants all of this land. They will be a blessing to every nation on earth,

english_verse: with his beautiful wife Rebekah. He was afraid that someone might kill him to get her, and so he told everyone that Rebekah was his sister.
translation_verse: o daa yɛlimi, “O nyɛla n tizɔpaɣa,” dama o daa zɔrila dabiɛm ni o yɛli ni o paɣa m-bala. O daa tɛhimi ni o yi yɛl’ lala, di pa shɛli ka nimaani nim’ maa ti ku o Ribɛka zuɣu, dama o daa nyɛla paɣ’ viɛlli.

english_verse: After Isaac had been there a long time, King Abimelech looked out a window and saw Isaac hugging and kissing Rebekah.
translation_verse: Yisahaku ni daa be nimaani ka di niŋ daba ayi ha, ka Filistianim’ Naa Abimilɛk daa ti lihi takɔro ni nya ka Yisahaku diɛmd’ o paɣ’ Ribɛka.

english_verse: Abimelech called him in and said, “Rebekah must be your wife! Why did you say she is your sister?” “Because I thought someone would kill me,” Isaac answered.
translation_verse: Ka Abimilɛk daa tim ti boli Yisahaku na ti bɔh’ o, “O nyɛla a paɣa; ka bɔ n-niŋ ka a yɛli ni o nyɛla a tizɔpaɣa?” Ka Yisahaku garigi yɛl’ o, “N tɛhimi ni n yi yɛli ni m paɣa m-bala, bɛ ni ku ma o zuɣu.”

english_verse: “Don't you know what you've done?” Abimelech exclaimed. “If someone had slept with her, you would have made our whole nation guilty!”
translation_verse: Ka Abimilɛk daa bɔh’ o, “Tuun’ bɔ ka a lee tum ti maa? Di pa shɛli ka yaŋɔnim’ ni so di zaŋ a paɣ’ maa dɔni. A naan chɛ ka di taali ʒin’ ti zuɣu.”

english_verse: Then Abimelech warned his people that anyone who even touched Isaac or Rebekah would be put to death.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Abimilɛk daa kpah’ o niriba zuɣu ni yɛli, “Ŋunkam niŋ doo ŋɔ bee o paɣ’ ŋɔ shɛli, bɛn’ kum’ o.”

english_verse: and Isaac was so successful that he became very rich.
translation_verse: Ka o nyamma daa yɛligi ka o leei bundana.

english_verse: In fact, the Philistines were jealous of the large number of sheep, goats, and slaves that Isaac owned,

english_verse: and they stopped up the wells that Abraham's servants had dug before his death.

english_verse: Finally, Abimelech said, “Isaac, I want you to leave our country. You have become too powerful to stay here.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Abimilɛk daa yɛli Yisahaku, “Yiɣisim’ ti sani, dama a mali kpiɔŋ gari ti.”

english_verse: Isaac left and settled in Gerar Valley,

translation_verse: Ka Gɛra biŋkɔbiguliba daa kana ti niŋ Yisahaku biŋkɔbiguliba maa naŋgbankpeeni yɛli, “Ti kom m-bala.” Dinzuɣu ka Yisahaku daa boli kɔbiliga maa yuli Ɛsɛk, bɛ ni daa niŋ o naŋgbankpeeni maa zuɣu.

english_verse: Isaac's servants dug another well, and the shepherds also quarreled about it. So that well was named “Jealous.”
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Yisahaku biŋkɔbiguliba maa daa lan gbi kɔbil’ shɛli, ka bɛ daa lan niŋ ba naŋgbankpeeni di zuɣu; dinzuɣu ka Yisahaku daa boli kɔbiliga maa yuli dimdi kɔbiliga.

english_verse: Finally, they dug one more well. There was no quarreling this time, and the well was named “Lots of Room,” because the Lord had given them room and would make them very successful.

translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa ka o sanna dindali maa yuŋ ti yɛl’ o, “Mani n-nyɛ a ba Ibrahimma Naawuni, di zɔri dabiɛm, n ni be a sani, ka niŋ alibarika niŋ a ni, ka chɛ ka a zuliya nab’ pam n dabili Ibrahimma zuɣu.”

translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu daa bɔhi piɛguliba maa, “M mabihi, ka tiŋkani ka yi lee yina?” Ka bɛ yɛl’ o, “Ti yila Haran na.”

english_verse: Then he asked, “Do you know Nahor's grandson Laban?” “Yes we do,” they replied.
translation_verse: Ka o bɔhi ba, “Yi mi Leeban Nahɔr bia la?” Ka bɛ yɛl’ o, “Ti mi o.”

english_verse: “How is he?” Jacob asked. “He's fine,” they answered. “And here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep.”
translation_verse: Ka o bɔhi ba, “O be wula?” Ka bɛ yɛl’ o, “O mal’ alaafee;” ka lan yɛli, “O bipuɣiŋga Reechɛl n-taɣiri piɛri kanna ŋɔ.”

english_verse: Jacob told them, “Look, the sun is still high up in the sky, and it's too early to bring in the rest of the flocks. Water your sheep and take them back to the pasture.”
translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu yɛli, “Nyama, wuntaŋ’ ni n-na bɔŋɔ, biŋkɔbiri maa taɣ’ kuli yiŋ’ saha na bi paai, dinzuɣu ŋɔŋmiya kom ti piɛri maa ka bɛ nyu, ka yi zaŋ ba chaŋ ka bɛ ti ŋub’ mɔri.”

english_verse: But they replied, “We can't do that until they all get here, and the rock has been rolled away from the well.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka bɛ yɛl’ o, “Ti ku tooi niŋ lala ka pa ni piɛri maa zaa laɣimmina pɔi ka bɛ naanyi paai kuɣili maa kɔbiliga maa noli, ka ti ŋɔŋ kom maa ti ba.”

english_verse: While Jacob was still talking with the men, his cousin Rachel came up with her father's sheep.
translation_verse: Yaakubu mini ba ni daa na kul tɔɣisiri saha shɛli maa, ka Reechɛl taɣ’ o ba piɛri paa’ na; dama ŋuna n-daa guli ba.

english_verse: He then kissed Rachel and started crying because he was so happy.
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Yaakubu daa gbaai Reechɛl kpariŋ mɔɣisi ka kum suhupiɛlli kuhigu pam.

english_verse: He told her that he was the son of her aunt Rebekah, and she ran and told her father about him.
translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu daa yɛli Reechɛl ni o nyɛla o ba dɔɣim, ka nyɛ Ribɛka bia, Ka Reechɛl daa guui kuli ti yɛl’ o ba.

english_verse: As soon as Laban heard the news, he ran out to meet Jacob. He hugged and kissed him and brought him to his home, where Jacob told him everything that had happened.
translation_verse: Leeban ni daa wum o tizɔpaɣ’ bia Yaakubu yɛla maa, ka o guui ka o sanna nti bɔb’ gbaag’ o m-mɔɣis’ o kpariŋ, ka zaŋ o kul’ o yiŋa. Ka Yaakubu daa yɛli Leeban binshɛlikam zaa.

english_verse: Laban said, “You are my nephew, and you are like one of my own family.” Jacob Marries Leah and Rachel After Jacob had been there for a month,
translation_verse: Ka Leeban yɛl’ o, “Yɛlimaŋli, a shiri nyɛla n ʒim.” Ka Yaakubu daa be o sani goli yini. Yaakubu tum tuma ti Leeban Reechɛl mini Liya zuɣu

english_verse: Laban said to him, “You shouldn't have to work without pay, just because you are a relative of mine. What do you want me to give you?”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Leeban daa bɔhi Yaakubu, “A ni nyɛ n dɔɣira maa zuɣu, a yɛn tumla tuma ti ma yoli? Yɛlim’ ma a ni bɔri ni n yo a shɛm?”

english_verse: Laban had two daughters. Leah was older than Rachel, but her eyes didn't sparkle, while Rachel was beautiful and had a good figure.
translation_verse: Liya nina daa dii ka alaafee, amaa ka Reechɛl ŋun daa viɛli pam ka o ninni kul nyɛlisira.

english_verse: Since Jacob was in love with Rachel, he answered, “If you will let me marry Rachel, I'll work seven years for you.”
translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu suhu daa yu Reechɛl ka o yɛli, “N ni tum tuma yuma ayopɔin ti a, Reechɛl ŋun nyɛ a bipuɣiŋga biasani ŋɔ zuɣu.”

english_verse: Laban replied, “It's better for me to let you marry Rachel than for someone else to have her. So stay and work for me.”
translation_verse: Ka Leeban yɛl’ o, “N yi zaŋ o ti a, di so ni n zaŋ o ti do’ so, kpalimmi n sani.”

english_verse: Jacob worked seven years for Laban, but the time seemed like only a few days, because he loved Rachel so much.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Yaakubu daa tum tuma yuma ayopɔin Reechɛl zuɣu, amaa ka di daa ŋmanila dabisa biɛla o sani, o ni daa yuri Reechɛl maa zuɣu.

english_verse: Jacob said to Laban, “The time is up, and I want to marry Rachel now!”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yaakubu daa yɛli Leeban, “N tum tuma maa paai di tariga, zaŋmi m paɣa maa ti ma ka n zaŋ o niŋ m paɣa.”

english_verse: So Laban gave a big feast and invited all their neighbors.
translation_verse: Ka Leeban daa laɣim nimaaninim’ zaa na ka bɛ ti puhi chuɣu.

english_verse: But that evening he brought Leah to Jacob, who married her and spent the night with her.
translation_verse: Amaa ka yuŋ daa ti paai ka o zaŋla o bipuɣiŋga Liya nti ti Yaakubu ka o zaŋ o niŋ o paɣa.

english_verse: Laban also gave Zilpah to Leah as her servant woman.
translation_verse: Leeban daa zaŋla o dab’ bipuɣiŋga Zilipa ti Liya ni o sɔŋd’ o.

english_verse: The next morning Jacob found out that he had married Leah, and he asked Laban, “Why did you do this to me? Didn't I work to get Rachel? Why did you trick me?”
translation_verse: Ka biɛɣu daa neei, ka di nyɛla Liya. Ka Yaakubu daa bɔhi Leeban, “Bɔ n-niŋ ka a niŋ ma lala? Reechɛl zuɣu ka n tum tuma ti a, ka bɔ n-niŋ ka a yɔhim ma?”

english_verse: Laban replied, “In our country the older daughter must get married first.
translation_verse: Ka Leeban yɛl’ o, “Di pala ti tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni kali ni bipuɣiŋga ŋun nyɛ biasani daŋ o biɛli doo kulibu.

english_verse: After you spend this week with Leah, you may also marry Rachel. But you will have to work for me another seven years.”
translation_verse: Chɛ ka ŋumbɔŋɔ amiliya dakulo ŋɔ naai pɔi, ka ti zaŋ ŋuni maa gba ti a, ka a tum tuma o zuɣu ti ma yuma ayopɔin pahi.”

english_verse: At the end of the week of celebration, Laban let Jacob marry Rachel, and he gave her his servant woman Bilhah. Jacob loved Rachel more than he did Leah, but he had to work another seven years for Laban.
translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu daa zaŋ Reechɛl niŋ o paɣa, ka yur’ o gari Liya; ka daa lan tum tuma yuma ayopɔin ti Leeban. Yaakubu ni dɔɣi bi’ shɛba

english_verse: The Lord knew that Jacob loved Rachel more than he did Leah, and so he gave children to Leah, but not to Rachel.
translation_verse: Yawɛ ni daa nya ka Yaakubu je Liya maa, ka o ti Liya nama, ka chɛ ka Reechɛl nyɛ paɣiŋoo.

english_verse: Leah gave birth to a son and named him Reuben. Then she said, “The Lord has taken away my sorrow. Now my husband will love me more than he does Rachel.”
translation_verse: Ka Liya daa niŋ pua n-dɔɣi bidibiga m-bol’ o yuli Rubin. Dama o daa yɛliya, Yawɛ nya m muɣisigu ni nyɛ shɛli; “Yɛlimaŋli, n yidan’ ni yu ma pumpɔŋɔ.”

english_verse: She had a second son and named him Simeon, because she said, “The Lord has heard that my husband doesn't love me.”
translation_verse: Ka o daa lan niŋ pua n-dɔɣi bidibiga ka yɛli, “Yawɛ ni baŋ ni bɛ je ma zuɣu ka o ti ma bidibiga ŋɔ gba;” ka daa bol’ o yuli Simiɔn.

english_verse: When Leah's third son was born, she said, “Now my husband will hold me close.” So this son was named Levi.
translation_verse: Ka o daa lan niŋ pua n-dɔɣi bidibiga ka yɛli, “Pumpɔŋɔ n yidan’ yipa ni zaŋ omaŋ’ tabili ma, dama n dɔɣi bidibis’ ata ti o;” dinzuɣu ka o daa bol’ o yuli Lɛvi.

english_verse: She had one more son and named him Judah, because she said, “I'll praise the Lord!”
translation_verse: Ka o daa lan niŋ pua n-dɔɣi bidibiga m-bol’ o yuli Juda ka yɛli, “Pumpɔŋɔ dina n ni paɣi Yawɛ.” Di nyaaŋa ka o daa chɛ dɔɣibu.

english_verse: Rachel was very jealous of Leah for having children, and she said to Jacob, “I'll die if you don't give me some children!”
translation_verse: Reechɛl ni daa nya ka o bi dɔɣi bihi ti Yaakubu maa zuɣu ka o daa zabir’ o biɛli nyuli, ka yɛli Yaakubu, “Tim’ ma bihi, di yi pa lala, n ni kpi.”

english_verse: But Jacob became upset with Rachel and answered, “Don't blame me! I'm not God.”
translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu daa yiɣis’ o suhu bahi Reechɛl zuɣu pam, ka bɔh’ o, “Mani n-nyɛ Naawuni ŋun ŋar’ a dɔɣim soli?”

english_verse: “Here, take my servant Bilhah,” Rachel told him. “Have children by her, and I'll let them be born on my knees to show that they are mine.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Reechɛl daa yɛli Yaakubu, “N dab’ bipuɣiŋga Biliha m-bɔŋɔ; zaŋm’ o dɔni ka o dɔɣi bihi ti ma, ka n zaŋ ba ʒili n naba zuɣu.”

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: Ka Biliha daa niŋ pua n-dɔɣi bidibiga ti Yaakubu.

english_verse: Rachel named him Dan, because she said, “God has answered my prayers. He judged in my favor and has given me a son.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Reechɛl daa yɛli, “Naawuni zahimmi n yɛla nya, ka deei n suhigu ka ti ma bidibiga”; dinzuɣu ka o daa bol’ o yuli Dan.

english_verse: Rachel said, “I've struggled hard with my sister, and I've won!” So she named the boy Naphtali.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Reechɛl daa yɛli, “N ni va m biɛli val’ shɛli din kpɛm’ pam la zuɣu ka n di nasara ŋɔ”; ka daa boli bia maa yuli Naftali.

english_verse: When Leah realized she could not have any more children, she let Jacob marry her servant Zilpah,
translation_verse: Liya ni daa nya ka o bi lan dɔɣiri maa, ka o daa zaŋ o dab’ bipuɣiŋga Zilipa ti Yaakubu ka o niŋ o paɣa.

english_verse: “I'm really lucky,” Leah said, and she named the boy Gad.
translation_verse: Ka Liya daa yɛli, “Zuɣusuŋ”; ka daa boli bia maa yuli Gaad.

english_verse: When they had another son,
translation_verse: Ka Zilipa daa lan dɔɣi bidibiga ti Yaakubu pahi.

english_verse: Leah exclaimed, “I'm happy now, and all the women will say how happy I am.” So she named him Asher. Love Flowers
translation_verse: Ka Liya daa yɛli, “N suhu paligiya! Dama paɣiba ni boli ma suhupiɛlli”; ka daa boli bia maa yuli Asha.

english_verse: During the time of the wheat harvest, Reuben found some love flowers and took them to his mother Leah. Rachel asked Leah for some of them,
translation_verse: Ka Rubin daa ti chaŋ mɔɣu ni alikama chɛbu saha ti bo ŋmaankpihiga na ti ti o ma Liya. Ka Reechɛl daa yɛli Liya, “N suhir’ a, niŋm’ a bia ŋmaankpihiga maa shɛli ti ma.”

english_verse: but Leah said, “It's bad enough that you stole my husband! Now you want my son's love flowers too.” “All right,” Rachel answered. “Let me have the flowers, and you can sleep with Jacob tonight.”
translation_verse: Ka Liya bɔh’ o, “A ni fa n yidan’ maa nyɛla yɛli bila? Ka a lan bɔri ni a fa n ŋmaankpihiga gba pahi?” Ka Reechɛl yɛl’ o, “Kpɛm’ o sani zuŋɔ yuŋ ŋɔ a bia ŋmaankpihiga maa zuɣu.”

english_verse: That evening when Jacob came in from the fields, Leah told him, “You're sleeping with me tonight. I hired you with my son's love flowers.” They slept together that night,
translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu daa ti yi mɔɣu ni na zaawuni, ka Liya yi nti tuh’ o soli yɛl’ o, “N yɛn kpɛla a sanna zuŋɔ, dama n zaŋla m bia ŋmaankpihiga yo a zuɣu.” Ka Yaakubu min’ o daa dɔni dindali maa yuŋ.

english_verse: and God answered Leah's prayers by giving her a fifth son.
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa deei Liya suhigu ka o niŋ pua n-dɔɣi bidibiga ŋun pah’ anu ti Yaakubu.

english_verse: Leah shouted, “God has rewarded me for letting Jacob marry my servant,” and she named the boy Issachar.
translation_verse: Ka Liya daa yɛli, “N ni zaŋ n dab’ bipuɣiŋga ti n yidan’ la zuɣu, Naawuni deei n suhigu;” ka boli bia maa yuli Isaka.

english_verse: she exclaimed, “God has given me a wonderful gift, and my husband will praise me for giving him six sons.” So she named the boy Zebulun.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Liya daa yɛli, “Naawuni ti ma pin’ suŋ, pumpɔŋɔ n yidan’ ni ti ma jilima, dama n dɔɣi bidibis’ ayɔbu ti o”; ka daa boli bia maa yuli Zɛbulɔn.

english_verse: Later, Leah had a daughter and named her Dinah.
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka o daa ti dɔɣi bipuɣiŋga m-bol’ o yuli Daina.

english_verse: Finally, God remembered Rachel—he answered her prayer by giving her a son. “God has taken away my disgrace,” she said.
translation_verse: Ka Reechɛl daa niŋ pua n-dɔɣi bidibiga ka yɛli, “Naawuni yihi ma vi ni;”

english_verse: “I'll name the boy Joseph, and I'll pray that the Lord will give me another son.” Jacob and Laban
translation_verse: ka daa boli bia maa yuli Yisifu ka yɛli, “Yawɛ tim ma bidib’ so pahi.” Yaakubu mini Leeban yɛla

english_verse: After Joseph was born, Jacob said to Laban, “Release me from our agreement and let me return to my own country.
translation_verse: Reechɛl ni daa dɔɣi Yisifu nyaaŋa ka Yaakubu daa yɛli Leeban, “Bahim’ ma ka n kuli n ya ni n yiŋa.

english_verse: You know how hard I've worked for you, so let me take my wives and children and leave.”
translation_verse: Zaŋmi m paɣiba mini m bi’ shɛb’ zuɣu n ni jɛm a ŋɔ ti ma ka n kuli, dama a mi n ni tum tuun’ shɛli ti a.”

english_verse: Jacob answered: You've seen how hard I've worked for you, and you know how your flocks and herds have grown under my care.
translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu yɛl’ o, “Amaŋmaŋ’ mi n ni tum shɛm ti a, ka lan mi n zuɣu ni chɛ ka a niɣi yɛligi shɛm.

english_verse: You didn't have much before I came, but the Lord has blessed everything I have ever done for you. Now it's time for me to start looking out for my own family.
translation_verse: N ni daa kana saha shɛl’ la, bɛ daa nyɛla biɛla; ka pumpɔŋɔ bɛ yipa nabimi pam, ka n yi kul ŋmaligi kpa luɣ’ shɛlikam polo, Yawɛ niŋdila alibarika niŋ a ni. Amaa ka pumpɔŋɔ, bɔ saha ka man’ lee yɛn zaŋ wolim gbaai ti n yiŋnim’ gba?”

english_verse: “How much do you want me to pay you?” Laban asked. Then Jacob told him: I don't want you to pay me anything. Just do one thing, and I'll take care of your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Ka o bɔh’ o, “Ka ala ka n lee yɛn yo a?” Ka Yaakubu yɛl’ o, “A yi ni niŋ n ni yɛn yɛli shɛm ŋɔ, di bi kpa talahi ni a yo ma shɛli. N na kul ni gul’ a biŋkɔbiri maa.

english_verse: Let me go through your flocks and herds and take the sheep and goats that are either spotted or speckled and the black lambs. That's all you need to give me.
translation_verse: Chɛ ka n kpe a biŋkɔbiri maa ni zuŋɔ ti gahim piɛ’ shɛb’ bɛn liɣisiliɣisi mini bɛn mali sabilimsabilim ni piɛbihi sabila ni bu’ shɛb’ bɛn mali sabilimsabilim mini bɛn liɣisiliɣisi ni bubihi sabila; ka bɛ leei n yɔri.

english_verse: In the future you can easily find out if I've been honest. Just look and see if my animals are either spotted or speckled, or if the lambs are black. If they aren't, they've been stolen from you.
translation_verse: Ka m biɛrimaŋtali tuma ni ti yi palo a yi ti kana ni a ti nya n yɔri maa dahin’ shɛli. Ka bu’ shɛb’ mini piɛbihi shɛb’ bɛn bi liɣisiliɣisi ka mali sabilimsabilim ni bɛn nyɛ zaɣ’ sabila yi ti be m biŋkɔbiri ni, di wuhiya ni n zu ba mi maa.”

english_verse: “I agree to that,” was Laban's response.
translation_verse: Ka Leeban daa yɛli, “Lala viɛla. Ti ni niŋ a ni yɛli shɛm maa.”

english_verse: Before the end of the day, Laban had separated his spotted and speckled animals and the black lambs from the others and had put his sons in charge of them.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Leeban daa gahim bula’ shɛb’ bɛn mali bomaboma ni sabilimsabilim mini bunyama bɛn zaa liɣisiliɣisi ni bɛn mali sabilimsabilim ni bɛn zaa mali piɛlimpiɛlim ni piɛbihi shɛb’ bɛn zaa nyɛ zaɣ’ sabila n-zaŋ ba ti o bihi ni bɛ guli ba,

english_verse: Then Laban made Jacob keep the rest of the sheep and goats at a distance of three days' journey.
translation_verse: ka daa chaŋ luɣ’ shɛli katiŋa din nyɛ daba ata soli chandi ka chɛ Yaakubu, ka Yaakubu daa gbib’ ŋun’ Leeban biŋkɔb’ shɛb’ bɛn kpalim la.

english_verse: Jacob cut branches from some poplar trees and from some almond and evergreen trees. He peeled off part of the bark and made the branches look spotted and speckled.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yaakubu daa chaŋ ti ŋmahi tihi balibu diba ata wula n-kɔrisikɔrisi di paɣiri ka chɛ ka di mali piɛlimpiɛlim, ka chɛ ka di piɛlimpiɛlim maa be palo ni ka di piɛlipiɛla.

english_verse: Then he put the branches where the sheep and goats would see them while they were drinking from the water trough. The goats mated there
translation_verse: Ka o daa zaŋ o ni kɔrisikɔrisi da’ shɛŋa maa sɔŋ biŋkɔbiri maa tooni kɔnyuri bɔɣili gbini luɣ’ shɛli biŋkɔbiri maa ni kanna ti nyuri kom. Ka biŋkɔbiri maa daa yi ti kana ni bɛ ti nyu kom ka duri taba,

english_verse: Some of the sheep that Jacob was keeping for Laban were already spotted. And when the others were ready to mate, he made sure that they faced in the direction of the spotted and black ones. In this way, Jacob built up a flock of sheep for himself and did not put them with the other sheep.
translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu daa woligi piɛbihi bɛ ko, ka ŋmaligi biŋkɔbiri maa nina kpa Leeban biŋkɔbiri bɛn mali bomaboma mini zaɣ’ sabila zaa la polo; ka wolig’ o biŋkɔbiri zali bɛ kɔŋko ka bi chɛ ka bɛ laɣim Leeban biŋkɔbiri maa ni.

english_verse: When the stronger sheep were mating near the drinking place, Jacob made sure that the spotted branches were there.
translation_verse: Ka biŋkɔb’ shɛb’ bɛn mali yaa daa yi ti duri taba, Yaakubu zaŋdila dari maa sɔŋ bɛ tooni kɔbɔɣili maa gbini ni bɛ be dari maa gbini duri taba.

english_verse: But he would not put out the branches when the weaker animals were mating. So Jacob got all of the healthy animals, and Laban got what was left.
translation_verse: Amaa o daa bi zaŋdi dari maa sɔŋdi biŋkɔb’ shɛb’ bɛn ka yaa la bɛn’ sani, ka di zuɣu daa chɛ ka Leeban biŋkɔbiri nyɛ zaɣ’ gbarima, ka Yaakubu dina nyɛ bɛn mali yaa,

english_verse: Jacob soon became rich and successful. He owned many sheep, goats, camels, and donkeys, as well as a lot of slaves.
translation_verse: Ka lala zuɣu daa chɛ ka Yaakubu leei bundana ka mali biŋkɔbiri pam, ka mali daba bɛn nyɛ dɔbba mini paɣiba ni laakumnim’ ni bunsi.

english_verse: Jacob heard that Laban's sons were complaining, “Jacob is now a rich man, and he got everything he owns from our father.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yaakubu daa wum ni Leeban bidibisi yɛrimi, “Yaakubu n-fa ti ba binshɛɣukam zaa, ka binshɛlikam din nyɛ ti ba dini, dina ka o zaŋ nya buni.”

english_verse: Jacob also noticed that Laban was not as friendly as he had been before.
translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu daa nya ka Leeban bi lan bɔr’ o yɛla kaman o ni daa pun bɔr’ o yɛla shɛm la.

english_verse: One day the Lord said, “Jacob, go back to your relatives in the land of your ancestors, and I will be with you.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Yaakubu, “Labim’ a ba min’ a dɔɣiriba tiŋgban’ ni. N ni be a sani.”

english_verse: Jacob sent for Rachel and Leah to meet him in the pasture where he kept his sheep,
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Yaakubu daa tim ti boli Reechɛl mini Liya ni bɛ ka o sanna o ni daa mal’ o biŋkɔbiri be mɔɣu ni luɣ’ shɛli la.

english_verse: and he told them: Your father isn't as friendly with me as he used to be, but the God my ancestors worshiped has been on my side.
translation_verse: Ka o daa ti yɛli ba, “N nyaya ka yi ba bi lan bɔri n yɛla kaman o ni daa yi bɔri n yɛla shɛm la. Amaa m ba Naawuni la kul be n sani.

english_verse: years to buy your sheep and goats. During that time you kept changing my wages.
translation_verse: Yi mi ni n tum tuma ni n yaa zaa ti yi ba.

english_verse: and that he keeps cheating me by changing my wages time after time. But God has protected me.
translation_verse: Amaa ka o ŋari ma. O taɣi n yɔri la siɣimsiɣim bupia, amaa Naawuni bi saɣi ka o niŋ ma shɛli.

english_verse: When your father said the speckled sheep would be my wages, all of them were speckled. And when he said the spotted ones would be mine, all of them were spotted.
translation_verse: O yi yɛli, ‘Bu’ shɛb’ bɛn liɣisiliɣisi ka n yɛn zaŋ yo a,’ buhi maa zaa ti dɔɣirila bubihi shɛb’ bɛn liɣisiliɣisi; ka o yi lan yɛli, ‘Bu’ shɛb’ bɛn mali bomaboma ka n yɛn zaŋ yo a,’ buhi maa zaa ti dɔɣirila bubihi shɛb’ bɛn mali bomaboma.

english_verse: That's how God has taken sheep and goats from your father and given them to me.
translation_verse: Lala ka Naawuni niŋ zaŋ yi ba biŋkɔbiri ti ma.

english_verse: Once, when the flocks were mating, I dreamed that all the rams were either spotted or speckled.
translation_verse: “Biŋkɔbiri maa tab’ dubu saha ka n daa ti zahim zahindi nya ka bulahi bɛn duri buhi maa nyɛla zaɣ’ bomaboma mini bɛn liɣisiliɣisi ni bɛn nyɛ zaɣ’ bɔribɔri.

english_verse: Then God's angel called me by name. I answered,
translation_verse: Di saha ka Naawuni malaika daa yɛli ma zahindi maa ni, ‘Yaakubu,’ ka n saɣi yɛli, ‘N-nyɛ ma!’

english_verse: and he said, “Notice that all the rams are either spotted or speckled. I know everything Laban is doing to you,
translation_verse: Ka o yɛli ma, ‘Kpuɣim’ a zuɣu lihi nya bula shɛb’ zaa bɛn duri buhi ŋɔ, bɛ nyɛla zaɣ’ bomaboma mini bɛn liɣisiliɣisi ni bɛn nyɛ zaɣ’ bɔribɔri, dama n nya Leeban ni niŋd’ a shɛm.

english_verse: and I am the God you worshiped at Bethel, when you poured olive oil on a rock and made a promise to me. Leave here at once and return to the land where you were born.”
translation_verse: Mani n-nyɛ Bɛtɛl Naawuni, luɣ’ shɛl’ a ni daa booi kpam bahi bimbini zuɣu ka po pɔri n san’ la. Yiɣisim’ tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni lab’ bɛ ni daa dɔɣ’ a tiŋgbɔn shɛl’ ni pumpɔŋɔ’ ”

english_verse: He treats us like foreigners and has even cheated us out of the bride price that should have been ours.
translation_verse: O lihi ti la tinzunnima. O zaŋ ti mi kɔhi, ka mali bɛ ni zaŋ laɣ’ shɛli yo ti zuɣu maa dira.

english_verse: So do whatever God tells you to do. Even the property God took from our father and gave to you really belongs to us and our children.
translation_verse: Naawuni ni deei binshɛlikam zaa ti ba sani maa nyɛla ti mini ti bihi dini; dinzuɣu Naawuni ni yɛl’ a ni a niŋm’ shɛlikam zaa, nyin’ niŋm’ li.”

english_verse: Then Jacob, his wives, and his children got on camels and left
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yaakubu daa zaŋ o paɣiba min’ o bihi balisi laakumnima,

english_verse: northern Syria for the home of his father Isaac in Canaan. Jacob took along all his flocks, herds, and other property.
translation_verse: ka taɣ’ o niɣi min’ o biŋkɔbbaligu shɛb’ zaa bɛn daa nyɛ o nyɔri m-pah’ o ni daa zali naɣ’ shɛb’ Mɛsopoteemia la zuɣu n-lu soli kuni Keenan tiŋgbɔŋ ni o ba Yisahaku sani.

english_verse: Before Rachel left, she stole the household idols while Laban was out shearing his sheep.
translation_verse: Leeban daa chaŋla o piɛri kɔbiri chɛbu, ka Reechɛl daa zu n-kpuɣ’ o ba wuna.

english_verse: When Jacob crossed the Euphrates River and headed for the hill country of Gilead, he took with him everything he owned. Laban Catches Up with Jacob
translation_verse: O daa zaŋla o ni mali binshɛɣukam zaa yiɣisi zo n-chaŋ ti gbaai Yufretiiz Mɔɣili du n-zaŋ o zuɣu kpa zoya ni tin’ shɛli din yuli booni Giliad la polo. Leeban kari Yaakubu naba

english_verse: Three days later Laban found out that Jacob had gone.
translation_verse: Di daba ata dali ka bɛ daa ti yɛli Leeban ni Yaakubu yiɣisiya zo.

english_verse: So he took some of his relatives along and chased after Jacob for seven days, before catching up with him in the hill country of Gilead.
translation_verse: Ka Leeban daa zaŋ o dɔɣiriba pa omaŋ’ zuɣu n-kari Yaakubu naba daba ayopɔin hal ti mir’ o zoya ni tiŋ’ shɛli din yuli daa booni Giliad maa.

english_verse: But God appeared to Laban in a dream that night and warned, “Don't say a word to Jacob. Don't make a threat or a promise.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Naawuni daa ka Leeban ŋun nyɛ Aram nir’ maa sanna yuŋ zahindi ni ti yɛl’ o, “Miri ka a yɛli Yaakubu yɛtɔɣ’ viɛlli bee yɛtɔɣ’ biɛɣu.”

english_verse: Jacob had set up camp in the hill country of Gilead, when Laban and his relatives came and set up camp in another part of the hill country. Laban went to Jacob
translation_verse: Ka Leeban daa kana ti paai Yaakubu. Yaakubu daa tila o suɣa zali zoya ni, ka Leeban mi min’ o dɔɣiriba maa daa ti bɛ suɣa zali zoya ni tin’ shɛli din yuli booni Giliad la.

english_verse: and said: Look what you've done! You've tricked me and run off with my daughters like a kidnapper.
translation_verse: Ka Leeban daa bɔhi Yaakubu, “Bɔzuɣu ka a ŋari ma zaŋ m bipuɣinsi zo kaman tɔbu ka a tuhi gbahi ba maa? Tuun’ bɔ ka a lee tum ma maa?

english_verse: Why did you sneak away without telling me? I would have given you a going-away party with singing and with music on tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Bɔ n-niŋ ka a ŋari ma ka sɔɣi zo, ka bi yɛli ma. N naan chɛbis’ a ni suhupiɛlli, ka ŋme goonjɛnim’ ka chaɣisi sayɛya ka yili yila niŋ a.

english_verse: You didn't even give me a chance to kiss my own grandchildren and daughters goodbye. That was really foolish.
translation_verse: Bɔ n-niŋ ka a bi chɛ ka m mɔɣisi n yaansi maa mini m bipuɣinsi maa kparima n-chɛbisi ba? A tum gala.

english_verse: I could easily hurt you, but the God your father worshiped has warned me not to make any threats or promises.
translation_verse: M mali yiko ni n di niŋ a zaɣ’ biɛɣu, amaa a ba Yisahaku Naawuni la sa yɛli ma yuŋ la, ‘Miri ka a yɛli Yaakubu yɛtɔɣ’ viɛlli bee zaɣ’ biɛɣu.’

english_verse: I can understand why you were eager to return to your father, but why did you have to steal my idols?
translation_verse: A ni bɔr’ a ba yiŋ’ la zuɣu ka a yiɣisi zɔri maa, ka bɔ n-niŋ ka a zu n-kpuɣi n wuna?”

english_verse: Jacob answered, “I left secretly because I was afraid you would take your daughters from me by force.
translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu daa garigi yɛli Leeban, “N daa zɔr’ a mi, dama n daa tɛhimi ni di pa shɛli ka a ti zaŋ kiŋkansi fa a bipuɣinsi maa n sani.

english_verse: If you find that any one of us has taken your idols, I'll have that person killed. Let your relatives be witnesses. Show me what belongs to you, and you can take it back.” Jacob did not realize that Rachel had stolen the household idols.
translation_verse: Amaa a yi nya a wuna maa so sani, bɛn’ kum’ o. Lihimi n nɛma ŋɔ ni nya, a bini yi be di ni, nyin’ yihim’ li ti dɔɣiriba ŋɔ zaa ninni.” Yaakubu daa bi mi ni Reechɛl n-zu n-kpuɣi wuna maa.

english_verse: Laban searched the tents of Jacob, Leah, and the two servant women, but did not find the idols. Then he went to Rachel's tent.
translation_verse: Ka Leeban daa kpe Yaakubu suɣili ni n-yi nimaani kpe Liya suɣili ni, ka yi nimaani kpe dabipaɣiba ayi la suɣa ni, amaa ka bi nya shɛli di ni. Ka o daa yi Liya suɣili ni chaŋ ti kpe Reechɛl suɣili ni.

english_verse: She had already hidden them in the cushion she used as a saddle and was sitting on it. Laban searched everywhere and did not find them.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Reechɛl daa kpuɣi wuna maa n-zaŋ niŋ laakum gal’ ni n-du n-ʒi di zuɣu. Ka Leeban daa vihi suɣili maa ni zaa bo li ka bi nya li.

english_verse: Rachel said, “Father, please don't be angry with me for not getting up; I'm having my period.” Laban kept on searching, but still did not find the idols.
translation_verse: Ka Reechɛl daa yɛl’ o ba, “N dana, di je suli niŋ ma n ni ku tooi yiɣisi zani a tooni maa zuɣu, dama paɣitali biɛhigu ni ka m be.” Ka Leeban daa vihi bo wuni maa ka bi nya li.

english_verse: Jacob became very angry and said to Laban: What have I done wrong? Have I committed some crime? Is that why you hunted me down?
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yaakubu suhu daa yiɣisi bahi Leeban zuɣu ka o bɔhi Leeban, “Taal’ bɔ ka n lee tum’ a? Ka alahichi dini ka n lee tum ka a kariti n naba na?

english_verse: After searching through everything I have, did you find anything of yours? If so, put it here, where your relatives and mine can see it. Then we can decide what to do.
translation_verse: A ni vihi m binshɛɣukam zaa ni maa, a yiŋ’ bimbɔ ka a nya di ni? Zaŋm’ li zali n dɔɣiriba min’ a dɔɣiriba ŋɔ ninni, ka bɛ baŋ ti ni ŋun mali yɛlimaŋli.

english_verse: If a wild animal killed one of your sheep or goats, I paid for it myself. In fact, you demanded the full price, whether the animal was killed during the day or at night.
translation_verse: Mɔɣu ni biŋkɔbiri daa yi gbaag’ a piɛɣu, m bi zaŋd’ o na ti wuhir’ a, amaa n daa yi gbaarila mmaŋmaŋ’ piɛɣu zal’ o zaani. Bɛ daa yi zu binshɛli wuntaŋ’ ni bee yuŋ, a chɛrimi ka n yo a li.

english_verse: I sweated every day, and I couldn't sleep at night because of the cold.
translation_verse: Wuntaŋ’ daa kul wɔbiri ma mi dabisili kam, ka wari mi kpɛri ma yuŋ, ka n gaani gom.

english_verse: If the fearsome God worshiped by Abraham and my father Isaac had not been on my side, you would have sent me away without a thing. But God saw my hard work, and he knew the trouble I was in, so he helped me. Then last night he told you how wrong you were. Jacob and Laban Make an Agreement
translation_verse: Ka n yaannim’ Naawuni ŋun nyɛ Ibrahimma Naawuni ka nyɛ Yisahaku ni jɛmdi so ŋɔ yi di ka n sani, biɛhiŋ kani, a naan chɛ ka n chaŋ ni nuzaŋa. Naawuni nya n wahala mini n ni tum tuun’ shɛŋa, ka sa kpah’ a zuɣu ni yuŋ maa.” Yaakubu mini Leeban lo tab’ alikauli

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “Leah and Rachel are my daughters, and their children belong to me. All these sheep you are taking are really mine too. In fact, everything you have belongs to me. But there is nothing I can do to keep my daughters and their children.
translation_verse: Ka Leeban daa yɛli Yaakubu, “Bipuɣinsi ŋɔ nyɛla m bipuɣinsi, ka bihi ŋɔ nyɛ m bihi, ka biŋkɔbiri ŋɔ nyɛ m biŋkɔbiri; ka a ni nya binshɛɣukam zaa kpe ŋɔ nyɛla n dini. Amaa zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ wula ka n yɛn niŋ m bipuɣinsi ŋɔ mini bɛ ni dɔɣi bi’ shɛb’ ŋɔ?

english_verse: So I am ready to make an agreement with you, and we will pile up some large rocks here to remind us of the agreement.”
translation_verse: Pumpɔŋɔ chɛ ka m min’ a lo tab’ alikauli, ka chɛ ka di leei shɛhira m min’ a sunsuuni.”

english_verse: After Jacob had set up a large rock,
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yaakubu daa pii kuɣili sa nimaani ni di nyɛ din teeri ba.

english_verse: he told his men to get some more rocks and pile them up next to it. Then Jacob and Laban ate a meal together beside the rocks.
translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu daa yɛl’ o dɔɣiriba, “Pihimiya kuɣa na,” ka bɛ daa pihi kuɣa maa na nti kahi li duhi, ka daa ʒini kuɣ’ duli maa gbini di bindirigu.

english_verse: Laban named the pile of rocks Jegar Sahadutha. But Jacob named it Galeed.
translation_verse: Ka Leeban daa boli di yuli Jɛgarisahaduta; ka Yaakubu mi boli di yuli Galiid.

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “This pile of rocks will remind us of our agreement.” That's why the place was named Galeed.
translation_verse: Ka Leeban daa yɛli Yaakubu, “Kuɣ’ duli ŋɔ nyɛla shɛhira m min’ a sunsuuni zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ.” Dinzuɣu ka bɛ daa boli di yuli Galiid.

english_verse: Laban also said, “This pile of rocks means that the Lord will watch us both while we are apart from each other.” So the place was also named Mizpah.
translation_verse: Ka Leeban daa yɛli, “Ti ni yɛn woligi tab’ ŋɔ, n suhiri Yawɛ ni o gul’ ti.” Dinzuɣu ka bɛ daa lan boli nimaani yuli Mizipa.

english_verse: Then Laban said: If you mistreat my daughters or marry other women, I may not know about it, but remember, God is watching us!
translation_verse: Leeban daa lan yɛli, “A yi nahim m bipuɣinsi ŋɔ bee a yi kpuɣi paɣiba pahi bɛ zuɣu, ka n ʒi di yɛla, nyin’ teemi ni Naawuni n nyɛ m min’ a shɛhiralana.

english_verse: Both this pile of rocks and this large rock have been set up between us as a reminder. I must never go past them to attack you, and you must never come past them to attack me.
translation_verse: Kuɣ’ duli ŋɔ mini kuɣ’ shɛli din yɛn teeri ti ŋɔ nyɛla shɛhira din wuhiri ni n ku yaɣ’ kuɣ’ duli maa zuɣu ka a sanna ti niŋ a zaɣ’ biɛɣu, ka a gba ku yaɣ’ kuɣ’ duli maa zuɣu ka n sanna ti niŋ ma zaɣ’ biɛɣu.

english_verse: My father Nahor, your grandfather Abraham, and their ancestors all worshiped the same God, and he will make sure that we each keep the agreement. Then Jacob made a promise in the name of the fearsome God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Ibrahimma Naawuni mini Nahɔr Naawuni ni bɛ yaannim’ Naawuni ŋɔ ni woligi yɛlimaŋli ti ti.” Ka Yaakubu daa po o ba Yisahaku ni jɛmdi Naawuni so maa.

english_verse: Jacob killed an animal and offered it as a sacrifice there on the mountain, and he invited his men to eat with him. After the meal they spent the night on the mountain.
translation_verse: Ka o daa mali sara zoli zuɣu n-laɣim’ o dɔɣiriba ni bɛ kana ka bɛ min’ o ti laɣim di bindirigu, ka bɛ daa kana ka bɛ min’ o ti laɣim di bindirigu maa ka kpalim be zoli maa zuɣu yuŋ hal ka biɛɣu ti neei.

english_verse: Early the next morning, Laban kissed his daughters and his grandchildren goodbye, then he left to go back home.
translation_verse: Ka Leeban daa ti daŋ yiɣisibu asibaasi m-mɔɣis’ o yaansi min’ o bipuɣinsi maa kparima, ka niŋ alibarika niŋ bɛ ni ka lab’ kuli.

english_verse: As Jacob was on his way back home, some of God's angels came and met him.
translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu daa yiɣisi chani ka Naawuni malaikanim’ chirig’ o sol’ ni;

english_verse: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is God's camp.” So he named the place Mahanaim.
translation_verse: ka o daa nya ba ka yɛli, “Naawuni sansani m-bɔŋɔ!” Dinzuɣu ka o daa boli nimaani yuli Mahanaim.

english_verse: Jacob sent messengers on ahead to Esau, who lived in the land of Seir, also known as Edom.
translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu daa tim tuumba o biɛli Iso sani Siɛr Ɛdom tiŋgbɔŋ ni, ka bɛ daŋ o tooni.

english_verse: Jacob told them to say to Esau, “Master, I am your servant! I have lived with Laban all this time,
translation_verse: O daa wuhi ba: “Yi ni ti yɛn yɛli n dan’ Iso shɛm m-bɔŋɔ: ‘A dabili Yaakubu ni yɛli shɛm m-bɔŋɔ: “N daa chaŋ ti bela Leeban sani hal ti paai pumpɔŋɔ.

english_verse: and now I own cattle, donkeys, and sheep, as well as many slaves. Master, I am sending these messengers in the hope that you will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: M mali niɣi mini bunsi ni biŋkɔbbaligu ni daba bɛn nyɛ dɔbba mini paɣiba; ka tim na ni n ti yɛli nyini n dana din ni chɛ ka a suhu maai ni mani.’ ”

english_verse: When the messengers returned, they told Jacob, “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is heading this way with
translation_verse: Ka tuumba maa daa ti labina ti yɛli Yaakubu, “Ti chaŋ a biɛli Iso sani, ka o zaŋ ninvuɣ’ kɔbisinahi pa omaŋ’ zuɣu n-kanna ni o ti tuh’ a soli.”

english_verse: Jacob was so frightened that he divided his people, sheep, cattle, and camels into two groups.
translation_verse: Ka dabiɛm daa gbaai Yaakubu pam ka o suhu zɔhira. Ka o daa pirig’ o niriba bɛn be o sani min’ o biŋkɔbbaligu ni o niɣi ni o laakumnim’ ʒii buyi,

english_verse: He thought, “If Esau attacks one group, perhaps the other can escape.”
translation_verse: ka yɛl’ o suhu ni, “Iso yi kana ti ku ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn be tooni ŋɔ, bɛn doli nyaaŋa la ni zo n-tiligi.”

english_verse: Then Jacob prayed: You, Lord, are the God who was worshiped by my grandfather Abraham and by my father Isaac. You told me to return home to my family, and you promised to be with me and make me successful.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yaakubu daa yɛli, “N yab’ Ibrahimma mini m ba Yisahaku Naawuni ŋɔ, Nyin’ Yawɛ, a daa yɛli ma, ‘Labim’ a ya min’ a dɔɣiriba sani ka n niŋ a zaɣ’ viɛlli.’

english_verse: Please rescue me from my brother. I am afraid he will come and attack not only me, but my wives and children as well.
translation_verse: N suhir’ a, fam’ ma m biɛli Iso nuu ni bahi. N zɔr’ o, dama di pa shɛli ka o ti kana ti ku m mini m bihi ni bɛ manim’ ŋɔ zaa.

english_verse: But you have promised that I would be a success and that someday it will be as hard to count my descendants as it is to count the grains of sand along the seashore.
translation_verse: Amaa ka a mi daa pun yɛli ma, ‘N ni niŋ a zaɣ’ viɛlli, ka chɛ ka a zuliya ti be kaman mɔɣ’ bihigu la, ka so ku tooi kali ba.’ ”

english_verse: After Jacob had spent the night there, he chose some animals as gifts for Esau:
translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu daa gbe nimaani dindali maa yuŋ, ka daa piig’ o biŋkɔbiri maa ni shɛb’ ni o ti o biɛli Iso.

english_verse: And Jacob told them to be sure to say that he was right behind them. Jacob hoped the gifts would make Esau friendly, so Esau would be glad to see him when they met.
translation_verse: ka lan yɛl’ o, ‘Ka din pahi nyɛla, a dabili Yaakubu doli ti nyaaŋa na.’ ” Dama Yaakubu daa yɛlila o suhu ni, “N yi chɛ ka bɛ zaŋ pini ŋɔ daŋ n tooni ti ti o, n ni maag’ o suhu, ka di nyaaŋa m min’ o nini yi ti nya taba, di pa shɛli o ni deei ma.”

english_verse: Jacob said, “I have seen God face to face, and I am still alive.” So he named the place Peniel.
translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu daa yɛli, “N nini nya Naawuni ka bi kpi.” Dinzuɣu ka o daa boli nimaani yuli Pɛniɛl.

english_verse: Jacob put servants in charge of each herd and told them, “Go ahead of me and keep a space between each herd.”
translation_verse: Ka o daa pirigi ba gbilligbilli n-zaŋ ba niŋ o tumtumdiba nuu ni, ka bɛ taɣiri ba gbilligbilli dol’ taba ka o yɛli ba, “Garimiya n tooni chani ka chɛ ka larigim be yi sunsuuni.”

english_verse: Then he said to the servant in charge of the first herd, “When Esau meets you, he will ask whose servant you are. He will want to know where you are going and who owns those animals in front of you.
translation_verse: O daa yɛl’ o tumtumdiba kpɛma, “M biɛli Iso yi ti tuhi ya soli bɔhi ya, ‘Ŋuni n-lee sun ya? Ka ya polo ka yi lee chana? Ka ŋuni n-lee su biŋkɔb’ shɛb’ bɛn be yi tooni ŋɔ?’

english_verse: So tell him, ‘They belong to your servant Jacob, who is coming this way. He is sending them as a gift to his master Esau.’ ”
translation_verse: Di saha yin’ yɛlimiy’ o, ‘A dabili Yaakubu n-su ba, ka zaŋ ba ti ti ni ti zaŋ ba na ti ti nyini n-dan’ Iso pini, ka din pahi nyɛla, omaŋmaŋ’ doli ti nyaaŋa na.’ ”

english_verse: Jacob also told the men in charge of the second and third herds and those who followed to say the same thing when they met Esau.
translation_verse: Lala ka o daa yɛl’ o tumtumda so ŋun pah’ ayi mini ŋun pah’ ata ni bɛn zaa daa taɣiri biŋkɔbiri maa; “Yi yi ti tuhi Iso soli, yin’ yɛlimiy’ o yɛtɔɣ’ yini maa,

english_verse: Jacob's men took the gifts on ahead of him, but he spent the night in camp. Jacob's Name Is Changed to Israel
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa zaŋ pini maa daŋ o tooni, ka ŋun’ maŋmaŋ’ daa kpalim gbe suɣa maa shee dindali maa yuŋ. Yaakubu mini ninvuɣ’ so vaya Pɛnuɛl

english_verse: Afterwards, Jacob went back and spent the rest of the night alone. A man came and fought with Jacob until just before daybreak.
translation_verse: ka ŋun’ Yaakubu kɔŋko daa kpalim be nyaaŋa. Di saha ka do’ so daa kana ka o min’ o ti kpe val’ ni n-va hal ka biɛɣ’ ti neerina.

english_verse: When the man saw that he could not win, he struck Jacob on the hip and threw it out of joint.
translation_verse: Doo maa ni daa nya ka o bi tooi nyaŋ Yaakubu maa, ka o daa shih’ o sakpuɣu, ka o sakpuɣu maa ŋmirigi bɛ ni daa vari saha shɛli maa.

english_verse: They kept on wrestling until the man said, “Let go of me! It's almost daylight.” “You can't go until you bless me,” Jacob replied.
translation_verse: Ka doo maa daa yɛl’ o, “Biɛɣu neera, chɛ ka n chaŋ.” Ka Yaakubu yɛl’ o, “N ku chɛ ka a chaŋ, faashee ka a niŋ alibarika niŋ n ni.”

english_verse: Then the man asked, “What is your name?” “Jacob,” he answered.
translation_verse: Ka doo maa bɔh’ o, “A yuli?” Ka o yɛl’ o, “N yuli Yaakubu.”

english_verse: The man said, “From now on, your name will no longer be Jacob. You will be called Israel, because you have wrestled with God and with men, and you have won.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka doo maa daa yɛl’ o, “A yuli ku lan booni Yaakubu, amaa a yuli ni boonila Izraɛl, dama a mini Naawuni ni ninsalinim’ vaya ka a di nasara.”

english_verse: The sun was coming up as Jacob was leaving Peniel. He was limping because he had been struck on the hip,
translation_verse: Wuntaŋ’ puhibu na saha ka Yaakubu daa yi Pɛnuɛl chana ka luri wɔbiliwɔbili, o sakpuɣu maa zuɣu.

english_verse: and the muscle on his hip joint had been injured. That's why even today the people of Israel don't eat the hip muscle of any animal.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu dindali zaŋ na hal ni zuŋɔ, Izraɛlnim’ bi saɣiri ŋubiri binsakpuɣu zuɣu nimdi, doo maa ni daa shihi Yaakubu sakpuɣu maa zuɣu.

translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu bidibisi maa daa yi mɔɣu ni na ti wum li ka bɛ suhu yiɣisi ka bɛ je suli; Shɛkɛm ni daa tum jɛrilim Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ni n-zaŋ Yaakubu bipuɣiŋga saɣim maa zuɣu. Dama di daa bi simdi ni lala niŋ.

english_verse: Hamor said to Jacob and his sons: My son Shechem really loves Dinah. Please let him marry her.
translation_verse: Ka Hamɔr daa yɛl’ o, “M bia Shɛkɛm bɔr’ a bipuɣiŋga, n suhir’ a, zaŋm’ o ti o ka o niŋ o paɣa.

english_verse: Why don't you start letting your families marry into our families and ours marry into yours?
translation_verse: Chɛ ka ti mini ya kpuɣiri tab’ bihi niŋdi ti paɣiba. Zaŋmiya yi bipuɣinsi tiri ti, ka kpuɣimi ti gba bipuɣinsi niŋdi yi paɣiba.

english_verse: You can share this land with us. Move freely about until you find the property you want; then buy it and settle down here.
translation_verse: Kpalimmiya be ti sani. Yi ni tooi be yi suhuri ni bɔri ni yi be luɣ’ shɛlikam tiŋgbani ŋɔ ni, ka gɔri kɔhigu yi yubu, ka su tiŋgbani maa luɣ’ shɛŋa polo.”

english_verse: Jacob's sons wanted to get even with Shechem and his father because of what had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Shɛkɛm ni daa dihi Yaakubu bidibisi maa tizɔpaɣ’ Daina vi maa zuɣu, ka bɛ daa garigi Shɛkɛm min’ o ba Hamɔr yɔhiŋgu garigibu.

english_verse: So they tricked them by saying: You're not circumcised! It would be a disgrace for us to let you marry Dinah now.
translation_verse: Bɛ daa yɛli ba mi, “Ti ku tooi zaŋ ti tizɔpaɣ’ ti ninvuɣ’ so ŋun bi guni, dama lala nyɛla vi ti sani.

english_verse: But we will let you marry her, if you and the other men in your tribe agree to be circumcised.
translation_verse: Amaa yɛl’ yini n naɣ’ beni ka ti ni bɔri ni yi niŋ li pɔi ka ti naanyi saɣi, dina n-nyɛ: yi chɛ ka yi dɔbba zaa guni m-be kaman tinima.

english_verse: Then your families can marry into ours, and ours can marry into yours, and we can live together like one nation.
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka ti ni saɣi zaŋdi ti bipuɣinsi tiri ya, ka ti gba kpuɣiri yi bipuɣinsi, ka kpalim be yi tiŋgbani ŋɔ ni ka ti mini ya leei ninvuɣ’ yinsi.

english_verse: But if you don't agree to be circumcised, we'll take Dinah and leave this place.
translation_verse: Amaa yi yi ku saɣi guni kaman ti ni yɛli shɛm maa, dindina ti ni zaŋ ti bipuɣiŋga maa yiɣisi chaŋ.”

english_verse: Shechem was the most respected person in his family, and he was so in love with Dinah that he hurried off to get everything done.
translation_verse: Ka nachimbil’ maa daa guni yomyom, dama o suhu daa yu’ Yaakubu bipuɣiŋga maa hal ti yaɣi. O daa nyɛla yulilana o daŋ ni.

english_verse: The two men met with the other leaders of their city and told them:
translation_verse: Di saha ka Hamɔr min’ o bia Shɛkɛm daa chaŋ tiŋ’ maa dunol’ ni nti yɛli tiŋ’ maa ni dɔbba,

english_verse: These people really are friendly. Why not let them move freely about until they find the property they want? There's enough land here for them and for us. Then our families can marry into theirs, and theirs can marry into ours.
translation_verse: “Niriba ŋɔ nyaŋ ninvuɣ’ maŋa pam, chɛliya ka ti chɛ ba ka bɛ be tiŋgbani ŋɔ ni n-gɔri kɔhigu bɛ yubu, dama tiŋgbani ŋɔ galisiya pam; ka chɛ ka ti kpuɣiri bɛ bipuɣinsi; ka ti gba zaŋdi ti bipuɣinsi tiri ba.

english_verse: We have to do only one thing before they will agree to stay here and become one nation with us. Our men will have to be circumcised just like theirs.
translation_verse: Amaa ti yi bɔri ni bɛ be ti sani ka ti mini ba nyɛ ninvuɣ’ yinsi, faashee ka ti dɔbba zaa guni m-be kaman bɛ ni be shɛm.

english_verse: Just think! We'll get their property, as well as their flocks and herds. All we have to do is to agree, and they will live here with us.
translation_verse: Ti yi saɣi ka bɛ be ti sani, bɛ niɣi mini bɛ binshɛɣukam ni bɛ biŋkɔbiri zaa ku leei ti dini?”

english_verse: Three days later the men who had been circumcised were still weak from pain. So Simeon and Levi, two of Dinah's brothers, attacked with their swords and killed every man in the town,
translation_verse: Di daba ata dali, niriba maa gunibu maa yuma ni daa na biɛri saha shɛli maa, ka Yaakubu bidibis’ ayi, Simiɔn mini Lɛvi bɛn daa nyɛ Daina tizɔdɔbba la daa zaŋ takɔbiri chaŋ ti liri tiŋ’ maa nima n-libigi ba ku bɛ dɔbba zaa.

english_verse: including Hamor and Shechem. Then they took Dinah and left.
translation_verse: Bɛ daa ku Hamɔr min’ o bia Shɛkɛm gba, ka zaŋ Daina Shɛkɛm yiŋa n-chaŋ bɛ chandi.

english_verse: Jacob's other sons came and took everything they wanted. All this was done because of the horrible thing that had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu bidib’ shɛb’ bɛn kpalim daa chaŋ ti kpe tiŋ’ maa puuni n-di nɛma bɛ tizɔpaɣ’ maa zuɣu.

english_verse: They took sheep, goats, donkeys, and everything else that was in the town or the countryside.
translation_verse: Bɛ daa gbahi bɛ biŋkɔbbaligu mini niɣi ni bunsi, ka zaŋ binshɛlikam zaa din be tiŋ’ maa puuni mini din be mɔɣu ni

english_verse: After taking everything of value from the houses, they dragged away the wives and children of their victims.
translation_verse: ni bɛ daazichi zaa ni bɛ paɣiba mini bɛ bihi ni binshɛɣukam din daa be bɛ yinsi zaa chaŋ.

english_verse: Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “Look what you've done! Now I'm in real trouble with the Canaanites and Perizzites who live around here. There aren't many of us, and if they attack, they'll kill everyone in my household.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yaakubu daa yɛli Simiɔn mini Lɛvi, “Yi bo yɛla ti ma, di ni chɛ ka jɛlinsi kpe m mini tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni nim’ bɛn nyɛ Keenannim’ mini Pɛrizinim’ ŋɔ sunsuuni, ka m mi niriba bi zooi. Bɛ yi laɣim kana ti liri ma, bɛ ni ku m mini n nyaaŋa zaa.”

english_verse: They answered, “Was it right to let our own sister be treated that way?”
translation_verse: Amaa ka bɛ yɛl’ o, “Bɔzuɣu ka bɛ niŋ ti tizɔpaɣ’ maa kaman pagɔrili n-nyɛ o maa?”

english_verse: Afterwards, we'll go to Bethel. I will build an altar there for God, who answered my prayers when I was in trouble and who has always been at my side.
translation_verse: ka ti yiɣisi chaŋ Bɛtɛl. M bɔri ni m mɛla bimbini nimaani zali Naawuni so ŋun daa deei n suhigu n nandahima nyabu dali, ka be n sani n ni chaŋ luɣ’ shɛlikam la.”

english_verse: So everyone gave Jacob their idols and their earrings, and he buried them under the oak tree near Shechem.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa zaŋ tinzun tiŋ’ wuna din be bɛ sani zaa mini bɛ ni daa kpa tibikpar’ shɛŋa ti Yaakubu, ka Yaakubu daa zaŋ li sɔɣi ti’ shɛli din nyɛ oki tia din miri Shɛkɛm la gbini.

english_verse: While Jacob and his family were traveling through Canaan, God terrified the people in the towns so much that no one dared bother them.
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa yiɣisi chana, ka dabiɛm gbaai tiŋ’ shɛŋa din daa gili ba nim’ pam, ka bɛ daa bi kari doli Yaakubu bihi maa.

english_verse: Jacob built an altar there and called it “God of Bethel,” because that was the place where God had appeared to him when he was running from Esau.
translation_verse: Ka o daa me sara maligu bimbini zali nimaani, ka boli di yuli Ɛlbɛtɛl, Naawuni ni daa kahig’ omaŋ’ wuh’ o saha shɛl’ o ni daa yi o biɛli sani zɔri la zuɣu.

english_verse: While they were there, Rebekah's personal servant Deborah died. They buried her under an oak tree and called it “Weeping Oak.” God Blesses Jacob at Bethel
translation_verse: Ka Dɛbɔra ŋun daa nyɛ Ribɛka yiŋ’ dabipaɣ’ la daa kpi, ka bɛ sɔɣ’ o oki ti’ shɛli din daa be Bɛtɛl tiŋli la gbini. Ka bɛ daa boli di yuli “Kumsi tia.”

english_verse: After Jacob came back to the land of Canaan, God appeared to him again. This time he gave Jacob a new name and blessed him by saying: I am God All-Powerful, and from now on your name will be Israel instead of Jacob. You will have many children. Your descendants will become nations, and some of the men in your family will even be kings.
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa lan yɛl’ o, “Mani n-nyɛ Naawuni Kpiɔŋlan’ Naa, dɔɣim’ bihi ka yi nabi; ka zuliya pam yi a ni na; ka nanim’ pam gba ti yi a zuliya ni na.

english_verse: I will give you the land that I promised Abraham and Isaac, and it will belong to your family forever.
translation_verse: N ni daa zaŋ tiŋgbɔn shɛli ti Ibrahimma mini Yisahaku la, n ni zaŋ li ti a, ka ni lan zaŋ li ti a zuliya a kalinsi nyaaŋa.”

english_verse: Jacob set up a large rock, so that he would remember what had happened there. Then he poured wine and olive oil on the rock to show that it was dedicated to God,
translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu daa pihi kuɣa m-me bimbini zali Naawuni ni daa tɔɣis’ o yɛtɔɣa luɣ’ shɛli maa, ka booi wain mini kpam bahi di zuɣu ti Naawuni.

english_verse: and he named the place Bethel. Benjamin Is Born
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Yaakubu daa boli Naawuni ni tɔɣis’ o yɛtɔɣa luɣ’ shɛli maa yuli Bɛtɛl. Reechɛl kum yɛla

english_verse: Jacob and his family had left Bethel and were still a long way from Ephrath, when the time came for Rachel's baby to be born.
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka bɛ daa yi Bɛtɛl chani ti miri Ɛfirat ka Reechɛl piligi wolisibu ka o wolisibu maa daa kpɛm’ pam.

english_verse: She was having a rough time, but the woman who was helping her said, “Don't worry! It's a boy.”
translation_verse: Ka di ni daa ti miig’ o pam saha shɛli ka paɣidɔɣisɔtɔɣinda yɛl’ o, “Di chɛ ka a suhu zɔhira, bidibiga n-lan bala.”

english_verse: Rachel was at the point of death, and right before dying, she said, “I'll name him Benoni.” But Jacob called him Benjamin.
translation_verse: Amaa ka o daa lee kpalim dɔɣibu maa ni. O ni daa ti yɛn bahi saha shɛli ka o daa boli bia maa yuli Bɛnɔni, amaa ka o ba mi daa bol’ o yuli Bɛnjamin.

english_verse: Rachel was buried beside the road to Ephrath, which is also called Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Reechɛl ni daa kpi maa, bɛ daa sɔɣ’ o la so’ shɛli din daa kuni Ɛfirat la sokpaŋa, nimaani ka bɛ booni Bɛtilihɛm pumpɔŋɔ ŋɔ.

english_verse: Jacob, also known as Israel, traveled to the south of Eder Tower, where he set up camp.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛl daa lan gbaai chandi n-kana ti ti o suɣa zali Ɛda pii tooni. Yaakubu bidibisi (

translation_verse: Izraɛl ni daa be tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni saha shɛli maa ka Rubin daa zaŋ ŋun’ o ba dabipaɣa Biliha dɔni, ka ŋun’ Izraɛl wum li. Yaakubu bidibisi daa nyɛla pinaayi.

english_verse: Jacob went to his father Isaac at Hebron, also called Mamre or Kiriath-Arba, where Isaac's father Abraham had lived as a foreigner.
translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu daa kul’ o ba Yisahaku sani Mamri bee Kiriatariba luɣ’ shɛli bɛ ni daa booni Hiburɔn ka di nyɛ Ibrahimma mini Yisahaku ni daa be shɛl’ la.

english_verse: Isaac died at the ripe old age of

english_verse: Esau and his three wives had five sons while in Canaan. Adah's son was Eliphaz; Basemath's son was Reuel; Oholibamah's three sons were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: ka Oholibama mi dɔɣi Jɛushi mini Jalam ni Kɔra. Iso ni daa dɔɣi bidib’ shɛb’ Keenan tiŋgbɔŋ ni m-bala.

english_verse: He did this because the land was too crowded and could not support him and his brother with their flocks and herds.
translation_verse: Dama bɛ ni daa mali binshɛŋa daa galisiya pam, ka di zuɣu chɛ ka bɛ ku tooi laɣim be luɣ’ yini. Bɛ niɣi zuɣu n-daa chɛ ka bɛ ni be luɣ’ shɛli maa bi saɣi ba.

english_verse: That's why Esau made his home in the hill country of Seir.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Iso daa chaŋ ti ʒini Ɛdom zoya tiŋ’ ni. Iso ka bɛ lan booni Ɛdom la.

english_verse: Esau and Adah's oldest son was Eliphaz, and the clans that descended from him were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz,
translation_verse: Iso zuliya bɛn daa nyɛ nanima m-bɔŋɔ. Bɛ daa nyɛla Iso bituuli Ɛlifaz bidibisi. Bɛn daa nyɛ nanim’ maa n-nyɛ: Tɛman mini Omari ni Zɛfo ni Kɛnaz

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: Iso paɣ’ Oholibama bidibisi bɛn daa nyɛ nanima n-daa nyɛ: Jɛushi mini Jalam ni Kɔra. Iso paɣ’ Oholibama Ana bipuɣiŋga la ni daa dɔɣi na’ shɛba m-bala.

english_verse: Lotan's sons were Hori and Heman; his sister was Timna.
translation_verse: Lɔtan bidibisi n-daa nyɛ: Hɔri mini Hɛman. Lɔtan tizɔpaɣa n-daa nyɛ Timna.

english_verse: Shobal's sons were Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
translation_verse: Shɔbal bidibisi n-daa nyɛ: Alivan mini Manahat ni Ɛbal ni Shɛfo ni Onam.

english_verse: Zibeon's sons were Aiah and Anah—the same Anah who found an oasis in the desert while taking the donkeys of his father out to pasture.
translation_verse: Zibiɔn bidibisi n-daa nyɛ: Aiya mini Ana ŋun daa gul’ o ba Zibiɔn bunsi ka ti nya kɔbilisirim mɔɣu ni la.

english_verse: Dishon's sons were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
translation_verse: Dishɔn bidibisi n-daa nyɛ: Hɛmdan mini Ishiban ni Itiran ni Kɛran.

english_verse: Ezer's sons were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
translation_verse: Ɛzɛr bidibisi n-daa nyɛ: Bilihan mini Zaavan ni Akan.

english_verse: Dishan's sons were Uz and Aran.
translation_verse: Dishan bidibisi n-daa nyɛ: Uzi mini Aran.
