english_verse: Issachar, you are a strong donkey resting in the meadows.
translation_verse: “Isaka ŋmanila bun’ so ŋun mali kpiɔŋ piɛri sunsuuni.

english_verse: You found them so pleasant that you worked too hard and became a slave.
translation_verse: O nyaya ka nimaani vuhim shee viɛla, ka di tiŋgbani biɛhigu mali kɔre. Dinzuɣu ka o deei talahi n-tumdi tuma kaman dabili la.

english_verse: Dan, you are the tribe that will bring justice to Israel.
translation_verse: “Dan ni ti nyɛla o niriba naa kaman Izraɛl zuliyanim’ ni yino.

english_verse: You are a snake that bites the heel of a horse, making its rider fall.
translation_verse: Dan ni ti ŋmanila sokpaŋ’ tinvurigu. O nyɛla sokpaŋ’ gariŋga ŋun dimdi wɔhu napɔŋkpaa, ka ŋun bar’ o lɛbiri lur’ o kpali zuɣu.

english_verse: Our Lord, I am waiting for you to save us.
translation_verse: “Yawɛ, n guhirila saha shɛli a ni yɛn tiligi ma.

english_verse: Gad, you will be attacked, then attack your attackers.
translation_verse: “Ŋmɛnditɔya ni ti liri Gaad, amaa o ni ti kari doli ba ti fa bɛ nɛma.

english_verse: Asher, you will eat food fancy enough for a king.
translation_verse: “Asha tiŋgban’ ni ni ti mali bindir’ suma. O ni ti mali bindir’ shɛŋa di ni simdi ni naa di.

english_verse: Naphtali, you are a wild deer with lovely fawns.
translation_verse: “Naftali ŋmanila walinyaŋ so ŋun gɔr’ o yubu, ka dɔɣi bi’ viɛla.

english_verse: Joseph, you are a fruitful vine growing near a stream and climbing a wall.
translation_verse: “Yisifu ŋmanila ti’ shɛli din wandi wala, ka nyɛ din ʒe n-tab’ kulibɔŋ, ka di wula zooi yaɣi kuligbiriŋ zuɣu.

english_verse: But you stood your ground, swiftly shooting back with the help of Jacob's God, the All-Powerful One— his name is the Shepherd, Israel's mighty rock.
translation_verse: Amaa o tɔbu ku kabi, ka ti yaannim’ Naawuni ŋun nyɛ kpiɔŋlan’ ŋɔ ni chɛ ka o nuhi mali kpiɔŋ ŋuna ŋun nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ gula, ka yihiri ba barina ni ŋɔ yuli zuɣu.

english_verse: Your help came from the God your father worshiped, from God All-Powerful. God will bless you with rain and streams from the earth; he will bless you with many descendants.
translation_verse: A ba Naawuni ni sɔŋ a. Naawuni ŋun nyɛ Kpiɔŋlan’ Naa ŋɔ ni chɛ ka saa mi a. O ni chɛ ka kom yi tiŋgbani puuni na a zuɣu. O ni ti a bihi mini niɣi pam.

english_verse: My son, the blessings I give are better than the promise of ancient mountains or eternal hills. Joseph, I pray these blessings will come to you, because you are the leader of your brothers.
translation_verse: A ba daalibarika mali kpiɔŋ gari zoya din doya sahakam ŋɔ mini kuŋkuna din kul beni sahakam ŋɔ daalibarika. Naawuni chɛ ka o daalibarika ŋɔ zaa be Yisifu ŋun min’ o mabihi daa woligi ŋɔ zuɣu ni, ka be o gbɛɣu zuɣu.

english_verse: Benjamin, you are a fierce wolf, destroying your enemies morning and evening.
translation_verse: Bɛnjamin ŋmanila kundun biɛɣu. O gbahiri binyara asiba ni zaawuni ŋubira.”

english_verse: These are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is how Jacob gave each of them their proper blessings. Jacob's Death
translation_verse: Bɛmbɔŋɔ zaa n-nyɛ Izraɛl zuliya pinaayi la. O ni daa yɛli ba shɛm ka niŋ alibarika shɛŋa din simdi bɛ zaa yinoyino niŋ bɛ ni shɛm m-bala. Yaakubu kpiya ka bɛ sɔɣ’ o.

english_verse: Both the cave and the land that goes with it were bought from the Hittites.
translation_verse: Ti daa da puu maa mini siliga din be di ni maa la Hitinim’ sani.”

english_verse: When Jacob had finished giving these instructions to his sons, he lay down on his bed and died.
translation_verse: Yaakubu ni daa tɔɣis’ o bihi maa yɛtɔɣa ŋɔ naai, o daa vuui la o naba pa o bindoo zuɣu dɔni n-leei Naawuni dini pah’ o yaannim’ zuɣu.

english_verse: Joseph started crying, then leaned over to hug and kiss his father.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yisifu daa va nti bɔb’ gbaag’ o ba n-kumdi ka mɔɣisir’ o kpariŋ.

english_verse: When the time of mourning was over, Joseph said to the Egyptian leaders, “If you consider me your friend, please speak to the king for me.
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa zaŋ dabisi’ shɛŋa kum o kuli maa ni daa ti gari, ka Yisifu daa yɛli Firawuna yiŋnima, “N suhiri ya, yi nini yi tiɣi ma, yin’ yɛlimiya Firawuna

english_verse: Just before my father died, he made me promise to bury him in his burial cave in Canaan. If the king will give me permission to go, I will come back here.”
translation_verse: ni m ba daa yɛli ma, ‘N saɣi kpibu; ka n yi ti kani, nyin’ zaŋm’ ma ti sɔɣi n ni daa gbi sil’ shɛli Keenan tiŋgbɔŋ ni ni bɛ ti zaŋ ma sɔɣi di ni la puuni; ka daa chɛ ka m-po di pɔri.’ Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ, n-suhir’ o ni o chɛ ka n chaŋ ti sɔɣi m ba ka labina.”

english_verse: The king answered, “Go to Canaan and keep your promise to your father.”
translation_verse: Ka Firawuna daa yɛl’ o, “Cham’ ti sɔɣ’ a ba kaman o ni daa chɛ ka a po ni a ni niŋ shɛm maa.”

english_verse: After crossing the Jordan River, Joseph stopped at Atad's threshing place, where they all mourned and wept seven days for Jacob.
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa ti paai Atad kabɔɣili din be Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili dul’ la shee, ka bɛ daa duhi bɛ yee n-kum nandahima kumsi nimaani; ka Yisifu daa chɛ ka bɛ zaŋ daba ayopɔin kum o ba kuli nimaani.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons did just as their father had instructed.
translation_verse: Ka o bihi maa daa niŋ kaman bɛ ba ni daa zali ba shɛm.

english_verse: After Jacob died, Joseph's brothers said to each other, “What if Joseph still hates us and wants to get even with us for all the cruel things we did to him?”
translation_verse: Yisifu biɛyanim’ ni daa nya ka bɛ ba kpi maa ka bɛ yɛli, “Di pa shɛli ka Yisifu zaɣisi ti ka bɔhi ti biɛri ti ni daa niŋ o zaɣ’ biɛ’ shɛl’ la zuɣu.”

english_verse: he told us, “You did some cruel and terrible things to Joseph, but you must ask him to forgive you.” Now we ask you to please forgive the terrible things we did. After all, we serve the same God that your father worshiped. When Joseph heard this, he started crying.
translation_verse: Yɛlimiya Yisifu, ‘Jaande chɛl’ a biɛyanim’ ŋɔ ni daa tum’ a taal’ shɛl’ la.’ Pumpɔŋɔ, tinim’ bɛn nyɛ a yaannim’ Naawuni daba ŋɔ suhir’ a mi, chɛl’ ti ni daa tum’ a taal’ shɛli maa ti ti.” Bɛ ni daa zaŋ yɛtɔɣa ŋɔ yɛli Yisifu, o daa kummi.

english_verse: Right then, Joseph's brothers came and bowed down to the ground in front of him and said, “We are your slaves.”
translation_verse: Ka o biɛyanim’ maa gba daa kana ti damd’ o tooni ka yɛli, “Ti nyɛla a daba.”

english_verse: But Joseph told them, “Don't be afraid! I have no right to change what God has decided.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Yisifu daa yɛli ba, “Di chɛliya ka dabiɛm mali ya, n ku tooi zaŋ mmaŋ’ zali Naawuni zaani.

english_verse: You tried to harm me, but God made it turn out for the best, so that he could save all these people, as he is now doing.
translation_verse: Yi daa lo ma la zaɣ’ biɛɣu, amaa ka Naawuni daa zaŋ li leei zaɣ’ suŋ ni di chɛ ka niriba pam ti tiligi kaman di ni nyɛ shɛm zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ.

english_verse: Don't be afraid! I will take care of you and your children.” After Joseph said this, his brothers felt much better. Joseph's Death
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu di chɛliya ka dabiɛm mali ya, n ni gbib’ yi mini yi bihi.” Lala ka o daa lan lo ba alikauli ka kpaŋsi bɛ suhuri. Yisifu kum yɛla

english_verse: Joseph lived in Egypt with his brothers until he died at the age of
translation_verse: Ka Yisifu min’ o ba yiŋnim’ daa kul be Ijipti. Yisifu daa niŋla yuun’ kɔbiga ni pia dunia yili ŋɔ.

english_verse: Joseph lived long enough to see Ephraim's children and grandchildren. He also lived to see the children of Manasseh's son Machir, and he welcomed them into his family.
translation_verse: Yisifu daa beni hal ti nya Ifriim bihi ni o yaantibichahi. O daa lan beni hal ti nya Manaasa bihi ni Makiri gba bihi n-zaŋ ba ʒil’ o naba zuɣu.

english_verse: Before Joseph died, he told his brothers, “I won't live much longer. But God will take care of you and lead you out of Egypt to the land he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
translation_verse: Ka Yisifu daa ti yɛl’ o zuliya maa, “N saɣi kpibu; amaa Naawuni ni ti ka yi sanna nti yihi ya tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni n-zaŋ ya kulisi o ni daa po pɔri n-zaŋ tiŋgbɔn shɛli ti Ibrahimma mini Yisahaku ni Yaakubu la ni.”

english_verse: Now promise me that you will take my body with you when God leads you to that land.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yisifu daa yɛli Izraɛlnim’ maa, “Naawuni yi ti yihi ya tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni, yin’ ʒimiya n kɔba mali kuli;” ka daa chɛ ka bɛ po di pɔri.

english_verse: After Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else in that generation had died,
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Yisifu min’ o mabihi maa ni bɛ ʒiɛman’ ni niriba zaa daa ti kpi.

english_verse: the people of Israel became so numerous that the whole region of Goshen was full of them.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Izraɛlnim’ maa daa dɔɣi bihi n-nabi ka yɛligi pam, ka mali yaa m-pali Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni zaa.

english_verse: Many years later a new king came to power. He did not know what Joseph had done for Egypt,
translation_verse: Ka na’ palo daa ti di Ijipti, ŋun’ daa bi mi Yisifu.

english_verse: and he told the Egyptians: There are too many of those Israelites in our country, and they are becoming more powerful than we are.
translation_verse: Ka ŋun’ daa yɛl’ o niriba, “Nyamiya, Izraɛlnim’ ŋɔ zooya, ka lan mali yaa gari ti.

english_verse: If we don't outsmart them, their families will keep growing larger. And if our country goes to war, they could easily fight on the side of our enemies and escape from Egypt.
translation_verse: Chɛliya ka ti bo so’ shɛli din ni chɛ ka bɛ ku lan nabi. Di yi pa lala ti mini ti dimnim’ yi ti yɛn tuhi, bɛ ni pahi ti dimnim’ maa zuɣu tuhi ti ka nya soli zo n-yi ti tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni.”

english_verse: The Egyptians put slave bosses in charge of the people of Israel and tried to wear them down with hard work. Those bosses forced them to build the cities of Pithom and Rameses, where the king could store his supplies.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka bɛ daa bo tuma zuɣulaannim’ ti ba ni bɛ chɛ ka bɛ tum tuun’ kpɛma hal ka bɛ shia ti yi bɛmaŋ’ ni, ka daa chɛ ka bɛ me Firawuna nɛma zaashee fɔntinsi ti o Pitom mini Ramɛsis.

english_verse: But even though the Israelites were mistreated, their families grew larger, and they took over more land. Because of this, the Egyptians feared them worse than before
translation_verse: Amaa bɛ ni daa kul niŋdi ba fitiina shɛm, lala ka bɛ zuliya maa daa kul nabiri ka yɛligiri pahira. Ka jɛlinsi mini dabiɛm daa kpe Ijiptinim’ maa suhuri ni zaŋ chaŋ bɛ polo.

english_verse: and made them work so hard
translation_verse: Ka Ijiptinim’ daa muɣisiri ba ka bɛ tumdi tuun’ kpɛma.

english_verse: that their lives were miserable. The Egyptians were cruel to the people of Israel and forced them to make bricks and to mix mortar and to work in the fields.
translation_verse: Bɛ daa chɛ ka Izraɛlnim’ maa nɔrila tandi, ka ŋmari bilichiisi, ka tumdi bɛ puri ni tuma zaa, ka lan muɣisiri ba ka bɛ tumdi tuun’ kpɛma ni di chɛ ka biɛhigu niŋ ba tom.

english_verse: Finally, the king called in Shiphrah and Puah, the two women who helped the Hebrew mothers when they gave birth.
translation_verse: Ka Ijipti naa maa daa ti lan yɛli Hiburunim’ maa paɣidɔɣisɔtɔɣindiba bɛn yuya daa booni Shifira mini Pua,

english_verse: He told them, “If a Hebrew woman gives birth to a girl, let the child live. If the baby is a boy, kill him!”
translation_verse: “Hiburu paɣ’ yi lan yɛn dɔɣi ka yi chaŋ ni yi ti deei bia, ka nya ka bia maa nyɛla bidibiga, yin’ kumiy’ o, amaa di yi nyɛ bipuɣiŋga, yin’ chɛliy’ o.”

english_verse: But the two women were faithful to God and did not kill the boys, even though the king had told them to.
translation_verse: Amaa ka paɣidɔɣisɔtɔɣindiba maa daa zɔri Naawuni ka bi niŋdi Ijipti naa ni daa yɛli ni bɛ niŋm’ shɛm maa, bɛ daa bi kuri bidibbihi maa.

english_verse: The king called them in again and asked, “Why are you letting those baby boys live?”
translation_verse: Ka Ijipti naa maa daa ti boli paɣidɔɣisɔtɔɣindiba maa na ti bɔhi ba, “Wula ka yi bi kuri bidibbihi maa ka chɛ ba?”

english_verse: They answered, “Hebrew women have their babies much quicker than Egyptian women. By the time we arrive, their babies are already born.”
translation_verse: Ka paɣidɔɣisɔtɔɣindiba maa daa yɛli Firawuna, “Hiburu paɣiba bɛn’ bi be kaman Ijipti paɣiba ni be shɛm, bɛ mali yaa pam. Paɣidɔɣisɔtɔɣinda ti yɛn paai ka bɛ pun dɔɣi.”

english_verse: God was good to the two women because they truly respected him, and he blessed them with children of their own. The Hebrews kept increasing
translation_verse: Paɣidɔɣisɔtɔɣindiba maa ni daa zɔri Naawuni maa zuɣu ka Naawuni daa ti ba bɛ dahalali bihi.

english_verse: until finally, the king gave a command to everyone in the nation, “As soon as a Hebrew boy is born, throw him into the Nile River! But you can let the girls live.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Firawuna daa wuh’ o niriba maa zaa, “Hiburunim’ maa yi lan dɔɣi bidibiga, yin’ zaŋm’ o ti lɔhi Nail Mɔɣili ni, amaa chɛliya bipuɣinsi bɛna.”

english_verse: A man from the Levi tribe married a woman from the same tribe,
translation_verse: Lɛvi do’ so daa ti kpuɣi Lɛvi zuliya ni paɣa.

english_verse: and she later had a baby boy. He was a beautiful child, and she kept him inside for three months.
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ maa daa ti niŋ pua n-dɔɣi bidibiga, ka paɣ’ maa daa nya ka o bia maa viɛli pam, ka o daa zaŋ o sɔɣiri hal ni chira ata.

english_verse: But when she could no longer keep him hidden, she made a basket out of reeds and covered it with tar. She put him in the basket and placed it in the tall grass along the edge of the Nile River.
translation_verse: O ni daa ti nya ka o ku lan tooi sɔɣ’ o yaha, ka o daa kpuɣi bɛ ni zaŋ kulikaɣa wuɣi piɛ’ shɛli n-zaŋ kootaali tanta li din ni chɛ ka kom ku tooi kpe di ni. Ka o daa zaŋ o bia maa niŋ di ni n-zaŋ li chaŋ ti zali kaɣili ni mɔɣili duli.

english_verse: The baby's older sister stood off at a distance to see what would happen to him.
translation_verse: Ka bia maa tizɔpaɣa daa ʒe kpaŋa ni o nya din yɛn niŋ’ o.

english_verse: About that time one of the king's daughters came down to take a bath in the river, while her servant women walked along the river bank. She saw the basket in the tall grass and sent one of them to pull it out of the water.
translation_verse: Ka Firawuna bipuɣiŋga daa ti ka mɔɣili maa ni na ni o ti su kom. Ka o min’ o paɣisara daa baɣisiri mɔɣili maa chana, ka o daa ti nya piɛɣu maa ni su kaɣili ni, ka o tim o paɣisara maa ni yino ni o chaŋ ti zaŋ li na.

english_verse: When the king's daughter opened the basket, she saw the baby crying and felt sorry for him. She said, “This must be one of the Hebrew babies.”
translation_verse: O ni daa zaŋ li na ka o piligi li n-nya bia maa, ka bia maa dii gbaai kuhigu. Ka di daa niŋ o yoli, ka o yɛli, “Hiburunim’ bihi la ni yino m-bala.”

english_verse: At once the baby's older sister came up and asked, “Do you want me to get a Hebrew woman to take care of the baby for you?”
translation_verse: Di saha ka bia maa tizɔpaɣ’ maa daa bɔhi Firawuna bipuɣiŋga maa, “N cham’ ti boli Hiburu paɣ’ so ŋun mali bihim na ka o ti mɔɣis’ a bia maa bihim ti a?”

english_verse: “Yes,” the king's daughter answered. So the girl brought the baby's mother,
translation_verse: Ka Firawuna bipuɣiŋga maa daa yɛl’ o, “Chama.” Di saha ka bipuɣiŋga maa daa zo n-kuli ti boli bia maa ma na.

english_verse: and the king's daughter told her, “Take care of this child, and I will pay you.” The baby's mother carried him home and took care of him.
translation_verse: Ka Firawuna bipuɣiŋga maa daa yɛl’ o, “Zaŋmi bia ŋɔ kuli ti wubis’ o ti ma ka n yo a.” Di saha ka paɣ’ maa daa zaŋ bia maa kuli ti wubis’ o.

english_verse: And when he was old enough, she took him to the king's daughter, who adopted him. She named him Moses because she said, “I pulled him out of the water.” Moses Escapes from Egypt
translation_verse: Ka bia maa daa ti kpaŋ ka o zaŋ o tahi ti ti nabipuɣiŋga maa, ka o zaŋ o leeg’ o bia, ka bol’ o yuli Musa, dama o daa yɛlimi, “Kom ni ka n yih’ o na.” Musa zo n-kuli Midian

english_verse: After Moses had grown up, he went out to where his own people were hard at work, and he saw an Egyptian beating one of them.
translation_verse: Musa ni daa ti bi doo, ka o daa ti yi n-chaŋ o niriba sani nti nya bɛ ni tumdi tuun’ kpeen’ shɛŋa, ka daa ti nya Ijipti do’ so ni buri o niriba Hiburunim’ maa ni yino.

english_verse: Moses looked around to see if anyone was watching, then he killed the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.
translation_verse: Ka o daa yul’ o luɣa ni ka bi nya so, ka daa ŋme n-ku Ijipti doo maa n-zaŋ o pi bihigu ni.

english_verse: When Moses went out the next day, he saw two Hebrews fighting. So he went to the man who had started the fight and asked, “Why are you beating up one of your own people?”
translation_verse: N-daa yi biɛɣu ka o lan yi n-chani ti nya Hiburunim’ maa niriba ayi ni zabira, ka o daa yɛli bɛ ni ŋun ka yɛlimaŋli “Bɔ n-niŋ ka a ŋmɛr’ a mabia maa?”

english_verse: The man answered, “Who put you in charge of us and made you our judge? Are you planning to kill me, just like you killed that Egyptian?” This frightened Moses because he was sure that people must have found out what had happened.
translation_verse: Ka dilan’ maa daa bɔh’ o, “Ŋuni n-lee zaŋ a leei ti zuɣulana ni ti sariakarita? A lomi ni a ku ma kaman a ni sa ku Ijipti doo la shɛm la?” Di saha ka dabiɛm daa gbaai Musa, ka o tɛhi ni o ni sa niŋ shɛli maa yi palo.

english_verse: When the king heard what Moses had done, he wanted to kill him. But Moses escaped and went to the land of Midian. One day, when Moses was sitting by a well,
translation_verse: Ka Firawuna daa wum di yɛla, ka bɔri ni o ku Musa. Amaa ka Musa daa zo Firawuna sani n-kuli Midian tiŋgbɔŋ ni. Dahin shɛli ka o daa ti ʒi kɔbiliga gbini

english_verse: the seven daughters of Jethro, the priest of Midian, came up to water their father's sheep and goats.
translation_verse: ka bipuɣins’ ayopɔin bɛn daa nyɛ Midian maligumaana so bihi daa ti kana ti toori kom niŋdi bɔɣili ni ni bɛ nyuhi bɛ ba biŋkɔbiri.

english_verse: Some shepherds tried to chase them away, but Moses came to their rescue and watered their animals.
translation_verse: Ka piɛguliba shɛb’ daa kana ti kari ba, amaa ka Musa daa yiɣisi zab’ bɛ zuɣu ka niŋ kom ti bɛ piɛri maa ka bɛ nyu.

english_verse: When Jethro's daughters returned home, their father asked, “Why have you come back so early today?”
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa ti kuli yiŋa, ka bɛ ba Riuɛl bɔhi ba, “Ka wula ka yi ti daŋ kundina lala?”

english_verse: They answered, “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds, and he even watered our sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yɛl’ o, “Ijipti do’ so n-fa ti piɛguliba maa nuu ni bahi hal ka ŋɔŋ kom ti ti ka ti nyuhi ti biŋkɔbiri maa.”

english_verse: “Where is he?” Jethro asked. “Why did you leave him out there? Invite him to eat with us.”
translation_verse: Ka o daa bɔh’ o bipuɣinsi maa, “Ka o be ya? Wula ka yi chɛ o zali samban’ ni? Bolimiy’ o na ka o ti di bindirigu.”

english_verse: Moses agreed to stay on with Jethro, who later let his daughter Zipporah marry Moses.
translation_verse: Ka Musa daa saɣi m-be bɛ sani, ka o daa zaŋ o bipuɣiŋga Zipɔra ti Musa.

english_verse: And when she had a son, Moses said, “I will name him Gershom, since I am a foreigner in this country.”
translation_verse: Ka o daa zaŋ o dɔɣi bidibiga ka yɛli, “Sana n-nyɛ ma tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni.” Dinzuɣu ka o daa boli bia maa yuli Gɛrishom.

english_verse: After the death of the king of Egypt, the Israelites still complained because they were forced to be slaves. They cried out for help,
translation_verse: Ka di daa mali ti niŋ yuun’ shɛŋa, ka Ijipti naa maa daa kpi. Ka Izraɛlnim’ maa daa na kul be bɛ dabitim maa ni fabinda, ka kuhiri bɔri sɔŋsim. Ka bɛ dabitim ni kuhigu maa daa paai Naawuni.

english_verse: and God heard their loud cries. He did not forget the promise he had made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa wum bɛ fabila maa, ka teeg’ o ni daa lo Ibrahimma mini Yisahaku ni Yaakubu alikauli shɛl’ la yɛla.

english_verse: and because he knew what was happening to his people, he felt sorry for them.
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa lihi lzraɛlnim’ maa, ka baŋ ni bɛ be muɣisigu ni.

english_verse: One day, Moses was taking care of the sheep and goats of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian, and Moses decided to lead them across the desert to Sinai, the holy mountain.
translation_verse: Musa daa gulila o deemba Jɛtro ŋun daa nyɛ Midian maligumaana la biŋkɔbbaligu maa. Ka o daa ti zaŋ ba ti kpe tiŋgban’ nɛli ni n-gari chaŋ Naawuni zoli din yuli booni Sinai la gbini.

english_verse: There an angel of the Lord appeared to him from a burning bush. Moses saw that the bush was on fire, but it was not burning up.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ malaika daa ti puhi yi o zuɣu buɣim niɛm puuni tutuɣu ni, ka Musa daa lihi nya ka buɣim diri tutuɣu ni, amaa ka lee bi diri tutuɣu maa.

english_verse: “This is strange!” he said to himself. “I'll go over and see why the bush isn't burning up.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Musa daa yɛli, “N ni birigi chaŋ ti nya lahizibu din chɛ ka buɣim maa bi diri tutuɣu maa.”

english_verse: When the Lord saw Moses coming near, he called him by name from the bush, and Moses answered, “Here I am.”
translation_verse: Yawɛ ni daa nya ka Musa birigi kanna ni o ti nya li maa, ka Naawuni daa bol’ o tutuɣu maa ni, “Musa! Musa!” Ka o garigi yɛli, “N-nyɛ ma.”

english_verse: God replied, “Don't come any closer. Take off your sandals—the ground where you are standing is holy.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Naawuni daa yɛl’ o, “Di miri kpe na, pirigim a namda maa, dama a ni ʒe luɣ’ shɛli ŋɔ nyɛla luɣ’ kasi shee.”

english_verse: I am the God who was worshiped by your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” Moses was afraid to look at God, and so he hid his face.
translation_verse: O daa lan yɛl’ o, “Mani n-nyɛ a yaannim’ Naawuni. Mani n-nyɛ Ibrahimma Naawuni; mani n-nyɛ Yisahaku Naawuni; mani n-nyɛ Yaakubu Naawuni.” Di saha ka Musa daa pɔb’ o nina, dama o daa zɔrila dabiɛm ni o yuuni Naawuni.

english_verse: The Lord said: I have seen how my people are suffering as slaves in Egypt, and I have heard them beg for my help because of the way they are being mistreated. I feel sorry for them,
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Musa, “N nya n niriba bɛn be Ijipti la muɣisigu, ka wum bɛ fabila zaŋ chaŋ bɛ tuma zuɣulaannim’ ni niŋdi ba fitiina shɛŋa la polo. M mi bɛ wahalanim’ maa zaa.

english_verse: and I have come down to rescue them from the Egyptians. I will bring my people out of Egypt into a country where there is a lot of good land, rich with milk and honey. I will give them the land where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka n kana ni n ti yihi ba Ijiptinim’ maa nuu ni, ka yihi ba tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni n-zaŋ ba tahi tiŋgban’ viɛlli din galisi ni; tiŋgban’ shɛli din mali bihim mini shiri pam, ka nyɛ Keenannim’ mini Hitinim’ ni Amɔrinim’ ni Pɛrizinim’ ni Hivinim’ ni Jɛbusinim’ ni su tiŋgbɔn shɛli.

english_verse: My people have begged for my help, and I have seen how cruel the Egyptians are to them.
translation_verse: Pumpɔŋɔ, nyama, n niriba Izraɛlnim’ maa fabila maa paai ma, ka n nya Ijiptinim’ maa ni tiri ba wahala shɛŋa maa zaa.

english_verse: Now go to the king! I am sending you to lead my people out of his country.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu kamina ka n ti tim a Firawuna sani ka a chaŋ ti yihi n niriba Izraɛlnim’ maa Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni.”

english_verse: But Moses said, “Who am I to go to the king and lead your people out of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Musa yɛli Naawuni, “M mi lee nyɛ ŋuni n-chani Firawuna sani nti yihiri Izraɛlnim’ Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ni?”

english_verse: God replied, “I will be with you. And you will know that I am the one who sent you, when you worship me on this mountain after you have led my people out of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ka o daa yɛli, “N ni be a sani. Dimbɔŋɔ mi n-yɛn nyɛ shihirili din wuhiri ni mani n-tim a, a yi ti yihi niriba maa Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni na, yi ni ti jɛmdi man’ Naawuni zoli ŋɔ zuɣu.”

english_verse: Moses answered, “I will tell the people of Israel that the God their ancestors worshiped has sent me to them. But what should I say, if they ask me your name?”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Musa yɛli Naawuni, “Ka n yi chaŋ ti yɛli Izraɛlnim’ maa, ‘Yi yaannim’ Naawuni n-tim ma yi sanna.’ Ka bɛ bɔhi ma, ‘O yuli lee booni bɔ?’ Man’ yɛlim’ ba wula?”

english_verse: God said to Moses: I am the eternal God. So tell them that the Lord, whose name is “I Am,” has sent you. This is my name forever, and it is the name that people must use from now on.
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa lan yɛli Musa, “Yɛlim’ Izraɛlnim’ maa ŋ-ŋɔ, ‘Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ yi yaannim’ Naawuni, Ibrahimma Naawuni ni Yisahaku Naawuni ni Yaakubu Naawuni la n-tim ma yi sanna. N yuli m-bala sahakam. Ʒiɛmani kam nim’ ni yɛn booni ma shɛm m-bala.

english_verse: Call together the leaders of Israel and tell them that the God who was worshiped by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob has appeared to you. Tell them I have seen how terribly they are being treated in Egypt,
translation_verse: Cham’ ti laɣim Izraɛl kpamba n-yɛli ba, ‘Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ yi yaannim’ Naawuni, Ibrahimma Naawuni ni Yisahaku Naawuni ni Yaakubu Naawuni n-yi n zuɣu ka yɛli ma, N nini nyan ya, ka nya yi ni diri wahala shɛŋa zaa Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ni.

english_verse: and I promise to lead them out of their troubles. I will give them a land rich with milk and honey, where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: Ka n lo alikauli ni n ni yihi ya Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni wahala maa ni n-zaŋ ya tahi Keenannim’ mini Hitinim’ ni Amɔrinim’ ni Pɛrizinim’ ni Hivinim’ ni Jɛbusinim’ tiŋgbɔŋ ni. Di nyɛla tiŋgban’ shɛli din mali bihim mini shiri pam.’

english_verse: The leaders of Israel will listen to you. Then you must take them to the king of Egypt and say, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Let us walk three days into the desert, where we can offer a sacrifice to him.”
translation_verse: “Di saha bɛ ni wum a yɛligu maa, ka a mini Izraɛl kpamba maa chaŋ Ijipti naa maa sani ti yɛl’ o, ‘Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Hiburunim’ Naawuni la n-ka ti sanna, ti suhir’ a mi, pumpɔŋɔ chɛ ka ti chaŋ tiŋgban’ nɛli ni daba ata chandi nti mali sara ti Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ ti Naawuni maa.’

english_verse: But I know that the king of Egypt won't let you go unless something forces him to.
translation_verse: M mi ni Ijipti naa maa ku chɛ ka yi chaŋ, naɣila n zaŋla kiŋkansi niŋ o.

english_verse: So I will use my mighty power to perform all kinds of miracles and strike down the Egyptians. Then the king will send you away.
translation_verse: N ni teegi n nuu n-tum alahiziba tuma n-darigi Ijiptinim’ maa tibili, di nyaaŋa ka o ni chɛ ka yi chaŋ.

english_verse: Every Israelite woman will go to her Egyptian neighbors or to any Egyptian woman living with them and ask them for gold and silver jewelry and for their finest clothes. The Egyptians will give them to you, and you will put these fine things on your sons and daughters. Carry all this away when you leave Egypt.
translation_verse: Izraɛl paɣ’ kam ni ti chaŋ o ʒiʒiinikpee sani bee o mini saan’ so ŋun laɣim be sani nti suh’ o anzinfa mini salima nɛma ni situra, ka yi zaŋ li niŋ yi bidibisi mini yi bipuɣinsi zaa din ni chɛ ka yi zaŋ Ijiptinim’ maa daazichi pam chaŋ.”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord, “Suppose everyone refuses to listen to my message, and no one believes that you really appeared to me?”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Musa daa garigi yɛli, “Ka bɛ yi ti bi niŋ ma yɛda, ka zaɣisi n yɛligu maa wumbu, ka yɛli ni a bi yi n zuɣu?”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “What's that in your hand?” “A walking stick,” Moses replied.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ bɔh’ o, “Bɔ n-lee be a nuu ni ŋɔ?” Ka o yɛli, “Jaaŋgbee.”

english_verse: “Throw it down!” the Lord commanded. So Moses threw the stick on the ground. It immediately turned into a snake, and Moses jumped back.
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl’ o, “Zaŋmi li bahi tiŋa.” Ka o zaŋ li bahi tiŋa ka di leei wahu, ka Musa tirisi lab’ nyaaŋa ka chɛ li.

english_verse: “Pick it up by the tail!” the Lord told him. And when Moses did this, the snake turned back into a walking stick.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Musa, “Zaŋm’ a nuu gbaag’ o zuli,” ka o daa zaŋ o nuu gbaag’ o zuli maa, ka di lan leei jaaŋgbee o nuu ni.

english_verse: “Do this,” the Lord said, “and the Israelites will believe that you have seen me, the God who was worshiped by their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
translation_verse: “Dina n-ni chɛ ka bɛ niŋ yɛda ni man’ Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ bɛ yaannim’ Ibrahimma mini Yisahaku ni Yaakubu Naawuni la shiri yi a zuɣu.”

english_verse: Next, the Lord commanded Moses, “Put your hand inside your shirt.” Moses obeyed, and when he took it out, his hand had turned white as snow—like someone with leprosy.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa lan yɛl’ o yaha, “Zaŋm’ a nuu niŋ a binyɛrigu ni.” Ka o zaŋ o nuu niŋ o binyɛrigu maa ni, o ni daa ti yihi li na, ka niŋgbuŋ dɔr’ biɛɣu gbaai li, ka di paligi zaa paratɛte kaman gumbɔrigu la.

english_verse: “Put your hand back inside your shirt,” the Lord told him. Moses did so, and when he took it out again, it was as healthy as the rest of his body.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Naawuni daa yɛl’ o yaha, “Zaŋm’ a nuu maa labisi niŋ a binyɛrigu maa ni.” Ka o daa lan zaŋ o nuu maa labisi niŋ o binyɛrigu maa ni, o ni daa ti yihi li na ka di min’ o niŋgbuŋ zaa lan nyɛla yim.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “If no one believes either of these miracles, take some water from the Nile River and pour it on the ground. The water will immediately turn into blood.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ yi ti kul zaɣisi alahiziba tuma ayi ŋɔ dihi tabili bee n-zaɣisi ni bɛ ku wum a yɛligu, nyin’ toomi Nail Mɔɣili la kom kpaai bahi tiŋkuŋ zuɣu ka di leei ʒim tiŋkuŋ maa zuɣu.”

english_verse: Moses replied, “I have never been a good speaker. I wasn't one before you spoke to me, and I'm not one now. I am slow at speaking, and I can never think of what to say.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Musa daa yɛli Yawɛ, “N Duuma, m pala zilinvaliŋgalana, hal dahin’ shɛli ha bee a ni tɔɣisiri mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ yɛtɔɣa pumpɔŋɔ ŋɔ. M bi tooi tɔɣisiri yɛtɔɣa yomyom, ka n zilinli bi tooi lɛbigira.”

english_verse: But the Lord answered, “Who makes people able to speak or makes them deaf or unable to speak? Who gives them sight or makes them blind? Don't you know that I am the one who does these things?
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yawɛ bɔh’ o, “Ŋuni n-lee chɛ ka ninsalinim’ tɔɣisiri yɛtɔɣa? Ŋuni n-lee chɛ ka bɛ nyɛ biriti bee tikpiranima bee n-nyara bee n-nyɛ zoomba? Pa man’ Yawɛ?

english_verse: Now go! When you speak, I will be with you and give you the words to say.”
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu chama, n ni be a nol’ ni n-wuh’ a a ni ti yɛn yɛli shɛm.”

english_verse: Moses begged, “Lord, please send someone else to do it.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka o yɛl’ o, “N Duuma, n suhir’ a, taɣimi tim so.”

english_verse: The Lord became angry with Moses and said: What about your brother Aaron, the Levite? I know he is a good speaker. He is already on his way here to visit you, and he will be happy to see you again.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ suhu daa yiɣisi bahi Musa zuɣu ka o yɛl’ o, “Pa a mabia n-nyɛ Aduna ŋun nyɛ Lɛvi nir’ la? M mi ni o nyɛla ŋun ni tooi tɔɣisi yɛtɔɣa viɛnyɛliŋga. Nyama, o nyɛla ŋun yɛn yina ti tuh’ a soli, ka o yi ti nya a, o suhu ni paligi pam.

english_verse: Aaron will speak to the people for you, and you will be like me, telling Aaron what to say. I will be with both of you as you speak, and I will tell each of you what to do.
translation_verse: O ni ti zan’ a zaani n-tɔɣisi niriba maa yɛtɔɣa ti a, ka a mi ti zani Naawuni zaani o sani.

english_verse: Now take this walking stick and use it to perform miracles. Moses Returns to Egypt
translation_verse: Zaŋmi jaaŋgbee ŋɔ niŋ a nuu ni mali chaŋ, dina ka a ti yɛn mali tumdi alahiziba tumtumsa maa.” Musa labi Ijipti

english_verse: Moses went to his father-in-law Jethro and asked, “Please let me return to Egypt to see if any of my people are still alive.” “All right,” Jethro replied. “I hope all goes well.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Musa daa labi kuli ti yɛl’ o deemba Jɛtro, “N suhir’ a mi, chɛ ka n labi Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ni n niriba sani nti nya bɛ na be bɛ nyɛviya ni.” Ka Jɛtro daa yɛli Musa, “Cham’ ni suhudoo.”

english_verse: But even before this, the Lord had told Moses, “Leave the land of Midian and return to Egypt. Everyone who wanted to kill you is now dead.”
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Musa Midian tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni, “Labimi Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ni, dama ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn daa lo ni bɛ ku a maa zaa kpiya.”

english_verse: So Moses put his wife and sons on donkeys and headed for Egypt, holding the walking stick that had the power of God.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Musa daa zaŋ o paɣ’ min’ o bidibisi balisi buŋa n-labi Ijipti, ka daa zaŋ Naawuni jaaŋgbee la gbib’ o nuu ni.

english_verse: On the way the Lord said to Moses: When you get to Egypt, go to the king and work the miracles I have shown you. But I will make him so stubborn that he will refuse to let my people go.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa lan yɛli Musa, “Nyama, a yi ti paai Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ni, nyin’ tummi alahiziba tuun’ shɛŋa zaa n ni niŋ a yiko ni a tum maa Firawuna tooni, amaa n ni ti chɛ ka o suhu kpaŋ pam, ka o ku chɛ ka niriba maa chaŋ.

english_verse: Then tell him that I have said, “Israel is my first-born son,
translation_verse: Ka a ti chaŋ ti yɛli Firawuna, Yawɛ ni yɛli shɛm m-bɔŋɔ: ‘Izraɛl nyɛla m bidib’ kpɛma.’

english_verse: and I commanded you to release him, so he could worship me. But you refused, and now I will kill your first-born son.” Zipporah's Son Is Circumcised
translation_verse: M pun yɛl’ a, ‘Chɛ ka m bia maa chaŋ ti jɛm ma,’ ka a zaɣisi ni a ku chɛ ka o chaŋ, dinzuɣu n ni ku a bidib’ kpɛma.”

english_verse: One night while Moses was in camp, the Lord was about to kill him.
translation_verse: Ka Musa daa chani nti paai luɣ’ shɛli gbe nimaani, ka Yawɛ daa kana ti bɔri ni o ku o.

english_verse: But Zipporah circumcised her son with a flint knife. She touched his legs with the skin she had cut off and said, “My dear son, this blood will protect you.”
translation_verse: Ka o paɣ’ Zipɔra daa bo kuɣili din dira n-gun’ o bidibiga, ka zaŋ di ʒim ʒe Musa naba ka yɛli, “Pumpɔŋɔ, a nyɛla n yidana ni yɛlimaŋli ʒim yihibu puuni.”

english_verse: So the Lord did not harm Moses. Then Zipporah said, “Yes, my dear, you are safe because of this circumcision.” Aaron Is Sent To Meet Moses
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa chɛ o. Di saha ka paɣ’ maa daa yɛli, “Gunibu ŋɔ zuɣu a shiri nyɛla n yidana ni yɛlimaŋli ʒim yihibu puuni.”

english_verse: The Lord sent Aaron to meet Moses in the desert. So Aaron met Moses at Mount Sinai and greeted him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Aduna, “Cham’ tiŋgban’ nɛli ni ti tuhi Musa soli.” Ka o daa chaŋ ti tuh’ o soli Naawuni zol’ la gbini m-mɔɣis’ o kpariŋ.

english_verse: Moses told Aaron what God had sent him to say; he also told him about the miracles God had given him the power to perform.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Musa daa zaŋ Yawɛ ni tim o ni o ti yɛli Aduna shɛm yɛl’ o, ka wuh’ o o ni yɛl’ o ni o tum alahiziba tuun’ shɛŋa zaa.

english_verse: Later they brought together the leaders of Israel,
translation_verse: Di saha ka Musa mini Aduna daa chaŋ ti laɣim Izraɛl kpamba zaa.

english_verse: and Aaron told them what the Lord had sent Moses to say. Then Moses worked the miracles for the people,
translation_verse: Ka Aduna daa yɛli ba Yawɛ ni daa yɛli Musa yɛtɔɣ’ shɛŋa maa zaa, ka daa tum alahiziba tumtumsa maa niriba maa ninni.

english_verse: and everyone believed. They bowed down and worshiped the Lord because they knew that he had seen their suffering and was going to help them.
translation_verse: Ka niriba maa daa niŋ yɛda. Bɛ ni daa wum ni Yawɛ baɣa be Izraɛlnim’ ni ka nya bɛ wahala maa, ka bɛ daa silim bɛ zuɣuri tiŋa n-jɛm Naawuni.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king of Egypt and told him, “The Lord God says, ‘Let my people go into the desert, so they can honor me with a celebration there.’ ”
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka Musa mini Aduna daa chaŋ Firawuna sani ti yɛl’ o, “Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni la ni yɛli shɛm m-bɔŋɔ: ‘Chɛ ka n niriba ŋɔ chaŋ tiŋgban’ nɛli ni ti puhi chuɣu ti ma.’ ”

english_verse: “Who is this Lord and why should I obey him?” the king replied. “I refuse to let you and your people go!”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Firawuna yɛli, “Ŋuni n-lee nyɛ Yawɛ, ka n ni wum o yɛligu ka chɛ ka Izraɛlnim’ maa chaŋ? M bi mi Yawɛ maa, dinzuɣu n ku chɛ ka Izraɛlnim’ maa chaŋ.”

english_verse: They answered, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Please let us walk three days into the desert where we can offer sacrifices to him. If you don't, he may strike us down with terrible troubles or with war.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yɛl’ o, “Hiburunim’ Naawuni n-daa ka ti sanna, dinzuɣu ti suhir’ a mi, chɛ ka ti chaŋ tiŋgban’ nɛli ni daba ata chandi ti mali sara jɛm Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ ti Naawuni ŋɔ, di yi pa lala o ni chɛ ka alɔbo lu ti zuɣu bee n-chɛ ka bɛ zaŋ takɔbi ku ti.”

english_verse: The king said, “Moses and Aaron, why are you keeping these people from working? Look how many you are keeping from doing their work. Now everyone get back to work!”
translation_verse: Firawuna daa lan yɛli, “Pumpɔŋɔ bɛ galisiya pam, ka yi bɔri ni bɛ chɛ tuma bebɔ?”

english_verse: That same day the king gave orders to his Egyptian slave bosses and to the Israelite men directly in charge of the Israelite slaves. He told them:
translation_verse: Dindali maa ka Firawuna daa zali bɛ tuma zuɣulaannim’ mini bɛn daa yuuni ba ka bɛ tumdi tuma maa zaligu yɛli,

english_verse: Don't give the slaves any more straw to put in their bricks. Force them to find their own straw wherever they can,
translation_verse: “Di lan chaŋya ti chɛ mɔri na ti ti ba ka bɛ ŋma bilichiisi maa. Chɛliya ka bɛ maŋmaŋ’ chani ti chɛri mɔri maa na.

english_verse: but they must make the same number of bricks as before. They are lazy, or else they would not beg me to let them go and sacrifice to their God.
translation_verse: Amaa bɛ ni yi kul ŋmari bilichiisi shɛm maa, lala ka bɛ na kul yɛn ŋmari li, di filimya li; bɛ nyɛla vinnyaɣinima, dina n-chɛ ka bɛ yɛli, ‘Chɛ ka ti chaŋ ti mali sara jɛm ti Naawuni.’

english_verse: Make them work so hard that they won't have time to listen to these lies.
translation_verse: Timiya ba tuun’ kpɛma pam ka bɛ tumda din ni chɛ ka bɛ ku lan gbilisi tibili wum yɔhiŋgu yɛtɔɣa.”

english_verse: The slave bosses and the men in charge of the slaves went out and told them, “The king says he will not give you any more straw.
translation_verse: Ka tuma zuɣulaannim’ mini bɛn daa yuuni ba ka bɛ tumdi tuma maa daa chaŋ ti yɛli ba, “Firawuna yɛliya, ‘N ku lan tin ya mɔri.

english_verse: Go and find your own straw wherever you can, but you must still make as many bricks as before.”
translation_verse: Yimaŋmaŋ’ chamiya ti bom’ mɔri yi n-ni nya li luɣ’ shɛli na, amaa yi tuma bi yɛn filim hal biɛla gba.’ ”

english_verse: The slaves went all over Egypt, looking for straw.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Izraɛlnim’ maa daa chani gindi Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni ni bɛ bo mɔri na.

english_verse: But the slave bosses were hard on them and kept saying, “Each day you have to make as many bricks as you did when you were given straw.”
translation_verse: Ka tuma zuɣulaannim’ maa daa kul muɣisiri ba ka yɛra, “Tummiya yi tuma naari dabisili kam kaman bɛ ni yi tiri ya mɔri ka yi tumdi li shɛm maa.”

english_verse: The bosses beat the men in charge of the slaves and said, “Why didn't you force the slaves to make as many bricks yesterday and today as they did before?”
translation_verse: Ka Firawuna tuma zuɣulaannim’ maa daa buri bɛ mi ni daa pii Izraɛl ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ ni bɛ lihiri bɛ tab’ maa ka bɛ tumdi tuma maa ka yɛra, “Bɔzuɣu ka yi bi ŋma bilichiisi sɔhila mini zuŋɔ kaman yi ni yi pun ŋmari li shɛm dabisili kam la?”

english_verse: Finally, the men in charge of the slaves went to the king and said, “Why are you treating us like this?
translation_verse: Di saha ka Izraɛl tuma kpamba maa daa chaŋ Firawuna sani nti fabili niŋ o ka yɛl’ o, “Wula ka a niŋdi tinim’ bɛn nyɛ a tumtumdiba ŋɔ lala?

english_verse: No one brings us any straw, but we are still ordered to make the same number of bricks. We are beaten with whips, and your own people are to blame.”
translation_verse: Bɛ bi lan tiri ti mɔri, amaa ka na kul yɛra, ‘Ŋmamiya bilichiisi maa!’ Nyam’ bɛ ni buri a tumtumdiba shɛm, amaŋmaŋ’ niriba maa tum din bi tuhi.”

english_verse: The king replied, “You are lazy—nothing but lazy! That's why you keep asking me to let you go and sacrifice to your Lord.
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl’ ba, “Yi nyɛla vinnyaɣinima, dina n-chɛ ka yi yɛli, ‘Chɛ ka ti chaŋ ti mali sara jɛm Yawɛ.’

english_verse: Get back to work! You won't be given straw, but you must still make the same number of bricks.”
translation_verse: Chamiya ti tum tuma maa, dama bɛ bi lan yɛn tin ya mɔri, amaa yi mi kul yɛn ŋmarila bilichiisi maa kaman yi ni yi pun ŋmari li shɛm tariga la.”

english_verse: The men knew they were in deep trouble when they were ordered to make the same number of bricks each day.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Izraɛl tuma kpamba maa daa baŋ ni yɛlli ka bɛ nya maa, bɛ ni daa yɛli ba ni bɛ kul ŋmam’ bilichiisi maa kaman bɛ ni yi pun ŋmari li shɛm tariga dabisili kam la zuɣu.

english_verse: After they left the king, they went to see Moses and Aaron, who had been waiting for them.
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa yi Firawuna sani labira, ka bɛ nya Musa mini Aduna ka bɛ ʒiɛya guhiri ba.

english_verse: Then the men said, “We hope the Lord will punish both of you for making the king and his officials hate us. Now they even have an excuse to kill us.” The Lord's Promise to Moses
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yɛli ba, “Yawɛ nyan ya ka ni darigi yi tibili. Yi chɛ ka Firawuna min’ o kpamba nyee nyɔni ti nyooni biɛɣu, ka zaŋ takɔbi niŋ bɛ nuu ni ni bɛ ku ti.” Musa fabili niŋ Naawuni

english_verse: Moses left them and prayed, “Our Lord, why have you brought so much trouble on your people? Is that why you sent me here?
translation_verse: Di saha ka Musa daa suhi Yawɛ yɛli, “Yaa n Duuma, bɔ n-niŋ ka a niŋ niriba ŋɔ zaɣ’ biɛɣu lala? Bɔzuɣu ka a tim ma na?

english_verse: Ever since you told me to speak to the king, he has caused nothing but trouble for these people. And you haven't done a thing to help.”
translation_verse: Dama saha shɛli n ni daa zaŋ a yuli kana ti tɔɣisi Firawuna yɛtɔɣa la, di saha maa zaŋ kana zuŋɔ, o kul niŋdila a niriba maa putɔɣu, ka a bi niŋ shɛli ni a fa a niriba maa bahi.”

english_verse: The Lord God told Moses: Soon you will see what I will do to the king. Because of my mighty power, he will let my people go, and he will even chase them out of his country.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Musa, “Pumpɔŋɔ a ni nya n ni yɛn niŋ Firawuna shɛm: N yi niŋ o firimiinsi o ni chɛ ka bɛ yi, yɛlimaŋli, n ni niŋ o firimiinsi, ka o kari ba yih’ o tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni.” Naawuni pii Musa

english_verse: My name is the Lord.
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa yɛli Musa yaha, “Mani n-nyɛ Yawɛ.

english_verse: But when I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, I came as God All-Powerful and did not use my name.
translation_verse: N daa yi Ibrahimma zuɣu, ka yi Yisahaku zuɣu, ka lan yi Yaakubu gba zuɣu n-wuhi ba ni mani n-nyɛ Naawuni ŋun nyɛ Kpiɔŋlan’ Naa, amaa n daa bi kahigi n yuli Yawɛ wuhi ba.

english_verse: I made an agreement and promised them the land of Canaan, where they were living as foreigners.
translation_verse: N daa lan lo ba alikauli ni n ni zaŋ Keenan tiŋgbɔŋ ti ba, bɛ ni daa nyɛ saamba be tiŋgbɔn shɛl’ ni la.

english_verse: Now I have seen how the people of Israel are suffering because of the Egyptians, and I will keep my promise.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu n wum Izraɛlnim’ maa fabila zaŋ chaŋ Ijiptinim’ ni zaŋ ba leei daba maa polo, ka teei n ni daa lo alikauli shɛli maa yɛla.

english_verse: Here is my message for Israel: “I am the Lord! And with my mighty power I will punish the Egyptians and free you from slavery.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu yɛlim’ Izraɛlnim’ maa ni mani n-nyɛ Yawɛ, ka n ni yihi ya Ijiptinim’ dabitim maa ni. N ni teei n nuu tum tuun’ kara n-darigi bɛ tibili ka tiligi ya.

english_verse: I will accept you as my people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I was the one who rescued you from the Egyptians.
translation_verse: N ni zaŋ ya leei n niriba, ka leei yi Naawuni, ka yi ti baŋ ni man’ Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ yi Naawuni ŋɔ n-yihi ya Ijiptinim’ ʒi’ tibisa ʒibu ni.

english_verse: I will bring you into the land that I solemnly promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and it will be yours. I am the Lord!”
translation_verse: N ni ti zaŋ ya tahi n ni daa po pɔri ni n zaŋ tiŋgbɔn shɛli ti Ibrahimma mini Yisahaku ni Yaakubu la ni. N ni ti zaŋ li tin ya ka di leei yi ni su shɛli. Dama mani n-nyɛ Yawɛ.”

english_verse: When Moses told this to the Israelites, they were too discouraged and mistreated to believe him.
translation_verse: Ka Musa daa chaŋ ti yɛli Izraɛlnim’ maa lala. Amaa ka bɛ daa zaɣisi li wumbu, bɛ suhugarigu mini bɛ ni daa be putɔɣu dabitim bandi shɛli ni maa zuɣu.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Musa,

english_verse: to demand that the king of Egypt let the Israelites leave.
translation_verse: “Cham’ ti yɛli Firawuna ŋun nyɛ Ijipti naa maa ni o chɛ ka Izraɛlnim’ maa yi o tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni.”

english_verse: But Moses replied, “I'm not a powerful speaker. If the Israelites won't listen to me, why should the king of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Musa daa garigi yɛli, “Izraɛlnim’ maa zaɣisiya ni bɛ ku wum n yɛligu, ka wula ka Firawuna ŋun’ lee ni wum mani ŋun bi tooi tɔɣisiri yɛtɔɣa ŋɔ yɛligu?”

english_verse: But the Lord sent Aaron and Moses with a message for the Israelites and for the king. He also ordered Aaron and Moses to free the people from Egypt. Family Record of Aaron and Moses

translation_verse: Ʒim la ni ti nyɛla shihirili din wuhiri yi ni be yi yiya shɛŋa ni. Ka n yi ti kuri Ijiptinim’ na ti paai ya ka nya ʒim maa, n ni kpahi yaɣ’ ya gari, ka yinim’ yi alɔbo maa ni.

english_verse: For seven days you must eat bread made without yeast. And on the first of these seven days, you must remove all yeast from your homes. If you eat anything made with yeast during this festival, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: “Di simdi ka yi ti ŋubi bɔrɔbɔro din ka dabindi daba ayopɔin; di dabisi’ tuuli dali maa, di simdi ka yi yihi dabindi kam yi yinsi. Ka so yi ti di dabindi daba ayopɔin ŋɔ puuni, dilan’ ni yi Izraɛl zuliya ni.

english_verse: Meet together for worship on the first and seventh days of the festival. The only work you are allowed to do on either of these two days is that of preparing the bread.
translation_verse: Di piligu dali, di simdi ka yi laɣim laɣiŋgu kasi, daba ayopɔin maa dali gba, di simdi ka yi lan laɣim laɣiŋgu kasi, ka di bi simdi ka yi tum tuma di dabisa maa ni, amaa yi ni tooi duɣi yi bindira dina.

english_verse: Celebrate this Festival of Thin Bread as a way of remembering the day that I brought your families and tribes out of Egypt. And do this each year.
translation_verse: Di simdi ni yi puhiri bɔrɔbɔro din ka dabindi maa chuɣu, dama dindali maa ka n daa yihi yi zuliya maa gbilligbilli Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ni. Dinzuɣu di simdi ka yi gbibi dabisili maa yi ʒiɛmani kam ni ka di nyɛ zaligu sahakam.

english_verse: Begin on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month by eating bread made without yeast. Then continue this celebration until the evening of the twenty-first day.
translation_verse: Gol’ tuuli maa biɛɣ’ pinaanahi dali zaawuni, di simdi ka yi ŋubiri bɔrɔbɔro din ka dabindi hal ni goli maa biɛɣ’ pisiniyini dali zaawuni.

english_verse: During these seven days no yeast is allowed in anyone's home, whether they are native Israelites or not. If you are caught eating anything made with yeast, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: Di bi simdi ka dabindi be yi yinsi daba ayopɔin maa ni. Ka ŋunkam di binshɛli din mali dabindi, dilan’ ni yi Izraɛlnim’ laɣiŋgu ni, dilan’ yi nyɛla sana bee tiŋbia.

english_verse: Stay away from yeast, no matter where you live. No one is allowed to eat anything made with yeast!
translation_verse: Di bi simdi ka yi di binshɛli din mali dabindi, Di simdi ni yi ŋubirila bɔrɔbɔro din ka dabindi luɣ’ shɛlikam zaa yi ni be.” Tuuli Yaɣigari chuɣu puhibu

english_verse: Moses called the leaders of Israel together and said: Each family is to pick out a sheep and kill it for Passover.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Musa daa boli Izraɛl kpamba zaa na nti yɛli ba, “Sokam bom’ biŋkɔb’ bila kaman o malibu ni nyɛ shɛm nti kɔrigi puhi Yaɣigari chuɣu.

english_verse: Make a brush from a few small branches of a hyssop plant and dip the brush in the bowl that has the blood of the animal in it. Then brush some of the blood above the door and on the posts at each side of the door of your house. After this, everyone is to stay inside until morning.
translation_verse: Ka zaŋya taaŋkɔro tim ʒi’ shɛli yi ni taɣi niŋ taha ni zali la ni n-zaŋ vie yi dunoya zuɣusahi mini dunɔpaɣira, ka di chɛliya ka so doli dunoli maa yi hal ni asiba.

english_verse: During that night the Lord will go through the country of Egypt and kill the first-born son in every Egyptian family. He will see where you have put the blood, and he will not come into your house. His angel that brings death will pass over and not kill your first-born sons.
translation_verse: Dama Yawɛ yɛn kpɛla tiŋ’ ŋɔ ni na nti ku Ijiptinima, ka o yi ti nya ʒim maa yili shɛli dunoli zuɣusaa mini dunɔpaɣira ni, o ni yaɣi lala yili maa gari, ka ku chɛ ka kum maa kpe yi yinsi ti kun ya.

english_verse: After you have entered the country promised to you by the Lord, you and your children must continue to celebrate Passover each year.
translation_verse: Ka yi yi ti paai Yawɛ ni daa lo alikauli ni o ni zaŋ tiŋgbɔn shɛli tin ya la ni, yin’ puhimiya di chuɣu maa.

english_verse: Your children will ask you, “What are we celebrating?”
translation_verse: Ka yi bihi yi ti bɔhi ya, ‘Yi ni niŋdi shɛli ŋɔ gbinni lee nyɛla dini?’

english_verse: And you will answer, “The Passover animal is killed to honor the Lord. We do these things because on that night long ago the Lord passed over the homes of our people in Egypt. He killed the first-born sons of the Egyptians, but he spared our children from death.” After Moses finished speaking, the people of Israel knelt down and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Yin’ yɛlimiya ba ni di nyɛla Yawɛ Yaɣigari chuɣu sara maligu. Dama o ni daa kuri Ijiptinima, o daa yaɣila tinim’ yiya gari, ka bi ku ti.” Di saha ka Izraɛlnim’ maa daa silim bɛ zuɣuri tiŋ’ jɛm Naawuni,

english_verse: Then they left and did what Moses and Aaron had told them to do. Death for the First-Born Sons
translation_verse: ka bɛ daa chaŋ ti niŋ Yawɛ ni yɛli Musa mini Aduna ni bɛ yɛli ba ka bɛ niŋ shɛm maa. Bikpamba kubu yɛla

english_verse: At midnight the Lord killed the first-born son of every Egyptian family, from the son of the king to the son of every prisoner in jail. He also killed the first-born male of every animal that belonged to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Dindali maa yuntisuɣu, ka Yawɛ daa kana ti ku Ijipti bikpamba zaa. Firawuna ŋun daa ʒi o nam ni la bidib’ kpɛm’ daa kpiya, hal dansarika so ŋun daa be vol’ ni sarika ni bidibituuli gba daa kpiya zaŋ tabili bɛ ni daa tuui dɔɣi biŋkɔb’ dib’ shɛb’ zaa.

english_verse: That night the king, his officials, and everyone else in Egypt got up and started crying bitterly. In every Egyptian home, someone was dead. The People of Israel Escape from Egypt
translation_verse: Ka Firawuna min’ o kpamba ni Ijiptinim’ zaa daa yiɣisi yuŋ maa ka kuŋ mɔni Ijipti fɔŋ ni zaa, dama yili shɛli daa kani ka kum bi ku nimaani.

english_verse: During the night the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Get your people out of my country and leave us alone! Go and worship the Lord, as you have asked.
translation_verse: Ka o daa boli Musa mini Aduna na yuŋ maa ti yɛli ba, “Yi mini Izraɛlnim’ zaa yiɣisimiya n tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni ka chɛ n niriba ŋɔ; chamiya ti jɛm Yawɛ kaman yi ni yɛli shɛm maa.

english_verse: Take your sheep, goats, and cattle, and get out. But ask your God to be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Zaŋmiya yi biŋkɔbbaligu mini yi niɣi zaa chaŋ kaman yi ni yɛli shɛm maa, ka suhiya Naawuni daalibarika niŋ n ni.”

english_verse: The Egyptians did everything they could to get the Israelites to leave their country as quickly as possible. They said, “Please hurry and leave. If you don't, we will all be dead.”
translation_verse: Ka Ijiptinim’ daa kul kpaŋsiri Izraɛlnim’ maa ni bɛ yim’ bɛ tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni yomyom, dama bɛ daa yɛlimi, “Di yi pa lala tinim’ gba kul kpimi maa.”

english_verse: So the Israelites quickly made some bread dough and put it in pans. But they did not mix any yeast in the dough to make it rise. They wrapped cloth around the pans and carried them on their shoulders.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Izraɛlnim’ maa daa zaŋ bɛ ni ŋɔri bɔrɔbɔro zim shɛli ka na bi niŋ dabindi niŋ di ni n-niŋ bɛ bɔrɔbɔro shɛr’ lahi ni n-guri adiikunim’ ni n-zaŋ pa bɛ bɔɣusapima zuɣu.

english_verse: The Israelites had already done what Moses had told them to do. They had gone to their Egyptian neighbors and asked for gold and silver and for clothes.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ maa daa lan niŋ kaman Musa ni daa yɛli ba ni bɛ niŋ shɛm la; bɛ daa suhi Ijiptinim’ maa anzinfa mini salima yɛri ni situra.

english_verse: The Lord had made the Egyptians friendly toward the people of Israel, and they gave them whatever they asked for. In this way they carried away the wealth of the Egyptians when they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa chɛ ka Ijiptinim’ maa niŋ ba nirilim ti ba bɛ ni kul suhi shɛlikam zaa. Ka bɛ daa zaŋ Ijiptinim’ maa daazichi pam pahi chaŋ. Izraɛlnim’ ni yi Ijipti shɛm

english_verse: The Israelites walked from the city of Rameses to the city of Succoth. There were about
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ maa daa yiɣisi Ramɛsis n-chaŋ Sukɔt, dɔbba kɔŋko kalinli daa nyɛla tuhi’ kɔbisiyɔbu m-pahi paɣiba mini bihi.

english_verse: Many other people went with them as well, and there were also a lot of sheep, goats, and cattle.
translation_verse: Ka zuliya shɛb’ gba niriba pam daa zaŋ bɛ biŋkɔbiri pam bɛn nyɛ piɛri ni buhi ni niɣi n-doli ba chaŋ.

english_verse: They left Egypt in such a hurry that they did not have time to prepare any food except the bread dough made without yeast. So they baked it and made thin bread.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ maa daa zaŋ bɛ ni ŋɔri bɔrɔbɔro zim shɛli Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ni la maani maha, dama dabindi daa ka di ni, bɛ mi daa bi ʒi bindir’ shɛli mali chaŋ, bɛ ni daa kari ba yihi Ijipti yomyom shɛm maa zuɣu.

english_verse: On that night the Lord kept watch for them, and on this same night each year Israel will always keep watch in honor of the Lord. Instructions for Passover
translation_verse: Dindali maa yuŋ ka Yawɛ daa guli ni o yihi Izraɛlnim’ Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni. Di yuŋ maa nyɛla Izraɛlnim’ zaa ni gbibi shɛli, ka di nyɛ Yawɛ guhibu yuŋ bɛ ʒiɛmani kam ni. Yaɣigari chuɣu puhibu zaligu

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following instructions for celebrating Passover: Only Israelites may eat the Passover meal.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Musa mini Aduna, “Yaɣigari chuɣu puhibu zaligu m-bɔŋɔ, Di bi simdi ka tinzun’ nira di Yaɣigari chuɣu bindirigu maa.

english_verse: Your slaves may eat the meal if they have been circumcised,
translation_verse: Amaa yi ni da dab’ so ka gun’ o, o ni tooi di bindirigu maa o gunibu nyaaŋa.

english_verse: but no foreigners who work for you are allowed to have any.
translation_verse: Ka ŋun nyɛ sana bee yi ni bu so paa bi simdi ni o di li.

english_verse: The entire meal must be eaten inside, and no one may leave the house during the celebration. No bones of the Passover lamb may be broken.
translation_verse: Di simdi ka yi ti di li la yili yin’ ni ka di bi simdi ni yi zaŋ di nimdi yi samban’ ni bee ŋ-ŋma di kɔbili.

english_verse: And all Israelites must take part in the meal.
translation_verse: Di simdi ka Izraɛlnim’ zaa dol’ li.

english_verse: If anyone who isn't an Israelite wants to celebrate Passover with you, every man and boy in that family must first be circumcised. Then they may join in the meal, just like native Israelites. No uncircumcised man or boy may eat the Passover meal!
translation_verse: Ka sana yi be yi sani ka bɔri ni o puhiri Yaɣigari chuɣu ŋɔ tiri Yawɛ jilima, yin’ chɛliya ka o gun’ o yiŋ’ bidibisi zaa, di saha o ni leei Izraɛl tiŋbia, ka ni tooi puhiri Yaɣigari chuɣu maa. Amaa di bi simdi ka ŋun bi guni di li.

english_verse: This law applies both to native Israelites and to those foreigners who live among you.
translation_verse: Di simdi ka yi mini saamba bɛn be yi sani zaa zaligu nyɛla zaɣ’ yini.”

english_verse: The Israelites obeyed everything the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron to tell them.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ zaa daa niŋ kaman Yawɛ ni daa zali Musa mini Aduna ni bɛ chɛ ka bɛ niŋ shɛm maa.

english_verse: And on that same day the Lord brought Israel's families and tribes out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Dindali maa ka Yawɛ daa yihi Izraɛlnim’ zaa Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni gbilligbilli.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Musa,

english_verse: “Dedicate to me the first-born son of every family and the first-born males of your flocks and herds. These belong to me.” The Festival of Thin Bread
translation_verse: “Zaŋmiya bidib’ tuuli kam ti ma. Bɛ ni kul tuui dɔɣi binshɛɣukam ka o nyɛ zaɣ’ lɔɣu, ninsal’ bee biŋkɔbigu Izraɛlnim’ sunsuuni nyɛla n dini.” Bɔrɔbɔro Din ka Dabindi Chuɣu Puhibu

english_verse: The Lord promised your ancestors that he would bring you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites. It is a land rich with milk and honey. Each year during the month of Abib, celebrate these events in the following way:
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ yi ti zaŋ ya tahi Keenannim’ mini Hitinim’ ni Amɔrinim’ ni Hivinim’ ni Jɛbusinim’ tiŋgban’ shɛli o ni daa lo yi yaannim’ alikauli ni o ni zaŋ tin ya, ka di nyɛ tiŋgban’ shɛli din mali bihim mini shiri pam la, yin’ puhimiya di chuɣu maa goli maa ni.

english_verse: For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast, and on the seventh day you are to celebrate a festival in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Di simdi ka yi ŋubiri bɔrɔbɔro din ka dabindi hal ni daba ayopɔin dali. Daba ayopɔin maa dali, di simdi ka yi puhiri Yawɛ chuɣu maa.

english_verse: During those seven days, you must not eat anything made with yeast or even have yeast anywhere near your homes.
translation_verse: Yi ni ŋubi bɔrɔbɔro din ka dabindi daba ayopɔin di dabisa maa ni. Di bi simdi ka yi chɛ ka so nya dabindi bɔrɔbɔro yi sani yi biɛhigu shee zaa.

english_verse: Then on the seventh day you must explain to your children that you do this because the Lord brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Dindali maa, yɛlimiya yi bihi Yawɛ ni daa niŋ shɛlikam zaa tin ya shɛm saha shɛli yi ni daa yi Ijipti na la, di zuɣu ka yi puhiri di chuɣu maa.

english_verse: This celebration will be like wearing a sign on your hand or on your forehead, because then you will pass on to others the teaching of the Lord, whose mighty power brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ka di ti leei shihirili shɛli din yɛn lo yi nuu ni, ka be yi gbɛri zuɣu n-chɛ ka yi teeri di yɛla din ni chɛ ka Yawɛ zaligu maa yɛla kul be yi noya ni, dama Yawɛ yiko nuu ka o daa zaŋ yihi ya Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ni.

english_verse: Celebrate this festival each year at the same time.
translation_verse: Di simdi ni yi puhiri di chuɣu maa di puhibu saha yuuni kam.” Bikpamba yɛla

english_verse: The Lord will give you the land of the Canaanites, just as he promised you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: “Ka Yawɛ yi ti zaŋ ya tahi Keenannim’ tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni nti zaŋ li tin ya kaman o ni daa lo yi mini yi yaannim’ alikauli shɛm la,

english_verse: From then on, you must give him every first-born son from your families and every first-born male from your animals, because these belong to him.
translation_verse: yin’ ti zaŋmiya bɛ ni tuui dɔɣi bi’ shɛba zaa ti Yawɛ. Yi biŋkɔbiri ni tuui dɔɣi zaɣilɔ’ shɛb’ zaa nyɛla Yawɛ dini.

english_verse: You can spare the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must spare every first-born son.
translation_verse: Amaa buŋdibbil’ tuuli kam, yin’ zaŋmiya piɛɣu zal’ o zaani, ka yi yi bi niŋ lala, dindina yin’ ŋmɛlimiya kab’ o nyiŋgoli. Di simdi ni yi zaŋ binshɛli taɣi yi tuuli bidibisi n-tiligi ba.

english_verse: In the future your children will ask what this ceremony means. Explain it to them by saying, “The Lord used his mighty power to rescue us from slavery in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ka a bia yi ti bɔh’ a daliri shɛli din chɛ ka a doli zaligu maa, nyin’ yɛlim’ o, ‘Ti ni daa nyɛ daba be Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ni la, Yawɛ n-daa zaŋ o nuu din mali kpiɔŋ n-yihi ti dabitim ni, lala zuɣu ka ti doli zaligu maa.

english_verse: The king stubbornly refused to set us free, so the Lord killed the first-born male of every animal and the first-born son of every Egyptian family. This is why we sacrifice to the Lord every first-born male of every animal and save every first-born son.”
translation_verse: Dama Firawuna ni daa niŋ tipawumli ka zaɣisi ni o ku chɛ ka ti yi o tiŋgbɔŋ ni chaŋ la, ka Yawɛ daa ku binshɛɣukam ni tuui dɔɣi bi’ shɛb’ zaa, ninsalinim’ zaŋ tabili biŋkɔbiri zaa, o daa ku bɛ ni tuui dɔɣi bi’ shɛba, dinzuɣu ka n zaŋdi binshɛɣukam ni tuui dɔɣi bi’ shɛb’ zaa m-maani sara tir’ o maa. Amaa m bihi bɛna, n zaŋla binshɛli zali bɛ zaani.

english_verse: This ceremony will serve the same purpose as a sign on your hand or on your forehead to tell how the Lord's mighty power rescued us from Egypt. The Lord Leads His People
translation_verse: Di simdi ka di ti leei shihirili be yi nuhi ni mini yi gbɛri zuɣu, dama Yawɛ daa zaŋla o yiko nuu yihi ti Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ni na.’ ” Sagbani daantaliga mini buɣim daantaliga

english_verse: After the king had finally let the people go, the Lord did not lead them through Philistine territory, though that was the shortest way. God had said, “If they are attacked, they may decide to return to Egypt.”
translation_verse: Firawuna ni daa chɛ ka Izraɛlnim’ maa yi o tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni, Naawuni daa bi zaŋ ba doli Filistianim’ tiŋgbɔŋ polo, nimaani polo ni daa nyɛ so’ jia maa zaa yoli, dama Naawuni daa yɛlimi, “Tɔbu yi ŋme niriba maa, bɛ tɛha ni taɣi ka bɛ zo n-labi Ijipti.”

english_verse: So he led them around through the desert and toward the Red Sea. The Israelites left Egypt, prepared for battle.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka o daa zaŋ ba golimgolim tiŋgban’ nɛli ni kpa Teeku Ʒiɛɣu polo. Izraɛlnim’ daa lola tɔbu n-yi Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni.

english_verse: Moses had them take the bones of Joseph, whose dying words had been, “God will come to your rescue, and when he does, be sure to take my bones with you.”
translation_verse: Ka Musa daa zaŋ Yisifu kɔba m-mali chaŋ kaman ŋun’ Yisifu ni daa chɛ ka Izraɛlnim’ po pɔri ni bɛ ni niŋ shɛm la. Dama Yisifu daa yɛli ba, “Naawuni yi ti ka yaŋɔ tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni na ti tiligi ya, ka yi yɛn chaŋ, yin’ zaŋmiya n kɔba mali chaŋ.”

english_verse: The people of Israel left Succoth and camped at Etham at the border of Egypt near the desert.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yiɣisi Sukɔt n-chaŋ ti dɔni Itam tiŋgban’ nɛl’ naŋgbaŋgbiriŋ.

english_verse: During the day the Lord went ahead of his people in a thick cloud, and during the night he went ahead of them in a flaming fire. That way the Lord could lead them at all times, whether day or night.
translation_verse: Ka sagban’ daantaliga din daa be niriba maa tooni wuntaŋ’ ni la mini buɣim daantaliga din daa be bɛ tooni yuŋ la daa na ʒi n-zo bɛ sani.

english_verse: At Etham the Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Musa,

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel to turn back and camp across from Pi-Hahiroth near Baal-Zephon, between Migdol and the Red Sea.
translation_verse: “Yɛlim’ Izraɛlnim’ ni bɛ ŋmaligi labi bɛ nyaaŋa nti dɔni Pihahirɔt tooni polo, Migidol mini teeku sunsuuni luɣ’ shɛli din miri Baalizɛfɔn la; dɔnimiya miri teeku maa noli.

english_verse: The king will think you were afraid to cross the desert and that you are wandering around, trying to find another way to leave the country.
translation_verse: Firawuna ni yɛli Izraɛlnim’ yɛla, ‘Bɛ bela tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni dari ginda, ka ʒi bɛ ni kpari shɛli polo, ka tiŋgban’ nɛli taɣi ba zali.’

english_verse: I will make the king stubborn again, and he will try to catch you. Then I will destroy him and his army. People everywhere will praise me for my victory, and the Egyptians will know that I really am the Lord. The Israelites obeyed the Lord and camped where he told them.
translation_verse: N ni chɛ ka Firawuna niŋ tipawumli n-kari doli ya na din ni chɛ ka n nya jilima Firawuna min’ o tɔbbi’ gbaliŋ maa zuɣu, ka Ijiptinim’ maa baŋ ni mani n-nyɛ Yawɛ.” Ka bɛ daa shiri niŋ lala.

english_verse: When the king of Egypt heard that the Israelites had finally left, he and his officials changed their minds and said, “Look what we have done! We let them get away, and they will no longer be our slaves.”
translation_verse: Ijipti naa ni daa wum ni Izraɛlnim’ maa zoya maa, ka o min’ o kpamba zaa suhuri daa lan taɣi zaŋ chaŋ bɛ polo ka bɛ yɛli, “Bɔzuɣu ka ti daa niŋ lala? Bɔzuɣu ka ti chɛ ka Izraɛlnim’ maa chaŋ ka chɛ ti tuma?”

english_verse: The king got his war chariot and army ready.
translation_verse: Di saha ka o daa mali chɛchɛbunsi shili, ka zaŋ o tɔbbihi pa omaŋ’ zuɣu.

english_verse: The Lord made the king so stubborn that he went after them, while the Israelites proudly went on their way.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa chɛ ka Firawuna niŋ tipawumli n-kari doli Izraɛlnim’ maa saha shɛli bɛ ni daa yi Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ni ni nasara la.

english_verse: But the king's horses and chariots and soldiers caught up with them while they were camping by the Red Sea near Pi-Hahiroth and Baal-Zephon.
translation_verse: Ka Ijiptinim’ maa mini Firawuna yuri ni chɛchɛbunsi ni wɔribariba zaa ni o tɔbbihi zaa daa doli Izraɛlnim’ maa ti paai ba, ka bɛ dola teeku noli luɣ’ shɛli din yuli booni Pihahirɔt din daa be Baalizɛfɔn tooni polo la.

english_verse: When the Israelites saw the king coming with his army, they were frightened and begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Firawuna ni daa mirina, ka Izraɛlnim’ maa daa lihi bɛ nyaaŋa n-nya ka Ijiptinim’ maa kani bɛ sanna, ka dabiɛm daa gbahi ba pam, ka bɛ kuhi pam niŋ Yawɛ,

english_verse: They also complained to Moses, “Wasn't there enough room in Egypt to bury us? Is that why you brought us out here to die in the desert? Why did you bring us out of Egypt anyway?
translation_verse: ka bɔhi Musa, “Gbala n-daa lee ka Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ni bee bɔzuɣu ka a zaŋ ti na ni ti ti kpi tiŋgban’ nɛli ŋɔ ni? Bɔzuɣu ka a niŋ ti lala? Bɔzuɣu ka a zaŋ ti yi Ijipti na?
