english_verse: I swear that not one of these Israelites will enter the land I promised to give their ancestors. These people have seen my power in Egypt and in the desert, but they will never see Canaan. They have disobeyed and tested me too many times.
translation_verse: bɛ so nini ku nya tiŋgbɔn shɛli n ni daa po ni n ni zaŋ ti bɛ yaannim’ la. Bɛn ʒiɛm ma la so nini ku nya li.

english_verse: But my servant Caleb isn't like the others. So because he has faith in me, I will allow him to cross into Canaan, and his descendants will settle there.
translation_verse: Amaa n dabili Kalɛb ni mali tɛhi’ shɛl’ la min’ o ni doli ma ni o suhu zaa la zuɣu, n ni zaŋ o kulis’ o ni daa chaŋ tiŋgbɔn shɛli maa ni, ka o zuliya ti su li.

english_verse: Now listen, Moses! The Amalekites and the Canaanites live in the valleys of Canaan. And tomorrow, you'll need to turn around and head back into the desert toward the Red Sea. The Israelites Are Punished for Complaining
translation_verse: To, Amalɛknim’ mini Keenannim’ ni be vinvama ni la zuɣu, biɛɣuni, sa ŋmaligimiya kpe mɔɣu n-doli Teeku Ʒiɛɣu polo.” Naawuni darigi bɛn ŋumdi bɛ kparima ni tibili

english_verse: The Lord told Moses and Aaron
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Musa mini Aduna,

english_verse: to give this message to the people of Israel: You sinful people have complained against me too many times! Now I swear by my own life that I will give you exactly what you wanted.
translation_verse: Yɛlim’ ba, ‘Man’ Yawɛ yɛliya: N ni be ŋɔ zuɣu, yi ni yɛli shɛm ka n wum maa, n ni niŋ ya lala.

english_verse: You will die right here in the desert, and your dead bodies will cover the ground. You have insulted me, and none of you men who are over
translation_verse: Yi ni kpi n-do mɔɣu ŋɔ ni; ka yinim’ bɛn yuma nyɛ yuun’ pisi zaŋ chani zaa, ka nyɛ bɛ ni daa sab’ shɛb’ yuya, ka yi nyɛ bɛn ŋum yi kparima ni niŋ ma la

english_verse: will enter the land that I solemnly promised to give you as your own—only Caleb and Joshua will go in.
translation_verse: zaɣ’ yino ku paai n ni daa po ni n ni chɛ ka yi be tiŋgbɔn shɛl’ ni la naɣila Jɛfune bia Kalɛb mini Nan bia Jɔshua kɔŋko.

english_verse: You were worried that your own children would be captured. But I, the Lord, will let them enter the land you have rejected.
translation_verse: Amaa yi bi’ shɛb’ yi ni yɛli ni bɛ ni gbahi ba chaŋ la, n ni zaŋ ba kulisi nimaani ka bɛ ti baŋ tiŋgbɔn shɛli yi ni ʒiɛm maa.

english_verse: You will die here in the desert!
translation_verse: Amaa yinim’ ni kpi n-kpalim mɔɣu ŋɔ ni.

english_verse: So they got up early the next morning and got ready to head toward the hill country of Canaan. They said, “We were wrong to complain about the Lord. Let's go into the land that he promised us.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa daŋ yiɣisibu asiba n-chani zoya din du pam zuɣu tinsi ni ka yɛra, “Tinima m-be kpe ŋɔ, ti ni kuli Yawɛ ni lo ti alikauli ni ti kuli tin’ shɛl’ maa ni, ti tum alahichi.”

english_verse: Ten of the men sent to explore the land had brought back bad news and had made the people complain against the Lord.
translation_verse: Musa ni daa tim ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ ka bɛ chaŋ ti puɣisi nya tiŋgbɔŋ maa, bɛ puuni ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn daa ʒi lahiba’ biɛɣu na nti yɛli zaŋ chaŋ tiŋgbɔŋ maa polo n-chɛ ka niriba maa zaa ŋum bɛ kparima ni niŋ Yawɛ la,

english_verse: But Moses replied, “You're disobeying the Lord! Your plan won't work,
translation_verse: Amaa ka Musa daa yɛli ba, “Bɔ n-niŋ ka yi kul birigiri Yawɛ zaligu? Dama lala ku nani.

english_verse: The Amalekites and the Canaanites came down from the hill country, defeated the Israelites, and chased them as far as the town of Hormah.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Amalɛknim’ mini Keenannim’ bɛn daa be zoya zuɣu tinsi maa ni daa yina ti lu bɛ zuɣu nyaŋ ba n-kari ba hal ni Hɔrima.

english_verse: The people of Israel were very sad after Moses gave them the Lord's message.
translation_verse: Ka Musa daa zaŋ yɛtɔɣa ŋɔ zaa yɛli niriba maa, ka bɛ daa kum pam.

english_verse: so don't even try it. The Lord refuses to help you, because you turned your backs on him. The Amalekites and the Canaanites are your enemies, and they will attack and defeat you.”
translation_verse: Amalɛknim’ mini Keenannim’ ni gunya soli n-zaŋ takɔbiri kun ya; yi ni chɛ Yawɛ dolibu maa zuɣu, Yawɛ ku be yi sani.”

english_verse: But the Israelites ignored Moses and marched toward the hill country, even though the sacred chest and Moses did not go with them.
translation_verse: Amaa ka bɛ daa bahi chaŋ zoya din du pam zuɣu tinsi maa ni, hal Musa mini Yawɛ Alikauli Adaka la ni daa kul kpalim be bɛ sansani maa ni la zaa yoli.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Yawɛ daa yɛli Musa:

english_verse: to give the Israelites the following laws about offering sacrifices:
translation_verse: Yɛlim’ Izraɛlnima: Yi yi ti paai n ni zaŋ tiŋgbɔn shɛli tin ya ni yi be di ni maa ni,

english_verse: Bulls or rams or goats are the animals that you may burn on the altar as sacrifices to please me. You may also offer sacrifices voluntarily or because you made a promise, or because they are part of your regular religious ceremonies. The smell of the smoke from these sacrifices is pleasing to me.
translation_verse: ka yi yɛn zaŋ nahu bee biŋkɔbbila mali sara shɛli bɛ ni zaŋdi nyɔri buɣim la bee alikauli palibu sara bee suhuyubu sara bee yi churi puhibu sara shɛŋa yi ni yɛn mali ka di ʒiɛɣu niŋ Yawɛ nyaɣisim la,

english_verse: If you sacrifice a young ram or goat, you must also offer a kilogram of your finest flour mixed with a liter of olive oil as a grain sacrifice. A liter of wine must also be poured on the altar.
translation_verse: Din pahi nyɛla, o lan bom’ wain din nyɛ binnyura sara la lita yini pahi bɛ ni zaŋdi sara shɛli nyɔri buɣim la zuɣu bee piɛbil’ kam sara zuɣu.

english_verse: If a bull is offered as a sacrifice to please me or to ask my blessing,
translation_verse: Saha shɛli yi yi ti zaŋ naɣilaa ni yi mali sara shɛli bɛ ni zaŋdi nyɔri buɣim la bee alikauli palibu sara bee suhudoo biɛrisuŋ sara ti Yawɛ,

english_verse: you must offer three kilograms of flour mixed with two liters of olive oil.
translation_verse: di saha yin’ bom’ zim viɛlli lita ata n-zaŋ kpam lita ayi ŋmir’ li;

english_verse: Two liters of wine must also be poured on the altar. The smell of this smoke is pleasing to me.
translation_verse: ka bo wain lita ayi din nyɛ binnyura sara la ni sara shɛli bɛ ni zaŋdi nyɔri buɣim ka di ʒiɛɣu niŋdi Yawɛ nyaɣisim la mali sara.

english_verse: If you are a native Israelite, you must obey these rules each time you offer a bull, a ram, or a goat as a sacrifice.
translation_verse: Di simdi ni Izraɛl tiŋbia kam ŋun yɛn mali sara shɛli bɛ ni zaŋdi nyɔri buɣim ka di ʒiɛɣu niŋdi Yawɛ nyaɣisim la niŋ dimbɔŋɔnima.

english_verse: This law will never change. I am the Lord, and I consider all people the same, whether they are Israelites or foreigners living among you.
translation_verse: Yi mini tinzunnim’ bɛn be yi sani zalikpana mini zaligu shɛŋa din pahi yɛn nyɛla yim.

english_verse: When you eat food in the land that I am giving you, remember to set aside some of it as an offering to me.
translation_verse: ni zaŋdi ya tahiri maa, ka yi ti di tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni bindirigu, yin’ zaŋmiya di shɛli ti Yawɛ.

english_verse: From the first batch of bread dough that you make after each new grain harvest, make a loaf of bread and offer it to me, just as you offer grain.
translation_verse: Yi yi ti tuui ŋɔri yi bɔrɔbɔro zim shɛli yin’ zaŋmiya di bɔrɔbɔro kpil’ yini ti pini kaman yi ni zaŋdi kabɔɣili ni chi tiri pini shɛm la.

english_verse: All your descendants must follow this law and offer part of the first batch of bread dough.
translation_verse: Di simdi ni yi zaŋdi yi ni tuui ŋɔri bɔrɔbɔro zim shɛli bɔrɔbɔro kpil’ yini tiri Yawɛ yi ʒiɛmani kam ni.

english_verse: The Lord also told Moses to tell the people what must be done if they ever disobey his laws:
translation_verse: din nyɛ zaligu shɛŋa zaa Yawɛ ni daa chɛ ka Musa zali ya dahin’ shɛli Yawɛ ni daa zali zaligunim’ maa zaŋ chaŋ yi ʒiɛmani kam ni polo la,

english_verse: If all of you disobey one of my laws without knowing it, you must offer a bull as a sacrifice to please me, together with a grain sacrifice, a wine offering, and a goat as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: dindina yi yi bi yu di niŋbu, ka niriba maa ʒi di yɛla, niriba zaa bɛn bom’ naɣilabil’ yino mali sara shɛli bɛ ni zaŋdi nyɔri buɣim ka di ʒiɛɣu niŋdi Yawɛ nyaɣisim la m-pahi di chi mini binnyura sara ni bula’ yino ŋun nyɛ alahichi sanyoo sara la zuɣu kaman zaligu ni wuhi shɛm mali sara.

english_verse: Then the priest will pray and ask me to forgive you. And since you did not mean to do wrong, and you offered sacrifices,
translation_verse: Bɛ ni bi yuri ka kɔŋ zaligunim’ maa dolibu maa zuɣu, bɛ bom’ bɛ ni zaŋdi sara shɛli nyɔri buɣim la mini bɛ daalahichi sanyoo sara tahi Yawɛ tooni na ka maligumaana ti zaŋ li mali sara Izraɛlnim’ zaa zuɣu, ka Yawɛ chɛ bɛ taali maa.

english_verse: But if one of you does wrong without knowing it, you must sacrifice a year-old female goat as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: So yi bi yuri ka tum alahichi, ŋun’ bom’ yuun’ yini bunyaŋ mali alahichi tumbu sara.

english_verse: The law will be the same for anyone who does wrong without meaning to, whether an Israelite or a foreigner living among you.
translation_verse: Ŋunkam nyɛ Izraɛl tiŋbia mini ninvuɣ’ so ŋun nyɛ tinzun nira m-be bɛ sani zaa, zaligu yini maa ka a yɛn zali bɛ ni ŋun chirim.

english_verse: But if one of you does wrong on purpose, whether Israelite or foreigner, you have sinned against me by disobeying my laws. You will no longer belong to my people. A Man Put to Death for Gathering Firewood on the Sabbath
translation_verse: Dama o ʒiɛm Yawɛ yɛligu ka tum birig’ o zaligu, ka di simdi ni bɛ shiri ku dilana, ka o daalahichi ʒi o zuɣu.

english_verse: Once, while the Israelites were traveling through the desert, a man was caught gathering firewood on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Izraɛlnim’ ni daa be mɔɣu ni saha shɛli maa, ka bɛ daa ti nya do’ so ka o kabiri dari Vuhim Dabisili dali.

english_verse: He was taken to Moses, Aaron, and the rest of the community.
translation_verse: Ka ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn daa nya o ka o kabiri dari maa daa zaŋ o tahi Musa mini Aduna ni niriba maa zaa sani.

english_verse: But no one knew what to do with him, so he was not allowed to leave.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa zaŋ o niŋ duu kpari, dama bɛ daa na bi mi bɛ ni yɛn niŋ o shɛm.

english_verse: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Tell the people to take that man outside the camp and stone him to death!”
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Musa, “Kumiya doo maa. Zaŋmiy’ o yi tiŋ’ tariga, ka niriba maa zaa ti pihi kuɣa lab’ o.”

english_verse: So he was killed, just as the Lord had commanded Moses. The Tassels on the People's Clothes
translation_verse: Ka niriba maa zaa daa zaŋ doo maa yi tiŋ’ maa tariga nti pihi kuɣa lab’ ku o kaman Yawɛ ni daa zali Musa shɛm. Binzusa zaligunima

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Musa, “Yɛlim’ Izraɛlnima,

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel, “Sew tassels onto the bottom edge of your clothes and tie a blue string to each tassel.
translation_verse: ni bɛ niŋm’ binzusa niŋ bɛ binyɛra luɣa ni bɛ ʒiɛmana zaa ni, ka niŋ mi sabilitim niŋ binzusa kam din be bɛ luɣa ni maa.

english_verse: I am the Lord your God who led you out of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Man’ Yawɛ n-nyɛ yi Naawuni ŋun daa yihi ya Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ni na ni n ti nyɛ yi Naawuni. Man’ Yawɛ n-nyɛ yi Naawuni.”

english_verse: Korah son of Izhar was a Levite from the Kohathite clan. One day he called together Dathan, Abiram, and On from the Reuben tribe, and the four of them decided to rebel against Moses. So they asked
translation_verse: bɛn daa yi Rubin zuliya ni na la daa ti zaŋ niriba mini Izraɛl ninvuɣ’ zuɣuri kɔbisiyi ni pihinu m-pa bɛmaŋ’ zuɣu chaŋ ti va n-zani Musa tooni. Niriba maa daa nyɛla bɛ ni pii shɛba, ka bɛ nyɛ niriba ni mi shɛb’ yɛla viɛnyɛliŋga.

english_verse: and Aaron and said, “Why do you think you're so much better than everyone else? We're part of the Lord's holy people, and he's with all of us. What makes you think you're the only ones in charge?”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa laɣim taai duŋ niŋ Musa mini Aduna. Bɛ daa yɛli ba mi, “Yi va n-ʒi pam. Dama niriba ŋɔ zaa yinoyino nyɛla bɛn be kasi, ka Yawɛ be bɛ sani. Ka bɔzuɣu ka yi ti duhi yimaŋ’ Yawɛ niriba sani lala?”

english_verse: When Moses heard this, he knelt down to pray.
translation_verse: Musa ni daa wum li, o daa teemi dɔni n-zaŋ o nina kpa tiŋa,

english_verse: Then he said to Korah and his followers: Tomorrow morning the Lord will show us the person he has chosen to be his priest, and that man will faithfully serve him.
translation_verse: ka yɛli Kɔra min’ o nyaandoliba maa, “Biɛɣuni asiba Yawɛ sa ni wuh’ o ni pii so ni ŋun be kasi ni o ni yɛn chɛ ka so ka o sanna. O ni pii so, o ni chɛ ka dilan’ ka o sanna.

english_verse: Korah, here is what you and your followers must do: Get some fire pans, fill them with coals and incense, and place them near the sacred tent. And the man the Lord chooses will be his priest. Korah, this time you Levites have gone too far!
translation_verse: Sa zaŋm’ labihi m-mooi buɣim niŋ di ni, ka niŋ tulaale zim pa di zuɣu n-zani Yawɛ tooni biɛɣuni, ka Yawɛ yi sa pii ninvuɣ’ so, ŋuna n-nyɛ ŋun be kasi. Yinim’ Lɛvi zuliya ŋɔ, yi va n-ʒi pam!”

english_verse: You know that the God of Israel has chosen you Levites from all Israel to serve him by being in charge of the sacred tent and by helping the community to worship in the proper way. What more do you want?
translation_verse: Yi ʒiɛmla Izraɛl Naawuni ni pii ya ka woligi ya Izraɛlnim’ ni n-zaŋ ya mir’ omaŋa ni yi tumdi tuma ŋun’ Yawɛ chirigibu shee suɣili la ni, ka zaani niriba maa tooni n-tumdi tuma sɔŋdi ba la?

english_verse: The Lord has given you a special responsibility, and now, Korah, you think you should also be his priest.
translation_verse: Ŋuna n-zaŋ a min’ a mabihi bɛn zaa nyɛ Lɛvinim’ la mir’ omaŋa. Di zaa yoli ka yi lan bɔri maligumaanitali tuma gba?

english_verse: Then Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, but they sent back this message: “We won't come!
translation_verse: Di saha ka Musa daa tim ti boli Ɛliab bihi, Datan mini Abiram. Ka bɛ daa yɛli, “Ti ku kana.

english_verse: It's bad enough that you took us from our rich farmland in Egypt to let us die here in the desert. Now you also want to boss us around!
translation_verse: A ni zaŋ ti yi tiŋgban’ shɛli din mali bihim mini shiri pam ni na ni a ti ku ti yɔɣu ŋɔ ni la nyɛla yɛlibila, ka a ti lan bɔri ni a zaŋ amaŋ’ leei naa su ti?

english_verse: Moses was very angry and said to the Lord, “Don't listen to these men! I haven't done anything wrong to them. I haven't taken as much as a donkey.”
translation_verse: Ka Musa suhu daa yiɣisi pam, ka o yɛli Yawɛ, “Di deei bɛ sara maligu. N na ʒi n-deei bɛ so buŋa, m mi na ʒi n-niŋ bɛ ni so zaɣ’ biɛ’ shɛli.”

english_verse: Then he said to Korah, “Tomorrow you and your followers must go with Aaron to the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ka Musa daa yɛli Kɔra, “A min’ a nyaandoliba maa zaa ni Aduna sa kam’ Yawɛ tooni na biɛɣuni.

english_verse: Each of you take along your fire pan with incense in it and offer the incense to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Yi zaa yinoyino kpuɣim’ o labila, ka di kalinli yiɣisi kɔbisiyi ni pihinu ka yi niŋ tulaale zim niŋ di ni n-zaŋ li ka Yawɛ tooni na. Ka a gba mini Aduna gbibi yi tulaale lahi.”

english_verse: The next day the men placed incense and coals in their fire pans and stood with Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ka sokam daa kpuɣ’ o laa m-mooi buɣim niŋ di ni, ka niŋ tulaale zim pa di zuɣu. Ka bɛ mini Musa ni Aduna daa zani Yawɛ chirigibu shee suɣili maa dunol’ ni.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Korah had convinced the rest of the Israelites to rebel against their two leaders. When that happened, the Lord appeared in all his glory
translation_verse: Di saha ka Kɔra daa laɣim ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn daa taai duŋ maa zaa Yawɛ chirigibu shee suɣili maa dunol’ ni. Ka Yawɛ jilima neesim daa neei niriba maa zaa sani.

english_verse: and said to Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Musa mini Aduna,

english_verse: “Get away from the rest of the Israelites so I can kill them at once!”
translation_verse: “Woligimiya yimaŋ’ ka chɛ niriba ŋɔ ka n ku ba pumpɔŋɔ.”

english_verse: But the two men bowed down and prayed, “Our God, you gave these people life. Why would you punish everyone here when only one man has sinned?”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa silim zaŋ bɛ nina kpa tiŋa ka yɛli, “Yaa Naawuni, nyin’ ŋun su vuhirigu kam zaa nyɛvili ŋɔ, wula ka ninvuɣ’ yino tum alahichi, ka a suhu yiɣisi bahi niriba ŋɔ zaa zuɣu?”

english_verse: The Lord answered Moses,
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Musa,

english_verse: “Tell the people to stay away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.”
translation_verse: “Yɛlim’ niriba maa, miligimiya Kɔra mini Datan ni Abiram biɛhigu shee.”

english_verse: Moses walked over to Dathan and Abiram, and the other leaders of Israel followed.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Musa daa yiɣisi ka Izraɛl kpamba daa dol’ o ka bɛ chaŋ Datan mini Abiram sani.

english_verse: Then Moses warned the people, “Get away from the tents of these sinful men! Don't touch anything that belongs to them or you'll be wiped out.”
translation_verse: Ka o daa yɛli niriba maa, “Miligimiya ninvuɣ’ biɛri ŋɔ suɣa shee, ka di shihiya bɛ binshɛɣu, di yi pa lala bɛ daalahichi maa zaa ni ʒin ya chaŋ.”

english_verse: Moses said to the crowd, “The Lord has chosen me and told me to do these things—it wasn't my idea. And here's how you will know:
translation_verse: Ka Musa daa yɛli, “Dimbɔŋɔ n-yɛn chɛ ka yi baŋ ni Yawɛ n-shiri tim ma na ni n ti tum tuma ŋɔ zaa, ka di pala mmaŋmaŋ’ yubu ka n tumda.

english_verse: If these men die a natural death, it means the Lord hasn't chosen me.
translation_verse: Niriba ŋɔ yi kpi kaman sokam zaa ni kpiri shɛm bee yɛl’ shɛli din paari sokam zaa yi paai ba, dindina, pa Yawɛ n-shiri tim ma na.

english_verse: But suppose the Lord does something that has never been done before. For example, what if a huge crack appears in the ground, and these men and their families fall into it and are buried alive, together with everything they own? Then you will know they have turned their backs on the Lord!”
translation_verse: Amaa Yawɛ yi chɛ ka so ni na ʒi n-nya yɛl’ shɛli niŋ ba, ka tiŋgbani yaai di noli vali ba tabili bɛ ni su binshɛɣukam zaa, ka bɛ kpe kpiimba biɛhigu shee zaɣ’ nɛma, dina n-ni chɛ ka yi baŋ ni bɛ ʒiɛm Yawɛ.”

english_verse: As soon as Moses said this, the ground under the men opened up
translation_verse: O ni daa yɛri maa, o noli daa na bi lu tiŋa, ka tiŋgbani bɔɣi bɛ naba ni.

english_verse: and swallowed them alive, together with their families and everything they owned. Then the ground closed back up, and they were gone.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ mini bɛ binshɛɣukam zaa daa kpe kpiimba biɛhigu shee zaɣ’ nɛma, ka tiŋgbani mum ba niŋ, ka bɛ daa bahi yoli niriba maa ni.

english_verse: The rest of the Israelites heard their screams, so they ran off, shouting, “We don't want that to happen to us!”
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ zaa bɛn daa miri ba daa wum bɛ kuhigu ka guui; dama bɛ daa yɛlimi, “Tiŋgbani ni vali ti gba!”

english_verse: Then the Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Musa,

english_verse: “Tell Aaron's son Eleazar to take the fire pans from the smoldering fire and scatter the coals. The pans are now sacred,
translation_verse: “Yɛlim’ maligumaana Aduna bia Ɛliɛza ni o yihim’ tulaale tuɣindi labihi maa buɣim niɛm maa ni n-kpaai di buɣim bahi katiŋa, dama di nyɛla din be kasi.

english_verse: because they were used for offering incense to me. Have them hammered into a thin layer of bronze as a covering for the altar. Those men died because of their sin, and now their fire pans will become a warning for the rest of the community.”
translation_verse: Dama alahichinim’ maa tulaale tuɣindi labihi maa leela din be kasi bɛ nyɛviya kɔŋbu maa zuɣu. Dinzuɣu zaŋmi li kuri gbiŋgbarinlinsi n-zaŋ li pa sara maligu bimbini zuɣu, dama bɛ daa zaŋ li mi ti Yawɛ; di nyɛla din be kasi. Di yi niŋ lala, di ni leei shihirili Izraɛlnim’ sani.”

english_verse: Eleazar collected the pans and had them hammered into a thin layer of bronze as a covering for the altar,
translation_verse: Ka maligumaana Ɛliɛza daa zaŋ buɣim ni daa di ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ maa ni daa zaŋ daanya tulaale tuɣindi labihi shɛŋa ti Naawuni maa n-kuri gbiŋgbarinlinsi pa sara maligu bimbini zuɣu.

english_verse: just as the Lord had told Moses. The pans were a warning to the Israelites that only Aaron's descendants would be allowed to offer incense to the Lord. Anyone else who tried to would be punished like Korah and his followers. The Israelites Rebel and Are Punished
translation_verse: Ka di teeri Izraɛlnima ni ninvuɣ’ so ŋun pa maligumaana, ka mi pa ŋun yi Aduna zuliya ni na ku lan kana ni o ti tuɣili tulaale zim Yawɛ tooni, ka din niŋ Kɔra min’ o nyaandoliba maa ti niŋ o kaman Yawɛ ni daa ka chɛ Musa yɛl’ o shɛm maa. Aduna fa niriba bahi

english_verse: The next day the people of Israel again complained against Moses and Aaron, “The two of you killed some of the Lord's people!”
translation_verse: Ka biɛɣu daa neei ka Izraɛlnim’ zaa daa taai duŋ niŋ Musa mini Aduna yɛra, “Yinima n-ku Yawɛ niriba maa.”

english_verse: As the people crowded around them, Moses and Aaron turned toward the sacred tent, and the Lord appeared in his glory in the cloud covering the tent.
translation_verse: Niriba maa ni daa laɣim lu Musa mini Aduna zuɣu saha shɛli maa, ka bɛ daa ŋmaligi lihi Yawɛ chirigibu shee suɣili maa polo nya ka sagbani pun sirigina ti pani di zuɣu, ka Yawɛ jilima neesim neei.

english_verse: So Moses and Aaron walked to the front of the tent,
translation_verse: Ka Musa mini Aduna daa ka Yawɛ chirigibu shee suɣili maa tooni na.

english_verse: where the Lord said to them,
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Musa,

english_verse: “Stand back! I am going to wipe out these Israelites once and for all.” They immediately bowed down and prayed.
translation_verse: “Miligim’ ka chɛ niriba ŋɔ, ka n ku ba pumpɔŋɔ!” Ka bɛ daa lu n-zaŋ bɛ nina kpa tiŋa.

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron, “Grab your fire pan and fill it with hot coals from the altar. Put incense in it, then quickly take it to where the people are and offer it to the Lord, so they can be forgiven. The Lord is very angry, and people have already started dying!”
translation_verse: Ka Musa daa yɛli Aduna. “Zaŋm’ a tulaale tuɣindi labila m-mooi buɣim bimbini zuɣu niŋ tulaale zim pa di zuɣu n-zaŋ li chaŋ niriba maa sani yomyom ti mali sara ti ba, dama Yawɛ suhu yiɣisi bahi bɛ zuɣu, ka alɔbo pun piligi.”

english_verse: Aaron walked back and stood with Moses at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Alɔbo maa ni daa chɛ, ka Aduna labi Musa sani Yawɛ min’ o niriba chirigibu shee suɣili maa dunol’ ni.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses:
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Musa, “Yɛlim’ Izraɛlnima

english_verse: Place these sticks in the tent right in front of the sacred chest where I appear to you.
translation_verse: Ka a zaŋ li ti sɔŋ Yawɛ min’ o niriba chirigibu shee suɣili maa ni Alikauli Adaka la tooni, n ni kani a sanna luɣ’ shɛl’ la.

english_verse: I will then choose a man to be my priest, and his stick will sprout. After that happens, I won't have to listen to any more complaints about you.
translation_verse: Ka n ni pii ninvuɣ’ so jaaŋgbee ni puhi vari. Lala ka n yɛn niŋ ka Izraɛlnim’ chɛ bɛ kparima ni ŋumbu shɛli bɛ ni ŋumdi niŋdi ya sahakam maa.”

english_verse: Moses told the people what the Lord had commanded, and they gave him the walking sticks from the twelve tribal leaders, including Aaron's from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Ka Musa daa yɛli Izraɛlnima, ka bɛ kpamba zaa daa bo jaaŋgbɛhi na ti ti o. Kpɛm’ kam jaaŋgbe’ yiniyini, ka di kalinli daa yiɣisi jaaŋgbɛhi pinaayi kaman bɛ dunoya ni daa nyɛ shɛm. Ka Aduna jaaŋgbee daa be bɛ jaaŋgbɛhi maa ni.

english_verse: Moses took them and placed them in the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ka Musa daa zaŋ jaaŋgbɛhi maa sɔŋ Yawɛ tooni alikauli suɣili maa ni.

english_verse: The next day when Moses went into the tent, flowers and almonds were already growing on Aaron's stick.
translation_verse: Ka biɛɣu daa neei, ka Musa kpe suɣili maa ni nti nya ka Aduna jaaŋgbee din daa nyɛ Lɛvinim’ din’ la puhila vari, ka daai pum n-wali alimɔnd wal’ moma.

english_verse: Moses brought the twelve sticks out of the tent and showed them to the people. Each of the leaders found his own and took it.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Musa daa zaŋ jaaŋgbɛhi maa Yawɛ tooni yi Izraɛlnim’ zaa sani ka bɛ ti nya. Ka sokam daa yih’ o jaaŋgbee.

english_verse: But the Lord told Moses, “Put Aaron's stick back! Let it stay near the sacred chest as a warning to anyone who might think of rebelling. If these people don't stop their grumbling about me, I will wipe them out.”
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Musa, “Zaŋm’ Aduna jaaŋgbee maa labisi ti sɔŋ Alikauli Adaka maa tooni, ka di nyɛ shihirili duŋ taariba maa sani, ka a chɛ ka bɛ chɛ bɛ kparima ni ŋumdi niŋdi ma, di yi pa lala, bɛ ni kpi.”

english_verse: The Israelites cried out to Moses, “We're done for
translation_verse: Di saha ka Izraɛlnim’ daa yɛli Musa, “Ti kpe yɔɣu, ti zaa ni kpi.

english_verse: and doomed if we even go near the sacred tent!”
translation_verse: Ŋunkam miri Yawɛ o biɛhigu shee ŋɔ yi ni kpi, dindina ti zaa kul kpimi maa.”

english_verse: You must see that they perform their duties. But if they go near any of the sacred objects or the altar, all of you will die.
translation_verse: Di simdi ni bɛ tumdi tuma sɔŋdi ya, ka tumdi bɛ tuma ni nyɛ shɛli zaa Yawɛ chirigibu shee suɣili maa ni; amaa bɛ di miri sara maligu shee lahi la bee sara maligu bimbini maa, bɛ yi niŋ lala, yi mini ba ni kpi.

english_verse: Follow these instructions, so I won't become angry and punish the Israelites ever again.
translation_verse: Yimaŋmaŋ’ tummi sara maligu shee mini sara maligu bimbini maa gbini tuma, ka di chɛ ka n suhu ku lan yiɣisi bahi Izraɛlnim’ zuɣu.

english_verse: I alone chose the Levites from all the other tribes to belong to me, and I have given them to you as your helpers.
translation_verse: Mani m-piig’ a dɔɣiriba Lɛvinima Izraɛlnim’ ni; bɛ nyɛla Yawɛ ni su shɛba; ka o zaŋ ba ti a ni bɛ tumdi Yawɛ chirigibu shee suɣili maa puuni tuma.

english_verse: But only you and your sons can serve as priests at the altar and in the most holy place. Your work as priests is a gift from me, and anyone else who tries to do that work must be put to death. The Priests' Share of Offerings Given to the Lord (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Amaa a min’ a bidibisi n-yɛn su maligumaanitali tuma ni sara maligu bimbini zuɣu tuma zaa ni chinchin’ tibisili la puuni tuma n-tumda. N zaŋ yi maligumaanitali maa tin ya pini, ka ninvuɣ’ so ŋun bi kpin’ li yi zaŋ omaŋ’ bali yi ni, bɛn kum’ o.” Maligumaaniba tarili

english_verse: You are allowed to eat the meat of those animals, just as you can eat the choice ribs and the right hind leg of the special sacrifices.
translation_verse: Amaa bɛ nimdi nyɛla yi dini kaman bɛ ni zaŋ biŋkɔbigu nyɔɣu polo mali bɛ ni zaŋdi sara shɛli gahiri zuɣusaa mini nudirigu gbalipaɣa ni nyɛ yi dini shɛm la.

english_verse: The Lord said to Aaron: I have put you in charge of the sacred gifts and sacrifices that the Israelites bring to me. And from now on, you, your sons, and your descendants will receive part of the sacrifices for sin, as well as part of the grain sacrifices, and the sacrifices to make things right. Your share of these sacrifices will be the parts not burned on the altar.
translation_verse: Yi tarili ni yɛn nyɛ shɛli sara maligu binshɛŋa din be kasi ka bɛ bi zaŋ li nyo buɣim m-bɔŋɔ: Bɛ sara maligu kam din be kasi ka bɛ zaŋ li ti ma, din nyɛ chi sara bee alahichi sara bee taali tumbu sara kam di nyɛla a min’ a bidibisi dini.

english_verse: Since these things are sacred, they must be eaten near the sacred tent, but only men are allowed to eat them.
translation_verse: Dimiya li, di nyɛla din be kasi. Dɔbba kɔŋko n-ni tooi di li. Di nyɛla din be kasi yi sani.

english_verse: You will also receive part of the special gifts and offerings that the Israelites bring to me. Any member of your family who is clean and acceptable for worship can eat these things.
translation_verse: Din lan nyɛ yi dini m-bɔŋɔ: Bɛ ni yihi shɛlikam pin’ shɛŋa zaa Izraɛlnim’ ni zaŋdi maani sara shɛli bɛ ni zaŋdi gahiri zuɣusaa la puuni, n zaŋ li ti a min’ a bidibisi ni a bipuɣinsi ni di nyɛ yi tarili, ka ŋunkam be a yiŋa, ka be nyam ni tooi di li.

english_verse: For example, when the Israelites bring me the first batches of oil, wine, and grain, you can have the best parts of those gifts.
translation_verse: “Bɛ ni zaŋ kpa’ viɛl’ shɛli mini wain viɛla zaa ni chi ni bindiri daŋda shɛŋa zaa ti man’ Yawɛ, n zaŋ li tin ya.

english_verse: And the first part of the crops from their fields and vineyards also belongs to you. The people will offer this to me, then anyone in your family who is clean may have some of it.
translation_verse: Bɛ tiŋgban’ ni tiwal’ shɛŋa din daŋ moobu zaa, ka bɛ zaŋ li na ti ti man’ Yawɛ, di nyɛla yi dini; ka ŋunkam be a yiŋa ka be nyam ni tooi di li.

english_verse: Everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me will now belong to you.
translation_verse: Bɛ ni zaŋ binshɛlikam ti Naawuni Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ni nyɛla yi dini.

english_verse: The first-born son in every Israelite family, as well as the first-born males of their flocks and herds, belong to me. But every first-born son and first-born donkey must be bought back from me.
translation_verse: “Bɛ yi dɔɣi bi’ tuuli kam zaa, di yi nyɛla ninsal’ bee biŋkɔbigu, ka bɛ zaŋ ba ti man’ Yawɛ, bɛ nyɛla yi dini. Amaa di simdi ni yi deei binshɛli bɛ ni zaŋ zali daadam bi’ tuuli zaashee; ka lan deei binshɛli bɛ ni zaŋ zali biŋkɔb’ so ŋun bi be nyam bi’ tuuli zaashee.

english_verse: The price for a first-born son who is at least one month old will be five pieces of silver, weighed according to the official standards.
translation_verse: Bɛ yi ti paai goli yini, nyin’ zalim’ ba ka bɛ yo anzinfa laɣibaligu diba anu, ka bɛ daa zali ba kaman Naawuni jɛmbu duu liɣiri zahimbu ni daa nyɛ shɛm.

english_verse: However, all first-born cattle, sheep, and goats belong to me and cannot be bought back. Splatter their blood on the altar and send their fat up in smoke, so I can smell it and be pleased.
translation_verse: Amaa niɣi mini piɛri ni buhi bɛna, di deeya binshɛli zali bɛ ni tuui dɔɣi bi’ shɛb’ zaashee n-tiligi ba, bɛ nyɛla bɛn be kasi. Niŋmiya bɛ ʒim mihi sara maligu bimbini, ka zaŋ bɛ kpam nyo buɣim mali sara; di ʒiɛɣu niŋdi Yawɛ nyaɣisim.

english_verse: From now on, the sacred offerings that the Israelites give to me will belong to you, your sons, and your daughters. This is my promise to you and your descendants, and it will never change.
translation_verse: “Izraɛlnim’ ni zaŋ pin’ shɛŋa din be kasi ti ma zaa, n zaŋ li ti a min’ a bidibisi ni a bipuɣinsi zaa ni di nyɛ yi dini sahakam. Di nyɛla yalim alikauli shɛli din yi man’ Yawɛ sanna ka n lo a min’ a zuliya maa sahakam.”

english_verse: You will not receive any land in Israel as your own. I am the Lord, and I will give you whatever you need. What the Levites Receive The Lord said to Aaron:
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Aduna, “A bi yɛn mali tiŋgbani bɛ tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni bee m-mali tarili bɛ sani. Mani n-nyɛ a tarili ni a ni su shɛli Izraɛlnim’ sani.” Lɛvinim’ tarili

english_verse: Ten percent of the Israelites' crops and one out of every ten of their newborn animals belong to me. But I am giving all this to the Levites as their pay for the work they do at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: “N zaŋ Izraɛlnim’ zaka din nyɛ bini pia kam puuni zaɣ’ yini la ti Lɛvinima ni di nyɛ bɛ ni tumdi tuun’ shɛŋa Yawɛ chirigibu shee suɣili ni la yɔri.

english_verse: They are the only ones allowed to work at the tent, and they must not let anyone else come near it. Those who do come near must be put to death, and the Levites will also be punished. This law will never change. Since the Levites won't be given any land in Israel as their own,
translation_verse: Amaa Lɛvinima n-yɛn tumdi Yawɛ chirigibu shee suɣili maa ni tuma ka bɛmaŋmaŋ’ daalahichi ʒi bɛ zuɣu. Lala n-yɛn nyɛ li yi ʒiɛmani kam ni. Lɛvinim’ mi ku pahi Izraɛlnim’ zuɣu su tiŋgbani palo.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Musa,

english_verse: to say to the Levites: When you receive from the people of Israel ten percent of their crops and newborn animals, you must offer a tenth of that to me.
translation_verse: “Yɛlim’ Lɛvinima, ‘Yi yi ti deei zaka bini pia kam puuni zaɣ’ yini Izraɛlnim’ sani, din nyɛ n ni deei shɛli bɛ sani tin ya ka di nyɛ yi tarili la, yin’ yihimiya di bini pia kam puuni zaɣ’ yini ti man’ Yawɛ, ka di nyɛ zaka binyɛra puuni mi zaka.

english_verse: Just as the Israelites give me part of their grain and wine, you must set aside part of what you receive
translation_verse: Dina n-yɛn nyɛ yi gba zaka, ka di be kaman kabɔɣili ni chi bee wain tɔɣiri bɔɣili ni wain zaka la.

english_verse: After you have dedicated the best parts to me, you can eat the rest, just as the Israelites eat part of their grain and wine after offering them to me.
translation_verse: Yɛlim’ ba yaha, ‘Yi yi ti yihi zaɣ’ viɛla maa zaka di ni, yinim’ Lɛvinim’ yin’ zaŋmiya din kpalim kaman kabɔɣili ni chi bee wain tɔɣiri bɔɣili ni wain zaka la.

english_verse: Your share may be eaten anywhere by anyone in your family, because it is your pay for working at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ka yi mini yi yiŋnim’ zaa ni tooi di li luɣ’ shɛlikam zaa; dama yi ni tumdi tuun’ shɛŋa Yawɛ chirigibu shee suɣili ni la yɔri m-bala.

english_verse: You won't be punished for eating it, as long as you have already offered the best parts to me. The gifts and sacrifices brought by the people must remain sacred, and if you eat any part of them before they are offered to me, you will be put to death.
translation_verse: Yi yi yihi di ni zaɣ’ viɛla zaka ka di li, yi bi tum taali. Amaa miriya ka yi ta Izraɛlnim’ pin’ shɛŋa din be kasi daɣiri; yi yi niŋ lala, yi ni kpi.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following law: The people of Israel must bring Moses a reddish-brown cow that has nothing wrong with it and that has never been used for plowing.
translation_verse: Yawɛ ni zali zaligu shɛŋa m-bɔŋɔ. Yɛlim’ Izraɛlnima ni bɛ bom’ naɣisa’ ʒee ŋun ka dalinli ni galimi, ka nyɛ bɛ ni na bi zaŋ naɣikɔra dapua n-niŋ so na.

english_verse: Moses will give it to Eleazar the priest, then it will be led outside the camp and killed while Eleazar watches.
translation_verse: Ka a zaŋ o ti maligumaana Ɛliɛza, ka o chɛ ka bɛ zaŋ o yi tintariga ti kɔrig’ o o ninni.

english_verse: He will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times in the direction of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ka ŋun’ maligumaana Ɛliɛza zaŋ o nubil’ tim o ʒim ni n-zaŋ li mihi Yawɛ chirigibu shee suɣili la tooni polo siɣimsiɣim buyopɔin.

english_verse: A priest is to throw a stick of cedar wood, a hyssop branch, and a piece of red yarn into the fire.
translation_verse: Di saha ka maligumaana maa zaŋ sida dari mini taaŋkɔro wulli ni mi’ ʒee bahi buɣim din diri nahu maa ni.

english_verse: After the ceremony, the priest is to take a bath and wash his clothes. Only then can he go back into the camp, but he remains unclean and unfit for worship until evening.
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka maligumaana maa paɣ’ o binyɛra ka su kom, ka naanyi kpe bɛ biɛhigu shee; amaa ka maligumaana maa ni leei ŋun bi be nyam hal ni zaawuni.

english_verse: The man who burned the cow must also wash his clothes and take a bath, but he is also unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Ka ninvuɣ’ so ŋun nyo naɣisaa maa buɣim maa, o paɣim’ o binyɛra ka su kom; o gba ni leei ŋun bi be nyam hal ni zaawuni.

english_verse: A man who isn't unclean must collect the ashes of the burnt cow and store them outside the camp in a clean place. The people of Israel can mix these ashes with the water used in the ceremony to wash away sin.
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka ninvuɣ’ so ŋun be nyam va naɣisaa maa tampiligim n-zaŋ li ti zali tiŋ’ tariga luɣ’ shɛli din be nyam, ka di nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ dini; ka bɛ mal’ li niŋdi kom din yihiri nir’ daɣiri ni la ni. Di nyɛla daɣiri yihibu sara.

english_verse: The man who collects the ashes must wash his clothes, but will remain unclean until evening. This law must always be obeyed by the people of Israel and the foreigners living among them. What Must Be Done after Touching a Dead Body The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ka ninvuɣ’ so ŋun va naɣisaa maa tampiligim maa, o paɣim o binyɛra ka leei ŋun bi be nyam hal ni zaawuni. Ka dimbɔŋɔ kul ni nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ mini tinzunnim’ bɛn be bɛ sani zaligu sahakam. Kpim’ shihibu

english_verse: If you touch a dead body, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: Ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn shihi ninsal’ ŋun kpi, bɛ ni leei bɛn bi be nyam daba ayopɔin.

english_verse: But if you wash with the water mixed with the cow's ashes on the third day and again on the seventh day, you will be clean and acceptable for worship. You must wash yourself on those days; if you don't, you will remain unclean.
translation_verse: Di simdi ni bɛ niŋ daɣiri yihibu kom niŋ bɛmaŋa daba ata dali mini dabisi’ shɛli din pahir’ ayopɔin dali, ka leei bɛn be nyam. Amaa bɛ yi bi niŋ lala daba ata mini dabisi’ shɛli din pahir’ ayopɔin maa dali, bɛ ku leei bɛn be nyam.

english_verse: Suppose you touch a dead body, but refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes. You will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean and will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn zaa shihi ninsal’ ŋun kpi ka bi yihi bɛmaŋ’ daɣiri ni, bɛ ta Yawɛ chirigibu shee suɣili daɣiri, di simdi ni yi yihi ba Izraɛlnim’ ni. Bɛ ni bi niŋ ko’ shɛli din yihiri nir’ daɣiri ni mihi ba la zuɣu; bɛ na kul nyɛla bɛn bi be nyam, ka bɛ na kul ni be lala biɛhigu maa ni.

english_verse: If someone dies in a tent while you are there, you will be unclean for seven days. And anyone who later enters the tent will also be unclean.
translation_verse: So yi kpi Yawɛ chirigibu shee suɣili la puuni, di mi zaligu m-bɔŋɔ: Ŋunkam be suɣili maa ni mini ŋunkam kpe di ni na ni leei ŋun bi be nyam hal ni daba ayopɔin.

english_verse: If you touch the body of someone who died or was killed, or if you touch a human bone or a grave, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: Ka ninvuɣ’ so ŋun be samban’ ni yi shihi bɛ ni zaŋ takɔbi ku so bee n-shihi ninvuɣ’ so ŋun kpi o dahalali kum bee n-shihi ninsal’ kɔbili bee gballi, dilana ni leei ŋun bi be nyam daba ayopɔin.

english_verse: Before you can be made clean, someone who is clean must take some of the ashes from the burnt cow and stir them into a pot of spring water. That same person must dip a hyssop branch in the water and ashes, then sprinkle it on the tent and everything in it, including everyone who was inside. If you have touched a human bone, a grave, or a dead body, you must be sprinkled with that water.
translation_verse: ka ninvuɣ’ so ŋun be nyam zaŋ taaŋkɔro vari tim kom maa ni n-zaŋ li mihi Yawɛ chirigibu shee suɣili maa mini di nɛma zaa ni niriba bɛn be di ni ni ninvuɣ’ so ŋun shihi ninsal’ kɔbili bee bɛ ni ku so bee kpima bee gballi.

english_verse: If this is done on the third day and on the seventh day, you will be clean. Then after you take a bath and wash your clothes, you can worship that evening.
translation_verse: Ŋunkam be nyam niŋm’ li mihi ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn bi be nyam daba ata dali ni daba ayopɔin dali. O niŋm’ lala yihi ba daɣiri ni daba ayopɔin dali, di nyaaŋa ka bɛ paɣi bɛ binyɛra ka su kom, zaŋ chaŋ zaawuni ka bɛ leei bɛn be nyam.

english_verse: If you are unclean and refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes, you will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean, and you will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Amaa ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn bi be nyam yi bi mali bɛmaŋ’ niŋ nyam ta Yawɛ sara maligu shee daɣiri, bɛ ni bi niŋ ko’ shɛli din yihiri nir’ daɣiri ni mihi ba la zuɣu, bɛ nyɛla bɛn bi be nyam, ka di simdi ni bɛ yihi ba Naawuni niriba ni.

english_verse: These laws will never change. The man who sprinkled the water and the ashes on you when you were unclean must also wash his clothes. And whoever touches this water is unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Dina n-yɛn nyɛ bɛ zaligu sahakam. Ka ninvuɣ’ so ŋun niŋ ko’ shɛli din yihiri nir’ daɣiri ni maa mihi so, ŋun’ paɣim’ o binyɛra; ka ŋun mi shihi kom maa ni leei ŋun bi be nyam hal ni zaawuni.

english_verse: When you are unclean, everything you touch becomes unclean, and anyone who touches you will be unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Ka ŋun bi be nyam maa yi shihi binshɛlikam, di ni leei din bi be nyam, ka ŋunkam mi shihi li ni leei ŋun bi be nyam hal ni zaawuni.

english_verse: The people of Israel arrived at the Zin Desert during the first month and set up camp near the town of Kadesh. It was there that Miriam died and was buried.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ zaa daa kana ti paai Zin yɔɣu ni gol’ so ŋun daŋ tooni puuni n-ʒini Kadɛshi. Ka Miriam daa kpi nimaani, ka bɛ sɔɣ’ o nimaani.

english_verse: The Israelites had no water, so they went to Moses and Aaron
translation_verse: Kom daa ka nimaani ka niriba maa ni nyu, ka bɛ daa laɣim taai duŋ niŋ Musa mini Aduna.

english_verse: and complained, “Moses, we'd be better off if we had died along with the others in front of the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ka niriba maa daa taai bahi Musa zuɣu, ka yɛl’ o, “Ti yi di daa pahi ti mabihi la zuɣu kpi Yawɛ tooni, di naan so.

english_verse: You brought us into this desert, and now we and our livestock are going to die!
translation_verse: Bɔzuɣu ka a zaŋ tinim’ Yawɛ niriba ŋɔ ka yɔɣu ŋɔ ni na ni ti mini ti biŋkɔbiri ti kpi kpe?

english_verse: Egypt was better than this horrible place. At least there we had grain and figs and grapevines and pomegranates. But now we don't even have any water.”
translation_verse: Ka bɔzuɣu ka a daa yihi ti Ijipti n-zaŋ ti na ti niŋ luɣ’ shɛli din bi viɛli ŋɔ? Luɣ’ shɛŋa nir’ ni yɛn biri chi bee n-sa fiig tihi bee n-sa wain tihi bee n-sa pumpɔrinchihi tihi kani, ka kom gba kani ka ti ni nyu.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the entrance to the sacred tent, where they bowed down. The Lord appeared to them in all of his glory
translation_verse: Di saha ka Musa mini Aduna daa yi niriba maa sani n-chaŋ Yawɛ chirigibu shee suɣili maa dunol’ ni ti gbani n-zaŋ bɛ nina kpa tiŋa. Ka Yawɛ jilima neesim daa neei bɛ sani.

english_verse: and said, “Moses, get your walking stick. Then you and Aaron call the people together and command that rock to give you water. That's how you will provide water for the people of Israel and their livestock.”
translation_verse: “Kpuɣim’ jaaŋgbee, ka a min’ a biɛli Aduna laɣim niriba maa na, ka a ti yɛli tampiŋ ŋɔ ni di chɛ ka kom yi di ni na bɛ zaa ninni. Lala ka a yɛn niŋ yihi kom tampiŋ maa ni na ti ba; ka bɛ mini bɛ biŋkɔbiri nyu.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed and took his stick from the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ka Musa daa shiri kpuɣi jaaŋgbee maa Yawɛ tooni kaman o ni daa zal’ o shɛm maa.

english_verse: After he and Aaron had gathered the people around the rock, he said, “Look, you rebellious people, and you will see water flow from this rock!”
translation_verse: Ka Musa mini Aduna daa laɣim niriba maa tampiŋ maa gbini ka Musa ti yɛli ba, “Yinim’ duŋtaariba ŋɔ, wummiya pumpɔŋɔ, ti chɛ ka kom yi kuɣili ŋɔ ni na n-tin ya?”

english_verse: He raised his stick in the air and struck the rock two times. At once, water gushed from the rock, and the people and their livestock had water to drink.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Musa daa kpuɣ’ o jaaŋgbee maa zuɣusaa ŋ-ŋme tampiŋ maa buyi, ka kom pam daa yi di ni na, ka niriba maa mini bɛ biŋkɔbiri maa daa nyu.

english_verse: But the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you refused to believe in my power, these people did not respect me. And so, you will not be the ones to lead them into the land I have promised.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Musa mini Aduna, “Yi bi niŋ ma yɛda, ka bi wuhi n ni be kasi shɛm Izraɛlnim’ sani, dinzuɣu yi ku zaŋ ba kuli tiŋgbɔn shɛli n ni zaŋ ti ba maa ni.”

english_verse: The Israelites had complained against the Lord, and he had shown them his holy power by giving them water to drink. So they named the place Meribah, which means “Complaining.” Israel Isn't Allowed To Go through Edom
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyɛla Mɛriba kom, luɣ’ shɛli Izraɛlnim’ mini Yawɛ ni daa yɛl’ tab’ finafina ni luɣ’ shɛli o ni daa wuhi ni o nyɛla ŋun be kasi. Ɛdom naa zaɣisiya ni o ku chɛ ka Izraɛlnim’ gari

english_verse: Moses sent messengers from Israel's camp near Kadesh with this message for the king of Edom: We are Israelites, your own relatives, and we're sure you have heard the terrible things that have happened to us.
translation_verse: Musa daa ti tim tuumba Ɛdom naa sani, ka bɛ yi Kadɛshi chaŋ ti yɛl’ o, “A mabihi Izraɛlnim’ ni yɛli shɛm m-bɔŋɔ: A mi wahala shɛli ti ni pun nya zaa yɛla.

english_verse: Our ancestors settled in Egypt and lived there a long time. But later the Egyptians were cruel to us,
translation_verse: A mi ti yaannim’ ni daa kuli Ijipti, ka ti be nimaani yuui pam, ka Ijiptinim’ maa daa nahim ti mini ti yaannim’ maa pam shɛm la yɛla.

english_verse: and when we begged our Lord for help, he answered our prayer and brought us out of that land. Now we are camped at the border of your territory, near the town of Kadesh.
translation_verse: Ka ti daa kuhi niŋ Yawɛ, ka o wum ti kuhigu maa ka daa tim o malaika na ka o ti yihi ti Ijipti maa na, ka ti kana ti be Kadɛshi tin’ shɛli din miri a tintariga la.

english_verse: Please let us go through your country. We won't go near your fields or vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. We will stay on the main road until we leave your territory.
translation_verse: Chɛ ka ti kpe a tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni gari. Ti ku tim yi puri ni bee yi wain tihi ni gari bee n-nyu yi kɔbilisi kom. Ti yɛn dolila solɔɣu gari. Ti ku ŋmaligi kpa nudirigu polo bee nuzaa polo hal ti yi a tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni.”

english_verse: But the king of Edom answered, “No, I won't let you go through our country! And if you try, we will attack you.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Ɛdomnim’ daa yɛl’ o, “Yi ku kpe ti tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni gari, yi yi niŋ lala, ti ni ŋmɛn ya tɔbu.”

english_verse: Moses sent back this message: “We promise to stay on the main road, and if any of us or our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. We just want to pass through.”
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa yɛl’ o, “Ti ni doli solɔɣu maa gari; ka ti mini ti biŋkɔbiri yi nyu yi kom, ti ni yo di zuɣu; ti ni kul bɔri shɛli nyɛla yi chɛ ka ti kana ti gari.”

english_verse: But the king insisted, “You can't go through our land!” Then Edom sent out its strongest troops
translation_verse: Amaa ka o daa lan yɛli, “Yi ku gari.” Ka Ɛdom naa maa daa zaŋ tɔbbihi pam bɛn gbib’ bidibbina pam kana ti gu ba soli.

english_verse: to keep Israel from passing through its territory. So the Israelites had to go in another direction. Aaron Dies
translation_verse: Ɛdom naa ni daa zaɣisi ni Izraɛlnim’ di tim bɛ tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni gari maa, ka Izraɛlnim’ maa daa taɣi doli shɛli polo gari. Aduna kum

english_verse: After the Israelites had left Kadesh and had gone as far as Mount Hor
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ zaa daa yi Kadɛshi m-mali ti paai Hɔr Zoli gbini.

english_verse: “Aaron, this is where you will die. You and Moses disobeyed me at Meribah, and so you will not enter the land I promised the Israelites.
translation_verse: “Aduna ku paai n ni zaŋ tiŋgbɔn shɛli ti Izraɛlnim’ maa ni, o ni kpi, yi ni daa zaɣisi n zaligu Mɛriba kom la yɛla ni la zuɣu.

english_verse: Moses, go with Aaron and his son Eleazar to the top of the mountain.
translation_verse: Zaŋm’ Aduna min’ o bia Ɛliɛza du Hɔr Zoli zuɣu na;

english_verse: Then take Aaron's priestly robe from him and place it on Eleazar. Aaron will die there.”
translation_verse: ka a ti yeei Aduna kpariti n-zaŋ li yɛl’ o bia Ɛliɛza; ka Aduna kpi nimaani n-chaŋ o yaannim’ sani.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed, and everyone watched as he and Aaron and Eleazar walked to the top of Mount Hor.
translation_verse: Ka Musa daa niŋ kaman Yawɛ ni zal’ o shɛm maa. Ka bɛ daa chaŋ ti du Hɔr Zoli maa niriba maa zaa ninni.

english_verse: Moses then took the priestly robe from Aaron and placed it on Eleazar. Aaron died there. When Moses and Eleazar came down,
translation_verse: Ka Musa daa yeei Aduna kpariti maa n-zaŋ li yɛli o bia Ɛliɛza; ka Aduna daa shiri kpi zoli maa zuɣu. Ka Musa mini Ɛliɛza daa yi zoli maa zuɣu siɣina.

english_verse: the people knew that Aaron had died, and they mourned his death for
translation_verse: Izraɛlnim’ zaa ni daa baŋ ni Aduna kpiya, ka bɛ zaa daa zaŋ biɛɣ’ pihita n-kum o kuli.

english_verse: The Israelites had to go around the territory of Edom, so when they left Mount Hor, they headed south toward the Red Sea. But along the way, the people became so impatient
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yiɣisi Hɔr Zoli maa gbini n-zaŋ doli Teeku Ʒiɛɣu polo ni bɛ lɔɣi Ɛdom tiŋgbɔŋ maa gari. Ka niriba maa suhuri daa ti yiɣisi pam soli maa ni.

english_verse: that they complained against God and said to Moses, “Did you bring us out of Egypt, just to let us die in the desert? There's no water out here, and we can't stand this awful food!”
translation_verse: Ka niriba maa daa yɛri Naawuni mini Musa finafina, “Bɔzuɣu ka yi yihi ti Ijipti na ni ti ti kpi mɔɣu ŋɔ ni? Dama bindirigu mini kom ka kpe, ka ti nyee nyɔni bindir’ chɔɣima ŋɔ.”

english_verse: Then the Lord sent poisonous snakes that bit and killed many of them.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa chɛ ka wɔɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn mal’ lɔɣu pam yina ti dimdi Izraɛlnima ka bɛ pam daa kpi.

english_verse: Some of the people went to Moses and admitted, “It was wrong of us to insult you and the Lord. Now please ask him to make these snakes go away.” Moses prayed,
translation_verse: Ka niriba maa daa ka Musa sanna ti yɛl’ o, “Ti tum alahichi, dama ti yɛl’ a mini Yawɛ finafina; suhim’ Yawɛ ti ti ka o vuui tinvura maa ka chɛ ti.” Ka Musa daa suhi Naawuni ti niriba maa.

english_verse: and the Lord answered, “Make a snake out of bronze and place it on top of a pole. Anyone who gets bitten can look at the snake and be saved from death.”
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Musa, “Malimi wahu ŋun mali lɔɣu n-zaŋ tabili da’ wɔɣinli; ka wahu yi dim sokam ka o lihi li, o ni tiligi.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed the Lord. And all of those who looked at the bronze snake lived, even though they had been bitten by the poisonous snakes. Israel's Journey to Moab
translation_verse: Ka Musa daa zaŋ daanya mali wahu maa n-zaŋ li tabili da’ wɔɣinli zuɣusaa; ka wahu daa yi dim so, ka o lihi li, o tiligirimi. Bɛ yi Hɔr Zoli gbini chaŋ Mɔabnim’ vinvamli ni

english_verse: As the Israelites continued their journey to Canaan, they camped at Oboth,
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa yiɣisi chaŋ ti dɔni Obɔt.

english_verse: After that, they crossed the Arnon River gorge and camped in the Moabite desert bordering Amorite territory. The Arnon was the border between the Moabites and the Amorites.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa ti lan yiɣisi nimaani chaŋ ti dɔni Arinɔn Mɔɣili yaɣili yɔ’ shɛli din zaŋ hal ni Amɔrinim’ tintariga la ni; dama Arinɔn Mɔɣili n-nyɛ Mɔabnim’ tintariga m-be Mɔabnim’ mini Amɔrinim’ sunsuuni.

english_verse: A song in The Book of the Lord's Battles mentions the town of Waheb with its creeks in the territory of Suphah. It also mentions the Arnon River,
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka di yɛli Yawɛ tɔbu tuhibu Litaafi ni, “Wahɛb fɔntiŋ’ din be Sufa bɔbili mini vinvama ni Arinɔn Mɔɣili

english_verse: with its valleys that lie alongside the Moabite border and extend to the town of Ar.
translation_verse: ni naɣilima ni vinvama din zaŋ hal ni Ar zaŋ lab’ Mɔabnim’ tintariga polo la.”

english_verse: From the Arnon, the Israelites went to the well near the town of Beer, where the Lord had said to Moses, “Call the people together, and I will give them water to drink.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa lan yiɣisi nimaani chaŋ ti paai kɔbili’ shɛŋa bɛ ni booni Bɛr la. Nimaani ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Musa, “Laɣimmi niriba maa na ka n ti ti ba kom.”

english_verse: That's also the same well the Israelites sang about in this song: Let's celebrate! The well has given us water.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Izraɛlnim’ daa yili yilli ŋɔ: “Yilimiya yila yɛli di yɛla; Kɔbiliga, chɛ ka kom yi a ni na;

english_verse: With their royal scepters, our leaders pointed out where to dig the well. The Israelites left the desert and camped near the town of Mattanah,
translation_verse: Kɔbil’ shɛli nabihi ni daa gbi. Kolibil’ shɛli niriba toondaannim’ ni daa gbi. Nam jaaŋgbɛhi ka bɛ daa zaŋ gbi li. Bɛ jaaŋgbɛhi ka bɛ daa zaŋ gbi li.” Ka bɛ daa yiɣisi yɔɣu maa ni chaŋ Matana,

translation_verse: ka daa ti lan yi Bamɔt mi chaŋ vinvamli shɛli din daa do Mɔab tintariga Pisiga zolɔŋni zaŋ lab’ tiŋgban’ nɛli polo la. Bɛ nyaŋ Naa Sihɔn mini Naa Ogi (Zaligu

english_verse: King Sihon had ruled from Heshbon, after defeating the Moabites and taking over their land north of the Arnon River gorge.
translation_verse: Dama Hɛshibɔn daa nyɛla Amɔrinim’ Naa Sihɔn tiŋa. Ŋuna n-daa tuhi Mɔab na’ kuro ka fa o tiŋgbɔŋ zaa zaŋ hal ni Arinɔn.

english_verse: The Israelites sent this message to King Sihon of the Amorites:
translation_verse: Di saha ka Izraɛlnim’ daa tim tuumba Amɔrinim’ Naa Sihɔn sani nti yɛl’ o,

english_verse: Please let us pass through your territory. We promise to stay away from your fields and vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. As long as we're in your land, we'll stay on the main road.
translation_verse: “Chɛli ka ti kpe a tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni gari. Ti ku birigi kpe mɔɣu ni bee n-tim yi wain tihi puri ni; ti mi ku nyu yi kɔbilisi kom. Ti kul yɛn dolila solɔɣu hal ti gari yi tintariga.”

english_verse: But Sihon refused to let Israel travel through his land. Instead, he called together his entire army and marched into the desert to attack Israel near the town of Jahaz.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Sihɔn daa zaɣisi ni Izraɛlnim’ di kpe o tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni gari. O daa laɣimla o tɔbbihi zaa n-chaŋ Jahaz din daa be yɔɣu maa ni la nti tuhi Izraɛlnima.

english_verse: Israel defeated them and took over the Amorite territory from the Arnon River gorge in the south to the Jabbok River gorge in the north. Beyond the Jabbok was the territory of the Ammonites, who were much stronger than Israel.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa zaŋ takɔbi ku o, ka deeg’ o tiŋgbɔŋ maa Arinɔn zaŋ ti paai Jabok n-lan zaŋ hal ni Ammɔnnim’ tintariga, dama Ammɔnnim’ daa gula bɛ tintariga viɛnyɛliŋga.

english_verse: The Israelites settled in the Amorite towns, including the capital city of Heshbon with its surrounding villages.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa fa Amɔrinim’ maa fɔntinsi zaa n-ʒini Hɛshibɔn zaŋ tabili di tiŋkpansi zaa.

english_verse: That's why the Amorites had written this poem about Heshbon: Come and rebuild Heshbon, King Sihon's capital city!
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka baansi yiini yila yɛra, “Kamiya Hɛshibɔn na, mɛmiya li. Chɛliya ka Sihɔn tiŋ’ maa zani.

english_verse: His armies marched out like fiery flames, burning down the town of Ar and destroying the hills along the Arnon River.
translation_verse: Dama buɣim daa yi Hɛshibɔn na, ka buɣim niɛm daa yi Sihɔn fɔŋ ni na. Di daa di Ar din be Mɔab la, ka di Arinɔn zoya zuɣu.

english_verse: You Moabites are done for! Your god Chemosh deserted your people; they were captured, taken away by King Sihon the Amorite.
translation_verse: Mɔabnima, mbusim be yi zuɣu! Yinim’ Chɛmɔshinima, Chɛmɔshi niriba ŋɔ ni bahi yoli zaa. O chɛ ka o bidibisi leei bɛn zo n-kpe yɔɣu, ka o bipuɣinsi mi leei Amɔrinim’ Naa Sihɔn daba.

english_verse: We completely defeated Moab. The towns of Heshbon and Dibon, of Nophah and Medeba are ruined and gone.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu bɛ zuliya bahila yoli zaŋ Hɛshibɔn hal ni Dibɔn, ka ti ŋmani saɣiri doya hal ka buɣim ti di m-paai Mɛdɛba.”

english_verse: After the Israelites had settled in the Amorite territory,
translation_verse: Dina n-daa chɛ ka Izraɛlnim’ ʒini Amɔrinim’ tiŋgbɔŋ ni.

english_verse: Moses sent some men to explore the town of Jazer. Later, the Israelites captured the villages surrounding it and forced out the Amorites who lived there. Israel Defeats King Og of Bashan (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Ka Musa daa tim ni bɛ ti puɣisi nya Jaza. Ka bɛ daa tuhi fa di tiŋkpansi, ka kari Amɔrinim’ bɛn daa be nimaani maa.

english_verse: The Israelites headed toward the region of Bashan, where King Og ruled, and he led his entire army to Edrei to meet Israel in battle.
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka bɛ daa ŋmaligi doli Bashan polo; ka Bashan Naa Ogi min’ o tɔbbihi zaa daa kana ti lu bɛ zuɣu Ɛdirɛi n-tuhi ba.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Don't be afraid of Og. I will help you defeat him and his army, just as you did King Sihon who ruled in Heshbon. Og's territory will be yours.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Musa, “Di zɔr’ o; dama n zaŋ o min’ o niriba ni o tiŋgbɔŋ zaa niŋ a nuu ni, niŋm’ o kaman a ni daa niŋ Amɔrinim’ Naa Sihɔn ŋun daa be Hɛshibɔn la shɛm la.”

english_verse: So the Israelites wiped out Og, his family, and his entire army—there were no survivors. Then Israel took over the land of Bashan.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa ku o min’ o bihi ni o niriba zaa hal ka o ninvuɣ’ yino gba bi tiligi; ka daa deeg’ o tiŋgbɔŋ maa su.

english_verse: Israel moved from there to the hills of Moab, where they camped across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. King Balak of Moab Hires Balaam To Curse Israel
translation_verse: Di saha ka Izraɛlnim’ daa yiɣisi chaŋ ti dɔni Mɔab bɔpiɛligu ni Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili duli zaŋ lab’ Jɛriko polo.

english_verse: When King Balak of Moab and his people heard how many Israelites there were and what they had done to the Amorites, he and the Moabites were terrified and panicked.
translation_verse: Ka Mɔabnim’ daa zɔri Izraɛlnim’ pam, dama Izraɛlnim’ maa daa galisiya pam. Dabiɛm daa kpe Mɔabnim’ pam Izraɛlnim’ maa zuɣu.

english_verse: They said to the Midianite leaders, “That huge mob of Israelites will wipe out everything in sight, like a bull eating grass in a field.” So King Balak
translation_verse: Ka Mɔabnim’ daa yɛli Midian kpamba, “Salo ni gbaliŋ ŋɔ ni naai binshɛlikam din gili ti zaa kaman naɣilaa ni ŋubiri mɔri mɔɣu ni shɛm la.” Zipɔr bia Balak n-daa nyɛ Mɔab naa di saha maa.

english_verse: sent a message to Balaam son of Beor who lived among his relatives in the town of Pethor near the Euphrates River. It said: I need your help. A large group of people has come here from Egypt and settled near my territory.
translation_verse: Ka o daa tim tuumba Bɛɔr bia Balaam sani Pɛtɔr din daa be Yufretiiz Mɔɣili duli Amawu tiŋgbɔŋ ni la nti bol’ o, ka yɛl’ o, “Ninvuɣ’ shɛba n-yi Ijipti na, bɛ kul yɛrigila luɣ’ shɛlikam zaa, ka ʒini miri ma.

english_verse: They are too powerful for us to defeat, so would you come and place a curse on them? Maybe then we can run them off. I know that anyone you bless will be successful, but anyone you curse will fail.
translation_verse: Kamina ti yɛli yɛtɔɣ’ biɛɣu bahi bɛ zuɣu ti ma. Bɛ ni mali kpiɔŋ gari ma ŋɔ, di pa shɛli ka n tooi tuhi nyaŋ ba n kari ba n tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni, dama m mi ni a yi niŋ alibarika niŋ so ni, o shiri ni nya alibarika; ka a mi yi yɛli yɛtɔɣ’ biɛɣu bahi so zuɣu, di ni di o.”

english_verse: The leaders of Moab and Midian left and took along money to pay Balaam. When they got to his house, they gave him Balak's message.
translation_verse: Ka Mɔab kpamba mini Midian kpamba maa daa zaŋ baɣibuɣiri liɣiri chaŋ Balaam sani ti yɛl’ o Balak ni yɛli shɛm.

english_verse: “Spend the night here,” Balaam replied, “and tomorrow I will tell you the Lord's answer.” So the officials stayed at his house.
translation_verse: Ka o yɛli ba, “Gbɛmiya kpe, ka n sa zaŋ Yawɛ ni yɛli ma shɛm yɛli ya.” Ka Mɔab kpamba maa daa gbe Balaam sani.

english_verse: During the night, God asked Balaam, “Who are these people at your house?”
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa ka Balaam sanna ti bɔh’ o, “Banima n-lee be a sani ŋɔ?”

english_verse: “They are messengers from King Balak of Moab,” Balaam answered. “He sent them
translation_verse: Ka Balaam daa yɛli Naawuni, “Zipɔr bia Balak ŋun nyɛ Mɔab naa la n-tim ba na ti yɛli ma,

english_verse: to ask me to go to Moab and put a curse on the people who have come there from Egypt. They have settled everywhere around him, and he wants to run them off.”
translation_verse: ‘Ninvuɣ’ shɛba n-yi Ijipti na, bɛ kul yɛrigila luɣ’ shɛlikam; kamina ti yɛli yɛtɔɣ’ biɛɣu bahi bɛ zuɣu ti ma; di pa shɛli ka n tooi tuhi nyaŋ ba ka kari ba.’ ”

english_verse: But God replied, “Don't go with Balak's messengers. I have blessed those people who have come from Egypt, so don't curse them.”
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa yɛli Balaam, “Di doli ba chaŋ, a mi miri ka a yɛli yɛtɔɣ’ biɛɣu bahi niriba maa zuɣu, dama bɛ nyɛla alibarika ni be shɛb’ ni.”

english_verse: The next morning, Balaam said to Balak's officials, “Go on back home. The Lord says I cannot go with you.”
translation_verse: Ka Balaam daa yiɣisi asiba n-yɛli Balak kpamba maa, “Labimiya kuli yi ya, dama Yawɛ zaɣisiya ni n di doli ya chaŋ.”

english_verse: The officials left and told Balak that Balaam refused to come.
translation_verse: Ka Mɔab kpamba maa daa yiɣisi labi Balak sani ti yɛl’ o, “Balaam zaɣisiya ni o ku dol’ ti kana.”
