Now Heshbon belonged to Reuben, and so did the following towns in the flatlands: Dibon, Bamoth-Baal, Beth-Baal-Meon, Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath, Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-Shahar on the hill in the valley, Beth-Peor, Slopes of Mount Pisgah, and Beth-Jeshimoth. Moses defeated Sihon and killed him and the Midianite chiefs who ruled parts of his kingdom for him. Their names were Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba.
translation_verse: m-pahi tin’ kar’ shɛŋa din zaa daa be tintan’ ni la mini Amɔrinim’ Naa Sihɔn ŋun daa diri ʒi Hɛshibɔn la ni daa su luɣ’ shɛlikam zaa la. Musa n-daa tuhi nyaŋ o mini Midian nanima. Midian nanim’ maa yuya m-bɔŋɔ: Ɛvi mini Rɛkɛm ni Zur ni Hur ni Rɛba bɛn daa nyɛ Sihɔn nabihi bɛn be tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni la.

english_verse: The Israelites also killed Balaam the son of Beor, who had been a fortuneteller.
translation_verse: M-pahi Bɛɔr bia Balaam ŋun daa nyɛ baɣa, ka Izraɛlnim’ daa zaŋ takɔb’ ku o pahi bɛ ni daa pun ku shɛb’ zuɣu la.

english_verse: This region with its towns and villages was the land for the Reuben tribe, and the Jordan River was its western border. The Land Moses Gave to the Gad Tribe
translation_verse: Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili noli n-daa nyɛ Rubin zuliya maa tiŋgbani tariga. Fɔntiŋ’ kara mini tiŋkpansi ŋɔ ka Musa daa zaŋ ti Rubin zuliya maa ni bɛ su li. Musa ni daa zaŋ tiŋgban’ shɛli ti Gaad zuliya

english_verse: Moses also gave land to each of the clans in the Gad tribe.
translation_verse: Musa daa lan zaŋ tiŋgbani maa shɛli ti Gaad zuliya kaman bɛ daŋ niriba ni nyɛ shɛm ni bɛ su li.

english_verse: It included the town of Jazer, and in the Gilead region their territory took in the land and towns as far east as the town of Aroer just west of Rabbah. This was about half of the land that had once belonged to the Ammonites.
translation_verse: Bɛ tiŋgbani tariga daa nyɛla Jaza zaŋ tabili Giliad tin’ kara zaa ni Amɔrinim’ tiŋgbani pirigili zaŋ hal ti paai Aroa din be Raba wulimpuhili polo la

english_verse: The land given to Gad stretched from Heshbon in the south to Ramath-Mizpeh and Betonim in the north, and even further north to Mahanaim and Lidebor.
translation_verse: ni Hɛshibɔn zaŋ hal ti paai Ramatimizipa mini Bɛtɔnim’ ni zaŋ hal ti paai Mahanaim zaŋ chaŋ Dɛbir tintariga

english_verse: Gad also received the eastern half of the Jordan River valley, which had been ruled by King Sihon of Heshbon. This territory stretched as far north as Lake Galilee, and included the towns of Beth-Haram, Beth-Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon.
translation_verse: ni Bɛtiharam vinvamli ni Bɛtinimira ni Sukɔt ni Zafɔn ni Hɛshibɔn Naa Sihɔn ni daa su luɣ’ shɛlikam zaa, ka Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili noli daa nyɛ di tiŋgbani tariga zaŋ chaŋ ti paai Kinɛrɛt Teeku tariga ha sirigili zaŋ lab’ Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili duli wulimpuhili polo la.

english_verse: These regions with their towns and villages were given to the Gad tribe. The Land Moses Gave to Half the Manasseh Tribe
translation_verse: Fɔntiŋ’ kara mini tiŋkpansi ŋɔ ka Musa daa zaŋ ti Gaad zuliya kaman bɛ daŋ niriba ni nyɛ shɛm ni bɛ su li. Musa ni zaŋ tiŋgban’ shɛli ti Manaasa zuliya bɛn be wulimpuhili polo

english_verse: Moses gave land east of the Jordan River to half of the clans from the Manasseh tribe.
translation_verse: Ka Musa daa lan zaŋ tiŋgbani maa shɛli ti Manaasa zuliya pirigili la kaman bɛ daŋ niriba ni nyɛ shɛm ni bɛ su li.

english_verse: Their land started at Mahanaim and took in the region that King Og of Bashan had ruled, including Ashtaroth and Edrei, the two towns where he had lived. The villages where the Jair clan settled were part of Manasseh's land, and so was the northern half of the region of Gilead. The clans of this half of Manasseh had
translation_verse: m-pahi Giliad pirigili ni Ashitarɔt ni Ɛdirɛi din daa nyɛ fɔntiŋ’ kar’ shɛŋa Bashan Naa Ogi ni daa su la. Musa daa zaŋ dimbɔŋɔnim’ tila Manaasa bia Makiri ni di nyɛ Makiri maa zuliya pirigili dini kaman bɛ daŋ niriba ni nyɛ shɛm.

english_verse: That was how Moses divided up the Moab Plains to the east of Jericho on the other side of the Jordan River, so these two and a half tribes would have land of their own.
translation_verse: Musa ni daa piri tiŋgbani maa tari Mɔab bɔpiɛligu la ni Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili duli mini Jɛriko wulimpuhili polo la shɛm m-bala.

english_verse: But Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord had promised that he would always provide for them.
translation_verse: Amaa Musa daa bi pirigi tiŋgbani maa shɛli ti Lɛvinim’ bɛna; Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni ŋɔ n-daa nyɛ bɛn’ tarili kaman o ni daa pun yɛli ba shɛm.

english_verse: One day while the Israelites were still camped at Gilgal, Caleb the son of Jephunneh went to talk with Joshua. Caleb belonged to the Kenaz clan, and many other people from the Judah tribe went with Caleb. He told Joshua: You know that back in Kadesh-Barnea the Lord talked to his prophet Moses about you and me.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Juda zuliya ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ daa ka Jɔshua sanna Giligal; ka Jɛfune ŋun daa nyɛ Kɛnizi nir’ la bia Kalɛb ŋun daa nyɛ bɛ ni yino la ti yɛli Jɔshua, “A mi Yawɛ ni daa pun yɛli Musa ŋun nyɛ Naawuni nir’ la m min’ a yɛla shɛm Kadɛshibarinia la.

english_verse: The other spies said things that made our people afraid, but I completely trusted the Lord God.
translation_verse: M mini ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn daa chaŋ chandi maa bɛn’ daa chɛ ka dabiɛm kpɛla Izraɛlnima, amaa ka man’ daa kul ʒe Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ n Naawuni ŋɔ yim.

english_verse: The same day I came back, Moses told me, “Since you were faithful to the Lord God, I promise that the places where you went as a spy will belong to you and your descendants forever.”
translation_verse: Ka Musa daa lo alikauli dindali maa yɛli, ‘Yɛlimaŋli a ni ʒe Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ n Naawuni ŋɔ yim maa zuɣu, a napɔna ni no tiŋgban’ shɛli zuɣu ŋɔ ni ti leeg’ a min’ a bihi ni yɛn su shɛli sahakam.’

english_verse: So I'm asking you for the hill country that the Lord promised me that day. You were there. You heard the other spies talk about that part of the hill country and the large, walled towns where the Anakim live. But maybe the Lord will help me take their land, just as he promised.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu zaŋm’ zoya tiŋgbani din nyɛ Yawɛ ni daa yɛli shɛli yɛla dindali maa ti ma. Dama amaŋmaŋ’ daa wumya dindali maa ni Anakinima m-be nimaani birini tin’ kara ni. Di pa shɛli Yawɛ ni be n sani n-chɛ ka n kari ba yihi ni kaman o ni daa pun yɛli shɛm maa.”

english_verse: Joshua prayed that God would help Caleb, then he gave Hebron to Caleb and his descendants.
translation_verse: Ka Jɔshua daa suhi alibarika niŋ Kalɛb ni; ka zaŋ Hiburɔn ti ŋun’ Kalɛb ŋun daa nyɛ Jɛfune bia la ni o su li.

english_verse: And Hebron still belongs to Caleb's descendants, because he was faithful to the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Ka Hiburɔn daa leei Jɛfune ŋun daa nyɛ Kɛnizi nir’ la bia Kalɛb ni su shɛli hal ni zuŋɔ, o ni daa ʒe Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni yim la zuɣu.

english_verse: Hebron used to be called Arba's Town, because Arba had been one of the greatest of the Anakim. There was peace in the land.
translation_verse: Hiburɔn yuli piligu ni ha daa nyɛla Kiriatariba; Ariba ŋɔ n-daa nyɛ Anakinim’ ni wɔɣirili. Ka tɔbu daa chɛ tuhibu bɛ tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni.

english_verse: Judah's southern border started at the south end of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Nudirigu polo tintariga maa daa kpuɣila Teeku Kpiŋ la tariga mini di kulinol’ ni n-zaŋ kpa nudirigu polo.

english_verse: As it went west from there, it ran south of Scorpion Pass to Zin, and then came up from the south to Kadesh-Barnea. It continued past Hezron up to Addar, turned toward Karka,
translation_verse: Di daa zaŋ kpala nudirigu polo maa hal ti paai Akirabim n-zaŋ nimaani hal ti paai Zin n-kul zaŋ kpa nudirigu polo maa hal ni Kadɛshibarinia n-zaŋ ti gari Hɛzirɔn m-mali ti paai Adda ŋ-ŋmaligi chaŋ Karika

english_verse: and ran along to Azmon. After that, it followed the Egyptian Gorge and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. This was also Israel's southern border.
translation_verse: n-gari chaŋ hal ni Azimɔn n-zaŋ lala hal ti paai Ijipti kulibɔŋ m-mali hal ti paai di tariga teeku ni. Yi nudirigu polo tiŋgbani tariga n-yɛn bala.

english_verse: Judah's eastern border ran the full length of the Dead Sea. The northern border started at the northern end of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Ka wulimpuhili polo tiŋgbani tariga yɛn kpuɣila Teeku Kpiŋ shee zaŋ hal ni Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili noli. Ka nuzaa polo tiŋgbani tariga mi piligi Yalim Teeku maa ni Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili noli shee

english_verse: From there it went west up to Beth-Hoglah, continued north of Beth-Arabah, and went up to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: n-zaŋ hal ni Bɛtihɔgila n-yi nimaani zaŋ gari hal ti paai Bɛtaraba nuzaa polo. Ka di tariga maa zaŋ lala hal ni Rubin bia Bɔhan kuɣili la gbini;

english_verse: From there, it went to Trouble Valley and Debir, then turned north and went to Gilgal, which is on the north side of the valley across from Adummim Pass. It continued on to Enshemesh, Enrogel,
translation_verse: ka di tariga maa lan yi Akɔr Vinvamli ni n-zaŋ hal ti paai Dɛbir n-zaŋ kpa nuzaa polo nti ŋmaligi kpa Giligal polo yaɣ’ shɛli polo din tuhi Adumim din daa be vinvamli maa nudirigu polo la. Ka daa lan kpuɣi nimaani n-zaŋ hal ni Ɛnshɛmɛsh kulibɔna ni m-mali hal ti paai Ɛnrɔgɛl.

english_verse: and up through Hinnom Valley on the land sloping south from Jerusalem. The city of Jerusalem itself belonged to the Jebusites. Next, the border went up to the top of the mountain on the west side of Hinnom Valley and at the north end of Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Ka yi nimaani hal ti gari Hinnom Bidibisi Vinvamli ni zaŋ lab’ Jɛbusi nudirigu polo, Jɛrusalɛm m-bala n-lan kpuɣi nimaani hal ti du zo’ shɛli din do Hinnom Vinvamli wulinluhili polo la zaŋ lab’ Rɛfaim Vinvamli tariga nuzaa polo.

english_verse: At the top of the mountain it turned and went to Nephtoah Spring and then to the ruins on Mount Ephron. From there, it went to Baalah, which is now called Kiriath-Jearim.
translation_verse: Ka tintariga maa daa lan kpuɣi zoli maa zuɣu n-zaŋ hal ti paai Nɛfitɔa kulibɔna n-yi nimaani zaŋ hal ti paai tiŋ’ kar’ shɛŋa din ʒi Ɛfurɔn Zoli zuɣu la. Ka di daa lan yi nimaani n-chaŋ ti ŋmaligi n-zaŋ hal ti paai Baala bee Kiriatijiarim.

english_verse: From Baalah the northern border curved west to Mount Seir and then ran along the northern ridge of Mount Jearim, where Chesalon is located. Then it went down to Beth-Shemesh and over to Timnah.
translation_verse: Ka di daa zaŋ chaŋ ha nti lan gili Baala wulinluhili polo n-zaŋ hal ti paai Ɛdom zoya ni n-zaŋ chaŋ hal ti baɣisi Jiarim Zoli nuzaa polo gari bee din nyɛ Chɛsalɔn la, ka di lan zaŋ nimaani hal ti paai Bɛtishɛmɛshi n-gari chaŋ ti baɣisi Timna gari.

english_verse: Next, Caleb started a war with the town of Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher.
translation_verse: Ka Kalɛb daa lan yi nimaani chaŋ ti lu Dɛbirinim’ zuɣu. Dɛbir tuuli yuli n-daa nyɛ Kiriatisɛfa.

english_verse: Joshua gave Caleb some land among the people of Judah, as God had told him to do. Caleb's share was Hebron, which at that time was known as Arba's Town, because Arba was the famous ancestor of the Anakim.
translation_verse: Naawuni ni daa zali Jɔshua shɛm zuɣu daa chɛ ka o ŋmaai Juda zuliya la tiŋgbani yaɣ’ shɛli polo bɛ ni booni Hiburɔn la ti Jɛfune bia Kalɛb. Kiriatariba, di gbinni nyɛla Hiburɔn.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah, Zanoah, En-Gannim, Tappuah, Enam, Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah, Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim.
translation_verse: Ka Kalɛb daa ŋme n-kari Anaki bidibis’ ata bɛn daa nyɛ: Shɛshai mini Ahiman ni Talimai bɛn daa nyɛ ŋun’ Anaki zuliya la bahi.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Zenan, Hadashah, Migdalgad, Dilan, Mizpeh, Joktheel, Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon, Cabbon, Lahmas, Chitlish, Gederoth, Beth-Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah.
translation_verse: Ka Kalɛb daa yɛli, “Ninvuɣ’ so ŋun ŋme n-nyaŋ Kiriatisɛfanim’ ka deei bɛ tiŋ’ maa, n ni zaŋ m bipuɣiŋga Akisa ti o paɣipini.”

english_verse: Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked her, “What's bothering you?”
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa ti kulisi Akisa na dahin’ shɛli, ka Otiniɛl daa kpam’ o jaande ni o suhim’ o ba tiŋgbani palo. Ka Akisa daa ti sheeg’ o buŋ’ zuɣu na; ka Kalɛb bɔh’ o, “Bɔ ka a bɔra?”

english_verse: She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so I really need some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.” Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds, named Higher Pond and Lower Pond. Towns in Judah's Land
translation_verse: Ka o garigi yɛl’ o, “Tim ma pini. A ni zaŋ Nɛgɛb tiŋgbani n-ti ma la zuɣu, tim ma kulibɔna din kom zɔri gba pahi.” Ka Kalɛb daa zaŋ zuɣusaa polo mini naɣiliŋga ni kulibɔna ti o pahi. Juda zuliya tinsi ni nyɛ shɛm

english_verse: The following is a list of the towns in each region given to the Judah clans:
translation_verse: Juda zuliya ni daa deei tiŋgban’ shɛli ni bɛ su li m-bɔŋɔ.

english_verse: The first region was located in the Southern Desert along the border with Edom, and it had the following
translation_verse: ni Lɛbaɔt ni Shilihim ni Ain ni Rimɔn: ka di zaa kalinli yiɣisi fɔntiŋ’ kara pihitayinika m-pahi di tiŋkpansi zuɣu.

english_verse: The second region was located in the northern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
translation_verse: ni Shaaraim ni Aditaim ni Gɛdɛra ni Gɛdɛrɔtaim: ka di zaa kalinli yiɣisi fɔntiŋ’ kara pinaanahi m-pahi di tiŋkpansi zuɣu.

english_verse: The third region was located in the southern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
translation_verse: ni Gɛdɛrɔt ni Bɛtidagɔn ni Naama ni Makɛda: ka di zaa kalinli yiɣisi fɔntiŋ’ kara pinaayɔbu m-pahi di tiŋkpansi zuɣu.

english_verse: The fourth region was located in the central part of the lower foothills, and it had the following nine towns with their surrounding villages: Libnah, Ether, Ashan, Iphtah, Ashnah, Nezib, Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah.
translation_verse: ni Kɛila ni Akizib ni Marɛsha ka di zaa kalinli yiɣisi fɔntiŋ’ kara awɛi m-pahi di tiŋkpansi zuɣu.

english_verse: The fifth region was located along the Mediterranean seacoast, and it had the following towns with their surrounding settlements and villages: Ekron and the towns between there and the coast, Ashdod and the larger towns nearby, Gaza, the towns from Gaza to the Egyptian Gorge, and the towns along the coast of the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Ashidɔd mini di fɔndi ni di tiŋkpansi ni Gaza mini di fɔndi ni di tiŋkpansi daa zaŋmi hal ti paai Ijipti kulibɔŋ mini Mɛditirɛniɛn Teeku noli tintariga la.

english_verse: The eighth region was located in the southeastern part of the hill country, and it had the following ten towns with their surrounding villages: Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Juttah, Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah, Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah.
translation_verse: ni Kain ni Gibia ni Timna: ka di zaa kalinli yiɣisi fɔntiŋ’ kara pia m-pahi di tiŋkpansi zuɣu.

english_verse: The eleventh region was located in the northern part of Judah's hill country, and it had the following two towns with their surrounding villages: Rabbah, and Kiriath-Baal, which is also called Kiriath-Jearim.
translation_verse: Kiriatibaal mini Raba gba daa beni: di daa nyɛla fɔntiŋ’ kara ayi m-pahi di tiŋkpansi zuɣu.

english_verse: The twelfth region was located in the desert along the Dead Sea, and it had the following six towns with their surrounding villages: Beth-Arabah, Middin, Secacah, Nibshan, Salt Town, and En-Gedi. The Jebusites
translation_verse: ni Nibishan ni Yalim Tiŋ’ la ni Ɛngɛdi: ka di zaa kalinli yiɣisi fɔntiŋ’ kara ayɔbu m-pahi di tiŋkpansi zuɣu.

english_verse: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and the people of the Judah tribe could not capture the city and get rid of them. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Judah.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Judanim’ daa bi tooi kari Jɛbusinim’ bɛn daa pun be Jɛrusalɛm la bahi. Dina n-chɛ ka Jɛbusinim’ mini Judanim’ na kul laɣim be Jɛrusalɛm hal ni zuŋɔ.

english_verse: The following is a description of the land that was divided among the clans of the Ephraim tribe. Their southern border started at Ataroth-Addar and went west to Upper Beth-Horon
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa zaŋ tiŋgban’ shɛli ti Ifriim zuliya kaman bɛ daŋ niriba ni nyɛ shɛm m-bɔŋɔ: bɛ tiŋgbani maa piligu shee daa kpuɣila Atarɔtada wulimpuhili polo n-zaŋ hal ni Bɛtihɔrɔn Duli polo

english_verse: Ephraim could not force the Canaanites out of Gezer, so there are still some Canaanites who live there among the Israelites. But now these Canaanites have to work as slaves for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Ifriim zuliya niriba maa daa lee bi kari Keenannim’ bɛn daa be Gɛza, dina n-chɛ ka Keenannim’ mini Ifriim zuliya niriba maa na kul laɣim’ be hal ni zuŋɔ; amaa ka bɛ lee chɛ ka Keenannim’ maa tumdi dabitim tuma tiri ba.

english_verse: The land of the Manasseh tribe went from its northern border with the Asher tribe south to Michmethath, which is to the east of Shechem. The southern border started there, but curved even farther south to include the people who lived around Tappuah Spring.
translation_verse: Manaasa zuliya niriba tiŋgbani maa daa zaŋmi hal ti paai Asha mini Mikimɛtat din be Shɛkɛm wulimpuhili polo la. Ka di tintariga bɔbili daa zaŋ kpa nudirigu polo m-mali hal ti paai Ɛntapuanima.

english_verse: The town of Tappuah was on Manasseh's border with Ephraim. Although the land around Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, the town itself belonged to Ephraim.
translation_verse: Manaasa zuliya niriba n-daa su Tapua tiŋgbani maa, amaa Tapua fɔŋ din daa ʒi Manaasa zuliya niriba tintariga la dina, Ifriim zuliya niriba n-daa su li.

english_verse: Manasseh was supposed to have the following towns with their surrounding villages inside the borders of Issachar's and Asher's tribal lands: Beth-Shan, Ibleam, Endor, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor, which is also called Naphath.
translation_verse: Isaka mini Asha tiŋgbana maa ni Manaasa zuliya niriba n-daa su fɔn shɛŋa mini tiŋkpan’ shɛŋa din be nimaani. Tinsi maa n-nyɛ: Bɛtishɛan mini di tiŋkpansi ni Ibiliam mini di tiŋkpansi ni Dɔrinim’ mini di tiŋkpansi ni Ɛndɔnim’ mini di tiŋkpansi ni Taanaknim’ mini di tiŋkpansi ni Mɛgidɔnim’ mini di tiŋkpansi; ka din pah’ ata n-nyɛ, Nafat.

english_verse: But the people of Manasseh could not capture these towns, so the Canaanites kept on living in them.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Manaasa zuliya niriba maa daa bi tooi kari tinsi maa nima; ka Keenannim’ maa daa kul kpalim be tinsi maa ni.

english_verse: When the Israelites grew stronger, they made the Canaanites in these towns work as their slaves, though they never did force them to leave. Joseph's Descendants Ask for More Land
translation_verse: Ka hal Izraɛlnim’ ni daa ti niŋ kpiɔŋ, bɛ daa bi kari Keenannim’ maa zaa, amaa ka daa naɣ’ lee muɣisiri ba mi ka bɛ tumdi tuma tiri ba. Ifriim zuliya mini Manaasa zuliya niriba suhiya ni bɛ ŋmaai tiŋgbani pahi ba

english_verse: One day the Joseph tribes came to Joshua and asked, “Why didn't you give us more land? The Lord has always been kind to us, and we have too many people for this small region.”
translation_verse: Ka Yisifu zuliya la daa ti bɔhi Jɔshua, “Bɔ n-niŋ ka a zaŋ tiŋgbani maa yaɣ’ yini polo din nyɛ din bi galisi ti ti? Yawɛ ni niŋ alibarika niŋ ti ni zuɣu, ti galisiya pam.”

english_verse: Joshua replied, “If there's not enough room for you in the hill country of Ephraim, then go into the forest that belonged to the Perizzites and the Rephaim. Clear out the trees and make more room for yourselves there.”
translation_verse: Ka Jɔshua garigi yɛli ba, “Yi yi galisi pam, ka Ifriim zuliya niriba zoya tiŋgban’ la pɔri ka bi saɣi ya, yin’ chamiya Pɛrizinim’ mini Rɛfaimnim’ tiŋgban’ ni yɔɣu la ni nti ŋma nyɔŋ ʒini.”

english_verse: “Even if we do that,” they answered, “there still won't be enough land for us in the hill country. And we can't move down into Jezreel Valley, because the Canaanites who live in Beth-Shan and in other parts of the valley have iron chariots.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ yɛl’ o, “Zoya tiŋgbani maa ku saɣ’ ti, ka Keenannim’ mi ʒi tintan’ ni, ka mali kuriti chɛchɛbunsi. Bɛ ni shɛb’ bɛn be Bɛtishɛan mini di tiŋkpansi ni bɛn be Jɛziriil Vinvamli ni la zaa mal’ li mi.”

english_verse: “Your tribes do have a lot of people,” Joshua admitted. “I'll give you more land. Your tribes are powerful,
translation_verse: Ka Jɔshua yɛli Yisifu zuliya bɛn nyɛ Ifriim mini Manaasa niriba maa, “Yi shiri galisiya pam, ka mali kpiɔŋ; ka di simdi ni yi mali tiŋgbani yaɣ’ bɔbili.

english_verse: so you can have the rest of the hill country, but it's a forest, and you'll have to cut down the trees and clear the land. You can also have Jezreel Valley. Even though the Canaanites there are strong and have iron chariots, you can force them to leave the valley.”
translation_verse: Ka zoya tiŋgban’ la ni kul nyɛ nyɔŋ la zaa yoli, yi ni tooi ŋma n-neei li ka di leei yi dini di piligu shee zaŋ ti kpa di tariga. Ka Keenannim’ maa ni kul mali kuriti chɛchɛbunsi ka mali kpiɔŋ la zaa yoli, yi ni tooi kari ba.”

english_verse: After Israel had captured the land, they met at Shiloh and set up the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ zaa daa ti laɣim Shilo n-zaŋ Naawuni jɛmbu tanti suɣili la kpa nimaani; ka bɛ ni daa tuhi deei tiŋgbɔn shɛli maa kul doya ka bɛ lihiri li.

english_verse: There were still seven tribes without any land,
translation_verse: Ka bɛ zuliya ayopɔin daa kpalim ka na bi deei bɛ tiŋgbana tarili.

english_verse: Just before the men left camp, Joshua repeated their orders: “Explore the land and write a description of it. Then come back to Shiloh, and I will find out from the Lord how to divide the land.”
translation_verse: Ka Jɔshua daa yɛli niriba bɛn yɛn chaŋ ti sab’ tiŋgbɔŋ maa yɛla ni nyɛ shɛm na maa, “Chamiya ti chaŋchaŋ gili tiŋgbɔŋ maa, ka sab’ tiŋgbɔŋ maa yɛla ni nyɛ shɛm ka labina; ka m bo kuɣa sɔŋ Yawɛ tooni Shilo kpe n-lihi nya n-tin ya.” Ka bɛ daa yiɣisi gbaai soli.

english_verse: The men left and went across the land, dividing it into seven regions. They wrote down a description of each region, town by town, and returned to Joshua at the camp at Shiloh.
translation_verse: Ka tuumba maa daa chaŋ ti kpe tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni chaŋchaŋ gil’ li, ka sab’ di yɛla ni nyɛ shɛm niŋ litaafi ni, ka lan pirigi di fɔndi ʒii buyopɔin zuɣu n-zaŋ labi ti ti Jɔshua Shilo sansani maa ni.

english_verse: Joshua found out from the Lord how to divide the land, and he told the tribes what the Lord had decided. Benjamin's Land
translation_verse: Ka Jɔshua daa bo kuɣa sɔŋ Yawɛ tooni Shilo n-lihi nya, ka daa piri tiŋgbɔŋ maa ti Izraɛlnim’ kaman di ni daa simdi ni bɛ zuliya kam deei shɛm.

english_verse: Benjamin was the first tribe chosen to receive land. The region for its clans lay between the Judah tribe on the south and the Joseph tribes on the north.
translation_verse: Bɛnjamin zuliya ka bɛ daa daŋ tiŋgbani tibu kaman bɛ daŋ niriba ni nyɛ shɛm. Bɛ tiŋgbani maa daa dola Juda mini Yisifu zuliya niriba tiŋgbana sunsuuni.

english_verse: Benjamin's northern border started at the Jordan River and went up the ridge north of Jericho, then on west into the hill country as far as the Beth-Aven Desert.
translation_verse: Zaŋ lab’ nuzaa polo, bɛ tiŋgbani maa daa piligila Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili ni n-zaŋ hal ti du Jɛriko nuzaa polo kuŋkuni n-zaŋ kpa wulinluhili polo ti du zoya zuɣu m-mali hal ti paai di tariga Bɛtavɛn yɔɣu ni.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth, Mizpeh, Chephirah, Mozah, Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah, Zelah, Haeleph, Gibeah, Kiriath-Jearim, and Jerusalem, which is also called Jebusite Town. These regions are the tribal lands of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Ka di tintariga bɔbili maa daa lan zaŋ nimaani n-kpa shɛli polo yaha nti ŋmaligi wulinluhili polo zoli gbini n-zaŋ kpa nudirigu polo hal ti paai Kiriatibaal .

english_verse: Benjamin's southern border started at the edge of Kiriath-Jearim and went east to the ruins and on to Nephtoah Spring.
translation_verse: Ka nudirigu polo tintariga mi kpuɣi Kiriatijiarim tintariga n-zaŋ hal ti paai Ɛfurɔn m-mali hal ti paai Nɛfitɔa kulibɔŋ ni,

english_verse: From there it went to the bottom of the hill at the northern end of Rephaim Valley. The other side of this hill faces Hinnom Valley, which is on the land that slopes south from Jerusalem. The border went down through Hinnom Valley until it reached Enrogel.
translation_verse: ka lan zaŋ nimaani hal ti paai zo’ shɛli din doya miri Hinnom Bidibisi Vinvamli din do Rɛfaim Vinvamli nuzaa polo ni, ka lan zaŋ nimaani hal ni Hinnom Vinvamli din be Jɛbusi nudirigu polo kuŋkuni zuɣu la m-mali lala hal ti sirigi Ɛnrɔgɛl polo ha.

english_verse: At Enrogel the border curved north and went to Enshemesh and on east to Geliloth, which is across the valley from Adummim Pass. Then it went down to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: Di daa lan ŋmaligi kpala nuzaa polo n-chaŋ hal ti paai Ɛnshɛmɛsh n-yi nimaani zaŋ hal ni Gɛlilɔt din be Adumim bimbini tooni la. Ka daa lan zaŋ nimaani hal ni Rubin bia Bɔhan kuɣili la gbini

english_verse: The border ran along the hillside north of Beth-Arabah, then down into the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: n-lan yi nimaani zaŋ kpa nuzaa polo ti du Bɛtaraba Zoli m-mali lala hal ti siɣi Araba.

english_verse: Inside the valley it went south as far as the northern hillside of Beth-Hoglah. The last section of the border went from there to the northern end of the Dead Sea, at the mouth of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Ka di tintariga maa lan zaŋ nimaani kpa nuzaa polo m-mali ti du Bɛtihɔgila kuŋkuni, ka di tintariga maa daa zaŋ hal ti paai di tariga Yalim Teeku duli nuzaa polo zaŋ lab’ Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili nudirigu polo. Di nudirigu polo tintariga n-daa bala.

english_verse: The Jordan River itself was Benjamin's eastern border. These were the borders of Benjamin's tribal land, where the clans of Benjamin lived.
translation_verse: Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili ni ka di wulimpuhili polo tintariga daa kpuɣi chaŋ. Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba ni daa deei tiŋgban’ shɛli ka di leei bɛ dini maa, ka tintarisi ŋɔ zaa daa gili niŋ sunsuuni.

english_verse: One region of Benjamin's tribal land had twelve towns with their surrounding villages. Those towns were Jericho, Beth-Hoglah, Emek-Keziz, Beth-Arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel, Avvim, Parah, Ophrah, Chephar-Ammoni, Ophni, and Geba.
translation_verse: ni Chɛfaramɔni ni Ofini ni Gɛba: ka di zaa kalinli yiɣisi fɔŋ kara pinaayi m-pahi di tiŋkpansi zuɣu.

english_verse: Simeon was the second tribe chosen to receive land, and the region for its clans was inside Judah's borders.
translation_verse: Simiɔn zuliya n-daa pah’ ayi n-nyɛ bɛ ni ti shɛb’ tiŋgbani kaman bɛ daŋ niriba ni nyɛ shɛm. Bɛ tiŋgbani maa daa bela Juda zuliya tiŋgban’ ni.

english_verse: In one region of Simeon's tribal land there were the following
translation_verse: ni Bɛtilɛbaut ni Sharuhɛn: ka di zaa kalinli yiɣisi fɔŋ kara pinaata m-pahi di tiŋkpansi zuɣu.

english_verse: and continued north to Gath-Hepher, Ethkazin, and Rimmonah, where it curved toward Neah
translation_verse: Ka yi nimaani n-zaŋ kpa wulimpuhili polo hal ni Gatihɛfa m-mali hal ni Ɛtikazin nti ŋmaligi kpa Niya polo n-zaŋ hal ti paai Rimɔn.

english_verse: In another region, Simeon had the following four towns with their surrounding villages: Enrimmon, Tachan, Ether, and Ashan.
translation_verse: Fɔŋ kar’ shɛŋa gba daa lan beni yaha. Dina n-nyɛ: Ain mini Rimɔn ni Ɛta ni Ashan: ka di zaa kalinli yiɣisi fɔŋ kara anahi m-pahi di tiŋkpansi zuɣu

english_verse: Simeon's land also included all the other towns and villages as far south as Baalath-Beer, which is also called Ramah of the South.
translation_verse: zaŋ tabili tiŋkpan’ shɛŋa zaa din gil’ li zaŋ hal ti paai Baalatibeer . Simiɔn zuliya niriba ni daa deei tiŋgban’ shɛli ka di leei bɛ dini m-bala.

english_verse: Simeon's tribal land was actually inside Judah's territory. Judah had received too much land for the number of people in its tribe, so part of Judah's land was given to Simeon. Zebulun's Land
translation_verse: Juda zuliya niriba tiŋgbani palo ni daa galisi pam zuɣu, ka bɛ daa ŋmaai di shɛli polo ti Simiɔn zuliya niriba; ka Simiɔn zuliya niriba tiŋgbani maa daa be Juda zuliya niriba tiŋgbani maa puuni. Bɛ ni zaŋ tiŋgban’ shɛli ti Zɛbulɔn zuliya niriba

english_verse: and became the northern border. Then it curved south around Hannathon and went as far west as Iphtahel Valley.
translation_verse: Zaŋ lab’ nuzaa polo mi di daa chaŋmi ti ŋmaligi kpa Hannatɔn polo n-zaŋ hal ti paai di tariga Ɛfitahɛl Vinvamli ni.

english_verse: Zebulun had twelve towns with their surrounding villages. Some of these were Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Jiralah, and Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Fɔŋ kar’ shɛŋa din pahi n-nyɛ: Katat mini Nahalal ni Shimrɔn ni Idala ni Bɛtilihɛm: ka di zaa kalinli yiɣisi fɔŋ kara pinaayi m-pahi di tiŋkpansi zuɣu.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem, Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath, Debirath, Kishion, Ebez, Remeth, En-Gannim, Enhaddah, Beth-Pazzez, Tabor, Shahazumah and Beth-Shemesh. Asher's Land
translation_verse: Fɔndi ŋɔ mini tiŋkpansi ŋɔ zaa daa bela Zɛbulɔn zuliya ni daa deei tiŋgban’ shɛli ka di leei bɛ dini kaman bɛ daŋ niriba ni nyɛ shɛm la puuni. Bɛ ni zaŋ tiŋgban’ shɛli ti Isaka zuliya niriba

english_verse: Issachar was the fourth tribe chosen to receive land. The northern border for its clans went from Mount Tabor east to the Jordan River. Their land included the following
translation_verse: Fɔndi ŋɔ mini di tiŋkpansi maa zaa daa bela Isaka zuliya ni daa deei tiŋgban’ shɛli, ka di leei bɛ dini kaman bɛ daŋ niriba ni nyɛ shɛm maa ni. Bɛ ni zaŋ tiŋgban’ shɛli ti Asha zuliya niriba

english_verse: then east to Beth-Dagon. On the southeast, Asher shared a border with Zebulun along the Iphtahel Valley. On the eastern side their border ran north to Beth-Emek, went east of Cabul, and then on to Neiel,
translation_verse: Ka di tintariga daa ŋmaligi kpa wulimpuhili polo n-zaŋ hal ni Bɛtidagɔn m-mali hal ti paai Zɛbulɔn mini Ifitahɛl Vinvamli din be Bɛtimɛk mini Nɛyɛl soli nuzaa polo la, ka kul zaŋ kpa nuzaa polo maa hal ti paai Kabul

english_verse: Abdon, Rehob, Hammon, Kanah, and as far north as the city of Sidon.
translation_verse: mini Ɛburɔn ni Rɛhɔb ni Hamɔn ni Kana m-mali hal ti paai Sidɔn din nyɛ tin’ tital’ la.

english_verse: Then it turned west to become the northern border and went to Ramah and the fortress-city of Tyre. Near Tyre it turned toward Hosah and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. Asher had a total of
translation_verse: Fɔndi ŋɔ mini di tiŋkpansi maa zaa daa bela Asha zuliya ni daa deei tiŋgban’ shɛli ka di leei bɛ dini kaman bɛ daŋ niriba ni nyɛ shɛm maa ni. Bɛ ni zaŋ tiŋgban’ shɛli ti Naftali zuliya niriba

english_verse: Naphtali was the sixth tribe chosen to receive land. The southern border for its clans started in the west, where the tribal lands of Asher and Zebulun meet near Hukkok. From that point it ran east and southeast along the border with Zebulun as far as Aznoth-Tabor. From there the border went east to Heleph, Adami-Nekeb, Jabneel, then to the town called Oak in Zaanannim, and Lakkum. The southern border ended at the Jordan River, at the edge of the town named Jehudah. Naphtali shared a border with Asher on the west.
translation_verse: Ka di tintariga daa ŋmaligi nimaani n-zaŋ kpa wulinluhili polo chaŋ hal ni Azinɔtitabo zaŋ ti paai Hukok n-zaŋ ti to Zɛbulɔn tiŋgbani nudirigu polo, ka zaŋ ti to Asha tiŋgbani mi wulinluhili polo, ka lan zaŋ ti to Juda gba tiŋgbani wulimpuhili polo Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili ni.

english_verse: Its clans received this land and these towns with their surrounding villages. Later, when enemies forced them to leave their tribal land, they went to the town of Leshem. They attacked the town, captured it, and killed the people who lived there. Then they settled there themselves and renamed the town Dan after their ancestor. Joshua's Land
translation_verse: Fɔndi ŋɔ mini di tiŋkpansi zaa daa bela Dan zuliya ni daa deei tiŋgban’ shɛli ka di leei bɛ dini kaman bɛ daŋ niriba ni nyɛ shɛm maa ni. Tiŋgban’ shɛli din bahindi nyaaŋa taribu

english_verse: The Israelites were still gathered in Shiloh in front of the sacred tent, when Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and the family leaders of Israel finished giving out the land to the tribes. The Lord had told the people to give Joshua whatever town he wanted. So Joshua chose Timnath-Serah in the hill country of Ephraim, and the people gave it to him. Joshua went to Timnath-Serah, rebuilt it, and lived there.
translation_verse: Maligumaana Ɛliɛza mini Nan bia Jɔshua ni Izraɛl kpamba n-daa pihi kuɣa sɔŋ Yawɛ tooni Shilo, tanti suɣili la dunol’ ni lihi nya, ka piri tiŋgbɔŋ maa yaɣili kam tari. Lala ka bɛ daa niŋ tari li naai.

english_verse: These Safe Towns were set up, so that if Israelites or even foreigners who lived in Israel accidentally killed someone, they could run to one of these towns. There they would be safe until a trial could be held, even if one of the victim's relatives came looking for revenge.
translation_verse: Tinsi ŋɔ ka bɛ daa pii ti Izraɛlnim’ zaa zaŋ tabili tinzunnim’ bɛn daa be bɛ ni. Bɛ daa niŋla lala ni di yi ti niŋ daliri ka so ku o kpee sarati kubu, ŋun’ zom’ kuli di ni tiligi ninvuɣ’ so ŋun dol’ o ni o ku o yo samli nuu ni hal ti paai saha shɛli bɛ ni yɛn kar’ o saria.

english_verse: One day the Lord told Joshua:
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Jɔshua.

english_verse: When Moses was still alive, I commanded him to tell the Israelites about the Safe Towns. Now you tell them that it is time to set up these towns.
translation_verse: “Yɛlim’ Izraɛlnim’ ni bɛ piim’ tiliginsim tinsi kaman n ni daa pun yɛli Musa shɛm la.

english_verse: If a person accidentally kills someone and the victim's relatives say it was murder, they might try to take revenge. Anyone accused of murder can run to one of the Safe Towns and be safe from the victim's relatives. The one needing protection will stand at the entrance to the town gate and explain to the town leaders what happened. Then the leaders will bring that person in and provide a place to live in their town.
translation_verse: O ni tooi zo n-kuli tinsi maa zaɣ’ yin’ ni chaŋ ti zani tiŋ’ maa dunɔdali gbini n-kahig’ o yɛla ni nyɛ shɛm zaa yɛli tiŋ’ maa kpamba; ka bɛ zaŋ o kpe tiŋ’ maa ni ti ti o biɛhigu shee, ka o kpalim be bɛ sani.

english_verse: One of the victim's relatives might come to the town, looking for revenge. But the town leaders must not simply hand over the person accused of murder. After all, the accused and the victim had been neighbors, not enemies.
translation_verse: Ka so yi dolina ni o ti ku o yo samli, bɛn’ di zaŋ o ti o, o ni ku o kpee maa ka di nyɛla sarati zuɣu, ka pa ni o min’ o pun malila taali la zuɣu.

english_verse: The citizens of that Safe Town must come together and hold a trial. They may decide that the victim was killed accidentally and that the accused is not guilty of murder. Everyone found not guilty must still live in the Safe Town until the high priest dies. Then they can go back to their own towns and their homes that they had to leave behind.
translation_verse: Ka o ni tooi be tiŋ’ maa ni hal ka bɛ ti kar’ o saria palɔni, ka o na kul ni be nimaani hal ni maligumaaniba zuɣulaan so ŋun beni ka o tum tuuni maa kum nyaaŋa, di saha ka o naanyi tooi lab’ o ya din nyɛ o ni daa zo luɣ’ shɛli maa ti beni.”

english_verse: The Israelites decided that the following three towns west of the Jordan River would be Safe Towns: Kedesh in Galilee in Naphtali's hill country, Shechem in Ephraim's hill country, and Kiriath-Arba in Judah's hill country. Kiriath-Arba is now called Hebron.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka bɛ daa pii Kɛdɛshi din be Galili Naftali zuliya niriba tiŋgban’ ni zoli zuɣu la mini Shɛkɛm din daa be Ifriim zuliya niriba tiŋgban’ ni zoli zuɣu la ni Kiriatariba din be Juda zuliya niriba tiŋgban’ ni zoli zuɣu la.

english_verse: The Israelites had already decided on the following three towns east of the Jordan River: Bezer in the desert flatlands of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead, which was a town that belonged to Gad, and Golan in Bashan, which belonged to Manasseh.
translation_verse: Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili duli zaŋ lab’ Jɛriko wulimpuhili polo, bɛ daa piila Bɛza din be Rubin zuliya niriba tiŋgban’ ni la mini Ramɔt din be Giliad Gaad zuliya niriba tiŋgban’ ni la ni Golan din be Bashan Manaasa zuliya niriba tiŋgban’ ni la.

english_verse: While the Israelites were still camped at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, the family leaders of the Levi tribe went to speak to the priest Eleazar, Joshua, and the family leaders of the other Israelite tribes. The leaders of Levi said, “The Lord told Moses that you have to give us towns and provide pastures for our animals.”
translation_verse: Izraɛlnim’ ni daa be Shilo Keenan tiŋgbɔŋ ni saha shɛli, ka Lɛvinim’ kpamba daa ka Maligumaana Ɛliɛza mini Nan bia Jɔshua ni Izraɛl zuliya kpamba sanna ti yɛli ba, “Yawɛ daa yɛli Musa ni o tim ti tin’ shɛŋa din mali biŋkɔbiri mɔri ŋubbu shee ka ti ʒini, ka ti biŋkɔbiri ŋubiri mɔri nimaani.”

english_verse: Since the Lord had said this, the leaders of the other Israelite tribes agreed to give some of the towns and pastures from their tribal lands to Levi.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Izraɛlnim’ daa pii fɔntinsi ŋɔ mini di biŋkɔbiri mɔri ŋubbu shee bɛmaŋmaŋ’ tiŋgbana ni ti Lɛvinima kaman Yawɛ ni daa zali ba shɛm.

english_verse: The leaders asked the Lord to show them in what order the clans of Levi would be given towns, and which towns each clan would receive. The Kohath clans were first. The descendants of Aaron, Israel's first priest, were given
translation_verse: Kɔhat daŋ niriba n-daa nyɛ bɛ ni daŋ shɛb’ tinsi tibu. Bɛ daa piila fɔntinsi pinaata Juda mini Simiɔn ni Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba tiŋgbana ni ti Aduna ŋun daa nyɛ Maligumaana la daŋ niriba.

english_verse: towns and the pastureland around them. Two of these towns were from the tribe of East Manasseh, four from Issachar, four from Asher, and three from Naphtali. Golan in Bashan and Beeshterah were from East Manasseh. Kishion, Daberath, Jarmuth, and En-Gannim were from Issachar. Mishal, Abdon, Helkath, and Rehob were from Asher. Kedesh in Galilee, Hammothdor, and Kartan were from Naphtali. Golan in Bashan and Kedesh in Galilee were also Safe Towns for people who had accidentally killed someone. Towns from Zebulun, Reuben, Gad
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa zaŋ Hiburɔn din nyɛ nir’ ni daa yi ku o kpee ka zo n-kuli tin’ shɛli n-tiligiri la mini di biŋkɔbiri mɔri ŋubbu shee ti Aduna ŋun daa nyɛ maligumaana la daŋ niriba. Ka bɛ daa lan zaŋ Libina

english_verse: The Lord had told Moses that he would show the Israelites which towns and pastures to give to the clans of Levi, and he did. Towns from Judah, Simeon, Benjamin
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa pihi kuɣa sɔŋ lihi nya, ka zaŋ fɔntinsi ŋɔ mini di tiŋkpansi m-pahi di biŋkɔbiri mɔri ŋubbu shee ti Lɛvinim’ kaman Yawɛ ni daa pun yɛli Musa shɛm la.

english_verse: The descendants of Aaron from the Kohath clans of Levi were priests, and they were chosen to receive towns first. They were given
translation_verse: Fɔntiŋ’ kara pinaata ni di biŋkɔbiri mɔri ŋubbu shee ka bɛ daa zaŋ ti maligumaaniba bɛn nyɛ Aduna zuliya niriba.

english_verse: The Lord gave the Israelites the land he had promised their ancestors, and they captured it and settled in it.
translation_verse: Lala ka Yawɛ daa zaŋ tiŋgbɔŋ maa ti Izraɛlnima kaman o ni daa pun lo bɛ yaannim’ alikauli shɛm la. Bɛ ni daa deei li naai, bɛ daa ʒinila di ni.

english_verse: There still were enemies around Israel, but the Lord kept his promise to let his people live in peace. And whenever the Israelites did have to go to war, no enemy could defeat them. The Lord always helped Israel win.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa ti ba vuhim bɛ tiŋgbɔŋ maa zaa ni kaman o ni daa pun lo bɛ yaannim’ alikauli shɛm la. Ka bɛ dimnim’ zaa puuni ninvuɣ’ yino gba daa bi tooi zani bɛ tooni, dama Yawɛ n-daa chɛ ka bɛ nyaŋ bɛ dimnim’ maa zaa.

english_verse: The Lord promised to do many good things for Israel, and he kept his promise every time.
translation_verse: Yawɛ daa chɛ ka o ni lo Izraɛlnim’ alikauli sun’ shɛŋa la zaa zaɣ’ yini gba bi yiɣisi. O daa chɛ ka di zaa niŋ pali.

english_verse: Joshua held a meeting with the men of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh, and he told them:
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka Jɔshua daa boli Rubin mini Gaad ni Manaasa zuliya pirigili la daŋ niriba na

english_verse: You have obeyed every command of the Lord your God and of his servant Moses. And you have done everything I've told you to do. It's taken a long time, but you have stayed and helped your relatives.
translation_verse: Yi mi bi chɛ yi mabihi ŋɔ bahi di saha maa hal ni zuŋɔ, amaa ka kul doli Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ yi Naawuni ŋɔ zaligunima.

english_verse: The Lord promised to give peace to your relatives, and that's what he has done. Now it's time for you to go back to your own homes in the land that Moses gave you east of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Ka pumpɔŋɔ, Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ yi Naawuni ŋɔ ti yi mabihi maa vuhim kaman o ni daa pun lo ba alikauli shɛm la, dinzuɣu labimiya kuli yi biɛhigu shee din be Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili duli polo, ka nyɛ Yawɛ dabili Musa ni daa pun zaŋ luɣ’ shɛli tin ya la.

english_verse: Moses taught you to love the Lord your God, to be faithful to him, and to worship and obey him with your whole heart and with all your strength. So be very careful to do everything Moses commanded.
translation_verse: Kpaŋmiya yimaŋ’ doli Yawɛ zaligu shɛŋa o ni daa chɛ ka o dabili Musa zali ya la. Dina n-nyɛ: Yumiya Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ yi Naawuni ŋɔ ka tumm’ o yubu, ka dol’ o zaligunima, ka zaŋ yimaŋ’ tabil’ o, ka kul jɛmm’ o ni yi suhuri zaa ni yi shia zaa.”

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh reached the western side of the Jordan River valley and built a huge altar there beside the river. When the rest of the Israelites heard what these tribes had done,
translation_verse: Ka so daa yɛli bɛ tab’ Izraɛlnim’ la, “Nyamiya, Rubin mini Gaad ni Manaasa zuliya pirigili la mɛla sara maligu bimbini zali Gɛlilɔt Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili polo na din nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ ni su luɣ’ shɛl’ la.”

english_verse: the Israelite men met at Shiloh to get ready to attack the two and a half tribes.
translation_verse: Izraɛlnim’ maa ni daa wum yɛlli maa, ka bɛ zaa daa laɣim Shilo na ni bɛ ti lo tɔbu chaŋ ti tuhi ba.

english_verse: Each of the ten tribes at Shiloh sent the leader of one of its families along with Phinehas.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Izraɛlnim’ maa daa pii maligumaana Ɛliɛza bia Finɛhas m-pahi bɛ daŋ kam ni dɔɣirikpamba pia zuɣu n-tim ba Rubin mini Gaad ni Manaasa zuliya pirigili maa sani Giliad tiŋgbɔŋ ni.

english_verse: Phinehas and these leaders went to Gilead and met with the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh. They said:
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa chaŋ Rubin mini Gaad ni Manaasa zuliya pirigili maa sani Giliad tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni

english_verse: All of the Lord's people have gathered together and have sent us to find out why you are unfaithful to our God. You have turned your backs on the Lord by building that altar. Why are you rebelling against him?
translation_verse: nti yɛli ba, “Yawɛ niriba Izraɛlnim’ zaa ni bɔhiri ya bɔhigu shɛli m-bɔŋɔ. ‘Tuumbiɛ’ bɔ ka yi lee tum zaŋ chaŋ Izraɛl Naawuni polo, din nyɛ yi ni me yimaŋmaŋ’ sara maligu bimbini zali, ka ŋmaligi ka chɛ Yawɛ dolibu zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ la? Yi yila Yawɛ nyaaŋa maa.

english_verse: Wasn't our people's sin at Peor terrible enough for you? The Lord punished us by sending a horrible sickness that killed many of us, and we still suffer because of that sin.
translation_verse: Ti ni daa tum alahichi shɛli Pɛɔr ka alɔbo lu ti zuɣu, ka ti na kul diri di wahala la bi galisi nyaŋ ti?

english_verse: Now you are turning your backs on the Lord again. If you don't stop rebelling against the Lord at once, he will be angry with the whole nation.
translation_verse: Ka yi mi ti lan ŋmaligi ka chɛ Yawɛ jɛmbu zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ? Ka yi yi yi Yawɛ nyaaŋa zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ, o suhu sa ni yiɣisi bahi tinim’ Izraɛlnim’ zaa zuɣu biɛɣuni.

english_verse: If you don't think your land is a fit place to serve God, then move across the Jordan and live with us in the Lord's own land, where his sacred tent is located. But don't rebel against the Lord our God or against us by building another altar besides the Lord's own altar.
translation_verse: Ka yi tiŋgbɔŋ maa yi bi bela nyam yin’ yiɣisimiya nimaani du tiŋgbɔn shɛli din nyɛ Yawɛ tiŋgbɔŋ ka o jɛmbu duu ʒe di ni ŋɔ na nti pii tiŋgbana ti sani ʒini. Amaa lee miriya ka yi yi Yawɛ nyaaŋa yi ni me yimaŋmaŋ’ sara maligu bimbini, ka chɛ Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ ti Naawuni ŋɔ sara maligu bimbin’ la zuɣu, ka zaŋ ti gba leeg’ o nyaanyiriba.

english_verse: Don't you remember what happened when Achan was unfaithful and took some of the things that belonged to God? This made God angry with the entire nation. Achan died because he sinned, but he also caused the death of many others.
translation_verse: Zɛra yaaŋa Ɛkan ni daa zaɣisi Naawuni noli ka kpuɣi binshɛŋa bɛ ni daa zaŋ ti Naawuni la, yi bi teei Naawuni suhu ni daa yiɣisi bahi Izraɛlnim’ zaa zuɣu shɛm la yɛla? Ka di pala Ɛkan kɔŋko n-daa kpi o daalahichi maa tumbu zuɣu.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord is the greatest God! We ask him to be our witness, because he knows whether or not we were rebellious or unfaithful when we built that altar. If we were unfaithful, then we pray that God won't rescue us today. Let us tell you why we built that altar,
translation_verse: “Yawɛ nyɛla ŋun gari wuna zaa, Yawɛ nyɛla Naawuni ŋun gari wuna zaa! O mi daliri din chɛ ka ti me sara maligu bimbini maa, ka ti bɔri ni ti chɛ ka yinim’ Izraɛlnim’ gba baŋ di daliri maa. Ti yi nyɛla nyaanyiriba ka me sara maligu bimbini ŋɔ bee ti yi lomi ni ti zaɣisi Yawɛ dolibu, yin’ di lan chɛ ka ti beni zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ.

english_verse: and we ask the Lord to punish us if we are lying. We didn't build it so we could turn our backs on the Lord. We didn't even build it so we could offer animal or grain sacrifices to please the Lord or ask his blessing.
translation_verse: Ka ti yi zaɣisila Yawɛ ka me sara maligu bimbini ŋɔ ni ti zaŋdi biŋkɔbiri maani sara pari di zuɣu nyɔri buɣim bee n-zaŋdi bindira sara bee suhudoo sara pari di zuɣu, ŋun’ Yawɛ maŋmaŋ’ ŋun’ darigim’ ti tibili.

english_verse: We built that altar because we were worried. Someday your descendants might tell our descendants, “The Lord made the Jordan River the boundary between us Israelites and you people of Reuben and Gad. The Lord is Israel's God, but you're not part of Israel, so you can't take part in worshiping the Lord.” Your descendants might say that and try to make our descendants stop worshiping and obeying the Lord.
translation_verse: Dama Yawɛ m-pun zaŋ Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili n-sɔŋ ti mini yinim’ Rubin mini Gaad zuliya niriba ŋɔ sunsuuni wuhi ti tintarisi ni nyɛ shɛm, dinzuɣu yi ka tarili Yawɛ sani.’ Di saha, di pa shɛli ka yi yaansi ti chɛ ka ti yaansi chɛ Yawɛ jɛmbu.

english_verse: That's why we decided to build the altar. It isn't for offering sacrifices, not even sacrifices to please the Lord.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka ti yɛli, ‘Chɛliya ka ti me sara maligu bimbini zali, ka di pala ti yɛn zaŋdila biŋkɔbiri m-maani sara pari di zuɣu nyɔri buɣim bee m-maani sara shɛli di zuɣu.

english_verse: Phinehas and the clan leaders were pleased when they heard the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh explain why they had built the altar. Then Phinehas told them, “Today we know that the Lord is helping us. You have not been unfaithful to him, and this means that the Lord will not be angry with us.”
translation_verse: Ka maligumaana Ɛliɛza bia Finɛhas daa yɛli Rubin mini Gaad ni Manaasa zuliya pirigili daŋ niriba maa, “Zuŋɔ ti baŋya ni Yawɛ be ti sani, dama yi bi tum tuumbiɛɣu zaŋ chaŋ Yawɛ sani. Yi fa Izraɛlnim’ Yawɛ nuu ni bahi.”

english_verse: Phinehas and the clan leaders left Gilead and went back to Canaan to tell the Israelites about their meeting with the Reuben and Gad tribes.
translation_verse: Di saha ka maligumaana Ɛliɛza bia Finɛhas mini Izraɛlnim’ daŋ kam ni dɔɣirikpamba maa daa yi Rubin mini Gaad zuliya niriba maa sani Giliad tiŋgbɔŋ ni n-zaŋ bɛ zilinkom lab’ Izraɛlnim’ maa sani Keenan tiŋgbɔŋ ni ti yɛli ba.

english_verse: The Israelites were happy and praised God. There was no more talk about going to war and wiping out the tribes of Reuben and Gad.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ ni daa lab’ ti yɛli shɛm maa tiɣi Izraɛlnim’ maa nini, ka bɛ paɣi Naawuni, ka bi lan yɛli tɔbu lo n-chaŋ ti tuhi ba, ka saɣim Rubin mini Gaad zuliya niriba ni daa ʒi tiŋgbɔn shɛl’ ni maa yɛla.

english_verse: The people of Reuben and Gad named the altar “A Reminder to Us All That the Lord Is Our God.”
translation_verse: Ka Rubin mini Gaad zuliya niriba maa daa yɛli, “Sara maligu bimbini ŋɔ nyɛla shɛhira bini ti mini ya sunsuuni ni Yawɛ n-nyɛ Naawuni.” Ka bɛ daa boli sara maligu bimbini maa yuli, “Shɛhira.”

english_verse: The Lord let Israel live in peace with its neighbors for a long time, and Joshua lived to a ripe old age.
translation_verse: Yawɛ ni daa ti Izraɛlnim’ vuhim ka bɛ dimnim’ bɛn gili ba niŋ sunsuuni bi tooi niŋ ba shɛli ka di yuui pam la nyaaŋa, Jɔshua gba daa kurigiya pam di saha maa.

english_verse: One day he called a meeting of the leaders of the tribes of Israel, including the old men, the judges, and the officials. Then he told them: I am now very old.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka o daa boli Izraɛlnim’ zaa mini bɛ kpamba ni bɛ zuɣulaannim’ ni bɛ sariakaritiba ni bɛ tuma kpamba na nti yɛli ba, “N kurigiya pam pumpɔŋɔ.

english_verse: You have seen how the Lord your God fought for you and helped you defeat the nations who lived in this land.
translation_verse: Ka yi mi nini nya Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ yi Naawuni ŋɔ ni niŋ zuliya shɛba shɛlikam zaa yi zuɣu la; dama Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ yi Naawuni ŋɔ n-nyɛ ŋun daa tuhi ba tin ya.

english_verse: There are still some nations left, but the Lord has promised you their land. So when you attack them, he will make them run away. I have already divided their land among your tribes, as I did with the land of the nations I defeated between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ yi Naawuni ŋɔ ni chɛ ka bɛ ŋmaligi yi tooni guui, ka kari ba ka bɛ zo ka chɛn ya. Ka yi deei bɛ tiŋgbana maa su kaman Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ yi Naawuni ŋɔ ni daa pun lɔn ya alikauli shɛm la.

english_verse: Be sure that you carefully obey everything written in The Book of the Law of Moses and do exactly what it says.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu lomiya ania n-doli dinkam sabi Musa zaligu ni la, ka miriya ka yi ŋmaligi kpa nudirigu polo bee nuzaa polo ka chɛ li.

english_verse: Don't have anything to do with the nations that live around you. Don't worship their gods or pray to their idols or make promises in the names of their gods.
translation_verse: Yi mi di zaŋya yimaŋ’ tabili zuliya shɛb’ bɛn na kpalim be yi ni la bee m-boli bɛ buɣa la yuya bee m-po ba bee n-jɛm ba bee n-damdi di tooni.

english_verse: Be as faithful to the Lord as you have always been.
translation_verse: Amaa kul ʒiɛnya Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ yi Naawuni ŋɔ yim kaman yi ni pun niŋdi shɛm hal ni zuŋɔ la.

english_verse: When you attacked powerful nations, the Lord made them run away, and no one has ever been able to stand up to you.
translation_verse: Dama Yawɛ pun kari zuliya shɛb’ bɛn galisi ka mali kpiɔŋ pam bahi ka chɛn ya, ka so na bi tooi zani yi tooni hal ni zuŋɔ.

english_verse: Any one of you can defeat a thousand enemy soldiers, because the Lord God fights for you, just as he promised.
translation_verse: Ka yi ninvuɣ’ yino kam karitimi doli ninvuɣ’ tuhili ka bɛ ŋmaligiri guura, Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ yi Naawuni ŋɔ ni tuhiri ba tiri ya kaman o ni daa pun lɔn ya alikauli shɛm la zuɣu.

english_verse: Be sure to always love the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu lomiya ania n-yuri Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ yi Naawuni ŋɔ.

english_verse: Don't ever turn your backs on him by marrying people from the nations that are left in the land. Don't even make friends with them. I tell you that if you are friendly with those nations, the Lord won't chase them away when you attack. Instead, they'll be like a trap for your feet, a whip on your back, and thorns in your eyes. And finally, none of you will be left in this good land that the Lord has given you.
translation_verse: dindina yin’ baŋmiya ni yi yi lan kariti doli zuliya shɛb’ bɛn na kpalim be yi ni maa, Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ yi Naawuni ŋɔ ku lan kari ba bahi tin ya. Amaa ka bɛ ni be kaman zana bee tɔna la n-gbahi ya; ka be kaman fiɛb’ shɛli din fiɛb’ yi puluɣa ni bee go’ shɛŋa din kuhiri yi ninni hal ka yi ti bahi yoli zaa tiŋgbɔn viɛl’ shɛli Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ yi Naawuni ŋɔ ni zaŋ tin ya ŋɔ ni.

english_verse: I will soon die, as everyone must. But deep in your hearts you know that the Lord has kept every promise he ever made to you. Not one of them has been broken.
translation_verse: “Pumpɔŋɔ, di kpalim biɛla ka n doli so shɛli sokam zaa ni dol’ la, ka yi zaa mi yi suhuri ni mini yi shihi ni ni Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ yi Naawuni ŋɔ ni lɔn ya bin sun’ shɛŋa zaa alikauli la zaɣ’ yini gba bi kɔŋ palibu. O chɛ ka di zaa niŋ pali hal ka di zaɣ’ yini gba bi kɔŋ palibu.

english_verse: Yes, when the Lord makes a promise, he does what he has promised. But when he makes a threat, he will also do what he has threatened. The Lord is our God. He gave us this wonderful land and made an agreement with us that we would worship only him. But if you worship other gods, it will make the Lord furious. He will start getting rid of you, and soon not one of you will be left in this good land that he has given you.
translation_verse: Ka yi mi yi bi gbibi Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ yi Naawuni ŋɔ daalikauli shɛli o ni lɔn ya maa, ka damdi buɣa tooni jɛm li, dindina Yawɛ suhu ni yiɣisi pam bahi yi zuɣu, ka yi bahi yoli yomyom tiŋgbɔn sun shɛli o ni zaŋ tin ya ŋɔ ni.”

english_verse: Joshua called the tribes of Israel together for a meeting at Shechem. He asked the leaders, including the old men, the judges, and the officials, to come up and stand near the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka Jɔshua daa lan laɣim Izraɛl zuliya maa zaa Shɛkɛm na nti boli bɛ kpamba mini sariakaritiba ni zuɣulaannima ni Izraɛl tuma zuɣulaannima, ka bɛ daa ka Naawuni tooni na.

english_verse: Then Joshua told everyone to listen to this message from the Lord, the God of Israel: Long ago your ancestors lived on the other side of the Euphrates River, and they worshiped other gods. This continued until the time of your ancestor Terah and his two sons, Abraham and Nahor.
translation_verse: Ka Jɔshua daa yɛli niriba maa zaa, “Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Izraɛl Naawuni ŋɔ yɛliya, ‘Yi yaannim’ Tɛra min’ o bihi Ibrahimma mini Nahɔr daa bela Yufretiiz Mɔɣili duli kurimbuni ha n-jɛmdi buɣa.

english_verse: But I brought Abraham across the Euphrates River and led him through the land of Canaan. I blessed him by giving him Isaac, the first in a line of many descendants.
translation_verse: Ka n daa zaŋ yi yab’ Ibrahimma Mɔɣili duli maa polo na nti chɛ ka o chaŋ gili Keenan tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ zaa. Ka n daa ti o bihi pam. N daa chɛ ka o dɔɣi Yisahaku;

english_verse: Then I gave Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the hill country of Mount Seir, but your ancestor Jacob and his children went to live in Egypt.
translation_verse: ka daa chɛ ka Yisahaku mi dɔɣi Yaakubu mini Iso. Ka n daa zaŋ Ɛdom zoya zuɣu tiŋgbani ti Iso ni di nyɛ o dini, amaa ka Yaakubu ŋun’ min’ o bihi daa yiɣisi kuli Ijipti.

english_verse: Later I sent Moses and his brother Aaron to help your people, and I made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians. I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, but the Egyptians got in their chariots and on their horses and chased your ancestors, catching up with them at the Red Sea.
translation_verse: N ni daa yihi yi yaannim’ maa Ijipti, ka bɛ kana ti paai teeku ni, di saha ka Ijiptinim’ daa yiɣisi zaŋ chɛchɛbunsi mini wɔribariba n-kari bɛ naba na hal ni Teeku Ʒiɛɣu ni.

english_verse: Your people cried to me for help, so I put a dark cloud between them and the Egyptians. Then I opened up the sea and let your people walk across on dry ground. But when the Egyptians tried to follow, I commanded the sea to swallow them, and they drowned while you watched. You lived in the desert for a long time,
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa kuhi niŋ ma, ka n daa zaŋ zibisim niŋ bɛ mini Ijiptinim’ maa sunsuuni, ka chɛ ka teeku kom mum ba niŋ n-di ba, ka yi nini daa nya n ni niŋ Ijiptinim’ maa shɛm. “ ‘Ka yi daa be mɔɣu ni yuui pam.

english_verse: then I brought you into the land east of the Jordan River. The Amorites were living there, and they fought you. But with my help, you defeated them, wiped them out, and took their land.
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka n daa zaŋ ya na ti paai Amɔrinim’ bɛn be Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili duli wulimpuhili polo la tiŋgbɔŋ ni. Ka bɛ daa tuhi ya, amaa ka n daa chɛ ka yi nyaŋ ba; ka n ku ba ka chɛ ka yi deei bɛ tiŋgbɔŋ maa su.

english_verse: King Balak decided that his nation Moab would go to war against you, so he asked Balaam to come and put a curse on you.
translation_verse: Ka Zipɔr bia Balak ŋun daa nyɛ Mɔab naa la daa ti yiɣisi lo tɔbu ni o tuhi Izraɛlnima, ka daa tim ti boli Bɛɔr bia Balaam ni o ti yɛl’ noli tin ya.

english_verse: But I wouldn't listen to Balaam, and I rescued you by making him bless you instead of curse you.
translation_verse: Amaa ka n daa bi saɣi ti Balaam, ka o daa naɣ’ niŋla alibarika niŋ yi ni; ka n daa tiligi ya Balak nuu ni.

english_verse: You crossed the Jordan River and came to Jericho. The rulers of Jericho fought you, and so did the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. I helped you defeat them all.
translation_verse: Ka yi daa gbaai Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili du n-ka Jɛriko na, ka bɛ lo tɔbu tuhi ya, ka n daa chɛ ka yi nyaŋ ba. Ka Amɔrinim’ mini Pɛrizinim’ ni Keenanim’ ni Hitinim’ ni Gɛrigashinim’ ni Hivinim’ ni Jɛbusinim’ gba daa ti lo tɔbu tuhi ya, amaa ka n daa chɛ ka yi nyaŋ bɛ gba.

english_verse: Your enemies ran from you, but not because you had swords and bows and arrows. I made your enemies panic and run away, as I had done with the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Ka n daa chɛ ka tabilakpihi lu bɛ zuɣu n-dim kari Amɔrinim’ nanima ayi la bahi; ka di daa pala yi takɔbiri bee yi tɔbiri zuɣu.

english_verse: You didn't have to work for this land—I gave it to you. Now you live in towns you didn't build, and you eat grapes and olives from vineyards and trees you didn't plant.
translation_verse: Ka n daa zaŋ tiŋgbɔn shɛli yi ni bi tum di tuun’ shɛli mini fɔntin’ shɛŋa yi ni bi me n-tin ya, ka yi be di ni diri ti’ shɛŋa yi ni bi sa mini olivi ti’ shɛŋa yi ni bi sa wala.’ ”

english_verse: Then Joshua told the people: Worship the Lord, obey him, and always be faithful. Get rid of the idols your ancestors worshiped when they lived on the other side of the Euphrates River and in Egypt.
translation_verse: “Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ lumiya Yawɛ sizuura, ka jɛm’ o ni yɛlimaŋli, ka ʒe o yim. Zaŋmiya wun’ shɛŋa yi yaannim’ ni daa jɛmdi Mɔɣili duli mini Ijipti la bahi ka jɛm Yawɛ.

english_verse: But if you don't want to worship the Lord, then choose here and now! Will you worship the same idols your ancestors did? Or since you're living on land that once belonged to the Amorites, maybe you'll worship their gods. I won't. My family and I are going to worship and obey the Lord!
translation_verse: Ka yi yi ku saɣi jɛm Yawɛ, yim’ piimiya yin’ ni jɛm so, yi yi ni jɛmla wun’ shɛŋa yi yaannim’ ni daa jɛmdi Mɔɣili dul’ la bee yi yi ni jɛmla Amɔrinim’ shɛb’ tiŋgbɔŋ ni yi ni be ŋɔ wuna la, yin’ piimiya, amaa man’ mini n yiŋnim’ ni jɛmla Yawɛ.”

english_verse: The people answered: We could never worship other gods or stop worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Ka niriba maa garigi yɛli, “Din’ kariya ka ti chɛ Yawɛ jɛmbu ka ŋmaligi jɛm wuna.

english_verse: The Lord is our God. We were slaves in Egypt as our ancestors had been, but we saw the Lord work miracles to set our people free and to bring us out of Egypt. Even though other nations were all around us, the Lord protected us wherever we went.
translation_verse: Dama ŋun’ Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ ti Naawuni ŋɔ n-daa yihi ti mini ti yaannima Ijipti luɣ’ shɛli din nyɛ dabitim ni la na, ka daa tum alahiziba tuun’ kara ti ninni, ka tiligi ti ti ni daa doli so’ shɛŋa zaa ni mini ti ni daa kpe zuliya shɛb’ ni garina nuu ni.

english_verse: And when we fought the Amorites and the other nations that lived in this land, the Lord made them run away. Yes, we will worship and obey the Lord, because the Lord is our God.
translation_verse: Ŋun’ Yawɛ n-daa lan kari Amɔrinim’ zaa bɛn daa be tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni, dinzuɣu tinim’ gba ni jɛmla Yawɛ, dama ŋuna n-nyɛ ti Naawuni.”

english_verse: Joshua said: The Lord is fearsome; he is the one true God, and I don't think you are able to worship and obey him in the ways he demands. You would have to be completely faithful, and if you sin or rebel, he won't let you get away with it.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Jɔshua yɛli ba, “Yi ku tooi jɛm Yawɛ dama o nyɛla Naawuni ŋun be kasi; ka nyɛ ŋun zabiri nyuli; ka ku chɛ yi tuumbiɛri bee yi daalahichi.

english_verse: If you turn your backs on the Lord and worship the gods of other nations, the Lord will turn against you. He will make terrible things happen to you and wipe you out, even though he had been good to you before.
translation_verse: Yi yi zaɣisi Yawɛ, ka ŋmaligi jɛm wuna, o ni ŋmaligi niŋ ya zaɣ’ biɛɣu m-bahi ya yoli zaa; o ni pun niŋ ya din viɛl’ la nyaaŋa.”

english_verse: But the people shouted, “We won't worship any other gods. We will worship and obey only the Lord!”
translation_verse: Ka niriba maa daa lan yɛli Jɔshua, “Aai, ti ni jɛm Yawɛ.”

english_verse: Joshua said, “You have heard yourselves say that you will worship and obey the Lord. Isn't that true?” “Yes, it's true,” they answered.
translation_verse: Ka Jɔshua yɛli ba, “Yinima n-di yimaŋ’ shɛhira ni yinim’ pii ni yi ni jɛmla Yawɛ ŋɔ.” Ka bɛ yɛli, “Tinima n-di timaŋ’ shɛhira maa.”

english_verse: Joshua said, “But you still have some idols, like those the other nations worship. Get rid of your idols! You must decide once and for all that you really want to obey the Lord God of Israel.”
translation_verse: Ka Jɔshua yɛli ba, “Dindina zaŋmiya wuna la bahi, ka zaŋya yi suhuri niŋ Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Izraɛl Naawuni ŋɔ ni.”

english_verse: The people said, “The Lord is our God, and we will worship and obey only him.”
translation_verse: Ka niriba maa daa yɛli Jɔshua, “Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ ti Naawuni ŋɔ ka ti kul ni jɛm, ka deeg’ o noli.”

english_verse: Joshua helped Israel make an agreement with the Lord that day at Shechem. Joshua made laws for Israel
translation_verse: Ka Jɔshua mini niriba maa daa lo alikauli dindali maa; ka o daa zali ba zaligu shɛŋa bɛ ni yɛn doli Shɛkɛm.

english_verse: and wrote them down in The Book of the Law of God. Then he set up a large stone under the oak tree at the place of worship in Shechem
translation_verse: Ka Jɔshua daa sab’ yɛtɔɣa ŋɔ niŋ Naawuni zaligu litaafi ni; ka bo kuɣ’ titali sɔŋ oki tia gbini nimaani Yawɛ jɛmbu duu.

english_verse: and told the people, “Look at this stone. It has heard everything that the Lord has said to us. Our God can call this stone as a witness if we ever reject him.”
translation_verse: Ka Jɔshua daa yɛli niriba maa zaa, “Nyamiya, kuɣili ŋɔ n-yɛn di ti shɛhira. Dama di wum yɛtɔɣ’ shɛŋa zaa Yawɛ ni tɔɣisi ti maa, dinzuɣu yi yi bi ʒe yi Naawuni maa yim, dina n-yɛn din ya shɛhira.”

english_verse: Joshua sent everyone back to their homes. Joshua, Joseph, and Eleazar Are Buried
translation_verse: Ka Jɔshua daa bahi niriba maa, ka bɛ zaa lab’ kuli bɛ ni su tiŋgban’ shɛŋa ni. Jɔshua mini Ɛliɛza kum yɛla

english_verse: Not long afterwards, the Lord's servant Joshua died at the age of
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka Yawɛ dabili Jɔshua Nan bia maa daa kpi. O daa niŋ dunia yil’ la yuun’ kɔbiga ni pia.

english_verse: The Israelites buried him in his own land at Timnath-Serah, north of Mount Gaash in the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa sɔɣ’ o omaŋmaŋ’ tiŋgban’ ni Timnatisɛra din be Ifriim tiŋgban’ ni zoya tiŋgban’ ni zaŋ labi Gaash Zoli nuzaa polo la.

english_verse: As long as Joshua lived, Israel worshiped and obeyed the Lord. There were other leaders old enough to remember everything that the Lord had done for Israel. And for as long as these men lived, Israel continued to worship and obey the Lord.
translation_verse: Izraɛlnim’ daa jɛm Yawɛ Jɔshua ni daa be o nyɛvil’ ni saha shɛl’ la zaa zaŋ tabili zuɣulaannim’ shɛb’ bɛn daa be Jɔshua kum nyaaŋa, ka daa mi Yawɛ ni daa tum tuun’ shɛŋa zaa ti Izraɛlnim’ la yɛla.

english_verse: When the people of Israel left Egypt, they brought the bones of Joseph along with them. They took the bones to the town of Shechem and buried them in the field that Jacob had bought for
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa zaŋ bɛ ni daa ʒi Yisifu kɔb’ shɛŋa yi Ijipti na la n-sɔɣi Shɛkɛm pal’ shɛli Yaakubu ni daa da Hamɔr ŋun daa nyɛ Shɛkɛm ba la bihi san’ la ni. O daa da li la anzinfa laɣibaligu kɔbiga. Ka tiŋgbani maa daa leei Yisifu zuliya niriba fali bini.

english_verse: When Eleazar the priest died, he was buried in the hill country of Ephraim on a hill that belonged to his son Phinehas.
translation_verse: Ka Aduna bia Ɛliɛza gba daa kpi, ka bɛ sɔɣ’ o Gibia fɔntin’ shɛli din be Ifriim zoya tiŋgban’ ni, ka o daa zaŋ li ti o bia Finɛhas la.

english_verse: After the death of Joshua, the Israelites asked the Lord, “Which of our tribes should attack the Canaanites first?”
translation_verse: Jɔshua kum nyaaŋa, ka Izraɛlnim’ daa bɔhi Naawuni, “Ka ŋun’ daŋ niriba n-lee yɛn daŋ tooni chaŋ ti tuhi Keenannim’ ŋɔ ti ti?”

english_verse: “Judah!” the Lord answered. “I'll help them take the land.”
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yɛli ba, “Juda zuliya niriba n-yɛn daŋ chandi, m pun zaŋ tiŋgbani maa niŋ bɛ nuu ni.”

english_verse: The people of Judah went to their relatives, the Simeon tribe, and said, “Canaanites live in the land God gave us. Help us fight them, and we will help you.” Troops from Simeon came to help Judah.
translation_verse: Ka Juda zuliya niriba maa daa yɛli bɛ mabihi Simiɔn daŋ niriba maa, “Pahimiya ti zuɣu ka ti chaŋ bɛ ni zaŋ tiŋgban’ shɛli ti ti la ni ti tuhi Keenannim’ maa. Ka ti gba pahi yi zuɣu ka ti chaŋ bɛ ni zaŋ tiŋgban’ shɛli tin ya la ni.” Ka Simiɔn zuliya niriba maa daa pahi bɛ zuɣu ka bɛ chaŋ.

english_verse: After that, they attacked the Canaanites who lived at Hebron, defeating the three clans called Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai. At that time, Hebron was called Kiriath-Arba.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa lan chaŋ ti lu Keenannim’ bɛn be Hiburɔn la nim’ zuɣu n-tuhi nyaŋ Shɛshai mini Ahiman ni Talimai. Otiniɛl tuhi nyaŋ Dɛbirinima (Jɔshua

english_verse: The king tried to escape, but soldiers from Judah caught him. They cut off his thumbs and big toes,
translation_verse: Ka Adɔnibɛzɛk daa guui, ka bɛ kari dol’ o ti gbaag’ o ŋ-ŋmah’ o nubihilɔri min’ o napombihilɔri bahi.

english_verse: They attacked Jerusalem, captured it, killed everyone who lived there, and then burned it to the ground.
translation_verse: Ka Juda zuliya niriba maa daa tuhi deei Jɛrusalɛm, ka zaŋ takɔbi ku di niriba, ka nyo li buɣim bahi.

english_verse: Judah's army fought the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, the Southern Desert, and the foothills to the west.
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka Juda zuliya niriba maa daa lan chaŋ ti tuhi Keenannim’ shɛb’ bɛn be zoya tinsi ni mini bɛn be Nɛgɛb ni bɛn be zolɔna ni tinsi ni la.

english_verse: From Hebron, Judah's army went to attack Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher.
translation_verse: Ka Juda zuliya niriba maa daa lan yi nimaani chaŋ ti liri Dɛbirinima. Bɛ daa tuui booni li la Kiriatisɛfa.

english_verse: Caleb's nephew Othniel captured Kiriath-Sepher, so Caleb let him marry Achsah. Othniel was the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz.
translation_verse: Ka Otiniɛl ŋun daa nyɛ Kalɛb tizo Kɛnaz bidibiga la daa chaŋ ti tuhi deei tiŋ’ maa, ka Kalɛb daa shiri zaŋ o bipuɣiŋga Akisa maa ti o ka o niŋ o paɣa.

english_verse: Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked, “What's bothering you?”
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa ti kulisi Akisa na dahin’ shɛli, ka o daa kpam Otiniɛl jaande ni o suhim’ o ba tiŋgbani palo. Ka Akisa daa ti sheeg’ o buŋ’ zuɣu na, ka Kalɛb bɔh’ o, “Bɔ ka a bɔra?”

english_verse: She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so please give me some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.” Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds named Higher Pond and Lower Pond.
translation_verse: Ka o garigi yɛl’ o, “Tim’ ma pini. A ni zaŋ Nɛgɛb ti ma la zuɣu, tim’ ma kulibɔna din kom zɔri gba pahi.” Ka Kalɛb daa zaŋ zuɣusaa polo mini naɣiliŋga ni kulibɔna ti o. Juda mini Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba di nasara

english_verse: The people who belonged to the Kenite clan were the descendants of the father-in-law of Moses. They left Jericho with the people of Judah and settled near Arad in the Southern Desert of Judah not far from the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Ka Musa deemba ŋun daa nyɛ Kɛn nir’ la daŋ niriba daa yiɣisi abie tihi tiŋ’ la ni n-dol’ Juda zuliya niriba maa ti ʒini Juda tiŋgban’ ni din lab’ Nɛgɛb polo m-miri Arad la. Bɛ daa ʒini pahila nimaani nim’ zuɣu.

english_verse: Judah's army helped Simeon's army attack the Canaanites who lived at Zephath. They completely destroyed the town and renamed it Hormah.
translation_verse: Ka Juda zuliya niriba mini bɛ mabia Simiɔn zuliya niriba daa chaŋ ti tuhi nyaŋ Keenannim’ bɛn be Zɛfat la n-ku ba zaa. Dinzuɣu ka bɛ daa boli tiŋ’ maa yuli Hɔrima.

english_verse: The Lord helped the army of Judah capture Gaza, Ashkelon, Ekron, and the land near those towns. They also took the hill country. But the people who lived in the valleys had iron chariots, so Judah was not able to make them leave or to take their land.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa sɔŋ Judanima ka bɛ tuhi deei zoya ni tinsi la, amaa ka lee bi tooi kari bɛn daa be bɔpiɛligu ni la, bɛ ni daa mali kuriti chɛchɛbunsi la zuɣu.

english_verse: The tribe of Judah gave the town of Hebron to Caleb, as Moses had told them to do. Caleb defeated the three Anakim clans and took over the town. The Benjamin Tribe Does Not Capture Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa zaŋ Hiburɔn ti Kalɛb kaman Musa ni daa pun yɛli shɛm la; ka o daa kari Anaki bidibis’ ata la nimaani.

english_verse: The Jebusites were living in Jerusalem, and the Benjamin tribe did not defeat them or capture the town. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Benjamin. The Ephraim and Manasseh Tribes Capture Bethel
translation_verse: Amaa ka Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba daa bi kari Jɛbusinim’ bɛn daa be Jɛrusalɛm la, dina n-chɛ ka Jɛbusinim’ mini Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba maa na kul laɣim be Jɛrusalɛm hal ni zuŋɔ. Yisifu zuliya niriba nyaŋ Bɛtɛlnima

english_verse: The Ephraim and Manasseh tribes were getting ready to attack Bethel, which at that time was called Luz. And the Lord helped them when they sent spies to find out as much as they could about Bethel.
translation_verse: Ka Yisifu zuliya niriba maa daa tim ni bɛ chaŋ ti puɣisi kaai Bɛtɛl nya di ni be shɛm. .

english_verse: While the spies were watching the town, a man came out, and they told him, “If you show us how our army can get into the town, we will make sure that you aren't harmed.”
translation_verse: Ka ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn daa chaŋ ni bɛ ti puɣisi kaai tiŋ’ maa daa ti chirigi do’ so ka o yi tiŋ’ maa ni na, ka bɛ yɛl’ o, “Ti suhir’ a, wuhim’ ti so’ shɛli din kuni tiŋ’ ŋɔ ni, ka ti niŋ a nirilim.”

english_verse: The man showed them, and the two Israelite tribes attacked Bethel, killing everyone except the man and his family. The two tribes made the man and his family leave,
translation_verse: Ka doo maa daa wuhi ba so’ shɛli din kuni tiŋ’ maa ni, ka Yisifu zuliya niriba maa daa kpe tiŋ’ maa ni ti zaŋ takɔbi ku tiŋ’ maa nima. Amaa ka daa chɛ do’ so ŋun wuhi ba tiŋ’ maa soli maa min’ o malibu ka bɛ chaŋ.

english_verse: so they went to the land of the Hittites, where he built a town. He named the town Luz, and that is still its name. Israel Does Not Get Rid of All the Canaanites
translation_verse: Ka doo maa daa zo n-kuli Hitinim’ tiŋgban’ ni n-daa ti me omaŋmaŋ’ tiŋa m-boli di yuli Luz; ka di yuli n-na kul bala hal ni zuŋɔ. Izraɛlnim’ ni daa bi kari ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ yɛla

english_verse: The Ephraim tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, so the Canaanites lived there with Israelites all around them.
translation_verse: Ka Ifriim zuliya niriba daa bi kari Keenannim’ bɛn be Gɛza, ka Keenannim’ maa daa kpalim be nimaani pahi bɛ zuɣu.

english_verse: The Zebulun tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Kitron and Nahalol, and the Canaanites stayed there with Israelites around them. But the people of Zebulun did force the Canaanites into slave labor.
translation_verse: Ka Zɛbulɔn zuliya niriba daa bi kari ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn be Kitirɔn bee ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn be Nahalol, ka Keenannim’ maa daa kpalim be nimaani pahi bɛ zuɣu; amaa ka bɛ daa lee muɣisiri ba ka bɛ tumdi tuma tiri ba.

english_verse: The Asher tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, and Rehob, and the Asher tribe lived with Canaanites all around them.
translation_verse: Ka Asha zuliya niriba maa mini Keenannim’ bɛn daa pun be tiŋgbani maa ni la kul laɣim be, bɛ ni daa bi kari ba maa zuɣu.

english_verse: The Naphtali tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Beth-Shemesh and Beth-Anath, but they did force the Canaanites into slave labor. The Naphtali tribe lived with Canaanites around them.
translation_verse: Ka Naftali zuliya niriba daa bi kari ninvuɣ’ shɛb bɛn be Bɛtishɛmɛshi bee bɛn be Bɛtanat, ka daa naɣ’ chɛ ka bɛ mini Keenannim’ bɛn daa pun be tiŋgbani maa ni la laɣim be, amaa ka bɛ lee muɣisiri Bɛtishɛmɛshinim’ mini Bɛtanatinim’ maa ka bɛ tumdi tuma tiri ba.

english_verse: The Amorites were strong enough to keep the tribe of Dan from settling in the valleys, so Dan had to stay in the hill country.
translation_verse: Ka Amɔrinim’ daa muɣisi Dan zuliya niriba n-kari ba labisi zoya ni tinsi la ni, ka daa bi saɣi ni bɛ siɣi tintan’ ni na.

english_verse: The Amorites on Mount Heres and in Aijalon and Shaalbim were also determined to stay. Later on, as Ephraim and Manasseh grew more powerful, they forced those Amorites into slave labor. The Amorite-Edomite Border
translation_verse: Ka Amɔrinim’ maa daa kul kpalim be Harihɛrɛs mini Aijalɔn ni Shaalibim, amaa ka Yisifu zuliya niriba daa muɣisi ba hal ka bɛ ti tumdi tuma tiri ba.

english_verse: The old Amorite-Edomite border used to go from Sela through Scorpion Pass into the hill country.
translation_verse: Ka Amɔrinim’ maa tintariga daa kpuɣi Akirabim hal ni Sɛla n-yi nimaani zaŋ du ha.

english_verse: The Lord's angel went from Gilgal to Bochim and gave the Israelites this message from the Lord: I promised your ancestors that I would give this land to their families, and I brought your people here from Egypt. We made an agreement that I promised never to break,
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ malaika daa yi Giligal chaŋ Bokim ti yɛli Izraɛlnima, “Naawuni yɛliya, mani n-daa yihi ya Ijipti n-zaŋ ya na ti niŋ tiŋgbɔn shɛli n ni daa lo yi yaannima alikauli ni n ni zaŋ li ti ba la ni. N daa yɛliya ni n ku lɔrigi alikauli shɛli n ni lɔn ya maa.

english_verse: and you promised not to make any peace treaties with the other nations that live in the land. Besides that, you agreed to tear down the altars where they sacrifice to their idols. Why haven't you kept your promise?
translation_verse: Ka di bi simdi ni yi lo ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn be tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni alikauli, naɣ’ wurimmiyala bɛ buɣa bimbina la. Amaa ka yi zaɣisi n ni zali ya shɛm maa niŋbu. Tuun’ bɔ ka yi lee tum maa?

english_verse: And so, I'll stop helping you defeat your enemies. Instead, they will be there to trap you into worshiping their idols.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ n yɛri ya mi, n ku lan kari niriba maa tin ya. Bɛ ni leei yi dimnima; ka bɛ wuna leei zana gbahi ya.”

english_verse: and they offered sacrifices to the Lord. From then on, they called that place “Crying.” Israel Stops Worshiping the Lord
translation_verse: Dina n-chɛ ka bɛ daa boli nimaani yuli Bokim. Ka bɛ daa mali sara ti Yawɛ nimaani. Jɔshua kum

english_verse: Joshua had been faithful to the Lord. And after Joshua sent the Israelites to take the land they had been promised, they remained faithful to the Lord until Joshua died at the age of
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa sɔɣ’ o omaŋmaŋ’ tiŋgban’ ni Timnatisɛra din be Ifriim tiŋgban’ ni zoya tiŋgban’ ni zaŋ labi Gaash Zoli nuzaa polo la.

english_verse: After a while the people of Joshua's generation died, and the next generation did not know the Lord or any of the things he had done for Israel.
translation_verse: Ka di ʒiɛmani maa niriba zaa gba daa ti kpi. Ka ʒiɛman’ shɛli din paya niriba daa yiɣisina. Bɛn’ daa bi mi Yawɛ bee m-mi o ni daa tum tuun’ shɛŋa ti Izraɛlnim’ la yɛla. Izraɛlnim’ chɛ Naawuni jɛmbu

english_verse: with the Israelites that he let other nations raid Israel and steal their crops and other possessions. Enemies were everywhere, and the Lord always let them defeat Israel in battle. The Lord had warned Israel he would do this, and now the Israelites were miserable. The Lord Chooses Leaders for Israel
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa yi lo tɔbu ni bɛ chaŋ ti tuhi bɛ dimnim’ saha shɛlikam, Yawɛ paarila o nuu bɛ zuɣu bɛ daalahichi tumbu zuɣu kaman o ni daa pun kpahi bɛ zuɣu ni ka po n-yɛli ba shɛm la. Ka nandahima daa mali ba pam.

english_verse: From time to time, the Lord would choose special leaders known as judges. These judges would lead the Israelites into battle and defeat the enemies that made raids on them.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yawɛ daa pii zuɣulaannim’ ti ba; ka zuɣulaannim’ maa daa tiligi ba ŋmɛnditoya maa nuu ni.

english_verse: In years gone by, the Israelites had been faithful to the Lord, but now they were quick to be unfaithful and to refuse even to listen to these judges. The Israelites disobeyed the Lord, and instead of worshiping him, they worshiped other gods.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Izraɛlnim’ daa ti zaɣisi zuɣulaannim’ maa noli; ka kul jɛmdila wuna. Di daa bi yuui ka bɛ ŋmaligi ka chɛ bɛ yaannim’ bɛn daa doli Yawɛ zaligunim’ ni daa doli so’ shɛl’ la, ka shiri bi dol’ li.

english_verse: When enemies made life miserable for the Israelites, the Lord felt sorry for them. He would choose a judge and help that judge rescue Israel from its enemies. The Lord was kind to Israel as long as that judge lived.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yi pii zuɣulaannim’ ti Izraɛlnim’ saha shɛlikam, o bela o ni pii zuɣulan’ so kam sani, ka tiligiri ba bɛ dimnim’ nuu ni zuɣulan’ maa ʒiɛman’ ni. Yawɛ daa zɔri ba nambɔɣu, bɛ dimnim’ maa ni daa nahindi ba ka muɣisiri ba, ka bɛ ŋuhiri shɛm la zuɣu.

english_verse: But afterwards, the Israelites would become even more sinful than their ancestors had been. The Israelites were stubborn—they simply would not stop worshiping other gods or following their teachings. The Lord Lets Enemies Test Israel
