english_verse: Then Boaz asked the man in charge of the harvest workers, “Who is that young woman?”
translation_verse: Ka Bɔaz daa bɔh’ o tumtumdib’ kpɛma, “Ka paɣisar’ ŋuni n-lee bɔŋɔ?”

english_verse: The man answered, “She is the one who came back from Moab with Naomi.
translation_verse: Ka o tumtumdib’ kpɛm’ maa garigi yɛl’ o, “Tinzun paɣisar’ so ŋun daa doli Naomi yi Mɔab tiŋgbɔŋ ni na la m-bala.

english_verse: She asked if she could pick up grain left by the harvest workers, and she has been working all morning without a moment's rest.”
translation_verse: O suhi ma mi ni n chɛ ka o doli kachɛriba maa nyaaŋa yihiri kayiha. Ka o kul bela o tuma ni asibaasi la zaa zaŋ kana pɔŋɔ, o na kul bi ʒini vuhi biɛla gba.”

english_verse: Boaz went over to Ruth and said, “I think it would be best for you not to pick up grain in anyone else's field. Stay here with the women
translation_verse: Di saha ka Bɔaz daa yɛli Rut, “M bia, chɛ ka n nyih’ a, di lan chaŋ so puu ni nti yihi kayiha ka pa ni m puu ŋɔ ni. Kul be paɣiba ŋɔ sani kpe n-tumm’ a tuma.

english_verse: and follow along behind them, as they gather up what the men have cut. I have warned the men not to bother you, and whenever you are thirsty, you can drink from their water jars.”
translation_verse: Lihimi puu maa ni n-nyari bɛ ni be luɣ’ shɛlikam polo chɛra, ka kul doli ba. M pun yɛli n kachɛriba bɛn nyɛ dɔbba maa ni bɛ miri ka bɛ niŋ a shɛli. Ka kɔnyuri yi ti mal’ a, nyin’ cham’ ti tooi bɛ ni ŋɔŋ kom pali kɔduɣ’ shɛŋa zal’ la ni nyu.”

english_verse: Ruth bowed down to the ground and said, “You know I come from another country. Why are you so good to me?”
translation_verse: Ka Rut daa gbani n-zaŋ o nina kpa tiŋa ka bɔhi Bɔaz, “Bɔ n-lee chɛ ka a ti niŋdi ma nirilim lala? Ka bee bɔ n-lee chɛ ka a ti lihi nya man’ ŋun nyɛ tinzun nir’ ŋɔ lala?”

english_verse: Boaz answered, “I've heard how you've helped your mother-in-law ever since your husband died. You even left your own father and mother to come and live in a foreign land among people you don't know.
translation_verse: Ka Bɔaz garigi yɛl’ o, “M pun wum a ni niŋ shɛlikam ti a yidan’ ma a yidan’ maa kum nyaaŋa zaŋ kana zuŋɔ yɛla. N lan mi a ni chɛ a ba min’ a ma ni a maŋmaŋ’ tiŋgbɔŋ, ka kana ni a ti be a ni ʒi ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ sani shɛm yɛla.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord God of Israel will reward you for what you have done. And now that you have come to him for protection, I pray that he will bless you.”
translation_verse: Yawɛ tim’ a a ni tum shɛm maa laara. Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Izraɛl Naawuni so baɣiri ni a ni kana ni a ti sɔɣ’ ŋɔ ni ti a laara din galisi.”

english_verse: Ruth replied, “Sir, it's good of you to speak kindly to me and make me feel so welcome. I'm not even one of your servants.”
translation_verse: Ka Rut daa yɛl’ o, “N dana, a niŋ ma nirilim pam. Hal m biɛhigu ni kul bi paag’ a paɣisara bɛn tumd’ a tuma ŋɔ ni yino gba biɛhigu maa zaa yoli, a kpaŋsi ma a ni tɔɣisi ma yɛtɔɣa ŋɔ shɛm maa puuni.”

english_verse: At mealtime Boaz said to Ruth, “Come, eat with us. Have some bread and dip it in the sauce.” At once she sat down with the workers, and Boaz handed her some roasted grain. Ruth ate all she wanted and had some left over.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa ti ʒini ni bɛ di bindirigu, ka Bɔaz yɛli Rut, “Kamina ti deei bɔrɔbɔro suɣi kpam.” Ka o daa kana ti ʒini kachɛriba maa sani, ka Bɔaz zaŋ chi bɔrɔbɔro ti o. Ka o daa ŋub’ li tiɣi ka guui shɛli.

english_verse: Ruth worked in the field until evening. Then after she had pounded the grain off the stalks, she had a large basket full of grain.
translation_verse: Ka Rut daa kul be o kayiha maa ni hal ka zaawuni ti paai, ka o daa zaŋ o ni nya shɛm tariga m-bu li yɛli ka di niŋ kilɔgiram pia.

english_verse: She took the grain to town and showed Naomi how much she had picked up. Ruth also gave her the food left over from her lunch.
translation_verse: Ka o daa zaŋ kabiɛlim maa ʒi n-kuli ti wuh’ o yidan’ ma o ni nya shɛm tariga. Ka daa lan zaŋ o ni ŋub’ ka guui bɔrɔbɔro shɛl’ la gba ti o.

english_verse: Naomi said, “Where did you work today? Whose field was it? God bless the man who treated you so well!” Then Ruth told her that she had worked in the field of a man named Boaz.
translation_verse: Ka Naomi daa bɔh’ o, “Ya ka a lee nya di zaa lala? Ŋun’ puu ni ka a chaŋ ti yih’ a kayiha maa? Naawuni niŋm’ alibarika niŋ ninvuɣ’ so ŋun lihi nya a maa ni!” Di saha ka Rut daa yɛli Naomi ni do’ so ŋun yuli booni Bɔaz la puu ni ka o chaŋ ti yihi kayiha maa.

english_verse: “The Lord bless Boaz!” Naomi replied. “He has shown that he is still loyal to the living and to the dead. Boaz is a close relative, one of those who is supposed to look after us.”
translation_verse: Ka Naomi yɛli, “Yawɛ ŋun paani o daalikauli bɛn ne mini kpiimba sani ŋɔ niŋm’ alibarika niŋ Bɔaz ni! Hal doo maa nyɛla ti dɔɣira ni Yɛlimaŋli.”

english_verse: Ruth told her, “Boaz even said I could stay in the field with his workers until they had finished harvesting all his grain.”
translation_verse: Ka Rut lan yɛli Naomi, “Ka din gari dimbɔŋɔ nyɛla, o yɛli ma ni n kul dol’ o kachɛriba yihimi kayiha maa hal ka bɛ ti chɛ n-naai.”

english_verse: Naomi replied, “My daughter, it's good that you can pick up grain alongside the women who work in his field. Who knows what might happen to you in someone else's field!”
translation_verse: Ka Naomi daa yɛli Rut, “M bia, a yi shiri chani Bɔaz puu maa ni nti yihiri kayiha maa, di so. Di pa shɛli ka a chaŋ so puu ni ka puu maa lan’ ti yih’ a halibiɛɣu.”

english_verse: And so, Ruth stayed close to the women, while picking up grain in his field. Ruth worked in the fields until the barley and wheat were harvested. And all this time she lived with Naomi.
translation_verse: Ka Rut daa shiri doli Bɔaz kachɛriba maa n-yihiri kayiha maa hal ka bɛ ti chɛ chi maa zaa naai. Ka Rut daa kul kpalim be o yidan’ ma maa sani.

english_verse: One day, Naomi said to Ruth: It's time I found you a husband, who will give you a home and take care of you.
translation_verse: Dahin shɛli ka Rut yidan’ ma Naomi daa ti yɛl’ o, “Di simdi ni m bo soli n-sɔŋ a ka a nya doo kuli, ka di chɛ ka a gba mal’ a dintoli biɛhigu shee.

english_verse: You have been picking up grain alongside the women who work for Boaz, and you know he is a relative of ours. Tonight he will be threshing the grain.
translation_verse: Teemi ni a ni daa doli Bɔaz so paɣisara yihiri kayiha la nyɛla ti dɔɣira. Wumma, yuŋ ŋɔ o ni be kabɔɣili ni m-buri chi.

english_verse: Now take a bath and put on some perfume, then dress in your best clothes. Go where he is working, but don't let him see you until he has finished eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu sum’ kom n-niŋ tulaale niŋ a ni, ka zaŋ a situr’ suma so n-chaŋ o ni be luɣ’ shɛli yeeni o chi maa. Amaa di chɛ ka o baŋ ni a be nimaani hal ka o ti di ka nyu n-naai.

english_verse: Watch where he goes to spend the night, then when he is asleep, lift the cover and lie down at his feet. He will tell you what to do.
translation_verse: O yi ti dɔni, nyin’ kpahimmi baŋ o ni dɔni luɣ’ shɛli maa, ka o ti ʒeei gom bahi ka a chaŋ o naba polo ti viig’ o chinchini baalim ka dɔni o naba tiŋli. O ni ti wuh’ a a ni yɛn niŋ shɛm.”

english_verse: Ruth answered, “I'll do whatever you say.”
translation_verse: Ka Rut yɛli, “N ni niŋ a ni yɛl’ shɛlikam maa zaa.”

english_verse: She went out to the place where Boaz was working and did what Naomi had told her.
translation_verse: Ka Rut daa chaŋ kabɔɣili maa ni nti shiri niŋ kaman o yidan’ ma maa ni daa wuh’ o ni o niŋ shɛm maa.

english_verse: After Boaz finished eating and drinking and was feeling happy, he went over and fell asleep near the pile of grain. Ruth slipped over quietly. She lifted the cover and lay down near his feet.
translation_verse: Ka Bɔaz daa ti di ka nyu n-naai, ka o suhu dɔni luɣ’ yini, ka o chaŋ kaʒee gbini ti dɔni ni o gbihi. Ka di daa tooi biɛla ha, ka Rut ti puɣisi chaŋ o naba polo ti viig’ o chinchini baalim ka dɔni o naba tiŋli.

english_verse: In the middle of the night, Boaz suddenly woke up and was shocked to see a woman lying at his feet.
translation_verse: Ka Bɔaz daa ti neei kaman yuntisuɣu saha n-lɛbig’ omaŋ’ tuug’ o ka di gar’ o, o ni nya ka paɣ’ do o naba tiŋli maa zuɣu.

english_verse: “Who are you?” he asked. “Sir, I am Ruth,” she answered, “and you are the relative who is supposed to take care of me. So spread the edge of your cover over me.”
translation_verse: Ka o bɔhi, “Ŋuni n-lee bala?” Ka o garigi yɛli, “N dana, man’ Rut m-bala. Kpuɣim’ ma leeg’ a paɣa, dama a nyɛla n dɔɣira ŋun ni tooi gbib’ ma.”

english_verse: Boaz replied: The Lord bless you! This shows how truly loyal you are to your family. You could have looked for a younger man, either rich or poor, but you didn't.
translation_verse: Ka Bɔaz yɛl’ o, “Yawɛ niŋm’ alibarika niŋ a ni. Hal a ni niŋ nirilim shɛli pumpɔŋɔ ŋɔ gar’ a ni pun niŋ a yidan’ ma nirilim shɛl’ la. A naan tooi chaŋ ti bo nachimbil’ so ŋun nyɛ bundana bee faralana, amaa a bi niŋ lala.

english_verse: It's true that I am one of the relatives who is supposed to take care of you, but there is someone who is an even closer relative.
translation_verse: Di nyɛla yɛlimaŋli ni n nyɛla a dɔɣim puuni ninvuɣ’ so ŋun su a gbibbu fukumsi, amaa ninvuɣ’ so ŋun nyɛ dɔɣim maa puuni nira ka miri dɔɣim maa gari ma gba beni.

english_verse: Stay here until morning, then I will find out if he is willing to look after you. If he isn't, I promise by the living God to do it myself. Now go back to sleep until morning.
translation_verse: Gbɛm’ kpe yuŋ ŋɔ, ka di sa neei ka ti nya dilan’ ni saɣi tum di tuma bee o ku saɣi. O yi saɣi ni o ni niŋ li, di viɛla, ka o yi bi saɣi, dindina m-po Yawɛ ŋun be ŋɔ ni n ni tum di tuma maa. Dinzuɣu dɔnimi ka biɛɣ’ neei.”

english_verse: Ruth lay down again, but she got up before daylight, because Boaz did not want anyone to know she had been there.
translation_verse: Ka o daa dɔni o naba tiŋli maa, amaa ka daa ti daŋ yiɣisibu asibaasi ŋaraŋara saha shɛli so ni ku tooi nya o baŋ o, dama Bɔaz daa bi bɔri ni so baŋ ni o ka nimaani na.

english_verse: Then he told her to spread out her cape. And he filled it with grain and placed it on her shoulder. When Ruth got back to town,
translation_verse: Ka Bɔaz daa yɛli Rut, “Pirigim’ a ni ye binyɛr’ shɛli pa zuɣusaa ŋɔ n-teei li sɔŋ.” Ka o daa pirigi li na, ka o tooi chi ka di ni paai kaman kilɔgiram pisi n-kpaai niŋ o di ni, ka kpuɣi li sɔŋ o ka o ʒi li kuli.

english_verse: She also said, “Boaz gave me this grain, because he didn't want me to come back without something for you.”
translation_verse: Ka lan yɛli, “O yɛli ma ni di bi simdi ni n lab’ kuna ni nuzaŋa, ka zaŋ chi ŋɔ zaa ti ma.”

english_verse: Naomi replied, “Just be patient and don't worry about what will happen. He won't rest until everything is settled today!”
translation_verse: Ka Naomi yɛli Rut, “M bia, guhimi nya yɛla maa zaa ni yɛn bahindi shɛm. Doo maa ku vuhi ka pa ni o nyala yɛla maa kpaa shee zuŋɔ.”

english_verse: In the meanwhile, Boaz had gone to the meeting place at the town gate and was sitting there when the other close relative came by. So Boaz invited him to come over and sit down, and he did.
translation_verse: Ka Bɔaz daa chaŋ ti ʒini tiŋ’ maa dunɔdali gbini niriba laɣiŋgu shee. Di saha ka Ɛlimɛlɛk dɔɣim puuni ninvuɣ’ so ŋun daa mir’ o la kana ni o ti gari nimaani, ka Bɔaz bol’ o, “Zɔri, kamina kpe ti ʒini.” Ka o daa kana ti ʒini.

english_verse: Then Boaz got ten of the town leaders and also asked them to sit down. After they had sat down,
translation_verse: Ka Bɔaz daa lan nya tiŋ’ maa ni kpamba pia m-boli ba ni bɛ gba kamina ti ʒin’ nimaani. Bɛ ni daa ʒini,

english_verse: he said to the man: Naomi has come back from Moab and is selling the land that belonged to her husband Elimelech.
translation_verse: ka o yɛl’ o dɔɣira maa, “Naomi ŋun yi Mɔab tiŋgbɔŋ ni na la mali tiŋgbani din nyɛ ti dɔɣira Ɛlimɛlɛk dini m-bɔri ni o kɔhi li,

english_verse: I'm telling you about this, since you are his closest relative and have the right to buy the property. If you want it, you can buy it now. These ten men and the others standing here can be witnesses. But if you don't want the property, let me know, because I am next in line. The man replied, “I'll buy it!”
translation_verse: ka n tɛhi ni di simdi ni n yɛl’ a di yɛla. To, a yi bɔri li, nyin’ dam’ li salo bɛn ʒi kpe ŋɔ mini n tiŋ’ kpamba ŋɔ ninni. Ka a yi bi bɔri li, nyin’ yɛlima, dama nyini n-nyɛ ŋun daŋ tooni n-simdi ni a da li, ka m paya.” Ka doo maa yɛl’ o, “N ni da li.”

english_verse: “If you do buy it from Naomi,” Boaz told him, “you must also marry Ruth. Then if you have a son by her, the property will stay in the family of Ruth's first husband.”
translation_verse: Ka Bɔaz yɛli, “Di viɛla, amaa a yi da tiŋgbani maa Naomi sani, shee ka a zaŋ Rut ŋun nyɛ pakoli ka lan nyɛ Mɔab nir’ la gba pahi, ka lala zuɣu chɛ ka ŋun kpi la zuliya na kul su tiŋgbani maa.”

english_verse: The man answered, “If that's the case, I don't want to buy it! That would make problems with the property I already own. You may buy it yourself, because I cannot.”
translation_verse: Ka doo maa yɛli, “Di yi nyɛla lala, hal n ni mali soli ni n da tiŋgbani maa la zaa yoli, n ni chɛ di dabu, dama di wuhiya ni mmaŋmaŋ’ bihi ti ku di li fali. Nyin’ dam’ li, man’ ku da li.”

english_verse: To make a sale legal in those days, one person would take off a sandal and give it to the other.
translation_verse: Di saha maa ha Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ni binyara zaŋ kɔhi tab’ zuɣu bee n-zaŋ taɣi tab’ yɛla ŋmaabu kali daa yi nyɛla ŋun kɔhiri pirig’ o namdili ti ŋun dara, lala ka Izraɛlnim’ daa yi niŋdi ŋmaari yɛla.

english_verse: So after the man had agreed to let Boaz buy the property, he took off one of his sandals and handed it to Boaz.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu doo maa ni daa yɛli Bɔaz ni o dam’ li maa, o daa pirigila o namdili ti Bɔaz.

english_verse: Boaz told the town leaders and everyone else: All of you are witnesses that today I have bought from Naomi the property that belonged to Elimelech and his two sons, Chilion and Mahlon.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Bɔaz daa yɛli tiŋ’ maa kpamba mini bɛn zaa daa be nimaani maa, “Yi zaa di ma shɛhira zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ ni n da Ɛlimɛlɛk min’ o bidibis’ ayi Kiliɔn ni Malɔn ni su binshɛɣukam zaa Naomi sani.

english_verse: You are also witnesses that I have agreed to marry Mahlon's widow Ruth, the Moabite woman. This will keep the property in his family's name, and he will be remembered in this town.
translation_verse: Ka din pahi nyɛla, Malɔn pakoli Rut ŋun nyɛ Mɔab nir’ la gba ni leegi m paɣa. Ka lala zuɣu chɛ ka ŋun kpi la zuliya na kul su tiŋgbani maa, ka o yuli ni be o niriba ni min’ o ya. Ka yinim’ mi n-di di shɛhira zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ.”

english_verse: The town leaders and the others standing there said: We are witnesses to this. And we pray that the Lord will give your wife many children, just as he did Leah and Rachel, the wives of Jacob. May you be a rich man in the tribe of Ephrath and an important man in Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Ka tiŋ’ maa kpamba mini bɛn pahi daa yɛli, “Iin, ti nyɛla di shɛhiranima.” Ka lan yɛli, “Yawɛ chɛ ka a paɣ’ maa be kaman Reechɛl mini Liya bɛn daa dɔɣi bihi pam ti Izraɛl la. Naawuni chɛ ka a tɔŋ Ɛfirat zuliya ni, ka chɛ ka a yuli du Bɛtilihɛm ŋɔ.

english_verse: May the children you have by this young woman make your family as famous as the family of Perez, the son of Tamar and Judah.
translation_verse: Yawɛ chɛ ka o ni yɛn ti a bi’ shɛba, ka paɣisarili ŋɔ dɔɣi ba ti a ni nyɛla bɛn ni ti chɛ ka a zuliya bemi kaman Pɛrɛz, Tama ni dɔɣ’ so ti Juda la.” Bɔaz zuliya

english_verse: After his birth, the women said to Naomi: Praise the Lord! Today he has given you a grandson to take care of you. We pray that the boy will grow up to be famous everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Ka paɣiba daa yɛli Naomi, “Paɣimi Yawɛ! O ti a yaaŋa ŋun nyɛ bidibiga zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ ni o ti gbib’ a. Yawɛ chɛ ka bia maa yuli ti du pam Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni!

english_verse: He will make you happy and take care of you in your old age, because he is the son of your daughter-in-law. And she loves you more than seven sons of your own would love you.
translation_verse: A bia paɣ’ maa yur’ a, ka tum din gari bidibis’ ayopɔin tuma ti a. O dɔɣi yaaŋa ŋun nyɛ bidibiga ti a, ka o ni ti nyɛla ŋun ni kpaŋsir’ a ni ŋun ni ti gbib’ a a kuriginsim saha.”

english_verse: Naomi loved the boy and took good care of him.
translation_verse: Ka Naomi daa kpuɣi bia maa ʒil’ o naba zuɣu m-mal’ o.

english_verse: The neighborhood women named him Obed, but they called him “Naomi's Boy.” When Obed grew up he had a son named Jesse, who later became the father of King David.
translation_verse: Ka tiŋ’ maa ni paɣiba daa boli bia maa yuli Obɛd ka yɛli, “Bɛ dɔɣi bidibiga ti Naomi!” Ka Obɛd daa ti dɔɣi Jɛsi, ka Jɛsi mi dɔɣi Naa Dauda. Dauda Yaannima

english_verse: Here is a list of the ancestors of David: Jesse, Obed, Boaz, Salmon, Nahshon, Amminadab, Ram, Hezron, and Perez.
translation_verse: ka Obɛd, dɔɣi Jɛsi, ka Jɛsi mi dɔɣi Naa Dauda.

english_verse: Elkanah lived in Ramah, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His great-great-grandfather was Zuph, so Elkanah was a member of the Zuph clan of the Ephraim tribe. Elkanah's father was Jeroham, his grandfather was Elihu, and his great-grandfather was Tohu.
translation_verse: Ifriim zuliya ni do’ so daa beni ka o yuli booni Ɛlikana, ka o daa be zoya ni tin’ shɛli din yuli booni Rama, ka di be Ifriim tiŋgban’ ni la. O daa nyɛla Jɛrɔham bia, ka Jɛrɔham daa nyɛ Ɛlihu bia, ka Ɛlihu daa nyɛ Tɔhu bia, ka Tɔhu mi nyɛ Zuf ŋun daa nyɛ Ifriim zuliya ni nir’ la bia.

english_verse: Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. Although Peninnah had children, Hannah did not have any.
translation_verse: Ɛlikana daa malila paɣiba ayi, yino yuli daa boonila Hanna, ka ŋun’ la mi yuli booni Pɛnina. Pɛnina n-daa nyɛ ŋun dɔɣi bihi, amaa ka Hanna ŋun’ daa bi dɔɣi bia.

english_verse: Once a year Elkanah traveled from his hometown to Shiloh, where he worshiped the Lord All-Powerful and offered sacrifices. Eli was the Lord's priest there, and his two sons Hophni and Phinehas served with him as priests.
translation_verse: Yuuni kam Ɛlikana daa yi yirila o ya n-chani Shilo ti jɛmdi Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Tɔbbihi Naa ŋɔ, ka maani sara nimaani. Ɛli bihi ayi bɛn yuya daa booni Hofini ni Finɛhas la n-daa nyɛ Yawɛ maligumaaniba nimaani.

english_verse: Whenever Elkanah offered a sacrifice, he gave some of the meat to Peninnah and some to each of her sons and daughters.
translation_verse: Ɛlikana daa yi kɔrigi binshɛli m-mali sara dahin’ shɛli o ŋmahirila nimdi tar’ o paɣ’ Pɛnina min’ o bidibisi ni o bipuɣinsi zaa.

english_verse: But he gave Hannah even more, because he loved Hannah very much, even though the Lord had kept her from having children of her own.
translation_verse: Hal o ni daa kul yur’ o paɣ’ Hanna maa zaa yoli, o daa kul ŋmaarila ninvuɣ’ yino kɔŋko tarili tir’ o, dama Yawɛ daa na bi ti o bia.

english_verse: Peninnah liked to make Hannah feel miserable about not having any children,
translation_verse: Ka o nyintaa daa yi kur’ o suli pam n-chɛ ka o suhu yiɣisira, Yawɛ ni daa bi ti o bia maa zuɣu.

english_verse: especially when the family went to the house of the Lord each year. One day, Elkanah was there offering a sacrifice, when Hannah began crying and refused to eat.
translation_verse: O daa kul niŋd’ o la lala yuuni kam. Bɛn dee daa yi kul chaŋ Yawɛ jɛmbu duu maa ni, o ni bahi miligi Hanna suhu ka o kum hal ti bi di bindirigu.

english_verse: So Elkanah asked, “Hannah, why are you crying? Why won't you eat? Why do you feel so bad? Don't I mean more to you than ten sons?”
translation_verse: Ka o yidan’ Ɛlikana daa bɔh’ o “Hanna, bɔ n-niŋ ka a mali suhugarigu, ka kumdi hal ti zaɣisi bindirigu? M bi gari bihi pia a sani?” Hanna mini Ɛli

english_verse: “Lord All-Powerful, I am your servant, but I am so miserable! Please let me have a son. I promise to give him to you for as long as he lives, and his hair will never be cut.”
translation_verse: Ka Hanna daa po pɔri yɛli, “Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Tɔbbihi Naa ŋɔ, a yi nya mani ŋun nyɛ a dab’ paɣ’ ŋɔ muɣisigu ŋɔ ka teei n yɛla, ka bi tam mani ŋun nyɛ a dab’ paɣ’ ŋɔ yɛla, amaa ka ti ma bidibiga, n ni zaŋ o n-labisi ti a hal ni o nyɛvili tariga, ka n ku chɛ ka piliŋ shih’ o zuɣu ni.”

english_verse: Hannah prayed silently to the Lord for a long time. But her lips were moving, and Eli thought she was drunk.
translation_verse: Hanna daa suhiri Naawuni la o suhu ni, amaa ka o naŋgbampiba lee damda, ka so daa bi wumd’ o kukoli. Dinzuɣu ka Ɛli daa tɛhi ni o nyula dam kuli,

english_verse: “How long are you going to stay drunk?” he asked. “Sober up!”
translation_verse: ka bɔh’ o, “Bɔ saha ka dam ŋɔ yɛn yi a ninni?” Ka yɛl’ o, “Chɛli wain nyubu.”

english_verse: “Sir, please don't think I'm no good!” Hannah answered. “I'm not drunk, and I haven't been drinking. But I do feel miserable and terribly upset. I've been praying all this time, telling the Lord about my problems.”
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu di zaŋ mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ ŋmahindi paɣ’ yoli, dama n ni kul be kpe saha shɛli maa zaa, n yɛlimuɣisira mini n suhugarigu yɛla ka n yɛri maa.”

english_verse: Eli replied, “Go home. Everything will be fine. The God of Israel will answer your prayer.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Ɛli garigi yɛl’ o, “Cham’ ni suhudoo. Izraɛl Naawuni ŋɔ ni deeg’ a suhigu maa, ka ti a a ni suh’ o shɛli maa.”

english_verse: “Sir, thank you for being so kind to me,” Hannah said. Then she left, and after eating something, she felt much better. Samuel Is Born
translation_verse: Ka Hanna daa yɛli “Chɛ ka mani ŋun nyɛ a dabipaɣ’ ŋɔ nya zuɣusuŋ a sani.” Di saha ka Hanna daa kuli ti di ka nyu, ka daa bi lan mali suhugarigu. Bɛ dɔɣi Samuɛl ka zaŋ o ti Naawuni

english_verse: Elkanah and his family got up early the next morning and worshiped the Lord. Then they went back home to Ramah. Later the Lord blessed Elkanah and Hannah
translation_verse: Ka Ɛlikana min’ o yiŋnim’ maa daa daŋ yiɣisibu asiba n-jɛm Yawɛ ka lab kuli bɛ ya Rama. Ka Ɛlikana min’ o paɣ’ Hanna daa ti dɔni, ka Yawɛ teei Hanna yɛla.

english_verse: with a son. She named him Samuel because she had asked the Lord for him. Hannah Gives Samuel to the Lord
translation_verse: Ka o daa niŋ pua n-dɔɣi bidibiga bol’ o yuli Samuɛl, dama Hanna daa yɛlimi, “N suh’ o la Yawɛ sani.”

english_verse: The next time Elkanah and his family went to offer their yearly sacrifice, he took along a gift that he had promised to give to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ka Ɛlikana min’ o yiŋnim’ zaa daa ti chaŋ Naawuni sani ni bɛ yaa ti mali yuuniyuuni sara la Yawɛ sani, ka pal’ o ni daa lo alikauli shɛl’ la.

english_verse: But Hannah stayed home, because she had told Elkanah, “Samuel and I won't go until he's old enough for me to stop nursing him. Then I'll give him to the Lord, and he can stay there at Shiloh for the rest of his life.”
translation_verse: Amaa Hanna ŋun’ daa bi chaŋ, dama o daa yɛlila o yidana, “Faashee bia maa ti ŋmaai bihili ka n zaŋ o tahi Yawɛ sani ka o ti kpalim be nimaani hal ni o nyɛvili tariga.”

english_verse: “You know what's best,” Elkanah said. “Stay here until it's time to stop nursing him. I'm sure the Lord will help you do what you have promised.” Hannah did not go to Shiloh until she stopped nursing Samuel.
translation_verse: Ka o yidan’ Ɛlikana daa yɛl’ o, “Niŋm’ a ni tɛhi ni shɛli viɛl’ a sani, kul guhim’ hal ka bia maa ti ŋmaai bihili. Yawɛ chɛ ka o yɛligu niŋ pali.” Ka Hanna daa kpalim yiŋa m-mal’ o bia maa hal ka o ti ŋmaai bihili.

english_verse: “Sir,” Hannah said, “a few years ago I stood here beside you and asked the Lord
translation_verse: Ka Hanna daa yɛli, “N dana, Naawuni dolim’ a nyɛvili.” Ka lan yɛli, “N dana, mani n-nyɛ paɣ’ so ŋun daa ʒe a tooni kpe n-suhiri Yawɛ la.

english_verse: to give me a child. Here he is! The Lord gave me just what I asked for.
translation_verse: Bia ŋɔ ka n daa suhi maa, ka Yawɛ daa deei n suhigu ka shiri ti ma n ni daa suh’ o bɔri shɛli maa.

english_verse: Now I am giving him to the Lord, and he will be the Lord's servant for as long as he lives.” Hannah Prays Elkanah worshiped the Lord there at Shiloh, and
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu n zaŋ o ti Yawɛ. O nyɛla Yawɛ ni yɛn su so hal ni o nyɛvili tariga.” Ka o daa chɛ o ti Yawɛ nimaani.

english_verse: Hannah prayed: You make me strong and happy, Lord. You rescued me. Now I can be glad and laugh at my enemies.
translation_verse: Ka Hanna daa suhi Naawuni yɛli, “Naawuni ti ma suhupiɛlli, ka chɛ ka n nya kpiɔŋ ŋun’ Yawɛ sani. N larila n dimnima, dama m mali suhupiɛlli n nasara dibu puuni.

english_verse: No other god is like you. And with you we are safer than on a high mountain.
translation_verse: “So kani m-be kasi kaman nyin’ Yawɛ, so lan kani m-pah’ a zuɣu. Tampin’ shɛli mi kani m-be kaman nyin’ Yawɛ.

english_verse: I can tell those proud people, “Stop your boasting! Nothing is hidden from the Lord, and he judges what we do.”
translation_verse: Chɛl’ barinyubo yɛtɔɣa tɔɣisibu, ka di lan chɛ ka karimbaan’ yɛtɔɣa yi a nol’ ni na yaha. Dama Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Naawuni ŋɔ mi binshɛɣukam, ka mi daadam ni niŋdi shɛlikam.

english_verse: Our Lord, you break the bows of warriors, but you give strength to everyone who stumbles.
translation_verse: Bɛn mali kpiɔŋ tɔbiri kabisiya, ka ninvuɣ’ gbarima nya yaa.

english_verse: People who once had plenty to eat must now hire themselves out for only a piece of bread. But you give the hungry more than enough to eat. A woman did not have a child, and you gave her seven, but a woman who had many was left with none.
translation_verse: Ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn daa diri tiɣiri zaŋ bɛmaŋ’ pa talima pumpɔŋɔ ni bɛ nya bindirigu di, amaa kum bi lan mali di ni daa mali shɛb’ la yaha. Paɣiŋoo dɔɣi bih’ ayopɔin, ka ŋun daa dɔɣi bihi pam la kɔŋ bihi.

english_verse: You take away life, and you give life. You send people down to the world of the dead and bring them back again.
translation_verse: Yawɛ n-nyɛ ŋun kura, ka lan nyɛ ŋun tiri nyɛvili. Ŋuna n-tahiri niriba kpiimba biɛhigu shee, ka lan neeri ba.

english_verse: Our Lord, you are the one who makes us rich or poor. You put some in high positions and bring disgrace on others.
translation_verse: Yawɛ n-chɛ ka ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ nyɛ nandaamba, ka chɛ ka shɛb’ mi nyɛ bundaannima. Ŋuna n-filindi nira, ŋuna n-lan duhiri nira.

english_verse: You lift the poor and homeless out of the garbage dump and give them places of honor in royal palaces. You set the world on foundations, and they belong to you.
translation_verse: Ŋuna n-yiɣisiri tarimba taŋkpaɣu ni, ka kpuɣiri nandaamba tampuli zuɣu ni o chɛ ka bɛ mini nabihi laɣim ʒini n-di kuɣ’ din mali jilima fali. Dama Yawɛ n-su dunia ŋɔ daantalisi, ka zaŋ dunia ŋɔ n-tam di zuɣu.

english_verse: You protect your loyal people, but everyone who is evil will die in darkness. We cannot win a victory by our own strength.
translation_verse: “O ni gul’ o ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn ʒe o yim, amaa o ni zaŋ ninvuɣ’ biɛri bɛna m-bahi zibisim ni; dama ninsal’ ku tooi di nasara omaŋmaŋ’ yiko ni.

english_verse: Our Lord, those who attack you will be broken in pieces when you fight back with thunder from heaven. You will judge the whole earth and give power and strength to your chosen king. Samuel Stays with Eli
translation_verse: Yawɛ dimnim’ ni chɛrisichɛrisi. Zallakudura Naa ni be alizanda ni ka tahi bɛ zuɣu na. Yawɛ ni kari dunia ŋɔ nim’ zaa saria. O ni ti o naa yaa, ka ti o ninvuɣ’ gahindili yiko.”

english_verse: Elkanah and Hannah went back home to Ramah, but the boy Samuel stayed to help Eli serve the Lord. Eli's Sons
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka Ɛlikana daa lab’ kul’ o ya Rama, ka bia maa daa be Ɛli ŋun daa nyɛ maligumaana maa sani n-tumdi Yawɛ tuma. Ɛli bidibisi

english_verse: Eli's sons were priests, but they were dishonest and refused to obey the Lord. So, while people were boiling the meat from their sacrifices, these priests would send over a servant with a large, three-pronged fork.
translation_verse: Bɛ mi baɣa daa ka maligumaaniba tuma ni nyɛ shɛm zaŋ chaŋ niriba maa sani. So daa yi kɔrigi biŋkɔbigu mali sara n-zaŋ di nimdi maa duɣira, maligumaana yiŋbia zaŋdila dirigu din mali jɛba ata kana

english_verse: The servant would stick the fork into the cooking pot, and whatever meat came out on the fork was taken back to Eli's two sons. That was how they treated every Israelite who came to offer sacrifices in Shiloh.
translation_verse: nti tim nimdi maa ni be ʒɛduɣ’ shɛli ni maa n-kuhi nimdi maa, ka nim’ shɛli din doli dirigu maa yina, maligumaana maa n-su li. Lala ka bɛ daa niŋdi Izraɛlnim’ zaa bɛn daa yi chani Shilo nti maani sara.

english_verse: Sometimes, when people were offering sacrifices, the servant would come over, even before the fat had been cut off and sacrificed to the Lord. Then the servant would tell them, “The priest doesn't want his meat boiled! Give him some raw meat that he can roast!”
translation_verse: Din pahi nyɛla, so daa yi mali sara, ka na bi yihi biŋkpam nyo buɣim, maligumaana yiŋbia kanimina ti yɛl’ o, “Ŋmaam’ nim’ kahili ti ma ka n ti ti maligumaana ka o she, dama o ku deei nin’ duɣirili a sani, naɣila nim’ kahili.”

english_verse: Usually the people answered, “Take what you want. But first, let us sacrifice the fat to the Lord.” “No,” the servant would reply. “If you don't give it to me now, I'll take it by force.”
translation_verse: Ka dilan’ yi yɛl’ o, “Chɛ ka ti zaŋ biŋkpam nyo buɣim pɔi, ka a naanyi ŋmaag’ a ni bɔri shɛm tariga.” O yɛrimi, “Aai, ŋmaam’ ti ma pumpɔŋɔ, di yi pa lala n ni zaŋ kiŋkansi ŋmaai li.”

english_verse: Eli's sons did not show any respect for the sacrifices that the people offered. This was a terrible sin, and it made the Lord very angry. Hannah Visits Samuel
translation_verse: Ka o bihi maa daalahichi daa ti galisi pam Yawɛ sani, dama bɛ daa bi tiri Yawɛ sara maligu pina maa jilima. Samuɛl be Shilo

english_verse: The boy Samuel served the Lord and wore a special linen garment

translation_verse: Yuuni kam o ma daa yi shɛrila binyɛr’ bila m-mali chani ti tir’ o saha shɛl’ o min’ o yidana daa yi ti chaŋ ni bɛ ti mali yuuniyuuni sara maa.

english_verse: Eli always blessed Elkanah and his wife and said, “Samuel was born in answer to your prayers. Now you have given him to the Lord. I pray that the Lord will bless you with more children to take his place.” After Eli had blessed them, Elkanah and Hannah would return home.
translation_verse: Ka Ɛli daa yi suhiri alibarika niŋdi Ɛlikana min’ o paɣ’ maa ni ka yɛri Ɛlikana, “Yawɛ ni chɛ ka a paɣ’ ŋɔ dɔɣi bihi ti a ka bɛ zan’ o ni zaŋ bi so ti ŋun’ Yawɛ ŋɔ zaani.” Di nyaaŋa ka bɛ lan lab’ kuli bɛ ya.

english_verse: The Lord was kind to Hannah, and she had three more sons and two daughters. But Samuel grew up at the Lord's house in Shiloh. Eli Warns His Sons
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa niŋ alibarika niŋ Hanna ni, ka o lan dɔɣi bidibis’ ata mini bipuɣins’ ayi. Ka Samuɛl daa kul be Yawɛ tooni hal ti zooi. Ɛli min’ o bihi

translation_verse: Ninsal’ yi tum o ninsal’ kpee taali, Yawɛ ni tim di sandaani.” Amaa ninsal’ yi tum Yawɛ taali, ŋuni n-lee ni tooi tim di sandaani? Amaa ka bɛ daa zaɣisi bɛ ba yɛligu maa wumbu, dama Yawɛ daa pun lo ni o ni ku ba.

english_verse: Out of all the tribes of Israel, I chose your family to be my priests. I wanted them to offer sacrifices and burn incense to me and to find out from me what I want my people to do. I commanded everyone to bring their sacrifices here where I live, and I allowed you and your family to keep those that were not offered to me on the altar. But you honor your sons instead of me! translation_verse: Ka di chaŋ wula ka a ti zaŋ pulaani kpɛh’ a kɔbili ni m-bɔr’ ni a fa n ni zali ni bɛ mali sara maligu shɛŋa, ka zaŋ sara maligu pin’ shɛŋa zaa na la? english_verse: I am the Lord, the God of Israel. I promised to always let your family serve me as priests, but now I tell you that I cannot do this any longer! I honor anyone who honors me, but I put a curse on anyone who hates me.

translation_verse: Nyama, dabisi’ shɛŋa kanna ka n ni ti mɔŋ a min’ a yab’ yiŋnim’ zaa yaa, ka ninkurigu ti ku be yi daŋ maa ni yaha.

english_verse: If I let anyone from your family be a priest, his life will be full of sadness and sorrow. But most of the men in your family will die a violent death!
translation_verse: N ni ti yɛn chɛ a yiŋ’ ŋɔ ni do’ so ka o be n sara maligu bimbini ŋɔ gbini nyɛla ŋun ti yɛn nya biɛrim o suhu ni, ka kum hal ka o nina ti fulim, ka niriba ti zaŋ takɔbi ku a yiŋnim’ zaa.

english_verse: To prove to you that I will do these things, your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, will die on the same day.
translation_verse: Ka binshɛɣu din ti yɛn niŋ a bidibis’ ayi bɛn nyɛ Hofini mini Finɛhas ti yɛn nyɛla shihirili a sani. Bɛ niriba ayi maa zaa ti yɛn kpila dahin yini.

english_verse: I have chosen someone else to be my priest, someone who will be faithful and obey me. I will always let his family serve as priests and help my chosen king.
translation_verse: Ka n ti pii maligumaana so ŋun ni ʒe ma yim ka tumdi n suhu mini n tɛha ni bɔri shɛlikam zaa; biɛhiŋ kani, n ni ti me o yili ti o, ka o ti be n ninvuɣ’ gahindili sani n-tumdi tuma sahakam.

english_verse: But if anyone is left from your family, he will come to my priest and beg for money or a little bread. He may even say to my priest, “Please let me be a priest, so I will at least have something to eat.”
translation_verse: Ka ŋunkam ti kpalim a yili ŋɔ ni ti chaŋ o sani ti maani bara n-suhir’ o liɣiri bee bɔrɔbɔro kpilli, ka ni ti yɛli, “N suhir’ a, zaŋm’ ma zali maligumaana so zaani din ni chɛ ka n nyari bindirigu dira.”

english_verse: Samuel served the Lord by helping Eli the priest, who was by that time almost blind. In those days, the Lord hardly ever spoke directly to people, and he did not appear to them in dreams very often. But one night, Eli was asleep in his room,

english_verse: The Lord had not spoken to Samuel before, and Samuel did not recognize the voice.

english_verse: When the Lord called out his name for the third time, Samuel went to Eli again and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” Eli finally realized that it was the Lord who was speaking to Samuel.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa lan boli Samuɛl yaha m-pahi buta, ka o lan yiɣisi chaŋ Ɛli sani ti yɛl’ o, “A ni boli ma la, n-nyɛ ma.” Di saha ka Ɛli daa baŋ ni Yawɛ m-booni bia maa,

english_verse: So he said, “Go back and lie down! If someone speaks to you again, answer, ‘I'm listening, Lord. What do you want me to do?’ ” Once again Samuel went back and lay down.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Ɛli daa yɛli Samuɛl, “Cham’ ti dɔni, o yi ti lan bol’ a, nyin’ yɛlima, ‘Yawɛ, yɛlima, a dabili wumda.’ ” Di saha ka Samuɛl daa lan lab’ ti dɔni o dooshee maa.

english_verse: The Lord then stood beside Samuel and called out as he had done before, “Samuel! Samuel!” “I'm listening,” Samuel answered. “What do you want me to do?”
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa lan kana ti zani nimaani m-boon’ o kaman o ni di pun boon’ o shɛm la, “Samuɛl! Samuɛl!” Ka Samuɛl daa garigi yɛli, “Yɛlima, a dabili wumda.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Samuel, I am going to do something in Israel that will shock everyone who hears about it!
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Samuɛl, “Nyama, n yɛn tumla tuun’ shɛli Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ni, ka ŋunkam ti wum li tiba puuni ni chahira.

english_verse: He knew that his sons refused to respect me, and he let them get away with it, even though I said I would punish his family forever.
translation_verse: M pun yɛl’ o ni n ni darig’ o yiŋnim’ tibili hal ni saha din ka bahigu, tuumbiɛ’ shɛli yɛla o ni pun mila zuɣu, dama o bihi mɔri man’ Naawuni ka o bi yihi ba di ni.

english_verse: I warned Eli that sacrifices or offerings could never make things right! His family has done too many disgusting things.

english_verse: The next morning, Samuel got up and opened the doors to the Lord's house. He was afraid to tell Eli what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Ka Samuɛl daa doya hal ka biɛɣu ti neei, ka o yiɣisi yooi Yawɛ jɛmbu duu maa dunoya, ka zɔr’ dabiɛm ni o yɛli Ɛli o ni nya ʒii shɛli maa yɛla.

english_verse: But Eli told him, “Samuel, my boy, come here!” “Yes, sir!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Ɛli daa bol’ o, “M bia Samuɛl.” Ka Samuɛl saɣi, “N-nyɛ ma.”

english_verse: Eli said, “What did God say to you? Tell me everything. I'll ask God to punish you terribly if you don't tell me every word he said!”
translation_verse: Ka Ɛli bɔh’ o, “Wula ka o sa lee yɛl’ a? Di sɔɣ’ ma shɛli, a yi sɔɣ’ ma yɛtɔɣ’ shɛli o ni yɛl’ a shɛlikam maa zaa puuni, Naawuni ŋun’ zaŋm’ o ni di yɛn niŋ ma shɛm maa niŋ a, hal ŋun’ niŋm’ a gari lala gba.”

english_verse: Samuel told Eli everything. Then Eli said, “He is the Lord, and he will do what's right.” The Lord Helps Samuel
translation_verse: Ka Samuɛl daa yɛl’ o binshɛɣukam, ka bi sɔɣ’ o shɛli. Ka Ɛli garigi yɛli, “Ŋuna n-nyɛ Yawɛ, o niŋm’ o ni nya ka shɛli viɛl’ o sani.”

english_verse: As Samuel grew up, the Lord helped him and made everything Samuel said come true.
translation_verse: Ka Samuɛl daa mali hal ti zooi, ka Yawɛ be o sani, ka chɛ ka o yɛtɔɣa zaa nyɛ yɛlimaŋli.

translation_verse: Bɛ daa ku Ɛli bidibis’ ayi bɛn daa nyɛ Hofini mini Finɛhas, ka fa Naawuni Daalikauli Adaka maa. Ɛli kum

english_verse: He went into town and told the news about the battle, and everyone started crying. Eli was afraid that something might happen to the sacred chest. So he was sitting on his chair beside the road, just waiting.

translation_verse: O ni daa kul boli Naawuni Daalikauli Adaka maa yuli maa, ka Ɛli dii yi o kuɣ’ maa zuɣu n-lɛb’ lu o kpali zuɣu ha dunɔdali maa gbini, ka o nyiŋgoli kabi ka o kpi, dama o daa kurigiya pam, ka lan nyɛ niŋgbuŋ titalilana. english_verse: But early the next morning, it had fallen over again and was lying facedown on the floor in front of the chest. The body of the statue was still in one piece, but its head and both hands had broken off and were lying on the stone floor in the doorway.

english_verse: This is why the priests and everyone else step over that part of the doorway when they enter the temple of Dagon in Ashdod.
translation_verse: Lala zuɣu ka Dagɔn tindaannim’ mini Ashidɔdnim’ bɛn zaa yɛn kpe Dagɔn duu maa ni bi lan tamdi di dunɔbia zuɣu kpɛri hal ni zuŋɔ.

english_verse: The Lord caused a lot of trouble for the people of Ashdod and their neighbors. He made sores break out all over their bodies, and everyone was in a panic.

english_verse: The people of Ashdod invited all the Philistine rulers to come to Ashdod, and they asked them, “What can we do with the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel?” “Send it to Gath,” the rulers answered. But after they took it there,
translation_verse: Di saha ka bɛ daa tim boli Filistia nanim’ zaa na nti bɔhi ba, “Wula ka ti lee yɛn niŋ Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni Daalikauli Adaka ŋɔ?” Ka bɛ garigi yɛli, “Chɛliya ka ti zaŋ Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni Daalikauli Adaka maa tahi Gaat.” Di saha ka bɛ daa zaŋ Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni Daalikauli Adaka maa tahi nimaani.

english_verse: so they sent the sacred chest to Ekron. But before they could take it through the town gates, the people of Ekron started screaming, “They've brought the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel! It will kill us and our families too!” The Philistines Send Back the Sacred Chest
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa zaŋ Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni Daalikauli Adaka maa tahi Ɛkurɔn. Amaa Naawuni Daalikauli Adaka maa ni daa paai Ɛkurɔn na, ka Ɛkurɔnnim’ daa kuhi yɛli, “Bɛ zaŋ Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni Daalikauli Adaka la tahi ti ya ŋɔ na ni di ti ku ti mini ti niriba.”

english_verse: The people of Ekron called for another meeting of the Philistine rulers and told them, “Send this chest back where it belongs. Then it won't kill us.” Everyone was in a panic, because God was causing a lot of people to die,
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka bɛ daa tim boli Filistia nanim’ zaa na ti yɛli ba, “Zaŋmiya Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni Daalikauli Adaka maa labisi di biɛhigu shee, ka di chɛliya ka di ku ti mini ti niriba.” Tiŋ’ maa nim’ zaa suhu daa saɣimmi, dama Naawuni daa darigi bɛ tibili n-chɛ ka alɔbo lu bɛ zuɣu ku ba pam.

english_verse: and those who had survived were suffering from the sores. They all cried to their gods for help.
translation_verse: Ka bintɔra daa tɔri ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn bi kpi mi, ka tiŋ’ maa nim’ daa kum pam.

english_verse: After the sacred chest had been in Philistia for seven months,
translation_verse: Yawɛ Daalikauli Adaka maa daa be Filistianim’ tiŋgbɔŋ ni la chira ayopɔin.

english_verse: the Philistines called in their priests and fortunetellers, and asked, “What should we do with this sacred chest? Tell us how to send it back where it belongs!”
translation_verse: Ka Filistianim’ daa ti tim boli tindaannim’ mini laasabuniŋdiba na ti bɔhi ba, “Wula ka ti lee yɛn niŋ Izraɛlnim’ Yawɛ Daalikauli Adaka ŋɔ? Ka ti yi yɛn zaŋ li labisi di biɛhigu shee, bɔ ka ti lee yɛn zaŋ pahi di zuɣu labisi?”

english_verse: “Don't send it back without a gift,” the priests and fortunetellers answered. “Send along something to Israel's God to make up for taking the chest in the first place. Then you will be healed, and you will find out why the Lord was causing you so much trouble.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yɛli ba, “Yi yi yɛn zaŋ Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni Daalikauli Adaka maa labisi, yin’ di zaŋya di kɔŋko labisi, amaa yin’ zaŋmiya alahichi sanyoo pini m-pahi di zuɣu din ni chɛ ka yi nya faako ka baŋ o ni darigiri yi tibili daliri shɛli zuɣu maa.”

english_verse: “What should we send?” the Philistines asked. The priests and fortunetellers answered: There are five Philistine rulers, and they all have the same disease that you have.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa bɔhi, “Bɔ n-lee nyɛ alahichi sanyoo pini ka ti yɛn zaŋ pahi ti ti o?” Ka bɛ daa yɛli ba, “Salima alɔbo diba anu mini salima jɛŋgbaris’ anu kaman yi tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni nanim’ kalinli ni nyɛ shɛm. Dama alɔbo yini maa n-daa lu yi mini yi nanim’ maa zaa zuɣu.

english_verse: So make five gold models of the sores and five gold models of the rats that are wiping out your crops. If you honor the God of Israel with this gift, maybe he will stop causing trouble for you and your gods and your crops.
translation_verse: Di simdi ka yi niŋ alɔbo shɛŋa mini jɛŋgbar’ shɛb’ bɛn bahi yi tiŋgbani ŋɔ yoli maa kɔtomsi, ka di lan simdi ni yi ti Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni maa jilima, di pa shɛli o ku lan darigi yi mini yi buɣa ni yi tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ tibili yaha.

english_verse: Don't be like the Egyptians and their king. They were stubborn, but when Israel's God was finished with them, they had to let Israel go.
translation_verse: Bɔzuɣu ka yi yɛn niŋ tipawumli kaman Ijiptinim’ mini Firawuna ni daa niŋ tipawumli shɛm la? O ni daa chɛ ka bɛ tum jɛrilim la nyaaŋa, pa bɛmaŋmaŋa n-daa ti chɛ ka niriba maa chaŋ?

english_verse: Get a new cart and two cows that have young calves and that have never pulled a cart. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take the calves back to their barn.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ malimiya tɔroko palli, ka bo niɣ’ ayi bɛn bihi na mɔɣira, ka nyɛ bɛ ni ʒi n-zaŋ dapuhi ga shɛba nti zaŋ tɔroko maa ga ba, amaa ka taɣiya bɛ bihi kuli yiŋ’ ka chɛ ba.

english_verse: Then put the chest on the cart. Put the gold rats and sores into a bag and put it on the cart next to the chest. Then send it on its way.
translation_verse: Ka zaŋya Yawɛ Daalikauli Adaka maa niŋ tɔroko maa ni, ka zaŋ salima binyara din nyɛ yi daalahichi sanyoo pini la zali baɣili di luɣili ni n-daai li bahi n-chɛ ka di chaŋ di ni bɔri shɛli polo.

english_verse: Watch to see if the chest goes on up the road to the Israelite town of Beth-Shemesh. If it goes back to its own country, you will know that it was the Lord who made us suffer so badly. But if the chest doesn't go back to its own country, then the Lord had nothing to do with the disease that hit us—it was simply bad luck.
translation_verse: Ka yi yuuni li n-nya di ni yɛn kpa shɛli polo. Di yi kpala dimaŋmaŋ’ ya Bɛtishɛmɛshi polo, yin’ baŋmiya ni ŋuna n-tum ti barina titaŋa ŋɔ zaa, amaa di yi bi kpa ni polo, ti lan baŋ ni o nuu ka ti daalɔbo maa ni, amaa di kul nyɛla din lu ti zuɣu dimaŋmaŋa.”

english_verse: The Philistines followed their advice. They hitched up the two cows to the cart, but they kept their calves in a barn.
translation_verse: Ka niriba maa daa niŋ lala, ka daa bo niɣ’ ayi bɛn bihi na mɔɣiri na nti zaŋ tɔroko maa ga ba, ka zaŋ naɣibihi maa niŋ duu n-yo ba niŋ di ni.

english_verse: Then they put the chest on the cart, along with the bag that had the gold rats and sores in it.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa zaŋ Yawɛ Daalikauli Adaka maa niŋ di puuni, ka zaŋ salima jɛŋgbaris’ adaka mini alɔbo kɔtomsi la niŋ di ni.

english_verse: The cows went straight up the road toward Beth-Shemesh, mooing as they went. The Philistine rulers followed them until they got close to Beth-Shemesh.
translation_verse: Ka niɣi maa daa dii zaŋ li lu solɔɣu n-kpa Bɛtishɛmɛshi polo, bɛ daa bi birigi kpa nudirigu polo bee nuzaa polo, bɛ daa kul chanimi ka kuhira. Ka Filistia nanim’ daa dol’ ba hal ni Bɛtishɛmɛshi tintariga.

english_verse: The people of Beth-Shemesh were harvesting their wheat in the valley. When they looked up and saw the chest, they were so happy that they stopped working and started celebrating.
translation_verse: Di saha Bɛtishɛmɛshinim’ daa bela vinvamli ni n-chɛri alikama, bɛ ni daa ti kpuɣi bɛ zuɣuri lihi nya Naawuni Daalikauli Adaka maa ka di niŋ ba suhupiɛlli.

english_verse: The cows left the road and pulled the cart into a field that belonged to Joshua from Beth-Shemesh, and they stopped beside a huge rock. Some men from the tribe of Levi were there. So they took the chest off the cart and placed it on the rock, and then they did the same thing with the bag of gold rats and sores. A few other people chopped up the cart and made a fire. They killed the cows and burned them as sacrifices to the Lord. After that, they offered more sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ka Lɛvinim’ daa kpuɣi Yawɛ Daalikauli Adaka maa mini adaka shɛli din daa pahi di zuɣu ka salima binyara be di ni la n-zaŋ li ti tam kuɣ’ titali maa zuɣu, ka Bɛtishɛmɛshinim’ zaŋ binyara nyo buɣim m-mali sara. Ka daa lan mali sara maligu shɛŋa ti Yawɛ dindali maa.

english_verse: When the five rulers of the Philistines saw what had happened, they went back to Ekron that same day.
translation_verse: Ka Filistia nanim’ anu maa ni daa nya lala maa, ka bɛ lab’ kul Ɛkurɔn dindali maa.

english_verse: That is how the Philistines sent gifts to the Lord to make up for taking the sacred chest. They sent five gold sores, one each for their towns of Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron.
translation_verse: Filistianim’ ni daa zaŋ bintɔra kɔtomsi salima din nyɛ alahichi sanyoo pini m-pahi ti ti Yawɛ la zaɣ’ yini daa nyɛla Ashidɔdnim’ dini, ka yini nyɛ Gazanim’ dini, ka yini nyɛ Ashikɛlɔnnim’ dini, ka yini nyɛ Gaatinim’ dini, ka yini mi nyɛ Ɛkurɔn nim’ dini.

english_verse: They also sent one gold rat for each walled town and for every village that the five Philistine rulers controlled. The huge stone where the Levites set the chest is still there in Joshua's field as a reminder of what happened. The Sacred Chest Is Sent to Kiriath-Jearim
translation_verse: Lala n-daa nyɛ salima jɛŋgbarisi la gba kaman Filistia nanim’ maa ni daa su fɔntiŋ’ kar’ shɛŋa bɛ ni daa me goondahi gili kalinli ni daa nyɛ shɛm zaŋ tabili tiŋkpansi din daa ka goma. Bɛ ni daa zaŋ Yawɛ Daalikauli Adaka maa tam kuɣ’ tital’ shɛli zuɣu maa na kul beni hal ni zuŋɔ n-nyɛ din daa niŋ Bɛtishɛmɛshi Jɔshua puu ni la shɛhira.

english_verse: and they started saying, “No other God is like the Lord! Who can go near him and stay alive? We'll have to send the chest away from here. But where can we send it?”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Bɛtishɛmɛshinim’ maa daa yɛli, “Ŋuni n-lee ni tooi zani Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Naawuni ŋun be kasi ŋɔ tooni? Ka o yi yi ti sani, banim’ sani ka o lee yɛn chaŋ?”

english_verse: They sent messengers to tell the people of Kiriath-Jearim, “The Philistines have sent back the sacred chest. Why don't you take it and keep it there with you?”
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka bɛ daa tim tuumba Kiriatijiarimnim’ sani ti yɛli ba, “Filistianim’ labisi Yawɛ Daalikauli Adaka la na, kamiyana ti kpuɣi li.”

english_verse: The people of Kiriath-Jearim got the chest and took it to Abinadab's house, which was on a hill in their town. They chose his son Eleazar to take care of it,
translation_verse: Ka Kiriatijiarimnim’ maa daa kana ti kpuɣi Yawɛ Daalikauli Adaka maa n-kuli ti zaŋ li tahi do’ so ŋun yuli daa booni Abinadab ka o yili be daboli zuɣu la yiŋa. Ka bɛ daa piig’ o bia Ɛliɛza ni o yuuni Yawɛ Daalikauli Adaka maa. Samuɛl ni su Izraɛlnim’ shɛm

english_verse: One day, Samuel told all the people of Israel, “If you really want to turn back to the Lord, then prove it. Get rid of your foreign idols, including the ones of the goddess Astarte. Turn to the Lord with all your heart and worship only him. Then he will rescue you from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Samuɛl daa yɛli Izraɛlnim’ zaa, “Yi yi ni ŋmaligi labi Yawɛ sani ni yi suhuri zaa, dindina yin’ yihimiya tinzun buɣa la zaa n-tabili buɣ’ shɛli din yuli booni Ashitarɔt la yi kɔbili ni, ka zaŋ yimaŋ’ zaa ti Yawɛ n-jɛmd’ o kɔŋko, ka o fan ya Filistianim’ nuu ni bahi.”

english_verse: The people got rid of their idols of Baal and Astarte and began worshiping only the Lord.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa zaŋ buɣ’ shɛŋa din daa be bɛ sani ka bɛ booni li Baalnim’ la mini buɣili Ashitarɔt labi, ka jɛmdila Yawɛ kɔŋko.

english_verse: Then Samuel said, “Tell everyone in Israel to meet together at Mizpah, and I will pray to the Lord for you.”
translation_verse: Ka Samuɛl daa yɛli ba, “Laɣimmiya Izraɛlnim’ zaa Mizipa ka n ti suhi Yawɛ tin ya.”

english_verse: The Israelites met together at Mizpah with Samuel as their leader. They drew water from the well and poured it out as an offering to the Lord. On that same day they went without eating to show their sorrow, and they confessed they had been unfaithful to the Lord. The Philistines Attack Israel
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa laɣim Mizipa n-tooi kom booi bahi Yawɛ tooni nimaani ka lo noli dindali maa ka yɛli, “Ti tum alahichi Yawɛ sani.” Ka Samuɛl daa nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ zuɣulana Mizipa maa.

english_verse: When the Philistine rulers found out about the meeting at Mizpah, they sent an army there to attack the people of Israel. The Israelites were afraid when they heard that the Philistines were coming.
translation_verse: Filistianim’ ni daa wum ni Izraɛlnim’ laɣimla Mizipa, ka bɛ nanim’ daa lo tɔbu n-chaŋ ni bɛ ti tuhi ba. Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa wum li ka dabiɛm gbahi ba.

english_verse: “Don't stop praying!” they told Samuel. “Ask the Lord our God to rescue us.”
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ maa daa yɛli Samuɛl, “Kul suhimi Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ ti Naawuni ŋɔ tim’ ti, ka o fa ti Filistianim’ ŋɔ nuu ni bahi.”

english_verse: Samuel begged the Lord to rescue Israel, then he sacrificed a young lamb to the Lord. Samuel had not even finished offering the sacrifice when the Philistines started to attack. But the Lord answered his prayer and made thunder crash all around them. The Philistines panicked and ran away.
translation_verse: Samuɛl ni daa na maani sara maa ka Filistianim’ maa vu m-mirina ni bɛ ti liri Izraɛlnima; amaa ka Yawɛ kukoli daa tahi pam dindali maa m-birim Filistianim’ maa ka bɛ ŋmaligi guui ka chɛ Izraɛlnima.

english_verse: The men of Israel left Mizpah and went after them as far as the hillside below Beth-Car, killing every enemy soldier they caught.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ maa daa dii yi Mizipa na n-kar’ doli Filistianim’ maa n-kuri ba hal ti miri Bɛtikar.

english_verse: The Philistines were so badly beaten that it was quite a while before they attacked Israel again. After the battle, Samuel set up a monument between Mizpah and the rocky cliffs. He named it “Help Monument” to remind Israel how much the Lord had helped them. For as long as Samuel lived, the Lord helped Israel fight the Philistines.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa nyaŋ Filistianim’ maa, ka bɛ daa bi lan buɣisi ni bɛ liri ba bɛ tiŋgbani maa ni yaha, ka Yawɛ daa kul darigiri Filistianim’ maa tibili Samuɛl ʒiɛmani maa ni zaa.

english_verse: The Israelites were even able to recapture their towns and territory between Ekron and Gath. Israel was also at peace with the Amorites. Samuel Is a Leader in Israel
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa lan deei Filistianim’ ni daa tuhi fa tiŋ’ shɛŋa bɛ sani zaa. Ɛkurɔn zaŋ hal ti kpa Gaat, bɛ daa fa bɛ tiŋgbana zaa Filistianim’ sani. Ka suhudoo daa lan niŋ bɛn’ Izraɛlnim’ maa mini Amɔrinim’ sunsuuni.

english_verse: Samuel was a leader in Israel all his life.
translation_verse: Ka Samuɛl daa niŋ Izraɛl zuɣulana hal ni o nyɛvili tariga.

english_verse: Every year he would go around to the towns of Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah where he served as judge for the people.
translation_verse: O daa gindila Bɛtɛl mini Giligal ni Mizipa yuuni kam nti maani Izraɛlnim’ yɛla nimaani zaa.

english_verse: Then he would go back to his home in Ramah and do the same thing there. He also had an altar built for the Lord at Ramah.
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka o lab’ kuli o ya Rama. Ŋuna n-daa lan maani Izraɛlnim’ yɛla nimaani gba. O daa lan me sara maligu bimbini nimaani ti Yawɛ.

english_verse: Samuel had two sons. The older one was Joel, and the younger one was Abijah. When Samuel was getting old, he let them be leaders at Beersheba.
translation_verse: O bidib’ kpɛm’ sani yuli daa boonila Joɛl, ka ŋun paya mi yuli booni Abija; Bɛ daa nyɛla Bɛrishiiba zuɣulaannima.

english_verse: But they were not like their father. They were dishonest and accepted bribes to give unfair decisions.
translation_verse: Amaa o bihi maa bɛn daa bi dol’ o naba, ka zaŋ bɛ zaŋsim niŋla bun’ ni, ka deeri birapu niriba sani, ka bi doli yɛlimaŋli soli maani bɛ yɛla.

english_verse: One day the nation's leaders came to Samuel at Ramah
translation_verse: Di saha ka Izraɛl kpamba zaa daa laɣim taba n-chaŋ Samuɛl sani Rama

english_verse: and said, “You are an old man. You set a good example for your sons, but they haven't followed it. Now we want a king to be our leader, just like all the other nations. Choose one for us!”
translation_verse: nti yɛl’ o, “Nyama, pumpɔŋɔ a kurigiya, ka a bihi ŋɔ mi bi dol’ a naba, dinzuɣu bom’ naa ti ti ka o su ti kaman zuliya kam ni mali nanim’ shɛm ŋɔ.”

english_verse: Samuel was upset to hear the leaders say they wanted a king, so he prayed about it.
translation_verse: Amaa bɛ ni daa yɛli Samuɛl, “Tim’ ti naa ka o su ti maa,” di daa bi palig’ o suhu; ka o daa suhi Yawɛ.

english_verse: The Lord answered: Samuel, do everything they want you to do. I am really the one they have rejected as their king.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ yɛl’ o, “Wummi niriba maa ni yɛl’ a shɛlikam maa zaa, dama pa nyini ka bɛ zaɣisi, amaa mani ka bɛ zaɣisi ni n di lan nyɛ bɛ naa maa.

english_verse: Ever since the day I rescued my people from Egypt, they have turned from me to worship idols. Now they are turning away from you.
translation_verse: Saha shɛli n ni daa yihi ba Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ni na hal ni zuŋɔ, bɛ tuma zaa kul wuhirila lala, bɛ zaɣisi ma ka jɛmdila buɣa, lala ka bɛ niŋd’ a gba maa.

english_verse: Do everything they ask, but warn them and tell them how a king will treat them.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ wummi bɛ ni yɛli shɛm maa, amaa lee kpahimi bɛ zuɣu ni, ka wuhi ba na’ so ŋun ti yɛn su ba biɛhigu ni ti yɛn nyɛ shɛm bɛ sani.”

english_verse: Samuel told the people who were asking for a king what the Lord had said:
translation_verse: Ka Samuɛl daa yɛli ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn zaa daa yɛl’ o ni o bom’ naa ti ba maa Yawɛ ni yɛli shɛm zaa.

english_verse: If you have a king, this is how he will treat you. He will force your sons to join his army. Some of them will ride in his chariots, some will serve in the cavalry, and others will run ahead of his own chariot.
translation_verse: O daa yɛli ba, “Na’ so ŋun ti yɛn sun ya biɛhigu ni ti yɛn nyɛ shɛm yi sani m-bɔŋɔ, o ni ti zaŋ yi bidibisi niŋ chɛchɛbumbariba mini wɔribariba, ka bɛ be o chɛchɛbuŋ’ tooni.

english_verse: Your daughters will have to make perfume or do his cooking and baking.
translation_verse: O ni ti zaŋ yi bipuɣinsi leeg o tulaalɛmaaniba min’ o bindir’ duɣiriba ni o bɔrɔbɔro shɛriba.

english_verse: The king will take your best fields, as well as your vineyards, and olive orchards and give them to his own officials.
translation_verse: O ni ti fa yi puri mini yi wain tihi ni yi Olivi tihi puri zaa din mali vuhim n-zaŋ ti o tumtumdiba.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your grain and grapes and give it to his officers and officials.
translation_verse: O ni ti deei yi bindira mini yi wain tihi wala pirigibu bupia kam puuni vaabu yim ti o kpambaliba min’ o tumtumdiba.

english_verse: The king will take your slaves and your best young men and your donkeys and make them do his work.
translation_verse: O ni ti fa yi tumtumdi’ dɔbba mini paɣiba, ka deei yi naɣ’ viɛla mini yi bun’ viɛla zaa ka bɛ tumd’ o tuma.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your sheep and goats. You will become the king's slaves,
translation_verse: O ni ti yihi biŋkɔb’ yino yi biŋkɔbiri pia kam puuni ka yi ti leeg’ o daba.

english_verse: and you will finally cry out for the Lord to save you from the king you wanted. But the Lord won't answer your prayers.
translation_verse: Di saha maa, yi ni ti fabili pam yi ni pii na’ so maa zuɣu, amaa ka Yawɛ ti ku garigi ya dindali maa.”

english_verse: The people would not listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We want to be like other nations. We want a king to rule us and lead us in battle.”
translation_verse: Ka ti gba biɛhigu ŋmani zuliya shɛb’ biɛhigu, ti naa maa ni su ti, ka ni yina n-gari tooni zaŋ ti tuhi tɔb’ kam.”

english_verse: Samuel listened to them and then told the Lord exactly what they had said.
translation_verse: Samuɛl ni daa wum niriba maa yɛligu maa, ka o gba daa lan zaŋ li yɛli Yawɛ.

english_verse: “Do what they want,” the Lord answered. “Give them a king.” Samuel told the people to go back to their homes.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ yɛli Samuɛl, “Wummi bɛ ni yɛli shɛm maa, ka bo naa ti ba.” Di saha ka Samuɛl daa yɛli Izraɛlnim’ maa, “Sokam labimi kul’ o ya.”

english_verse: Kish was a wealthy man who belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. His father was Abiel, his grandfather was Zeror, his great-grandfather was Becorath, and his great-great-grandfather was Aphiah.
translation_verse: Bɛnjamin zuliya ni do’ so daa beni ka o yuli booni Kish, o daa nyɛla Abiɛl bia, ka Abiɛl mi nyɛ Zɛro bia, ka Zɛro nyɛ Bɛkɔrat bia, ka Bɛkɔrat mi daa nyɛ Afia ŋun daa nyɛ Bɛnjamin zuliya ni nir’ la bia, o daa mali buni pam.

english_verse: Kish had a son named Saul, who was better looking and more than a head taller than anyone else in all Israel.
translation_verse: O daa mali bidibiga ka o yuli booni Sool, O daa nyɛla nachimbil’ viɛlli. Do’ so daa ka Izraɛl n-viɛl’ gar’ o; ka o daa lan wɔɣ’ gari sokam.

english_verse: Kish owned some donkeys, but they had run off. So he told Saul, “Take one of the servants and go look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Ka Sool ba Kish bunsi daa ti bɔrigi dahin’ shɛli ka o yɛl’ o bia Sool, “Zaŋmi tumtumdiba ŋɔ ni yino pah’ amaŋ’ zuɣu ka yi chaŋ ti bo bunsi maa shee.”

english_verse: Saul and the servant went through the hill country of Ephraim and the territory of Shalishah, but they could not find the donkeys. Then they went through the territories of Shaalim and Benjamin, but still there was no sign of the donkeys.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yiɣisi chaŋ hal ti paai zoya ni tin’ shɛli din yuli booni Ifriim n-zaŋ gari Shalisha tiŋgbɔŋ ni nti bi nya ba, ka zaŋ gari Shaalim ka bɛ ti ka nimaani. Di saha ka bɛ daa lan zaŋ gari Bɛnjamin tiŋgban’ ni nti bi nya ba.

english_verse: Finally they came to the territory where the clan of Zuph lived. “Let's go back home,” Saul told his servant. “If we don't go back soon, my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us!”
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa ti paai Zuf, ka Sool daa yɛl’ o tumtumda so ŋun daa be o sani maa, “Kamina ka ti lab’ kuli, di yi pa lala m ba ni chɛ bunsi ŋɔ yɛla tɛhibu ka kpalim tɛhirila ti yɛla.”

english_verse: “Wait!” the servant answered. “There's a man of God who lives in a town near here. He's amazing! Everything he says comes true. Let's talk to him. Maybe he can tell us where to look.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka o tumtumda maa daa yɛl’ o, “Nyama, Naawuni ninvuɣ’ gahindili be tiŋ’ ŋɔ ni ka bɛ tir’ o jilima pam. O yɛligu bi yiɣisira. Chɛ ka ti chaŋ o sani, di pa shɛli o ni tooi wuhi ti ti chandi ŋɔ ni yɛn nyɛ shɛm.”

english_verse: Saul said, “How can we talk to the prophet when I don't have anything to give him? We don't even have any bread left in our sacks. What can we give him?”
translation_verse: Ka Sool daa bɔh’ o tumtumda maa, “Ti yi chaŋ bɔ ka ti lee yɛn ti o? Dama ti lan ka bindirigu ti koligu ŋɔ ni bee bɔ ka ti lee mali? Ti ka pin’ shɛli din ni ti Naawuni nir’ maa.”

english_verse: “I have a small piece of silver,” the servant answered. “We can give him that, and then he will tell us where to look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Ka tumtumda maa garigi yɛli Sool, “M mali anzinfa laɣifu kpe, n ni zaŋ li ti Naawuni nir’ maa ka o wuhi ti ti ni yɛn doli so’ shɛli.”

english_verse: “Great!” Saul replied. “Let's go to the man who can see visions!” He said this because in those days God would answer questions by giving visions to prophets. Saul and his servant went to the town where the prophet lived.
translation_verse: Ka Sool daa yɛli, “Mbo, di viɛla, garim’ ka ti chaŋ.” Ka bɛ daa chaŋ Naawuni nir’ maa ni daa be tiŋ’ maa ni luɣ’ shɛli maa.

english_verse: As they were going up the hill to the town, they met some young women coming out to get water, and the two men said to them, “We're looking for the man who can see visions. Is he in town?”
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa duri daboli n-kpɛri tiŋ’ maa ni, ka bɛ daa tuhi’ paɣisara soli ka bɛ chani kuliga, ka bɛ bɔhi ba, “Ŋun nyari niriba yɛla la beni?”

english_verse: “Yes, he is,” they replied. “He's in town today because there's going to be a sacrifice and a sacred meal at the place of worship. In fact, he's just ahead of you. Hurry
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yɛli, “O beni,” ka lan yɛli, “Nyamiya, ŋuna kul be yi tooni chani maa ha; kpaŋ chamiya, pumpɔŋɔ ka o na yoli paana, dama bɛ yɛn malila sara daboli zuɣu zuŋɔ.

english_verse: and you should find him right inside the town gate. He's on his way out to the place of worship to eat with the invited guests. They can't start eating until he blesses the sacrifice. If you go now, you should find him.”
translation_verse: Yi yi kul kpe tiŋ’ maa puuni, yi ni nya o pɔi ka o naanyi chaŋ chuɣu maa ni daboli maa zuɣu, dama o yi bi chaŋ niriba maa ku di bindirigu; ŋuna n-yɛn suhi alibarika niŋ sara maligu maa ni, di nyaaŋa ka bɛnkam beni naanyi di. Dinzuɣu chamiya pumpɔŋɔ, yi ni nya o yomyom.”

english_verse: They went to the town, and just as they were going through the gate, Samuel was coming out on his way to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa du n-kpe tiŋ’ maa ni. Bɛ ni daa kpɛri tiŋ’ maa ni, ka bɛ nya Samuɛl ka o yiri ni o chaŋ sara maligu daboli maa zuɣu.

english_verse: The day before Saul came, the Lord had told Samuel,
translation_verse: Sool chandi maa dazɔhigu dali, Yawɛ daa pun daŋ kahigi wuhi Samuɛl yɛli,

english_verse: “I've seen how my people are suffering, and I've heard their call for help. About this time tomorrow I'll send you a man from the tribe of Benjamin, who will rescue my people from the Philistines. I want you to pour olive oil on his head to show that he will be their leader.”
translation_verse: “Biɛɣuni ŋ-ŋɔ tasaha, n sa ni yihi nachimbil’ Bɛnjamin tiŋgban’ ni n-tim o a sanna, ka a ti booi nam kpam bah’ o zuɣu ni ka o leei n niriba Izraɛlnim’ naa. O ni ti tiligi n niriba Filistianim’ nuu ni, dama n nya n niriba maa ni diri wahala shɛli, ka wum bɛ fabila.”

english_verse: Samuel looked at Saul, and the Lord told Samuel, “This is the man I told you about. He's the one who will rule Israel.”
translation_verse: Samuɛl ni daa nya Sool’ maa, ka Yawɛ yɛl’ o, “N ni sa yɛl’ a ninvuɣ’ so yɛla la m-bala, Ŋuna n-yɛn su n niriba maa.”

english_verse: Saul went over to Samuel in the gateway and said, “A man who can see visions lives here in town. Could you tell me the way to his house?”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Sool daa chaŋ Samuɛl sani tiŋ’ maa gooni dunol’ ni nti yɛl’ o, “Wuhim ma ŋun nyari niriba yɛla la yiŋa.”

english_verse: “I am the one who sees visions!” Samuel answered. “Go on up to the place of worship. You will eat with me today, and in the morning I'll answer your questions.
translation_verse: Ka Samuɛl yɛl’ o, “Mani n-nyɛ nyar’ maa, daŋmi n tooni chaŋ daboli ŋɔ zuɣu, dama zuŋɔ m min’ a ni laɣim di bindirigu, ka n sa yɛl’ a din be a zuɣu ni biɛɣuni asiba ka chɛ ka a kuli.

english_verse: Don't worry about your donkeys that ran off three days ago. They've already been found. Everything of value in Israel now belongs to you and your family.”
translation_verse: Di yi nyɛla yi bun’ shɛb’ bɛn bɔrigi zuŋɔ daba ata la bɛna, di lan chɛ ka bɛ yɛla muɣis’ a, dama bɛ nya ba. Ka ŋuni ka Izraɛlnim’ zaa lee yuuni bɔra? Pa a min’ a zuliya zaa?”

english_verse: “Why are you telling me this?” Saul asked. “I'm from Benjamin, the smallest tribe in Israel, and my clan is the least important in the tribe.” Saul Eats with Samuel and Stays at His House
translation_verse: Ka Sool yɛl’ o, “Pa Bɛnjamin zuliya din pɔri gari Izraɛl zuliyanim’ zaa la ni nira n-nyɛ ma? Pa n yiŋnim’ m-pɔri gari sokam Bɛnjamin zuliya maa ni? Ka wula ka a ti tɔɣisiri ma yɛtɔɣa ŋɔ?”

english_verse: Then Samuel told the cook, “I gave you the best piece of meat and told you to set it aside. Bring it here now.” The cook brought the meat over and set it down in front of Saul. “This is for you,” Samuel told him. “Go ahead and eat it. I had this piece saved especially for you, and I invited these guests to eat with you.” After Saul and Samuel had finished eating,
translation_verse: Di saha ka ŋun daa duɣi bindirigu maa daa zaŋ biŋgbalipaɣ’ nimpuɣili ni din pahi di zuɣu na nti zali Sool tooni. Ka Samuɛl yɛl’ o, “Nyama, ti ni di zaŋ shɛli zali maa n-ʒe a tooni maa. Ŋubimi li, dama nyini ka ti di zaŋ li zali gu hal ni pumpɔŋɔ ŋɔ ni di chɛ ka a mini saamba ŋɔ laɣim di.” Ka Sool mini Samuɛl daa laɣim di dindali maa.

english_verse: they went down from the place of worship and back into town. A bed was set up for Saul on the flat roof of Samuel's house,
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa yi daboli maa zuɣu kuli yiŋa, ka bɛ daa zaŋ bindoo n-du pii zuɣu ti yɛrigi sɔŋ Sool, ka o daa dɔni nimaani gbihi. Samuɛl booi nam leebu kpam bahi Sool zuɣu ni ka o leei naa

english_verse: and Saul slept there. About sunrise the next morning, Samuel called up to Saul on the roof, “Time to get up! I'll help you get started on your way.” Saul got up. He and Samuel left together
translation_verse: Nolɔɣu kukoli saha ka Samuɛl daa ti boli Sool pii maa zuɣu yɛl’ o, “Yiɣisim’ ka m biɛl’ a zali soli.” Ka Sool yiɣisi ka o mini Samuɛl daa lu soli.

english_verse: and had almost reached the edge of town when Samuel stopped and said, “Tell your servant go on. Stay here with me for a few minutes, and I'll tell you what God has told me.” Samuel Tells Saul He Will Be King After the servant had gone,
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa ti yiri tiŋ’ maa tariga, ka Samuɛl yɛli Sool, “Yɛlim’ a tumtumda maa ni o cham’ ti tooni, o yi chaŋ naai nyin’ zanim’ kpe biɛla, ka n yɛl’ a Naawuni ni yɛli shɛm.”

english_verse: When you leave me today, you'll meet two men near Rachel's tomb at Zelzah in the territory of Benjamin. They'll tell you, “The donkeys you've been looking for have been found. Your father has forgotten about them, and now he's worrying about you! He's wondering how he can find you.”
translation_verse: A yi yi n sani zuŋɔ kuna, a ni tuhi niriba ayi soli Reechɛl gballi din be Zɛliza, Bɛnjamin tiŋgban’ ni la gbini ka bɛ yɛl’ a, ‘Yi ni daa yi n-chaŋ ni yi ti bo bun’ shɛb’ shee la, ti nya ba. Ka pumpɔŋɔ bɛ yɛla bi lan muɣis’ a ba, a yɛla n-kpalim muɣis’ o. Ka o kul yɛra, “Ka wula ka n yɛn niŋ zaŋ chaŋ m bia ŋɔ polo?” ’

english_verse: Go on from there until you reach the big oak tree at Tabor, where you'll meet three men on their way to worship God at Bethel. One of them will be leading three young goats, another will be carrying three round loaves of bread, and the last one will be carrying a clay jar of wine.
translation_verse: Di saha, a yi yi nimaani n-chaŋ ti paai Tabo oki tia la gbini, a ni tuhi niriba ata soli ka bɛ chani Bɛtɛl Naawuni sani ni bɛ ti mali sara. Bɛ ni yino ni ti vɔri bubih’ ata, ka yino gbibi bɔrɔbɔro kpil’ ata, ka ŋun’ la mi nyaɣiri wain koligu pali.

english_verse: After they greet you, they'll give you two loaves of bread.
translation_verse: Bɛ ni ti puh’ a ka ti a bɔrɔbɔro kpil’ ayi, ka a deei li bɛ nuu ni.

english_verse: Next, go to Gibeah, where the Philistines have an army camp. As you're going into the town, you'll meet a group of prophets coming down from the place of worship. They'll be going along prophesying while others are walking in front of them, playing small harps, small drums, and flutes.
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka a yi nimaani nti paai Naawuni zoli din be Gibia Filistia tɔbbihi ni be shɛl’ la. A yi yi nimaani nti yɛn kpe tiŋ’ puuni, a ni tuhi anab’ bɔbili soli ka bɛ yi zoli zuɣu n-siɣirina ka ŋmɛri mɔɣilɔnim’ ka chaɣisiri chaɣisa, ka ŋmɛri goonjɛnima, ka pɛbiri yuhi, ka tɔɣisir’ anabitali yɛtɔɣa.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord will suddenly take control of you. You'll become a different person and start prophesying right along with them.
translation_verse: Di saha Yawɛ shia ni siɣi a zuɣu na pam, ka a pahi bɛ zuɣu n-tɔɣisir’ anabitali yɛtɔɣa ka a biɛhigu taɣi.

english_verse: After these things happen, do whatever you think is right! God will help you.
translation_verse: Ka shihira ŋɔ zaa yi ti niŋ a nyin’ niŋm’ a nuu ni ni tooi niŋ shɛlikam, dama Naawuni be a sani.

english_verse: Then go to Gilgal. I'll come a little later, so wait for me. It may even take a week for me to get there, but when I come, I'll offer sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask for his blessings. I'll also tell you what to do next. Saul Goes Back Home
translation_verse: Ka a ti daŋ n tooni chaŋ Giligal, nyama, n ni ka nimaani na ti mali sara shɛli bɛ ni zaŋdi nyɔri buɣim la mini suhudoo sara maligunima. Di simdi ka a ti guhi ma nimaani daba ayopɔin hal ka n ti kana ti wuh’ a a ni yɛn niŋ shɛm.”

english_verse: As Saul turned around to leave Samuel, God made Saul feel like a different person. That same day, everything happened just as Samuel had said.
translation_verse: Sool ni daa ŋmaligi Samuɛl sani ni o chaŋ, ka Naawuni taɣ’ o suhu. Ka shihira ŋɔ zaa daa niŋ pali dindali maa.

english_verse: When Saul arrived at Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. The Spirit of God suddenly took control of him, and right there in the middle of the group he began prophesying.
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa ti paai Gibia ka anab’ bɔbili shiri tuh’ o soli ka Naawuni shia daa siɣ’ o zuɣu na pam, ka o pahi bɛ zuɣu n-tɔɣisiri anabitali yɛtɔɣa.

english_verse: Some people who had known Saul for a long time saw that he was speaking and behaving like a prophet. They said to each other, “What's happened? How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Ka bɛnkam pun mi o ni daa ti nya ka o tɔɣisiri anabitali yɛtɔɣa maa, ka bɛ yɛli taba, “Ka bɔ n-lee siɣi Kish bia ŋɔ zuɣu na? Sool gba nyɛla anabi?”

english_verse: “Why not?” one of them answered. “Saul has as much right to be a prophet as anyone else!” That's why everyone started saying, “How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Ka do’ so daa be nimaani n-garigi bɔhi ba, “Ka anabinim’ maa ba lee nyɛ ŋuni?” Dinzuɣu lala yɛtɔɣili maa daa leei yɛtɔɣ’ ŋahili ka bɛ mal’ li yɛra, “Sool gba nyɛla anabi?”

english_verse: After Saul stopped prophesying, he went to the place of worship.
translation_verse: O ni daa tɔɣisi anabitali yɛtɔɣa maa naai, o daa chaŋ ti dula daboli zuɣu.

english_verse: Later, Saul's uncle asked him, “Where have you been?” Saul answered, “Looking for the donkeys. We couldn't find them, so we went to talk with Samuel.”
translation_verse: Ka o bapir’ daa ti bɔh’ o min’ o tumtumda maa, “Ya ka yi lee chaŋ?” Ka Sool garigi yɛl’ o, “Ti daa chaŋla bunsi la bɔbu; ka daa ti bo ba je ka chaŋ Samuɛl sani.”

english_verse: “And what did he tell you?” Saul's uncle asked.
translation_verse: Ka o bapir’ maa daa yɛl’ o, “N suhir’ a mi, yɛlim’ ma Samuɛl ni yɛl’ a shɛm.”

english_verse: Saul answered, “He told us the donkeys had been found.” But Saul didn't mention that Samuel had chosen him to be king. The Lord Shows Israel that Saul Will Be King
translation_verse: Ka Sool daa yɛl’ o bapir’ maa, “O kahigimi wuhi ti ni yi nya bunsi maa.” Amaa Samuɛl ni daa yɛl’ o nam yɛtɔɣa la dina, o daa bi saɣi yɛl’ o di shɛli yɛla. Bɛ zaŋ Sool leei naa

english_verse: Samuel sent messengers to tell the Israelites to come to Mizpah and meet with the Lord.
translation_verse: Dahin shɛli ka Samuɛl daa ti boli niriba ni bɛ laɣim Yawɛ sanna Mizipa.

english_verse: When everyone had arrived, Samuel said: The Lord God of Israel told me to remind you that he had rescued you from the Egyptians and from the other nations that abused you.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa laɣimna, ka o yɛli Izraɛlnim’ maa, “Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni ŋɔ ni yɛli shɛm m-bɔŋɔ, ‘Mani n-daa yihi yinim’ Izraɛlnim’ Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ni, ka fan ya Ijiptinim’ mini na’ shɛb’ bɛn daa niŋdi ya fitiina la zaa nuu ni bahi.’

english_verse: God has rescued you from your troubles and hard times. But you have rejected your God and have asked for a king. Now each tribe and clan must come near the place of worship so the Lord can choose a king.
translation_verse: Amaa zuŋɔ yi zaɣisi yi Naawuni ŋun daa yihi ya azaaba mini muɣisigu ni maa. Ka yɛli, ‘Aai! Bom’ naa ti ti.’ Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ yi zuliya kam laɣimmi tab’ gbilligbilli ka Yawɛ sanna.”

english_verse: Samuel brought each tribe, one after the other, to the altar, and the Lord chose the Benjamin tribe.
translation_verse: Ka Samuɛl daa zaŋ zuliyanim’ maa zaa zali ka bɛ vihi nya, ka piila Bɛnjamin zuliya.

english_verse: Next, Samuel brought each clan of Benjamin there, and the Lord chose the Matri clan. Finally, Saul the son of Kish was chosen. But when they looked for him, he was nowhere to be found.
translation_verse: Ka o daa chɛ ka Bɛnjamin zuliya maa ni daŋ kam niriba laɣim gbilligbilli, ka bɛ vihi nya, ka piila Matiri daŋ. Di nyaaŋa ka o daa zaŋ Matiri daŋ maa ni dɔbba zaa zali, ka bɛ vihi nya, ka piila Kish bia Sool. Amaa bɛ ni daa ti bɔr’ o bɛ daa bi nya o.

english_verse: The people prayed, “Our Lord, is Saul here?” “Yes,” the Lord answered, “he is hiding behind the baggage.”
translation_verse: Ka daa lan bɔhi Yawɛ, “Doo maa ka kpe na?” Ka Yawɛ daa yɛl’ ba, “Nyamiya, o sɔɣ’ be kpalansi ŋɔ nyaaŋa.”

english_verse: The people ran and got Saul and brought him into the middle of the crowd. He was more than a head taller than anyone else.
translation_verse: Di saha ka bɛ daa zo n-chaŋ ti zaŋ o na, ka o ni daa kana nti zani niriba maa sani, o daa wɔɣ’ gari sokam.

english_verse: “Look closely at the man the Lord has chosen!” Samuel told the crowd. “There is no one like him!” The crowd shouted, “Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Ka Samuɛl daa yɛli niriba maa zaa, “Yi nya Yawɛ ni pii so maa? Niriba ŋɔ zaa ni so bi be kaman ŋuna.” Ka niriba maa zaa daa kuhi yɛli, “Naawuni dolim’ naa maa nyɛvili.”

english_verse: Samuel explained the rights and duties of a king and wrote them all in a book. He put the book in one of the shrines where the Lord was worshiped. Then Samuel sent everyone home.
translation_verse: Ka Samuɛl daa yɛl’ niriba maa naa ni mali so’ shɛŋa min’ o talahi tuma ni nyɛ shɛm. Ka daa sab’ li niŋ litaafi ni n-zaŋ li ti sɔŋ Yawɛ tooni. Di saha ka Samuɛl daa bahi niriba maa zaa ka bɛ wurim, ka sokam kul’ o ya.

english_verse: God had encouraged some young men to become followers of Saul, and when he returned to his hometown of Gibeah, they went with him.
translation_verse: Ka Sool gba daa kul’ o ya Gibia, ka dɔbba bɛn mali suhukpeeni, ka Naawuni yɛligu maa kpe bɛ suhuri ni daa pahi dol’ o kuli.

english_verse: But some worthless fools said, “How can someone like Saul rescue us from our enemies?” They did not want Saul to be their king, and so they didn't bring him any gifts. But Saul kept calm.
translation_verse: Amaa ka ninvuɣ’ yo’ shɛb’ daa yɛra, “Wula ka doo ŋɔ yɛn tooi niŋ tiligi ti?” Ka bɛ daa ʒiɛm o, ka zaɣis’ o pina tibu. Amaa ka o daa kul shini.

english_verse: About this time, King Nahash of Ammon came with his army and surrounded the town of Jabesh in Gilead. The people who lived there told Nahash, “If you will sign a peace treaty with us, you can be our ruler, and we will pay taxes to you.”
translation_verse: Dahin shɛli ka Ammɔnnim’ na’ so ŋun yuli daa booni Nahash la daa ti lo tɔb’ na nti teei gili Jabɛshi din be Giliad tintariga la nima. Ka Jabɛshi dɔbba zaa daa yɛli naa Nahash, “Chɛ ka ti min’ a tɔɣisi ka a zali ti zaligu ka ti jɛmd’ a.”

english_verse: Nahash answered, “Sure, I'll sign a treaty! But not before I insult Israel by poking out the right eye of every man who lives in Jabesh.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Ammɔnnim’ naa Nahash daa yɛl’ ba, “Yi yi ni saɣi ka n fɔɣi yi nudiriti polo nimbihi zaa din ni chɛ ka Izraɛlnim’ zaa nya filiŋ, n ni chɛ ka m mini ya tɔɣisi.”

english_verse: The town leaders said, “Give us seven days so we can send messengers everywhere in Israel to ask for help. If no one comes here to save us, we will surrender to you.”
translation_verse: Ka Jabɛshi kpamba daa yɛl’ o, “Tim ti daba ayopɔin ka ti tim Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ni zaa ti yɛl’ ba, ka so yi kani ŋun ni fa ti bahi, di saha ti ni zaŋ timaŋ’ ti a.”

english_verse: Some of the messengers went to Gibeah, Saul's hometown. They told what was happening at Jabesh, and everyone in Gibeah started crying.
translation_verse: Tuumba maa ni daa ti paai Gibia din nyɛ Sool ya la nti yɛli yɛlli maa ka di lu niriba tiba ni, bɛ daa dii duhila kuŋa n-kuhiri pampam.

english_verse: Just then, Saul came in from the fields, walking behind his oxen. “Why is everyone crying?” Saul asked. They told him what the men from Jabesh had said.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Sool daa dol’ o naɣikɔra yi puuni kunna ti wum kuhigu maa ka bɔhi, “Ka bɔ n-niŋ niriba maa ka bɛ zaa ti kuhiri lala?” Ka bɛ daa yɛl’ o Jabɛshinim’ ni ʒi lahiba’ shɛli maa na.

english_verse: Then the Spirit of God suddenly took control of Saul and made him furious.
translation_verse: Sool ni daa wum yɛtɔɣa maa, ka Naawuni shia siɣ’ o zuɣu na ni kpiɔŋ pam, ka o suhu daa yiɣisi pam,

english_verse: Saul killed two of his oxen, cut them up in pieces, and gave the pieces to the messengers. He told them to show the pieces to everyone in Israel and say, “Saul and Samuel are getting an army together. Come and join them. If you don't, this is what will happen to your oxen!” The Lord made the people of Israel terribly afraid. So all the men came together
translation_verse: Ka o gbah’ o naɣikɔra ayi n-ku ŋ-ŋmahiŋmahi ba n-chɛ ka tuumba zaŋ li gili Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni zaa n-tari niriba ka yɛra, “Ŋunkam bi yina n-dol’ Sool mini Samuɛl chaŋ tɔb’ ni, lala n-yɛn niŋ dilan’ naɣikɔra.” Ka Yawɛ yɛla dabiɛm daa gbahi niriba maa, ka bɛ zaa daa yina naŋgbanyini.

english_verse: Saul and his officers sent the messengers back to Jabesh with this promise: “We will rescue you tomorrow afternoon.” The messengers went back to the people at Jabesh and told them that they were going to be rescued. Everyone was encouraged!
