english_verse: David made this a law for Israel, and it has been the same ever since.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa zaŋ li lee kali ni zaligu Izraɛlnim’ zaa sani, ka bɛ dol’ li hal ni zuŋɔ.

english_verse: David went back to Ziklag with everything they had taken from the Amalekites. He sent some of these things as gifts to his friends who were leaders of Judah, and he told them, “We took these things from the Lord's enemies. Please accept them as a gift.”
translation_verse: Dauda ni daa labi Zikilag, o daa piila o ni tuhi di neen’ shɛŋa maa shɛli nti ti o zɔnim’ bɛn daa nyɛ Juda kpamba la ka yɛli ba, “N ni tuhi Yawɛ dimnim’ ka di neen’ shɛŋa ka m pii tin ya na maa.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Philistines were fighting Israel at Mount Gilboa. Israel's soldiers ran from the Philistines, and many of them were killed.
translation_verse: Filistianim’ mini Izraɛlnim’ daa ti tuhiri tɔbu, ka Izraɛlnim’ daa ŋmaligi guui ka chɛ Filistianim’ maa; ka Filistianim’ maa daa dol’ ba ti ku ba Gilibɔa Zoli zuɣu.

english_verse: The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons, and they killed his sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
translation_verse: Ka Filistianim’ maa daa kari ti paai Sool min’ o bidibisi n-ku o bidibisi bɛn daa nyɛ Jɔnatan mini Abinadab ni Malikishua.

english_verse: The fighting was fierce around Saul, and he was badly wounded by enemy arrows.
translation_verse: Ka tɔb’ maa daa kpaɣi mii Sool, ka peentɔriba daa nya o n-to o piɛm ti o daŋ pam.

english_verse: Saul told the soldier who carried his weapons, “Kill me with your sword! I don't want these worthless Philistines to torture and make fun of me.” But the soldier was afraid to kill him. Saul then took out his own sword; he stuck the blade into his stomach, and fell on it.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Sool daa yɛl’ o gbaɣinɔʒira, “Ŋoom’ a takɔbi n-kuhi ku ma, di so ka bɛn bi gundi ŋɔ ti kana ti zaŋ bɛ takɔbiri kuhi ku ma, ka zaŋ ma diɛm.” Amaa ka dabiɛm daa gbaag’ o gbaɣinɔʒira maa pam ka o bi saɣi ku o. Dinzuɣu ka Sool daa zaŋ omaŋmaŋ’ takɔbi zali n-lu di zuɣu.

english_verse: When the soldier knew that Saul was dead, he killed himself in the same way.
translation_verse: Sool gbaɣinɔʒiri maa ni daa nya ka Sool kpi maa, ka o gba lu o takɔbi zuɣu kpi m-pah’ o zuɣu.

english_verse: Saul was dead, his three sons were dead, and the soldier who carried his weapons was dead. They and all his soldiers died on that same day.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu Sool min’ o bidibis’ ata ni o gbaɣinɔʒira ni o niriba zaa ni daa laɣim kpi dahin yini shɛm m-bala.

english_verse: The Israelites on the other side of Jezreel Valley and the other side of the Jordan learned that Saul and his sons were dead. They saw that the Israelite army had run away. So they ran away too, and the Philistines moved into the towns the Israelites had left behind.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ bɛn daa be vinvamli maa yaɣ’ din’ la mini bɛn daa be Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili dul’ la daa nya ka Izraɛlnim’ ŋmaligi guui, ka Sool min’ o bidibisi kpi, ka bɛ daa yi n-zo ka chɛ bɛ tinsi, ka Filistianim’ maa daa kana ti be di ni.

english_verse: The day after the battle, when the Philistines returned to the battlefield to take the weapons of the dead Israelite soldiers, they found Saul and his three sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa.
translation_verse: N-daa yi biɛɣu ka Filistianim’ maa chaŋ ni bɛ ti yeei bɛ ni ku shɛb’ maa nɛma, ka daa nya ka Sool min’ o bidibis’ ata maa lu n-dola Gilibɔa Zoli zuɣu.

english_verse: The people who lived in Jabesh in Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul's body.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Jabɛshigiliadnim’ daa wum Filistianim’ ni niŋ Sool shɛm maa,

english_verse: So one night, some brave men from Jabesh went to Beth-Shan. They took down the bodies of Saul and his sons, then brought them back to Jabesh and burned them.
translation_verse: ka bɛ dɔbba bɛn zaa mali suhukpeeni daa yi n-chaŋ yuŋ ti yihi Sool min’ o bidibisi maa Bɛtishan gooni maa zuɣu n-zaŋ ba chaŋ Jabɛshi ti nyo ba buɣim nimaani.

english_verse: They buried the bones under a small tree in Jabesh, and for seven days, they went without eating to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa va bɛ kɔba ti sɔɣi Jabɛshi tiŋ’ puuni tamarisik tia gbini, ka lo noli daba ayopɔin.

english_verse: Saul was dead. Meanwhile, David had defeated the Amalekites and returned to Ziklag.
translation_verse: Dauda ni daa tuhi Amalɛknim’ maa ka labina Naa Sool kum maa nyaaŋa, o daa kpalimla Zikilag daba ayi.

english_verse: Three days later, a soldier came from Saul's army. His clothes were torn, and dirt was on his head. He went to David and knelt down in front of him.
translation_verse: Nyama di daba ata dali ka do’ so daa ti yi Sool sansan’ ni n-zo m-paana ka o binyɛra chahi, ka taŋkpaɣu puɣ’ o zuɣu. O ni daa ti paai Dauda sani, o daa lumi gbani Dauda tooni lu o sizuura.

english_verse: David asked, “Where did you come from?” The man answered, “From Israel's army. I barely escaped with my life.”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa bɔh’ o, “Ya ka a yina?” Ka o garigi yɛl’ o, “Izraɛlnim’ sansan’ ni ka n yi n-zo na maa.”

english_verse: “Who won the battle?” David asked. The man said, “Our army turned and ran, but many were wounded and died. Even King Saul and his son Jonathan are dead.”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda yɛl’ o, “Yɛlim’ ma din niŋ.” Ka o yɛl’ o, “Tɔbbihi maa ŋmaligimi guui, ka bɛ pam lu tɔb’ maa ni, ka Sool min’ o bia Jɔnatan gba lu tɔb’ maa ni.”

english_verse: The young man replied: I was on Mount Gilboa and saw King Saul leaning on his spear. The enemy's war chariots and cavalry were closing in on him.
translation_verse: Ka nachimbil’ so ŋun daa yɛl’ o li maa yɛli, “Di daa niŋla daliri ka n chaŋ Gilibɔa Zoli zuɣu nti chirigi Sool ka o zaŋ omaŋ’ dalim’ o kpani, ka chɛchɛbunsi mini wɔribariba daa kabiri kani o sanna.

english_verse: When he turned around and saw me, he called me over. I went and asked what he wanted.
translation_verse: Ka o daa ŋmaligi lih’ o nyaaŋa nya ma ka boli ma, ka n garigi yɛl’ o, ‘N-nyɛ ma.’

english_verse: Saul asked me, “Who are you?” “An Amalekite,” I answered.
translation_verse: Ka o bɔhi n ni nyɛ ninvuɣ’ so, ka n yɛl’ o, ‘N nyɛla Amalɛk nira.’

english_verse: Then he said, “Kill me! I'm dying, and I'm in terrible pain.”
translation_verse: Ka o yɛli ma, ‘Kamina ti zani baɣili ma n-ku ma, dama n nya daŋ pam, ka m mi shia na bi siɣi.’

english_verse: So I killed him. I knew he was too badly wounded to live much longer. Then I took his crown and his arm-band, and I brought them to you, Your Majesty. Here they are.
translation_verse: Di saha ka n daa chaŋ ti zani baɣil’ o n-ku o, ka pilig’ o zuɣupiligu din be o zuɣu ni, ka lan pirigi baŋ’ din be o nuu ni na, dama n daa baŋya ni o ni lu n-doya shɛm maa, o ku lan gali. Dinzuɣu ka n zaŋ o nɛma maa na ni n ti ti nyini n dana.”

english_verse: At once, David and his soldiers tore their clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda daa gbaag’ omaŋmaŋ’ binyɛra n-dar’ chahi li, ka bɛnkam daa be o sani gba daa niŋ lala.

english_verse: They cried all day long and would not eat anything. Everyone was sad because Saul, his son Jonathan, and many of the Lord's people had been killed in the battle.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa kum ka fabili pam, ka lo noli Sool min’ o bia Jɔnatan ni Yawɛ niriba Izraɛlnim’ zuɣu dindali hal ni zaawuni, bɛ ni daa zaŋ takɔbiri ku ba maa zuɣu.

english_verse: David asked the young man, “Where is your home?” The man replied, “My father is an Amalekite, but we live in Israel.”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa bɔhi nachimbil’ so ŋun daa yɛl’ o li maa, “Tiŋ’ kani ka a lee yina?” Ka o garigi yɛl’ o, “N nyɛla Amalɛk saan’ so ŋun be a tiŋgbani ŋɔ ni bia.”

english_verse: David said to him, “Why weren't you afraid to kill the Lord's chosen king? And you even told what you did. It's your own fault that you're going to die!” Then David told one of his soldiers, “Come here and kill this man!” David Sings in Memory of Saul
translation_verse: Ka Dauda yɛl’ o, “A ʒim yihibu taali ʒi a zuɣu, dama amaŋmaŋ’ noli n-di a shɛhira yɛli, ‘Mani n-ku Yawɛ ni pii ninvuɣ’ so maa.’ ” Dauda fabili Naa Sool mini Jɔnatan zuɣu

english_verse: David sang a song in memory of Saul and Jonathan,
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa fabili fabila ŋɔ Sool min’ o bia Jɔnatan zuɣu,

english_verse: Israel, your famous hero lies dead on the hills, and your mighty warriors have fallen!
translation_verse: Bɛ ku Izraɛl jilima zoya din du pam zuɣu, ka wɔɣira lu.

english_verse: Don't tell it in Gath or spread the news on the streets of Ashkelon. The godless Philistine women will be happy and jump for joy.
translation_verse: Di moliya di yɛla gili Gaat fɔŋ ni; yi mi di moliya di yɛla doli Ashikɛlɔn solɔri, ka di zuɣu chɛ ka Filistia bipuɣinsi yiɣi jam, bee n-chɛ ka bɛn bi gundi ŋɔ bipuɣinsi suhuri paligi.

english_verse: Don't let dew or rain fall on the hills of Gilboa. Don't let its fields grow offerings for God. There the warriors' shields were smeared with mud, and Saul's own shield was left unpolished.
translation_verse: “Yinim’ Gilibɔa zoya, maligim bee saa ku lan lu yi zuɣu na bee bimbilima ti lan bili yi zolɔna ni. Dama nimaani ka kpiɔŋlaannim’ bidibbina nya filiŋ. Ka Sool nyɔtaɣirigu bi lan nya kpam ʒe.

english_verse: The arrows of Jonathan struck, and warriors died. The sword of Saul cut the enemy apart.
translation_verse: Jɔnatan tɔbu daa ʒi n-lab’ kuli ka pa ni o ni ku ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ ʒim mini kpiɔŋlaannim’ kpam n-varim li. Ka Sool mi takɔbi na ʒi n-chɛ n-ziŋ.

english_verse: It was easy to love Saul and Jonathan. Together in life, together in death, they were faster than eagles and stronger than lions.
translation_verse: Sool mini Jɔnatan, n yurinima bɛn veeni yurilim. Bɛ daa bi woligi taba bɛ nyɛviya ni mini bɛ kum ni. Bɛ daa valim gari tɔrili. Bɛ daa mali kpiɔŋ gari gbuɣima.

english_verse: Women of Israel, cry for Saul. He brought you fine red cloth and jewelry made of gold.
translation_verse: Yinim’ Izraɛl bipuɣinsi, kummiya Sool zuɣu. Ŋuna n-zaŋ mulifu viɛlli soli ya. Ŋuna n-zaŋ salima yɛri yɛli ya.

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen in the heat of battle, and Jonathan lies dead on the hills of Gilboa.
translation_verse: Nyam’ kpiɔŋlaannim’ ni lu tɔb’ sunsuuni shɛm! Bɛ ku Jɔnatan sɔŋ zoya zuɣu!

english_verse: Jonathan, I miss you most! I loved you like a brother. You were truly loyal to me, more faithful than a wife to her husband.
translation_verse: M mabia Jɔnatan, n suhu saɣimya pam a zuɣu. M min’ a biɛhigu daa lu n-taɣili tab’ pam. A yurilim zaŋ chaŋ n sani daa mali alahiziba, ka galisi pam gari paɣ’ ni mali yurilim shɛm.

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen, and their weapons are destroyed.
translation_verse: Nyam’ kpiɔŋlaannim’ ni lu tɔb’ sunsuuni shɛm, ka bɛ bidibbina bahi yoli!

english_verse: Later, David asked the Lord, “Should I go back to one of the towns of Judah?” The Lord answered, “Yes.” David asked, “Which town should I go to?” “Go to Hebron,” the Lord replied.
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka Dauda daa bɔhi Yawɛ, “N cham’ Juda tin’ shɛl’ ni ti ʒini?” Ka Yawɛ yɛl’ o, “Chama.” Ka Dauda lan bɔhi, “N cham’ tiŋ’ kani?” Ka o yɛl’ o, “Cham’ Hiburɔn.”

english_verse: David went to Hebron with his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail. Ahinoam was from Jezreel, and Abigail was the widow of Nabal from Carmel.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda daa zaŋ o paɣiba ayi la Ahinɔam ŋun daa yi Jɛziriil na la mini Abigeel Nabal pakoli ŋun mi daa yi Kamɛl na la chaŋ Hiburɔn.

english_verse: David also told his men and their families to come and live in the villages near Hebron.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa zaŋ ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn zaa be o sani mini bɛ malibu na ka bɛ ti ʒini Hiburɔn fɔndi ni.

english_verse: The people of Judah met with David at Hebron and poured olive oil on his head to show that he was their new king. Then they told David, “The people from Jabesh in Gilead buried Saul.”
translation_verse: Ka Judanim’ daa kana ti booi kpam bahi Dauda zuɣu ni nimaani n-zaŋ o leei Judanim’ naa. Ka bɛ daa yɛli Dauda ni Jabɛshigiliadnima n-daa sɔɣi Sool.

english_verse: David sent messengers to tell them: The Lord bless you! You were kind enough to bury Saul your ruler,
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa tim tuumba Jabɛshigiliadnim’ maa sani ti yɛli ba, “Yawɛ niŋmi alibarika niŋ yi ni yi ni daa wuhi yi ʒiɛyimtali ni nyɛ shɛm zaŋ chaŋ yi dan’ Naa Sool sani, ka sɔɣ’ o la zuɣu.

english_verse: and I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you. I will be your friend because of what you have done.
translation_verse: Pumpɔŋɔ Yawɛ ni wuhi ya o yurilim min’ o ʒiɛyimtali ni nyɛ shɛm zaŋ chaŋ yi sani; ka man’ gba ni niŋ ya zaɣ’ viɛlli yi ni daa tum tuun’ shɛli maa zuɣu.

english_verse: Saul is dead, but the tribe of Judah has made me their king. So be strong and have courage. Ishbosheth Becomes King of Israel
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ kpaŋsimiya yimaŋa ka mali suhukpeeni, dama yi dan’ Sool kpiya ka Judanim’ mi zaŋ ma leei bɛ naa.” Bɛ zaŋ Ishibɔshɛt leei Izraɛlnim’ naa

english_verse: Abner the son of Ner had been the general of Saul's army. He took Saul's son Ishbosheth across the Jordan River to Mahanaim
translation_verse: Ka Sool tɔbbihi sapashin’ kpɛm’ Abinɛr ŋun daa nyɛ Nɛr bia la daa zaŋ Sool bia Ishibɔshɛt n-zo chaŋ Mahanaim

english_verse: and made him king of Israel, including the areas of Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, and Benjamin.
translation_verse: nti zaŋ o leei naa ni o su Giliad mini Ashur ni Jɛziriil ni Ifriim ni Bɛnjamin tiŋgbana ni Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ zaa.

english_verse: and he ruled from Hebron for seven and a half years. The War between David and Ishbosheth
translation_verse: Saha shɛli Dauda ni daa di nam ʒi Hiburɔn n-su Judanim’ maa yuma daa nyɛla yuma ayopɔin ni chira ayɔbu. Tɔb’ lu Judanim’ mini Izraɛlnim’ sunsuuni

english_verse: One day, Abner and the soldiers of Ishbosheth left Mahanaim and went to Gibeon.
translation_verse: Ka Abinɛr ŋun daa nyɛ Nɛr bia la mini Sool bia Ishibɔshɛt la tɔbbihi daa yi Mahanaim chaŋ Gibiɔn.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab the son of Zeruiah was leading David's soldiers, and the two groups met at the pool in Gibeon. Abner and his men sat down on one side of the pool, while Joab and his men sat on the other side.
translation_verse: Ka Jɔab ŋun daa nyɛ Zɛruya bia la mini Dauda tɔbbihi mi daa yi n-chaŋ ti paai ba Gibiɔn biaŋ ni n-chaŋ ti ʒini biaŋ maa yaɣ’ yini polo ka bɛn’ la mi chaŋ ti ʒini biaŋ maa yaɣ’ din’ la polo.

english_verse: Abner yelled to Joab, “Let's get some of our best soldiers to stand up and fight each other!” Joab agreed,
translation_verse: Ka Abinɛr daa yɛli Jɔab, “Chɛ ka nachimba maa yiɣisi diɛm ka ti nya,” Ka Jɔab yɛli, “Chɛ ka bɛ yiɣisi.”

english_verse: and twelve of Ishbosheth's men from the tribe of Benjamin got up to fight twelve of David's men.
translation_verse: Di saha ka bɛ daa yiɣisi kaman bɛ kalinli ni nyɛ shɛm, ka ninvuɣ’ pinaayi daa yi Bɛnjamin mini Ishibɔshɛt Sool bia maa polo na, ka ninvuɣ’ pinaayi mi yi Dauda tɔbbihi maa polo na.

english_verse: They grabbed each other by the hair and stabbed each other in the side with their daggers. They all died right there! That's why the place in Gibeon is called “Field of Daggers.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ zaa ti gbahi tab’ zuɣuri, ka zaŋ takɔbiri kuhi tab’ puluɣa ni, ka bɛ zaa laɣim lu n-kpi. Dinzuɣu ka bɛ daa boli nimaani Hɛlikatihazurim, ka di be Gibiɔn.

english_verse: Then everyone started fighting. Both sides fought very hard, but David's soldiers defeated Abner and the soldiers of Israel.
translation_verse: Ka nimmoo tɔb’ daa bili dindali maa, ka Naa Dauda tɔbbihi maa daa tuhi nyaŋ Abinɛr mini Izraɛlnim’ maa.

english_verse: Zeruiah's three sons were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel could run as fast as a deer in an open field,
translation_verse: Ka Zɛruya bidibis’ ata daa be nimaani, bɛna n-nyɛ Jɔab mini Abishai ni Asahɛl. Asahɛl daa guurimi kaman molifu la.

english_verse: When Abner turned and saw him, he said, “Is that you, Asahel?” Asahel answered, “Yes it is.”
translation_verse: Ka Abinɛr daa ti ŋmaligi lih’ o nyaaŋa nya o ka bɔh’ o, “Asahɛl, nyini m-bala?” Ka o yɛli, “Mani m-bala.”

english_verse: Abner said, “There are soldiers all around. Stop chasing me and fight one of them! Kill him and take his clothes and weapons for yourself.” But Asahel refused to stop.
translation_verse: Ka Abinɛr yɛl’ o, “Ŋmaligim’ a nudirigu bee a nuzaa polo n-gbaai nachimba ŋɔ ni yino n-fa o ni mali shɛli.” Amaa ka Asahɛl bi ŋmaligi ka chɛ o dolibu.

english_verse: Abner said, “If you don't turn back, I'll have to kill you! Then I could never face your brother Joab again.”
translation_verse: Ka Abinɛr ti lan yɛl’ o, “Ŋmaligim’ ka chɛ ma dolibu; bɔ n-niŋ ka a yɛn chɛ ka n ku a? N yi ku a wula ka n lee yɛn niŋ lih’ a biɛli Jɔab ninni?”

english_verse: But Asahel would not turn back, so Abner struck him in the stomach with the back end of his spear. The spear went all the way through and came out of his back. Asahel fell down and died. Everyone who saw Asahel lying dead just stopped and stood still.
translation_verse: Amaa ka o daa zaɣisi ni o ku ŋmaligi; dinzuɣu ka Abinɛr daa zaŋ o kpani zuɣu polo to o pul’ ni ka di pili yi o yaaŋa zuɣu, ka o daa lu nimaani kpi. Ka bɛn zaa daa paai Asahɛl ni lu luɣ’ shɛli kpi maa kpalim zani baalim.

english_verse: But Joab and Abishai went after Abner. Finally, about sunset, they came to the hill of Ammah, not far from Giah on the road to Gibeon Desert.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Jɔab mini Abishai bɛn’ daa kari doli Abinɛr, zaŋ chaŋ wuntan’ luhili saha ka bɛ daa paai Amma Zoli din be Gia polo Gibiɔn mɔɣu ni soli zuɣu la gbini.

english_verse: Abner brought the men of Benjamin together in one group on top of a hill, and they got ready to fight.
translation_verse: Ka Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba daa ti laɣim zaŋ bɛ noya naai Abinɛr ka bɛ min’ o leei zaɣ’ yini n-du zoli maa zuɣu ti zani.

english_verse: Abner shouted to Joab, “Aren't we ever going to stop killing each other? Don't you know that the longer we keep on doing this, the worse it's going to be when it's all over? When are you going to order your men to stop chasing their own relatives?”
translation_verse: Ka Abinɛr daa ti kuhi bahi Jɔab ha bɔh’ o, “Ti kul yɛn zaŋla takɔbiri ŋɔ n-kuri tab’ hal ni saha din ka bahigu? A bi mi ni di bahigu ti yɛn nyɛla dimdi din ku naai? Bɔ saha ka a yɛn yɛl’ a niriba maa ka bɛ chɛ bɛ mabihi ŋɔ kari doli?”

english_verse: Joab shouted back, “I swear by the living God, if you hadn't spoken, my men would have chased their relatives all night!”
translation_verse: Ka Jɔab daa yɛli, “Hal ka Naawuni ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu, a yi di bi yɛli shɛli, biɛhiŋ kani, n niriba ŋɔ naan kari doli bɛ mabihi maa hal ni biɛɣuni asiba.”

english_verse: Joab took his trumpet and blew the signal for his soldiers to stop chasing the soldiers of Israel. At once, the fighting stopped.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Jɔab daa piɛbi kikaa, ka niriba maa kpalim zani ka bi lan kariti doli Izraɛlnim’ maa bee n-lan tuhiri ba.

english_verse: Abner and his troops marched through the Jordan River valley all that night. Then they crossed the river and marched all morning until they arrived back at Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Ka Abinɛr min’ o niriba maa daa chaŋ yuŋ maa zaa n-gari Araba ti gbaai Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili du, zaŋ chaŋ wuntaŋ’ daa ti yɛn zani zuɣu ni ka bɛ paai Mahanaim.

english_verse: As soon as Joab stopped chasing Abner, he got David's troops together and counted them. There were
translation_verse: Ka Jɔab daa yi Abinɛr karibu maa yɔɣu labina nti laɣim Dauda tɔbbihi maa zali ka bɛ ni ninvuɣ’ pisiyinika daa kani m-pahi Asahɛl zuɣu.

english_verse: Joab and his troops carried Asahel's body to Bethlehem and buried him in the family burial place. Then they marched all night and reached Hebron before sunrise.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa zaŋ Asahɛl chaŋ Bɛtilihɛm ti sɔɣ’ o o ba siliga din daa be nimaani la puuni. Ka Jɔab min’ o niriba maa daa ŋmaligi doli tab’ yuŋ labi, zaŋ chaŋ biɛɣu daa ti yɛn neei, ka bɛ paai Hiburɔn.

english_verse: As the war went on between the families of David and Saul, Abner was gaining more power than ever in Saul's family.
translation_verse: Tɔb’ daa yi ti lu Naa Sool niriba mini Dauda niriba sunsuuni saha shɛlikam, di saha Abinɛr nyarila yaa Sool niriba maa sani.

english_verse: He had even slept with a wife of Saul by the name of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah. But Saul's son Ishbosheth told Abner, “You shouldn't have slept with one of my father's wives!”
translation_verse: Sool mam daa beni ka o yuli booni Rizipa. O daa nyɛla Aiya bipuɣiŋga, ka Ishibɔshɛt daa ti bɔhi Abinɛr, “Bɔ n-niŋ ka a zaŋ m ba mam maa dɔni?”

english_verse: Abner was very angry because of what Ishbosheth had said, and he told Ishbosheth: Am I some kind of worthless dog from Judah? I've always been loyal to your father's family and to his relatives and friends. I haven't turned you over to David. And yet you talk to me as if I've committed a crime with this woman.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Abinɛr suhu daa yiɣisi pam Ishibɔshɛt yɛtɔɣa maa zuɣu, ka o daa bɔh’ o, “Judanim’ baa n-nyɛ ma? N kul ʒiɛla a ba Sool min’ o mabihi ni o zɔnim’ zaa yim hal ni zuŋɔ, ka bi saɣi zaŋ a niŋ Dauda nuu ni, di zaa yoli ka a ti zaŋ ma taali paɣ’ zuɣu!”

english_verse: I ask God to punish me if I don't help David get what the Lord promised him!
translation_verse: O daa lan yɛli, “N yi bi chɛ ka Naawuni ni daa lo Dauda alikauli yɛli

english_verse: God said that he wouldn't let anyone in Saul's family ever be king again and that David would be king instead. He also said that David would rule both Israel and Judah, all the way from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south.
translation_verse: ni o ni yihi Sool nam ni ka zaŋ ŋun’ Dauda ʒili nam gbandi maa zuɣu, ka o su Judanim’ mini Izraɛlnim’ zaa, zaŋ Dan hal ti kpa Bɛrishiiba la niŋ pali, Naawuni ŋun darigim n tibili, hal ŋun darigim n tibili pam gba.”

english_verse: Ishbosheth was so afraid of Abner that he could not even answer.
translation_verse: Ka Ishibɔshɛt daa kɔŋ o ni yɛn yɛli Abinɛr shɛm, dama o daa zɔr’ o mi.

english_verse: Abner sent some of his men to David with this message: “You should be the ruler of the whole nation. If you make an agreement with me, I will persuade everyone in Israel to make you their king.”
translation_verse: Ka Abinɛr daa tim tuumba Dauda sani Hiburɔn ni bɛ ti yɛl’ o, “Ŋuni n-lee lan su tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ? Chɛ ka m min’ a lo tab’ alikauli, ka n sɔŋ a n-zaŋ Izraɛlnim’ zaa na ti ti a.”

english_verse: David sent this message back: “Good! I'll make an agreement with you. But before I will even talk with you about it, you must get Saul's daughter Michal back for me.”

translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa ti paai Nakɔn kabɔɣili ni, ka naɣila’ shɛb’ bɛn daa vɔri tɔroko maa tuui, di saha ka Yuza daa teeg’ o nuu gbaai Naawuni Daalikauli Adaka maa mali.

english_verse: The Lord God was very angry with Uzzah for doing this, and he killed Uzzah right there beside the chest.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ suhu daa yiɣisi bahi Yuza zuɣu, ka o ku o nimaani sɔŋ Alikauli Adaka maa luɣili ni o ni daa zaŋ o nuu gbaai Alikauli Adaka maa zuɣu.

english_verse: David got angry with God for killing Uzzah. He named that place “Bursting Out Against Uzzah,” and that's what it's still called.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa je suli Yawɛ ni daa yiɣis’ o suhu bahi Yuza zuɣu shɛm maa zuɣu; ka bɛ daa boli nimaani yuli Pɛrɛzuza hal ni zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ.

english_verse: David was afraid of the Lord and thought, “Should I really take the sacred chest to my city?”
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ yɛla daa gbaai Dauda dabiɛm pam dindali maa ka o yɛli, “Ka wula ka n lee yɛn niŋ zaŋ Alikauli Adaka ŋɔ kuli n yiŋa?”

english_verse: He decided not to take it there. Instead, he turned off the road and took it to the home of Obed Edom, who was from Gath.
translation_verse: Di zuɣu ka Dauda daa bi lan bɔri ni o zaŋ Yawɛ Daalikauli Adaka maa kuli ŋun’ Dauda tiŋ’ la ni, amaa ka daa zaŋ li ŋmaligi tahi la Obɛdɛdom ŋun daa nyɛ Gaat nir’ la yiŋa.

english_verse: The chest stayed there for three months, and the Lord greatly blessed Obed Edom, his family, and everything he owned. Then someone told King David, “The Lord has done this because the sacred chest is in Obed Edom's house.” At once, David went to Obed Edom's house to get the chest and bring it to David's City. Everyone was celebrating.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yɛli Naa Dauda ni Yawɛ niŋla alibarika niŋ Obɛdɛdom min’ o malibu zaa ni, Naawuni Daalikauli Adaka maa zuɣu. Di saha ka Dauda daa chaŋ ti kpuɣi Naawuni Daalikauli Adaka maa Obɛdɛdom yiŋa n-zaŋ li kuli ŋun’ Dauda tiŋ’ la ni ni suhupiɛlli.

english_verse: They put the chest inside a tent that David had set up for it. David worshiped the Lord by sacrificing animals and burning them on an altar,
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa zaŋ Yawɛ Daalikauli Adaka maa na ti zali di zaashee Dauda ni daa pun chɛ ka bɛ ti suɣ’ shɛli zal’ li la puuni. Ka Dauda daa mali sara shɛli bɛ ni zaŋdi nyɔri buɣim la mini suhudoo sara maligu Yawɛ tooni.

english_verse: He gave all the men and women in the crowd a small loaf of bread, some meat, and a handful of raisins, then everyone went home. Michal Talks to David
translation_verse: ka daa zaŋ maha tari Izraɛl salo bɛn nyɛ dɔbba mini paɣiba maa zaa, ka sokam daa deei mahi’ yiniyini mini nim’ kpillikpilli ni bɛ ni zaŋ wain tihi wala m-pahi mali mahi’ shɛŋa zaɣ’ yiniyini pahi. Di nyaaŋa ka sokam daa wurim kuli bɛ yinsi.

english_verse: David went home so he could ask the Lord to bless his family. But Saul's daughter Michal went out and started yelling at him. “You were really great today!” she said. “You acted like a dirty old man, dancing around half-naked in front of your servants' slave-girls.”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa lab’ yiŋa ni o ti suhi alibarika niŋ o yiŋ’ nim’ ni. Amaa ka Sool bipuɣiŋga Mikal la daa yina ti tuhi Dauda soli yɛl’ o, “Izraɛl naa ti omaŋ’ jilima zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ, dama o pirigiya ka chɛ o zaɣim o kpamba dabipaɣiba tooni kaman jɛrigu ŋun bi zɔri vi ni pirigiri ka chɛr’ o zaɣim shɛm la.”

english_verse: David told her, “The Lord didn't choose your father or anyone else in your family to be the leader of his people. The Lord chose me, and I was celebrating in honor of him.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa garigi yɛli Mikal, “Yawɛ ŋun daa pii ma ka duhi ma gar’ a ba min’ o yiŋnim’ zaa, ka zaŋ ma leei nabia ni n su Izraɛlnim’ bɛn nyɛ ŋun’ Yawɛ niriba ŋɔ tooni ka n di wari waa maa, ka di simdi ni m mali suhupiɛlli Yawɛ tooni.

english_verse: I'll show you just how great I can be! I'll even be disgusting to myself. But those slave-girls you talked about will still honor me!”
translation_verse: Hal n ni filim mmaŋa n-gari ŋ-ŋɔ gba, ka lihi ʒiɛm mmaŋa, amaa dabipaɣiba shɛb’ yɛla a ni yɛli ŋɔ bɛn’ ni ti ma jilima.”

english_verse: But I will never put an end to my agreement with him, as I put an end to my agreement with Saul, who was king before you.
translation_verse: Amaa n ti ku yihi n suhu o ni kaman n ni daa yihi n suhu Sool ŋun daŋ a tooni la ni shɛm la,

english_verse: Then one day, as David was talking with Nathan the prophet, David said, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest has to stay in a tent.”
translation_verse: di saha ka naa daa yɛli anab’ Neetan, “Nyama, m bela sida dari yil’ ni, amaa ka Naawuni Daalikauli Adaka ŋɔ dim be suɣili ni.”

english_verse: Nathan replied, “The Lord is with you, so do what you want!”
translation_verse: Ka Neetan daa yɛli naa, “Cham’ ti niŋ a ni lo a suhu ni ni a niŋ shɛm, Yawɛ ʒe a nyaaŋa.”

english_verse: That night, the Lord told Nathan
translation_verse: Amaa dindali maa yuŋ ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Neetan,

english_verse: to go to David and give him this message: David, you are my servant, so listen to what I say. Why should you build a temple for me?
translation_verse: “Cham’ ti yɛli n dabili Dauda ni man’ Yawɛ bɔhir’ o, ‘A yɛn mɛla duu ti ma ka m be di ni?’

english_verse: I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them.
translation_verse: Saha shɛli n ni daa yihi Izraɛlnim’ Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ni na la hal ni zuŋɔ n na ʒi m be duu, amaa suɣili ni ka n kul be ka yi mali ma ginda.

english_verse: I chose leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
translation_verse: Luɣ’ shɛlikam zaa m mini n niriba Izraɛlnim’ maa ni daa chaŋ, n daa na mi m-bɔhi sariakaritib’ shɛb’ n ni daa pii zali ni bɛ su n niriba Izraɛlnim’ la, ‘Bɔ n-niŋ ka yi bi zaŋ sida dari me duu ti ma?’ ”

english_verse: David, this is what I, the Lord All-Powerful, say to you. I brought you in from the fields where you took care of sheep, and I made you the leader of my people.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ yɛlimi n dabili Dauda ni man’ Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ tɔbbihi zaa naa ŋɔ yɛliya, “Mani n-daa yih’ a mɔɣu ni piɛgulibo ni na ni a ti leegi n niriba Izraɛlnim’ toondana n-su ba.

english_verse: Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
translation_verse: Ka a daa yi kul chani luɣ’ shɛlikam, m bela a sani, ka nyaŋ a dimnim’ zaa ti a, ka duh’ a yuli kaman dunia ŋɔ ninvuɣ’ kara yuya ni du shɛm.

english_verse: I have given my people Israel a land of their own where they can live in peace, and they won't have to tremble with fear any more. Evil nations won't bother them, as they did
translation_verse: N ni bo biɛhigu shee ti n niriba Izraɛlnima, ka zaŋ ba ʒili nimaani ka bɛ be bɛ dahalali tiŋgbɔŋ ni ka so ku lan dam ba yaha; ka ninvuɣ’ galima ku lan nahim ba kaman bɛ ni daa yi niŋdi ba shɛm

english_verse: when I let judges rule my people. And I have kept your enemies from attacking you. Now I promise that you and your descendants will be kings.
translation_verse: saha shɛli n ni daa pii zuɣulaannim’ zali ka bɛ su n niriba Izraɛlnim’ maa la. N ni chɛ ka a nya nyee vuhi a dimnim’ zaa sani. M-pahi, man’ Yawɛ lan yɛl’ a ni n ni me yili ti a,

english_verse: I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried in the tomb of your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler,
translation_verse: ka a dabisa yi ti pali ka a dɔni a yaannim’ tooni, n ni piig’ a bihi ni yino ŋun nyɛ a dahalali bia n-chɛ ka o nam nya zaashee zani.

english_verse: and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: Ŋuna n-ni ti me yili ti n yuli jilima, ka n ti chɛ ka o nam zani hal ni saha din ka bahigu.

english_verse: I will be his father, and he will be my son. When he does wrong, I'll see that he is corrected, just as children are corrected by their parents.
translation_verse: Mani n-ni ti nyɛ o ba ka o mi nyɛ m bia, ka o yi ti tum taali, n ni zaŋ fiɛbiga fiɛb’ o n-saɣis’ o kaman ninsalinim’ ni saɣisiri bɛ bihi shɛm.

english_verse: After all, you really are Israel's God, the Lord All-Powerful. You've told me that you will let my descendants be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
translation_verse: Dama nyini Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Tɔbbihi Naa, ka nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni ŋɔ n-kahigi dimbɔŋɔ wuhi mani a dabili ŋɔ ka yɛli, ‘N ni me a yili ti a,’ dinzuɣu ka mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ mali suhukpeeni n-suhir’ a suhigu ŋɔ.

english_verse: David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. Then he sat there and prayed: Lord All-Powerful, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us,
translation_verse: Di saha ka Naa Dauda daa kpe nti ʒini Yawɛ tooni ka yɛli, “Yaa n Duuma NAAWUNI, m mi lee nyɛ ŋuni, ka n daŋ lee nyɛ dini, ka a ti zaŋ ma zali zaashee ŋɔ tatabo ni?

english_verse: I am your servant, and you know my thoughts, so there is nothing more that I need to say.
translation_verse: Yaa n Duuma NAAWUNI, bɔ yɛla ka man’ Dauda lee lan yɛn yɛl’ a yaha? Dama a mi man’ a dabili Dauda.

english_verse: You have done this wonderful thing, and you have let me know about it, because you wanted to keep your promise.
translation_verse: A daalikauli min’ a suhu yubu zuɣu, ka a tum tuun’ kara ŋɔ zaa ni a chɛ ka man’ ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ baŋ li.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are greater than all others. No one is like you, and you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu, Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Naawuni ŋɔ, nyini n-nyɛ ŋun galisi, dama so kani m-be ka nyini, ka Naawuni so mi lan kani m-pah’ a zuɣu kaman ti ni wum shɛm ti tiba ni.

english_verse: And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so your people could live here.
translation_verse: Zuliya shɛli lan be dunia ŋɔ ni ŋ-ŋman’ a niriba Izraɛlnima? Bee nyin’ Naawuni na mi n-tiligi zuliya shɛba n-zaŋ ba leeg’ a dahalali niriba, ka tum tuun’ kara din mali dabiɛm bɛ sani? Bee n-kari zuliya shɛb’ mini bɛ buɣa zaa kpɛhi yɔɣu ka chɛ a niriba maa ni di chɛ ka a yuli du?

english_verse: You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
translation_verse: Yawɛ, nyini n-daa zaŋ a niriba Izraɛlnim’ leeg’ a dahalali niriba ʒiɛmani kam ni, ka leei bɛ Naawuni.

english_verse: Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord God All-Powerful rules Israel, and David's descendants are his chosen kings.”
translation_verse: din ni chɛ ka bɛ tibig’ a yuli ʒiɛmani kam ni ka yɛra, ‘Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Tɔbbihi Naa ŋɔ n-nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni,’ ka a chɛ ka mani a dabili Dauda zuliya nya zaashee zani a tooni.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are God. You have promised me some very good things, and you can be trusted to do what you promise.
translation_verse: “Ka pumpɔŋɔ, yaa n Duuma NAAWUNI, nyini n-nyɛ Naawuni, ka a yɛligu nyɛ yɛlimaŋli, ka a lo a dabili bin’ suŋ ŋɔ.

english_verse: Please bless my descendants and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already promised, and I'm sure that you will bless my family forever.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ n suhir’ a ni a niŋ alibarika niŋ man’ a dabili ŋɔ daŋ ni din ni chɛ ka n daŋ kul ʒiɛya ʒiɛmani kam ni nyin’ Naawuni sani; dama nyini Yawɛ n-daa yɛli lala, ka a daalibarika kul ni be man’ a dabili ŋɔ daŋ ni ʒiɛmani kam ni.”

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard. David's sons were priests.
translation_verse: Ka Jɛhɔiada bia Bɛnaaya su tɔbbi’ shɛb’ bɛ ni daa booni Chɛrɛtinim’ mini Pɛlɛtinim’ la fukumsi. Ka Dauda bidibisi gba daa nyɛ maligumaaniba.

english_verse: David also defeated the Moabites. Then he made their soldiers lie down on the ground, and he measured them off with a rope. He would measure off two lengths of the rope and have those men killed, then he would measure off one length and let those men live. The people of Moab had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
translation_verse: Ka o daa lan chaŋ ti tuhi nyaŋ Mɔabnima, ka chɛ ka bɛ dɔni tiŋa m-pie taba ʒii buta zuɣu, ka o chɛ ka bɛ ku ʒii buyi zuɣu niriba zaa ka chɛ yim zuɣu niriba. Ka Mɔabnim’ maa daa leei Dauda daba, ka yɔri farigu o sani.

english_verse: David set out for the Euphrates River to build a monument there. On his way, he defeated the king of Zobah, whose name was Hadadezer the son of Rehob.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa lan chaŋ ti tuhi nyaŋ Hadadɛza ŋun daa nyɛ Rɛhɔb bia ka nyɛ Zɔba naa la, saha shɛli ŋun Hadadɛza ni daa chaŋ ni o ti tuhi deei Yufretiiz Mɔɣili polo la.

english_verse: He left some of his soldiers in Damascus, and the Arameans had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him. Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda daa tahi tɔbbihi ti ʒili Damaskus ka Sirianim’ maa daa leei Dauda ni su shɛba, ka bɛ yɔri farigu o sani. Ka Yawɛ daa chɛ ka Dauda kul diri nasara o ni chaŋ luɣ’ shɛlikam.

english_verse: Hadadezer's officers had carried their arrows in gold cases hung over their shoulders, but David took these cases and brought them to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa fa Hadadɛza sapashin’ kpamba ni daa mali salima nyɔtaɣiri’ shɛŋa n-zaŋ li kuli Jɛrusalɛm.

english_verse: He also took a lot of bronze from the cities of Betah and Berothai, which had belonged to Hadadezer.
translation_verse: Ka Naa Dauda daa lan kpuɣi daanya pam Bɛta mini Bɛrɔtai din daa nyɛ Hadadɛza ni su fɔntin’ shɛŋa la ni.

english_verse: King Toi of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Toi heard that David had attacked and defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Joram to praise and congratulate David. Joram also brought him gifts made of silver, gold, and bronze.
translation_verse: ka o daa tim o bia Jɔram ni o cham’ ti puhi Naa Dauda ni o zuɣusuŋ, o ni daa tuhi nyaŋ Hadadɛza ka di nasara maa zuɣu. Dama ŋun’ Tɔi mini Hadadɛza daa kul tuhirila tab’ waawaayili. Ka Jɔram daa zaŋ pina din nyɛ salima mini anzinfa ni daanya n-chaŋ ti ti Naa Dauda.

english_verse: David gave these to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold that he had captured from
translation_verse: Ka Naa Dauda daa zaŋ o ni daa tuhi nyaŋ zuliya shɛb’ zaa ka va anzinfa mini salim’ shɛŋa la pahi di zuɣu ti Yawɛ.

english_verse: Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Abiathar the son of Ahimelech, were the priests. Seraiah was the secretary.
translation_verse: Ka Ahitub bia Zadok mini Abiata bia Ahimɛlɛk nyɛ maligumaaniba, ka Sɛraya nyɛ gbansabira.

english_verse: Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
translation_verse: Ka Zɛruya bia Jɔab la daa su tɔbbihi fukumsi ka Jɛhɔshafat Ahilud bia la nyɛ gbansabira wulana.

english_verse: One day, David thought, “I wonder if any of Saul's family are still alive. If they are, I will be kind to them, because I made a promise to Jonathan.”
translation_verse: Dahin shɛli ka Dauda daa ti bɔhi, “Sool daŋ ni ninvuɣ’ so na beni ka n ni niŋ o nirilim Jɔnatan zuɣu?”

english_verse: David called in Ziba, one of the servants of Saul's family. David said, “So you are Ziba.” “Yes, Your Majesty, I am.”
translation_verse: Ka ninvuɣ’ so ŋun daa nyɛ Sool tumtumda ka o yuli booni Ziba la daa be nimaani, ka bɛ daa bol’ o ti Naa Dauda ka o ti bɔh’ o, “Nyini n-nyɛ Ziba?” Ka o garigi yɛli’, “Naa, mani.”

english_verse: David asked, “Are any of Saul's family still alive? If there are, I want to be kind to them.” Ziba answered, “One of Jonathan's sons is still alive, but he can't walk.”
translation_verse: Ka naa daa bɔh’ o “So na be Sool daŋ ni ka n ni niŋ o nirilim kaman Naawuni ni bɔri shɛm?” Ka Ziba daa yɛli naa, “Jɔnatan bidibiga na beni, o mi nyɛla gbarigu.”

english_verse: “Where is he?” David asked. Ziba replied, “He lives in Lo-Debar with Machir the son of Ammiel.”
translation_verse: Ka naa bɔh’ o, “O be ya?” Ka Ziba daa yɛli naa, “O be Ammiɛl bia Makiri la yiŋa Lɔdɛba.”

english_verse: David sent some servants to bring Jonathan's son from Lo-Debar. His name was Mephibosheth, and he was the grandson of Saul. He came to David and knelt down. David asked, “Are you Mephibosheth?” “Yes, I am, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Ka Sool yaaŋa Mɛfibɔshɛt ŋun daa nyɛ Jɔnatan bia maa daa ka Naa Dauda sanna nti lu n-gbani Dauda tooni lu o sizuura. Ka Dauda bol’ o, “Mɛfibɔshɛt.” Ka o garigi yɛli, “N-nyɛ mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili maa.”

english_verse: David said, “Don't be afraid. I'll be kind to you because Jonathan was your father. I'm going to give you back the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul. Besides that, you will always eat with me at my table.”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yɛl’ o, “Di zɔri dabiɛm, dama n ni niŋ a nirilim a ba Jɔnatan zuɣu, ka zaŋ a yab’ Sool ni daa su tiŋgban’ shɛli zaa ti a, ka lan chɛ ka m min’ a laɣindi ʒiini diri sahakam.”

english_verse: Mephibosheth knelt down again and said, “Why should you care about me? I'm worth no more than a dead dog.”
translation_verse: Ka o daa lan lu Dauda sizuura ka yɛli, “Ka mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ mi lee nyɛ ŋuni, ka a ti lihi nya mani ŋun nyɛ ba’ kpiŋ ŋɔ lala”

english_verse: David called in Ziba, Saul's chief servant, and told him, “Since Mephibosheth is Saul's grandson, I've given him back everything that belonged to your master Saul and his family.
translation_verse: Di saha ka naa daa boli Ziba ŋun daa nyɛ Sool tumtumda la na ti yɛl’ o, “Sool min’ o daŋ zaa ni daa su shɛlikam zaa n ni zaŋ li ti a dan’ yaaŋa ŋɔ.

english_verse: When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had beaten them, they made peace with Israel and accepted David as their ruler. The Arameans were afraid to help Ammon any more.
translation_verse: Ka na’ shɛb’ zaa bɛn daa be Hadadɛza sulinsi ni nya Izraɛlnim’ ni tuhi nyaŋ ba maa, ka bɛ daa kana ti tim sandaani niŋ Izraɛlnim’ maa ka zaŋ bɛmaŋ’ ti ba. Di saha zaŋ chana ka Sirianim’ maa daa zɔri dabiɛm ni bɛ lan sɔŋ Ammɔnnim’ yaha.

english_verse: David said, “Nahash was kind to me, and I will be kind to his son.” So he sent some officials to the country of Ammon to tell Hanun how sorry he was that his father had died.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yɛli, “N ni be Hanun Nahash bia ŋɔ yɛlimaŋli biɛhigu kaman o ba ni daa be ma yɛlimaŋli biɛhigu shɛm la.” Dinzuɣu ka o daa tim tuumba ni bɛ chaŋ ti sɔɣi Nahash kuli maa ti o. Ka Dauda tuumba maa daa ti paai Ammɔnnim’ maa tiŋgbɔŋ ni,

english_verse: But Hanun's officials told him, “Do you really believe David is honoring your father by sending these people to comfort you? He probably sent them to spy on our city, so he can destroy it.”
translation_verse: amaa ka Ammɔn nabihi daa yɛli bɛ dan’ Hanun, “A tɛhiya ni Dauda ni tim tuumba na ka bɛ ti sɔɣi kuli maa wuhiri ni yɛlimaŋli biɛhigu ka o be a maa? Dauda timla niriba ŋɔ na ni bɛ ti vihi baŋ yaŋɔ daashili zaa ka tuhi nyaŋ ti.”

english_verse: Hanun arrested David's officials and had their beards shaved off on one side of their faces. He had their robes cut off just below the waist, and then he sent them away.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Hanun daa chɛ ka bɛ gbahi Dauda tuumba maa m-pini bɛ zaa teensi pirigilipirigili bahi ka chɛ pirigilipirigili, ka daa lan ŋmahi bɛ binyɛra bɛ sakpuɣa zuɣu bahi ka chɛ ka bɛ chaŋ.

english_verse: They were terribly ashamed. When David found out what had happened to his officials, he sent a message and told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then you can come home.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yɛli Dauda, ka o tim ni bɛ ti tuhi ba soli, dama vi daa mali tuumba maa pam. Ka naa daa yɛli ba, “Kpalimmiya be Jɛriko hal ka yi teensi maa ti bili, ka yi naanyi kuna.”

english_verse: The Ammonites realized that they had made David very angry, so they hired more foreign soldiers. Twenty thousand of them were foot soldiers from the Aramean cities of Beth-Rehob and Zobah,
translation_verse: Ammɔnnim’ ni daa baŋ ni bɛ leei Dauda dimnim’ maa, ka bɛ daa chaŋ Sirianim’ tinsi ni Bɛtirɛhɔb mini Zɔba nti da Sirianim’ tɔbbi’ shɛb’ bɛn’ nyɛ tinchandiba tuhi’ pisi, ka Maaka naa daa yina ni tɔbbihi tuhili, ka Tɔbinim’ gba daa yina ni tɔbbihi tuhi’ pinaayi.

english_verse: Be brave and fight hard to protect our people and the cities of our God. I pray that the Lord will do whatever pleases him.”

english_verse: and he said to Amnon, “What's the matter? You're the king's son! You shouldn't have to go around feeling sorry for yourself every morning.” Amnon said, “I'm in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.”
translation_verse: Ka Jɔnadab daa bɔhi Amnɔn, “Nabia, bɔ n-niŋ ka a kpalim mali suhugarigu biɛɣukam lala? Yɛlim’ ma din muɣis’ a. Ka Amnɔn daa yɛl’ o, “N kɔre n-kpe m mabia Absalom tizɔpaɣ’ Tama ni.”

english_verse: Jonadab told him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, ask him to send Tamar, so you can watch her cook something for you. Then she can serve you the food.”
translation_verse: Ka Jɔnadab daa yɛli Amnɔn, “Dɔnim’ a garo zuɣu n-niŋ kaman a biɛrimi la, ka a ba yi ti kana ni o ti kaag’ a, nyin’ yɛlim’ o, ‘Chɛ ka n tizɔpaɣ’ Tama kana ti mali bɔrɔbɔro ti ma ka n ŋubi, ka yuun’ o ka o duɣi bindirigu kpe n-zaŋ li na ti gbib’ o nuu ni ka n di.’ ”

english_verse: So Amnon went to bed and pretended to be sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please, ask Tamar to come over. She can make some special bread while I watch, and then she can serve it to me.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Amnɔn daa dɔni n-shiri niŋ kaman o biɛrimi la. Ka naa daa ti kana ni o ti kaag’ o, ka Amnɔn yɛl’ o, “Naa, chɛ ka Tama kana ti mali maha ti ma n ninni, ka zaŋ li na ti gbib’ o nuu ni ka n ŋubi.”

english_verse: David told Tamar, “Go over to Amnon's house and fix him some food.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda daa tim ti yɛli Tama, “Cham’ a tizɔdoo Amnɔn yiŋa nti niŋ bindirigu ti o.”

english_verse: When she got there, he was lying in bed. She mixed the dough, made the loaves, and baked them while he watched.
translation_verse: Ka Tama daa chaŋ o tizɔdoo Amnɔn yiŋa ka o ti domi. Ka o daa niŋ zim ŋɔri mahibiɛli m-mali maha o nini maa ni

english_verse: Then she took the bread out of the pan and put it on his plate, but he refused to eat it. Amnon said, “Send the servants out of the house.” After they had gone,
translation_verse: n-yaai li mahilaa ni ti zal’ o tooni, ka o zaɣisi li ŋubbu, ka yɛl’ o, “Karimi sokam ka bɛ yi ka chɛ ma,” ka bɛ zaa daa yi.

english_verse: he said to Tamar, “Serve the food in my bedroom.” Tamar picked up the bread that she had made and brought it into Amnon's bedroom.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Amnɔn daa yɛli Tama, “Zaŋmi bindirigu maa kpɛhi n dugbɛrili puuni nti gbib’ li a nuu ni ka n di.” Ka Tama daa zaŋ o ni mali mahi’ shɛŋa maa kpɛh’ o tizɔdoo Amnɔn dugbɛrili maa ni.

english_verse: But as she was taking it over to him, he grabbed her and said, “Come to bed with me!”
translation_verse: Amaa o ni daa ti zaŋ li mir’ o na ni o di ka o dii gɔh’ o nuu ni ka yɛl’ o, “N tizɔpaɣa, chɛ ka m min’ a dɔni.”

english_verse: She answered, “No! Please don't force me! This sort of thing isn't done in Israel. It's disgusting!
translation_verse: Ka o daa garigi yɛl’ o, “Aai, m biɛli, di zaŋ kiŋkansi doli ma, dama tuuni ŋɔ na ʒi n-tum Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni, di tum jɛrilim tuuni ŋɔ.

english_verse: Think of me. I'll be disgraced forever! And think of yourself. Everyone in Israel will say you're nothing but trash! Just ask the king, and he will let you marry me.”
translation_verse: Ka ya polo ka n lee yɛn zaŋ vi ŋɔ kpe? Ka sokam ni bol’ a jɛrigu Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ni, dinzuɣu jaande, yɛlim’ naa, o ni zaŋ ma ti a.”

english_verse: But Amnon would not listen to what she said. He was stronger than she was, so he overpowered her and raped her.
translation_verse: Amaa ka o daa zaɣisi wumbu. Ka o ni daa mali yaa gari Tama maa zuɣu, ka o zaŋ kpeengarigu dɔn’ o.

english_verse: Then Amnon hated her even more than he had loved her before. So he told her, “Get up and get out!”
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Amnɔn daa kul lan je Tama yɛlli zaa, hal ka o ni daa je o shɛm maa gar’ o ni daa yur’ o shɛm la gba. Di saha ka Amnɔn daa yɛl’ o, “Yiɣisim’ yi.”

english_verse: She said, “Don't send me away! That would be worse than what you have already done.” But Amnon would not listen.
translation_verse: Amaa ka o daa garigi yɛl’ o, “Aai, m biɛli, a ni kariti ma shɛm ŋɔ n-lee bie n-gari a ni niŋ ma shɛm maa gba.” Amaa ka Amnɔn daa zaɣis’ o yɛligu maa wumbu;

english_verse: He called in his servant and said, “Throw this woman out and lock the door!”
translation_verse: ka daa boli nachimbil’ so ŋun daa tumd’ o tuma na ti yɛl’ o, “Zaŋm’ paɣ’ ŋɔ yihi ka kpari dunoli.”

english_verse: The servant made her leave, and he locked the door behind her. The king's unmarried daughters used to wear long robes with sleeves.
translation_verse: Di saha o daa yɛla saalo’ bɔɣiwɔɣila, dama di saha maa nabipuɣinsi bɛn daa na ʒi dɔbba ni daa yi yɛri saalo’ shɛŋa m-bala. Ka o tumtumda maa daa daag’ o yihi ka kpari dunoli.

english_verse: Tamar tore the robe she was wearing and put ashes on her head. Then she covered her face with her hands and cried loudly as she walked away. Absalom Kills Amnon
translation_verse: Ka Tama daa niŋ tampiligim buɣ’ o zuɣu ka darigi cheeg’ o ni daa ye saalo’ shɛli maa, ka kah’ o nuhi pa o zuɣu ni n-kuhiri pampam chana.

english_verse: Tamar's brother Absalom said to her, “How could Amnon have done such a terrible thing to you! But since he's your brother, don't tell anyone what happened. Just try not to think about it.” Tamar soon moved into Absalom's house, but she was always sad and lonely.
translation_verse: Ka o tizɔdoo Absalom daa nya o ka bɔh’ o, “A tizɔdoo Amnɔn zaŋ a mi dɔni yɔɣu?” Ka daa yɛl’ o, “N tizɔpaɣa niŋmi suɣilo, a tizɔdoo m-bala, di chɛ ka di muɣis’ a.” Di saha ka Tama daa leei bɛ ni ku lan bo paɣ’ so, ka o kpalim ʒi o tizɔdoo Absalom yiŋa.

english_verse: Absalom treated Amnon as though nothing had happened, but he hated Amnon for what he had done to his sister Tamar.
translation_verse: Amaa Absalom daa bi yɛli Amnɔn zaɣ’ biɛɣu bee zaɣ’ viɛlli, dama o daa lan je Amnɔn yɛlli o ni daa zaŋ kiŋkansi niŋ o tizɔpaɣ’ Tama shɛm maa zuɣu. Absalom bɔhi Amnɔn biɛri

english_verse: Two years later, Absalom's servants were cutting wool from his sheep in Baal-Hazor near the town of Ephraim, and Absalom invited all of the king's sons to be there.
translation_verse: Di yuma ayi nyaaŋa ka Absalom daa ti yɛn chɛ o piɛri kɔbiri Baalihazɔr din mini Ifriim bi wɔɣ’ ni tab’ la, ka daa boli nabihi zaa ni bɛ kana.

english_verse: Then he went to David and said, “My servants are cutting the wool from my sheep. Please come and join us!”
translation_verse: Ka Absalom daa chaŋ naa sani ti yɛl’ o, “Naa nyama, a dabili yɛn chɛla o piɛri kɔbiri, ka bɔri ni naa min’ o kpamba zaa kana.”

english_verse: David answered, “No, my son, we won't go. It would be too expensive for you.” Absalom tried to get him to change his mind, but David did not want to go. He only said that he hoped they would have a good time.
translation_verse: Amaa ka naa daa yɛli Absalom, “Aai, m bia, di chɛ ka ti zaa kana, di yi nyɛ lala, ti yɛla ni ti muɣis’ a pam.” Ka Absalom daa kpaŋ omaŋa ni o chɛ ka o chaŋ, amaa ka o daa zaɣisi, ka naɣ’ suhila alibarika niŋ o ni.

english_verse: Absalom said, “If you won't go, at least let my brother Amnon come with us.” David asked, “Why should he go with you?”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Absalom daa yɛli naa, “ N suhir’ a mi, a yi ku chaŋ, nyin’ lee chɛ ka ti mini m mabia Amnɔn chaŋ.” Ka naa daa bɔh’ o, “Bɔzuɣu ka a lee bɔri ni yi min’ o chaŋ?”

english_verse: But Absalom kept on insisting, and finally David let Amnon and all his other sons go with Absalom. Absalom prepared a banquet fit for a king.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Absalom daa kpaŋ omaŋ’ hal ka o ti saɣi ka Amnɔn mini nabihi maa zaa daa dol’ o chaŋ.

english_verse: But he told his servants, “Keep an eye on Amnon. When he gets a little drunk from the wine and is feeling relaxed, I'll give the signal. Then kill him! I've commanded you to do it, so don't be afraid. Be strong and brave.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Absalom daa yɛl’ o tumtumdiba, “Lihimiya, yi yi ti nya ka Amnɔn nyu wain kuli ka n yɛli ya, ‘Kumiya Amnɔn,’ yin’ kumiy’ o. Di zɔriya dabiɛm, mani m-puhi ya. Maliya suhukpeeni ka tum bidibilim tuma.”

english_verse: Absalom's servants killed Amnon, just as Absalom had told them. The rest of the king's sons quickly rode away on their mules to escape from Absalom.
translation_verse: Ka Absalom tumtumdiba maa daa shiri niŋ Amnɔn kaman Absalom ni wuhi ba ni bɛ niŋ o shɛm maa. Di saha ka nabihi maa zaa daa dii yiɣisi ba bɛ buntaansi zo.

english_verse: While they were on their way to Jerusalem, someone told David, “Absalom has killed all of your sons! Not even one is left.”
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa na be soli kuna ka lahibali ti nti to Dauda, “Absalom ku nabihi la zaa, hal bɛ yino bi lan kpalim.”

english_verse: David got up, and in his sorrow he tore his clothes and lay down on the ground. His servants remained standing, but they tore their clothes too.
translation_verse: Di saha ka naa daa yiɣisi dari chah’ o binyɛra, ka teei dɔni tiŋgban’ ni ka kpambaliba bɛn daa be o sani gba dari chahi bɛ binyɛra.

english_verse: Then David's nephew Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, not all of your sons were killed! Only Amnon is dead. On the day that Amnon raped Tamar, Absalom decided to kill him.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Dauda mabia Shamma dapala Jɔnadab daa yɛli, “N dana, di tɛhi ni bɛ ku nabihi maa zaa, Amnɔn kɔŋko n-kpi. Absalom n-chɛ ka bɛ ku o, ka dimbɔŋɔ maa nyɛla o ni pun lo shɛli dahin’ shɛli o ni daa zaŋ kiŋkansi dɔn’ o tizɔpaɣa Tama la zuɣu.

english_verse: Don't worry about the report that all your sons were killed. Only Amnon is dead,
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ n dan’ naa, di chɛ ka di muɣis’ a kaman a bihi maa zaa n-shiri kpi la, dama Amnɔn kɔŋko n-kpi.”

english_verse: and Absalom has run away.” One of the guards noticed a lot of people coming along the hillside on the road to Horonaim. He went and told the king, “I saw some men coming along Horonaim Road.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Absalom daa zo. Ka nachimbil’ so ŋun daa guli nayili maa daa ti kpuɣ’ o zuɣu lihi nya niriba pam ni doli Hɔrɔnaim soli m-baɣisiri zoli kanna.

english_verse: Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, look! Here come your sons now, just as I told you.”
translation_verse: Ka Jɔnadab daa yɛli naa, “Nyama, nabihi maa kunna kaman mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ ni pun yɛl’ a shɛm la.”

english_verse: No sooner had he said it, than David's sons came in. They were weeping out loud, and David and all his officials cried just as loudly.
translation_verse: Nyama, o ni daa kul yɛri maa o noli daa na bi lu tiŋa, ka nabihi maa dii kpɛna nti duhi bɛ yee kumda, ka naa min’ o kpamba zaa gba daa kum pam.

english_verse: David still felt so sad over the loss of Amnon that he wanted to take his army there and capture Absalom.
translation_verse: Ka naa suhu daa ti giri zaŋ chaŋ Amnɔn kum maa polo, o ni daa nya ka o lan kani maa zuɣu, ka o suhu lan yu ni o kari Absalom naba.

english_verse: Joab knew that David couldn't stop thinking about Absalom,
translation_verse: Ka Zɛruya bia Jɔab ni daa ti baŋ ni Naa Dauda suhu lu Absalom ni,

english_verse: The woman from Tekoa went to David. She bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, please help me!”
translation_verse: Tɛkɔa paɣ’ maa ni daa ti paai naa tooni, o daa lumi gbani zaŋ o nini kpa tiŋa n-lu naa sizuura ka yɛli, “Naa, fam ma bahi.”

english_verse: David asked, “What's the matter?” She replied: My husband is dead, and I'm a widow.
translation_verse: Ka naa daa bɔh’ o, “Bɔ n-lee muɣis’ a?” Ka o garigi yɛli, “Mbaye, n yidan’ kpimi ka n kpalim pakoli.

english_verse: I had two sons, but they got into a fight out in a field where there was no one to pull them apart, and one of them killed the other.
translation_verse: Mani ŋun nyɛ a dabipaɣ’ ŋɔ daa malila bidibis’ ayi, ka bɛ daa ti chaŋ puu ni ti zabi, ka so kani ŋun ni goo’ ba, ka yino daa ŋme n-ku ŋun’ la.

english_verse: Now all of my relatives have come to me and said, “Hand over your son! We're going to put him to death for killing his brother.” But what they really want is to get rid of him, so they can take over our land. Please don't let them put out my only flame of hope! There won't be anyone left on this earth to carry on my husband's name.
translation_verse: Ka pumpɔŋɔ bɛ dɔɣiriba zaa suhuri yiɣisimi bahi mani ŋun nyɛ a dabipaɣ’ ŋɔ zuɣu ka yɛli, “Zaŋm’ ŋun ku o mabia maa ti ti ka ti ku o, o ni ku o mabia maa zuɣu din ni chɛ ka bɛ ku falidir’ maa gba. Lala n-ni chɛ ka bɛ kpihi buɣimsal’ shɛli din kpalim maa din ni chɛ ka bɛ kpihim n yidan’ maa zuliya min’ o yuli dunia yili.”

english_verse: “Go on home,” David told her. “I'll take care of this matter for you.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka naa daa yɛli paɣ’ maa, “Lab’ kuli, ka n lihi a yɛlli maa zuɣu.”

english_verse: The woman said, “I hope your decision doesn't cause any problems for you. But if it does, you can blame me.”
translation_verse: Ka Tɛkɔa paɣ’ maa daa yɛli, “N dana, chɛ ka a ni yɛn niŋ shɛlikam zambu ʒi m mini n daŋ zaa zuɣu, ka a min’ a nam ʒiishee ŋɔ ku mali taali di puuni.”

english_verse: He said, “If anyone gives you trouble, bring them to me, and it won't happen again!”
translation_verse: Ka naa daa yɛl’ o, “So yi lan yɛl’ a shɛli, nyin’ tahim’ o n sanna, ka o ku lan tooi niŋ a shɛli yaha.”

english_verse: “Please,” she replied, “swear by the Lord your God that no one will be allowed to kill my son!” He said, “I swear by the living Lord that no one will touch even a hair on his head!”
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ maa daa yɛli, “Naa, n suhir’ a mi, pom’ Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ a Naawuni ŋɔ ni a ku chɛ ka ŋun yɛn bɔhi ʒim yihibu biɛri maa ku o din ni chɛ ka bɛ ku ku m bia maa.” Ka naa daa yɛl’ o, “Hal ka Yawɛ ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu, a bia maa zabigu zaɣ’ yini gba ku yi o zuɣu ni lu tiŋa.”

english_verse: Then she asked, “Your Majesty, may I say something?” “Yes,” he answered.
translation_verse: Ka paɣa maa daa lan yɛli, “N dan’ naa, n suhir’ a, chɛ ka n yɛl’ a yɛtɔɣili ŋɔ.” Ka o yɛl’ o, “Yɛlima.”

english_verse: The woman said: Haven't you been hurting God's people? Your own son had to leave the country. And when you judged in my favor, it was the same as admitting that you should have let him come back.
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ maa daa yɛl’ o, “Ka bɔ n-niŋ ka a lo ni a niŋ Naawuni niriba zaɣ’ biɛɣu? Dama naa yi bi chɛ ka o bia ŋun be yɔɣu la labina yaha, dindina naa yɛtɔɣa ŋɔ nyɛla din gbaag’ omaŋmaŋa.

english_verse: We each must die and disappear like water poured out on the ground. But God doesn't take our lives. Instead, he figures out ways of bringing us back when we run away.
translation_verse: Di kpala talahi ni ti zaa kpi; ti ŋmanila kom din kpaai bahi tiŋa ka nir’ ku lan tooi va li la. Amaa Naawuni ni tiligi ninvuɣ’ so ŋun bi yih’ o bia ŋun zo n-kpe yɔɣu o daŋ ni.

english_verse: Your Majesty, I came here to tell you about my problem, because I was afraid of what someone might do to me. I decided to come to you, because I thought you could help.
translation_verse: Pumpɔŋɔ n kamina ni n ti yɛli nyini n dan’ naa dimbɔŋɔ, dama niriba maa chɛmi ka dabiɛm gbaai ma pam ka n tɛhi ni n yi yɛli nyin’ naa, di pa shɛli a ni niŋ man’ ŋun nyɛ o dabipaɣ’ ŋɔ ni bɔr’ shɛm maa.

english_verse: In fact, I knew that you would listen and save my son and me from those who want to take the land that God gave us.
translation_verse: Dama naa ni wum n fabila maa ka fa m mini m bia ŋun nyɛ a dabili maa ninvuɣ’ so ŋun bɔr’ ni o ku ti n-kpihim ti birili Naawuni ni zaŋ tiŋgbɔn shɛli ti ti ŋɔ ni la nuu ni bahi.

english_verse: I can rest easy now that you have given your decision. You know the difference between right and wrong just like an angel of God, and I pray that the Lord your God will be with you.
translation_verse: Man’ ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ daa lan tɛhimi ni nyin’ naa yɛligu nyɛla din ni ti ma vuhim, dama nyini n dan’ naa ŋmanila Naawuni malaika ŋun mi zaɣ’ suŋ ni zaɣ’ biɛɣu. Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ a Naawuni ŋɔ ni be a sani.”

english_verse: Then David said to the woman, “Now I'm going to ask you a question, and don't try to hide the truth!” The woman replied, “Please go ahead, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka naa daa garigi yɛli paɣ’ maa, “N yi bɔh’ a bɔhigu nyin’ di sɔɣi ma shɛli.” Ka paɣ’ maa yɛl’ o, N dan’ naa, bɔhim’ ma.

english_verse: but only to show you the other side of this problem. You must be as wise as the angel of God to know everything that goes on in this country.”
translation_verse: A dabili Jɔab bɔrimi ni o mali yɛla zali dɛde, dina n-chɛ ka o niŋ lala maa. Amaa n dan’ mali yɛm kaman Naawuni malaika ni mali yɛm shɛm la din ni tooi baŋ binshɛɣukam din be dunia ŋɔ ni.”

english_verse: David turned to Joab and said, “It seems that I have already given my decision. Go and bring Absalom back.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka naa daa yɛli Jɔab, “Nyama, pumpɔŋɔ n saɣ’ a ni bɔri shɛm maa, cham’ ti zaŋ Absalom na.”

english_verse: Joab went to Geshur to get Absalom. But when they came back to Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Di saha ka Jɔab daa yiɣisi chaŋ Gɛshur nti zaŋ Absalom kuli Jɛrusalɛm na.

english_verse: David told Joab, “I don't want to see my son Absalom. Tell him to stay away from me.” So Absalom went to his own house without seeing his father. Absalom Was Handsome
translation_verse: Ka naa daa yɛl’ o, “Chɛ ka o be omaŋmaŋ’ yiŋa, o di chɛ ka n nini nya o. Dinzuɣu ka Absalom daa be omaŋmaŋ’ yiŋa, ka bi chani naa sani.” Absalom mini Naa Dauda tɔɣisiya

english_verse: No one in all Israel was as handsome and well-built as Absalom.
translation_verse: So daa ka Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ zaa ni n-viɛli paai Absalom. O daa ka dalinli o napɔnvari ni zaŋ hal ni o zuɣu ni.

english_verse: His hair grew so thick and heavy that when he got it cut once a year, it weighed over two kilograms.
translation_verse: O daa yi chɛ o zabiri o zaŋdila nayili sania zahim li ka di tibisim nyɛ kaman kilɔgiram ayi.

english_verse: Absalom had three sons. He also had a daughter named Tamar, who grew up to be very beautiful. Absalom Finally Sees David
translation_verse: Absalom daa dɔɣila bidibis’ ata ni bipuɣin’ yino ŋun yuli daa booni Tama, o daa nyɛla paɣisar’ viɛlli.

english_verse: Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years without seeing his father.
translation_verse: Absalom daa niŋ yuma ayi Jɛrusalɛm ka o nini bi nya naa.

english_verse: He wanted Joab to talk to David for him. So one day he sent a message asking Joab to come over, but Joab refused. Absalom sent another message, but Joab still refused.
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Absalom daa tim ti boli Jɔab ni o kana ka o tim o naa sani, amaa ka Jɔab daa zaɣisi kandina. Ka o lan tim pahi buyi, amaa ka Jɔab kul bahi zaɣisi kandina.

english_verse: Finally, Absalom told his servants, “Joab's barley field is right next to mine. Go set it on fire!” And they did.
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Absalom daa yɛl’ o tumtumdiba, “Nyamiya, Jɔab puu m-baɣi m puu ka siŋkaafa be di ni la, chamiya ti niŋ buɣim nyo li. Ka Absalom tumtumdiba maa daa shiri chaŋ ti niŋ buɣim nyo puu maa.”

english_verse: Joab went to Absalom's house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Jɔab daa yiɣisi chaŋ Absalom yiŋa nti bɔh’ o, “Bɔ zuɣu ka a chɛ ka a tumtumdiba nyo m puu buɣim?”

english_verse: Absalom answered, “You didn't pay any attention when I sent for you. I want you to ask my father why he told me to come back from Geshur. I was better off there. I want to see my father now! If I'm guilty, let him kill me.”
translation_verse: Ka Absalom daa garigi yɛli Jɔab, “Nyama, n daa tim na ti bol’ a ni a kana ka n tim a naa sani ka a ti bɔh’ o “Bɔzuɣu ka n lee yi Gɛshur n-kul’ kpɛna? N yi di na kpalim be nimaani di di so. Dinzuɣu, pumpɔŋɔ zaŋm’ ma chaŋ naa sani, n yi mali taali, ŋun’ kum’ ma.”

english_verse: Joab went to David and told him what Absalom had said. David sent for Absalom, and Absalom came. He bowed very low, and David leaned over and kissed him.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Jɔab daa chaŋ naa sani ti yɛl’ o, ka naa daa chɛ ka bɛ boli Absalom, ka o kana ti damdi naa tooni, ka naa daa mɔɣis’ o kpariŋ.

english_verse: Some time later, Absalom got himself a chariot with horses to pull it, and he had
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka Absalom daa bo chɛchɛbuŋ’ mini yuri ka zaŋ ninvuɣ’ pihinu bah’ o tooni.

english_verse: He would get up early each morning and wait by the side of the road that led to the city gate. Anyone who had a complaint to bring to King David would have to go that way, and Absalom would ask each of them, “Where are you from?” If they said, “I'm from a tribe in the north,”
translation_verse: Absalom daa yi daŋdi la yibu n-chani ti zaani tiŋ’ maa dunoli sokpaŋa, ka so daa yi ti mali yɛlli chani naa sani ni o ti mal’ li, o boon’ o mi na ti bɔh’ o, “Tiŋ’ kani ka a lee yina?” Ka dilan’ yi yɛli, “Mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ nyɛla Izraɛl zuliya yaakaza nira.”

english_verse: Absalom would say, “You deserve to win your case. It's too bad the king doesn't have anyone to hear complaints like yours.
translation_verse: Absalom dii yɛrila dilana, “Nyama, a yɛtɔɣa viɛla ka tuhi, amaa naa bi bo so zal’ o zaani ni o wum a ni mali shɛli.”

english_verse: Whenever anyone came to Absalom and started bowing down, he would reach out and hug and kiss them.
translation_verse: Ka ŋunkam daa yi mir’ o ni o damd’ o tiŋa n-lu o sizuura, o teerila o nuu gbaai dilana m-mɔɣis’ o kpariŋ.

english_verse: That's how he treated everyone from Israel who brought a complaint to the king. Soon everyone in Israel liked Absalom better than they liked David.
translation_verse: Lala ka Absalom daa yi niŋdi Izraɛlnim’ bɛn zaa kani naa sanna ni o ti kari bɛ yɛtɔɣa saria ti ba, ka di zuɣu daa chɛ ka Izraɛlnim’ suhuri lɛbigi ŋun’ Absalom polo.

english_verse: Four years later, Absalom said to David, “Please, let me go to Hebron. I have to keep a promise that I made to the Lord,
translation_verse: Di yuma anahi nyaaŋa ka Absalom daa chaŋ ti yɛli naa, “Naa, n suhir’ a mi, chɛ ka n chaŋ Hiburɔn nti pali n ni daa lo Yawɛ alikauli shɛli nimaani.

english_verse: when I was living with the Arameans in Geshur. I promised that if the Lord would bring me back to live in Jerusalem, I would worship him in Hebron.”
translation_verse: Dama mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ ni daa be Gɛshur Aram tiŋgbɔŋ ni la, ka n daa lo alikauli yɛli, ‘Yawɛ yi ti chɛ ka n labi Jɛrusalɛm, n ni jɛm o Hiburɔn.’ ”

english_verse: David gave his permission, and Absalom went to Hebron.
translation_verse: Ka naa daa yɛl’ o, “Cham’ ni suhudoo.” Ka o daa yiɣisi chaŋ Hiburɔn.

english_verse: A messenger came and told David, “Everyone in Israel is on Absalom's side!”
translation_verse: Ka so daa kana ti yɛli Dauda, “Izraɛlnim’ suhuri lɛbigila Absalom polo.”

english_verse: David's officials were in Jerusalem with him, and he told them, “Let's get out of here! We'll have to leave soon, or none of us will escape from Absalom. Hurry! If he moves fast, he could catch us while we're still here. Then he will kill us and everyone else in the city.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda daa yɛl’ o kpamba bɛn be o sani zaa, “Yiɣisimiya ka ti zo, di yi pa lala ti ti ku tooi lan zo n-yi Absalom nuu ni. Ti zomiya yomyom, di yi pa lala o ni gbahi ti pumpɔŋɔ n-niŋ ti zaɣ’ biɛɣu, ka zaŋ takɔbi ku ya ŋɔ nima.”

english_verse: David left behind ten of his wives to take care of the palace, but the rest of his family and his officials and soldiers went with him. They stopped at the last house at the edge of the city.
translation_verse: Naa min’ o niriba maa zaa ni daa yiri tiŋ’ maa ni, bɛ daa zanila yili shɛli din’ bahindi nyaaŋa.

english_verse: Then David stood there and watched while his regular troops and his bodyguards marched past. The last group was the
translation_verse: Ka o kpamba maa zaa daa kana ti gar’ o zuɣu, ka Chɛrɛtinim’ mini Pɛlɛtinim’ ni Gaatinim’ ninvuɣ’ kɔbisiyɔbu bɛn daa doli naa yi Gaat la na zaa daa gar’ o tooni.

english_verse: David spoke to Ittai and said, “You're a foreigner from the town of Gath. You don't have to leave with us. Go back and join the new king!
translation_verse: Di saha ka naa daa yɛli Itai ŋun daa nyɛ Gaat nir’ la, “Bɔzuɣu ka yi mi dol’ ti chana? Labimiya ka yi mini naa maa ti be, dama yinim’ nyɛla tinzunnima, ka lan nyɛ yi yanim’ ni kari shɛb’ bahi na.

english_verse: You haven't been with me very long, so why should you have to follow me, when I don't even know where I'm going? Take your soldiers and go back. I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you.”
translation_verse: Kulla sɔhila ka yi paai kpe na; ka n chɛ ka yi doli ma chani gindi ka m bi mi n ni kuni luɣ’ shɛli polo gba? Zaŋm’ a mabihi maa ka yi labi. Yawɛ ni wuhi ya o yurilim din bi naari min’ o ʒiɛyimtali.”

english_verse: Ittai answered, “Your Majesty, just as surely as you and the Lord live, I will go where you go, no matter if it costs me my life.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Itai daa garigi yɛli naa, “Hal ka Yawɛ ŋun be ŋɔ mini nyini n dan’ naa ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu, nyini n dan’ ni yɛn kpe luɣ’ shɛlikam zaa, di yi nyɛla kum shee bee nyɛvili shee, nimaani ka man’ ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ yɛn kpe.”

english_verse: “Then come on!” David said. So Ittai and all his men and their families walked on past David. David Sends the Sacred Chest Back to Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yɛli Itai, “Dindina garim’ ka ti chaŋ.” Di saha ka Itai ŋun daa nyɛ Gaat nir’ maa min’ o niriba zaa ni bibihi bɛn daa be o sani zaa gari tooni.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem were crying and moaning as David and everyone with him passed by. He led them across Kidron Valley and along the road toward the desert.
translation_verse: Naa min’ o niriba maa ni daa yiri maa, tiŋ’ maa nim’ zaa daa duhila kuŋa n-kum pam. Ka Naa daa chaŋ ti gbaai Kidirɔn kulibɔŋ du, ka o min’ o niriba maa zaa daa zaŋ kpa mɔɣu polo.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests were there along with several men from the tribe of Levi who were carrying the sacred chest. They set the chest down, and left it there until David and his followers had gone out of the city.
translation_verse: Ka Abiata daa yina, nyama, ka Zadok gba mini Lɛvinim’ zaa daa kpuɣi Naawuni Daalikauli Adaka la na ti zaŋ li zali hal ka niriba maa zaa ti yi tiŋ’ maa ni na.

english_verse: Then David said: Zadok, take the sacred chest back to Jerusalem. If the Lord is pleased with me, he will bring me back and let me see it and his tent again.
translation_verse: Di saha ka naa daa yɛli Zadok, “Zaŋmi Naawuni Daalikauli Adaka maa labisi tiŋ’ maa puuni ti zali, Yawɛ nini yi tiɣi ma, o ni lan zaŋ ma labisina ka n nini ti nya di min’ o biɛhigu shee.

english_verse: But if he says he isn't pleased with me, then let him do what he knows is best.
translation_verse: Amaa o yi yɛli ma, ‘N nini bi lan tiɣ’ a.’ Nyama, mani m-bɔŋɔ, O niŋmi ma kaman o ni nya ka shɛli viɛl’ o sani.”

english_verse: Zadok, you are a good judge of things, so return to the city and don't cause any trouble. Take your son Ahimaaz with you. Abiathar and his son Jonathan will also go back.
translation_verse: Ka naa daa lan yɛli Zadok ŋun daa nyɛ maligumaana maa, “Nyama, a mini Abiata zaŋmiya yi bidibis’ ayi bɛn nyɛ a bia Ahimaaz mini Abiata bia Jɔnatan n-labi tiŋ’ maa puuni ni suhudoo.

english_verse: I'll wait at the river crossing in the desert until I hear from you.
translation_verse: Nyamiya, n ni gbaai kulibɔŋ ŋɔ du nti guhiri mɔɣu ni hal ka yi ti tim na ti yɛli ma lahibali din beni.”

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar took the sacred chest back into Jerusalem and stayed there.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Zadok mini Abiata daa zaŋ Naawuni Daalikauli Adaka maa labisi Jɛrusalɛm, ka daa kpalim be nimaani.

english_verse: David went on up the slope of the Mount of Olives. He was barefoot and crying, and he covered his head to show his sorrow. Everyone with him was crying, and they covered their heads too.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Dauda daa chaŋ ti du Olivi tihi Zoli n-chani ka kumda. O daa zaŋla bini pil’ o zuɣu, ka chani napɔn’ zaŋa. Ka ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn zaa daa be o sani gba zaŋ bina pil’ bɛ zuɣuri n-kumdi dol’ o chana.

english_verse: Someone told David, “Ahithophel is helping Absalom plot against you!” David said, “Please, Lord, keep Ahithophel's plans from working!” David Sends Hushai Back as a Spy
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yɛli Dauda ni Ahitɔfɛl gba pahila Absalom zuɣu. Ka Dauda yɛli, “Yawɛ, n suhir’ a mi, chɛ ka Ahitɔfɛl ni yɛn wuhi yikombiɛlim yɛtɔɣ’ shɛŋa zaa leei jɛrilim.”

english_verse: When David reached the top of the Mount of Olives, he met Hushai the Archite at a place of worship. Hushai's robe was torn, and dust was on his head.
translation_verse: Dauda ni daa ti paai zoli maa zuɣu luɣ’ shɛli bɛ ni daa yi jɛmdi Naawuni la, nyama, ka Hushai ŋun nyɛ Ariki nir’ la daa chɛh’ omaŋmaŋ’ binyɛrigu ka kɔri taŋkpaɣu puɣ’ o zuɣu n-ka Naa Dauda sanna.

english_verse: David told him: If you come with me, you might slow us down.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yɛl’ o, “A yi doli ma, a yɛla ni ti muɣisi ma.

english_verse: Go back into the city and tell Absalom, “Your Majesty, I am your servant. I will serve you now, just as I served your father in the past.” Hushai, if you do that, you can help me ruin Ahithophel's plans.
translation_verse: Amaa a yi labi tiŋ’ maa puuni nti yɛli Absalom, ‘N dan’ naa, n ni leeg’ a kpambala. Kaman n ni yi kul nyɛ a ba kpambala shɛm, lala ka n yɛn nyɛ a gba kpambala, dina n-ni chɛ ka a nyaŋ Ahitɔfɛl yikombiɛlim maa ti ma.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests will be there with you, and you can tell them everything you hear in the palace.
translation_verse: Zadok mini Abiata bɛn nyɛ maligumaaniba la be nimaani. Dinzuɣu a yi ti kul wum shɛlikam nayili maa, nyin’ yɛlim’ Zadok mini Abiata bɛn nyɛ maligumaaniba maa.

english_verse: David's advisor Hushai slipped back into Jerusalem, at just about the same time Absalom was coming in.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda zɔsimo Hushai daa labi tiŋ’ puuni ti saɣisi saha shɛli Absalom ni kpɛri Jɛrusalɛm na.

english_verse: David had started down the other side of the Mount of Olives, when he was met by Ziba, the chief servant of Mephibosheth. Ziba had two donkeys that were carrying
translation_verse: Dauda ni daa yiɣisi zoli maa zuɣu n-tirisi tooni biɛla ha, ka Ziba ŋun daa nyɛ Mɛfibɔshɛt tumtumda la daa taɣi bɛ ni pa bun’ shɛb’ gaya kana ti tuhi ba soli. Bunsi maa daa ʒirila bɔrɔbɔro kpil’ kɔbiga mini wain tiwala din kuui zaza yila kɔbiga ni tiwal’ moma bini kɔbiga ni wain koligu pali.

english_verse: “What's all this?” David asked. Ziba said, “The donkeys are for your family to ride. The bread and fruit are for the people to eat, and the wine is for them to drink in the desert when they are tired out.”
translation_verse: Ka naa daa bɔhi Ziba, “Bɔzuɣu ka a ʒi dimbɔŋɔnim’ zaa na?” Ka Ziba garigi yɛl’ o, “Bunsi ŋɔ nyɛla naa min’ o malibu ni yɛn ba shɛba, ka bɔrɔbɔro ŋɔ mini tiwal’ moma ŋɔ nyɛ nachimba bindirigu. Ka wain ŋɔ mi nyɛ bɛ ni shɛb’ bɛn ti tarigi yɔɣu ŋɔ ni ni yɛn nyu shɛli.”

english_verse: “And where is Mephibosheth?” David asked. Ziba answered, “He stayed in Jerusalem, because he thinks the people of Israel want him to rule the kingdom of his grandfather Saul.”
translation_verse: Ka naa daa bɔhi Ziba, “Ka a dan’ bia la lee be ya polo?” Ka Ziba garigi yɛli naa, “Nyama, o kpalim Jɛrusalɛm, dama o yɛlimi, ‘Pumpɔŋɔ Izraɛlnim’ ni zaŋ n yab’ nam ŋɔ ti ma.’ ”

english_verse: David then told him, “Everything that used to belong to Mephibosheth is now yours.” Ziba said, “Your Majesty, I am your humble servant, and I hope you will be pleased with me.” Shimei Curses David
translation_verse: Di saha ka naa daa yɛli Ziba, “Nyama, Mɛfibɔshɛt ni daa su shɛlikam zaa leeg’ a dini pumpɔŋɔ.” Ka Ziba garigi yɛli, “N nyɛla ŋun luri n dan’ sizuura. Chɛ ka nyini n dan’ naa nini kul tiɣiri ma sahakam.” Naa Dauda mini Shimɛi

english_verse: David was near the town of Bahurim when a man came out and started cursing him. The man was Shimei the son of Gera, and he was one of Saul's distant relatives.
translation_verse: Naa Dauda ni daa ti paai Bahurim, ka Sool daŋ ni do’ so ŋun daa nyɛ Gɛra bia ka o yuli booni Shimɛi la daa yina ti turi ba.

english_verse: He threw stones at David, at his soldiers, and at everyone else, including the bodyguards who walked on each side of David.
translation_verse: Hal Naa Dauda kpambaliba zaa mini ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn mali kpiɔŋ ni daa be o nudirigu min’ o nuzaa polo maa zaa yoli, doo maa daa pihila kuɣa labiri Dauda mini ba zaa.

english_verse: Shimei was yelling at David, “Get out of here, you murderer! You good-for-nothing,
translation_verse: Ka Shimɛi daa kul turi ba ka yɛra, “Wara, wara, nyin’ ninvuɣ’ kur’ ŋɔ, nyin’ ninvuɣ’ yoli ŋɔ.

english_verse: the Lord is paying you back for killing so many in Saul's family. You stole his kingdom, but now the Lord has given it to your son Absalom. You're a murderer, and that's why you're in such big trouble!”
translation_verse: A ni daa ku Sool so min’ o yiŋnim’ shɛba, ka di nam zan’ o zaani la biɛri ka Yawɛ bɔhir’ a, ka fa a nam maa ti a bia Absalom maa. Nyama a bahila yoli maa, dama a nyɛla ninvuɣ’ kura.”

english_verse: Abishai said, “Your Majesty, this man is as useless as a dead dog! He shouldn't be allowed to curse you. Let me go over and chop off his head.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Abishai ŋun daa nyɛ Zɛruya bia la daa yɛli naa “Bɔ n-niŋ ka ba’ kpiŋ ŋɔ doli yɛri n dan’ naa zilima lala? Chɛ ka n chaŋ ti ŋma o zuɣu.”

english_verse: David replied, “What will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? If Shimei is cursing me because the Lord has told him to, then who are you to tell him to stop?”
translation_verse: Amaa ka naa daa yɛli, “Yinim’ Zɛruya bihi ŋɔ, wula ka n yɛn niŋ ya? Di yi nyɛla Yawɛ n-yɛl’ o, ‘Tum’ Dauda,’ ŋuni n-lee ni tooi bɔh’ o, “Bɔ n-niŋ ka a niŋdi lala?”

english_verse: Then David said to Abishai and all his soldiers: My own son is trying to kill me! Why shouldn't this man from the tribe of Benjamin want me dead even more? Let him curse all he wants. Maybe the Lord did tell him to curse me.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yɛli Abishai min’ o kpamba maa, “Nyamiya, mmaŋmaŋ’ bia m-bɔri ni o ku ma la, di ni ti be ka Bɛnjamin zuliya ni nir’ ŋɔ? Chɛliy’ o ka o tu ma, dama Yawɛ n-zal’ o lala.

english_verse: But if the Lord hears these curses and sees the trouble I'm in, maybe he will have pity on me instead.
translation_verse: Di pa shɛli o turi ŋɔ zuɣu ni chɛ ka Yawɛ lihi n wahala ŋɔ ka niŋ ma din viɛli zuŋɔ.”

english_verse: David and the others went on down the road. Shimei went along the hillside by the road, cursing and throwing rocks and dirt at them.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda min’ o niriba maa daa lu solɔɣu chana, ka Shimɛi daa be zolɔŋni m-baɣisir’ o luɣili polo dol’ o chani tur’ o, ka labir’ o kuɣa, ka toori taŋkpaɣu chɛr’ o.

english_verse: When David and those with him came to the Jordan River, they were tired out. But after they rested, they felt much better. Hushai Meets Absalom
translation_verse: Ka naa mini ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn zaa daa be o sani maa daa mali ti paai Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili ni ka di wum ba pam, ka o zani nimaani vuhi.

english_verse: By this time, Absalom, Ahithophel, and the others had reached Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ka Absalom min’ o niriba zaa ni Izraɛlnim’ daa chaŋ ti kpe Jɛrusalɛm, ka Ahitɔfɛl gba daa be o sani.

english_verse: David's friend Hushai came to Absalom and said, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Ka Hushai ŋun daa nyɛ Ariki nir’ ka nyɛ Dauda zɔsimo la daa chaŋ Absalom sani ti yɛl’ o, “Naawuni dolimi naa nyɛvili! Naawuni dolimi naa nyɛvili!”

english_verse: But Absalom asked Hushai, “Is this how you show loyalty to your friend David? Why didn't you go with him?”
translation_verse: Ka Absalom daa bɔhi Hushai, “A ʒiɛyimtali zaŋ chaŋ a zo maa sani ni bahindi shɛm m-bala? Bɔ n-niŋ ka a bi dol’ a zo maa chaŋ?”

english_verse: Hushai answered, “The Lord and the people of Israel have chosen you to be king. I can't leave. I have to stay and serve the one they've chosen.
translation_verse: Ka Hushai daa garigi yɛli Absalom, “Aai Yawɛ min’ o niriba ŋɔ ni Izraɛlnim’ ni pii ninvuɣ’ so, o sani ka n yɛn be ka o su ma.

english_verse: Besides, it seems right for me to serve you, just as I served your father.” Ahithophel's Advice
translation_verse: M-pahi, ŋuni ka n lan yɛn jɛm ka pa ni n dan’ Dauda bia? N ni daa kul jɛmd’ a ba shɛm, lala ka n yɛn jɛm a gba.”

english_verse: Absalom turned to Ahithophel and said, “Give us your advice! What should we do?”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Absalom daa bɔhi Ahitɔfɛl, “Wuhim’ ti ti ni yɛn niŋ shɛm.”
