translation_verse: O ni daa na kul yɛri lala saha shɛli maa, ka Jɔnatan, ŋun daa nyɛ maligumaana Abiata bia la dii paana. Ka Adɔnija yɛl’ o, “Kpɛmina, dama a nyɛla ninvuɣ’ suŋ, ka ʒiri lahiba’ suŋ na.”

english_verse: Jonathan answered: No, I don't! David has just announced that Solomon will be king.
translation_verse: Ka Jɔnatan daa garigi yɛli Adɔnija, “Aai, dama ti dan’ Naa Dauda zaŋ Sulemaana leei naa;

english_verse: Solomon rode David's own mule to Gihon Spring, and Zadok, Nathan, Benaiah, and David's special bodyguards went with him. When they got there, Zadok and Nathan made Solomon king. Then everyone celebrated all the way back to Jerusalem. That's the noise you hear in the city.
translation_verse: ka maligumaana Zadok mini anabi Neetan pun booi kpam bah’ o zuɣu ni n-leeg’ o nam Gihɔn; ka bɛ yi nimaani na m-mali suhupiɛlli, dina n-chɛ ka bɛ yɔri vuri tiŋ’ puuni maa. Di vuri ka yi wum maa.

english_verse: Solomon is now king.
translation_verse: Sulemaana ʒini nam ʒiishee.

english_verse: And listen to this! David's officials told him, “We pray that your God will help Solomon to be an even greater king!” David was in his bed at the time, but he bowed
translation_verse: Ka din pahi nyɛla naa kpambaliba kana ni bɛ ti puhi ti dan’ Naa Dauda ni o zuɣusuŋ ka yɛra, ‘A Naawuni ŋɔ chɛ ka Sulemaana yuli du n-gar’ a yuli, ka chɛ ka o nam gar’ a nam.’ Ka Naa Dauda maŋmaŋ’ daa zaŋ o zuɣu silim tiŋa o bindoo zuɣu;

english_verse: and prayed, “I praise you, Lord God of Israel. You have made my son Solomon king and have let me live to see it.”
translation_verse: ka suhi Naawuni yɛli, “Paɣimiya Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni ŋun chɛ ka m bihi ni yino ʒini n nam ʒiishee zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ, ka mmaŋmaŋ’ nini nya li ŋɔ.”

english_verse: Adonijah's guests shook with fear when they heard this news, and they left as fast as they could.
translation_verse: Di saha ka dabiɛm daa gbaai Adɔnija saamba maa zaa, ka bɛ vaai yiɣisi, ka bɛ zaa yinoyino zaŋ kpa o kpabu polo.

english_verse: Someone told Solomon, “Adonijah is afraid of you and is holding onto the corners of the altar. He wants you to promise that you won't kill him.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yɛli Sulemaana, “Nyama, Adɔnija zɔrila nyin’ Naa Sulemaana, dama nyama, o gbaala sara maligu bimbini bin’ yila la gbibi ka yɛra, ‘Faashee Naa Sulemaana daŋ po pɔri yɛli ma ni o ku ku man’ ŋun nyɛ o dabili ŋɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Solomon answered, “If Adonijah doesn't cause any trouble, I won't hurt him. But if he does, I'll have him killed.”
translation_verse: Ka Sulemaana daa yɛli, “O yi nyɛ ninvuɣ’ suŋ, hal o zabigu zaɣ’ yini gba ku lu tiŋa, amaa ninvuɣ’ biɛtali yi be o kɔbili ni, o ni kpi.”

english_verse: Then he sent someone to the altar to get Adonijah. After Adonijah came and bowed down, Solomon said, “Adonijah, go home.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Naa Sulemaana daa tim ka bɛ chaŋ ti siɣis’ o bimbini maa zuɣu na. Ka o daa kana nti damdi lu Naa Sulemaana sizuura. Ka Sulemaana daa yɛl’ o, “Kulim’ a yiŋa.”

english_verse: Not long before David died, he told Solomon:
translation_verse: Dauda ni daa ti miri kum saha shɛli, ka o daa saɣis’ o bia Sulemaana yɛli,

english_verse: My son, I will soon die, as everyone must. But I want you to be strong and brave.
translation_verse: “N yɛn dolila dunianim’ zaa ni doli so’ shɛl’ la. Mali yaa,

english_verse: Do what the Lord your God commands and follow his teachings. Obey everything written in the Law of Moses. Then you will be a success, no matter what you do or where you go.
translation_verse: ka wuhi ni a nyɛla doo, ka deei Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ a Naawuni ŋɔ saɣisigu ka dol’ o soya min’ o zaligunim’ ni o fukumsi zalikpana la ni o zaligu shɛŋa din pahi ni o shɛhira shɛŋa din sabi Musa zaligu ni la, ka di chɛ ka a tɔŋ a ni niŋdi shɛlikam ni min’ a ni kul ŋmaligi luɣ’ shɛlikam polo

english_verse: You and your descendants must always faithfully obey the Lord. If you do, he will keep the solemn promise he made to me that someone from our family will always be king of Israel.
translation_verse: din ni chɛ ka Yawɛ pal’ o ni daa lo ma alikauli shɛli yɛli, ‘A bihi yi ni gbib’ bɛmaŋa, ka doli ma ni ʒiɛyimtali ni bɛ suhuri zaa ni bɛ shia zaa, a kul ku kɔŋ ninvuɣ’ so ŋun ni ʒiini Izraɛl nam ʒiishee la.’

english_verse: Solomon, don't forget what Joab did to me by killing Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether, the two commanders of Israel's army. He killed them as if they were his enemies in a war, but he did it when there was no war. He is guilty, and now it's up to you to punish him
translation_verse: “Ka din pahi nyɛla, a mi Zɛruya bia Jɔab la ni daa niŋ ma shɛm la. O ni daa niŋ Izraɛl tɔbbihi sapashin’ kpamba ayi bɛn yuya nyɛ Abinɛr Nɛr bia mini Amasa Jɛta bia la shɛm la. O daa ku ba la zabili ni kani saha shɛli n-yo bɛ ni daa ku ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ tɔb’ ni la ʒim yihibu samli; ka daa zaŋ ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn ka taali ʒim vie o shɛlɔrigu din lo n sheeni min’ o namda.

english_verse: in the way you think best. Whatever you do, don't let him die peacefully in his old age.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu niŋm’ a ni nya ka di simdi shɛm a yɛm tuma puuni, amaa lee di chɛ ka o zuɣu ti paligi ka o kpi ni suhudoo.

english_verse: Be sure to do something about Shimei son of Gera from Bahurim in the territory of Benjamin. He cursed and insulted me the day I went to Mahanaim. But later, when he came to meet me at the Jordan River, I promised that I wouldn't kill him.
translation_verse: “Ka Gɛra bia Shimɛi ŋun nyɛ Bɛnjamin zuliya ni nira, ka yi Bahurim na la gba beni. O daa tu ma tu’ biɛri dahin’ shɛli n ni daa chaŋ Mahanaim la, amaa o ni daa kana nti tuhi ma soli Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili ni la, n daa po Yawɛ yɛl’ o, ‘N ku zaŋ takɔb’ ku a.’

english_verse: Now you must punish him. He's an old man, but you're wise enough to know that you must have him killed. David Dies
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ, baŋmi ni o nyɛla ninvuɣ’ so ŋun mali taali, dama a nyɛla yɛndana; a mi a ni yɛn niŋ o shɛm chɛ ka o zuɣu piɛlli maa kpe gballi ni ni ʒim.” Naa Dauda kum yɛla

english_verse: he saddled his donkey and went after them. He found them and brought them back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ka Shimɛi daa yiɣisi n-zaŋ gali pa o buŋa n-chaŋ Gaat naa Akishi sani ni o ti bo o daba maa shee. Ka o daa shiri bo n-nya ba n-zaŋ ba lab’ yiŋ’ na.

english_verse: Joab's family will always suffer because of what he did, but the Lord will always bless David's family and his kingdom with peace.
translation_verse: Lala ka bɛ ʒim yihibu maa taali yɛn labina ti ʒini ŋun’ Jɔab min’ o nyaaŋa zuɣu hal ni saha din ka bahigu. Amaa Dauda min’ o nyaaŋa ni o yiŋnim’ ni o nam ʒiishee ni mali suhudoo din yi Yawɛ sanna sahakam.”

english_verse: His son Solomon became king and took control of David's kingdom. Adonijah Is Killed
translation_verse: Ka Sulemaana daa di nam ʒin’ o ba Dauda nam ʒiishee, ka o nam maa daa ba n-zani viɛnyɛliŋga. Adɔnija kum yɛla

english_verse: One day, Adonijah went to see Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, and she asked, “Is this a friendly visit?” “Yes.
translation_verse: Di saha ka napaɣ’ Hagit bia Adɔnija daa ti ka Sulemaana ma Batishiiba sanna. Ka Batishiiba bɔh’ o, “Alaafee ka a kana maa?” Ka o garigi yɛli, “Iin, alaafee”

english_verse: I just want to talk with you.” “All right,” she told him, “go ahead.”
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka o daa yɛli, “M malila yɛtɔɣ’ shɛli ni n yɛl’ a.” Ka Batishiiba yɛl’ o, “Yɛlima.”

english_verse: “You know that I was king for a little while,” Adonijah replied. “And everyone in Israel accepted me as their ruler. But the Lord wanted my brother to be king, so now things have changed.
translation_verse: Ka o yɛli, “A mi ni mani n-daa su nam ŋɔ, ka Izraɛlnim’ zaa daa yu ni mani n-di li, amaa ka nam maa ti ŋmaligi leela n tizo dini, dama Yawɛ n-zaŋ li ti o.

english_verse: Would you do me a favor?” “What do you want?” Bathsheba asked.
translation_verse: Ka pumpɔŋɔ bin’ yini ka m bɔri ni n suh’ a; a mi di mɔŋ ma li.”

english_verse: “All right,” she said. “I'll ask him.”
translation_verse: Ka Batishiiba yɛli, “Di viɛla, n ni yɛli naa ti a.”

english_verse: When Bathsheba went to see Solomon, he stood up to meet her, then bowed low. He sat back down and had another throne brought in, so his mother could sit at his right side.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Batishiiba daa yiɣisi chaŋ Naa Sulemaana sani ni o ti tɔɣis’ o di yɛtɔɣa ti Adɔnija. Ka naa daa yiɣisi ti tuh’ o soli n-damd’ o tiŋa, ka lab’ ti ʒin’ o nam ʒiishee, ka chɛ ka bɛ zaŋ kuɣ’ na nti ti naa ma ka o ʒin’ o nudirigu polo.

english_verse: Bathsheba sat down and then asked, “Would you do me a small favor?” Solomon replied, “Mother, just tell me what you want, and I will do it.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Batishiiba daa yɛli naa, “M bɔri ni n suh’ a la bimbil’ yini, a mi di mɔŋ ma li.” Ka naa yɛl’ o, “M ma, yɛlim’ ma a ni bɔri shɛli maa, dama n ku mɔŋ a li.”

english_verse: “Allow your brother Adonijah to marry Abishag,” she answered.
translation_verse: Ka o yɛli, “Zaŋm’ Abishag Shunɛm paɣisarili la ti a biɛli Adɔnija ka o n-niŋ o paɣa.”

english_verse: Solomon said: What? Let my older brother marry Abishag? You may as well ask me to let him rule the kingdom! And why don't you ask such favors for Abiathar and Joab?
translation_verse: Ka Naa Sulemaana daa yɛl’ o ma, “Ka bɔ n-niŋ ka a suhirila Abishag Shunɛm paɣisarili maa n-tiri Adɔnija? Dindina suhim’ ma nam ŋɔ gba ti o; dama o nyɛla m biɛli, ka maligumaana Abiata mini Zɛruya bia Jɔab la be o polo.”

english_verse: I swear in the name of the Lord that Adonijah will die because he asked for this! If he doesn't, I pray that God will severely punish me.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Naa Sulemaana daa po Yawɛ n-yɛli, “Adɔnija yi bi kɔŋ o nyɛvili yɛtɔɣili ŋɔ zuɣu, Naawuni ŋun’ niŋm’ ma zaɣ’ biɛɣu gar’ lala!

english_verse: The Lord made me king in my father's place and promised that the kings of Israel would come from my family. Yes, I swear by the living Lord that Adonijah will die today.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ Naawuni ŋun be, ka nyɛ ŋun zaŋ ma ʒili m ba Dauda nam ʒiishee, ka me yili ti ma kaman o ni daa lo ma alikauli shɛm la zuɣu, n ni chɛ ka bɛ ku Adɔnija zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ.”

english_verse: “Benaiah,” Solomon shouted, “go kill Adonijah.” So Adonijah died. Abiathar Is Sent Back Home
translation_verse: Di saha maa ka Naa Sulemaana daa tim Jɛhɔiada bia Bɛnaaya ka o chaŋ ti ŋme o luhi ka o kpi. Abiata karibu mini Jɔab kum yɛla

english_verse: Solomon sent for Abiathar the priest and said: Abiathar, go back home to Anathoth! You ought to be killed too, but I won't do it now. When my father David was king, you were in charge of the sacred chest, and you went through a lot of hard times with my father.
translation_verse: Ka naa daa yɛli maligumaana Abiata, “Kulim’ a ya Anatɔt. Dama a di simdila kubu, amaa n ku chɛ ka bɛ ku a pumpɔŋɔ, a ni daa ʒiri Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Naawuni ŋɔ Alikauli Adaka m-be m ba Dauda tooni la min’ a ni daa di m ba wahala balibu kam la zuɣu.”

english_verse: But I won't let you be a priest of the Lord anymore. And so the promise that the Lord had made at Shiloh about the family of Eli came true. Joab Is Killed
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Sulemaana daa kari maligumaana Abiata Yawɛ maligumaanitali tuma ni, ka di chɛ ka Yawɛ ni daa yɛli shɛm zaŋ chaŋ Ɛli yiŋnim’ polo Shilo la niŋ pali.

english_verse: Joab had not helped Absalom try to become king, but he had helped Adonijah. So when Joab learned that Adonijah had been killed, he ran to the sacred tent and grabbed hold of the corners of the altar for protection.
translation_verse: Ka di lahibali daa ti nti to Jɔab, dama Jɔab daa nyɛla ŋun ʒe Adɔnija nyaaŋa hal o ni daa bi ʒe Absalom ŋun’ nyaaŋa la zaa yoli. Ka ŋun’ Jɔab daa zo n-chaŋ Yawɛ Jɛmbu Duu nti gbaai sara maligu bimbini binyila gbibi.

english_verse: When Solomon heard about this, he sent someone to ask Joab, “Why did you run to the altar?” Joab sent back his answer, “I was afraid of you, and I ran to the Lord for protection.” Then Solomon shouted, “Benaiah, go kill Joab!”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yɛli Naa Sulemaana, “Jɔab zo nti bela Yawɛ jɛmbu duu, nyama, o be sara maligu bimbini luɣili ni.” Ka Sulemaana daa tim Jɛhɔiada bia Bɛnaaya ka yɛl’ o, “Cham’ ti ŋme o luhi.”

english_verse: Benaiah went to the sacred tent and yelled, “Joab, the king orders you to come out!” “No!” Joab answered. “Kill me right here.” Benaiah went back and told Solomon what Joab had said.
translation_verse: Ka Bɛnaaya daa chaŋ Naawuni jɛmbu duu maa ni nti yɛli Jɔab, “Naa yɛliya ni a yim’ na.” Amaa ka Jɔab daa yɛli, “Aai, n ni kpi kpe.” Ka Bɛnaaya daa lab’ naa sani nti yɛl’ o, “Jɔab ni yɛli shɛm, ka garigi shɛm m-bɔŋɔ.”

english_verse: Solomon replied: Do what Joab said. Kill him and bury him! Then my family and I won't be responsible for what he did to Abner the commander of Israel's army and to Amasa the commander of Judah's army. He killed those innocent men without my father knowing about it. Both of them were better men than Joab. Now the Lord will make him pay for those murders.
translation_verse: Yawɛ ni zaŋ o ni daa yihi ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ ʒim la taali ʒil’ o, dama o daa gbahi niriba ayi bɛn nyɛ wuntizɔriba gar’ o n-ku ba ka m ba Dauda ʒi di yɛla. Bɛna n-nyɛ: Nɛr bia Abinɛr ŋun daa nyɛ Izraɛl tɔbbihi sapashin’ kpɛm’ la mini Jɛta bia Amasa, ŋun daa nyɛ Juda tɔbbihi sapashin’ kpɛm’ la.

english_verse: Benaiah went back and killed Joab. His body was taken away and buried near his home in the desert.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Jɛhɔiada bia Bɛnaaya maa daa chaŋ ti ŋme o luhi n-ku o, ka bɛ daa zaŋ o ti sɔɣ’ omaŋmaŋ’ yiŋ’ din daa be mɔɣu ni la.

english_verse: Solomon put Benaiah in Joab's place as army commander, and he put Zadok in Abiathar's place as priest. Shimei Is Killed
translation_verse: Ka naa daa zaŋ Jɛhɔiada bia Bɛnaaya maa n-leei tɔbbihi sapashin’ kpɛma n-zali Jɔab zaani, ka zaŋ maligumaana Zadok mi n-zali Abiata zaani. Shimɛi kum yɛla

english_verse: Solomon sent for Shimei and said, “Build a house here in Jerusalem and live in it. But whatever you do, don't leave the city!
translation_verse: Di saha ka naa daa tim ti boli Shimɛi na nti yɛl’ o, “Mɛm’ a yili Jɛrusalɛm ŋɔ n-ʒi kpe, ka miri ka a yi kpe n-chaŋ luɣ’ shɛlikam.

english_verse: If you ever cross Kidron Valley and leave Jerusalem, you will be killed. And it will be your own fault.”
translation_verse: Dama a yi ti yi ya ŋɔ n-chaŋ ti baai du Kidirɔn kulibɔŋ dahin’ shɛli, nyin’ baŋmi ni a ni kpi ka biɛhiŋ kani, ka a ʒim yihibu taali kpalim ʒi amaŋmaŋ’ zuɣu.”

english_verse: About three years later, two of Shimei's servants ran off to King Achish in Gath. When Shimei found out where they were,
translation_verse: Amaa zaŋ chaŋ yuma ata naabu saha, ka di daa ti niŋ daliri ka Shimɛi daba niriba ayi yi o sani n-zo n-chaŋ Maaka bia Akishi ŋun daa nyɛ Gaat naa la sani. Ka bɛ daa yɛli Shimɛi, “Nyama, a daba la be Gaat.”

english_verse: Someone told Solomon that Shimei had gone to Gath and was back.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yɛli Sulemaana ni Shimɛi yila Jɛrusalɛm n-chaŋ Gaat ka labina.

english_verse: Solomon sent for him and said: Shimei, you promised in the name of the Lord that you would never leave Jerusalem. I warned you that you would die if you did. You agreed that this was fair, didn't you?
translation_verse: Ka naa daa tim ti boli Shimɛi na nti bɔh’ o, “N daa bi chɛ ka a po Yawɛ ka n kpah’ a zuɣu ni yɛli ni a yi ti yi kpe chaŋ luɣ’ shɛlikam dahin’ shɛli, nyin’ baŋmi ni a ni kpi ka biɛhiŋ kani? Ka a daa yɛli ma, ‘A ni yɛli shɛm maa viɛla, n ni dol’ a noli.’

english_verse: You have disobeyed me and have broken the promise you made to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ka di chaŋ wula ka a bi dol’ a ni daa po pɔ’ shɛli Yawɛ sani maa mini zaligu shɛli n ni daa zal’ a maa?”

english_verse: I know you remember all the cruel things you did to my father David. Now the Lord is going to punish you for what you did.
translation_verse: Ka naa daa lan yɛl’ o, “A mi amaŋmaŋ’ suhu ni a ni daa tum m ba Dauda tuumbiɛ’ shɛŋa la zaa, dinzuɣu Yawɛ ni labis’ a tuumbiɛri maa zaa ʒil’ a.

english_verse: “Benaiah,” Solomon shouted, “kill Shimei.” So Shimei died. Solomon was now in complete control of his kingdom.
translation_verse: Di saha maa ka naa daa bahi Jɛhɔiada bia Bɛnaaya noli, ka o chaŋ ti ŋme Shimɛi luhi ka o kpi. Di saha ka nam maa daa nya zaashee zani Sulemaana nuu ni.

english_verse: At that time, there was no temple for worshiping the Lord, and everyone offered sacrifices at the local shrines.
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa na bi me Yawɛ jɛmbu duu la zuɣu, niriba daa maani sara la maligu bimbina zuɣu.

english_verse: I'll also give you what you didn't ask for. You'll be rich and respected as long as you live, and you'll be greater than any other king.
translation_verse: Ka n ni lan ti a a ni bi suhi ma shɛli gba pahi. Dina n-nyɛ: N ni ti a azichi mini jilima, ka di chɛ ka bɛ ku zaŋ na’ so m-buɣis’ a hal ni a nyɛvili tariga.

english_verse: Solomon loved the Lord and followed his father David's instructions, but Solomon also offered sacrifices and burned incense at the shrines.
translation_verse: Sulemaana daa yuri Yawɛ, ka dol’ o ba Dauda ni daa zal’ o shɛm, o daa naɣ’ maanila sara maligunim’ ka tuɣindi tulaale zim sara maligu bimbina zuɣu.

english_verse: One night while Solomon was in Gibeon, the Lord God appeared to him in a dream and said, “Solomon, ask for anything you want, and I will give it to you.”
translation_verse: Gibiɔn maa ka Yawɛ daa ti ka Sulemaana sanna zahindi ni yuŋ nti yɛl’ o, “Suhim’ a ni bɔri ni n ti a shɛli.”

english_verse: Solomon answered: My father David, your servant, was honest and did what you commanded. You were always loyal to him, and you gave him a son who is now king.
translation_verse: Ka Sulemaana yɛli, “A daa yur’ a dabili m ba Dauda pam, o ni daa dol’ a ni ʒiɛyimtali mini wuntitali ni biɛritibitali o suhu ni la zuɣu, ka a daa yu o yurilim maa tatabo, ka ti o bidibiga ni o ʒin’ o nam ʒiishee zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ.

english_verse: Lord God, I'm your servant, and you've made me king in my father's place. But I'm very young and know so little about being a leader.
translation_verse: Ka pumpɔŋɔ, Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Naawuni ŋɔ, a zaŋ mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ leei naa n-ʒili m ba Dauda nam maa ʒiishee hal n ni na kul nyɛ bia ŋɔ zaa yoli, ka m mi bi mi n ni yɛn su niriba shɛm.

english_verse: And now I must rule your chosen people, even though there are too many of them to count.
translation_verse: Ka mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ nyɛla ŋun be a niriba bɛn nyɛ a ni pii shɛba, ka bɛ galisi pam ka ka kalinli ŋɔ sunsuuni.

english_verse: Please make me wise and teach me the difference between right and wrong. Then I will know how to rule your people. If you don't, there is no way I could rule this great nation of yours.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu tim’ man’ ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ yɛm din ni zaŋ gbib’ a niriba maa, ka tooi baŋ zaɣ’ suŋ ni zaɣ’ biɛɣu woligibu; dama ŋuni n-lee ni tooi gbib’ a niriba bɛn galisi pam ŋɔ?”

english_verse: God said: Solomon, I'm pleased that you asked for this. You could have asked to live a long time or to be rich. Or you could have asked for your enemies to be destroyed. Instead, you asked for wisdom to make right decisions.
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa yɛl’ o, “A ni suhila yɛm ka bi suhi nyɛvil’ wɔɣinli bee azichi bee a dimnim’ nyaŋbu, amaa ka suhila yɛm din ni chɛ ka a baŋ din tuhi la zuɣu,

english_verse: If you obey me and follow my commands, as your father David did, I'll let you live a long time.
translation_verse: Ka a yi ni doli n soya mini n zaligunima ni n fukumsi zalikpana la kaman a ba Dauda ni daa dol’ li shɛm la, dindina n ni ti a nyɛvili wɔɣinli.”

english_verse: Solomon woke up and realized that God had spoken to him in the dream. english_verse: Asa became king of Judah in the twentieth year of Jeroboam's rule in Israel,
translation_verse: Izraɛl Naa Jɛrɔbɔam ni daa di nam zaŋ chaŋ yuun’ pisi saha ka Asa daa leei Juda naa.

english_verse: He forced the prostitutes at the shrines to leave the country, and he got rid of the idols his ancestors had made.
translation_verse: O daa kari dɔbba dagɔr’ tuma tiŋgbani maa ni, ka wurim buɣ’ shɛŋa zaa o yaannim’ ni daa me n-zal’ la.

english_verse: As long as Asa lived, he was completely faithful to the Lord, even though he did not destroy the local shrines.
translation_verse: Asa daa bi wurim luɣ’ shɛŋa bɛ ni daa jɛmdi buɣa la, amaa di zaa yoli, o daa ʒe Yawɛ yim o suhu ni hal ni o nyɛvili tariga.

english_verse: One time, Baasha invaded Judah and captured the town of Ramah. He started making the town stronger, so he could put troops there to stop people from going in and out of Judah.
translation_verse: Izraɛl Naa Baasha daa ti chaŋmi ti liri Judanima, ka me Rama zali ni o chɛ ka so ku lan tooi yi Juda Naa Asa sani chaŋ luɣ’ shɛli bee n-yi shɛli polo ka o sanna.

english_verse: When Asa heard about this, he took the silver and gold from his palace and from the Lord's temple. He gave it to some of his officials and sent them to Damascus with this message for King Benhadad of Syria:
translation_verse: Di saha ka Asa daa zaŋ anzinfa mini salima din zaa be Yawɛ jɛmbu duu mini nayili n-ti o kpambaliba n-tim ba ni bɛ zaŋm’ li ti ti Siria Naa Bɛnhadad ŋun daa nyɛ Tabirimmɔn bia, ka nyɛ Hɛziɔn yaaŋa ka be Damaskus la, ka yɛl’ o,

english_verse: “Our fathers signed a peace treaty. Why don't we do the same thing? This silver and gold is a present for you. So, would you please break your treaty with Baasha and force him to leave my country?”
translation_verse: “Chɛ ka ti laɣ’ tab’ zɔri m-be kaman m ba min’ a ba ni daa be shɛm la. Nyama, n zaŋla anzinfa mini salima ŋɔ ti a pini. Saɣimm’ a mini Izraɛl Naa Baasha zɔtal’ la, ka di zuɣu chɛ ka o zaŋ o tɔbbihi yiɣisi ka chɛ ma.”

english_verse: Benhadad did what Asa asked and sent the Syrian army into Israel. They captured the towns of Ijon, Dan, and Abel-Bethmaacah, and the territories of Chinneroth and Naphtali.
translation_verse: Ka Bɛnhadad daa wum Naa Asa ni yɛli shɛm maa, ka tim o sapashin’ kpamba mini bɛ tɔbbihi ka bɛ chaŋ ti liri Izraɛlnim’ fɔntinsi n-tuhi nyaŋ Ijɔn mini Dan ni Ɛbɛlibɛtimaaka ni Kinɛrɔt zaa zaŋ tabili Naftali tiŋgbani zaa.

english_verse: When Baasha heard about it, he left Ramah and went back to Tirzah.
translation_verse: Baasha ni daa wum lala, ka o chɛ Rama mɛbu, ka be Tiriza.

english_verse: Everything else Asa did while he was king, including his victories and the towns he rebuilt, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. When he got older, he had a foot disease.
translation_verse: Asa tuun’ shɛŋa din pahi min’ o kpiɔŋ ni o ni daa tum shɛlikam zaa ni o ni daa me tin’ shɛŋa zaa, bɛ sab’ di yɛla niŋ Juda nanim’ litaafi ni. Amaa o ni daa ti kurigi, naba polo dɔro n-daa gbaag’ o.

english_verse: Nadab son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in Asa's second year as king of Judah, and he ruled two years.
translation_verse: Naa Asa ni daa di nam zaŋ chaŋ yuma ayi saha, ka Nadab Jɛrɔbɔam bia daa leei Izraɛl naa. O daa diya su Izraɛlnim’ la yuma ayi.

english_verse: Nadab disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of his father, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: O daa tum alahichi Yawɛ sani, ka dol’ o ba soli tum alahichi ka chɛ ka Izraɛlnim’ gba tum alahichi.

english_verse: The Lord's prophet Ahijah had earlier said, “Not one man or boy in Jeroboam's family will be left alive.” And, as soon as Baasha became king, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family,
translation_verse: Baasha ni daa kul di nam maa, di daa bi yuui ka o ku Jɛrɔbɔam yiŋnim’ zaa kaman Yawɛ ni daa chɛ ka anabi Ahija Shilo nir’ la yɛli shɛm la. O daa bi chɛ hal bɛ ni ninvuɣ’ yino gba; o daa kula bɛ zaa.

english_verse: Everything else Nadab did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Nadab ni daa tum tuun’ shɛŋa pahi min’ o ni daa pun tum tuun’ shɛlikam zaa, bɛ sab’ di yɛla niŋ Izraɛl nanim’ litaafi ni.

english_verse: King Asa of Judah and King Baasha of Israel were always at war. King Baasha of Israel
translation_verse: Asa mini Izraɛl Naa Baasha daa kul tuhirila tab’ tɔbu hal ni bɛ nyɛviya tariga. Izraɛl Naa Baasha yɛla

english_verse: Baasha son of Ahijah became king of Israel in Asa's third year as king of Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Juda Naa Asa ni daa di nam zaŋ chaŋ yuma ata saha, ka Ahija bia Baasha daa leei Izraɛlnim’ zaa naa n-ʒi Tiriza. O daa niŋla nam maa ni yuun’ pisinaanahi.

english_verse: Baasha also disobeyed the Lord by acting like Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: O daa tum alahichi Yawɛ sani, ka daa doli Jɛrɔbɔam daalahichi tumbu soli min’ o ni daa chɛ ka Izraɛlnim’ tum alahichi shɛl’ la soli.

english_verse: The Lord sent Jehu son of Hanani to say to Baasha:
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa chɛ ka o yɛligu paai Hanani bia Jɛhu zaŋ chaŋ Baasha polo yɛli,

english_verse: Nobody knew who you were until I, the Lord, chose you to be the leader of my people Israel. And now you're acting exactly like Jeroboam by causing the Israelites to sin. What you've done has made me so angry
translation_verse: “A daa pala shɛli ka n duh’ a ka piig’ a leei n niriba Izraɛlnim’ zuɣulana. Ka a mi ti dolila Jɛrɔbɔam soli n-chɛ ka n niriba Izraɛlnim’ maa tum alahichi, ka bɛ ni tum alahichi shɛŋa maa zuɣu chɛ ka n suhu yiɣisi.

english_verse: that I will destroy you and your family, just as I did the family of Jeroboam.
translation_verse: Nyama, n ni kpihim nyin’ Baasha min’ a daŋ niriba zaa birili; ka niŋ a yiŋa kaman n ni daa niŋ Nɛbat bia Jɛrɔbɔam yiŋ’ shɛm la.

english_verse: Dogs will eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
translation_verse: Ka ninvuɣ’ so ŋun nyɛ Baasha daŋ ni nir’ yi kpi yiŋa, bahi n-yɛn ŋub’ o; ka ŋun mi kpi mɔɣu ni, juri n-yɛn di o.”

english_verse: Baasha made the Lord very angry, and that's why the Lord gave Jehu this message for Baasha and his family. Baasha constantly disobeyed the Lord by following Jeroboam's sinful example—but even worse, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family! Everything else Baasha did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. Baasha died and was buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah became king. King Elah of Israel
translation_verse: Ka din pahi nyɛla, Yawɛ daa zaŋ o ni bɔri ni o yɛli Baasha min’ o daŋ niriba shɛm n-yɛlila Hanani bia anabi Jɛhu, o ni daa tum alahichi shɛŋa Yawɛ san’ la zaa min’ o nuhi tuun’ shɛŋa o ni daa tum n-chɛ ka Yawɛ suhu yiɣisi, ka daa doli Jɛrɔbɔam biɛhigu soli, ka lan nyɛ ŋun daa ku Jɛrɔbɔam min’ o daŋ niriba la zuɣu. Izraɛl naa Ɛla yɛla

english_verse: Elah son of Baasha became king of Israel after Asa had been king of Judah for
translation_verse: Juda Naa Asa ni daa di nam zaŋ chaŋ yuun’ pisinaayɔbu saha, ka Baasha bia Ɛla daa di Izraɛl nam ʒi Tiriza. O daa niŋla nam maa ni yuma ayi.

english_verse: Omri did more evil things than any king before him.
translation_verse: Ka Omri daa ti tum alahichi Yawɛ sani n-gari na’ shɛb’ bɛn zaa daa daŋ o tooni la.

english_verse: Zimri commanded half of Elah's chariots, and he made plans to kill Elah. One day, Elah was in Tirzah, getting drunk at the home of Arza, his prime minister,
translation_verse: Amaa ka Zimiri ŋun daa nyɛ o sapashin’ so ŋun su o chɛchɛbunsi pirigili fukumsi la daa lo nia biɛɣu zaŋ chaŋ o polo. Dahin shɛli ka Naa Ɛla daa ti chaŋ Tiriza, do’ so ŋun yuli booni Ariza ka o su nayili fukumsi la yiŋa nti nyu dam kuli,

english_verse: when Zimri went there and killed Elah. So Zimri became king in the twenty-seventh year of Asa's rule in Judah.
translation_verse: ka Zimiri daa kana nti ŋme o luhi ku o; ka daa di nam zan’ o zaani. Juda Naa Asa ni daa di nam zaŋ chaŋ yuun’ pisinaayopɔin saha ka dimbɔŋɔ daa niŋ maa.

english_verse: As soon as Zimri became king, he killed everyone in Baasha's family. Not one man or boy in his family was left alive—even his close friends were killed.
translation_verse: Zimiri ni daa kul di n-ʒin’ o nam ʒiishee, di daa bi yuui ka o ku Baasha daŋ niriba zaa. O daa ku dɔbba bɛn nyɛ o daŋ ni niriba min’ o zɔnim’ zaa.

english_verse: Baasha's family was completely wiped out, just as the Lord's prophet Jehu had warned.
translation_verse: Zimiri daa ku Baasha daŋ niriba maa zaa kaman Yawɛ ni daa chɛ ka anabi Jɛhu yɛli shɛm zaŋ chaŋ Naa Baasha polo la.

english_verse: Everything else Elah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Zimri of Israel
translation_verse: Ka Naa Ɛla ni daa tum tuun’ shɛŋa pahi min’ o ni daa pun tum tuun’ shɛlikam zaa, bɛ sab’ di yɛla niŋ Izraɛl nanim’ litaafi ni. Izraɛl naa Zimiri yɛla

english_verse: Zimri became king of Israel in Asa's twenty-seventh year as king of Judah, but he ruled only seven days from Tirzah. Israel's army was camped near Gibbethon in Philistia under the command of Omri. The soldiers heard that Zimri had killed Elah, and they made Omri their king that same day.
translation_verse: Tɔbbihi bɛn daa doya maa ni daa wum li, bɛ yɛlimi, “Zimiri lo nia biɛɣu n-ku naa.” Dinzuɣu ka Izraɛlnim’ zaa daa zaŋ Omri ŋun daa nyɛ sapashin’ kpɛm’ la n-leei Izraɛl naa sansani maa ni dindali maa.

english_verse: At once, Omri and his army marched to Tirzah and attacked.
translation_verse: Ka Omri mini Izraɛl tɔbbihi zaa daa yi Gibɛtɔn n-chaŋ ti teei gili Tiriza.

english_verse: When Zimri saw that the town was captured, he ran into the strongest part of the palace and killed himself by setting it on fire.
translation_verse: Zimiri ni daa baŋ ni bɛ nyaŋ bɛ tiŋ’ maa nim’ maa, ka o daa du nayili birini nti niŋ buɣim nyo nayili maa, ka di di n-ku omaŋmaŋa.

english_verse: Everything else Zimri did while he was king, including his rebellion against Elah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Omri of Israel
translation_verse: Ka Zimiri ni daa tum tuun’ shɛŋa pahi min’ o ni daa lo nia biɛ’ shɛli maa, bɛ sab’ di yɛla niŋ Izraɛl nanim’ litaafi ni. Izraɛl Naa Omri yɛla

english_verse: After Zimri died, some of the Israelites wanted Tibni son of Ginath to be king, but others wanted Omri.
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa Izraɛlnim’ daa pirigila buyi; bɛ pirigili daa bɔri ni bɛ zaŋla Ginat bia Tibini leei naa, ka pirigili mi bɔri ni bɛ zaŋla Omri leei naa.

english_verse: in the thirty-first year of Asa's rule in Judah. Omri ruled Israel for twelve years. The first six years he ruled from Tirzah,
translation_verse: Juda Naa Asa ni daa di nam zaŋ chaŋ yuun’ pihita ni yini saha, ka Omri daa leei Izraɛl naa maa. O daa niŋla o nam maa ni yuun’ pinaayi. O daa diya ʒinila Tiriza yuma ayɔbu.

english_verse: He acted just like Jeroboam and made the Lord God of Israel angry by causing the Israelites to sin and to worship idols.
translation_verse: Dama o daa dolila Nɛbat bia Jɛrɔbɔam soli, ka tumdi alahichi shɛŋa o ni daa tum n-chɛ ka Izraɛlnim’ jɛm buɣa n-tum alahichi, ka di chɛ ka Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni ŋɔ suhu yiɣisi la.

english_verse: Everything else Omri did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Ka Omri ni daa tum tuun’ shɛŋa pahi min’ o ni daa wuhi kpiɔŋ shɛm, bɛ sab’ di yɛla niŋ Izraɛl nanim’ litaafi ni.

english_verse: Omri died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab became king. King Ahab of Israel
translation_verse: Ka Omri daa ti kani, ka bɛ sɔɣ’ o Samaria; ka o bia Ɛhab daa di nam zan’ o zaani. Izraɛl Naa Ɛhab yɛla

english_verse: Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa's rule in Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Juda Naa Asa ni daa di nam zaŋ chaŋ yuun’ pihinahaayika saha, ka Omri bia Ɛhab daa leei Izraɛl naa. O daa diya ʒinila Samaria n-su Izraɛlnim’ la yuun’ pisinaayi.

english_verse: Ahab did more things to disobey the Lord than any king before him.
translation_verse: Ka Ɛhab ŋun daa nyɛ Omri bia la daa tum alahichi Yawɛ sani n-gari na’ shɛb’ bɛn zaa daa daŋ o tooni la.

english_verse: He acted just like Jeroboam. Even worse, he married Jezebel the daughter of King Ethbaal of Sidon and started worshiping Baal.
translation_verse: O daa bi nya ka di nyɛ shɛli ni o tum Nɛbat bia Jɛrɔbɔam ni daa tum alahichi shɛŋa la tatabo. O daa kpuɣila Sidɔn Naa Ɛtibaal bipuɣiŋga Jɛzibɛl n-niŋ o paɣa, ka daa jɛmdi buɣili Baal.

english_verse: Ahab built an altar and temple for Baal in Samaria
translation_verse: O daa mɛla buɣili Baal maligu bimbini zali o ni daa me Baal jɛmbu du’ shɛli zali Samaria la puuni.

english_verse: and set up a sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. Ahab did more to make the Lord God of Israel angry than any king of Israel before him.
translation_verse: Ɛhab daa lan mɛla buɣili Ashɛra gba binnani zali. O daa tum din ni yiɣisi Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ Duuma Naawuni ŋɔ suhu n-gari Izraɛl na’ shɛb’ bɛn zaa daa daŋ o tooni la.

english_verse: While Ahab was king, a man from Bethel named Hiel rebuilt the town of Jericho. But while Hiel was laying the foundation for the town wall, his oldest son Abiram died. And while he was finishing the gates, his youngest son Segub died. This happened just as the Lord had told Joshua to say many years ago.
translation_verse: O ʒiɛman’ ni ka Hiɛl ŋun daa yi Bɛtɛl na daa lab’ me Jɛriko zali. Amaa o ni daa zali di tanzaa, ka o bidib’ kpɛm’ Abiram kpi; ka o daa ti mali duno’ yɔra n-yo li, ka o bidibiga Sɛgub ŋun nyɛ biasani kpi. Dimbɔŋɔ daa niŋmi kaman Yawɛ ni daa chɛ ka Jɔshua Nan bia yɛli shɛm la.

english_verse: Elijah was a prophet from Tishbe in Gilead. One day he went to King Ahab and said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord, the God of Israel. And I swear in his name that it won't rain until I say so. There won't even be any dew on the ground.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Ilaija ŋun daa nyɛ Tishibi nira ka yi Tishibi din be Giliad na la daa yɛli Naa Ɛhab, “Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ Duuma Naawuni ŋun be ka nyɛ n ni ʒe so tooni ŋɔ zuɣu, di ni niŋ yuma shɛm ka saa bee maligim ku lan tɔɣisi lu tiŋ’ na, naɣila mani nti yɛli ni di niŋm’ lala yaha.”

english_verse: Later, the Lord said to Elijah,
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Ilaija,

english_verse: “Leave and go across the Jordan River so you can hide near Cherith Creek.
translation_verse: “Yim’ kpe n-zaŋ kpa wulimpuhili polo n-chaŋ ti sɔɣi dɔni miri Chɛrit kulibɔŋ din be Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili wulimpuhili polo la.

english_verse: You can drink water from the creek, and eat the food I've told the ravens to bring you.”
translation_verse: Kom be kulibɔŋ maa ni ka a ni nyura, ka n zali kahiŋkɔri ni bɛ tahiri bindirigu na ti tir’ a.”

english_verse: Ravens brought him bread and meat twice a day, and he drank water from the creek.
translation_verse: Ka kahiŋkɔri maa daa shiri tahiri bindirigu mini nimdi na nti tir’ o asiba ni zaawuni; ka o daa nyuri kulibɔŋ maa ni kom.

english_verse: But after a while, it dried up because there was no rain. Elijah Helps a Widow in Zarephath
translation_verse: Ka di daa niŋ daba ayi ha, ka kulibɔŋ maa kom maa nyuui, saa ni daa bi lan miri bɛ tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni la zuɣu.

english_verse: The Lord told Elijah,
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Ilaija,

english_verse: “Go to the town of Zarephath in Sidon and live there. I've told a widow in that town to give you food.”
translation_verse: “Yiɣisim’ chaŋ Zarɛfat din be Sidɔn tiŋgban’ ni la nti be ni. Nyama, n yɛli pako’ so ŋun be nimaani ni o tim a bindirigu.”

english_verse: When Elijah came near the town gate of Zarephath, he saw a widow gathering sticks for a fire. “Would you please bring me a cup of water?” he asked.
translation_verse: Ka Ilaija daa yiɣisi chani Zarɛfat nti yɛn kpe tiŋ’ maa ni ka nya pako’ so ka o be nimaani pihiri dari, ka o bol’ o yɛl’ o, “Kpɛm’ ti tooi kom biɛla niŋ pipia ni ti ma na ka n nyu.”

english_verse: As she left to get it, he asked, “Would you also please bring me a piece of bread?”
translation_verse: Pakoli maa ni da kpɛri ni o ti tooi kom maa na, ka o lan bol’ o yɛli, “Piim’ mahili mali ma na.”

english_verse: The widow answered, “In the name of the living Lord your God, I swear that I don't have any bread. All I have is a handful of flour and a little olive oil. I'm on my way home now with these few sticks to cook what I have for my son and me. After that, we will starve to death.”
translation_verse: Ka pakoli maa yɛl’ o, “Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ a Naawuni ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu, m bi mali maha zali. Zim din ni pali nukurigu kɔŋko m-be duɣu ni ni kpam biɛla din be kpaŋman’ ni. Dina ka m pihiri dari biɛla ŋɔ ni n kpe nti mali ka m mini m bidibiga ŋɔ zaŋ ŋub’ ka naanyi kpi.”

english_verse: Elijah said, “Everything will be fine. Do what you said. Go home and fix something for you and your son. But first, please make a small piece of bread and bring it to me.
translation_verse: Ka Ilaija yɛl’ o, “Di chɛ ka a suhu zɔhira; cham’ ti niŋ a ni yɛli shɛm maa, amaa lee daŋ mali mahili zaɣ’ bila n-ti ma na, ka naanyi chaŋ ti mal’ a min’ a bidibiga maa mi dini.

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel has promised that your jar of flour won't run out and your bottle of oil won't dry up before he sends rain for the crops.”
translation_verse: Dama Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni ŋɔ yɛliya ni zim maa ku naai di duɣu ni, ka kpam la gba ku naai di ŋman’ ni hal ti paai dahin’ shɛli ŋun’ Yawɛ ni yɛn chɛ ka saa mi.”

english_verse: The widow went home and did exactly what Elijah had told her. She and Elijah and her family had enough food for a long time.
translation_verse: Ka pakoli maa daa kpe nti shiri niŋ kaman Ilaija ni yɛli shɛm maa, ka o min’ o bidibiga maa ni o yiŋnim’ zaa kul nyari bindirigu diri dabisi’ gbaliŋ.

english_verse: The Lord kept the promise that his prophet Elijah had made, and she did not run out of flour or oil. Elijah Brings a Boy Back to Life
translation_verse: Ka zim maa daa shiri bi naai di duɣu maa ni; ka kpam la gba daa bi naai di ŋmani maa ni kaman Yawɛ ni daa chɛ ka Ilaija pun yɛli shɛm la.

english_verse: Several days later, the son of the woman who owned the house got sick, and he kept getting worse, until finally he died.
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka pakoli ŋun su yili maa bidibiga maa daa ti biɛra, ka di muɣis’ o hal ka o ti tarigi.

english_verse: The woman shouted at Elijah, “What have I done to you? I thought you were God's prophet. Did you come here to cause the death of my son as a reminder that I've sinned against God?”
translation_verse: Ka pakoli maa daa bɔhi Ilaija, “Bɔ ka n lee niŋ nyini ŋun nyɛ Naawuni nir’ ŋɔ? A kamina ni a ti teei ma n daalahichi yɛla ka chɛ ka m bidibiga ŋɔ kpi?”

english_verse: “Bring me your son,” Elijah said. Then he took the boy from her arms and carried him upstairs to the room where he was staying. Elijah laid the boy on his bed
translation_verse: Ka Ilaija yɛl’ o, “Zaŋm’ a bia maa ti ma.” Ka o daa deei bia maa paɣ’ maa sani n-zaŋ o du jirambisa zuɣusaa o ni daa be du’ shɛl’ ni nti zaŋ o sɔŋ omaŋmaŋ’ garo zuɣu;

english_verse: and prayed, “Lord God, why did you do such a terrible thing to this woman? She's letting me stay here, and now you've let her son die.”
translation_verse: ka duh’ o yee suhi Naawuni bɔh’ o, “Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ n Naawuni ŋɔ, bɔ n-niŋ ka a chɛ ka n ni kana ti be pako’ so sani ŋɔ bidibiga ŋɔ kpi n-ti o suhusaɣiŋgu?”

english_verse: Elijah stretched himself out over the boy three times, while praying, “Lord God, bring this boy back to life!”
translation_verse: Di saha ka o daa teeg’ omaŋ’ pa bia maa zuɣu napɔŋ buta, ka suhi Yawɛ, yɛli, “Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ n Naawuni ŋɔ, chɛ ka bia ŋɔ nyɛvili lab’ o ni na yaha.”

english_verse: The Lord answered Elijah's prayer, and the boy started breathing again.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa deei Ilaija suhigu, ka chɛ ka bia maa nyɛvili lab’ o ni na ka o neei.

english_verse: Elijah picked him up and carried him downstairs. He gave the boy to his mother and said, “Look, your son is alive.”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaija daa zaŋ bia maa yi jirambisa maa zuɣu n-siɣina kpɛhi yili maa ni nti ti o ma maa ka yɛli, “Nyama, a bia maa lan leei nyɛvililana yaha!”

english_verse: “You are God's prophet!” the woman replied. “Now I know that you really do speak for the Lord.”
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ maa yɛli Ilaija, “Pumpɔŋɔ n yipa baŋya ni a nyɛla Naawuni nira, ka Yawɛ yɛligu shɛli a ni mali tɔɣisiri nyɛla yɛlimaŋli.”

english_verse: For three years no rain fell in Samaria, and there was almost nothing to eat anywhere. The Lord said to Elijah, “Go and meet with King Ahab. I will soon make it rain.” So Elijah went to see Ahab.
translation_verse: Ka Ilaija daa yiɣisi chaŋ ni o ti zaŋ omaŋ’ wuhi Naa Ɛhab. Kum daa mii Samarianim’ pam di saha maa.

english_verse: At that time Obadiah was in charge of Ahab's palace, but he faithfully worshiped the Lord. In fact, when Jezebel was trying to kill the Lord's prophets, Obadiah hid
translation_verse: ka Jɛzibɛl ni daa ti kuri Yawɛ daanabinim’ la, ŋuna n-daa zaŋ anabinim’ kɔbiga m-pirigi ba pihinunu n-sɔɣi vokaba ni, ka tiri ba bindirigu mini kom).

english_verse: and said, “We have to find something for our horses and mules to eat. If we don't, we will have to kill them. Let's look around every creek and spring in the country for some grass.
translation_verse: Ka Ɛhab daa yɛl’ o, “Cham’ gili tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ kulibɔna mini vinvama zaa ni nti lihi nya ti ni nya mɔri ti ti yuri mini ti buntaansi ŋɔ n-tiligi ba din ni chɛ ka ti ku kɔŋ bɛ shɛba.”

english_verse: As Obadiah was walking along, he met Elijah. Obadiah recognized him, bowed down, and asked, “Elijah, is it really you?”
translation_verse: Obadia ni daa gbaai chandi, o nini nyabu yim ka o ti nya Ilaija m-baŋ o, ka teei dɔni n-zaŋ o nina kpa tiŋa ka yɛli, “N dan’ Ilaija, nyini m-bala?”

english_verse: Obadiah replied: King Ahab would kill me if I told him that. And I haven't even done anything wrong.
translation_verse: Ka Obadia bɔhi Ilaija, “Tuumbiɛ’ bɔ ka n lee tum ka a bɔri ni a chɛ ka Ɛhab ku man’ ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ?

english_verse: I swear to you in the name of the living Lord your God that the king has looked everywhere for you. He sent people to look in every country, and when they couldn't find you, he made the leader of each country swear that you were not in that country.
translation_verse: Hal ka Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ a Naawuni ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu, zuliya shɛba bee na’ so n-kani ka n dan’ naa bi tim nimaani nti bɔ a; ka bɛ yi yɛli ni a kani, faashee ka dilan’ chɛ ka lala zuliya maa nim’ po ni bɛ shiri bi nya a.

english_verse: Do you really want me to tell him you're here?
translation_verse: Ka pumpɔŋɔ ka a ti yɛli ma, ‘Cham’ ti yɛli a dan’ naa, “Nyama, Ilaija be kpe.” ’

english_verse: What if the Lord's Spirit takes you away as soon as I leave? When Ahab comes to get you, he won't find you. Then he will surely kill me. I have worshiped the Lord since I was a boy.
translation_verse: Ka n yi kul yi a sani chaŋ, Yawɛ shia ni kana nti kpuɣ’ a kpa shɛli polo n ni ʒi, ka n chaŋ ti yɛli Ɛhab ka o ti bi nya a, o ni ku ma, hal man’ ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ ni kul nyɛ ŋun doli Yawɛ viɛnyɛliŋga m bilim ni ha la zaa yoli.

english_verse: Elijah said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord All-Powerful, and I swear in his name that I will meet with Ahab today.”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaija garigi yɛl’ o, “Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Tɔbbihi Naa ŋun be, ka nyɛ n ni ʒe so tooni ŋɔ zuɣu, n shiri ni zaŋ mmaŋ’ wuhi Ɛhab zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ.”

english_verse: Obadiah left and told Ahab where to find Elijah. Ahab went to meet Elijah,
translation_verse: Ka Obadia daa ŋmaligi chaŋ ti yɛli Ɛhab, ka o daa chaŋ ni o ti nya Ilaija.

english_verse: and when he saw him, Ahab shouted, “There you are, the biggest troublemaker in Israel!”
translation_verse: Ɛhab ni daa nya Ilaija, o daa bɔh’ o mi, “Nyin’ ŋun nahindi Izraɛlnim’ maa m-bala?”

english_verse: Elijah answered: You're the troublemaker—not me! You and your family have disobeyed the Lord's commands by worshiping Baal.
translation_verse: Ka Ilaija garigi yɛl’ o, “Pa mani n-nyɛ ŋun nahindi Izraɛlnima, amaa a min’ a daŋ niriba n-nahindi Izraɛlnima. Dama yinima n-zaɣisi Yawɛ zaligunim’ dolibu, ka jɛmdila Baal buɣa.

english_verse: Call together everyone from Israel to meet me on Mount Carmel. Be sure to bring along the
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ timmi laɣim Izraɛlnim’ zaa mini Baal anabinim’ kɔbisinahi ni pihinu ni Ashɛra anabinim’ kɔbisinahi bɛn diri Jɛzibɛl yiŋ’ la n-zaŋ ba ka n sanna Kamɛl Zoli zuɣu.

english_verse: Ahab got everyone together, then they went to meet Elijah on Mount Carmel.
translation_verse: Ka Ɛhab daa tim ti laɣim Izraɛlnim’ zaa mini anabinim’ maa na Kamɛl Zoli zuɣu.

english_verse: Elijah stood in front of them and said, “How much longer will you try to have things both ways? If the Lord is God, worship him! But if Baal is God, worship him!” The people did not say a word.
translation_verse: Ka Ilaija daa kana ti zani miri niriba maa zaa ka bɔhi ba, “Bɔ saha ka yi leei kul yɛn chɛ yi tɛha buyiyi ŋɔ? Yawɛ n-yi nyɛ Naawuni, yin’ doliy’ o, ka Baal n-yi nyɛ Naawuni, yin’ doliy’ o.” Ka niriba maa daa bi garigi yɛl’ o shɛli.

english_verse: Bring us two bulls. Baal's prophets can take one of them, kill it, and cut it into pieces. Then they can put the meat on the wood without lighting the fire. I will do the same thing with the other bull, and I won't light a fire under it either.
translation_verse: Timiya ti naɣilah’ ayi, ka chɛ ka bɛ pii naɣila’ yino kɔrigi ŋ-ŋmahiŋmah’ o pa dari zuɣu, ka di niŋ buɣim niŋ li; ka n gba kɔrigi naɣila’ ŋun’ la ŋ-ŋmahiŋmah’ o pa dari zuɣu ka ku niŋ buɣim niŋ li.

english_verse: The prophets of Baal will pray to their god, and I will pray to the Lord. The one who answers by starting the fire is God. “That's a good idea,” everyone agreed.
translation_verse: Ka yi suhi yi Naawuni maa, ka n gba suhi Yawɛ, ka Naawuni so ŋun chɛ ka buɣim taai nimdi maa, ŋuna n-nyɛ Naawuni.” Ka Niriba maa zaa yɛli, “A ni yɛli shɛm maa viɛla.”

english_verse: Elijah said to Baal's prophets, “There are more of you, so you go first. Pick out a bull and get it ready, but don't light the fire. Then pray to your god.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Ilaija daa yɛli Baal anabinim’ maa, “Yi ni galisi maa zuɣu, daŋmiya pii yi naɣilaa kɔrigi ŋ-ŋmahiŋmah’ o pa, ka suhi yi buɣili maa; amaa ka lee di niŋ buɣim niŋ li.

english_verse: They chose their bull, then they got it ready and prayed to Baal all morning, asking him to start the fire. They danced around the altar and shouted, “Answer us, Baal!” But there was no answer.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa zaŋ bɛ ni zaŋ naɣila’ so ti ba kɔrigi ŋ-ŋmahiŋmahi pa, ka gbaai Baal maa suhibu asiba hal ni wuntaŋ’ zuɣusaa saha n-kul yɛra, “Baal, garigim’ ti!” Ka bɛ daa kul yiɣirimi jɛmdi gindi bimbin’ shɛli bɛ ni me n-zali maa, amaa ka bi wum so kukoli, ka so mi bi garigi ba.

english_verse: At noon, Elijah began making fun of them. “Pray louder!” he said. “Baal must be a god. Maybe he's daydreaming or using the toilet or traveling somewhere. Or maybe he's asleep, and you have to wake him up.”
translation_verse: Ka di daa mali ti paai wuntaŋ’ zuɣusaa saha, ka Ilaija gbaai ba ansarisi malibu yɛra, “O nyɛla Naawuni, dinzuɣu suhimiya pampam, dama di pa shɛli o na bɔhirila o suhi bee o na yimi bee o go n-chaŋla tinshee katiŋa bee ŋun’ gbihirimi, ka di simdi ni yi neeg’ o.”

english_verse: The prophets kept shouting louder and louder, and they cut themselves with swords and knives until they were bleeding. This was the way they worshiped,
translation_verse: Ka anabinim’ maa daa kul kuhiri pampam, ka mali suhi mini kpana ŋ-ŋmari bɛmaŋa ka chɔhiri bɛmaŋa kaman bɛ taara ni daa nyɛ shɛm hal ka ʒim ti puhiri yiri bɛ niŋgbuna ni na.

english_verse: and they kept it up until time for the evening sacrifice. But there was no answer of any kind.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa kul niŋdi lala hal ka wuntaŋ’ zuɣusaa saha ti gari, ka bɛ kul mali lala hal ti paai zaawuni sara malibu saha, ka bi wum so kukoli, ka so mi bi garigi ba.

english_verse: Then he used twelve stones to build an altar in honor of the Lord. Each stone stood for one of the tribes of Israel, which was the name the Lord had given to their ancestor Jacob. Elijah dug a ditch around the altar, large enough to hold about
translation_verse: n-daa zaŋ kuɣa maa me Yawɛ jɛmbu sara maligu bimbini maa zali, ka chɛ ka bɛ gaai bɔɣili gil’ li; ka bɔɣili maa ni tooi deei kom kaman lita pinaanahi laasabu.

english_verse: He placed the wood on the altar, then they cut the bull into pieces and laid the meat on the wood. He told the people, “Fill four large jars with water and pour it over the meat and the wood.” After they did this,
translation_verse: Ka o daa kab’ dari pa bimbin’ maa zuɣu, ka ŋmahiŋmahi naɣilaa maa nimdi pa dari maa zuɣu, ka yɛli ba, “Niŋmiya kom pali koyuya anahi n-kpaai li tɛli sara shɛli bɛ ni zaŋdi nyɔri buɣim ŋɔ mini dari maa.”

english_verse: he told them to do it two more times. They did exactly as he said
translation_verse: Ka o lan yɛli, “Niŋmiya lala pahi buyi.” Ka bɛ niŋ lala pahi buyi. Ka o lan yɛli, “Niŋmiya lala pahi buta.” Ka bɛ niŋ lala pahi buta.

english_verse: until finally, the water ran down the altar and filled the ditch.
translation_verse: Ka kom maa daa zo n-gili bimbini maa, ka pali bɔɣili la gba.

english_verse: When it was time for the evening sacrifice, Elijah prayed: Our Lord, you are the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. Now, prove that you are the God of this nation, and that I, your servant, have done this at your command.
translation_verse: Ka sara malibu saha daa ti paai, ka anabi Ilaija vu m-miri sara maligu bimbini maa ka suhi Naawuni yɛli, “Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Ibrahimma mini Yisahaku ni Izraɛl Naawuni ŋɔ, zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ, chɛ ka niriba ŋɔ baŋ ni nyini n-nyɛ Naawuni Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni; ka baŋ ni n nyɛla a dabili, ka lan baŋ ni a ni wuhi ma shɛm ka n niŋ ŋɔ.

english_verse: Please answer me, so these people will know that you are the Lord God, and that you will turn their hearts back to you.
translation_verse: Yawɛ, Garigim’ ma, garigim’ ma din ni chɛ ka niriba ŋɔ baŋ ni nyini Yawɛ n-nyɛ Naawuni, ka lan nyɛ ŋun ŋmaligi bɛ suhuri labis’ a sanna.”

english_verse: The Lord immediately sent fire, and it burned up the sacrifice, the wood, and the stones. It scorched the ground everywhere around the altar and dried up every drop of water in the ditch.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa chɛ ka buɣim kana ti taai di nimdi maa mini dari maa ni kuɣa ni taŋkpaɣu, ka chɛ ka ko’ shɛli din daa be bɔɣili maa ni farifari nyuui.

english_verse: When the crowd saw what had happened, they all bowed down and shouted, “The Lord is God! The Lord is God!”
translation_verse: Ka niriba maa zaa ni daa nya lala maa, ka bɛ teei dɔni n-zaŋ bɛ nina kpa tiŋa ka yɛra, “Yawɛ n-shiri nyɛ Naawuni, Yawɛ n-shiri nyɛ Naawuni”

english_verse: Just then, Elijah said, “Grab the prophets of Baal! Don't let any of them get away.” So the people captured the prophets and took them to Kishon River, where Elijah killed every one of them. It Starts To Rain
translation_verse: Ka Ilaija daa yɛli niriba maa, “Gbahimiya Baal daanabinim’ maa, ka di chɛliya ka bɛ ni so zo n-tiligi.” Ka bɛ daa gbahi ba, ka Ilaija zaŋ ba sirigi Kishɔn kulibɔŋ ni nti ku ba nimaani. Saa mibu yɛla

english_verse: Elijah told Ahab, “Get something to eat and drink. I hear a heavy rain coming.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Ilaija daa yɛli Ɛhab, “Cham’ ti di ka nyu, dama saa vura.”

english_verse: Ahab left, but Elijah climbed back to the top of Mount Carmel. Then he stooped down with his face almost to the ground
translation_verse: Ka Ɛhab ni daa chaŋ ni o ti di ka nyu saha shɛli maa, ka Ilaija daa du Kamɛl Zoli zuɣu nti kurim n-zaŋ o nini kpa o duna;

english_verse: and said to his servant, “Look toward the sea.” The servant left. And when he came back, he said, “I looked, but I didn't see anything.” Elijah told him to look seven more times.
translation_verse: ka yɛl’ o tumo, “Cham’ ti lihi teeku polo.” Ka o daa chaŋ ti lihi ka yɛli, “M bi nya shɛli.” Ka Ilaija yɛl’ o, “Labimi yaha n-niŋ lala hal ti paai siɣimsiɣim buyopɔin.”

english_verse: After the seventh time the servant replied, “I see a small cloud coming this way. But it's no bigger than a fist.” Elijah told him, “Tell Ahab to get his chariot ready and start home now. Otherwise, the rain will stop him.”
translation_verse: Napɔŋ din pahir’ ayopɔin maa ni, ka o daa ti yɛli, “N nya sagban’ bila ka di be kaman ninsal’ nuu la n-yi teeku polo na.” Ka o yɛl’ o, “Cham’ ti yɛli Ɛhab, ‘Malim’ a chɛchɛbuŋ’ shili n-yiɣisi kuli, di yi pa lala saa ni taɣ’ a sɔŋ.’ ”

english_verse: A few minutes later, it got very cloudy and windy, and rain started pouring down. So Elijah wrapped his coat around himself, and the Lord gave him strength to run all the way to Jezreel. Ahab followed in his chariot.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ yiko daa kpe Ilaija ni, ka o voog’ o shɛlɔrigu lo n-zo n-daŋ Ɛhab tooni ti paai Jɛziriil dunɔdali gbini.

english_verse: Ahab told his wife Jezebel what Elijah had done and that he had killed the prophets.
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka Ɛhab daa yɛl’ o paɣ’ Jɛzibɛl Ilaija ni niŋ shɛlikam zaa min’ o ni zaŋ takɔbi ku Baal daanabinim’ zaa shɛm yɛla.

english_verse: She sent a message to Elijah: “You killed my prophets. Now I'm going to kill you! I pray that the gods will punish me even more severely if I don't do it by this time tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Ka Jɛzibɛl daa tim ti yɛli Ilaija, “Biɛɣuni ŋ-ŋɔ tasaha n yi sa bi ku a kaman a ni ku anabinim’ ŋɔ shɛm maa, n wuna bɛn’ kum’ ma.”

english_verse: Elijah was afraid when he got her message, and he ran to the town of Beersheba in Judah. He left his servant there,
translation_verse: Ka dabiɛm daa gbaai Ilaija, ka o yiɣisi zo ni o tilig’ o nyɛvili. O daa zaŋla o tumo la n-zo n-kuli Bɛrishiiba din be Juda tiŋgbɔŋ ni la nti chɛ o nimaani.

english_verse: then walked another whole day into the desert. Finally, he came to a large bush and sat down in its shade. He begged the Lord, “I've had enough. Just let me die! I'm no better off than my ancestors.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka ŋun’ maŋmaŋ’ daa kpe mɔɣu chaŋ dabisi’ muni chandi nti teei ʒini ti’ shɛli gbini n-suhiri Naawuni bɔri ni o kpi. O daa yɛlimi, “Yawɛ, di saɣiya, deemi n nyɛvili pumpɔŋɔ, dama m bi so n yaannima.”

english_verse: Then he lay down in the shade and fell asleep. Suddenly an angel woke him up and said, “Get up and eat.”
translation_verse: Ka o daa dɔni tia maa gbini gbihi. Ka malaika daa shih’ o ka yɛl’ o, “Yiɣisim’ di bindirigu.”

english_verse: Elijah looked around, and by his head was a jar of water and some baked bread. He sat up, ate and drank, then lay down and went back to sleep.
translation_verse: Ka o yiɣisi lihi nya ka bɛ ni she mahi’ kpil’ shɛli kuɣ’ tula zuɣu mini kɔgaɣili n-ʒe o zuɣu polo. Ka o daa di ka nyu, ka lan lab’ dɔni.

english_verse: So Elijah sat up and ate and drank. The food and water made him strong enough to walk
translation_verse: Ka Ilaija daa yiɣisi di ka nyu, ka bindirigu maa daa ti o kpiɔŋ wuntaŋ’ ni mini yuŋ biɛɣ’ pihinahi, ka o chaŋ hal ti paai Sinai Zoli din nyɛ Naawuni zol’ la zuɣu.

english_verse: and he spent the night there in a cave. The Lord Appears to Elijah While Elijah was on Mount Sinai, the Lord asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
translation_verse: Ka o daa kpe vokabili puuni zoli maa zuɣu nti gbe nimaani. Ka Yawɛ daa bɔh’ o, “Ilaija, bɔ ka a lee niŋdi kpe?”

english_verse: He answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaija garigi yɛli, “N zabirila nyuli tiri nyin’ Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Tɔbbihi Naawuni ŋɔ; dama Izraɛlnim’ yi a mini ba daalikauli la nyaaŋa; ka daag’ a sara maligu bimbina luhi; ka zaŋ takɔbi ku a daanabinima; ka n kɔŋko nti kpalim, ka bɛ bɔri ni bɛ ku man’ gba.”

english_verse: “Go out and stand on the mountain,” the Lord replied. “I want you to be there when I pass by.” All at once, a strong wind shook the mountain and shattered the rocks. But the Lord was not in the wind. Next, there was an earthquake, but the Lord was not in the earthquake.
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl’ o, “Cham’ ti du n-tam zoli din do man’ Yawɛ tooni ŋɔ zuɣu. Dama Yawɛ yɛn garila nimaani.” Ka sanʒiɛ’ titali din mali kpiɔŋ daa yiɣisi ʒiɛri wurindi zoli maa, ka ŋmari kuɣa sɔŋdi Yawɛ tooni, amaa ka Yawɛ daa ka di ni. Ka tiŋgbani dambu daa doli sanʒiɛɣu maa nyaaŋa na, amaa ka Yawɛ ka tiŋgbani dambu maa ni.

english_verse: Then there was a fire, but the Lord was not in the fire. Finally, there was a gentle breeze,
translation_verse: Ka buɣim daa doli tiŋgbani dambu maa nyaaŋa na, amaa ka Yawɛ daa ka buɣim maa gba ni. Ka kukol’ balli zaɣ’ bilifu daa ti doli buɣim maa dibu nyaaŋa na.

english_verse: and when Elijah heard it, he covered his face with his coat. He went out and stood at the entrance to the cave. A voice asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
translation_verse: Ilaija ni daa wum li saha shɛli, o daa zaŋla o binyɛrigu pɔb’ o nina yi nti ʒe vokabili maa dunol’ ni. Nyama, ka kukoli maa daa bɔh’ o, “Ilaija, bɔ ka a lee niŋdi kpe?”

english_verse: Elijah answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
translation_verse: Ka o garigi yɛli, “N zabirila nyuli tiri nyin’ ŋun nyɛ Tɔbbihi Naawuni ŋɔ, dama Izraɛlnim’ yi a mini ba daalikauli la nyaaŋa, ka daag’ a sara maligu bimbina luhi, ka zaŋ takɔbi ku a daanabinim’ zaa, ka n kɔŋko nti kpalim, ka bɛ bɔri ni bɛ ku man’ gba.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Elijah, you can go back to the desert near Damascus. And when you get there, appoint Hazael to be king of Syria.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yɛl’ o, “Labimi mɔɣu ni luɣ’ shɛli din miri Damaskus la. A yi paai nimaani, nyin’ boom’ kpam bahi Hazaɛl zuɣu ni ka o leei Siria naa;

english_verse: Then appoint Jehu son of Nimshi to be king of Israel, and Elisha son of Shaphat to take your place as my prophet.
translation_verse: ka booi kpam bahi Nimshi bia Jɛhu zuɣu ni ka o leei Izraɛl naa; ka lan booi kpam bahi Shafat ŋun nyɛ Ɛbɛlimɛhola nir’ la bia Ilaisha zuɣu ni, ka o mi leeg’ anabi zani a zaani.

english_verse: Hazael will start killing the people who worship Baal. Jehu will kill those who escape from Hazael, and Elisha will kill those who escape from Jehu.
translation_verse: Ka ninvuɣ’ so ŋun ti zo n-yi Hazaɛl takɔbi kubu ni, Jɛhu ŋun’ kum’ o; ka ŋun ti zo n-yi Jɛhu takɔbi kubu ni, Ilaisha mi ŋun’ kum’ o.

english_verse: Elijah left and found Elisha plowing a field with a pair of oxen. There were eleven other men in front of him, and each one was also plowing with a pair of oxen. Elijah went over and put his own coat on Elisha.
translation_verse: Ka Ilaija daa ŋmaligi nimaani chaŋ ti nya Shafat bia Ilaisha maa ka o malila naɣikɔra siɣimsiɣim bupinaayi zuɣu ka bɛ be o tooni kɔra; omaŋmaŋ’ n-daa mali bɛn pahiri bupinaayi maa kɔra. Ka Ilaija daa chaŋ ti gar’ o sani ka pirig’ o binyɛrigu pa o zuɣu.

english_verse: Elisha stopped plowing and ran after him. “Let me kiss my parents goodbye, then I'll go with you,” he said. “You can go,” Elijah said. “But remember what I've done for you.”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha daa chɛ naɣikɔra maa, ka guui doli Ilaija nti yɛl’ o, “Chɛ ka n chɛbisi m ba mini m ma pɔi ka naanyi dol’ a.” Ka Ilaija yɛl’ o, “Labima, ka n yɛl’ a la wula?

english_verse: Elisha left and took his oxen with him. He killed them and boiled them over a fire he had made with the wood from his plow. He gave the meat to the people who were with him, and they ate it. Then he left with Elijah and became his assistant.
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha daa lab’ o naɣikɔra maa sani nti zaŋ ba kɔrigi, ka zaŋ bɛ dapuhi m-mali buɣim duɣi ba n-zaŋ ti niriba ka bɛ ŋubi. Di nyaaŋa ka o daa chaŋ ti doli Ilaija n-sɔŋd’ o.

translation_verse: Ka o daa chaŋ kuliga ni nti kpaai yalim maa bahi kom maa ni ka yɛli, “Yawɛ yɛliya, n chɛ ka kom maa leei ko’ viɛlli; ka pumpɔŋɔ zaŋ chana, di ku lan ku so bee n-chɛ ka paɣiba zaŋdi bahira.”

english_verse: The water has been fine ever since, just as Elisha said. Some Boys Make Fun of Elisha
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu kom maa na kul nyɛla ko’ viɛlli hal ni zuŋɔ kaman Ilaisha ni daa yɛli shɛm maa.

english_verse: Elisha left and headed toward Bethel. Along the way some boys started making fun of him by shouting, “Go away, baldy! Get out of here!”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha daa ti yi nimaani n-chani Bɛtɛl. O ni daa yi soli n-chani ha, ka bidibbihi nya o m-maani o ansarisi yɛra, “Zuɣupalo ŋɔ lana, chama! Zuɣupalo ŋɔ lana, chama!”

english_verse: Elisha turned around and stared at the boys. Then he cursed them in the name of the Lord. At once two bears ran out of the woods and ripped to pieces
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha daa ŋmaligi nya ba, ka zaŋ Yawɛ yuli yɛli ba noli. Ka gbuɣin’ nyama ayi daa yi tibɔŋ ni na nti dim ku bidibbihi pihinahinaayi.

english_verse: Elisha went up to Mount Carmel, then returned to Samaria.
translation_verse: Ka o daa yi nimaani chaŋ Kamɛl Zoli zuɣu, ka daa ti yi nimaani lab’ Samaria.

english_verse: Joram son of Ahab became king of Israel in Jehoshaphat's eighteenth year as king of Judah. Joram ruled twelve years from Samaria
translation_verse: Juda Naa Jɛhɔshafat ni daa di nam zaŋ chaŋ yuun’ pisaayika saha, ka Ɛhab bia Jɛhɔram daa di Izraɛl nam Samaria. O daa niŋ la o nam maa ni yuun’ pinaayi.

english_verse: and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He tore down the stone image his father had made to honor Baal, and so he wasn't as sinful as his parents.
translation_verse: O daa tum alahichi Yawɛ sani. Amaa o daa lee bi tummi kaman o ba min’ o ma ni daa tum shɛm la; dama o daa wurim o ba ni daa me Baal binwɔɣinli shɛli zal’ la.

english_verse: But he kept doing the sinful things that Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel to do. The Country of Moab Rebels against Israel
translation_verse: Amaa o daa tum Nɛbat bia Jɛrɔbɔam ni daa tum alahichi shɛli n-chɛ ka Izraɛlnim’ tum alahichi la tatabo. O daa bi lɔɣ’ li.

english_verse: For many years the country of Moab had been controlled by Israel and was forced to pay taxes to the kings of Israel. King Mesha of Moab raised sheep, so he paid the king of Israel
translation_verse: Mɔab Naa Mɛsha daa wumsirila piɛri, ka di daa kpala talahi ni o tahiri piɛbihi polo tuhi’ kɔbiga mini piɛlahi tuhi’ kɔbiga kɔbiri yuuni kam nti tiri Izraɛl naa.

english_verse: But soon after the death of Ahab, Mesha rebelled against Israel.
translation_verse: Amaa Ɛhab kum nyaaŋa, ka Mɔab naa maa daa zaɣisi ni o ku lan niŋ lala ti Izraɛl naa.

english_verse: One day, Joram left Samaria and called together Israel's army.
translation_verse: Ka Naa Jɛhɔram daa dii yiɣisi Samaria di saha maa n-chaŋ ti laɣim Izraɛl tɔbbihi zaa.

english_verse: He sent this message to King Jehoshaphat of Judah, “The king of Moab has rebelled. Will you go with me to attack him?” “Yes, I will,” Jehoshaphat answered. “I'm on your side, and my soldiers and horses are at your command.
translation_verse: Di saha maa ka o daa tim Juda Naa Jɛhɔshafat sani ti yɛl’ o, “Mɔab naa zaɣisi ma jɛmbu. A ni pahi n zuɣu ka ti chaŋ ti tuh’ o?” Ka o garigi yɛl’ o, “N ni chaŋ. A ni be shɛm lala n-nyɛ ma. N niriba bemi ka a niriba, ka n yuri be ka a yuri.”

english_verse: So Joram, Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom led their troops out. But seven days later, there was no drinking water left for them or their animals.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛl naa mini Juda naa ni Ɛdom naa daa laɣim chaŋ. Ka bɛ daa chaŋ ti paai daba ayopɔin chandi tariga ka kom pooi ba, hal ka shɛli kani ka bɛ tɔbbihi mini bɛ ni daa ʒiri biŋkɔb’ shɛb’ chani ni nyu.

english_verse: Joram cried out, “This is terrible! The Lord must have led us out here to be captured by Moab's army.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Izraɛl naa daa yɛli, “Mbaye! Yawɛ zaŋla ti nanima ata ŋɔ na ni o ti niŋ Mɔabnim’ nuu ni!”

english_verse: Jehoshaphat said, “Which of the Lord's prophets is with us? We can find out from him what the Lord wants us to do.” One of Joram's officers answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He was one of Elijah's closest followers.”
translation_verse: Ka Jɛhɔshafat bɔh’ o, “Yawɛ anab’ so ka kpe ka ti ni bɔh’ o baŋ Yawɛ ni yɛli shɛm?” Di saha ka Izraɛl naa sapashinnim’ ni yino daa garigi yɛli, “Shafat bia Ilaisha, ŋun daa nyɛ Ilaija sɔŋda la be kpe.”

english_verse: Jehoshaphat replied, “He can give us the Lord's message.” The three kings went over to Elisha,
translation_verse: Ka Jɛhɔshafat yɛli, “Yawɛ yɛligu be o ni.” Dinzuɣu ka Izraɛl naa mini Jɛhɔshafat ni Ɛdom naa daa chaŋ o sani.

english_verse: and he asked Joram, “Why did you come to me? Go talk to the prophets of the foreign gods your parents worshiped.” “No,” Joram answered. “It was the Lord who led us out here, so that Moab's army could capture us.”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha daa ti bɔhi Izraɛl naa, “M min’ a yɛla bi kpa. Cham’ a ba min’ a ma daanabinim’ la sani.” Amaa ka Izraɛl naa maa yɛl’ o, “Aai, Yawɛ n-zaŋ ti nanima ata ŋɔ na ni o ti niŋ Mɔabnim’ nuu ni.”

english_verse: Elisha said to him, “I serve the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as he lives, I swear I wouldn't even look at you if I didn't respect King Jehoshaphat.”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha yɛli, “N ni jɛmdi Yawɛ so ŋun nyɛ Tɔbbihi Naa ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu, di yi di pala n ni ti Juda Naa Jɛhɔshafat jilima zuɣu, n naan ku ŋmaligi lih’ a bee nti nya a.

english_verse: Then Elisha said, “Send for someone who can play the harp.” The harpist began playing, and the Lord gave Elisha this message for Joram:
translation_verse: Amaa bomiya baaŋa ti ma na pumpɔŋɔ.” Baaŋa maa ni daa ti yiini yila saha shɛli, ka Yawɛ yiko siɣi Ilaisha zuɣu na,

english_verse: The Lord says that this dry riverbed will be filled with water.
translation_verse: ka o yɛli, “Yawɛ ni yɛli shɛm m-bɔŋɔ, ‘N ni chɛ ka kom tɛli baa din kuui ŋɔ ni zaa.’

english_verse: You won't feel any wind or see any rain, but there will be plenty of water for you and your animals.
translation_verse: Yawɛ lan yɛli, ‘Yi ku nya pɔhim bee saa, amaa kom ni tɛli baa ŋɔ ni ka yi mini yi niɣi ni yi biŋkɔbiri nyu.’ ”

english_verse: That simple thing isn't all the Lord is going to do. He will also help you defeat Moab's army.
translation_verse: Ka dimbɔŋɔ nyɛla yɛl’ bila Yawɛ sani. O ni lan zaŋ Mɔabnim’ niŋ yi nuu ni;

english_verse: You will capture all their walled cities and important towns. You will chop down every good tree and stop up every spring of water, then ruin their fertile fields by covering them with rocks.
translation_verse: ka yi ŋme n-nyaŋ bɛ ni me birininim’ gili bɛ tin’ shɛŋa la nim’ mini tiŋ’ gahinda la, ka ŋma bɛ ti’ suŋ kam zaa luhi; ka ŋari bɛ kɔbil’ nina zaa, ka kahi kuɣa sɔŋ luɣ’ shɛŋa din tam vuhiri shee zaa n-saɣim li.

english_verse: The next morning, while the sacrifice was being offered, water suddenly started flowing from the direction of Edom, and it flooded the land.
translation_verse: Dindali maa kaai biɛɣ’ asibaasi sara maligu saha, ka kom daa yi Ɛdom polo n-zo na ti tɛli tiŋgbani zaa.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the people of Moab had heard that the three kings were coming to attack them. They had called together all of their fighting men, from the youngest to the oldest, and these troops were now standing at their border, ready for battle.
translation_verse: Mɔabnim’ zaa ni daa wum ni nanim’ shɛb’ kana ni bɛ ti tuhi ba, bɛ daa laɣimla bipola zaŋ tabili ninkura zaa bɛn ni tooi ye gbaɣinɔnim’ na nti sɔŋ bɛ tintariga.

english_verse: When they got up that morning, the sun was shining across the water, making it look red. The Moabite troops took one look
translation_verse: Ka Mɔabnim’ maa daa yiɣis’ asibaasi, ka wuntaŋ’ nyeei kpe kom maa, ka bɛ nya ka di do bɛ tooni ha m-mɔhi kaman ʒim la.

english_verse: and shouted, “Look at that blood! The armies of those kings must have fought and killed each other. Come on, let's go take what's left in their camp.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yɛli, “Ʒim m-bala. Nanim’ maa ŋ-ŋmaligi zabi n-ku tab’ maa! Dinzuɣu Mɔabnima, chamiya ti di nɛma!”

english_verse: But when they arrived at Israel's camp, the Israelite soldiers came out and attacked them, until they turned and ran away. Israel's army chased them all the way back to Moab, and even there they kept up the attack.
translation_verse: Amaa ka bɛ daa mali ti paai Izraɛlnim’ sansan ni, ka Izraɛlnim’ maa daa yiɣisi lu bɛ zuɣu, ka Mɔabnim’ maa ŋmaligi guui, ka Izraɛlnim’ kari doli ba ŋ-ŋmɛri kuri ba chana.

english_verse: The Israelites destroyed the Moabite towns. They chopped down the good trees and stopped up the springs of water, then covered the fertile fields with rocks. Finally, the only city left standing was Kir-Hareseth, but soldiers armed with slings surrounded and attacked it.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa saɣim Mɔabnim’ maa tinsi; ka sokam daa kahi kuɣa nti bahi bɛ tiŋgbani maa luɣ’ shɛŋa din vuhiri shee hal ka di zaa ti nyɛla kuɣa noli; ka ŋari bɛ kɔbil’ nina; ka ŋma bɛ ti’ suŋ kam zaa luhi. Ka bɛ tin’ titali din yuli booni Kiriharɛsɛt la kɔŋko n-daa ti kpalim, ka kuɣilɔnlabiriba daa chaŋ ti teei gil’ li ŋ-ŋme n-nyaŋ ba.

english_verse: He then grabbed his oldest son who was to be the next king and sacrificed him as an offering on the city wall. The Israelite troops were so horrified that they left the city and went back home.
translation_verse: Di saha ka o daa zaŋ o zuu ŋun ti yɛn di nam zan’ o zaani mali maligu gooni zuɣu n-zaŋ o nyo buɣim. Ka suli daa gbaai Izraɛlnima, ka bɛ ŋmaligi lab’ bɛ ya ka chɛ o.

english_verse: One day the widow of one of the Lord's prophets said to Elisha, “You know that before my husband died, he was a follower of yours and a worshiper of the Lord. But he owed a man some money, and now that man is on his way to take my two sons as his slaves.”
translation_verse: Anab’ so pakoli daa ti yɛli Ilaisha, “A dab’ so ŋun yi nyɛ n yidan’ la kpiya. Ka a mi mi ni a dabili maa daa nyɛla ŋun zɔri Yawɛ, amaa ka o sandana kana ni o ti zaŋ m bidibis’ ayi nti leeg’ o daba.”

english_verse: “Maybe there's something I can do to help,” Elisha said. “What do you have in your house?” “Sir, I have nothing but a small bottle of olive oil.”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha bɔh’ o, “Ka bɔ ka a lee bɔri ni n niŋ ti a? Yɛlim’ ma a ni mali shɛl’ a yiŋa.” Ka o yɛl’ o, “A dabipaɣa ka shɛli; kulla kpaŋman’ yini kɔŋko ka m mali.”

english_verse: Elisha told her, “Ask your neighbors for their empty jars. And after you've borrowed as many as you can,
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha yɛl’ o, “Cham’ a ʒiʒiinitab’ sani nti suhi kpaŋman’ kuma pam na, pa biɛla.

english_verse: go home and shut the door behind you and your sons. Then begin filling the jars with oil and set each one aside as you fill it.”
translation_verse: Ka a chɛ ka a min’ a bidibisi maa kpe yi duu ka yo yimaŋ’ niŋ di puuni, ka zaŋ kpam maa m-boori niŋdi ŋmana maa ni; ŋman’ yini yi ti pali, ka yi vuui li zali kpaŋa.”

english_verse: The woman left. Later, when she and her sons were back inside their house, the two sons brought her the jars, and she began filling them.
translation_verse: Ka pakoli maa daa yi o sani kuli nti chɛ ka o min’ o bihi maa kpe duu ka yo bɛmaŋ’ niŋ di puuni; ka o bihi maa zaŋdi ŋmana n-zaan’ o, ka o boori kpam maa niŋdi di ni.

english_verse: At last, she said to one of her sons, “Bring me another jar.” “We don't have any more,” he answered, and the oil stopped flowing from the small bottle.
translation_verse: Ka ŋmana maa zaa daa ti pali; ka o yɛl’ o bidibisi maa ni yino, “Zaŋm’ ŋman’ shɛl’ na.” Ka o yɛl’ o, “Ŋman’ shɛl’ lan kani.” Ka kpam maa mi dii ŋmaai, ka bi lan yirina.

english_verse: After she told Elisha what had happened, he said, “Sell the oil and use part of the money to pay what you owe the man. You and your sons can live on what is left.” Elisha Brings a Rich Woman's Son Back to Life
translation_verse: Ka pakoli maa daa lab’ ti yɛli Naawuni daanab’ maa. Ka Ilaisha yɛl’ o, “Cham’ ti zaŋ kpam maa kɔhi n-yo yi samli maa, ka chɛ din kpalim ka a min’ a bidibisi maa dira.” Ilaisha mini Shunɛm paɣ’ bundan’ yɛla

english_verse: Once, while Elisha was in the town of Shunem, he met a rich woman who invited him to her home for dinner. After that, whenever he was in Shunem, he would have a meal there with her and her husband.
translation_verse: Dahin shɛli ka Ilaisha daa ti chaŋ Shunɛm ka paɣ’ bundaan’ so daa be nimaani m-balim o ni o dim’ bindirigu. Dinzuɣu o daa yi ti doli nimaani polo saha shɛlikam, o kpɛrila yili maa ni ti diri bindirigu.

english_verse: Some time later the woman said to her husband, “I'm sure the man who comes here so often is a prophet of God.
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ bundan’ maa daa ti yɛl’ o yidana, “Nyama, pumpɔŋɔ m baŋya ni do’ so ŋun doli yiri ti sanna waawaayili ŋɔ nyɛla Naawuni ninvuɣ’ gahindili.

english_verse: Why don't we build him a small room on the flat roof of our house? We can put a bed, a table and chair, and an oil lamp in it. Then whenever he comes, he can stay with us.”
translation_verse: Chɛ ka ti me dubil’ tam ti yil’ ŋɔ zuɣusaa, ka bo garo mini teebuli ni kuɣa ni firila zali di ni, o yi ti lan ka ti sanna ka o kpe nimaani.”

english_verse: The next time Elisha was in Shunem, he stopped at their house and went up to his room to rest.
translation_verse: Dahin’ shɛli ka Ilaisha daa ti chaŋ nimaani n-kpe duu maa ni ni o ti vuhi.

english_verse: He said to his servant Gehazi, “This woman has been very helpful. Have her come up here to the roof for a moment.” She came, and Elisha told Gehazi to say to her, “You've gone to a lot of trouble for us, and we want to help you. Is there something we can request the king or army commander to do?” The woman answered, “With my relatives nearby, I have everything I need.”
translation_verse: Ka o yɛli Gɛhaazi, “Yɛlim’ o, ‘Nyama, a niŋ wahala pam sɔŋ ti; ka bɔ ka a lee bɔri ni ti niŋ ti a? A bɔri ni ti yɛli naa bee sapashin’ kpɛm’ yɛtɔɣ’ shɛli ti a?’ ” Ka paɣ’ maa garigi yɛli, “Mmaŋmaŋ’ niriba ni ka m be maa.”

english_verse: “Then what can we do for her?” Elisha asked Gehazi. Gehazi replied, “I do know that her husband is old, and that she doesn't have a son.”
translation_verse: Ka o bɔhi, “Ka bɔ ka ti lee yɛn niŋ ti paɣa maa?” Ka Gɛhaazi garigi yɛl’ o, “To, paɣ’ maa ka bidibiga, ka o yidana mi kurigi.”

english_verse: “Ask her to come here again,” Elisha told his servant. He called for her, and she came and stood in the doorway of Elisha's room.
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha yɛli, “Bolim’ o na.” Ka o daa boli paɣ’ maa, ka o kana ti zani dunol’ ni.

english_verse: Elisha said to her, “Next year at this time, you'll be holding your own baby son in your arms.” “You're a man of God,” the woman replied. “Please don't lie to me.”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha yɛl’ o, “Zaŋ chaŋ yuuni na ŋ-ŋɔ tasaha a ni gbib’ bidibiga a nuu ni.” Ka paɣ’ maa yɛli, “Aai. Wɛi, n dana, a nyɛla Naawuni nira, di yɔhim’ man’ ŋun nyɛ a dab’ paɣ’ ŋɔ!”

english_verse: But a few months later, the woman got pregnant. She gave birth to a son, just as Elisha had promised.
translation_verse: Amaa ka paɣ’ maa daa shiri niŋ pua n-dɔɣi bidibiga shɛɣuni kaman Ilaisha ni daa yɛl’ o ni o ni dɔɣi saha shɛli maa.

english_verse: One day while the boy was still young, he was out in the fields with his father, where the workers were harvesting the crops.
translation_verse: Ka bia maa daa mali ti zooi. Dahin shɛli ka o daa ti dol’ o ba chaŋ puu ni kachɛriba sani.

english_verse: Suddenly he shouted, “My head hurts. It hurts a lot!” “Carry him back to his mother,” the father said to his servant.
translation_verse: Ka o daa ti yɛl’ o ba, “Wɛi, n zuɣu n-yaara, n zuɣu n-yaara!” Ka bia maa ba yɛl’ o tumtumdi so, “Zaŋm’ bia maa kuli ti ti o ma.”

english_verse: loaves of bread made from the first barley that was harvested. Elisha said, “Give it to the people so they can eat.”
translation_verse: Ka doo maa daa zaŋ bia maa nti ti o ma; ka o zaŋ o ʒil’ o naba zuɣu n-gbib’ o hal ti paai wuntaŋ’ zuɣusaa saha, ka o leei Naawuni dini.

english_verse: She carried him upstairs to Elisha's room and laid him across the bed. Then she walked out and shut the door behind her.
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ maa daa zaŋ bia maa n-du n-kpɛhi ti sɔŋ Naawuni nir’ maa garo zuɣu; ka yina n-vooi dunoli yo.

english_verse: The woman called to her husband, “I need to see the prophet. Let me use one of the donkeys. Send a servant along with me, and let me leave now, so I can get back quickly.”
translation_verse: Ka o daa bol’ o yidana n-yɛl’ o, “Chɛ ka tumtumdi’ yino zaŋ bun’ yino ti ma na, ka n chaŋ yomyom ti nya Naawuni nir’ ŋɔ ka labina.”

english_verse: “Why do you need to see him today?” her husband asked. “It's not the Sabbath or time for the New Moon Festival.” “That's all right,” she answered.
translation_verse: Ka o yidan’ maa bɔh’ o, “Bɔzuɣu ka a bɔri ni a chaŋ o sani zuŋɔ? Zuŋɔ pala gol’ palli dabisili bee Vuhim Dabisili.” Ka paɣ’ maa yɛli, “Di bi galim.”

english_verse: She left at once for Mount Carmel to talk with Elisha. When Elisha saw her coming, he said, “Gehazi, look! It's the woman from Shunem.
translation_verse: Ka o daa yiɣisi n-chaŋ Naawuni nir’ maa sani Kamɛl Zoli zuɣu. Naawuni Nir’ maa ni daa nya paɣ’ maa ka o kanna ka o yɛl’ o sɔŋda Gɛhaazi, “Nyama, Shunɛm paɣ’ la m-be katiŋ’ kanna ŋɔ.

english_verse: Run and meet her. And ask her if everything is all right with her and her family.” “Everything is fine,” she answered Gehazi.
translation_verse: Guum’ yomyom tuh’ o soli ti bɔh’ o, ‘A min’ a yidan’ ni yi bia la mal’ alaafee?’ ” Ka o garigi yɛli Gɛhaazi, “Ti mal’ alaafee.”

english_verse: But as soon as she got to the top of the mountain, she went over and grabbed Elisha by the feet. Gehazi started toward her to push her away, when Elisha said, “Leave her alone! Don't you see how sad she is? But the Lord hasn't told me why.”
translation_verse: O ni daa mali ti paai Naawuni nir’ maa sani zoli maa zuɣu, o daa gbaala o napɔŋ, ka Gɛhaazi kana ni o ti daag’ o bahi, ka Naawuni nir’ maa yɛl’ o, “Chɛl’ o. O malila yɛli muɣisirili ka Yawɛ zaŋ li sɔɣi ma ka bi kahigi li wuhi ma.”

english_verse: The woman said, “Sir, I begged you not to get my hopes up, and I didn't even ask you for a son.”
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ maa bɔhi Ilaisha, “N daa yɛli nyini n dana ni a tim ma bia? N daa pun bi yɛl’ a ni a di yɔhim ma?”

english_verse: “Gehazi, get ready and go to her house,” Elisha said. “Take along my walking stick, and when you get there, lay it on the boy's face. Don't stop to talk to anyone, even if they try to talk to you.”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha daa yɛli Gɛhaazi, “Malim’ shili kpuɣi n jaaŋgbee ŋɔ chaŋ. A yi ti nya so sol’ ni, nyin’ di puh’ o; ka so yi puh’ a, nyin’ di saɣi. A yi ti paai, nyin’ zaŋmi n jaaŋgbee maa pa bia maa ninni.”

english_verse: But the boy's mother said to Elisha, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I won't leave without you.” So Elisha got up and went with them.
translation_verse: Ka bia maa ma maa daa yɛli Ilaisha, “Yawɛ ŋun be ŋɔ mini nyin’ ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu, n ku chaŋ ka chɛ a.” Ka Ilaisha daa yiɣisi dol’ o.

english_verse: Gehazi ran on ahead and laid Elisha's walking stick on the boy's face, but the boy didn't move or make a sound. Gehazi ran back to Elisha and said, “The boy didn't wake up.”
translation_verse: Ka Gɛhaazi daa daŋ tooni nti zaŋ jaaŋgbee maa pa bia maa ninni, amaa ka vuhim bee nyɛvili shɛhirili kani. Dinzuɣu ka o daa ŋmaligi labina ti tuhi Ilaisha soli n-yɛl’ o, “Bia maa bi neei.”

english_verse: Elisha arrived at the woman's house and went straight to his room, where he saw the boy's body on his bed.
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha daa paai yili maa ni nti nya ka bia maa kpi n-dola o garo zuɣu.

english_verse: He walked in, shut the door, and prayed to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ka o daa kpe duu maa ni, ka vooi dunoli yo bɛ niriba ayi maa niŋ, ka suhi Yawɛ.
