english_verse: Then he got on the bed and stretched out over the dead body, with his mouth on the boy's mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hand on his hands. As he lay there, the boy's body became warm.
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka o daa chaŋ ti teei dɔni bia maa zuɣu n-zaŋ o noli min’ o nina kpa bia maa noli ni o nina, ka zaŋ o nuhi pa o nuhi zuɣu; ka teeg’ omaŋ’ dolisi bia maa, ka o niŋgbuna piligi biibu.

english_verse: Elisha got up and walked back and forth in the room, then he went back and leaned over the boy's body. The boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha daa yiɣisi chaŋchaŋ gili duu maa ni, ka ti lan lab’ ti teei dɔni bia maa zuɣu yaha. Ka bia maa daa tihim siɣimsiɣim buyopɔin, ka neeg’ o nina.

english_verse: Elisha called out to Gehazi, “Ask the boy's mother to come here.” Gehazi did, and when she was at the door, Elisha said, “You can take your son.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka o daa boli Gɛhaazi na ti yɛl’ o, “Bolim’ Shunɛm paɣ’ maa na.” Ka o bol’ o. Ka paɣ’ maa kana, ka o ti yɛl’ o, “Kpuɣim’ a bia.”

english_verse: She came in and bowed down at Elisha's feet. Then she picked up her son and left. Elisha Makes Some Stew Taste Better
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ maa daa kana ti lu n-gbani Ilaisha naba ni n-zaŋ o zuɣu silim tiŋa, ka kpuɣ’ o bia maa yi. Alahiziba tumtumsa ayi din pahi

english_verse: Later, Elisha went back to Gilgal, where there was almost nothing to eat, because the crops had failed. One day while the prophets who lived there were meeting with Elisha, he said to his servant, “Prepare a big pot of stew for these prophets.”
translation_verse: Ka kum daa ti lu, ka Ilaisha lab’ Giligal na. Ka anabinim’ daa ti ʒi o sani, ka o yɛl’ o sɔŋda, “Zaŋm’ duɣ’ titali tam n-duɣi ʒiɛri ti anabinim’ ŋɔ.”

english_verse: One of them went out into the woods to gather some herbs. He found a wild vine and picked as much of its fruit as he could carry, but he didn't know that the fruit was very sour. When he got back, he cut up the fruit and put it in the stew.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ ni yino daa yi n-chaŋ ni o ti bo ʒiɛvari na nti nya mɔɣu ni yɔɣili m-pɔhi li buɣi na nti ŋmahiŋmahi li niŋ ʒɛduɣu maa ni, ka bi mi di ni nyɛ shɛli.

english_verse: The stew was served, and when the prophets started eating it, they shouted, “Elisha, this stew tastes terrible! We can't eat it.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa ti tooi li ti niriba maa ni bɛ piɛbi. Bɛ ni daa piɛbiri ʒiɛri maa ka bɛ ti kuhi yɛli, “Wɛi, Naawuni nira, Lɔɣu be duɣu maa ni!” Ka bɛ daa kɔŋ li piɛbbu.

english_verse: “Bring me some flour,” Elisha said. He sprinkled the flour in the stew and said, “Now serve it to them.” And the stew tasted fine. Elisha Feeds One Hundred People
translation_verse: Ka o daa yɛli, “Dindina niŋmiya zim ti ma na.” Ka o daa zaŋ zim maa yuɣisi ʒiɛri maa ni ka yɛli ba, “Toomiya li ti niriba maa ka bɛ piɛbi.” Ka barina shɛli daa lan ka di ni yaha.

english_verse: So the servant served the bread and grain to the people. They ate and still had some left over, just as the Lord had promised.
translation_verse: Ka o sɔŋda maa daa zaŋ li ti ba. Ka bɛ daa shiri ŋub’ li ka guui kaman Yawɛ ni daa pun yɛli shɛm maa.

english_verse: Naaman was the commander of the Syrian army. The Lord had helped him and his troops defeat their enemies, so the king of Syria respected Naaman very much. Naaman was a brave soldier, but he had leprosy.
translation_verse: Naaman ŋun daa nyɛ Siria naa sapashin’ kpɛma daa nyɛla ninvuɣ’ titali, ka mali jilima pam o naa maa sani, dama o zuɣu ka Yawɛ daa tiri Sirianim’ nasara. O daa mali kpiɔŋ pam, ka lan nyɛ tɔbutuhir’ biiŋa; amaa ka kɔŋ’ lee mal’ o.

english_verse: One day while the Syrian troops were raiding Israel, they captured a girl, and she became a servant of Naaman's wife.
translation_verse: Sirianim’ daa ti chaŋ ti tuhi Izraɛlnima, ka gbaai bipuɣimbil’ so kuli ka o ti tumdi tuma sɔŋdi Naaman paɣa.

english_verse: When Naaman told the king what the girl had said,
translation_verse: Ka Naaman daa chaŋ o naa sani nti yɛl’ o, “Izraɛl bipuɣimbil’ la ni yɛli shɛm m-bɔŋɔ.”

english_verse: the king replied, “Go ahead! I will give you a letter to take to the king of Israel.” Naaman left and took along
translation_verse: Ka Siria naa maa daa yɛl’ o, “Cham’ pumpɔŋɔ! N ni sab’ gbaŋ ti a ka a mali ti ti Izraɛl naa.” Ka Naaman daa bo anzinfa laɣibaligu tuhi’ pia mini salima laɣibaligu tusaayɔbu ni binyɛr’ suma din nyɛ chuɣu binyɛra pia chaŋ.

english_verse: He also carried the letter to the king of Israel. It said, “I am sending my servant Naaman to you. Would you cure him of his leprosy?”
translation_verse: Ka o daa zaŋ gbaŋ maa nti ti Izraɛl naa. O ni daa sabi gbaŋ maa n-yɛli shɛm m-bɔŋɔ: “Gbaŋ ŋɔ yi paag’ a, nyin’ baŋmi ni mani n-chɛ ka Naaman ŋun nyɛ n tumtumda ŋɔ ka a sanna ni a ti tib’ o kɔŋ’ ŋɔ.”

english_verse: Elisha sent someone outside to say to him, “Go wash seven times in the Jordan River. Then you'll be completely cured.”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha daa tim tumo ni o yim’ na ti yɛli Naaman ni o cham’ Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili ni nti mim di ni siɣimsiɣim buyopɔin ka o niŋgbuna lab’ dimaŋ’ ni ka o nya alaafee.

english_verse: When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes in fear and shouted, “That Syrian king believes I can cure this man of leprosy! Does he think I'm God with power over life and death? He must be trying to pick a fight with me.”
translation_verse: Izraɛl naa maa ni daa ti karim gbaŋ maa, o daa darigimi toog’ o binyɛrigu ka yɛli, “N nyɛla Naawuni ka ni tooi ku nir’ ka lan neeg’ o, ka doo ŋɔ ti yɛri ma ni n tibimi nir’ kɔŋa? Nir’ yi kpahim yɛlli maa, a ni baŋ ni vuri ka o bɔri ma maa!”

english_verse: As soon as Elisha the prophet heard what had happened, he sent the Israelite king this message: “Why are you so afraid? Send the man to me, so that he will know there is a prophet in Israel.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Ilaisha ŋun nyɛ Naawuni nir’ maa daa wum Izraɛl naa ni darigi toog’ o binyɛrigu shɛm maa yɛla, ka tim ti bɔhi naa maa, “Bɔ n-niŋ ka a darigi toog’ a binyɛrigu? Chɛ ka doo maa ka n sanna nti baŋ ni anabi be Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni.”

english_verse: Naaman left with his horses and chariots and stopped at the door of Elisha's house.
translation_verse: Ka Naaman daa zaŋ o yuri min’ o chɛchɛbuŋa ŋ-ŋmaligi chaŋ ti zani Ilaisha yiŋ’ dunol’ ni.

english_verse: But Naaman stormed off, grumbling, “Why couldn't he come out and talk to me? I thought for sure he would stand in front of me and pray to the Lord his God, then wave his hand over my skin and cure me.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Naaman daa je suli ŋ-ŋmaligi chani ka yɛra, “Man’ di mi ni o yɛn yimina nti zani n-suhi Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ o Naawuni maa, ka zaŋ o nuu gahigahi kpe, ka chɛ ka n kɔŋ’ maa naai.

english_verse: What about the Abana River or the Pharpar River? Those rivers in Damascus are just as good as any river in Israel. I could have washed in them and been cured.”
translation_verse: Abana mini Faaripa mɔɣa din be Damaskus la bi so koma zaa din be Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni? N naan dii ku chaŋ nimaani nti mim ka nya alaafee?” Dinzuɣu ka o suhu daa yiɣisi pam ka o ŋmaligi chaŋ.

english_verse: His servants went over to him and said, “Sir, if the prophet had told you to do something difficult, you would have done it. So why don't you do what he said? Go wash and be cured.”
translation_verse: Ka o tumtumdiba daa chaŋ o sani nti yɛl’ o, “Ti ba, anab’ maa yi di yɛl’ a ni a niŋm’ binshɛli din to pam, a naan ku niŋ li? Di ni ti be ka o ni yɛl’ a mi, ‘Cham’ ti mim kom ni ka nya alaafee ŋɔ?’ ”

english_verse: Naaman walked down to the Jordan; he waded out into the water and stooped down in it seven times, just as Elisha had told him. At once, he was cured, and his skin became as smooth as a child's.
translation_verse: Ka Naaman daa saɣi, ka chaŋ ti mim Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili ni siɣimsiɣim buyopɔin kaman Naawuni nir’ maa ni daa yɛl’ o shɛm maa, ka nya alaafee zaa. Ka o niŋgbuna lab’ dimaŋ’ ni m-be kaman bibil’ niŋgbuna la.

english_verse: Naaman and his officials went back to Elisha. Naaman stood in front of him and announced, “Now I know that the God of Israel is the only God in the whole world. Sir, would you please accept a gift from me?”
translation_verse: Ka o mini bɛn daa dol’ o chaŋ maa zaa daa lab’ Naawuni nir’ maa sani ka o ti chaŋ ti zan’ o tooni ka yɛli, “M baŋya pumpɔŋɔ ni Naawuni ka dunia ŋɔ ni luɣ’ shɛli m-pahi Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni zuɣu; dinzuɣu deem’ pin’ shɛli man’ ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ ni yɛn ti a ŋɔ.”

english_verse: “I am a servant of the living Lord,” Elisha answered, “and I swear that I will not take anything from you.” Naaman kept begging, but Elisha kept refusing.
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha yɛli, “Yawɛ ŋun be ka n jɛmd’ o ŋɔ zuɣu, n ku deei pin’ shɛli a sani.” Ka Naaman daa balim o ni o deem’ li, amaa ka o zaɣisi.

english_verse: Finally Naaman said, “If you won't accept a gift, then please let me take home as much soil as two mules can pull in a wagon. Sir, from now on I will offer sacrifices only to the Lord.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Naaman daa yɛli Ilaisha, “A yi ku deei m pini, dindina, n suhir’ a, nyin’ chɛ ka bɛ tooi taŋkpaɣu ka di saɣi buntaans’ ayi ʒibu ti mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ ka n zaŋ kuli, dama pumpɔŋɔ zaŋ chana, mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ ku lan zaŋ binshɛli nyo buɣim bee m-mali sara ti buɣili kam yaha naɣila Yawɛ ka n ni jɛm.

english_verse: But I pray that the Lord will forgive me when I go into the temple of the god Rimmon and bow down there with the king of Syria.”
translation_verse: Ka dimbɔŋɔ puuni, m mali tahima ni n yi ti doli n naa chaŋ Siria buɣili Rimɔn jɛmbu duu nti damdi di tooni, biɛhiŋ kani, Yawɛ ni chɛ mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ taali.”

english_verse: “Go on home, and don't worry about that,” Elisha replied. Then Naaman left. Elisha Places a Curse on Gehazi After Naaman had gone only a short distance,
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha yɛl’ o, “Kulim’ ni suhudoo.” Naaman ni daa chaŋ, o daa na bi paai shɛli,

english_verse: Gehazi said to himself, “Elisha let that Syrian off too easy. He should have taken Naaman's gift. I swear by the living Lord that I will talk to Naaman myself and get something from him.”
translation_verse: ka Naawuni nira Ilaisha sɔŋda Gɛhaazi yɛl’ o suhu ni, “N dana fa Naaman ŋun nyɛ Siria nir’ ŋɔ bahi, o ni zaɣis’ o ni ʒi pin’ shɛŋa na nti ti o la zuɣu. Yawɛ ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu, n ni kar’ o naba ti deei shɛli o sani.”

english_verse: So he hurried after Naaman. When Naaman saw Gehazi running after him, he got out of his chariot to meet him. Naaman asked, “Is everything all right?”
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Gɛhaazi daa shiri yiɣisi kariti Naaman naba. Ka Naaman daa ti nya ka so zɔri dol’ o nyaaŋa na, ka o sheeg’ o chɛchɛbuŋ zuɣu n-chaŋ ti tuh’ o soli bɔh’ o, “Alaafee?”

english_verse: “Yes,” Gehazi answered. “But my master has sent me to tell you about two young prophets from the hills of Ephraim. They came asking for help, and now Elisha wants to know if you would give them
translation_verse: Ka Gɛhaazi yɛli, “Alaafee. N dana n-tim ma na ni nti yɛl’ a ni nachimbih’ ayi bɛn nyɛ anabinima n-yi Ifriim zoya tiŋ’ ni kana; ni o suhir’ a ni a ti ba anzinfa laɣibaligu tuhili mini binyɛr’ suma ayi din nyɛ chuɣu binyɛra na.”

english_verse: “Sure,” Naaman replied. “But why don't you take twice that amount of silver?” He convinced Gehazi to take it all, then put the silver in two bags. He handed the bags and the clothes to his two servants, and they carried them for Gehazi.
translation_verse: Ka Naaman yɛl’ o, “Chɛ ka n zaŋ anzinfa laɣibaligu tusaayi ti a.” Ka o daa balim o zaŋ anzinfa laɣibaligu tusaayi mini binyɛr’ suma ayi din nyɛ chuɣu binyɛra maa n-niŋ kpalans’ ayi ni lo n-zaŋ ʒil’ o tumtumdiba ayi, ka bɛ zaŋ li ʒi m-be Gɛhaazi tooni.

english_verse: When they reached the hill where Gehazi lived, he took the bags from the servants and placed them in his house, then sent the men away. After they had gone,
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa ti paai zoli maa gbini, ka o deei li bɛ sani n-zaŋ kpɛhi duu; ka chɛbisi ba ka bɛ ŋmaligi labi.

english_verse: Gehazi went in and stood in front of Elisha, who asked, “Gehazi, where have you been?” “Nowhere, sir,” Gehazi answered.
translation_verse: Ka o daa kpe n-chaŋ ti zan’ o dan’ Ilaisha tooni, ka Ilaisha bɔh’ o, “Gɛhaazi, ya polo ka a lee chaŋ?” Ka o garigi yɛl’ o, “Mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ bi chaŋ luɣ’ shɛli.”

english_verse: Elisha asked, “Don't you know that my spirit was there when Naaman got out of his chariot to talk with you? Gehazi, you have no right to accept money or clothes, olive orchards or vineyards, sheep or cattle, or servants.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Ilaisha bɔh’ o, N shia di ka a sani saha shɛli doo la ni di yi o chɛchɛbuŋ’ ni n-kana ti tuh’ a sol’ la? Pumpɔŋɔ nyɛla saha shɛli di ni simdi ni a deeri liɣiri mini binyɛra ni olivi tihi ni tihi puri ni piɛri ni niɣi ni dabidɔbba ni dabipaɣiba?

english_verse: Because of what you've done, Naaman's leprosy will now be on you and your descendants forever!” Suddenly, Gehazi's skin became white with leprosy, and he left.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu Naaman kɔŋ’ maa ni lu a min’ a bihi zuɣu n-kul maliya sahakam! Ka Gɛhaazi daa ŋmalig’ o sani n-yi ni kɔŋa; ka o niŋgbuna dii paligi laɣilaɣi kaman gumbɔrigu la.

english_verse: One day the prophets said to Elisha, “The place where we meet with you is too small.
translation_verse: Dahin shɛli ka anabinim’ shɛb’ daa ti yɛli Ilaisha, “Nyama, luɣ’ shɛli ti ni be ka a wuhiri ti ŋɔ pɔri pam.

english_verse: Why don't we build a new meeting place near the Jordan River? Each of us could get some wood, then we could build it.” “That's a good idea,” Elisha replied, “get started.”
translation_verse: Chɛ ka ti chaŋ Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili ni, ka ti zaa ti ŋma dari na nti me duri pahi beni.” Ka o garigi yɛli ba, “Chamiya.”

english_verse: “Aren't you going with us?” one of the prophets asked. “Yes, I'll go,” Elisha answered,
translation_verse: Di saha ka bɛ ni yino daa yɛl’ o, “A yi di saɣi n-dol’ ti chaŋ.” Ka o garigi yɛli, “N ni chaŋ.”

english_verse: and he left with them. They went to the Jordan River and began chopping down trees.
translation_verse: Ka o daa pahi bɛ zuɣu ka bɛ chaŋ. Ka bɛ daa paai Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili ni nti gbaai dari maa ŋmabu.

english_verse: “Where did it fall in?” Elisha asked. The prophet pointed to the place, and Elisha cut a stick and threw it into the water at that spot. The ax head floated to the top of the water.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Naawuni nir’ maa daa bɔh’ o, “Ya polo ka di lu?” Ka o wuh’ o di shee, ka Ilaisha ŋmaai daɣu n-zaŋ bahi nimaani n-chɛ ka lɛbiɛlim maa puhi pan’ na.

english_verse: “Now get it,” Elisha told him. And the prophet reached in and grabbed it. Elisha Stops an Invasion of the Syrian Army
translation_verse: Ka o yɛli doo maa, “Yihim’ li,” ka o zaŋ o nuu tim ha yihi li. Bɛ nyaŋ Siria tɔbbihi

english_verse: Time after time, when the king of Syria was at war against the Israelites, he met with his officers and announced, “I've decided where we will set up camp.”
translation_verse: Siria naa daa ti lo tɔbu ni o tuhi Izraɛlnima, ka daa niŋ o sapashinnim’ saawara, yɛli, “Luɣili yaakaza ka n yɛn chaŋ ti dɔni.”

english_verse: Each time, Elisha would send this warning to the king of Israel: “Don't go near there. That's where the Syrian troops have set up camp.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Naawuni nir’ maa daa tim ti yɛli Izraɛl naa, “Miri ka a doli yaakaza polo, dama Sirianim’ yɛn chaŋ ti dɔni la nimaani.”

english_verse: The king of Syria was furious when he found out what was happening. He called in his officers and asked, “Which one of you has been telling the king of Israel our plans?”
translation_verse: Ka yɛlli maa daa muɣisi Siria naa maa pam ka o bol’ o sapashinnim’ na nti bɔhi ba, “Yi ni ŋuni n-lee be Izraɛl naa polo?”

english_verse: “None of us, Your Majesty,” one of them answered. “It's an Israelite named Elisha. He's a prophet, so he can tell his king everything—even what you say in your own room.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ ni yino garigi yɛl’ o, “N dan’ naa, ti ni so bi be o polo. Amaa anabi Ilaisha ŋun be Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ni la n-yɛri Izraɛl naa a ni be a duu tɔɣisiri yɛtɔɣ’ shɛlikam.”

english_verse: “Find out where he is!” the king ordered. “I'll send soldiers to bring him here.” They learned that Elisha was in the town of Dothan and reported it to the king.
translation_verse: Ka o yɛli ba, “Chamiya ti nya o ni be luɣ’ shɛli ka n tim ka bɛ ti gbaag’ o na.” Ka bɛ daa ti yɛl’ o, “O be Dɔtan.”

english_verse: He ordered his best troops to go there with horses and chariots. They marched out during the night and surrounded the town.
translation_verse: Ka o daa tim tɔbbihi pam, ka bɛ zaŋ yuri mini chɛchɛbunsi n-chaŋ yuŋ ti teei gili tiŋ’ maa.

english_verse: When Elisha's servant got up the next morning, he saw that Syrian troops had the town surrounded. “Sir, what are we going to do?” he asked.
translation_verse: Ka biɛɣu daa ti neerina asibaasi, ka Ilaisha sɔŋda yina nti nya ka tɔbbihi mini yuri ni chɛchɛbunsi n-kul teei gili bɛ tiŋ’ maa zaa. Ka Ilaisha sɔŋda maa kuhi yɛli, “Mbaye, n dana! Ka wula ka ti lee yɛn niŋ?”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Elisha answered. “There are more troops on our side than on theirs.”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha garigi yɛl’ o, “Di chɛ ka dabiɛm mal’ a, dama bɛn be ti sani gari bɛn be bɛ sani.”

english_verse: Then he prayed, “Lord, please help him to see.” And the Lord let the servant see that the hill was covered with fiery horses and flaming chariots all around Elisha.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Ilaisha daa suhi Yawɛ yɛli, “Neem’ o nina ka o nya.” Ka Yawɛ daa neei nachimbil’ maa nina ka o lihi nya ka yuri mini buɣim chɛchɛbunsi n-kul pali zoli zuɣu n-teei gili Ilaisha.

english_verse: As the Syrian army came closer, Elisha prayed, “Lord, make those soldiers blind!” And the Lord blinded them with a bright light.
translation_verse: Ka Sirianim’ maa daa kana ni bɛ ti liri Ilaisha, ka Ilaisha suhi Yawɛ yɛli, “N suhir’ a, chɛ ka niriba ŋɔ zom!” Ka o daa chɛ ka bɛ shiri zom kaman Ilaisha ni daa suh’ o yɛli shɛm maa.

english_verse: Elisha told the enemy troops, “You've taken the wrong road and are in the wrong town. Follow me. I'll lead you to the man you're looking for.” Elisha led them straight to the capital city of Samaria.
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha daa yɛli ba, “Pa yi ni chani tin’ shɛli maa soli m-bɔŋɔ; pa yi mi ni chani tin’ shɛli maa m-bɔŋɔ. Doliya ma ka n zaŋ ya tahi yi ni bɔri so maa sani.” Ka o daa zaŋ ba tahi Samaria.

english_verse: When all the soldiers were inside the city, Elisha prayed, “Lord, now let them see again.” The Lord let them see that they were standing in the middle of Samaria.
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa ti kul kpe Samaria puuni, ka Ilaisha suhi Yawɛ yɛli, “Neem’ niriba ŋɔ nina n-chɛ ka bɛ nya.” Ka Yawɛ daa neei bɛ nina maa, ka bɛ lihi nya ka bɛ bela Samaria puuni.

english_verse: The king of Israel saw them and asked Elisha, “Should I kill them, sir?”
translation_verse: Izraɛl naa ni daa nya ba, o daa bɔhila Ilaisha, “M ba, n kum ba? N kum ba?”

english_verse: “No!” Elisha answered. “You didn't capture these troops in battle, so you have no right to kill them. Instead, give them something to eat and drink and let them return to their leader.”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha garigi yɛl’ o, “Di ku ba. A ni ku a ni zaŋ a takɔb’ min’ a tɔbu n-gbahi shɛb’ leeg’ a daba? Bomi la bindirigu ti ba ka bɛ di ka nyu kom, ka lab’ bɛ naa sani.”

english_verse: The king ordered a huge meal to be prepared for Syria's army, and when they finished eating, he let them go. For a while, the Syrian troops stopped invading Israel's territory. King Benhadad of Syria Attacks Samaria
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛl naa maa daa chɛ ka bɛ duɣi bindira pam ti ba, ka bɛ di ka nyu n-naai, ka o chɛ ka bɛ lab’ kuli bɛ naa sani. Ka Sirianim’ daa bi lan kana ti liri Izraɛlnim’ yaha. Naa Bɛnhadad min’ o tɔbbihi teei gili Samaria

english_verse: Some time later, King Benhadad of Syria called his entire army together, then they marched to Samaria and attacked.
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka Siria Naa Bɛnhadad daa ti zaŋ o tɔbbihi zaa n-chaŋ ti teei gili Samaria.

english_verse: One day as the king of Israel was walking along the top of the city wall, a woman shouted to him, “Please, Your Majesty, help me!”
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛl naa daa ti doli tiŋ’ maa gooni zuɣusaa n-chani garita, ka paɣ’ so kuhi yɛl’ o, “N dan’ naa, sɔŋm’ ma!”

english_verse: “Let the Lord help you!” the king said. “Do you think I have grain or wine to give you?”
translation_verse: Ka naa maa yɛl’ o, “Yawɛ yi bi sɔŋ a, wula ka man’ ni tooi sɔŋ a? M malila chi bee wain?”

english_verse: Then he asked, “What's the matter anyway?” The woman answered, “Another woman and I were so hungry that we agreed to eat our sons. She said if we ate my son one day, we could eat hers the next day.
translation_verse: Ka bɔh’ o, “Bɔ n-lee muɣis’ a?” Ka paɣ’ maa yɛl’ o, “Paɣ’ ŋɔ n-daa yɛli ma, ‘Zaŋm’ a bidibiga ŋɔ ka ti duɣi ŋubi zuŋɔ; ka sa zaŋ m mi bidibiga duɣi ŋubi biɛɣuni.’

english_verse: So yesterday we cooked my son and ate him. But today when I went to her house to eat her son, she had hidden him.”
translation_verse: Ka ti zaŋ m bia duɣi ŋubi n-kaai biɛɣu, ka n yɛl’ o, ‘Zaŋm’ a bidibiga la na ka ti duɣi ŋub’, ka ŋun’ zaŋ o bidibiga maa ti sɔɣi.’ ”

english_verse: The king tore off his clothes in sorrow, and since he was on top of the city wall, the people saw that he was wearing sackcloth underneath.
translation_verse: Naa maa ni daa wum paɣ’ maa yɛtɔɣa maa, ka o darigi toog’ omaŋmaŋ’ binyɛrigu, ka doli gooni maa zuɣu garita. Ka niriba nya o ka o yɛla buɣu ka di be o binyɛrigu tiŋli.

english_verse: He said, “I pray that God will punish me terribly, if Elisha's head is still on his shoulders by this time tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Ka o daa yɛli, “N yi bi ŋma Shafat bia Ilaisha la zuɣu zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ, Naawuni ŋun’ niŋm’ ma din gari lala.”

english_verse: Then he sent a messenger to Elisha. Elisha was home at the time, and the important leaders of Israel were meeting with him. Even before the king's messenger arrived, Elisha told the leaders, “That murderer is sending someone to cut off my head. When you see him coming, shut the door and don't let him in. I'm sure the king himself will be right behind him.”
translation_verse: Ka o daa tim ni bɛ ti gbaai Ilaisha na. Di saha maa Ilaisha mini kpeen’ shɛba n-daa ʒi o yiŋa. Ka naa tumo maa daa na bi paana ka Ilaisha yɛli kpamba maa, “Nyamiya, ninvuɣ’ kur’ la ni tim ni bɛ kana ti ŋma n zuɣu shɛm. Nyamiya, Tumo maa yi paana, yin’ yomiya dunoli n-dihi li gbibi ka di chɛliya ka o kpe na. O dan’ napɔn chichiba n-kul vuri dol’ o nyaaŋa ŋɔ na.”

english_verse: Before Elisha finished talking, the messenger came up and said, “The Lord has made all these terrible things happen to us. Why should I think he will help us now?”
translation_verse: O noli daa na bi lu tiŋa, ka naa maa paag’ o sanna ti yɛl’ o, “Ti muɣisigu ŋɔ yila Yawɛ sanna! Ka bɔzuɣu ka n lan yɛn guhi ŋun’ Yawɛ yaha?”

english_verse: Elisha answered, “I have a message for you. The Lord promises that tomorrow here in Samaria, you will be able to buy a large sack of flour or two large sacks of barley for almost nothing.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Ilaisha daa yɛl’ o, “Wummi Yawɛ ni yɛli shɛm. O yɛliya ni biɛɣuni ŋ-ŋɔ tasaha, bɛ sa ni kɔhi zim balli din tibisim nyɛ kilɔgiram ata anzinfa laɣibaligu zaɣ’ yini, ka kɔhi chi kilɔgiram ayɔbu mi anzinfa laɣibaligu zaɣ’ yini Samaria ŋɔ dunɔdal’ ni.”

english_verse: The chief officer there with the king replied, “I don't believe it! Even if the Lord sent a rainstorm, it couldn't produce that much grain by tomorrow.” “You will see it happen, but you won't eat any of the food,” Elisha warned him. The Syrian Army Stops Its Attack
translation_verse: Ka sapashin’ so ŋun daa guli naa maa yɛli Naawuni nir’ maa, “Hal Yawɛ yi yooi zuɣusaa soya bahi gba, lala ku tooi niŋ!” Ka Ilaisha yɛl’ o, “A nini sa ni nya li, amaa ka a nol’ lee ku to li.” Siria tɔbbihi zoya

english_verse: About the same time, four men with leprosy were just outside the gate of Samaria. They said to each other, “Why should we sit here, waiting to die?
translation_verse: Niriba anahi bɛn daa nyɛ kɔnsi daa do Samaria sambani polo dunol’ shee. Ka bɛ daa ti bɔhi taba, “Bɔzuɣu ka ti lee yɛn ʒi kpe hal ti kpi?

english_verse: There's nothing to eat in the city, so we would starve if we went inside. But if we stay out here, we will die for sure. Let's sneak over to the Syrian army camp and surrender. They might kill us, but they might not.”
translation_verse: Ti yi yɛli, ‘Chɛliya ka ti kpe tiŋ’ ŋɔ puuni,’ kum be di ni, ka ti ni kpi; ka ti mi yi ʒi kpe, ti ni kpi. Dinzuɣu chɛliya ka ti chaŋ Sirianim’ sansani ŋɔ ni, bɛ yi ti chɛ ti, ti ni be; ka bɛ yi ti ku ti, ka ti dii kpi.”

english_verse: They said to each other, “This isn't right. Today is a day to celebrate, and we haven't told anyone else what has happened. If we wait until morning, we will be punished. Let's go to the king's palace at once and tell the good news.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka bɛ daa yɛli taba, “Ti bi niŋ din tuhi. Zuŋɔ nyɛla lahiba’ suŋ dabisili. Ka ti yi zaŋ li shini hal ni biɛɣu ti neei, tibidarigibo shɛli ni ti paai ti. Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ chɛliya ka ti chaŋ ti yɛli nayilinima.”

english_verse: They went back to Samaria and shouted up to the guards at the gate, “We've just come from the Syrian army camp, and all the soldiers are gone! The tents are empty, and the horses and donkeys are still tied up. We didn't see or hear anybody.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa chaŋ ti boli ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn guli tiŋ’ maa dunɔdali n-yɛli ba, “Ti chaŋla Sirianim’ sansan’ la ni nti bi nya so bee n-wum so damli, amaa ka bɛ tanti suɣa la beni; ka bɛ yuri mini bɛ bunsi gba loya pahi.”

english_verse: The king got out of bed and said to his officers, “I know what those Syrians are doing. They know we're starving, so they're hiding in the fields, hoping we will go out to look for food. When we do, they can capture us and take over our city.”
translation_verse: Ka naa daa yiɣisi yuŋ’ maa n-yɛl’ o kpambaliba, “N ni yɛli ya Sirianim’ maa ni lo ni bɛ niŋ ti shɛm. Bɛ mi ni kum mali ti, dinzuɣu ka bɛ yi bɛ sansani maa ni n-chaŋ ti sɔɣi, ka tɛhira, ‘Bɛ yi yi bɛ tiŋ’ maa ni na, ti ni gbahi ba zaɣ’ nɛma, ka kpe bɛ tiŋ’ maa ni.’ ”

english_verse: One of his officers replied, “We have a few horses left—why don't we let some men take five of them and go to the Syrian camp and see what's happening? We're going to die anyway like those who have already died.”
translation_verse: Ka o kpambaliba maa ni yino yɛl’ o, “Chɛ ka ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ zaŋ yur’ anu bɛn kpalim ŋɔ chaŋ, dama ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ ninvuɣ’ gbaliŋ bɛn be tiŋ’ ŋɔ puuni gba kul bela barina ni kaman bɛn pun kpi la. Dinzuɣu chɛ ka ti tim ba ka bɛ chaŋ ti nya.”

english_verse: They found two chariots, and the king commanded the men to find out what had happened to the Syrian troops.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa pii wɔribariba ayi, ka naa maa tim ba Siria tɔbbihi maa sani ka yɛli ba, “Chamiya ti nya.”

english_verse: The men rode as far as the Jordan River. All along the way they saw clothes and equipment that the Syrians had thrown away as they escaped. Then they went back to the king and told him what they had seen.
translation_verse: Ka niriba maa daa chaŋ ti doli bɛ naba hal ni Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili ni n-nya ka Sirianim’ maa situra mini bɛ neen’ shɛŋa bɛ ni zo ka chɛ m-bahi kul dɔndo sol’ ni. Ka tuumba maa daa labina ti yɛli naa.

english_verse: At once the people went to the Syrian camp and carried off what was left. They took so much that a large sack of flour and two large sacks of barley sold for almost nothing, just as the Lord had promised.
translation_verse: Di saha ka niriba daa yi n-chaŋ Sirianim’ sansani maa ni nti ʒe bɛ nɛma. Ka bɛ daa kɔhi zim balli din tibisim nyɛ kilɔgiram ata anzinfa laɣibaligu zaɣ’ yini, ka kɔhi chi din tibisim nyɛ kilɔgiram ayɔbu mi anzinfa laɣibaligu zaɣ’ yini kaman Yawɛ ni daa pun yɛli shɛm la.

english_verse: The king of Israel had put his chief officer in charge of the gate, but he died when the people trampled him as they rushed out of the city.
translation_verse: Naa daa chɛ ka o sapashin’ so ŋun gul’ o la n-ʒe n-guli dunɔdali, ka niriba daa no o dunɔdali maa ni hal ka o ti kpi kaman Naawuni nir’ maa ni daa pun yɛli shɛm saha shɛli naa ni daa ka o sanna la.

english_verse: But the officer refused to believe that even the Lord could do that. So Elisha warned him that he would see it happen, but would not eat any of the food.
translation_verse: sapashini maa daa yɛlila Naawuni nir’ maa, “Hal Yawɛ yi yooi zuɣusaa soya bahi gba, lala ku tooi niŋ!” Ka Naawuni nir’ maa yɛl’ o, “A nini sa ni nya bindirigu maa, amaa ka a noli lee ku to li.”

english_verse: And that's exactly what happened—the officer was trampled to death.
translation_verse: Ka di daa shiri niŋ o lala, dama niriba daa no o dunɔdali maa ni hal ka o ti kpi.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the king was asking Gehazi the servant of Elisha about the amazing things Elisha had been doing.
translation_verse: Di saha naa maa daa tɔɣisirila Gɛhaazi ŋun daa nyɛ Naawuni nir’ maa sɔŋda la yɛtɔɣa n-yɛr’ o, “Yɛlim’ ma Ilaisha ni daa tum tuun’ kar’ shɛŋa zaa yɛla.”

english_verse: While Gehazi was telling him that Elisha had brought a dead boy back to life, the woman and her son arrived. “Here's the boy, Your Majesty,” Gehazi said. “And this is his mother.”
translation_verse: O ni daa yɛri naa maa Ilaisha ni daa neei kpim’ kum ni shɛm saha shɛli maa, ka o ni daa neei paɣ’ so bia kum ni maa kana nti yɛli naa maa ni o labisim’ o yili min’ o tiŋgbani ti o. Ka Gɛhaazi daa yɛli naa maa, “N dana, n-nyɛ paɣ’ maa, Ilaisha ni daa neeg’ o bi’ so kum ni maa mi m-bɔŋɔ.”

english_verse: Some time later Elisha went to the capital city of Damascus to visit King Benhadad of Syria, who was sick. And when Benhadad was told he was there,
translation_verse: Dahin shɛli ka Ilaisha daa ti ka Damaskus na. Di saha maa ka Siria Naa Bɛnhadad daa biɛra. Ka bɛ daa yɛl’ o, “Naawuni nir’ la be yaŋɔ.”

english_verse: Hazael left with forty camel loads of the best things made in Damascus as a gift for Elisha. He found the prophet and said, “Your servant, King Benhadad, wants to know if he will get well.”
translation_verse: Ka Hazaɛl daa bo Damaskus binshɛɣukam n-ʒili laakumnim’ pihinahi chaŋ ni o ti puhi Naawuni nir’ maa. Ka Hazaɛl daa paai ti zani Ilaisha tooni ka yɛl’ o, “A bia Siria Naa Bɛnhadad n-tim ma a sanna ni n ti bɔh’ a nya o ni kpaŋ o barigu ŋɔ ni?”

english_verse: “Tell him he will,” Elisha said to Hazael. “But the Lord has already told me that Benhadad will definitely die.”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha daa yɛl’ o, “Cham’ ti yɛli naa maa ni biɛhiŋ kani, o ni kpaŋ; amaa Yawɛ lee kahigi wuhi ma ni o ni bahi kpi.”

english_verse: Elisha stared at him until Hazael was embarrassed, then Elisha began crying.
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha daa mirig’ o nina kpa Hazaɛl n-kul lihir’ o hal ka vi ti gbaag’ o. Ka Ilaisha kumda.

english_verse: “Sir, why are you crying?” Hazael asked. Elisha answered, “Because I know the terrible things you will do to the people of Israel. You will burn down their walled cities and slaughter their young men. You will even crush the heads of their babies and rip open their pregnant women.”
translation_verse: Ka Hazaɛl bɔh’ o, “N dana, bɔzuɣu ka a kumda?” Ka Ilaisha garigi yɛl’ o, “N ni mi a ni ti yɛn niŋ Izraɛlnim’ zaɣ’ biɛ’ shɛli zuɣu n-chɛ ka n kumdi maa. A ni ti nyo bɛ birininim’ buɣim, ka zaŋ takɔbi ku bɛ nachimbihi, ka ŋme n-chɛrisichɛrisi bɛ bibihi, ka karigi bɛ paɣipuhinim’ puya.”

english_verse: “How could I ever do anything like that?” Hazael replied. “I'm only a servant and don't have that kind of power.” “Hazael, the Lord has told me that you will be the next king of Syria.”
translation_verse: Ka Hazaɛl bɔh’ o, “Ya ka a dabili ŋun nyɛ baa ŋɔ yɛn nya yiko n-tum tuun’ karili ŋɔ!” Ka Ilaisha garigi yɛl’ o, “Yawɛ kahigi wuhi ma ni a ni ti leei Siria naa.”

english_verse: But the very next day, Hazael got a thick blanket; he soaked it in water and held it over Benhadad's face until he died. Hazael then became king. King Jehoram of Judah (
translation_verse: Amaa ka biɛɣu daa neei, ka Hazaɛl niŋ kom mahigi bɔdua n-zaŋ pa naa maa ninni hal ka o ti leei Naawuni dini. Ka Hazaɛl daa di nam zan’ o zaani. Juda Naa Jɛhɔram yɛla (

english_verse: So Jehoram and his cavalry marched to Zair, where the Edomite army surrounded him and his commanders. During the night he attacked the Edomites, but he was defeated, and his troops escaped to their homes.
translation_verse: Di saha maa ka Jɛhɔram daa zaŋ o chɛchɛbunsi zaa n-yiɣisi yuŋ chaŋ Zairi, ka o min’ o chɛchɛbunsi sapashinnim’ ti lu Ɛdomnim’ bɛn daa teei gil’ o zuɣu n-niŋ ba buɣim; amaa ka o tɔbbihi daa zo n-kuli.

english_verse: While Jehoram was king, the people of Edom rebelled and chose their own king.
translation_verse: O ʒiɛman’ ni ka Ɛdomnim’ daa zaɣisi ni Judanim’ ku lan su ba; ka daa pii so n-leei bɛmaŋmaŋ’ naa.

english_verse: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat became king of Judah in Joram's fifth year as king of Israel, while Jehoshaphat was still king of Judah.
translation_verse: Izraɛl Naa Jɔram ŋun daa nyɛ Ɛhab bia la ni daa di nam zaŋ chaŋ yuma anu saha, ka Juda Naa Jɛhɔram ŋun daa nyɛ Jɛhɔshafat bia la daa di nam.

english_verse: Jehoram disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He married Ahab's daughter and was as sinful as Ahab's family and the kings of Israel.
translation_verse: O daa dolila Izraɛl nanim’ naba n-tum kaman Ɛhab min’ o daŋ ni daa tum shɛm la, dama o paɣ’ daa nyɛla Ɛhab bipuɣiŋga. O daa tum alahichi Yawɛ sani.

english_verse: But the Lord refused to destroy Judah, because he had promised his servant David that someone from his family would always rule in Judah.
translation_verse: Amaa Yawɛ daa bi yu ni o bahi Judanim’ yoli o dabili Dauda zuɣu, dama o daa pun lo Dauda alikauli ni o ni zaŋ firila ti o min’ o bidibisi.

english_verse: Everything else Jehoram did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Jɛhɔram ni daa tum tuun’ shɛŋa pahi min’ o ni daa pun tum shɛlikam, bɛ sab’ di yɛla niŋ Juda nanim’ litaafi shɛli bɛ ni booni Yɛlikura litaafi la ni.

english_verse: Jehoram died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Ahaziah then became king. King Ahaziah of Judah (
translation_verse: Ka Jɛhɔram daa ti leei Naawuni dini, ka bɛ sɔɣ’ pah’ o yaannim’ zuɣu Dauda tiŋ’ la ni, ka o bia Ahazia daa di nam zan’ o zaani. Juda Naa Ahazia yɛla (

english_verse: Ahaziah son of Jehoram became king of Judah in the twelfth year of Joram's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Ɛhab bia Izraɛl Naa Jɔram ni daa di nam zaŋ chaŋ yuun’ pinaayi saha, ka Juda Naa Jɛhɔram bia Ahazia gba daa di nam.

english_verse: Since Ahaziah was related to Ahab's family, he acted just like them and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong.
translation_verse: Ahazia gba daa dolila Ɛhab daŋ niriba naba n-tum alahichi Yawɛ sani kaman Ɛhab daŋ niriba maa ni daa tum shɛm la, dama o daa nyɛla Ɛhab daŋ niriba maa deemba.

english_verse: Ahaziah went with King Joram of Israel to attack King Hazael and the Syrian troops at Ramoth in Gilead. Joram was wounded in that battle,
translation_verse: Ka ŋun’ Ahazia daa pahi Ɛhab bia Jɔram la zuɣu, ka bɛ lo tɔbu chaŋ ni bɛ ti tuhi Siria Naa Hazaɛl Ramɔtigiliad, ka Sirianim’ daa ti ti Jɔram daŋa.

english_verse: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
translation_verse: Piligu ni, Naawuni daa namla zuɣusaa mini dunia.

english_verse: The earth was barren, with no form of life; it was under a roaring ocean covered with darkness. But the Spirit of God was moving over the water. The First Day
translation_verse: Dunia ŋɔ daa ka taɣinamsi, di daa kul bela vau, ka zibisim limsi bɔɣ’ zilinli, ka Naawuni shia daa be kom zuɣusaa ginda.

english_verse: God said, “I command light to shine!” And light started shining.
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa yɛli, “Neesim, neema!” Ka neesim dii neei.

english_verse: God looked at the light and saw that it was good. He separated light from darkness
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa nya ka neesim maa viɛla, ka o woligi neesim maa ka chɛ zibisim.

english_verse: and named the light “Day” and the darkness “Night.” Evening came, then morning—that was the first day. The Second Day
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa boli neesim maa wuntaŋ’ ni, ka boli zibisim maa mi yuŋ. Ka di daa niŋ zaawuni, di nyaaŋa ka biɛɣu neei; ka di niŋ dabisili din daŋ tooni.

english_verse: God said, “I command a dome to separate the water above it from the water below it.”
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa yɛli, “Foliŋga, niŋmi kom ŋɔ sunsuuni m-pirigi kom maa buyi.”

english_verse: and named it “Sky.” Evening came, then morning—that was the second day. The Third Day
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa boli foliŋga maa “Zuɣusaa.” Ka di daa niŋ zaawuni, di nyaaŋa ka biɛɣu neei; ka di niŋ dabisili din pah’ ayi.

english_verse: God said, “I command the water under the sky to come together in one place, so there will be dry ground.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa lan yɛli, “Kom din be foliŋga tiŋli ŋɔ laɣimmi dɔni luɣ’ yini, ka chɛ ka tiŋgban’ kuŋ yi n-dɔni.” Ka di daa shiri niŋ lala.

english_verse: God named the dry ground “Land,” and he named the water “Ocean.” God looked at what he had done and saw that it was good.
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa boli tiŋgban’ kuŋ maa “Tiŋgbani,” ka boli kom din laɣim do luɣ’ yini maa mi “Teeku.” Ka Naawuni daa nya li ka di viɛla.

english_verse: God said, “I command the earth to produce all kinds of plants, including fruit trees and grain.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa lan yɛli, “Binyɛra din bindi tiŋgban’ ni ka mali biɛlim mini tihi din wala mali kpila balibu kam zaa, bilimiya.” Ka di daa shiri niŋ lala.

english_verse: The earth produced all kinds of vegetation. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Ka binyɛra din bindi tiŋgban’ ni ka mali biɛlim mini tihi din wala mali kpila balibu kam zaa shiri bili. Ka Naawuni daa nya li ka di viɛla.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the third day. The Fourth Day
translation_verse: Ka di daa niŋ zaawuni, di nyaaŋa ka biɛɣu neei; ka di niŋ dabisili din pah’ ata.

english_verse: God said, “I command lights to appear in the sky and to separate day from night and to show the time for seasons, special days, and years.
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa lan yɛli, “Neesim shɛŋa neemiya zuɣusaa sagbana ni n-woligi wuntaŋ’ ni ka chɛ yuŋ,” ka neesim maa wuhiri shihira ni saha ni dabisa ni yuma;

english_verse: I command them to shine on the earth.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: ka lan nyɛ zuɣusaa neesim din ne dunia ni. Ka di daa shiri niŋ lala.

english_verse: God made two powerful lights, the brighter one to rule the day and the other to rule the night. He also made the stars.
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa lan nam neesim kara ayi n-chɛ ka din galisi pam la ne wuntaŋ’ ni, ka chɛ ka din pa di zuɣu mi ne yuŋ; ka daa nam saŋmarisi gba.

english_verse: Then God put these lights in the sky to shine on the earth,
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa zaŋ ba niŋ foliŋga maa zuɣusaa ni bɛ ne dunia ŋɔ ni,

english_verse: to rule day and night, and to separate light from darkness. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: ka su wuntaŋ’ ni mini yuŋ, ka woligi neesim ka chɛ zibisim. Ka Naawuni daa nya li ka di viɛla.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fourth day. The Fifth Day
translation_verse: Ka di daa niŋ zaawuni, di nyaaŋa ka biɛɣu neei; ka di niŋ dabisili din pah’ anahi.

english_verse: God said, “I command the ocean to be full of living creatures, and I command birds to fly above the earth.”
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa lan yɛli, “Chɛ ka binnɛma pam be kom ni, ka chɛ ka noonsi be zuɣusaa sagbana tiŋli yiɣiri gindi dunia ni.”

english_verse: So God made the giant sea monsters and all the living creatures that swim in the ocean. He also made every kind of bird. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa lan nam binnɛma zaɣ’ kara niŋ teeku ni, ka nam binnɛma balibu kam bɛn be kom ni chana ni noonsi balibu kam. Ka Naawuni daa nya ba ka bɛ viɛla.

english_verse: Then he gave the living creatures his blessing—he told the ocean creatures to increase and live everywhere in the ocean and the birds to increase everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Ka o daa niŋ alibarika niŋ bɛ ni ka yɛli ba, “Dɔɣimiya ka wɔɣi n-nab’ pali teeku mini dunia.”

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fifth day. The Sixth Day
translation_verse: Ka di daa niŋ zaawuni, di nyaaŋa ka biɛɣu neei; ka di niŋ dabisili din pah’ anu.

english_verse: God said, “I command the earth to give life to all kinds of tame animals, wild animals, and reptiles.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa lan yɛli, “Binnɛma balibu kam, bɛnya tiŋgbani zuɣu; niɣi mini binnɛma bɛn gbamdi tiŋa ni mɔɣu ni biŋkɔbiri balibu kam.” Ka di shiri niŋ lala.

english_verse: God made every one of them. Then he looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa nam mɔɣu ni biŋkɔbiri balibu kam zaa, ka nam niɣi balibu kam zaa, ka nam binnɛma bɛn gbamdi tiŋa balibu kam zaa. Ka Naawuni daa nya ba ka bɛ viɛla.

english_verse: God said, “Now we will make humans, and they will be like us. We will let them rule the fish, the birds, and all other living creatures.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Naawuni daa lan yɛli, “Chɛliya ka ti nam ninsala ŋ-ŋmahindi timaŋa, ka o be kaman ti ni be shɛm ŋɔ, ka chɛ ka bɛ su zahim mini noonsi ni niɣi ni dunia ŋɔ zaa ni binnɛma balibu kam bɛn gbamdi dunia ŋɔ ni fukumsi.”

english_verse: So God created humans to be like himself; he made men and women.
translation_verse: Naawuni daa nam ninsala ŋ-ŋmahindila omaŋa, ka o be kaman Naawuni ni be shɛm. O daa nam ba la doo mini paɣa.

english_verse: God gave them his blessing and said: Have a lot of children! Fill the earth with people and bring it under your control. Rule over the fish in the ocean, the birds in the sky, and every animal on the earth.
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa niŋ alibarika niŋ bɛ ni ka yɛli ba, “Dɔɣimiya n-nab’ pali dunia ŋɔ n-su di fukumsi; ka su teeku puuni zahim mini noonsi ni binnɛma balibu kam bɛn be dunia ŋɔ ni.”

english_verse: And I have given the green plants as food for everything else that breathes, including animals, both wild and tame, and birds. And so it was.
translation_verse: ka zaŋ bimbilli kam din maha n-ti mɔɣu ni biŋkɔbiri balibu kam mini binnɛma balibu kam bɛn mali nyɛvili zaŋ tabili noonsi balibu kam ni binnɛma balibu kam bɛn gbamdi tiŋgban’ ni ni bɛ dira.” Ka di daa shiri niŋ lala.

english_verse: God looked at what he had done. All of it was very good! Evening came, then morning—that was the sixth day.
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa nya o ni nam binshɛɣukam maa zaa, ka di viɛl’ pam. Ka di daa niŋ zaawuni, di nyaaŋa ka biɛɣu neei; ka di niŋ dabisili din pah’ ayɔbu.

english_verse: So the heavens and the earth and everything else were created. The Seventh Day
translation_verse: Lala ka Naawuni daa nam zuɣusaa mini dunia ŋɔ ni di binshɛɣukam zaa naai.

english_verse: That's how God created the heavens and the earth. The Garden of Eden When the Lord God made the heavens and the earth,
translation_verse: Naawuni ni daa nam zuɣusaa mini dunia ŋɔ binshɛɣukam zaa shɛm m-bala. Idɛn puu Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Naawuni ŋɔ ni daa nam dunia ŋɔ mini zuɣusaa dahin’ shɛli,

english_verse: no grass or plants were growing anywhere. God had not yet sent any rain, and there was no one to work the land.
translation_verse: tutuɣu daa na kani, ka binshɛli mi daa na bi bili yi tiŋgban’ ni na, dama Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Naawuni ŋɔ daa bi chɛ ka saa mira, ka so mi daa kani kɔra;

english_verse: But streams came up from the ground and watered the earth.
translation_verse: amaa kom daa puhiri yirila tiŋ’ na m-mahigiri tiŋgbani zaa.

english_verse: The Lord God took some soil from the ground and made a man. God breathed life into the man, and the man started breathing.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Naawuni ŋɔ daa zaŋ tiŋgban’ ni taŋkpaɣu n-nam ninsala, ka vuhi nyɛvili vuhim niŋ o nyee ni; ka ninsal’ leei ŋun mali nyɛvili.

english_verse: The Lord made a garden in a place called Eden, which was in the east, and he put the man there.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Naawuni ŋɔ daa nam puu niŋ Idɛn din be wulimpuhili polo n-zaŋ o ni nam ninsal’ so maa niŋ nimaani.

english_verse: The Lord God filled the garden with all kinds of beautiful trees and fruit trees. Two other trees were in the middle of the garden. One of these gave life—the other gave the wisdom to know the difference between right and wrong.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Naawuni ŋɔ daa chɛ ka tia kam din lihibu viɛla ka simdi dibu bili yi tiŋgban’ ni na. Ka nyɛvili tia mini tia din chɛri ka nir’ baŋdi zaɣ’ suŋ ni zaɣ’ biɛɣu gba daa be puu maa sunsuuni.

english_verse: From Eden a river flowed out to water the garden, then it divided into four rivers.
translation_verse: Ka mɔɣili kom daa zɔri yiri Idɛn na n-teeni puu maa; ka di daa woligi n-niŋ mɔɣ’ anahi nimaani.

english_verse: The first one is the Pishon River that flows through the land of Havilah,
translation_verse: Mɔɣ’ shɛli din daŋ tooni yuli m-booni Pishɔn. Dina n-zɔri gindi Havila tiŋgbɔŋ zaa, ka salima be nimaani.

english_verse: where pure gold, rare perfumes, and precious stones are found.
translation_verse: Ka di tiŋgbɔŋ maa salima viɛl’ pam; ka tulaale tihi mini kuɣ’ viɛla gba be nimaani.

english_verse: The second is the Gihon River that winds through Ethiopia.
translation_verse: Ka mɔɣ’ shɛli din pah’ ayi yuli booni Gihɔn. Dina n-nyɛ din zɔri gindi Itiɔpia tiŋgbɔŋ.

english_verse: The Tigris River that flows east of Assyria is the third, and the fourth is the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Ka mɔɣ’ shɛli din pah’ ata yuli booni Tigiris. Dina n-zɔri kpari Asiria wulimpuhili polo. Ka mɔɣ’ shɛli din pah’ anahi mi yuli booni Yufretiiz.

english_verse: The Lord God put the man in the Garden of Eden to take care of it and to look after it.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Naawuni ŋɔ daa zaŋ ninsal’ maa niŋ Idɛn puu maa ni ni o kɔr’ li, ka yuuni li.

english_verse: But the Lord told him, “You may eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Naawuni ŋɔ daa yɛli ninsal’ maa, “Dim’ tihi din be puu ŋɔ ni wala;

english_verse: except the one that has the power to let you know the difference between right and wrong. If you eat any fruit from that tree, you will die before the day is over!”
translation_verse: amaa ti’ shɛli din chɛri ka nir’ baŋdi zaɣ’ suŋ mini zaɣ’ biɛɣu la, miri ka a di li, dama a yi ti di li dahin’ shɛli, a ni kpi.”

english_verse: The Lord God said, “It isn't good for the man to live alone. I will make a suitable partner for him.”
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Naawuni ŋɔ daa yɛli, “Di bi simdi ni doo be o ko, n ni nam sɔŋda ŋun simd’ o ti o.”

english_verse: So the Lord God made him fall into a deep sleep, and he took out one of the man's ribs. Then after closing the man's side,
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Naawuni ŋɔ daa chɛ ka gom gbaai doo maa pam, o ni daa gbihiri saha shɛli maa, ka o daa yih’ o sapir’ kɔb’ yini ka daai nimaani nimdi ŋari;

english_verse: the Lord made a woman out of the rib. The Lord God brought her to the man,
translation_verse: ka zaŋ o ni daa yihi sapir’ kɔb’ shɛli maa nam paɣa n-zaŋ o ti doo maa.

english_verse: and the man exclaimed, “Here is someone like me! She is part of my body, my own flesh and bones. She came from me, a man. So I will name her Woman!”
translation_verse: Di saha ka doo maa daa yɛli, “Mmaŋmaŋ’ kɔbili mini mmaŋmaŋ’ niŋgbuŋ m-bɔŋɔ. O yuli m-booni paɣa, dama doo niŋgbuŋ ni ka o yina.”

english_verse: That's why a man will leave his own father and mother. He marries a woman, and the two of them become like one person.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka doo ŋmaligir’ o ba min’ o ma sani n-zaŋd’ omaŋ’ tabind’ o paɣa, ka bɛ niriba ayi maa be kaman ninvuɣ’ yino la.

english_verse: Although the man and his wife were both naked, they were not ashamed.
translation_verse: Doo maa min’ o paɣ’ maa daa bela bɛ zaɣim, amaa ka di bi mali ba vi.

english_verse: The snake was sneakier than any of the other wild animals that the Lord God had made. One day it came to the woman and asked, “Did God tell you not to eat fruit from any tree in the garden?”
translation_verse: Wahu daa nyɛla yɛmbimbiɛrilana n-gari Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Naawuni ŋɔ ni daa nam mɔɣu ni biŋkɔb’ shɛb’ zaa. Ka wahu daa ti bɔhi paɣ’ maa, “Naawuni yɛliya ni yi miri ka yi di puu ŋɔ ni ti’ shɛli wala?”

english_verse: The woman answered, “God said we could eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ maa yɛli wahu maa, “Ti ni tooi di ti’ shɛŋa din be puu ŋɔ ni wala;

english_verse: except the one in the middle. He told us not to eat fruit from that tree or even to touch it. If we do, we will die.”
translation_verse: amaa Naawuni yɛl’ ti, ‘Miriya ka yi di ti’ shɛli din be puu ŋɔ sunsuuni ŋɔ wala bee n-shihi li gba, yi yi niŋ lala, yi ni kpi.’ ”

english_verse: “No, you won't!” the snake replied.
translation_verse: Amaa ka wahu maa yɛli paɣ’ maa, “Yi ku kpi.

english_verse: “God understands what will happen on the day you eat fruit from that tree. You will see what you have done, and you will know the difference between right and wrong, just as God does.”
translation_verse: Dama Naawuni mi ni yi yi di li, yi nini ni neei, ka yi be kaman ŋun’ Naawuni, ka mi zaɣ’ suŋ ni zaɣ’ biɛɣu.”

english_verse: The woman stared at the fruit. It looked beautiful and tasty. She wanted the wisdom that it would give her, and she ate some of the fruit. Her husband was there with her, so she gave some to him, and he ate it too.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu paɣ’ maa ni daa nya ka tia maa wala lihibu mali kɔre, ka viɛl’ ni dibu, ka lan nyɛ ti’ shɛli din ni ti nir’ baŋsim maa, ka o pɔhigi li di, ka zaŋ di shɛli ti ti o yidana, ka o gba di.

english_verse: At once they saw what they had done, and they realized they were naked. Then they sewed fig leaves together to cover themselves.
translation_verse: Di saha maa ka bɛ niriba ayi maa zaa nini daa shiri neei, ka bɛ nya ka bɛ bela bɛ zaɣim, ka bɛ daa ŋahi fiig tia vari she n-zaŋ so.

english_verse: Late in the afternoon, when the breeze began to blow, the man and woman heard the Lord God walking in the garden. So they hid behind some trees. Sin Brings a Curse
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Naawuni ŋɔ daa ti be puu maa ni zaawun’ mahili saha n-chani ginda, ka doo maa min’ o paɣ’ maa wum o damli, ka zo nti sɔɣi puu maa ni tihi ni ni Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Naawuni ŋɔ di nya ba.

english_verse: The Lord God called out to the man and asked, “Where are you?”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Naawuni ŋɔ daa boli doo maa m-bɔh’ o, “Ya polo ka a lee be?”

english_verse: The man answered, “I was naked, and when I heard you walking through the garden, I was frightened and hid!”
translation_verse: Ka o garigi yɛli, “N wumla a damli puu ŋɔ ni ka dabiɛm gbaai ma, dama m bela n zaɣim, dina n-chɛ ka n sɔɣi maa.”

english_verse: “How did you know you were naked?” God asked. “Did you eat any fruit from that tree in the middle of the garden?”
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni bɔh’ o, “Ŋuni n-lee yɛl’ a ni a bela a zaɣim? A dila ti’ shɛli n ni yɛl’ a ni a miri ka a di la?”

english_verse: “It was the woman you put here with me,” the man said. “She gave me some of the fruit, and I ate it.”
translation_verse: Ka doo maa yɛli, “A ni zaŋ paɣ’ so ti ma ni o be n san’ la, ŋuna n-zaŋ tia maa walli maa ti ma ka n di.”

english_verse: The Lord God then asked the woman, “What have you done?” “The snake tricked me,” she answered, “and I ate some of that fruit.”
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Naawuni ŋɔ bɔhi paɣ’ maa, “Bɔ n-niŋ ka a niŋ lala?” Ka paɣ’ maa yɛli, “Wahu n-yɔhim ma ka n di li.” Naawuni darigi alahichinim’ tibili

english_verse: So the Lord God said to the snake: “Because of what you have done, you will be the only animal to suffer this curse— For as long as you live, you will crawl on your stomach and eat dirt.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Naawuni ŋɔ daa yɛli wahu, “A ni niŋ shɛm ŋɔ zuɣu, n ni yɛli noli ti a n-gari yiŋ’ biŋkɔbiri mini mɔɣu ni biŋkɔbiri zaa; a ni nyɛritila a puli zuɣu, ka diri taŋkpaɣu hal ni a nyɛvil’ tariga.

english_verse: You and this woman will hate each other; your descendants and hers will always be enemies. One of hers will strike you on the head, and you will strike him on the heel.”
translation_verse: Ka n ni zaŋ dimdi niŋ a mini paɣ’ sunsuuni ni a zuliya min’ o zuliya sunsuuni, ka paɣ’ zuliya maa ni ti ŋme m-bɔr’ a zuɣu, ka a mi zuliya ti dim o zuliya napɔŋkpaa.”

english_verse: Then the Lord God said to the woman, “You will suffer terribly when you give birth. But you will still desire your husband, and he will rule over you.”
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa yɛli paɣ’ maa, “N ni chɛ ka a nya biɛrim pam bihi dɔɣibu ni; a shiri ni nya biɛrim bihi dɔɣibu ni; amaa di zaa yoli, a kɔre kul ni be a yidan’ ni, ka o ni su a.”

english_verse: The Lord said to the man, “You listened to your wife and ate the fruit I told you not to eat. And so, the ground will be under a curse because of what you did. As long as you live, you will have to struggle to grow enough food.
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa ŋmaligi yɛli Adam mi, “A ni deeg’ a paɣ’ noli, ka di ti’ shɛli n ni yɛl’ a ni a miri ka a di la zuɣu, n yɛli noli niŋ tiŋgban’ ni a zuɣu; a yɛn tumdila tuun’ kpɛma di ni n-nyari bindirigu diri hal ni a nyɛvil’ tariga.

english_verse: Your food will be plants, but the ground will produce thorns and thistles.
translation_verse: Ka gɔhi mini tutu’ shɛŋa din mali gɔhi ni bili tiŋgban’ ni a zuɣu; ka a ni diri tiŋgban’ ni tihi wala.

english_verse: You will sweat all your life to earn a living; you were made out of soil, and you will once again turn into soil.”
translation_verse: A ni tum tuun’ kpɛma ka woligu yiri a ni ka a nyari bindirigu diri hal ti lab’ tiŋgbani maa ni, dama di ni ka a daa yina. Taŋkpaɣu n-nyɛ a, ka a ni ti lan lab’ taŋkpaɣu maa ni yaha.”

english_verse: The man Adam named his wife Eve because she would become the mother of all who live.
translation_verse: Adam daa bol’ o paɣ’ maa yul’ la Awa, dama ŋuna n-daa nyɛ ninsalinim’ zaa ma.

english_verse: Then the Lord God made clothes out of animal skins for the man and his wife.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Naawuni ŋɔ daa zaŋ biŋkɔbiri gbana n-she n-ti Adam min’ o paɣ’ maa ka bɛ so. Naawuni yihi Adam mini Awa Idɛn puu ni

english_verse: The Lord said, “They now know the difference between right and wrong, just as we do. But they must not be allowed to eat fruit from the tree that lets them live forever.”
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Naawuni ŋɔ daa yɛli, “Nyama, pumpɔŋɔ ninsal’ bemi kaman ti ni be shɛm, ka mi zaɣ’ suŋ ni zaɣ’ biɛɣu, ka di pa shɛli ka o ti pɔhigi nyɛvili tia la walli di m-be hal ni saha din ka bahigu.”

english_verse: So the Lord God sent them out of the Garden of Eden, where they would have to work the ground from which the man had been made.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Naawuni ŋɔ daa kar’ o yihi Idɛn puu maa ni ni o ti kɔr’ o ni daa yi tiŋgban’ shɛli ni na maa.

english_verse: Then God put winged creatures at the entrance to the garden and a flaming, flashing sword to guard the way to the life-giving tree.
translation_verse: O ni daa kari ninsal’ yihi Idɛn puu maa ni maa, o daa zaŋla chɛrubinim’ mini takɔbi din nyɛ buɣim niɛm ka ŋmaligiri luɣilikam zali Idɛn puu maa wulimpuhili polo ni bɛ gu so’ shɛli din chani ti’ shɛli din tiri nyɛvil’ maa gbini.

english_verse: Adam and Eve had a son. Then Eve said, “I'll name him Cain because I got him with the help of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Ka doo maa min’ o paɣa Awa daa laɣim ka o niŋ pua n-dɔɣi Keen ka yɛli, “N nya ninsala Yawɛ sɔŋsim zuɣu.”

english_verse: Later she had another son and named him Abel. Abel became a sheep farmer, but Cain farmed the land.
translation_verse: Ka o daa ti lan dɔɣ’ o tizo Ɛbɛl gba. Ɛbɛl daa nyɛla piɛgula, ka Keen mi nyɛ pukpara.

english_verse: One day, Cain gave part of his harvest to the Lord,
translation_verse: Dahin shɛli ka Keen daa ti zaŋ o puu ni bindira na nti mali sara Yawɛ sani,

english_verse: and Abel also gave an offering to the Lord. He killed the first-born lamb from one of his sheep and gave the Lord the best parts of it. The Lord was pleased with Abel and his offering,
translation_verse: ka Ɛbɛl mi daa zaŋ o buzɔŋ ni piɛbil’ tuuli ni o kpam na nti mali sara, ka Yawɛ Naawuni nini daa tiɣi Ɛbɛl min’ o sara maa,

english_verse: but not with Cain and his offering. This made Cain so angry that he could not hide his feelings.
translation_verse: amaa ka o nini daa bi tiɣi Keen ŋun’ min’ o sara maa. Dinzuɣu ka Keen suhu daa yiɣisi pam, ka o zuŋ o ninni.

english_verse: The Lord said to Cain: What's wrong with you? Why do you look so angry?
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa bɔhi Keen, “Bɔ n-niŋ ka a chɛ ka a suhu yiɣisi, ka a zuŋ a ninni?

english_verse: If you had done the right thing, you would be smiling. But you did the wrong thing, and now sin is waiting to attack you like a lion. Sin wants to destroy you, but don't let it!
translation_verse: A yi di niŋ din simdi, n naan ku deei li? Ka a yi bi niŋ din simdi, alahichi do a dunol’ ni m-bɔri ni di nyaŋ a, amaa di niŋ kamaata ni a nyaŋ li.”

english_verse: Cain said to his brother Abel, “Let's go for a walk.” And when they were out in a field, Cain attacked and killed him.
translation_verse: Dahin shɛli ka Keen daa ti yɛl’ o tizo Ɛbɛl, “Ti cham’ mɔɣu ni.” Bɛ ni daa ti be mɔɣu maa ni saha shɛli, ka Keen yiɣisi lu o tizo Ɛbɛl maa zuɣu n-ku o.

english_verse: Afterwards the Lord asked Cain, “Where is Abel?” “How should I know?” he answered. “Am I supposed to look after my brother?”
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa bɔhi Keen, “A tizo Ɛbɛl be ya?” Ka Keen garigi yɛli, “M bi mi; mani n-nyɛ n tizo maa gula?”

english_verse: Then the Lord said: Why have you done this terrible thing? You killed your own brother, and his blood flowed onto the ground. Now his blood is calling out for me to punish you.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ bɔh’ o, “Tuun’ bɔ ka a lee tum maa? A tizo maa ʒim kukoli kuhigu n-yi tiŋgban’ ni ka n sanna.

english_verse: And so, I'll put you under a curse. Because you killed Abel and made his blood run out on the ground, you will never be able to farm it again.
translation_verse: Ka pumpɔŋɔ, noli yɛlibu ni yi tiŋgban’ shɛli din yaai di noli n-deeg’ a tizo maa ʒim a nuu ni maa na di a.

english_verse: When you try to farm the land, it won't produce anything for you. From now on, you'll be without a home, and you'll spend the rest of your life wandering from place to place.
translation_verse: Ka a yi lan ko puu tiŋgbani maa ni, di bindira ku lan niŋ viɛnyɛliŋga. A ni leei ŋun ka kpɛhili shee, ka leei ŋun dari gindi dunia ŋɔ ni.”

english_verse: “This punishment is too hard!” Cain said.
translation_verse: Ka Keen yɛli Yawɛ, “N tibidarigibo maa galisiya gari ma.

english_verse: “You're making me leave my home and live far from you. I will have to wander about without a home, and just anyone could kill me.”
translation_verse: Nyama, a kari ma tiŋgbani ŋɔ ni, ka kari ma a sani; ka n leei ŋun ka kpɛhili shee, ka leei ŋun dari gindi dunia ŋɔ ni, ka ŋunkam ti nya ma ni ku ma.”

english_verse: “No!” the Lord answered. “Anyone who kills you will be punished seven times worse than I am punishing you.” So the Lord put a mark on Cain to warn everyone not to kill him.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yɛl’ o, “Di ku niŋ lala. So yi ku nyin’ Keen, bɛn’ kum’ niriba ayopɔin yo a kubu maa samli.” Ka Yawɛ daa dalim Keen ni di chɛ ka so ti nya o, ka ku ku o.

english_verse: But Cain had to go far from the Lord and live in the Land of Wandering, which is east of Eden. More and More People
translation_verse: Ka Keen daa yi Yawɛ sani n-chaŋ ti be tiŋgban’ shɛli din be Idɛn puu la wulimpuhili polo, ka di yuli booni Nɔd la. Keen zuliya

english_verse: Later, Cain and his wife had a son named Enoch. At the time Cain was building a town, and so he named it Enoch after his son.
translation_verse: Ka Keen min’ o paɣ’ daa laɣim ka o niŋ pua n-dɔɣi Inok. Ka Keen daa me o tiŋa n-zaŋ o bia Inok maa yuli m-bol’ li Inok.

english_verse: Then Enoch had a son named Irad, who had a son named Mehujael, who had a son named Methushael, who had a son named Lamech.
translation_verse: Ka Inok daa dɔɣi Irad; ka Irad daa nyɛ Mɛhujaɛl ba, ka Mɛhujaɛl nyɛ Mɛtushaɛl ba, ka Mɛtushaɛl mi nyɛ Lamɛk ba.

english_verse: Lamech and Adah had two sons, Jabal and Jubal. Their son Jabal was the first to live in tents and raise sheep and goats. Jubal was the first to play harps and flutes.
translation_verse: O tizo yuli n-daa booni Jubal. Ŋun’ mi n-daa nyɛ ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn ŋmɛri mɔɣilɔnim’ mini yupiɛbiriba yaba.

english_verse: Lamech and Zillah had a son named Tubal Cain who made tools out of bronze and iron. They also had a daughter, whose name was Naamah.
translation_verse: Ka Zilla mi daa dɔɣi Tubalikeen ŋun daa nyɛ ŋun zaŋ daanya mini kuriti m-mali tuma nɛma balibu kam zaa la. Ka Tubalikeen tizɔpaɣ’ daa nyɛ Naama.

english_verse: Anyone who tries to get even with me will be punished ten times more than anyone who tries to get even with Cain.”

english_verse: he said: These people are working together because they all speak the same language. This is just the beginning. Soon they will be able to do anything they want.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yɛli, “Nyama, bɛ ni nyɛ zuliya yini ka mali zuliya yɛtɔɣ’ yini maa zuɣu ka bɛ tumdi lala maa, ka bɛ ni lo ni bɛ niŋ shɛm piligu n-na bɔŋɔ; ka binshɛli kani ka bɛ ni bɔri ni bɛ niŋ li ka di ku nani.

english_verse: Let's go down and confuse them! We'll make them speak different languages, and they won't be able to understand each other.
translation_verse: Chɛliya ka ti chaŋ bɛ sani nti chɛ ka bɛ yɛtɔɣa woli taba, ka di chɛ ka bɛ ku lan tooi wum tab’ yɛtɔɣa.”

english_verse: So the people had to stop building the city, because the Lord confused their language and scattered them all over the earth. That's how the city of Babel got its name. The Descendants of Shem
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa boli nimaani yuli Babɛl, dama nimaani ka Yawɛ daa chɛ ka bɛ yɛtɔɣa woligiwoligi; nimaani ka o daa lan wurim ba kpɛhi dunia ŋɔ luɣ’ shɛlikam zaa. Shɛm daŋ niriba (
