translation_verse: Di saha ka bɛ daa gbaai bua n-kɔrigi zaŋ Yisifu binyɛrigu tim bua maa ʒim ni

english_verse: After this, they took the coat to their father and said, “We found this! Look at it carefully and see if it belongs to your son.”
translation_verse: n-zaŋ o binyɛr’ wɔɣinli din bɔɣiri wɔɣ’ maa nti ti bɛ ba ka yɛl’ o, “Ti pihi li mi, lihim’ li nya, a bia binyɛrigu m-bala bee pa dina.”

english_verse: Jacob knew it was Joseph's coat and said, “It's my son's coat! Joseph has been torn to pieces and eaten by some wild animal.”
translation_verse: Ka o daa baŋ li ka yɛli, “M bia maa binyɛrigu m-bala; mɔɣu ni biŋkɔbigu n-gbaag’ o maa. Biɛhiŋ kani, ŋ-ŋɔ o kul dari tɔhitɔhila Yisifu zaa.”

english_verse: Jacob mourned for Joseph a long time, and to show his sorrow he tore his clothes and wore sackcloth.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yaakubu daa darigi toog’ o binyɛrigu, ka zaŋ buɣu so o shee ni n-kum o bia maa kuli dabisi’ gbaliŋ.

english_verse: All of Jacob's children came to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. “No,” he said, “I will go to my grave, mourning for my son.” So Jacob kept on grieving.
translation_verse: Ka o bidibisi min’ o bipuɣinsi zaa daa kana ni bɛ ti maag’ o suhu, amaa ka o daa zaɣisi ka yɛli, “N ni kum m bia maa zuɣu hal ti paag’ o kpiimba biɛhigu shee.” Lala ka o ba daa kum o zuɣu.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Midianites had sold Joseph in Egypt to a man named Potiphar, who was the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Ka Midiannim’ maa daa zaŋ Yisifu chaŋ Ijipti nti kɔhi Pɔtifa ŋun daa nyɛ tɔbbi’ shɛb’ bɛn guli Firawuna la sapashin’ kpɛm’ zuɣu.

english_verse: About that time Judah left his brothers in the hill country and went to live near his friend Hirah in the town of Adullam.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Juda daa yi o mabihi maa sani chaŋ Adulam nti be do’ so ŋun yuli daa booni Hira la sani.

english_verse: While there he met the daughter of Shua, a Canaanite man. Judah married her,
translation_verse: Ka Juda daa ti nya Keenan do’ so ŋun yuli daa booni Shua la bipuɣiŋga n-kpuɣ’ o; ka daa zaŋ o niŋ o paɣa,

english_verse: and they had three sons. He named the first one Er;
translation_verse: ka o niŋ pua n-dɔɣi bidibiga, ka o bol’ o yuli Ɛr.

english_verse: The third one was born when Judah was in Chezib, and she named him Shelah.
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ maa daa ti lan dɔɣi bidibiga m-bol’ o yuli Shɛla. Chɛzib ka o daa be ka dɔɣ’ o.

english_verse: Later, Judah chose Tamar as a wife for Er, his oldest son.
translation_verse: Ka Juda daa bo paɣ’ ti o bituuli Ɛr. Paɣ’ maa yuli n-daa booni Tama.

english_verse: But Er was very evil, and the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Juda bituuli Ɛr maa daa nyɛ ninvuɣ’ biɛɣu Yawɛ sani, ka Yawɛ daa ku o.

english_verse: Onan knew the child would not be his, and when he had sex with Tamar, he made sure that she would not get pregnant.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Onan daa mi ni o bi yɛn su bihi maa. Dinzuɣu o min’ o biɛli pakoli maa daa yi ti dɔni, o daa yihirila o kom bahi tiŋa ni di chɛ ka o ku dɔɣi bihi ti o biɛli maa.

english_verse: The Lord wasn't pleased with Onan and took his life too.
translation_verse: Ka o ni daa niŋ shɛm maa bi niŋ Yawɛ nyaɣisim, ka o daa ku o gba.

english_verse: Judah did not want the same thing to happen to his son Shelah, and he told Tamar, “Go home to your father and live there as a widow until my son Shelah is grown.” So Tamar went to live with her father.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Juda daa yɛl’ o bia pakoli Tama, “Kulim’ a ba yiŋ’ ti ʒini pakolim hal ka m bia Shɛla ti zooi.” O daa zɔrimi ni Shɛla gba ti kpi kaman o biɛyanim’ maa ni daa kpi shɛm maa. Dinzuɣu ka Tama daa kul’ o ba yiŋ’ ti ʒiya.

english_verse: Some years later Judah's wife died, and he mourned for her. He then went with his friend Hirah to the town of Timnah, where his sheep were being sheared.
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka Juda paɣ’ ŋun daa nyɛ Shua bipuɣiŋga la daa kpi. O ni daa mal’ o kuli naai nyaaŋa ka o min’ o zo Hira ŋun daa nyɛ Adulam nir’ la chaŋ Timna ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn daa chɛr’ o piɛri kɔbiri la sani.

english_verse: Tamar found out that her father-in-law Judah was going to Timnah to shear his sheep.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yɛli Tama, “A yidan’ ba chanila Timna ni o ti chɛ o piɛri kɔbiri.”

english_verse: She also realized that Shelah was now a grown man, but she had not been allowed to marry him. So she decided to dress in something other than her widow's clothes and to cover her face with a veil. After this, she sat outside the town of Enaim on the road to Timnah.
translation_verse: Di saha ka o daa pirig’ o pako’ chinchina sɔŋ ka zaŋ sariga pa m-mulis’ omaŋ’ chaŋ ti ʒini Ɛnaim dunoli din daa be Timna soli zuɣu la shee; dama o daa nyaya ka Shɛla bi doo, ka bɛ bi chɛ ka o kpuɣ’ o.

english_verse: When Judah came along, he did not recognize her because of the veil. He thought she was a prostitute
translation_verse: Juda ni daa nya o, o daa tɛhiya ni o nyɛla pagɔrili, dama o daa zaŋla sariga m-pil’ lims’ o ninni.

english_verse: “What do you want?” he asked in return. “The ring on that cord around your neck,” was her reply. “I also want the special walking stick you have with you.” He gave them to her, they slept together, and she became pregnant.
translation_verse: Ka Juda bɔh’ o, “Bɔ ka a lee bɔri ni n zaŋ ti a ka di nyɛ alikauli lɔbu shɛhira?” Ka paɣ’ maa garigi yɛl’ o, “Zaŋm’ a nintua din mali dalinli ŋɔ mini zoligo ŋɔ ni a jaaŋgbee din be a nuu ni ŋɔ ti ma.” Di saha ka o daa zaŋ li ti o, ka zaŋ o dɔni, ka o daa niŋ pua.

english_verse: After returning home, Tamar took off the veil and dressed in her widow's clothes again.
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka paɣ’ maa daa yiɣisi kuli nti paai sariga maa sɔŋ, ka lan zaŋ o pako’ chinchina maa so.

english_verse: Judah asked his friend Hirah take a goat to the woman, so he could get back the ring and walking stick, but she wasn't there.
translation_verse: Ka Juda daa zaŋ bubil’ polli maa ti o zo ŋun daa nyɛ Adulam nir’ la ni o ti ti paɣ’ maa ka deeg’ o neen’ shɛŋa din daa nyɛ alikauli lɔbu shɛhira la na, amaa ka o daa bi nya paɣ’ maa.

english_verse: Hirah asked the people of Enaim, “Where is the prostitute who sat along the road outside your town?” “There's never been one here,” they answered.
translation_verse: Ka o daa bɔhi tiŋ’ maa ni dɔbba, “Ka jɛmbu duu pagɔr’ so ŋun yi ʒiini Inaim palli naŋgbanyee ŋɔ la lee be ya?” Ka bɛ yɛl’ o, “Pagɔr’ so na ʒi n-ka kpe na.”

english_verse: Hirah went back and told Judah, “I couldn't find the woman, and the people of Enaim said no prostitute had ever been there.”
translation_verse: Ka o daa lab’ ti yɛli Juda, “M bi nya paɣ’ maa; ka tiŋ’ maa nim’ yɛli ma ni pagɔr’ so na ʒi n-ka kpe na.”

english_verse: “If you couldn't find her, we'll just let her keep the things I gave her,” Judah answered. “And we'd better forget about the goat, or else we'll look like fools.”
translation_verse: Ka Juda daa yɛl’ o, “Chɛ ka o zaŋ nɛma maa leeg’ o dini, di yi pa lala, niriba ni la ti; nyama, n-chɛ ka a zaŋ bubil’ polli maa ni a ti ti o, ka a bi tooi bo n-nya o.”

english_verse: About three months later someone told Judah, “Your daughter-in-law Tamar has behaved like a prostitute, and now she's pregnant!” “Drag her out of town and burn her to death!” Judah shouted.
translation_verse: Zaŋ chaŋ chira ata saha ka so daa ti yɛli Juda, “Tama ŋun nyɛ a bia pakol’ la gɔrila pagɔrisigu, ka din pahi di zuɣu nyɛla, o niŋla pua o pagɔrisigu maa gɔbu ni.” Ka Juda daa yɛli, “Zaŋmiy’ o na ti niŋ buɣim nyo o.”

english_verse: As Tamar was being dragged off, she sent someone to tell her father-in-law, “The man who gave me this ring, this cord, and this walking stick is the one who got me pregnant.”
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa zaŋ paɣ’ maa yina, ka o tim ti yɛl’ o yidan’ ba Juda, “Do’ so ŋun su nɛma ŋɔ n-ti ma pua maa. N suhir’ a, lihim’ li nya ŋuni n-lee su li. Nɛma maa n-nyɛ: nintua din mali dalinli ŋɔ mini zoligo ŋɔ ni jaaŋgbee ŋɔ.”

english_verse: “Those are mine!” Judah admitted. “She's a better person than I am, because I broke my promise to let her marry my son Shelah.” After this, Judah never slept with her again.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Juda daa baŋ nɛma maa ka yɛli, “Paɣ’ maa nyɛla wuntizɔra n-gari ma, n ni bi zaŋ o ti m bia Shɛla la zuɣu.” Ka o daa bi saɣi ka o mini paɣ’ maa lan dɔni yaha.

english_verse: Tamar later gave birth to twins. But before either of them was born, one of them stuck a hand out of her womb. The woman who was helping tied a red thread around the baby's hand and explained, “This one came out first.”
translation_verse: O ni daa wolisira, ka bi’ yino zaŋ o nuu tirina, ka paɣidɔɣisɔtɔɣinda daa zaŋ gali ʒee lo o nuu maa ka yɛli, “Ŋumbɔŋɔ ka bɛ daŋ dɔɣibu.”

english_verse: At once his hand went back in, and the other child was born first. The woman then said, “What an opening you've made for yourself!” So they named the baby Perez.
translation_verse: Amaa ka o daa fɔh’ o nuu maa kpɛhi, ka o mabia maa daŋ o yibuna; ka paɣidɔɣisɔtɔɣinda maa yɛli, “A niŋla kpaɣikpaɣi nya soli yina maa!” Dinzuɣu ka bɛ daa bol’ o yuli Pɛrɛz.

english_verse: When the brother with the red thread was born, they named him Zerah.
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka o mabia maa gba daa yina ka gali ʒee maa lo o nuu, ka bɛ daa bol’ o mi yuli Zɛra.

english_verse: So Joseph lived in the home of Potiphar, his Egyptian owner. Soon Potiphar realized that the Lord was helping Joseph to be successful in whatever he did.
translation_verse: Ka o dan’ maa daa nya ka Yawɛ be Yisifu sani, ka chɛ ka o ni niŋdi shɛlikam zaa tɔŋda.

english_verse: Potiphar liked Joseph and made him his personal assistant, putting him in charge of his house and all of his property.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Pɔtifa suhu daa yu Yisifu pam, ka Yisifu daa tumd’ o tuma, ka o zaŋ o leeg’ o yiŋ’ tumtumdiba zuɣulana, ka zaŋ o binshɛɣukam zaa niŋ o nuu ni.

english_verse: Potiphar left everything up to Joseph, and with Joseph there, the only decision he had to make was what he wanted to eat. Joseph was well-built and handsome,
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Pɔtifa daa zaŋ o ni mali shɛlikam zaa niŋ Yisifu nuu ni. Yisifu ni daa be o sani maa zuɣu, o baɣa daa lan ka shɛl’ ni n-naɣ’ pahila bindir’ shɛl’ o ni daa diri ni. Yisifu daa yi nachimbil’ viɛlli pam, ka o lihibu viɛla.

english_verse: and Potiphar's wife soon noticed him. She asked him to make love to her,
translation_verse: Ka di daa niŋ daba ayi ka Yisifu dan’ maa paɣ’ ti lihir’ o kɔre lihigu, ka yɛl’ o, “Chɛ ka m min’ a dɔni.”

english_verse: but he refused and said, “My master isn't worried about anything in his house, because he has placed me in charge of everything he owns.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Yisifu daa zaɣisi ka yɛl’ o dan’ paɣ’ maa, “Nyama, n ni be n dan’ sani ŋɔ, o baɣa lan ka shɛl’ ni yil’ ŋɔ. O zaŋ o ni mali shɛlikam niŋla n nuu ni.

english_verse: No one in my master's house is more important than I am. The only thing he hasn't given me is you, and that's because you are his wife. I won't sin against God by doing such a terrible thing as this.”
translation_verse: O bi galisi gari ma yili ŋɔ puuni, o mi bi mɔŋ ma shɛli naɣila nyini, dama a nyɛla o paɣa; ka wula ka n ni tooi tum ninvuɣ’ biɛtali tuun’ titali ŋɔ n-tum alahichi zaŋ chaŋ Naawuni sani?”

english_verse: She kept begging Joseph day after day, but he refused to do what she wanted or even to go near her.
translation_verse: Hal o ni daa kul yɛri Yisifu lala dabisili kam maa zaa yoli, Yisifu daa bi saɣi ni o min’ o dɔni.

english_verse: One day, Joseph went to Potiphar's house to do his work, and none of the other servants were there.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Yisifu daa ti kpe yili maa ni dahin’ shɛli ni o ti tum o tuma, ka ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn daa be yili maa ni kani.

english_verse: Potiphar's wife grabbed hold of his coat and said, “Make love to me!” Joseph ran out of the house, leaving his coat there in her hands.
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ maa daa gbaai Yisifu binyɛrigu gbib’ ka yɛl’ o, “Chɛ ka m min’ a dɔni.” Amaa ka Yisifu daa fuɣ’ o binyɛrigu maa niŋ paɣ’ maa nuu ni, ka guui yi yili maa ni.

english_verse: she called in her servants and said, “Look! This Hebrew has come just to make fools of us. He tried to rape me, but I screamed for help.
translation_verse: ka o daa boli ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn daa be o yiŋ’ maa na nti yɛli ba, “Nyamiya, o ni zaŋ Hiburu nir’ maa na ka o ti lihi ʒiɛm ti shɛm, o kpɛmina ni o ti zaŋ ma dɔni, ka n kuhi pam.

english_verse: And when he heard me scream, he ran out of the house, leaving his coat with me.”
translation_verse: O ni wum ka n duhi n yee kuhi pam maa, ka o chɛ o binyɛrigu bahi ma ka guui yi yili ŋɔ.”

english_verse: Potiphar's wife kept Joseph's coat until her husband came home.
translation_verse: Di saha ka o daa zaŋ Yisifu binyɛrigu maa sɔŋ baɣil’ omaŋ’ hal ka Yisifu dan’ maa ti kuna.

english_verse: But when I screamed for help, he left his coat and ran out of the house.”
translation_verse: amaa n ni di kul duhi n yee kuhi pam saha shɛli, ka o chɛ o binyɛrigu ŋɔ bahi ma ka guui yi yili ŋɔ.”

english_verse: and threw Joseph in the same prison where the king's prisoners were kept. While Joseph was in prison,
translation_verse: Ka Yisifu dan’ maa daa gbaag’ o n-zaŋ o ti niŋ sarika ni din nyɛ luɣ’ shɛli bɛ ni daa zaŋ naa sarikanim’ niŋ, ka o daa be sarika maa ni.

english_verse: the Lord helped him and was good to him. He even made the jailer like Joseph so much that
translation_verse: Amaa ka Naawuni daa be Yisifu sani ka niŋ o nirilim, ka chɛ ka dansarika gul’ maa suhu yu o.

english_verse: he put him in charge of the other prisoners and of everything that was done in the jail.
translation_verse: Ka dansarika gul’ maa daa zaŋ sarikanim’ bɛn zaa be sarika maa ni niŋ Yisifu nuu ni, ka Yisifu daa nyɛ ŋun niŋdi binshɛɣukam zaa nimaani.

english_verse: The jailer did not worry about anything, because the Lord was with Joseph and made him successful in all that he did.
translation_verse: Ka dansarika gul’ maa daa bi lan lihir’ o ni zaŋ binshɛlikam niŋ Yisifu nuu ni maa, dama Yawɛ daa be Yisifu sani, ka o daa yi niŋ shɛlikam, Yawɛ chɛrimi ka di tɔŋ.

english_verse: While Joseph was in prison, both the king's personal servant and his chief cook made the king angry. So he had them thrown into the same prison with Joseph.
translation_verse: ka o daa zaŋ ba ti kpɛhi duu o tɔbbihi bɛn daa gul’ o la sapashin’ kpɛm’ yiŋ’ luɣ’ shɛli bɛ ni daa zaŋ Yisifu ti niŋ maa.

english_verse: They spent a long time in prison, and the official in charge of the palace guard, made Joseph their servant.
translation_verse: Ka tɔbbihi sapashin’ kpɛm’ maa daa zaŋ ba niŋ Yisifu nuu ni ka o sɔŋdi ba. Ka bɛ daa be duu maa ni n-niŋ daba ayi.

english_verse: The next morning, when Joseph went to see the men, he could tell they were upset,
translation_verse: Ka Yisifu daa ti kpe bɛ sani asiba n-nya ka bɛ malila suhugarigu.

english_verse: “We each had a dream last night,” they answered, “and there is no one to tell us what they mean.” Joseph replied, “Doesn't God know the meaning of dreams? Now tell me what you dreamed.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ yɛl’ o, “Ti sa zahimla zahima ka bi nya ŋun ni wuhi ti di gbinni.” Ka Yisifu bɔhi ba, “Pa Naawuni n-wuhiri zahindi gbinni? N suhiri ya, yɛlimiya ma yi zahima maa.”

english_verse: with three branches. As soon as it budded, it blossomed, and its grapes became ripe.
translation_verse: ka tiwula ata be di zuɣu, ka di ni sa kul piligi puhiri vari ka dii daai pum n-wali wala ka di mooi.

english_verse: I held the king's cup and squeezed the grapes into it, then I gave the cup to the king.”
translation_verse: Ka Firawuna pipia daa be n nuu ni, ka m pɔhi wain tiwala maa kahim di kom niŋ Firawuna pipia maa ni n-zaŋ li ti ti ŋun’ Firawuna.”

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three branches stand for three days,
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yisifu daa yɛl’ o, “Di gbinni m-bɔŋɔ: Tiwula ata maa nyɛla daba ata.

english_verse: and in three days the king will pardon you. He will make you his personal servant again, and you will serve him his wine, just as you used to do.
translation_verse: Zaŋ chaŋ daba ata dali, Firawuna ni chɛ ka bɛ kana ti yih’ a nti lan zaŋ a labis’ a tuma ni; ka a ni lan zaŋdi Firawuna pipia maa ni binnyura maa ti tir’ o kaman a ni daa pun nyɛ o wain tɔɣira shɛm la.

english_verse: But when these good things happen, please don't forget to tell the king about me, so I can get out of this place.
translation_verse: Amaa di yi ti niŋ a viɛnyɛla, n suhir’ a, nyin’ teemi n yɛla, ka niŋ ma nirilim n-zaŋ n yɛtɔɣa tɔɣisi Firawuna; ka lala chɛ ka n yi sarika ŋɔ ni.

english_verse: I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and here in Egypt I haven't done anything to deserve being thrown in jail.
translation_verse: Dama yɛlimaŋli, bɛ daa zu ma la Hiburu tiŋgbɔŋ ni na; ka kpe gba, m bi tum taal’ shɛli ka di simdi ni bɛ zaŋ ma kpɛhi sarika.”

english_verse: When the chief cook saw that Joseph had given a good meaning to the dream, he told Joseph, “I also had a dream. In it I was carrying three breadbaskets stacked on top of my head.
translation_verse: Bɔrɔbɔro shɛriba kpɛm’ la ni daa wum di gbinni ka di viɛl’ maa, ka o daa yɛli Yisifu, “N gba sa zahimla zahindi. Bɔrɔbɔro piɛr’ ata n-sa tam n zuɣu ni,

english_verse: The top basket was full of all kinds of baked things for the king, but birds were eating them.”
translation_verse: ka bindira balibu kam din nyɛ bɛ ni daa she shɛli ti Firawuna be piɛ’ shɛli din tam zuɣusaa ni, amaa ka noombihi lee kana ti diri li n zuɣu ni piɛri maa ni.”

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three baskets are three days,
translation_verse: Ka Yisifu daa garigi yɛl’ o, “Di gbinni m-bɔŋɔ: Piɛr’ ata maa nyɛla daba ata.

english_verse: and in three days the king will cut off your head. He will hang your body on a pole, and birds will come and peck at it.
translation_verse: Zaŋ chaŋ daba ata dali, Firawuna ni chɛ ka bɛ kana ti yih’ a ti ŋma a zuɣu, ka zaŋ a yili tia ka noonsi di a nimdi.”

english_verse: and had the cook put to death. Everything happened just as Joseph had said it would,
translation_verse: amaa ka daa chɛ ka bɛ zaŋ o bɔrɔbɔro shɛriba kpɛm’ maa ti yil’ tia kaman Yisifu ni daa yɛli ba shɛm maa.

english_verse: but the king's personal servant completely forgot about Joseph.
translation_verse: Amaa di zaa yoli, wain booriba kpɛm’ la daa tam Yisifu yɛla ka bi teeg’ o yɛla.

english_verse: Two years later the king of Egypt dreamed he was standing beside the Nile River.
translation_verse: Yuma ayi nyaaŋa ka Firawuna daa ti zahim zahindi n-nya ka o ʒiɛla Nail Mɔɣili duli.

english_verse: Suddenly, seven fat, healthy cows came up from the river and started eating grass along the bank.
translation_verse: Ka naɣ’ kara ayopɔin bɛn niŋgbuna kul nyɛlisiri daa yi Nail Mɔɣili maa ni na ti ŋubiri mɔri.

english_verse: ate the fat, healthy cows. When this happened, the king woke up.
translation_verse: Ka naɣ’ kɔri bɛn daa gaŋsigaŋsi maa daa zaŋ naɣ’ kara ayopɔin bɛn niŋgbuna daa kul nyɛlisiri la ŋubi. Ka Firawuna daa yirigi neei.

english_verse: The king went back to sleep and had another dream. This time seven full heads of grain were growing on a single stalk.
translation_verse: Ka o daa lan gbihi n-zahim zahindi din pah’ ayi. Kawaan’ kara ayopɔin din viɛla n-daa nyaɣi kawaan’ kaɣ’ yini zuɣu.

english_verse: Later, seven other heads of grain appeared, but they were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Ka kawaan’ kɔr’ ayopɔin din nyɛ biisim polo pɔhim ni ŋme shɛli ka di zaɣi daa to n-yina pahi kawaan’ kara maa zuɣu.

english_verse: The thin heads of grain swallowed the seven full heads. Again the king woke up, and it had only been a dream.
translation_verse: Ka kawaan’ kɔri maa daa zaŋ kawaan’ kara ayopɔin maa vali. Ka Firawuna daa yirigi neei n-nya ka di nyɛla zahindi.

english_verse: The next morning the king was upset. So he called in his magicians and wise men and told them what he had dreamed. None of them could tell him what the dreams meant.
translation_verse: Ka di daa muɣis’ o pam asibaasi, ka o tim ti boli Ijipti timanim’ mini baŋdiba zaa na, ka ŋun’ Firawuna daa yɛli ba o zahima maa, amaa ka so daa kani n-nyɛ ŋun ni tooi wuhi Firawuna o zahima maa gbinni.

english_verse: The king's personal servant said: Now I remember what I was supposed to do.
translation_verse: Di saha ka wain booriba kpɛm’ la daa yɛli Firawuna, “N teegi n galimi ni nyɛ shɛli zuŋɔ.

english_verse: When you were angry with me and your chief cook, you threw us both in jail in the house of the captain of the guard.
translation_verse: Nyin’ Firawuna suhu ni daa ti yiɣisi bah’ a tumtumdiba zuɣu, ka a zaŋ m min’ a bɔrɔbɔro shɛriba kpɛm’ ti kpɛhi duu a tɔbbihi bɛn gul’ a sapashin’ kpɛm’ yiŋ’ la,

english_verse: One night we both had dreams, and each dream had a different meaning.
translation_verse: ti daa ti zahimla zahindi yuŋ dahin yini, ka ti zaa yino kam zahindi daa mali di gbinni.

english_verse: A young Hebrew, who was a servant of the captain of the guard, was there with us at the time. When we told him our dreams, he explained what each of them meant,
translation_verse: Ka Hiburu nachimbil’ so ŋun nyɛ a tɔbbihi bɛn gul’ a la sapashin’ kpɛm’ dabili daa be ti sani, ka ti yɛl’ o, ka o daa wuhi ti ti zaa yinoyino zahindi gbinni ni nyɛ shɛm.

english_verse: and everything happened just as he said it would. I got my job back, and the cook was put to death.
translation_verse: O ni daa kul wuhi ti di gbinni shɛm, di daa ti shiri niŋla pali; a daa labisi ma n tuma ni, ka chɛ ka bɛ zaŋ a bɔrɔbɔro shɛriba kpɛm’ la mi ti yili tia.”

english_verse: The king sent for Joseph, who was quickly brought out of jail. He shaved, changed his clothes, and went to the king.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Firawuna daa tim ka bɛ chaŋ ti boli Yisifu n-zaŋ o sarika maa ni na yomyom; ka o daa pini o ninni ka taɣi binyɛra ye n-kpe Firawuna sani.

english_verse: The king said to him, “I had a dream, yet no one can explain what it means. I am told that you can interpret dreams.”
translation_verse: Ka Firawuna daa ti yɛli Yisifu, “N zahimla zahindi ka bi nya so ŋun ni wuhi ma di gbinni; ka n wum ka bɛ yɛli ma ni bɛ yi yɛl’ a zahindi ni nyɛ shɛm, a ni tooi wuhi di gbinni.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Joseph answered, “I can't do it myself, but God can give a good meaning to your dreams.”
translation_verse: Ka Yisifu daa garigi yɛli Firawuna, “Pa mani n-wuhiri di gbinni maa, amaa Naawuni ni wuhi nyin’ Firawuna di gbinni ka di niŋ a nyaɣisim.”

english_verse: The king told Joseph: I dreamed I was standing on the bank of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Firawuna daa yɛli Yisifu, “N zahindi maa puuni, n daa ʒiɛla Nail Mɔɣili duli;

english_verse: I saw seven fat, healthy cows come up out of the river, and they began feeding on the grass.
translation_verse: ka naɣ’ kara ayopɔin bɛn niŋgbuna kul nyɛlisiri daa yi Nail Mɔɣili maa ni na ti ŋubiri mɔri,

english_verse: Next, seven skinny, bony cows came up out of the river. I have never seen such terrible looking cows anywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: ka naɣ’ kɔri bɛba ayopɔin shɛb’ bɛn kul gaŋsigaŋsi daa yina n-ka bɛ sanna, ka n nini daa na ʒi n-nya bɛ tatabo Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni.

english_verse: But you couldn't tell it, because these skinny cows were just as skinny as they were before. At once, I woke up.
translation_verse: amaa bɛ ni daa zaŋ ba ŋub’ maa, so daa naan ku tooi baŋ ni bɛ zaŋ ba ŋubi, dama bɛ daa na kul gaŋsigaŋsimi, ka be kaman bɛ ni daa pun be shɛm. Di nyaaŋa ka n daa yirigi neei.

english_verse: I also dreamed that I saw seven heads of grain growing on one stalk. The heads were full and ripe.
translation_verse: N zahindi maa puuni, n daa lan nya ka kawana ayopɔin nyaɣi tam kawaan’ kaɣ’ yini zuɣu n-kul ŋmɛlim baribara;

english_verse: Then seven other heads of grain came up. They were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: ka kawaan’ kɔr’ ayopɔin din nyɛ biisim ni kpe shɛli ka di kul zaɣizaɣimi to n-yina pahi di zuɣu,

english_verse: These heads of grain swallowed the full ones. I told my dreams to the magicians, but none of them could tell me the meaning of the dreams.
translation_verse: ka kawaan’ kɔr’ ayopɔin maa daa zaŋ kawaan’ kar’ ayopɔin maa vali. Ka n zaŋ li yɛli timanima, amaa ka bɛ ni so bi tooi wuhi ma di gbinni.”

english_verse: Joseph replied: Your Majesty, both of your dreams mean the same thing, and in them God has shown what he is going to do.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yisifu daa yɛli Firawuna, “A zahima maa nyɛla zaɣ’ yini, Naawuni n-kahig’ o ni yɛn niŋ shɛli wuhi nyin’ Firawuna maa.

english_verse: The seven good cows stand for seven years, and so do the seven good heads of grain.
translation_verse: Naɣ’ kara bɛba ayopɔin la gbinni nyɛla yuma ayopɔin, ka kawaan’ kar’ ayopɔin la gba gbinni nyɛla yuma ayopɔin; zahindi maa kul nyɛla zaɣ’ yini.

english_verse: The seven skinny, ugly cows that came up later also stand for seven years, as do the seven bad heads of grain that were scorched by the desert wind. The dreams mean there will be seven years when there won't be enough grain.
translation_verse: Naɣ’ kɔri bɛba ayopɔin bɛn daa yina n-kul gaŋsigaŋsi la gbinni nyɛla yuma ayopɔin, ka kawaan’ kɔr’ ayopɔin din daa nyɛ biisim ni kpe shɛl’ la gba gbinni nyɛla kum lubu yuma ayopɔin.

english_verse: It is just as I said—God has shown what he intends to do.
translation_verse: Di nyɛla kaman n ni pun yɛli nyin’ Firawuna shɛm la, Naawuni n-kahig’ o ni yɛn niŋ shɛli wuh’ a.

english_verse: For seven years Egypt will have more than enough grain,
translation_verse: Yuma ayopɔin din kanna puuni, bindira ni niŋ pam Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ zaa ni.

english_verse: The famine will be so bad that no one will remember that once there had been plenty.
translation_verse: Ka so ti ku mi ni bindira daa niŋya pam kum shɛli din yɛn doli di nyaaŋa na maa zuɣu, dama kum maa ni ti mii pam.

english_verse: God has given you two dreams to let you know that he has definitely decided to do this and that he will do it soon.
translation_verse: Ka nyin’ Firawuna ni nya zahindi maa buyi la wuhiya ni Naawuni n-zal’ li, ka ni chɛ ka di ku yuui, ka di niŋ.

english_verse: Your Majesty, you should find someone who is wise and will know what to do, so that you can put him in charge of all Egypt.
translation_verse: “Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ, piim’ ninvuɣ’ so ŋun mali dahin’ shɛli tɛha ni yɛm n-zaŋ Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ yɛla niŋ o nuu ni.

english_verse: Then appoint some other officials to collect one fifth of every crop harvested in Egypt during the seven years when there is plenty.
translation_verse: Di lan simdi ni a pii kpambal’ shɛb’ ka bɛ su tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ tuma fukumsi, ka bɛ ti laɣim bindira pirigibu bunu puuni yim zuɣu zali bindira ni ti yɛn niŋ pam yuma ayopɔin shɛŋa puuni la.

english_verse: Give them the power to collect the grain during those good years and to store it in your cities.
translation_verse: Ka a chɛ ka bɛ laɣim yuma ayopɔin shɛŋa din kanna ŋɔ ni bindira din yɛn niŋ pam maa zaa zali, ka di nyɛ a ni zaŋ bindir’ shɛli niŋ fukumsi fɔntinsi ni ka bɛ gbib’ li.

english_verse: It can be stored until it is needed during the seven years when there won't be enough grain in Egypt. This will keep the country from being destroyed because of the lack of food. Joseph Is Made Governor over Egypt
translation_verse: Ka lala bindira maa ni nyɛ a tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni bindira n-ʒiɛya gu yuma ayopɔin shɛŋa ni kum ni ti yɛn lu Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni maa, ka di chɛ ka kum ti ku ku tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ nima.” Bɛ zaŋ Yisifu leei Ijipti gomna

english_verse: The king and his officials liked this plan.
translation_verse: Ka Firawuna min’ o kpambaliba nini daa tiɣ’ o ni yɛli shɛm maa.

english_verse: So the king said to them, “Who could possibly handle this better than Joseph? After all, the Spirit of God is with him.”
translation_verse: Ka Firawuna daa bɔh’ o kpambaliba maa, “Ti ni tooi nya ninvuɣ’ so ka o be kaman Naawuni Shia ni be do’ so ni ŋɔ?”

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “God is the one who has shown you these things. No one else is as wise as you are or knows as much as you do.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Firawuna daa yɛli Yisifu, “Naawuni ni wuh’ a dimbɔŋɔ zaa maa zuɣu, so kani m-mali tɛhi’ wɔɣila ni yɛm kaman nyini.

english_verse: I'm putting you in charge of my palace, and everybody will have to obey you. No one will be over you except me.
translation_verse: Nyini n-yɛn su n yili ŋɔ fukumsi, ka a yi kul yɛli shɛlikam, n niriba zaa ni niŋ li; kulla n nam ʒiishee ŋɔ ka n yɛn zaŋ gar’ a.”

english_verse: Then the king took off his royal ring and put it on Joseph's finger. He gave him fine clothes to wear and placed a gold chain around his neck.
translation_verse: Ka ŋun’ Firawuna daa pirig’ o nuu ni nintu’ shɛli o ni mali dalindi binyara n-zaŋ li piri Yisifu, ka zaŋ bimpiɛl’ viɛlli kparibu yɛl’ o, ka zaŋ salima dolibi yɛl’ o;

english_verse: He also let him ride in the chariot next to his own, and people shouted, “Make way for Joseph!” So Joseph was governor of Egypt.
translation_verse: ka chɛ ka o kpe n-ʒin’ o chɛchɛbuŋ’ din pah’ ayi puuni, ka chɛ ka bɛn be o tooni kuhiri yɛra, “Damdimiy’ o tiŋa!” Lala ka o daa niŋ zaŋ Yisifu leei Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ maa zaa zuɣulana.

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “Although I'm king, no one in Egypt is to do anything without your permission.”
translation_verse: Ka din pahi nyɛla, Firawuna daa lan yɛli Yisifu, “Mani n-nyɛ Firawuna, so ku tooi kpuɣ’ o nuu zuɣusaa bee n-vuug’ o napɔŋ Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ zaa ni, ka pa ni nyini m-bah’ o noli.”

english_verse: He gave Joseph the Egyptian name Zaphenath Paneah. And he let him marry Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, a priest in the city of Heliopolis. Joseph traveled all over Egypt.
translation_verse: Ka Firawuna daa boli Yisifu yuli Zafɛnatipania, ka zaŋ Pɔtifɛra ŋun daa nyɛ Hɛliopolis tindan’ la bipuɣiŋga Asɛnat n-ti Yisifu ni o niŋ o paɣa. Ka Yisifu daa yiri chani gindi Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ maa.

english_verse: Joseph collected and stored up the extra grain in the cities of Egypt near the fields where it was harvested.
translation_verse: Ka Yisifu daa laɣim yuma ayopɔin maa bindira zaa din daa niŋ pam Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ni maa n-sɔŋ fɔntinsi ni, ka laɣim fɔntiŋ’ kam ni puri ni bindira n-sɔŋ lala tinsi maa ni.

english_verse: In fact, there was so much grain that they stopped keeping record, because it was like counting the grains of sand along the beach.
translation_verse: Yisifu daa laɣim bindira maa sɔŋ ka di galisim ti ŋmanila teeku ni bihigu hal ka o ti bi lan niŋdi di laasabu, dama nir’ daa naan ku tooi lan niŋ di laasabu.

english_verse: Their first son was named Manasseh, which means, “God has let me forget all my troubles and my family back home.”
translation_verse: Yisifu daa bol’ o bidib’ kpɛm’ yul’ la Manaasa dama o daa yɛlimi, “Naawuni chɛ ka n tam n wahala la zaa mini n dɔɣiriba yɛla.”

english_verse: His second son was named Ephraim, which means “God has made me a success in the land where I suffered.”
translation_verse: Ka o daa boli bidib’ so ŋun pah’ ayi mi yuli Ifriim, ka yɛli, “Naawuni ti ma nama n ni di wahala tiŋgbɔn shɛl’ ni ŋɔ.”

english_verse: Egypt's seven years of plenty came to an end,
translation_verse: Ka yuma ayopɔin shɛŋa puuni bindira ni daa niŋ pam Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ni maa daa ti gari,

english_verse: and the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. There was not enough food in other countries, but all over Egypt there was plenty.
translation_verse: ka yuma ayopɔin shɛŋa puuni kum ni daa yɛn lu la piligi kaman Yisifu ni daa pun yɛli shɛm la. Kum maa daa lula luɣilikam zaa tiŋgbɔna ni; amaa ka bindira daa be Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ din’ zaa ni.

english_verse: When the famine finally struck Egypt, the people asked the king for food, but he said, “Go to Joseph and do what he tells you to do.”
translation_verse: Kum maa ni daa ti mii Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ni zaa saha shɛli, ka niriba daa kuhiri niŋdi Firawuna ni o tim’ ba bindira. Ka Firawuna daa yɛli Ijiptinim’ zaa, “Chamiya Yisifu sani, o yi ti yɛli ya ni yi niŋm’ shɛli, yin’ niŋmiya li.”

english_verse: People from all over the world came to Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was so severe in their countries.
translation_verse: Ka din pahi nyɛla dunia zaa daa kala Ijipti na Yisifu sani ni bɛ ti da kawana, dama kum maa daa miila dunia ŋɔ luɣilikam zaa.

english_verse: When Jacob found out there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you just sitting here, staring at one another?
translation_verse: Yaakubu ni daa ti wum ni kawana be Ijipti, ka o bɔh’ o bihi, “Bɔzuɣu ka yi lihiri taba?”

english_verse: I have heard there is grain in Egypt. Go down and buy some, so we won't starve to death.”
translation_verse: O daa yɛli ba, “N wumya ni kawana be Ijipti, chamiya nimaani nti da li ti ti na, ka ti tiligi ka ku kpi.”

english_verse: Ten of Joseph's brothers went to Egypt to buy grain.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yisifu biɛyanim’ ninvuɣ’ pia la daa chaŋ Ijipti ni bɛ ti da kawana.

english_verse: But Jacob did not send Joseph's younger brother Benjamin with them; he was afraid that something might happen to him.
translation_verse: Amaa Yaakubu daa bi chɛ ka Bɛnjamin ŋun nyɛ Yisifu tizo la dol’ o biɛyanim’ maa chaŋ, dama o daa zɔrimi ni binshɛli ti niŋ o.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons joined others from Canaan who were going to Egypt because of the terrible famine.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Yaakubu bihi mini ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ daa kana ni bɛ ti da bindira maa, dama kum maa daa lula Keenan tiŋgbɔŋ ni gba.

english_verse: Since Joseph was governor of Egypt and in charge of selling grain, his brothers came to him and bowed with their faces to the ground.
translation_verse: Yisifu ni daa nyɛ Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ maa gomna la zuɣu, ŋuna n-daa nyɛ ŋun kɔhiri bindira maa tiŋgbɔŋ maa nim’ zaa zuɣu. Ka Yisifu biɛyanim’ maa daa kana ti damd’ o tooni n-zaŋ bɛ zuɣuri silim tiŋa.

english_verse: Joseph remembered what he had dreamed about them and said, “You're spies! You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Ka Yisifu daa teei o ni daa zahim zahin’ shɛŋa zaŋ chaŋ bɛ polo la, ka yɛli ba, “Yi nyɛla puɣisiriba, yi kamina ni yi ti nya ti tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ gbariginsim ni nyɛ shɛm.”

english_verse: “No sir,” they replied. “We're your servants, and we have only come to buy grain.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ yɛl’ o, “Aai, ti dana, a daba kala bindira dabu na.

english_verse: We're honest men, and we come from the same family—we're not spies.”
translation_verse: Tinim’ a daba ŋɔ zaa nyɛla do’ yino bihi, ti nyɛla ninvuɣ’ maŋa, ti pala puɣisiriba.”

english_verse: “That isn't so!” Joseph insisted. “You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Ka Yisifu yɛli ba, “Aai, yi kana ni yi ti nyala ti tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ gbariginsim ni nyɛ shɛm.”

english_verse: But they explained, “Sir, we come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and one of our brothers is dead.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ yɛl’ o, “Tinim’ a daba ŋɔ nyɛla do’ yino ŋun be Keenan tiŋgbɔŋ ni bihi pinaayi, ŋun nyɛ ti zaa ha biasani be ti ba maa sani ka yino ŋun’ kani.”

english_verse: and I'm going to find out the truth. I swear by the life of the king that you won't leave this place until your youngest brother comes here.
translation_verse: Ti ni yɛn niŋ shɛm buɣisi ya m-bɔŋɔ: m po Firawuna ni yi ku kuli ka pa ni yi tizo ŋun nyɛ yi zaa biasani maa gba kala kpe na.

english_verse: Choose one of you to go after your brother, while the rest of you stay here in jail. That will show whether you are telling the truth. But if you are lying, I swear by the life of the king that you are spies!
translation_verse: Chɛliya ka yi ni yino kuli ti zaŋ yi tizo maa na, ka yinim’ bɛn kpalim be sarika ni, ka ti buɣisi yi ni yɛli shɛm maa nya yɛlimaŋli ka yi yɛli maa, di yi pa lala, m po Firawuna ni yi shiri nyɛla puɣisiriba.

english_verse: Joseph kept them all under guard for three days,
translation_verse: Ka o daa shiri zaŋ bɛ zaa niŋ sarika ni daba ata.

english_verse: before saying to them: Since I respect God, I'll give you a chance to save your lives.
translation_verse: Daba ata maa dali, ka Yisifu daa yɛli ba, “Niŋmiya dimbɔŋɔ ka tiligi, dama n zɔri Naawuni.

english_verse: If you are honest men, one of you must stay here in jail, and the rest of you can take the grain back to your starving families.
translation_verse: Yi yi shiri nyɛla yɛlimaŋyɛriba, yin’ chɛliya ka yi mabi’ yino kpalim be sarika ŋɔ ni, ka chɛ ka yi bɛn kpalim ʒi bindira kuli ti ti kum ni mali yi yiŋnim’ shɛb’ maa,

english_verse: But you must bring your youngest brother to me. Then I'll know that you are telling the truth, and you won't be put to death. Joseph's brothers agreed
translation_verse: ka zaŋ yi tizo maa na ka n ti nya o, ka di wuhi ni yi yɛligu maa nyɛla yɛlimaŋli, ka yi tiligi.” Ka bɛ daa shiri niŋ lala.

english_verse: and said to one another, “We're being punished because of Joseph. We saw the trouble he was in, but we refused to help him when he begged us. That's why these terrible things are happening.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka bɛ daa yɛri taba, “Yɛlimaŋli, ti ni daa niŋ ti mabia la shɛm la samli n-yɔri ti ŋɔ, o ni daa balim ti ka ti daa nya o suhusaɣiŋgu ni nyɛ shɛm, amaa ka zaɣisi wumbu la; dinzuɣu ka suhusaɣiŋgu ŋɔ ti paai ti gba maa.”

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Didn't I tell you not to harm the boy? But you wouldn't listen, and now we have to pay the price for killing him.”
translation_verse: Ka Rubin daa bɔhi ba, “N daa bi yɛli ya ni yi di niŋ bia maa shɛli? Amaa ka yi daa zaɣisi wumbu. Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ, o kubu maa biɛri m-bɔhiri ti maa.”

english_verse: They did not know that Joseph could understand them, since he was speaking through an interpreter.
translation_verse: Bɛ daa bi mi ni Yisifu wum bɛ ni yɛri shɛm maa, dama so n-daa deeri yɛtɔɣa maa lɛbigiri tiri ba.

english_verse: Joseph turned away from them and cried, but soon he turned back and spoke to them again. Then he had Simeon tied up and taken away while they watched. Joseph's Brothers Return to Canaan
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yisifu daa ŋmaligi bɛ sani n-chaŋ ti kum; ka lan lab’ bɛ sanna nti tɔɣisi ba yɛtɔɣa. Ka o daa gbaai Simiɔn n-chɛ ka bɛ lo o mihi bɛ zaa ninni. Yisifu biɛyanim’ lab’ Keenan

english_verse: Joseph gave orders for his brothers' grain sacks to be filled with grain and for their money to be put in their sacks. He also gave orders for them to be given food for their journey home. After this was done,
translation_verse: Ka Yisifu daa bahi noli ni bɛ niŋm’ kawana pali bɛ kpalansi ka labisi bɛ zaa yinoyino liɣiri niŋ bɛ kpalansi maa ni, ka bo bɛ sol’ ni bindirigu ti ba. Ka bɛ daa shiri niŋ lala ti ba.

english_verse: they each loaded the grain on their donkeys and left.
translation_verse: Di saha ka bɛ daa zaŋ bɛ kawana ʒili bɛ bunsi lu soli.

english_verse: When they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to get some grain for his donkey, and at once he saw his moneybag.
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa ti paai luɣ’ shɛli bɛ ni yɛn gbe, ka bɛ ni yino lɔrig’ o kpalaŋa ni o niŋ bindirigu ti o buŋa ka nya ka liɣiri be o kpalaŋ’ maa nol’ ni;

english_verse: “Here's my money!” he told his brothers. “Right here in my sack.” They were trembling with fear as they stared at one another and asked themselves, “What has God done to us?”
translation_verse: ka o yɛl’ o mabihi maa, “Bɛ zaŋla n liɣiri labisi niŋ ma, dina m-be n kpalaŋ’ ni ŋɔ.” Ka bɛ suhuri daa fuŋ di zuɣu, ka bɛ ni sɔhiri ka bɛ bɔhiri taba, “Ka tuun’ bɔ ka Naawuni lee tum ti ŋɔ?”

english_verse: When they returned to the land of Canaan, they told their father Jacob everything that had happened to them:
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa ti paai bɛ ba Yaakubu sani Keenan tiŋgbɔŋ ni, bɛ daa yɛl’ o la dinkam zaa niŋ ba, ka lan yɛl’ o,

english_verse: But we told him, “We're honest men, not spies.
translation_verse: Amaa ka ti daa yɛl’ o, ‘Ti pala puɣisiriba, ti nyɛla yɛlimaŋyɛriba.

english_verse: We come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and the other is dead.”
translation_verse: Ti nyɛla do’ yino bidibisi pinaayi; ka ti ni yino daa kani, ka ŋun nyɛ ti zaa biasani be ti ba maa sani Keenan tiŋgbɔŋ ni.’

english_verse: Then the governor of Egypt told us, “I'll find out if you really are honest. Leave one of your brothers here with me, while you take the grain to your starving families.
translation_verse: Di saha ka do’ so ŋun nyɛ tiŋgbɔŋ maa gomna maa yɛl’ ti, ‘Yi ni yɛn niŋ shɛm chɛ ka m baŋ ni yi nyɛla yɛlimaŋyɛriba m-bɔŋɔ: chɛliya yi ni yino n sani, ka zaŋ kawana kuli ti ti yi yiŋnim’ shɛb’ kum ni muɣisi maa;

english_verse: But bring your youngest brother to me, so I can be certain that you are honest men and not spies. After that, I'll let your other brother go free, and you can stay here and trade.”

english_verse: When the brothers started emptying their sacks of grain, they found their moneybags in them. They were frightened, and so was their father Jacob,
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa kpaai bɛ kawana, bɛ zaa liɣiri daa lɔnlomi be bɛ kpalansi ni, bɛ mini bɛ ba ni daa nya liɣiri maa, ka di gari ba.

translation_verse: Ka bɛ ba Yaakubu yɛli ba, “Yi chɛ ka n kɔŋ m bihi. Yisifu lan kani, ka Simiɔn gba kani, ka yi yɛn zaŋ Bɛnjamin mi chaŋ pumpɔŋɔ, n zuɣu ka yɛla ŋɔ zaa ʒini.”

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Father, if I don't bring Benjamin back, you can kill both of my sons. Trust me with him, and I'll bring him back.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Rubin daa yɛl’ o ba, “N yi bi ʒi Bɛnjamin kuna, nyin’ kum’ m bidibis’ ayi ŋɔ, chɛl’ o niŋ n nuu ni, n ni ʒi o kuna ti ti a.”

english_verse: But Jacob said, “I won't let my son Benjamin go down to Egypt with the rest of you. His brother is already dead, and he is the only son I have left. I am an old man, and if anything happens to him on the way, I'll die from sorrow, and all of you will be to blame.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka o yɛli, “M bia maa ku doli ya chaŋ, dama o biɛli kpiya, ka o kɔŋko n-kpalim. Shɛli yi niŋ o yi ni yɛn chaŋ chandi shɛli ŋɔ ni, yi ni chɛ ka n dɔni kabiri puuni ni n kɔb’ piɛla ŋɔ ni suhugarigu.”

english_verse: The famine in Canaan got worse,

english_verse: Jacob asked, “Why did you cause me so much trouble by telling the governor you had another brother?”

english_verse: They answered, “He asked a lot of questions about us and our family. He wanted to know if you were still alive and if we had any more brothers. All we could do was answer his questions. How could we know he would tell us to bring along our brother?”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ garigi yɛl’ o, “Doo maa n-daa bɔhi ti ti mini ti dɔɣiriba yɛla pam hal ti bɔhi ti, ‘Yi ba na be o nyɛvil’ ni? Yi mali tizo?’ Ka ti mi daa garig’ o bɔhigunim’ maa; ti daa lee yɛn niŋ wula baŋ ni o ni yɛl’ ti, ‘Zaŋmiya yi tizo maa na’? ”

english_verse: Then Judah said to his father, “Let Benjamin go with me, and we will leave at once, so that none of us will starve to death.

english_verse: Their father said: If Benjamin must go with you, take the governor a gift of some of the best things from our own country, such as perfume, honey, spices, pistachio nuts, and almonds.
translation_verse: Di saha ka bɛ ba Izraɛl daa yɛli ba, “Di yi nyɛ lala, yin’ niŋmiya ŋ-ŋɔ: zaŋmiya tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni tiwal’ viɛla n-niŋ yi kpalansi ni n-ʒi m-mali chaŋ ti ti doo maa pini; ka ʒi tisum shɛli bɛ ni zaŋdi maani tim la mini shiri biɛla ni tulaale ni suri ni kpakpa ni dɔbino.

english_verse: Also take along twice the amount of money for the grain, because there must have been some mistake when the money was put back in your sacks.

english_verse: The brothers took the gifts, twice the amount of money, and Benjamin. Then they hurried off to Egypt. When they stood in front of Joseph,

english_verse: When Joseph came home, they gave him the gifts they had brought, and they bowed down to him.

english_verse: After Joseph had asked how they were, he said, “What about your elderly father? Is he still alive?”

english_verse: They answered, “Your servant our father is still alive and well.” And again they bowed down to Joseph.

english_verse: When Joseph looked around and saw his brother Benjamin, he said, “This must be your youngest brother, the one you told me about. God bless you, my son.”
translation_verse: Ka Yisifu daa kpuɣ’ o zuɣu nya o tizo Bɛnjamin ŋun nyɛ o ma puuni bia la, ka bɔhi ba, “Yi ni daa yɛli ma yi tizɔbil’ so yɛla la m-bɔŋɔ?” Di saha ka o daa yɛli, “M bia, Naawuni niŋm’ alibarika niŋ a ni!’ ”

english_verse: “Good!” the man replied, “I'll do what you have said. But only the one who has the cup will become my slave. The rest of you can go free.”

translation_verse: “Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ, n yi lab’ m ba ŋun nyɛ a dabili maa sani, ka bia maa bi dol’ ti labi, dindina o nyɛvili ni tab’ bia maa nyɛvil’ la zuɣu,

translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ, n suhir’ a, chɛ ka mani a dabili ŋɔ kpalim leegi n dan’ dabili ka chɛ bia maa, ka a chɛ ka o dol’ o biɛyanim’ maa kuli.

english_verse: How can I face my father if Benjamin isn't with me? I couldn't bear to see my father in such sorrow.
translation_verse: Dama bia maa yi bi doli ma kuli, wula ka n lee yɛn niŋ n-tooi labi m ba sani? N zɔri ni n nini nya zaɣ’ biɛ’ shɛli din yɛn paai m ba maa.”

english_verse: Since Joseph could no longer control his feelings in front of his servants, he sent them out of the room. When he was alone with his brothers, he told them, “I am Joseph.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yisifu daa kɔŋ omaŋ’ gbaabu ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn daa ʒe o sani maa zaa tooni, ka kuhi yɛli, “Sokam yiɣisim’ n sani yi.” Dinzuɣu so daa ka Yisifu sani saha shɛl’ o ni daa yɛl’ o biɛyanim’ maa o ni nyɛ so.

english_verse: Then he cried so loudly that the Egyptians heard him and told about it in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Ka o daa kuhi pam ka Ijiptinim’ ti wum o kuhigu maa, hal ka Firawuna yiŋnim’ gba ti wum o kuhigu maa.

english_verse: Joseph asked his brothers if his father was still alive, but they were too frightened to answer.
translation_verse: Ka Yisifu daa yɛl’ o biɛyanim’ maa, “Man’ Yisifu m-bala. M ba na be o nyɛvil’ ni?” Amaa ka di daa gar’ o biɛyanim’ maa pam, ka bɛ kɔŋ o garigibu.

english_verse: Joseph told them to come closer to him, and when they did, he said: Yes, I am your brother Joseph, the one you sold into Egypt.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yisifu daa yɛl’ o biɛyanim’ maa, “Saɣisimiya miri ma na.” Ka bɛ daa saɣisi mir’ o. Ka o yɛli ba, “Mani yi tizo Yisifu so yi ni daa zaŋ kɔhi Ijipti ŋɔ la m-bala.

english_verse: Don't worry or blame yourselves for what you did. God is the one who sent me ahead of you to save lives.
translation_verse: Ka pumpɔŋɔ di chɛliya ka yi suhuri saɣim bee n-je suli niŋ taba, yi ni daa zaŋ ma kɔhi kpe ŋɔ maa zuɣu, dama Naawuni n-daa chɛ ka n daŋ yi tooni na ni n ti fa niriba nyɛviya bahi.

english_verse: There has already been a famine for two years, and for five more years no one will plow fields or harvest grain.
translation_verse: Yuma ayi ka kum ŋɔ na niŋ tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni maa, ka di na kpalim yuma anu, ka so ku ko bee n-kpuɣi puu atam.

english_verse: But God sent me on ahead of you to keep your families alive and to save you in this wonderful way.
translation_verse: Naawuni n-daa chɛ ka n daŋ yi tooni na ni n ti fa yi bɛn na kpalim, ka tiligi yi niriba pam nyɛviya tin ya.

english_verse: After all, you weren't really the ones who sent me here—it was God. He made me the highest official in the king's court and placed me over all Egypt.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pa yinima n-daa tahi ma kpe na, amaa Naawuni n-daa tahi ma na nti zaŋ ma leei Firawuna ba ni ŋun su o yiŋnim’ zaa fukumsi, ka lan zaŋ ma leei Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ zaa zuɣulana.

english_verse: Now hurry back and tell my father that his son Joseph says, “God has made me ruler of Egypt. Come here as quickly as you can.
translation_verse: “Niŋmiya yomyom kuli m ba sani ti yɛl’ o, “A bia Yisifu ni yɛli shɛm m-bɔŋɔ: Naawuni zaŋ ma leei Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ zaa zuɣulana, dinzuɣu niŋmi yomyom yiɣisi kuli n sanna

english_verse: You will live near me in the region of Goshen with your children and grandchildren, as well as with your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: nti ʒini Goshɛn tiŋgban’ ni miri ma. Zaŋm’ a bihi min’ a yaansi ni a biŋkɔbbaligu ni a niɣi ni a ni mali binshɛɣukam zaa na;

english_verse: I will take care of you there during the next five years of famine. But if you don't come, you and your family and your animals will starve to death.”
translation_verse: ka n ti tir’ a bindira nimaani, dama kum maa yuma na kpalim yuma anu, di yi pa lala kum maa ni ti miig’ a min’ a yiŋnim’ ni a ni mali binshɛɣukam zaa.

english_verse: All of you, including my brother Benjamin, can tell by what I have said that I really am Joseph.
translation_verse: “Ka pumpɔŋɔ yimaŋmaŋ’ mini n tizo Bɛnjamin zaa nini nyaya ni mmaŋmaŋa n-yaagi n noli yɛli ya yɛtɔɣa ŋɔ.

english_verse: Tell my father about my great power here in Egypt and about everything you have seen. Hurry and bring him here.
translation_verse: Yɛlimiya m ba n ni nya jilima shɛli zaa Ijipti ŋɔ mini yimaŋmaŋ’ nini ni nya shɛlikam zaa. Niŋmiya yomyom chaŋ ti zaŋ m ba kuli kpe na.”

english_verse: Joseph was still crying as he kissed each of his other brothers. After this, they started talking with Joseph.
translation_verse: Ka Yisifu daa mɔɣis’ o biɛyanim’ maa zaa kparima ka kum pam, di nyaaŋa ka o biɛyanim’ maa daa naanyi tɔɣis’ o yɛtɔɣa.

english_verse: When it was told in the palace that Joseph's brothers had come, the king and his officials were happy.
translation_verse: Lahibali ni daa ti nti to Firawuna yiŋa ni Yisifu biɛyanima n-kana, di daa niŋ Firawuna min’ o kpambaliba nyaɣisim pam.

english_verse: So the king said to Joseph: Tell your brothers to load their donkeys and return to Canaan.
translation_verse: Ka Firawuna daa yɛli Yisifu, “Yɛlim’ a biɛyanim’ maa ni bɛ ʒilim’ bɛ bunsi ʒiya n-lab’ Keenan tiŋgbɔŋ ni

english_verse: Tell them to bring their father and their families here. I will give them the best land in Egypt, and they can eat and enjoy everything that grows there.
translation_verse: nti zaŋ yi ba mini yi malibu kuli n sanna ka n ti tin ya tiŋgban’ viɛlli Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni, ka yi ti diri tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni bindira yi yubu.

english_verse: Also tell your brothers to take some wagons from Egypt for their wives and children to ride in. And be sure they bring their father.
translation_verse: ‘Yɛlim’ ba yaha ni bɛ zaŋm’ tɔrokɔnim’ Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni m-mali kuli ti zaŋ bɛ paɣiba mini bɛ bibihi ni yi ba n-kuli kpe na.

english_verse: They can leave their possessions behind, because they will be given the best of everything in Egypt.
translation_verse: Bɛ di chɛ ka bɛ suhuri zɔhiri zaŋ chaŋ bɛ ni mali shɛlikam ʒibu na polo, dama Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ luɣ’ viɛlli shee ka bɛ yɛn ʒini.’ ”

english_verse: Jacob's sons agreed to do what the king had said. And Joseph gave them wagons and food for their trip home, just as the king had ordered.
translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu bihi maa daa niŋ lala, ka Yisifu daa zaŋ tɔrokɔnim’ maa ti ba kaman Firawuna ni daa zali shɛm, ka bo bɛ sol’ ni bindira ti ba.

english_verse: Joseph gave some new clothes to each of his brothers, but to Benjamin he gave five new outfits and
translation_verse: Ka Yisifu daa ti bɛ zaa yinoyino chuɣu puhibu binyɛra, amaa ka daa bo anzinfa laɣibaligu pihita mini chuɣu puhibu binyɛra ata ti Bɛnjamin.

english_verse: To his father he sent ten donkeys loaded with the best things in Egypt, and ten other donkeys loaded with grain and bread and other food for the return trip.
translation_verse: Ka o daa bo Ijipti bin suma n-ʒili bunsi pia ni bɛ zaŋ ti ti o ba, ka lan chɛ ka bɛ su kawana mini bɔrɔbɔro ni di ti nyɛ o ba sol’ ni bindira n-ʒili bunnyama pia pahi.

english_verse: Then he sent his brothers off and told them, “Don't argue on the way home!”
translation_verse: Di saha ka o daa chɛbis’ o biɛyanim’ maa. Bɛ ni daa yiɣisi ni bɛ chaŋ, ka Yisifu yɛli ba, “Miriya ka yi ŋme tab’ naŋgbankpeeni sol’ ni.”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers left Egypt, and when they arrived in Canaan,
translation_verse: Di saha ka bɛ daa yi Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni n-kuli Keenan tiŋgbɔŋ ni bɛ ba Yaakubu sani

english_verse: they told their father that Joseph was still alive and was the ruler of Egypt. But their father was so surprised that he could not believe them.
translation_verse: nti yɛl’ o, “Yisifu na be o nyɛvil’ ni, ka nyɛla Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ zaa zuɣulana.” Ka Yaakubu yɛma daa ŋma, dama o daa bi niŋ ba yɛda.

english_verse: Then they told him everything Joseph had said. When he saw the wagons Joseph had sent, he felt much better
translation_verse: Amaa bɛ ni daa zaŋ yɛtɔɣ’ shɛŋa zaa Yisifu ni tɔɣisi ba n-yɛl’ o, ka o nya tɔroko’ shɛŋa Yisifu ni daa zaŋ ti na ni bɛ ti kpuɣ’ o na la, ka o suhu daa kpaŋ;

english_verse: and said, “Now I can believe you! My son Joseph must really be alive, and I will get to see him before I die.”
translation_verse: ka Izraɛl daa yɛli, “Di saɣiya! M bia Yisifu na shiri be o nyɛvil’ ni. N ni chaŋ ti nya o pɔi ka naanyi kpi.”

english_verse: Jacob packed up everything he owned and left for Egypt. On the way he stopped near the town of Beersheba and offered sacrifices to the God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Yaakubu daa zaŋ o ni mali binshɛɣukam zaa n-yiɣisi chaŋ Bɛrishiiba nti mali sara o ba Yisahaku Naawuni ŋɔ sani.

english_verse: That night, God spoke to him in a dream and said, “Jacob! Jacob!” “Here I am,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa tɔɣisi Yaakubu yɛtɔɣa ʒii puuni yuŋ. O daa bol’ o mi, “Yaakubu, Yaakubu.” Ka o saɣi ka yɛli, “N nyɛ ma.”

english_verse: God said, “I am God, the same God your father worshiped. Don't be afraid to go to Egypt. I will give you so many descendants that one day they will become a nation.
translation_verse: Di saha ka o daa yɛl’ o, “Mani n-nyɛ Naawuni ŋun nyɛ a ba Naawuni. Di zɔri dabiɛm ni a kuli Ijipti, dama n ni chɛ ka a daŋ niriba ti leei zuliya bɛn galisi pam.

english_verse: I will go with you to Egypt, and later I will bring your descendants back here. Your son Joseph will be at your side when you die.”
translation_verse: M min’ a ni chaŋ Ijipti, ka n ti lan zaŋ a labisi kpe na yaha; ka Yisifu maŋmaŋ’ nuu ni ti daag’ a nina pɔbi.”

english_verse: When Jacob went to Egypt, his children who were born in northern Syria also went along with their families. Jacob and his wife Leah had a total of
translation_verse: Liya ni daa dɔɣi bidib’ shɛb’ min’ o bipuɣiŋga Daina ti Yaakubu Mɛsopoteemia la m-bala. O mini Liya zuliya bɛn nyɛ bidibisi mini bipuɣinsi zaa kalinli daa nyɛla ninvuɣ’ pihitanaata.

english_verse: The king will call you in and ask what you do for a living.
translation_verse: Firawuna yi boli ya ti bɔhi ya, ‘Tuun’ bɔ ka yi lee tumda?’

english_verse: Jacob and Zilpah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Leah, had a total of
translation_verse: bɛna n-nyɛ Zilipa so Leeban ni daa zaŋ ti o bipuɣiŋga Liya la bidib’ shɛb’ o ni daa dɔɣi ti Yaakubu, ka bɛ zaa kalinli daa nyɛ ninvuɣ’ pinaayɔbu.

english_verse: Jacob and Bilhah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Rachel, had seven children and grandchildren. Their son Dan took his son Hushim. Their son Naphtali took his sons Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
translation_verse: Biliha ŋun daa nyɛ Leeban ni daa zaŋ so ti o bipuɣiŋga Reechɛl la ni daa dɔɣi bidib’ shɛb’ ti Yaakubu m-bala; ka bɛ zaa kalinli daa nyɛla niriba ayopɔin.

english_verse: Sixty-six members of Jacob's family went to Egypt with him, not counting his daughters-in-law.
translation_verse: Izraɛl bihi min’ o yaansi bɛn daa dol’ o kuli Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ni kalinli daa nyɛla ninvuɣ’ pihiyɔbunaayɔbu. O bidibisi paɣiba daa ka bɛ kalinli maa ni.

english_verse: Jacob had sent his son Judah ahead of him to ask Joseph to meet them in Goshen.
translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu daa tim Juda ni o daŋmi tooni ti yɛli Yisifu ka o wuhi ba soli din kuni Goshɛn; ka bɛ daa mali hal ti paai Goshɛn tiŋgbɔŋ ni.

english_verse: So Joseph got in his chariot and went to meet his father. When they met, Joseph hugged his father around the neck and cried for a long time.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yisifu daa mali shili n-kpe o chɛchɛbuŋ’ ni chaŋ Goshɛn ni o ti nya o ba Izraɛl. Bɛ ni daa ti nya taba, ka Yisifu chaŋ o sani nti zaŋ o nuhi m-bɔb’ gbaag’ o ba n-zaŋ o zuɣu pa o nyiŋgoli zuɣu n-kum yuui.

english_verse: Jacob said to Joseph, “Now that I have seen you and know you are still alive, I am ready to die.”
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛl daa yɛli Yisifu, “N yi kpi pumpɔŋɔ, m paɣiya, n ni nya a ni n nini ka baŋ ni a na be a nyɛvil’ ni maa zuɣu.”

english_verse: Then Joseph said to his brothers and to everyone who had come with them: I must go and tell the king that you have arrived from Canaan.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yisifu daa yɛl’ o biɛyanim’ maa min’ o ba malibu maa zaa, “N ni chaŋ ti yɛli Firawuna, ‘M ba min’ o malibu ni m biɛyanim’ bɛn be Keenan tiŋgbɔŋ ni la kuli n sanna.

english_verse: I will tell him that you are shepherds and that you have brought your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Bɛ nyɛla bɛn guli piɛri mini niɣi, ka ʒi bɛ piɛri mini bɛ niɣi maa ni bɛ ni mali shɛlikam zaa na.’

english_verse: When he does, be sure to say, “We are shepherds. Our families have always raised sheep.” If you tell him this, he will let you settle in the region of Goshen. Joseph wanted them to say this to the king, because the Egyptians did not like to be around anyone who raised sheep.
translation_verse: yin’ yɛlimiy’ o, ‘Tinim’ a daba ŋɔ yaannim’ nyɛla biŋkɔbiguliba, ka ti gba nyɛ bɛn guli biŋkɔbiri ti bilim ni hal ni wayo,’ din ni chɛ ka o chɛ ka yi ʒini Goshɛn tiŋgban’ ni, dama Ijiptinim’ je piɛguliba yɛlli.”

english_verse: who asked them, “What do you do for a living?” “Sir, we are shepherds,” was their answer. “Our families have always raised sheep.
translation_verse: Ka Firawuna daa bɔhi Yisifu biɛyanim’ maa, “Tuun’ bɔ n-lee nyɛ yi tuma?” Ka bɛ yɛl’ o, “Tinim’ a daba ŋɔ mini ti yaannim’ nyɛla piɛguliba.”

english_verse: But in our country all the pastures are dried up, and our sheep have no grass to eat. So we, your servants, have come here. Please let us live in the region of Goshen.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa lan yɛli Firawuna, “Tinim’ a daba ŋɔ kamina ni ti ti ʒini tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni, dama kum maa miiya pam Keenan tiŋgbɔŋ ni, ka ti biŋkɔbiri bi nyari mɔri ŋubira; ka pumpɔŋɔ ti suhir’ a mi ni a chɛ ka ti ʒini Goshɛn tiŋgban’ ni”

english_verse: The king said to Joseph, “It's good that your father and brothers have arrived.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Firawuna daa yɛli Yisifu, “A ba min’ a biɛyanim’ kul’ a sanna.

english_verse: I will let them live anywhere they choose in the land of Egypt, but I suggest that they settle in Goshen, the best part of our land. I would also like for your finest shepherds to watch after my own sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Nyini n-su Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ fukumsi, zaŋm’ a ba min’ a biɛyanim’ maa ʒili luɣ’ viɛlli shee; chɛ ka bɛ ʒini Goshɛn tiŋgban’ ni. Ka a yi mi bɛ ni bɛn mi biŋkɔbiri gbibbu, nyin’ chɛ ka bɛ guli n niɣi.”

english_verse: Then Joseph brought his father Jacob and introduced him to the king. Jacob gave the king his blessing,
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Yisifu daa zaŋ o ba Yaakubu chaŋ Firawuna sani, ka Yaakubu daa suhi alibarika niŋ Firawuna ni.

english_verse: and the king asked him, “How old are you?”
translation_verse: Ka Firawuna daa bɔhi Yaakubu, “A yuma ala?”

english_verse: Then Jacob gave the king his blessing once again and left.
translation_verse: Ka Yaakubu daa suhi alibarika niŋ Firawuna ni ka yiɣisi kuli.

english_verse: Joseph obeyed the king's orders and gave his father and brothers some of the best land in Egypt near the city of Rameses.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yisifu daa zaŋ o ba min’ o biɛyanim’ maa ʒili Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni, ka ŋmaai tiŋgban’ viɛlli Ramɛsis tiŋgban’ ni ti ba kaman Firawuna ni daa yɛl’ o shɛm.

english_verse: So Joseph sold them the grain that had been stored up, and he put the money in the king's treasury.
translation_verse: Ka Yisifu daa laɣisi bɛ ni daa kɔhi kawana laɣ’ shɛli Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ni mini Keenan tiŋgbɔŋ ni zaa n-zaŋ li tahi Firawuna yiŋa nti ti o.

english_verse: But when everyone had run out of money, the Egyptians came to Joseph and demanded, “Give us more grain! If you don't, we'll soon be dead, because our money's all gone.”
translation_verse: Ka Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ni nim’ mini Keenan tiŋgbɔŋ ni nim’ ni daa ti di bɛ liɣiri zaa naai saha shɛli, ka Ijiptinim’ zaa daa ka Yisifu sanna ti yɛl’ o, “Tim’ ti bindirigu, bɔzuɣu ka a yɛn lihiri ti ka ti kpi? Dama ti liɣiri zaa naaya.”

english_verse: “If you don't have any money,” Joseph answered, “give me your animals, and I'll let you have some grain.”
translation_verse: Ka Yisifu daa garigi yɛli ba, “Yi liɣiri yi naai, yin’ zaŋmiya yi biŋkɔbiri na ti taɣi bindirigu.”

english_verse: Then the people came to him and said: Sir, there's no way we can hide the truth from you. We are broke, and we don't have any more animals. We have nothing left except ourselves and our land.
translation_verse: Yuuni maa ni daa ti gari, ka bɛ daa lan lab’ o sanna yuuni din paya ni ti yɛl’ o, “N dana, ti ku sɔɣ’ a, ti di ti liɣiri zaa; ka ti niɣi zaa nyɛla nyin’ n dan’ dini; ti lan ka binshɛɣu nyin’ n dan’ tooni m-pahila ti niŋgbuna ŋɔ mini ti puri.

english_verse: Don't let us starve and our land be ruined. If you'll give us grain to eat and seed to plant, we'll sell ourselves and our land to the king. We'll become his slaves.
translation_verse: Ka bɔzuɣu ka a ni lihiri ti ka ti mini ti puri maa zaa kpi? Zaŋm’ bindirigu taɣi ti mini ti puri maa, ka ti mini ti puri maa zaa leei Firawuna daba; ka ti ti bimbira din ni chɛ ka ti gali ka ku kpi, ka ti puri maa gba ku kpalim doya yoli.”

english_verse: The famine became so severe that Joseph finally bought every piece of land in Egypt for the king
translation_verse: Ka Yisifu daa da Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ maa puri zaa n-ti Firawuna; dama Ijiptinim’ zaa daa zaŋla bɛ puri kɔhi, kum maa ni daa mii ba pam maa zuɣu. Ka puri maa daa leei Firawuna dini.

english_verse: and made everyone the king's slaves,
translation_verse: Ka Yisifu daa chɛ ka Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ zaa niriba leei daba.

english_verse: except the priests. The king gave the priests a regular food allowance, so they did not have to sell their land.
translation_verse: Maligumaaniba kɔŋko puri ka Yisifu daa bi da. Dama Firawuna daa tirila maligumaaniba maa laɣidira, dina ka bɛ daa mali dira, dinzuɣu ka bɛn’ daa bi kɔhi bɛ puri maa.

english_verse: Then Joseph said to the people, “You and your land now belong to the king. I'm giving you seed to plant,
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yisifu daa yɛli niriba maa, “Nyamiya, n da yi mini yi puri n-ti Firawuna zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ. Pumpɔŋɔ deemiya bimbira ŋɔ zali nti biri.

english_verse: but one fifth of your crops must go to the king. You can keep the rest as seed or as food for your families.”
translation_verse: Ka yi yi ti kpuɣi puri maa atam, yin’ pum’ li sɔŋ ʒiibunu n-vaai di yim zuɣu ti Firawuna, ka yi mi zaŋ di ʒiibunahi la ka yi mini yi yiŋnim’ ni yi bihi di, ka chɛ di shɛli zali nti biri.”

english_verse: “Sir, you have saved our lives!” they answered. “We are glad to be slaves of the king.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yɛl’ o, “N dana, a tiligi ti nyɛviya; ka di yi niŋ a nyaɣisim, ti ni leei Firawuna daba.”

english_verse: Then Joseph made a law that one fifth of the harvest would always belong to the king. Only the priests did not lose their land. Jacob Becomes an Old Man
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Yisifu daa zali zaligu zaŋ chaŋ Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ puri polo ni bɛ yi ti kpuɣi puri atam, bɛn’ zaŋm’ di pirigibu ʒiibunu puuni yim zuɣu ti Firawuna. Ka lala n-na kul nyɛ li hal ni zuŋɔ. Kulla maligumaaniba kɔŋko puri n-daa bi leei Firawuna ni su shɛli. Yaakubu ni bɔri binshɛli ka di nyɛ din bahindi nyaaŋa

english_verse: The people of Israel made their home in the land of Goshen, where they became prosperous and had large families.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa be Ijipti Goshɛn tiŋgban’ ni. Bɛ daa nya azichi pam nimaani, ka daa dɔɣi bihi ka bɛ zuliya maa nab’ pam.

english_verse: When Jacob knew he did not have long to live, he called in Joseph and said, “If you really love me, you must make a solemn promise not to bury me in Egypt.
translation_verse: Izraɛl ni daa ti miri kum, o daa bolila o bia Yisifu ti yɛl’ o, “A yi ni niŋ n ni bɔri shɛm ŋɔ, nyin’ zaŋm’ a nuu tim n gbalipini lɔŋni ka lo alikauli ni a ni tum ma ʒiɛyimtali tuma ni yɛlimaŋli. Di sɔɣi ma Ijipti ŋɔ,

english_verse: Instead, bury me in the place where my ancestors are buried.” “I will do what you have asked,” Joseph answered.
translation_verse: amaa zaŋm’ ma ti sɔŋla m banim’ dooshee. Ʒimiya ma yi Ijipti ŋɔ kuli nti sɔɣi ma bɛ sɔɣibu shee.” Ka Yisifu yɛl’ o, “N ni niŋ a ni yɛli shɛm maa.”

english_verse: “Will you give me your word?” Jacob asked. “Yes, I will,” Joseph promised. After this, Jacob bowed down and prayed at the head of his bed.
