translation_verse: Ka Amɔrinim’ maa tintariga daa kpuɣi Akirabim hal ni Sɛla n-yi nimaani zaŋ du ha.

english_verse: The Lord's angel went from Gilgal to Bochim and gave the Israelites this message from the Lord: I promised your ancestors that I would give this land to their families, and I brought your people here from Egypt. We made an agreement that I promised never to break,
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ malaika daa yi Giligal chaŋ Bokim ti yɛli Izraɛlnima, “Naawuni yɛliya, mani n-daa yihi ya Ijipti n-zaŋ ya na ti niŋ tiŋgbɔn shɛli n ni daa lo yi yaannima alikauli ni n ni zaŋ li ti ba la ni. N daa yɛliya ni n ku lɔrigi alikauli shɛli n ni lɔn ya maa.

english_verse: and you promised not to make any peace treaties with the other nations that live in the land. Besides that, you agreed to tear down the altars where they sacrifice to their idols. Why haven't you kept your promise?
translation_verse: Ka di bi simdi ni yi lo ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn be tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni alikauli, naɣ’ wurimmiyala bɛ buɣa bimbina la. Amaa ka yi zaɣisi n ni zali ya shɛm maa niŋbu. Tuun’ bɔ ka yi lee tum maa?

english_verse: And so, I'll stop helping you defeat your enemies. Instead, they will be there to trap you into worshiping their idols.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ n yɛri ya mi, n ku lan kari niriba maa tin ya. Bɛ ni leei yi dimnima; ka bɛ wuna leei zana gbahi ya.”

english_verse: and they offered sacrifices to the Lord. From then on, they called that place “Crying.” Israel Stops Worshiping the Lord
translation_verse: Dina n-chɛ ka bɛ daa boli nimaani yuli Bokim. Ka bɛ daa mali sara ti Yawɛ nimaani. Jɔshua kum

english_verse: Joshua had been faithful to the Lord. And after Joshua sent the Israelites to take the land they had been promised, they remained faithful to the Lord until Joshua died at the age of
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa sɔɣ’ o omaŋmaŋ’ tiŋgban’ ni Timnatisɛra din be Ifriim tiŋgban’ ni zoya tiŋgban’ ni zaŋ labi Gaash Zoli nuzaa polo la.

english_verse: After a while the people of Joshua's generation died, and the next generation did not know the Lord or any of the things he had done for Israel.
translation_verse: Ka di ʒiɛmani maa niriba zaa gba daa ti kpi. Ka ʒiɛman’ shɛli din paya niriba daa yiɣisina. Bɛn’ daa bi mi Yawɛ bee m-mi o ni daa tum tuun’ shɛŋa ti Izraɛlnim’ la yɛla. Izraɛlnim’ chɛ Naawuni jɛmbu

english_verse: with the Israelites that he let other nations raid Israel and steal their crops and other possessions. Enemies were everywhere, and the Lord always let them defeat Israel in battle. The Lord had warned Israel he would do this, and now the Israelites were miserable. The Lord Chooses Leaders for Israel
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa yi lo tɔbu ni bɛ chaŋ ti tuhi bɛ dimnim’ saha shɛlikam, Yawɛ paarila o nuu bɛ zuɣu bɛ daalahichi tumbu zuɣu kaman o ni daa pun kpahi bɛ zuɣu ni ka po n-yɛli ba shɛm la. Ka nandahima daa mali ba pam.

english_verse: From time to time, the Lord would choose special leaders known as judges. These judges would lead the Israelites into battle and defeat the enemies that made raids on them.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yawɛ daa pii zuɣulaannim’ ti ba; ka zuɣulaannim’ maa daa tiligi ba ŋmɛnditoya maa nuu ni.

english_verse: In years gone by, the Israelites had been faithful to the Lord, but now they were quick to be unfaithful and to refuse even to listen to these judges. The Israelites disobeyed the Lord, and instead of worshiping him, they worshiped other gods.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Izraɛlnim’ daa ti zaɣisi zuɣulaannim’ maa noli; ka kul jɛmdila wuna. Di daa bi yuui ka bɛ ŋmaligi ka chɛ bɛ yaannim’ bɛn daa doli Yawɛ zaligunim’ ni daa doli so’ shɛl’ la, ka shiri bi dol’ li.

english_verse: When enemies made life miserable for the Israelites, the Lord felt sorry for them. He would choose a judge and help that judge rescue Israel from its enemies. The Lord was kind to Israel as long as that judge lived.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yi pii zuɣulaannim’ ti Izraɛlnim’ saha shɛlikam, o bela o ni pii zuɣulan’ so kam sani, ka tiligiri ba bɛ dimnim’ nuu ni zuɣulan’ maa ʒiɛman’ ni. Yawɛ daa zɔri ba nambɔɣu, bɛ dimnim’ maa ni daa nahindi ba ka muɣisiri ba, ka bɛ ŋuhiri shɛm la zuɣu.

english_verse: But afterwards, the Israelites would become even more sinful than their ancestors had been. The Israelites were stubborn—they simply would not stop worshiping other gods or following their teachings. The Lord Lets Enemies Test Israel
translation_verse: Amaa zuɣulan’ maa daa yi ti kpi, bɛ lan ŋmaligirimi tumdi tuumbiɛ’ shɛŋa din bie n-gari bɛ yaannim’ dini. Bɛ daa kul jɛmdila wuna ka damdir’ li tiŋa. Bɛ daa bi saɣi chɛ bɛ tuumbiɛri maa shɛli bee n-chɛ bɛ tipawumli soya la dolibu.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel and said: The Israelites have broken the agreement I made with their ancestors. They won't obey me,
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Yawɛ suhu daa yiɣisi pam bahi Izraɛlnim’ zuɣu ka o yɛli, “Niriba ŋɔ ni saɣim alikauli shɛli n ni daa lo bɛ yaannima, ka zaɣisi n nol’ la zuɣu,

english_verse: so I'll stop helping them defeat their enemies. Israel still had a lot of enemies when Joshua died,
translation_verse: n ku lan kari zuliya shɛb’ Jɔshua ni daa bi kari ka kpi la ti ba.

english_verse: and I'm going to let those enemies stay. I'll use them to test Israel, because then I can find out if Israel will worship and obey me as their ancestors did.
translation_verse: N ni chɛ ba n-zaŋ ba buɣisi Izraɛlnim’ nya bɛ ni doli man’ Yawɛ soli kaman bɛ yaannim ni daa niŋ shɛm.”

english_verse: That's why the Lord had not let Joshua get rid of those enemy nations all at once.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Yawɛ daa bi kari zuliya shɛb’ bɛn kpalim maa yomyom, ka mi daa bi chɛ ka Jɔshua kari ba.

english_verse: And the Lord had another reason for letting these enemies stay. The Israelites needed to learn how to fight in war, just as their ancestors had done. Each new generation would have to learn by fighting
translation_verse: O daa niŋ lala ni o wuhila Izraɛl ʒiɛmani kam niriba tɔbu tuhibu yɛla, di bahi bamdi bɛ ni shɛb’ bɛn nini daa na ʒi n-nya tɔbu tuhibu la.

english_verse: the Philistines and their five rulers, as well as the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites that lived in the Lebanon Mountains from Mount Baal-Hermon to Hamath Pass.
translation_verse: Zuliya shɛb’ bɛn daa kpalim maa n-nyɛ: Filistia nanima anu mini Keenannim’ zaa ni Sidɔnnim’ ni Hivinim’ bɛn be Lɛbanɔn Zoli zuɣu n-zaŋ Baalihɛrimɔn Zoli zuɣu hal ti paai Lɛbohamat dunoli shee la.

english_verse: Moses had told the Israelites what the Lord had commanded them to do, and now the Lord was using these nations to find out if Israel would obey.
translation_verse: Bɛ daa nyɛla Yawɛ ni zaŋ shɛb’ ni o buɣisi Izraɛlnim’ nya bɛ ni dol’ o zaligu shɛŋa o ni daa zaŋ ti Musa ka o ti bɛ yaannim’ la bee bɛ ku dol’ li.

english_verse: But they refused. And some of them even married Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites who lived all around them. That's how they started worshiping foreign gods. Othniel
translation_verse: Bɛ daa kpuɣi bɛ bipuɣinsi niŋ bɛ paɣiba, ka zaŋ bɛmaŋmaŋ’ bipuɣinsi ti bɛ bidibisi; ka jɛmdi bɛ wuna. Otiniɛl yɛla

english_verse: The Israelites sinned against the Lord by forgetting him and worshiping idols of Baal and Astarte.
translation_verse: Izraɛlnim’ daa tum alahichi Yawɛ sani. Bɛ daa tam Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ bɛ Naawuni maa yɛla, ka ŋmaligi jɛmdila Baalnim’ mini Ashɛranima.

english_verse: This made the Lord angry, so he let Israel be defeated by King Cushan Rishathaim of northern Syria, who ruled Israel eight years and made everyone pay taxes.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Yawɛ suhu daa yiɣisi bahi Izraɛlnim’ zuɣu ka o zaŋ ba niŋ Mɛsopoteemia naa Kushanrishataim nuu ni ka Izraɛlnim’ daa jɛm o yuma anii.

english_verse: The Israelites begged the Lord for help, and so he chose Othniel to rescue them. Othniel was the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Izraɛlnim’ daa ti kum niŋ Yawɛ, ka Yawɛ ti ba ninvuɣ’ so ŋun ni fa ba bahi, ka o daa fa ba bahi. Dilana n-nyɛ Otiniɛl ŋun daa nyɛ Kalɛb tizo Kɛnaz bia la.

english_verse: and Israel was at peace until Othniel died about
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Otiniɛl Kɛnaz bia maa daa kpi. Ɛhud yɛla

english_verse: Once more the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let them be defeated by King Eglon of Moab,
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa lan tum alahichi zaŋ chaŋ Yawɛ sani yaha. Ka Yawɛ daa ti Mɔab Naa Ɛgilɔn kpiɔŋ ka o lu Izraɛlnim’ zuɣu, bɛ ni daa tum alahichi shɛli zaŋ chaŋ ŋun’ Yawɛ sani maa zuɣu.

english_verse: who had joined forces with the Ammonites and the Amalekites to attack Israel. Eglon and his army captured Jericho.
translation_verse: Ka Naa Ɛgilɔn daa laɣim Ammɔnnim’ mini Amalɛknima m-pah’ o min’ o niriba zuɣu chaŋ ti tuhi nyaŋ Izraɛlnima, ka fa dɔbino tihi tiŋ’ la bɛ sani.

english_verse: Then he ruled Israel for
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa jɛm Mɔab Naa Ɛgilɔn maa yuun’ pisaayika.

english_verse: Ehud and some other Israelites took the taxes to Eglon, who was a very fat man. As soon as they gave the taxes to Eglon, Ehud said it was time to go home.
translation_verse: Ɛhud ni daa zaŋ bɛ farigu binyara maa yo n-naai, o daa chɛmi ka ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn ʒi li tahi na kuli.

english_verse: The Israelites begged the Lord for help, and the Lord chose Ehud from the Benjamin tribe to rescue them. They put Ehud in charge of taking the taxes to King Eglon, but before Ehud went, he made a double-edged dagger. Ehud was left-handed, so he strapped the dagger to his right thigh, where it was hidden under his robes.
translation_verse: Ka Ɛhud daa kuri su’ shɛli din mali naŋgbana ayi, ka di wɔɣilim nyɛ kaman sɛntimita pihinu ka o zaŋ li lo n-tabil’ o nudirigu gbalipini n-ye o binyɛrigu limsi li.

english_verse: Ehud went with the other Israelites as far as the statues at Gilgal. Then he turned back and went upstairs to the room where Eglon had his throne. Ehud said, “Your Majesty, I need to talk with you in private.” Eglon replied, “Don't say anything yet!” His officials left the room, and Eglon stood up as Ehud came closer. “Yes,” Ehud said, “I have a message for you from God!”
translation_verse: Ka naa maa daa ʒi o dufahirili zuɣusaa zɔntu’ mahili ni, ka Ɛhud ka o sanna ti yɛl’ o, “M malila yɛtɔɣ’ shɛli din yi Naawuni sanna ni n-yɛl’ a.” Ka naa maa vaai yiɣis’ o ʒiishee zani.

english_verse: Ehud pulled out the dagger with his left hand and shoved it so far into Eglon's stomach
translation_verse: Ka Ɛhud daa zaŋ o gɔbiga tim o nudirigu gbalipini maa polo darigi ŋoog’ o sua maa n-zaŋ kuhi naa maa puli;

english_verse: that even the handle was buried in his fat. Ehud left the dagger there. Then after closing and locking the doors to the room, he climbed through a window onto the porch
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Ɛhud daa yi zɔntua maa ni na ka vooi di dunoya yo n-kpari li pa o zuɣu.

english_verse: and left. When the king's officials came back and saw that the doors were locked, they said, “The king is probably inside relieving himself.”
translation_verse: Ɛhud ni daa yina kuli naai, ka naazɔnim’ daa kpe nti nya ka dufahirili zuɣusaa zɔntua maa dunoya yomi kpari, ka bɛ tɛhi ni naa maa kpɛla zɔntua maa ni du’ bil’ ni ni o ti wɔɣis’ omaŋa.

english_verse: They stood there waiting until they felt foolish, but Eglon still didn't open the doors. Finally, they unlocked the doors and found King Eglon lying dead on the floor.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa guhi ka di yuui ha, amaa ka o kul bi yoori zɔntua maa dunoya maa; ka bɛ daa zaŋ saafɛbia yooi li nya ka bɛ naa maa kpimi do tiŋa.

english_verse: But by that time, Ehud had already escaped past the statues. Ehud went to the town of Seirah
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa kpalim guhiri saha shɛli maa, ka Ɛhud daa chaŋ hal ti gari kuɣikpɛra shee la n-zo n-kuli Siɛra tiligi.

english_verse: in the hill country of Ephraim and started blowing a trumpet as a signal to call the Israelites together. When they came, he shouted, “Follow me! The Lord will help us defeat the Moabites.” The Israelites followed Ehud down to the Jordan valley, and they captured the places where people cross the river on the way to Moab. They would not let anyone go across,
translation_verse: Ka Ɛhud daa yɛli ba, “Doli ya ma, dama Yawɛ zaŋ yi dimnim’ Mɔabnim’ niŋ yi nuu ni.” Ka bɛ daa dol’ o chaŋ ti gu so’ shɛli Mɔabnim’ ni yɛn doli gbaai Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili du, ka daa bi saɣi ka so doli nimaani du.

english_verse: Moab was so badly defeated that it was a long time before they were strong enough to attack Israel again. And Israel was at peace for
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa nyaŋ Mɔabnim’ dindali maa, ka nya vuhim bɛ tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni yuun’ pihinii. Shamga yɛla

english_verse: Shamgar the son of Anath was the next to rescue Israel. In one battle, he used a sharp wooden pole to kill
translation_verse: Ŋun daa pa Ɛhud zuɣu n-daa nyɛ Anat bia Shamga ŋun daa zaŋ naɣikpar’ kpaa ku Filistianim’ ninvuɣ’ kɔbisiyɔbu la. Ŋun’ gba daa fa Izraɛlnim’ bahi.

english_verse: After the death of Ehud, the Israelites again started disobeying the Lord.
translation_verse: Ɛhud kum nyaaŋa, Izraɛlnim’ daa lan tum alahichi zaŋ chaŋ Yawɛ sani yaha.

english_verse: So the Lord let the Canaanite King Jabin of Hazor conquer Israel. Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, lived in Harosheth-Ha-Goiim.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa zaŋ ba niŋ Keenan Naa Jabin ŋun daa diri ʒi Hazɔr, ka o sapashin’ kpɛm’ nyɛ Sisɛra ŋun daa be Harɔshɛtihagɔim la nuu ni.

english_verse: “Stand at the entrance to the tent,” Sisera told her. “If someone comes by and asks if anyone is inside, tell them ‘No.’ ”
translation_verse: Ka Sisɛra yɛl’ o, “Ʒe dunoli maa ni. So yi ti kana ti bɔh’ a ni so be kpe, nyin’ yɛlim’ o ni so kani.”

english_verse: Deborah the wife of Lappidoth was a prophet and a leader of Israel during those days.
translation_verse: Di saha maa Dɛbɔra ŋun daa nyɛ anabi, ka nyɛ Lapidɔt paɣ’ la n-daa nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ zuɣulana.

english_verse: She would sit under Deborah's Palm Tree between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, where Israelites would come and ask her to settle their legal cases.
translation_verse: O daa yi ʒiinila Dɛbɔra dɔbino tia din be Rama mini Bɛtɛl sunsuuni Ifriim tiŋgban’ ni zoya zuɣu tiŋ’ la ni gbini, ka Izraɛlnim’ chan’ o sani ka o ti kariti bɛ yɛla saria tiri ba.

english_verse: One day, Barak the son of Abinoam was in Kedesh in Naphtali, and Deborah sent word for him to come and talk with her. When he arrived, she said: I have a message for you from the Lord God of Israel! You are to get together an army of
translation_verse: Dahin shɛli ka o daa ti tim Kɛdɛshi din be Naftali tiŋgban’ ni la ti boli Barak Abinɔam bia na ti yɛl’ o, “Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Izraɛl Naawuni ŋɔ yɛli nyin’ Barak, ‘Cham’ ti laɣim a niriba Tabo Zoli zuɣu m-pii ninvuɣ’ tuhi’ pia Naftali mini Zɛbulɔn zuliya niriba ni.

english_verse: The Lord will trick Sisera into coming out to fight you at the Kishon River. Sisera will be leading King Jabin's army as usual, and they will have their chariots, but the Lord has promised to help you defeat them.
translation_verse: Ka n chɛ ka Jabin sapashin’ kpɛm’ Sisɛra zaŋ o chɛchɛbunsi min’ o tɔbbihi kana ti chirigi ya Kishɔn Mɔɣili ni; ka n zaŋ o niŋ a nuu ni.”

english_verse: “All right, I'll go!” she replied. “But I'm warning you that the Lord is going to let a woman defeat Sisera, and no one will honor you for winning the battle.” Deborah and Barak left for Kedesh,
translation_verse: Ka Dɛbɔra yɛli, “N ni dol’ a chaŋ, amaa pa nyini nti yɛn nya a chandi maa nasara dibu jilima, dama Yawɛ ni ti chɛ ka paɣa n-nyaŋ Sisɛra.” Ka Dɛbɔra daa yiɣisi doli Barak chaŋ Kɛdɛshi.

english_verse: At this time, Heber of the Kenite clan was living near the village of Oak in Zaanannim, not far from Kedesh. The Kenites were descendants of Hobab, the father-in-law of Moses, but Heber had moved and had set up his tents away from the rest of the clan.
translation_verse: Di saha maa Hɛbɛr ŋun daa nyɛ Kɛn nir’ la daa woligimi ka chɛ Kɛnnim’ bɛn daa nyɛ Hɔbab, Musa deemba daŋ niriba la, ka zaŋ o tanti yi kpaŋ’ ha ti kpa Zaananim oki tia la gbini miri Kɛdɛshi.

english_verse: When Sisera learned that Barak had led an army to Mount Tabor,
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa yɛli Sisɛra ni Barak Abinɔam bia la be Tabo Zoli zuɣu,

english_verse: Deborah shouted, “Barak, it's time to attack Sisera! Because today the Lord is going to help you defeat him. In fact, the Lord has already gone on ahead to fight for you.” Barak led his
translation_verse: Ka Dɛbɔra daa yɛli Barak, “Yiɣisima! Yawɛ m-be a tooni mal’ a chana. Zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ, Yawɛ zaŋ Sisɛra niŋ a nuu ni.” Di saha ka Barak daa yiɣisi ka tɔbbihi tuhi’ pia dol’ o ka bɛ yi Tabo Zoli zuɣu siɣi.

english_verse: And during the battle, the Lord confused Sisera, his chariot drivers, and his whole army. Everyone was so afraid of Barak and his army, that even Sisera jumped down from his chariot and tried to escape.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa chɛ ka Sisɛra min’ o chɛchɛbunsi ni o tɔbbihi zaa birim Barak tooni, ka Barak daa zaŋ takɔbi ku ba. Ka Sisɛra daa sheeg’ o chɛchɛbuŋ’ zuɣu na guui.

english_verse: Barak's forces went after Sisera's chariots and army as far as Harosheth-Ha-Goiim. Sisera's entire army was wiped out.
translation_verse: Ka Barak daa kari doli chɛchɛbunsi maa mini tɔbbihi maa hal ni Harɔshɛtihagɔim nti ku Sisɛra tɔbbihi maa zaa hal ka bɛ ni yino gba bi tiligi.

english_verse: Only Sisera escaped. He ran to Heber's camp, because Heber and his family had a peace treaty with the king of Hazor. Sisera went to the tent that belonged to Jael, Heber's wife.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Sisɛra daa guui hal ti paai Hɛbɛr Kɛn nir’ la paɣ’ Jaɛl tanti gbini; dama zabili daa lan ka Hazɔr Naa Jabin mini Hɛbɛr Kɛn nir’ maa yiŋnim’ sunsuuni.

english_verse: She came out to greet him and said, “Come in, sir! Please come on in. Don't be afraid.” After they had gone inside, Sisera lay down, and Jael covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Ka Jaɛl daa yina tuhi Sisɛra soli yɛl’ o, “N dana, ŋmaligim’ kpe kpe na, ka di chɛ ka a suhu zɔhira.” Ka o daa ŋmaligi kpe o sani tanti maa ni; ka paɣ’ maa ti zaŋ chinchini pil’ o.

english_verse: “Could I have a little water?” he asked. “I'm thirsty.” Jael opened a leather bottle and poured him some milk, then she covered him back up.
translation_verse: Ka Sisɛra yɛl’ o, “Kɔnyuri m-mali ma. N suhir’ a, tim ma kom biɛla ka n nyu.” Ka paɣ’ maa daa yooi bihim koligu m-booi bihim ti o ka o nyu, ka o lan zaŋ chinchini pil’ o.

english_verse: Sisera was exhausted and soon fell fast asleep. Jael took a hammer and drove a tent-peg through his head into the ground, and he died.
translation_verse: Ka Sisɛra daa dɔni gbihi di ni daa wum’ o pam zuɣu. Ka Jaɛl Hɛbɛr paɣ’ maa daa kpuɣi tanti kpaa mini zali m-puɣisi chaŋ ti zaŋ li ba Sisɛra tapaɣa n-kpahi li ti ba tiŋ’ ka o kpi.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Barak had been following Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him. “The man you're looking for is inside,” she said. “Come in and I'll show him to you.” They went inside, and there was Sisera—dead and stretched out with a tent-peg through his skull.
translation_verse: Nyama, ka Barak daa ti biɛhiri Sisɛra naba na, ka Jaɛl yi nti tuh’ o soli ka yɛl’ o, “Kamina, ka n ti wuh’ a a ni bɔri ninvuɣ’ so maa.” Ka Barak daa kpe o tanti maa ni nti nya ka tanti kpaa n-kpahi Sisɛra tapaɣa ti ba tiŋ’ ka o kpi n-doya.

english_verse: That same day God defeated the Canaanite King Jabin while the Israelites looked on, and his army was no longer powerful enough to attack the Israelites.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu dindali maa ka Naawuni daa chɛ ka Izraɛlnim’ nyaŋ Keenan Naa Jabin.

english_verse: Jabin grew weaker while the Israelites kept growing stronger, until at last the Israelites destroyed him.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa niŋ ŋun’ Keenan Naa Jabin maa muɣisigu hal ti ku o.

english_verse: After the battle was over that day, Deborah and Barak sang this song:
translation_verse: Dindali maa ka Dɛbɔra mini Barak Abinɔam bia la daa yili yilli ŋɔ:

english_verse: Listen, kings and rulers, while I sing for the Lord, the God of Israel.
translation_verse: Nanima, wummiya! Zuɣulaannima, wummiya! N ni yili yila niɣim n kukoli paɣi Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Izraɛl Naawuni ŋɔ.

english_verse: In the time of Shamgar son of Anath, and now again in Jael's time, roads were too dangerous for caravans. Travelers had to take the back roads,
translation_verse: Shamga Anat bia saha la mini Jaɛl saha la, sochandiba bɛn daari doli taba daa bi lan chana, ka bɛn gɔri mi kpalim baɣisirila sokpansi.

english_verse: and villagers couldn't work in their fields. Then Deborah took command, protecting Israel as a mother protects her children.
translation_verse: Di saha maa kpariba daa chɛla bɛ tuma Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ni hal ka nyin’ Dɛbɔra ti yiɣisi. O daa yiɣisiya m-bemi kaman Izraɛlnim’ ma la.

english_verse: The Israelites worshiped other gods, and the gates of their towns were then attacked. But they had no shields or spears to fight with.
translation_verse: Izraɛlnim’ ni daa pii wun’ pala la, di saha ka tɔbu daa be bɛ tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni. Ninvuɣ’ tuhi’ pihinahi bɛn be Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ni ŋuni n-daa lee mali nyɔtaɣirigu bee kpani?

english_verse: I praise you, Lord, and I am grateful for those leaders and soldiers who volunteered.
translation_verse: N suhu zaa kul bela Izraɛl sapashinnim’ bɛn zaŋ bɛ nyɛviya pa talima ni bɛ suhu yubu la ni. Paɣimiya Yawɛ!

english_verse: Listen, everyone! Whether you ride a donkey with a padded saddle or have to walk.
translation_verse: Yinim’ bɛn bari bun’ piɛla ka ʒi bunnyaampar’ gahinda zuɣu mini yinim’ bɛn doli soya, yɛlimiya di yɛla.

english_verse: Even those who carry water to the animals will tell you, “The Lord has won victories, and so has Israel.” Then the Lord's people marched down to the town gates
translation_verse: Wummiya! Baansi bɛn be kɔbilisi gbini yɛri Yawɛ nasara dibu yɛla nimaani, nasara din nyɛ Izraɛl kpariba nasara! Di nyaaŋa ka Yawɛ niriba daa chaŋ dari dibu chandi yi bɛ tinsi ni na.

english_verse: and said, “Deborah, let's go! Let's sing as we march. Barak, capture our enemies.”
translation_verse: Dɛbɔra, yiɣisima, yiɣisima. Yiɣisima, yiɣisima, Yilimi yilli! Barak Abinɔam bia, yiɣisim’ zaŋ a ni gbahi ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ daba la kuli!

english_verse: The Lord's people who were left joined with their leaders and fought at my side.
translation_verse: Di saha ka nabihi bɛn daa kpalim yina, ka Yawɛ niriba daa yina ni bɛ ti tuhi wɔɣira ti o.

english_verse: Troops came from Ephraim, where Amalekites once lived. Others came from Benjamin; officers and leaders came from Machir and Zebulun.
translation_verse: Bɛ daa yila Ifriim tiŋgban’ ni, ka vinvamli ni na, n-doli nyin’ Bɛnjamin min’ a daŋ niriba. Ka sapashin’ kpamba daa yi Makiri na, ka sapashim’ bihi mi daa yi Zɛbulɔn na.

english_verse: The rulers of Issachar came along with Deborah, and Issachar followed Barak into the valley. But the tribe of Reuben was no help at all!
translation_verse: Ka Isaka zuliya ni toondaannim’ daa doli Dɛbɔra; Isaka zuliya niriba maa daa ʒe Barak yim, ka dol’ o du o napɔŋkpahi siɣi vinvamli maa ni. Amaa Rubin zuliya niriba bɛn’ noya daa wolimi.

english_verse: Reuben, why did you stay among your sheep pens? Was it to listen to shepherds whistling for their sheep? No one could figure out why Reuben wouldn't come.
translation_verse: Bɔ n-chɛ ka bɛ daa kpalim bɛ piɛri sani ni bɛ wumdi piɛguliba ni piɛbiri yuhi booni piɛri shɛm? Iin, Rubin zuliya niriba bɛn’ noya daa wolimi.

english_verse: The people of Gilead stayed across the Jordan. Why did the tribe of Dan remain on their ships and the tribe of Asher stay along the coast near the harbors?
translation_verse: Ka Giliadnim’ daa kpalim be Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili duli. Ka bɔ n-chɛ ka Dan zuliya niriba la mi daa kpalim be bɛ ŋarima gbini? Asha zuliya niriba gba daa kpalim be teeku duli. Bɛ daa kpalim ʒinila teeku duli maa.

english_verse: But soldiers of Zebulun and Naphtali risked their lives to attack the enemy.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Zɛbulɔn mini Naftali zuliya niriba bɛn’ daa zaŋ bɛ nyɛviya pa talima tɔb’ ni zoya zuɣu.

english_verse: Canaanite kings fought us at Taanach by the stream near Megiddo— but they couldn't rob us of our silver.
translation_verse: Ka nanim’ daa kana Taanak Mɛgido kulibɔŋ la ni ti tuhi tɔbu. Ka Keenan nanim’ daa tuhi, amaa ka bi di nɛma din nyɛ anzinfa.

english_verse: From their pathways in the sky the stars fought Sisera,
translation_verse: Ka saŋmarisi daa yi zuɣusaa na ti tuhi tɔbu; bɛ daa yila bɛ biɛhigu shee na ti tuhi Sisɛra.

english_verse: and his soldiers were swept away by the ancient Kishon River. I will march on and be brave.
translation_verse: Ka Kishɔn Mɔɣili kokpɛɣu daa ʒi ba chaŋ. Kishɔn kom din zɔri n-daa ʒi ba chaŋ. N ni chaŋ dari dibu chandi. N ni chaŋ dari dibu chandi ni kpiɔŋ!

english_verse: Sisera's horses galloped off, their hoofs thundering in retreat.
translation_verse: Ka yuri daa balisira, ka bɛ takarifiɛma tɔri tiŋ’ yɔri vuri.

english_verse: The Lord's angel said, “Put a curse on Meroz Town! Its people refused to help the Lord fight his powerful enemies.”
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ malaika daa yɛli, “Yɛlimiya noli ti Mɛrɔz,” “yɛlimiya no’ biɛɣu ti di niriba, bɛ ni bi kana ti sɔŋ Yawɛ n-tuhi bɛn mali kpiɔŋ sɔŋ o la zuɣu.”

english_verse: But honor Jael, the wife of Heber from the Kenite clan. Give more honor to her than to any other woman who lives in tents. Yes, give more honor to her than to any other woman.
translation_verse: Hɛbɛr ŋun nyɛ Kɛn nir’ la paɣa Jaɛl mal’ alibarika pam paɣiba ni. Paɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn be tanti suɣa puuni, ŋuna m-mal’ alibarika.

english_verse: Sisera asked for water, but Jael gave him milk— cream in a fancy cup.
translation_verse: Sisɛra daa suh’ o la kom, amaa ka o ti o la bihim; o daa zaŋ bihim maa niŋla pipi’ viɛli ni na ti ti o.

english_verse: She reached for a tent-peg and held a hammer in her right hand. And with a blow to the head, she crushed his skull.
translation_verse: Ka Jaɛl daa kpuɣi tanti kpaa niŋ o nu’ yin’ ni, ka kpuɣi zali niŋ o nudirigu ni n-zaŋ tanti kpaa maa ba Sisɛra tapaɣa n-kpahi li ti ba tiŋa.

english_verse: She and her wisest women gave the same answer:
translation_verse: Ka o paɣ’ tab’ bɛn mali yɛm daa garig’ o yɛli, Aai. Ka o garigi yɛl’ omaŋa,

english_verse: “Sisera and his troops are finding treasures to bring back— a woman, or maybe two, for each man, and beautiful dresses for those women to wear.”
translation_verse: “Di pa shɛli bɛ ŋme n-dila nɛma, ka bɔri ni bɛ pir’ li tari taba; ka tɔbbia kam nya paɣisar’ yino bee bɛba ayi, ka Sisɛra nya chinchin’ suŋ, ka man’ gba nya nɛma maa ni yɛri zaɣ’ suma ayi ye.”

english_verse: Our Lord, we pray that all your enemies will die like Sisera. But let everyone who loves you shine brightly like the sun at dawn. Midian Steals Everything from Israel There was peace in Israel for about
translation_verse: Yawɛ, chɛ ka a dimnim’ zaa kpi lala, amaa ka chɛ ka a zɔnim’ mi ne kaman wuntaŋ’ ni puhirina ni yaa n-ne shɛm la. Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa nya vuhim bɛ tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni yuun’ pihinahi.

english_verse: Then once again the Israelites started disobeying the Lord, so he let the nation of Midian control Israel for seven years.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa ti tum alahichi Yawɛ sani, ka Yawɛ daa zaŋ ba niŋ Midiannim’ nuu ni yuma ayopɔin.

english_verse: The Midianites were so cruel that many Israelites ran to the mountains and hid in caves.
translation_verse: Ka Midiannim’ daa nyaŋ Izraɛlnima; ka Izraɛlnim’ maa zo nti sɔɣi bɔɣa din daa be zoya zuɣu puuni mini tampima voya ni ni luɣ’ shɛŋa bɛ n-ni tooi sɔɣi zani tuhi tɔbu.

english_verse: Every time the Israelites planted crops, the Midianites invaded Israel together with the Amalekites and other eastern nations.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa yi ti kul biri bimbirili kam, Midiannim’ maa mini Amalɛknim’ ni wulimpuhili polo nim’ kanimina ti lu bɛ zuɣu.

english_verse: They rode in on their camels, set up their tents, and then let their livestock eat the crops as far as the town of Gaza. The Midianites stole food, sheep, cattle, and donkeys. Like a swarm of locusts, they could not be counted, and they ruined the land wherever they went.
translation_verse: Dama bɛ daa yi zaŋdila bɛ tantinim’ mini bɛ niɣi ni bɛ laakumnim’ kanna ti luri bɛ zuɣu, ka bɛ galisim ŋmanila toli. Ka bɛ mini laakumnim’ maa daa ka kalinli. Dinzuɣu bɛ daa yi ti kana bɛ saɣindila bɛ tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni binshɛɣukam.

english_verse: The Midianites took almost everything that belonged to the Israelites, and the Israelites begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Izraɛlnim’ ni daa kum niŋ Yawɛ Midiannim’ zuɣu maa,

english_verse: I am your God, and I told you not to worship Amorite gods, even though you are living in the land of the Amorites. But you refused to listen. The Lord Chooses Gideon
translation_verse: N daa yɛli ya, ‘Man’ Yawɛ n-nyɛ yi Naawuni, dinzuɣu miriya ka yi jɛm Amɔrinim’ shɛb’ tiŋgbɔŋ ni yi ni be ŋɔ wuna la.’ Amaa ka yi zaɣisi n noli.”

english_verse: One day an angel from the Lord went to the town of Ophrah and sat down under the big tree that belonged to Joash, a member of the Abiezer clan. Joash's son Gideon was nearby, threshing grain in a shallow pit, where he could not be seen by the Midianites.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ malaika daa ti kana ti ʒi oki tia din daa be Ofira ka nyɛ Jɔash ŋun daa nyɛ Abiɛza zuliya ni nir’ ni su shɛl’ la gbini. Ka o bia Gidiɔn daa sɔɣi be nimaani wain tɔɣiri bɔɣili ni buri alikama ka bi bɔri ni Midiannim’ nya o.

english_verse: The angel appeared and spoke to Gideon, “The Lord is helping you, and you are a strong warrior.”
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ malaika maa daa ka o sanna ti yɛl’ o, “Nyin’ ŋun nyɛ suhukpeendana ni kpiɔŋlan’ ŋɔ, Yawɛ be a sani.”

english_verse: Gideon answered, “Please don't take this wrong, but if the Lord is helping us, then why have all of these awful things happened? We've heard how the Lord performed miracles and rescued our ancestors from Egypt. But those things happened long ago. Now the Lord has abandoned us to the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Ka Gidiɔn yɛl’ o, “Ndana, n suhir’ a, Yawɛ yi be ti sani, di chaŋ wula ka yɛla ŋɔ zaa paai ti? Ti yaannim’ ni yɛl’ ti ni Yawɛ daa tum alahiziba tuun’ shɛŋa la zaa lee bela ya? Bɛ daa kul bɔhira, ‘Pa Yawɛ n-daa yihi ti Ijipti na la?’ Amaa pumpɔŋɔ o chɛ ti mi bahi, ka zaŋ ti niŋ Midiannim’ nuu ni.”

english_verse: Then the Lord himself said, “Gideon, you will be strong, because I am giving you the power to rescue Israel from the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ ŋmaligi yɛl’ o, “Mani n-tim a, zaŋm’ a kpiɔŋ ŋɔ chaŋ ti fa Izraɛlnim’ Midiannim’ nuu ni bahi.”

english_verse: Gideon replied, “But how can I rescue Israel? My clan is the weakest one in Manasseh, and everyone else in my family is more important than I am.”
translation_verse: Ka Gidiɔn garigi yɛl’ o, “Ndana, wula ka n lee yɛn niŋ n-tooi fa Izraɛlnim’ bahi? Nyama, n daŋ niriba nyɛla bɛn ka yaa Manaasa zuliya ni, ka m mi nyɛ ŋun pɔri n yiŋnim’ ni.”

english_verse: “Gideon,” the Lord answered, “you can rescue Israel because I am going to help you! Defeating the Midianites will be as easy as beating up one man.”
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ yɛl’ o, “N ni be a sani, ka chɛ ka a ŋme n-ku Midiannim’ kaman ninvuɣ’ yino n-nyɛ ba la.”

english_verse: Gideon said, “It's hard to believe that I'm actually talking to the Lord. Please do something so I'll know that you really are the Lord.
translation_verse: Ka Gidiɔn daa yɛli, “A nini yi tiɣi ma, nyin’ wuhim’ ma shihirili din wuhiri ni nyin’ Yawɛ n-tɔɣisiri ma yɛtɔɣa ŋɔ.

english_verse: And wait here until I bring you an offering.” “All right, I'll wait,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: N suhir’ a, ni a di chaŋ, ka m bo pin’ na ti ti a.” Ka o yɛl’ o, “N ni guh’ a hal ka a ti labina.”

english_verse: Gideon went home and killed a young goat, then started boiling the meat. Next, he opened a big sack of flour and made it into thin bread. When the meat was done, he put it in a basket and poured the broth into a clay cooking pot. He took the meat, the broth, and the bread and placed them under the big tree.
translation_verse: Ka Gidiɔn daa kuli ti gbaai bubil’ kɔrigi, ka tooi zim kilɔgiram pia m-mali bɔrɔbɔro din ka dabindi. Ka daa zaŋ nimdi maa n-niŋ piɛɣu ni, ka zaŋ ʒiɛri mi niŋ ʒɛduɣu ni n-zaŋ li ka oki tia maa gbinna ti ti o.

english_verse: God's angel said, “Gideon, put the meat and the bread on this rock, and pour the broth over them.” Gideon did as he was told.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ malaika maa daa yɛl’ o, “Zaŋm’ nimdi maa mini bɔrɔbɔro din ka dabindi maa pa tampiŋ ŋɔ zuɣu, ka kpaai ʒiɛri maa pol’ li.” Ka Gidiɔn daa niŋ lala.

english_verse: The angel was holding a walking stick, and he touched the meat and the bread with the end of the stick. Flames jumped from the rock and burned up the meat and the bread. When Gideon looked, the angel was gone.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ malaika maa daa zaŋ o ni gbib’ jaaŋgbe’ shɛli o nuu ni nyol’ ni shihi nimdi maa mini bɔrɔbɔro maa. Ka buɣim daa yi tampiŋ maa ni na taai nimdi maa mini bɔrɔbɔro din ka dabindi maa n-di li zaa. Ka Yawɛ malaika maa daa ŋmaligi chaŋ, ka Gidiɔn bi lan nya o.

english_verse: Gideon realized that he had seen one of the Lord's angels. “Oh!” he moaned. “Now I'm going to die.”
translation_verse: Di saha maa ka Gidiɔn daa baŋ ni Yawɛ malaika m-bala; ka kuhi yɛli, “Mbaye! Yaa n Duuma NAAWUNI, dama n nini nya Yawɛ malaika!”

english_verse: “Calm down!” the Lord told Gideon. “There's nothing to be afraid of. You're not going to die.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Yawɛ yɛl’ o, “Di chɛ ka dabiɛm mal’ a. Chɛ ka a suhu doya, a ku kpi.”

english_verse: Gideon built an altar for worshiping the Lord and called it “The Lord Calms Our Fears.” It still stands there in Ophrah, a town in the territory of the Abiezer clan. Gideon Tears Down Baal's Altar
translation_verse: Ka Gidiɔn daa me sara maligu bimbini ti Yawɛ nimaani, ka bol’ li, “Yawɛ nyɛla suhudoo.” Ka di na kul ʒe Ofira Abiɛzanim’ ni su luɣ’ shɛl’ la hal ni zuŋɔ.

english_verse: That night the Lord spoke to Gideon again: Get your father's second-best bull, the one that's seven years old. Use it to pull down the altar where your father worships Baal and cut down the sacred pole next to the altar.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Gidiɔn dindali maa yuŋ, Gbaam’ a ba naɣilaa, ka bo naɣila’ so ŋun pah’ ayi ka nyɛ yuma ayopɔin ka daag’ a ba ni me Baal bimbin’ shɛl’ la luhi, ka ŋmaai Ashɛra ŋmahinli binwɔɣinli din ʒe m-baɣ’ li la luhi;

english_verse: Then build an altar for worshiping me on the highest part of the hill where your town is built. Use layers of stones for my altar, not just a pile of rocks. Cut up the wood from the pole, make a fire, kill the bull, and burn it as a sacrifice to me.
translation_verse: ka me bimbini n-chɛ ka di kuɣa do m-pa tab’ zuɣu viɛnyɛliŋga tam zoli ŋɔ zuɣu n-ti Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ yi Naawuni ŋɔ; ka zaŋ naɣila’ so ŋun pah’ ayi la mali sara zaŋ o pa Ashɛra ŋmahinli binwɔɣinli shɛli a ni daai luhi la dari zuɣu n-nyo li buɣim.

english_verse: Gideon chose ten of his servants to help him, and they did everything God had said. But since Gideon was afraid of his family and the other people in Ophrah, he did it all at night.
translation_verse: Ka Gidiɔn daa zaŋ o tumtumdiba ninvuɣ’ pia pa omaŋ’ zuɣu chaŋ ti niŋ Yawɛ ni yɛl’ o ni o niŋ shɛm maa. O daa zɔrila o yiŋnim’ min’ o yanim’ ni o niŋ li wuntaŋ’ ni, dinzuɣu ka o daa niŋ li la yuŋ.

english_verse: When the people of the town got up the next morning, they saw that Baal's altar had been knocked over, and the sacred pole next to it had been cut down. Then they noticed the new altar covered with the remains of the sacrificed bull.
translation_verse: Ka biɛɣu daa neei ka tiŋ’ maa nim’ yina ti nya ka bɛ wurimla Baal bimbini maa, ka daai Ashɛra ŋmahinli binwɔɣinli din ʒe m-baɣ’ li la luhi, ka me bimbin’ shɛli zali di zaashee maa, ka zaŋ naɣila’ so ŋun pah’ ayi mali sara pa di zuɣu n-nyo o buɣim.

english_verse: “Who could have done such a thing?” they asked. And they kept on asking, until finally someone told them, “Gideon the son of Joash did it.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ bɔhiri taba, “Ka ŋuni n-lee tum tuuni ŋɔ?” Ka bɛ daa vihi di zuɣu hal ka so ti yɛli ba ni Gidiɔn Jɔash bia la n-tum tuuni maa.

english_verse: The men of the town went to Joash and said, “Your son Gideon knocked over Baal's altar and cut down the sacred pole next to it. Hand him over, so we can kill him!”
translation_verse: Di saha ka tiŋ’ maa nim’ daa yɛli Jɔash, “Yihim’ a bia maa na ka ti ku o. O ni wurim Baal bimbini, ka ŋmaai Ashɛra ŋmahinli binwɔɣinli din ʒe m-baɣ’ li la luhi la zuɣu.”

english_verse: The crowd pushed closer and closer, but Joash replied, “Are you trying to take revenge for Baal? Are you trying to rescue Baal? If you are, you will be the ones who are put to death, and it will happen before another day dawns. If Baal really is a god, let him take his own revenge on someone who tears down his altar.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Jɔash daa bɔhi bɛn zaa kana ti lir’ o maa, “Yi zanila Baal zaani? Yi zabirila o zuɣu? Ŋunkam zabir’ o zuɣu, zaŋ chaŋ biɛɣ’ asiba bɛ ni ku dilana. O yi nyɛla wuni, yin’ chɛliy’ o ka o zab’ omaŋ’ zuɣu, dama o bimbini ka bɛ wurim maa.”

english_verse: That same day, Joash changed Gideon's name to Jerubbaal, explaining, “He tore down Baal's altar, so let Baal take revenge himself.” Gideon Defeats the Midianites
translation_verse: Dindali maa zaŋ chana, bɛ daa booni Gidiɔn la Jɛrubaal, Di gbinni nyɛla, “Chɛliya ka buɣili Baal min’ o va; dama o bimbini ka o wurim maa.”

english_verse: All the Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations got together and crossed the Jordan River. Then they invaded the land of Israel and set up camp in Jezreel Valley.
translation_verse: Di saha maa ka Midiannim’ mini Amalɛknim’ ni wulimpuhili polo nim’ zaa daa laɣim kana ti gbaai Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili du n-zaŋ bɛ tantinim’ ti kpa Jɛziriil Vinvamli ni.

english_verse: The Lord's Spirit took control of Gideon, and Gideon blew a trumpet as a signal for the men in the Abiezer clan to follow him.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Yawɛ Shia daa siɣi Gidiɔn zuɣu na, ka o zaŋ kikaa piɛb’ boli Abiɛza daŋ niriba ni bɛ kana ti dol’ o.

english_verse: He also sent messengers to the tribes of Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, telling the men of these tribes to come and join his army. Then they set out toward the enemy camp.
translation_verse: Ka o daa tim tuumba Manaasa zuliya niriba zaa sani nti boli ba ka bɛ kana ti dol’ o. Ka o daa lan tim ti boli Asha mini Zɛbulɔn ni Naftali zuliya niriba, ka bɛ gba daa kana ti pahi bɛ zuɣu.

english_verse: Gideon prayed to God, “I know that you promised to help me rescue Israel, but I need proof. Tonight I'll spread a sheep skin on the stone floor of that threshing-place over there. If you really will help me rescue Israel, then tomorrow morning let there be dew on the skin, but let the stone floor be dry.”
translation_verse: Nyama, n yɛn zaŋla piɛ’ gbaŋ sɔŋ kabɔɣili ni, maligim yi lula piɛ’ gbaŋ maa kɔŋko zuɣu, ka bi lu m-mahigi tiŋgbani gil’ li, dindina m baŋya ni a shiri ni chɛ ka n fa Izraɛlnim’ bahi kaman a ni yɛli shɛm.”

english_verse: And that's just what happened. Early the next morning, Gideon got up and checked the sheep skin. He squeezed out enough water to fill a bowl.
translation_verse: Ka di daa shiri niŋ lala. Biɛɣu ni daa neei, ka Gidiɔn yiɣisi asiba, o daa kahim piɛ’ gbaŋ maa zuɣu maligim palila pipia.

english_verse: But Gideon prayed to God again. “Don't be angry with me,” Gideon said. “Let me try this just one more time, so I'll really be sure you'll help me. Only this time, let the skin be dry and the stone floor be wet.”
translation_verse: Ka Gidiɔn daa lan yɛli Naawuni, “N suhir’ a, di chɛ ka a suhu yiɣisi bahi n zuɣu, m bɔrimi ni n lan zaŋ piɛ’ gbaŋ maa sɔŋ buɣisi bin’ yini pahi. N suhir’ a, chɛ ka maligim lu m-mahigi tiŋgbani gili piɛ’ gbaŋ maa, amaa ka chɛ ka piɛ’ gbaŋ maa zuɣu kuma.”

english_verse: That night, God made the stone floor wet with dew, but he kept the sheep skin dry.
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa shiri niŋ lala dindali maa yuŋ. O daa chɛ ka piɛ’ gbaŋ maa zuɣu kummi, amaa ka chɛ ka maligim lu m-mahigi tiŋgbani din gil’ li zaa.

english_verse: Early the next morning, Gideon and his army got up and moved their camp to Fear Spring. The Midianite camp was to the north, in the valley at the foot of Moreh Hill.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Jɛrubaal mini ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn be o sani zaa daa daŋ yibu chaŋ ti dɔni baɣili Harɔd kulibɔŋ. Ka Midiannim’ mi daa do vinvamli ni zaŋ lab’ nuzaa polo miri Mɔre daboli.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Gideon, your army is too big. I can't let you win with this many soldiers. The Israelites would think that they had won the battle all by themselves and that I didn't have anything to do with it.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Gidiɔn, “A niriba maa galisiya pam ni n zaŋ Midiannim’ niŋ bɛ nuu ni. Di yi niŋ lala Izraɛlnim’ ni nyu bara niŋ ma ka yɛli, ‘Tinima n-tuhi fa timaŋa.’

english_verse: So call your troops together and tell them that anyone who is really afraid can leave Mount Gilead and go home.” Twenty-two thousand men returned home, leaving Gideon with only
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu yɛlim’ niriba maa ni ŋunkam zɔri dabiɛm ka o ni sɔhira, ŋun’ lab’ kuli.” Ka Gidiɔn daa buɣisi ba lala, ka ninvuɣ’ tuhi’ pisinaayi daa lab’ kuli; ka chɛ ninvuɣ’ tuhi’ pia kɔŋko.

english_verse: but if you're still afraid, you and your servant Purah should sneak down to their camp.
translation_verse: Amaa a yi zɔri dabiɛm ni a chaŋ, nyin’ zaŋm’ a tumtumda Pura pah’ amaŋ’ zuɣu chaŋ.

english_verse: “Gideon,” the Lord said, “you still have too many soldiers. Take them down to the spring and I'll test them. I'll tell you which ones can go along with you and which ones must go back home.”
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Gidiɔn, “niriba maa na kul galisiya. Zaŋm’ ba chaŋ kuliga ni ka n ti buɣisi ba nimaani ti a; ka n yi yɛl’ a ni so ni dol’ a chaŋ, dilana n-ni dol’ a chaŋ; ka m mi yi ti yɛl’ a ni so ku dol’ a chaŋ, dilan’ shiri ku dol’ a chaŋ”

english_verse: When Gideon led his army down to the spring, the Lord told him, “Watch how each man gets a drink of water. Then divide them into two groups—those who lap the water like a dog and those who kneel down to drink.”
translation_verse: Ka Gidiɔn daa zaŋ niriba maa chaŋ kuliga ni, ka Yawɛ ti yɛli Gidiɔn, “Ŋunkam mal’ o zilinli nyuri kom kaman baa la, nyin’ woligim’ o zal’ o ko; ka ŋunkam mi ti gban’ tiŋ’ nyura, nyin’ woligim’ o gba zal’ o ko.”

english_verse: Three hundred men scooped up water in their hands and lapped it, and the rest knelt to get a drink.
translation_verse: Ka ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn daa zaŋ bɛ nuhi tooi kom maa m-mali bɛ zilima nyur’ li kalinli daa yiɣisi kɔbisita, amaa ka bɛn kpalim la bɛn’ zaa daa gbanila tiŋ’ nyura.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Gideon, your army will be made up of everyone who lapped the water from their hands. Send the others home. I'm going to rescue Israel by helping you and your army of
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Gidiɔn, “Ninvuɣ’ kɔbisita shɛb’ bɛn mali bɛ zilima nyuri kom ŋɔ ka n ni zaŋ fan ya bahi, ka zaŋ Midiannim’ maa niŋ yi nuu ni. Dinzuɣu chɛ ka ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn kpalim maa zaa lab’ kuli.”

english_verse: That night, the Lord said to Gideon. “Get up! Attack the Midianite camp. I am going to let you defeat them,
translation_verse: Dindali maa yuŋ ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Gidiɔn, “Yiɣisim’ chaŋ ti liri Midiannim’ maa, dama n zaŋ ba niŋ a nuu ni.

english_verse: When you hear what the Midianites are saying, you'll be brave enough to attack.” Gideon and Purah worked their way to the edge of the enemy camp, where soldiers were on guard duty.
translation_verse: A ni ti wum bɛ ni yɛn yɛli shɛm. Ka di nyaaŋa a ni nya kpiɔŋ chaŋ ti liri ba.” Ka o min’ o tumtumda Pura daa chaŋ ti zani miri bɛ dimnim’ maa tɔbbi’ shɛb’ bɛn lo kpara do sansan’ maa tariga.

english_verse: The camp was huge. The Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations covered the valley like a swarm of locusts. And it would be easier to count the grains of sand on a beach than to count their camels.
translation_verse: Ka Midiannim’ mini Amalɛknim’ ni Wulimpuhili polo nim’ la zaa daa laɣim do vinvamli maa ni, ka bɛ galisim ŋmanila toli. Bɛ laakumnim’ daa ka kalinli; bɛ galisim daa ŋmanila teeku noli bihigu.

english_verse: Gideon overheard one enemy guard telling another, “I had a dream about a flat loaf of barley bread that came tumbling into our camp. It hit the headquarters tent, and the tent flipped over and fell to the ground.”
translation_verse: Gidiɔn ni daa mali ti paai nimaani saha shɛli, ka o wum ka Midiannim’ maa ni so yɛr’ o kpee o ni zahim zahindi shɛm. O daa yɛlimi, “Nyama, n zahimla zahindi nya ka bɔrɔbɔro kpilli bilim na ti kpe Midiannim’ sunsuuni n-kana ti kpe tanti shɛl’ ni ŋ-ŋme li, ka di lu n-lɛb’ pil’ tiŋa n-dɔni talisi tiŋ’ zaa.”

english_verse: The other soldier answered, “Your dream must have been about Gideon, the Israelite commander. It means God will let him and his army defeat the Midianite army and everyone else in our camp.”
translation_verse: Ka o kpee maa garigi yɛl’ o, “Dimbɔŋɔ nyɛla Jɔash bia Gidiɔn ŋun nyɛ Izraɛl nir’ la takɔbi. Naawuni pun zaŋ Midiannim’ mini bɛ tɔbbihi ŋɔ zaa niŋ o nuu ni.”

english_verse: As soon as Gideon heard about the dream and what it meant, he bowed down to praise God. Then he went back to the Israelite camp and shouted, “Let's go! The Lord is going to let us defeat the Midianite army.”
translation_verse: Gidiɔn ni daa wum doo maa zahindi maa mini di gbinni ni wuhi shɛm maa, ka o daa paɣi Naawuni pam, ka ŋmaligi lab’ Izraɛlnim’ sani ti yɛli ba, “Yiɣisimiya ka ti chaŋ, Yawɛ zaŋ Midiannim’ maa zaa niŋ yi nuu ni.”

english_verse: Gideon said, “When we get to the enemy camp, spread out and surround it. Then wait for me to blow a signal on my trumpet. As soon as you hear it, blow your trumpets and shout, ‘Fight for the Lord! Fight for Gideon!’ ”
translation_verse: M mini bɛn be n sani yi ti kul piɛb’ ti kikahi; yi gba yin’ piɛbimiya yi kikahi bɛ sansani maa luɣilikam zaa ka kuhi yɛli, “Tuhimiya ti Yawɛ mini Gidiɔn.”

english_verse: Gideon and his group reached the edge of the enemy camp a few hours after dark, just after the new guards had come on duty. Gideon and his soldiers blew their trumpets and smashed the clay jars that were hiding the torches.
translation_verse: Ka Gidiɔn mini ninvuɣ’ kɔbiga bɛn daa be o sani maa daa mali ti paai sansani maa shee yuntisuɣu saha tiŋguliba ni deeri tab’ tuma saha shɛli n-dii piɛb’ bɛ kikahi ka ŋme ŋ-ŋma bɛ ni gbib’ duɣubihi shɛŋa maa.

english_verse: The rest of Gideon's soldiers blew the trumpets they were holding in their right hands. Then they smashed the jars and held the burning torches in their left hands. Everyone shouted, “Fight with your swords for the Lord and for Gideon!”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ ninvuɣ’ kɔbisita maa zaa daa niŋ lala, ka chɛ bɛ firilanim’ gbib’ bɛ nuzahi ni, ka gbib’ kikahi mi bɛ nudiriti ni m-piɛbiri ka kuhiri yɛra, “Yawɛ mini Gidiɔn takɔbi!”

english_verse: The enemy soldiers started yelling and tried to run away. Gideon's troops stayed in their positions surrounding the camp
translation_verse: Ka Gidiɔn min’ o tɔbbihi maa zaa daa kul ba n-ʒe bɛ zaashɛhi ni gili Midiannim’ sansani maa, ka Midiannim’ maa daa kuhi ka yiɣisi guui.

english_verse: and blew their trumpets again. As they did, the Lord made the enemy soldiers pull out their swords and start fighting each other. The enemy army tried to escape from the camp. They ran to Acacia Tree Town, toward Zeredah, and as far as the edge of the land that belonged to the town of Abel-Meholah near Tabbath.
translation_verse: Gidiɔn min’ o tɔbbihi maa ni daa kul piɛb’ bɛ kikahi kɔbisita maa saha shɛli, ka Yawɛ daa chɛ ka bɛ dimnim’ maa zaŋ bɛ takɔbiri ŋmaligi lu tab’ zuɣu n-kari tab’ kpa Zɛrɛra polo m-mali hal ti paai Bɛtishita n-zaŋ hal ni Ɛbɛlimɛhola tintariga din baɣi Tabat la.

english_verse: Gideon sent word for more Israelite soldiers to come from the tribes of Naphtali, Asher, and both halves of Manasseh to help fight the Midianites.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa ŋme kuŋ’ boli Izraɛlnim’ zaa bɛn nyɛ Naftali mini Asha ni Manaasa zuliya niriba zaa, ka bɛ kana ti doli Midiannim’ maa.

english_verse: He also sent messengers to tell all the men who lived in the hill country of Ephraim, “Come and help us fight the Midianites! Put guards at every spring, stream, and well, as far as Beth-Barah before the Midianites can get to them. And guard the Jordan River.” Troops from Ephraim did exactly what Gideon had asked,
translation_verse: Ka Gidiɔn daa lan tim Ifriim tiŋgban’ ni zoya zuɣu tinsi ni ti boli niriba n-yɛli ba, “Kamiyana ti tuhi Midiannima. Chamiya ti gu ba kulibɔna ni hal ti paai Bɛtibara zaŋ hal ni Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili ni.” Ka Ifriim zuliya niriba zaa daa yina n-chaŋ ti gu kulibɔna maa ni hal ti paai Bɛtibara n-zaŋ hal ni Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili ni.

english_verse: and they even helped chase the Midianites on the east side of the Jordan River. These troops captured Raven and Wolf, the two Midianite leaders. They killed Raven at a large rock that has come to be known as Raven Rock, and they killed Wolf near a wine-pit that has come to be called Wolf Wine-Pit. The men of Ephraim brought the heads of the two Midianite leaders to Gideon.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa gbahi Midian nabih’ ayi. Bɛ yuya m-booni Orɛb mini Ziib. Ka bɛ daa ku Orɛb bɛ ni daa booni tampin’ shɛli Orɛb la gbini; ka daa ku Ziib mi Ziib wain tɔɣibo shee. Bɛ ni daa kariti doli Midiannim’ maa, ka bɛ daa ti zaŋ Orɛb mini Ziib zuɣuri na ti ti Gidiɔn Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili duli.

english_verse: But the men were really upset with Gideon and complained, “When you went to war with Midian, you didn't ask us to help! Why did you treat us like that?”
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Ifriim zuliya niriba daa kana ti bɔhi Gidiɔn, “Bɔ n-niŋ ka a daa yɛn chaŋ ti tuhi Midiannim’ ka bi bol’ ti? Bɔzuɣu ka a niŋ ti lala?” Ka bɛ daa galim’ o pam di zuɣu.

english_verse: Gideon answered: Don't be upset! Even though you came later, you were able to do much more than I did. It's just like the grape harvest: The grapes your tribe doesn't even bother to pick are better than the best grapes my family can grow.
translation_verse: Ka o daa yɛli ba, “N ku tooi zaŋ n ni tum shɛm buɣisi yi ni tum shɛm. Hal yinim’ Ifriim zuliya niriba ni tum biɛla shɛli maa gari tinim’ Abiɛza daŋ niriba ni tum shɛm zaa.

english_verse: Besides, God chose you to capture Raven and Wolf. I didn't do a thing compared to you. By the time Gideon had finished talking, the men of Ephraim had calmed down and were no longer angry with him. Gideon Finishes Destroying the Midianite Army
translation_verse: Naawuni daa zaŋ Midiannim’ nanim’ niŋ yi nuu ni. Bɛna n-nyɛ: Orɛb mini Ziib. Ka n ni tum shɛli lee nyɛla dini, ka n-ni tooi zaŋ li buɣisi yi dini?” Ka o ni daa yɛli shɛm ŋɔ zuɣu chɛ ka bɛ suhuyiɣisili zaŋ chaŋ o sani maa kpi.

english_verse: The town of Succoth was nearby, so he went there and asked, “Please give my troops some food. They are worn out, but we have to keep chasing Zebah and Zalmunna, the two Midianite kings.”
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka o daa yɛli Sukɔtinima, “N suhiri ya, niŋmiya bɔrɔbɔro ti n niriba bɛn doli ma ŋɔ; dama di wum ba pam, ka m mi na kariti dolila Midian nanim’ Zɛba mini Zalimuna.”

english_verse: The town leaders of Succoth answered, “Why should we feed your army? We don't know if you really will defeat Zebah and Zalmunna.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Sukɔt kpamba daa bɔh’ o, “A na bi gbahi Zɛba mini Zalimuna, ka bɔzuɣu ka ti lee yɛn ti a bindirigu?”

english_verse: “Just wait!” Gideon said. “After the Lord helps me defeat them, I'm coming back here. I'll make a whip out of thorns and rip the flesh from your bones.”
translation_verse: Ka Gidiɔn yɛli ba, “To, di pa taali! Amaa Yawɛ yi zaŋ Zɛba mini Zalimuna niŋ n nuu ni, n ni zaŋ ya pa mɔɣu ni gɔhi zuɣu n du n-tam yi zuɣu nɔn ya.”

english_verse: After leaving Succoth, Gideon went to Penuel and asked the leaders there for some food. But he got the same answer as he did at Succoth.
translation_verse: Ka Gidiɔn daa yi nimaani chaŋ Pɛnuɛl nti lan suhi bɛ gba bindirigu. Ka Pɛnuɛluɛlnim’ daa garigi yɛl’ o kaman Sukɔtinim’ ni daa yɛl’ o shɛm maa.

english_verse: “I'll come back safe and sound,” Gideon said, “but when I do, I'm going to tear down your tower!”
translation_verse: Ka o daa yɛli Pɛnuɛluɛlnim’ maa, “N yi ti labina ni alaafee, n ni daai yi pii ŋɔ luhi.”

english_verse: Gideon went to the town officials and said, “Here are Zebah and Zalmunna. Remember how you made fun of me? You said, ‘We don't know if you really will defeat those two Midianite kings. So why should we feed your worn-out army?’ ”
translation_verse: Ka Gidiɔn daa chaŋ Sukɔt ti yɛli ba, “N-nyɛ Zɛba mini Zalimuna. Yi daa mɔŋ m mini n tɔbbi’ shɛb’ di ni daa wum pam la bindirigu, ka maani ma ansarisi yɛra, ‘A na bi gbahi Zɛba mini Zalimuna n-kpɛh’ a nuu ni, ka bɔzuɣu ka ti lee yɛn ti a bindirigu?’ ”

english_verse: Gideon reached the enemy camp by going east along Nomad Road past Nobah and Jogbehah. He made a surprise attack,
translation_verse: Ka Gidiɔn daa baɣisi mɔɣu maa tariga zaŋ kpa Nɔba mini Jɔgbɛha wulimpuhili polo nti lu bɛ tɔbbihi maa zuɣu, dama tɔbbihi maa daa bi mali shili gu.

english_verse: and the enemy panicked. Zebah and Zalmunna tried to escape, but Gideon chased and captured them.
translation_verse: Ka Midian nanima ayi bɛn nyɛ: Zɛba mini Zalimuna daa guui, ka Gidiɔn kari doli ti gbahi ba, ka chɛ ka bɛ tɔbbihi zaa suhuri chihi.

english_verse: After the battle, Gideon set out for home. As he was going through Heres Pass,
translation_verse: Ka Jɔash bia Gidiɔn maa daa yi tɔb’ maa ni kuni ka zaŋ doli yi Hɛrɛs kunkuni polo.

english_verse: he caught a young man who lived in Succoth. Gideon asked him who the town officials of Succoth were, and the young man wrote down
translation_verse: Ka o daa gbaai Sukɔt nachimbil’ so m-bɔh’ o bɔhigu. Ka nachimbil’ maa daa kali Sukɔt kpamba pisopɔinnaayopɔin wuhi Gidiɔn.

english_verse: Gideon made a whip from thorn plants and used it to beat the town officials.
translation_verse: Ka o daa gbahi Sukɔt kpamba n-zaŋ ba pa mɔɣu ni gɔhi zuɣu n-du n-tam bɛ zuɣu n-no ba. O daa niŋla lala ni o wuhi Sukɔtinim’ maa yɛm.

english_verse: Afterwards he went to Penuel, where he tore down the tower and killed all the town officials.
translation_verse: Ka o daa lan daai Pɛnuɛluɛlnim’ pii la luhi, ka ku tiŋ’ maa ni dɔbba.

english_verse: Then Gideon said, “Zebah and Zalmunna, tell me about the men you killed at Tabor.” “They were a lot like you,” the two kings answered. “They were dignified, almost like royalty.”
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka Gidiɔn daa bɔhi Zɛba mini Zalimuna, “Ninvuɣ’ banim’ ka yi daa lee ku Tabo la?” Ka bɛ garigi yɛl’ o, “Bɛ zaa daa bela a ni be shɛm ŋɔ, bɛ daa ŋmanila nabihi.”

english_verse: “They were my very own brothers!” Gideon said. “I swear by the living Lord that if you had let them live, I would let you live.”
translation_verse: Ka Gidiɔn yɛli ba, “M mabihi n-daa bala. M mini ba zaa nyɛla ma pu’ yin’ ni bihi. Yawɛ zuɣu, yi yi di daa chɛ ba, n naan ku kun ya.”

english_verse: kilograms. In addition, there was the gold from the camels' ornaments and from the beautiful jewelry worn by the Midianite kings. Gideon also took their purple robes.
translation_verse: Di saha ka o daa ŋmaligi yɛl’ o bidib’ tuuli Jɛta, “Yiɣisim’ ku ba.” Amaa ka bia maa daa bi saɣi ŋ-ŋoog’ o takɔbi. O daa zɔrila dabiɛm, o ni daa na nyɛ bipolli la zuɣu.

english_verse: “What's the matter, Gideon?” Zebah and Zalmunna asked. “Do it yourself, if you're not too much of a coward!” Gideon jumped up and killed them both. Then he took the gold ornaments from the necks of their camels. The Israelites Ask Gideon To Be Their King
translation_verse: Ka Zɛba mini Zalimuna daa yɛli Gidiɔn, Amaŋmaŋ’ yiɣisim’ ku ti. Dama doo ni be shɛm lala n-nyɛ o kpiɔŋ gba!.” Ka Gidiɔn daa yiɣisi ku Zɛba mini Zalimuna, ka yihi bɛ laakumnim’ nyiŋgoya ni nachiinsi binyara.

english_verse: After the battle with the Midianites, the Israelites said, “Gideon, you rescued us! Now we want you to be our king. Then after your death, your son and then your grandson will rule.”
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka Izraɛlnim’ daa yɛli Gidiɔn, “Leemi ti naa su ti; ka a bidibiga min’ a nyaaŋa gba ti nyɛ ti nanim’ su ti, a ni fa ti Midiannim’ nuu ni bahi ŋɔ zuɣu.”

english_verse: “No,” Gideon replied, “I won't be your king, and my son won't be king either. Only the Lord is your ruler.
translation_verse: Ka Gidiɔn yɛli ba, “N ku leei yi naa; ka m bidibiga gba ku leei yi naa sun ya; Yawɛ n-nyɛ yi naa ŋun sun ya.”

english_verse: But I will ask you to do one thing: Give me all the earrings you took from the enemy.” The enemy soldiers had been Ishmaelites, and they wore gold earrings.
translation_verse: Amaa ka o daa lee yɛli ba, “Bin’ shɛli ka n naɣ’ bɔri ni n suhi ya, Yi zaa piim’ tibikpara yi ni ŋme n-di neen’ shɛŋa la ni ti ma.” .

english_verse: The Israelite soldiers replied, “Of course we will give you the earrings.” Then they spread out a robe on the ground and tossed the earrings on it.
translation_verse: Ka niriba maa garigi yɛli Gidiɔn, “Ti ni zaŋ li ti a ni ti suhuri zaa.” Ka bɛ daa teei binyɛrigu sɔŋ, ka sokam zaa zaŋd’ o ni ŋme n-di tibikpar’ shɛŋa na ti pari di zuɣu.

english_verse: He even had a wife who lived at Shechem. They had a son, and Gideon named him Abimelech.
translation_verse: Ka o mam ŋun daa be Shɛkɛm gba daa dɔɣ’ o bidib’ yino, ka o bol’ o yuli Abimilɛk.

english_verse: Gideon lived to be an old man. And when he died, he was buried in the family tomb in his hometown of Ophrah, which belonged to the Abiezer clan.
translation_verse: Ka Jɔash bia Gidiɔn maa daa mali hal ti kurigi ka naanyi kpi, ka bɛ daa zaŋ o sɔɣ’ o ba Jɔash siliga ni Abiɛza daŋ niriba ya Ofira.

english_verse: Soon after Gideon's death, the Israelites turned their backs on God again. They set up idols of Baal and worshiped Baal Berith as their god.
translation_verse: Gidiɔn kum nyaaŋa, di daa bi yuui ka Izraɛlnim’ lan ŋmaligi jɛmdila Baalnima. Bɛ daa zaŋla alikauli lɔbu Baal n-leei bɛ wuni.

english_verse: The Israelites forgot that the Lord was their God, and that he had rescued them from the enemies who lived around them.
translation_verse: Izraɛlnim’ daa tam Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ bɛ Naawuni ŋun daa tiligi ba bɛ dimnim’ bɛn gili bɛ luɣilikam zaa nuu ni la yɛla.

english_verse: Besides all that, the Israelites were unkind to Gideon's family, even though Gideon had done so much for Israel.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa bi lan ʒe Jɛrubaal malibu yim, o ni daa tum tuun’ sun’ shɛli ti Izraɛlnim’ la gba zuɣu.

english_verse: and told them to say to the leaders of Shechem, “Do you think it would be good to have all
translation_verse: “Bɔhimiya Shɛkɛmnim’ zaa, yi lee yuya ni Gidiɔn bidibisi pisopɔin la zaa n-sun ya bee yi paɣiya ni o bidib’ yino n-sun ya? Teemiya ni n nyɛla yimaŋmaŋ’ niŋgbuŋ ni yi ʒim.”

english_verse: Abimelech's uncles talked it over with the leaders of Shechem who agreed, “Yes, it would be better for one of our relatives to be king.”
translation_verse: Ka o mayilinim’ maa daa zan’ o zaani n-zaŋ o yɛtɔɣa tɔɣisi Shɛkɛmnim’ zaa ti o, ka Shɛkɛmnim’ maa daa wuhi ni bɛ ni doli Abimilɛk, dama ni o nyɛla bɛ mabia.

english_verse: Abimelech and his soldiers went to his father's home in Ophrah and brought out Gideon's other sons to a large rock, where they murdered all
translation_verse: Ka o daa chaŋ o ba yiŋ’ Ofira nti ku o ba bihi ninvuɣ’ pisopɔin bɛn nyɛ Gidiɔn bidibisi la tampin’ yini zuɣu. Amaa ka Jɔtam ŋun daa nyɛ Gidiɔn kaluɣ’ la ŋun’ daa sɔɣi, ka bɛ bi nya o ku o.

english_verse: The leaders of Shechem, including the priests and the military officers, met at the tree next to the sacred rock in Shechem to crown Abimelech king.
translation_verse: Ka Shɛkɛmnim’ mini Bɛtimilɔnim’ zaa daa laɣim chaŋ Shɛkɛm oki tia din nyɛ bɛ tiŋgban’ la gbini nti leei Abimilɛk nam.

english_verse: Jotham heard what they were doing. So he climbed to the top of Mount Gerizim and shouted down to the people who were there at the meeting: Leaders of Shechem, listen to me, and maybe God will listen to you.
translation_verse: Jɔtam ni daa wum li, ka o chaŋ ti du n-tam Gɛrizim Zoli zuɣu n-kuhi yɛli ba, “Yinim’ Shɛkɛmnima, wummiya n ni yɛn yɛli ya shɛm ŋɔ, ka Naawuni wum yi gba ni yɛn yɛli shɛm!

english_verse: Once the trees searched for someone to be king; they asked the olive tree, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Dahin shɛli ka tihi daa laɣim ni bɛ bɔ ŋun yɛn nyɛ bɛ naa. Ka bɛ daa yɛli Olivi tia, ‘Ti bɔri ni nyini n-leei ti naa.’

english_verse: But the olive tree replied, “My oil brings honor to people and gods. I won't stop making oil, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Olivi tia bɔhi ba, ‘N chɛli bɛ ni mali ma doori kpa’ shɛli ka di tiri wuna mini ninsalinim’ jilima la tuma ka leei tihi naa?’

english_verse: Then they asked the fig tree, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Ka tihi maa daa chɛ ka yɛli fiig tia, ‘Ti bɔri ni nyini n-leei ti naa.’

english_verse: But the fig tree replied, “I won't stop growing my delicious fruit, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Ka fiig tia bɔhi ba, ‘N chɛli n wal’ viɛla din nyaɣisi la wolibu, ka leei tihi naa?’

english_verse: Next they asked the grape vine, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Ka tihi maa daa chɛ ka ŋmaligi yɛli wain tia, ‘Ti bɔri ni nyini n-leei ti naa.’

english_verse: But the grape vine replied, “My wine brings cheer to people and gods. I won't stop making wine, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka wain tia maa bɔhi ba, ‘N chɛli n wain shɛli din tiri wuna mini ninsalinim’ suhupiɛlli la tɔɣibu, ka leei tihi naa?’

english_verse: Finally, they went to the thornbush and asked, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Di saha ka tihi maa zaa daa chaŋ ti yɛli tanyibiga, ‘Ti bɔri ni nyini n-leei ti naa.’

english_verse: The thornbush replied, “If you really want me to be your king, then come into my shade and I will protect you. But if you're deceiving me, I'll start a fire that will spread out and destroy the cedars of Lebanon.” After Jotham had finished telling this story, he said:
translation_verse: Ka tanyibiga yɛli ba, ‘Yi yi shiri bɔri ni n leei yi naa ni yɛlimaŋli, yin’ kamiyana ti ʒini m mahim, ka yi yi ku niŋ lala, dindina, n ni chɛ ka buɣim yi n ni na ti di Lɛbanɔn sida tihi’.

english_verse: My father Gideon risked his life for you when he fought to rescue you from the Midianites. Did you reward Gideon by being kind to his family? No, you did not! You attacked his family and killed all
translation_verse: Amaa ka yi ti yiɣisi zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ n-lu m ba malibu zuɣu n-zaŋ o bidibisi pisopɔin pa tampin yini zuɣu ku ba; ka zaŋ Abimilɛk ŋun nyɛ o dab’ paɣ’ bia la leei yi naa ni o su Shɛkɛmnima o ni nyɛ yi dɔɣira la zuɣu.

english_verse: So, you leaders of Shechem, if you treated Gideon and his family the way you should have, then I hope you and Abimelech will make each other very happy.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu yi ni niŋ shɛm zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ yi nyɛla din tuhi ni jilima ka yi ti Gidiɔn min’ o malibu maa, yin’ maliya suhupiɛlli zaŋ chaŋ Abimilɛk sani, ka o gba mali suhupiɛlli zaŋ chaŋ yi sani.

english_verse: But if it was wrong to treat Gideon and his family the way you did, then I pray that Abimelech will destroy you with fire, and I pray that you will do the same to him.
translation_verse: Amaa di yi pa lala, buɣim din yim’ Abimilɛk ni na ti di yinim’ Shɛkɛmnim’ mini Bɛtimilɔnima; ka chɛ ka buɣim yi yinim’ Shɛkɛmnim’ mini Bɛtimilɔnim’ gba ni na ti di Abimilɛk.”

english_verse: Jotham ran off and went to live in the town of Beer, where he could be safe from his brother Abimelech. Abimelech Destroys Shechem
translation_verse: Ka Jɔtam daa zo n-kuli Bɛr nti be nimaani, dama o daa zɔrila o biɛli Abimilɛk.

english_verse: Abimelech had been a military commander of Israel for three years,
translation_verse: Ka Abimilɛk daa di nam maa su Izraɛlnim’ yuma ata.

english_verse: Then they sent some men to hide on the hilltops and watch for Abimelech and his troops, while they sent others to rob everyone that went by on the road. But Abimelech found out what they were doing.
translation_verse: Ka Shɛkɛmnim’ daa bo niriba n-chɛ ka bɛ chaŋ ti sɔɣi do zoya zuɣu gu Abimilɛk, ka daa kul fari bɛnkam zaa doli nimaani gariti nɛma. Ka bɛ daa yɛli Abimilɛk di yɛla.

english_verse: One day, Gaal son of Ebed went to live in Shechem. His brothers moved there too, and soon the leaders of Shechem started trusting him.
translation_verse: Ka Ɛbɛd bia Gaal min’ o mabihi daa ti ka Shɛkɛm na, Ka Shɛkɛmnim’ daa niŋ o naani.

english_verse: The time came for the grape harvest, and the people of Shechem went into their vineyards and picked the grapes. They gathered the grapes and made wine. Then they went into the temple of their god and threw a big party. There was a lot of eating and drinking, and before long they were cursing Abimelech.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ zaa daa chaŋ bɛ wain puri ni ti pihi wain wala na nti kahim di kom niŋ wain n-zaŋ li chaŋ bɛ wuni jɛmbu duu ti puhi chuɣu nimaani, ka diri ka nyura, ka turi Abimilɛk.

english_verse: Gaal said: Hamor was the founder of Shechem, and one of his descendants should be our ruler. But Abimelech's father was Gideon, so Abimelech isn't really one of us. He shouldn't be our king, and we shouldn't have to obey him or Zebul, who rules Shechem for him.
translation_verse: Ka Ɛbɛd bia Gaal maa daa yɛli, “Ŋuni n-lee nyɛ Abimilɛk, ka tinim’ Shɛkɛmnim’ ti jɛmd’ o? Gidiɔn bia mini Zɛbul ŋun nyɛ o sapashin’ kpɛm’ la daa bi jɛmdila Hamɔr ŋun daa nyɛ Shɛkɛmnim’ yab’ la niriba? Ka bɔzuɣu ka ti yɛn jɛm’ o?

english_verse: If I were the ruler of Shechem, I'd get rid of that Abimelech. I'd tell him, “Get yourself an even bigger army, and we will still defeat you.”
translation_verse: Mani n-yi di nyɛ niriba ŋɔ toondana, n naan kpimsi Abimilɛk birili zaa. N naan yɛl’ o, ‘Bom’ tɔbbihi pam pahi kana.’ ”

english_verse: This is what I think you should do. Lead your army here during the night and hide in the fields.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ zaŋm’ a niriba yi yuŋ chaŋ mɔɣu ni nti sɔɣ’ dɔni gu ba.

english_verse: Get up the next morning at sunrise and rush out of your hiding places to attack the town. Gaal and his followers will come out to fight you, but you will easily defeat them.
translation_verse: Ka biɛɣuni asiba, wuntaŋ’ yi sa kul puhi na, yin’ kamiyana ti liri ba tiŋ’ maa ni. Gaal min’ o niriba maa yi sa yina ni yi mini ba zaŋ nya taba, yin’ niŋmiya ba yi ni bɔri shɛm.”

english_verse: So one night, Abimelech led his soldiers to Shechem. He divided them into four groups, and they all hid near the town.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Abimilɛk min’ o niriba daa yiɣisi yuŋ chaŋ ti piri tab’ ʒii bunahi zuɣu n-dɔni gili Shɛkɛm.

english_verse: The next morning, Gaal went out and stood in the opening of the town gate. Abimelech and his soldiers left their hiding places,
translation_verse: Ka Ɛbɛd bia Gaal maa daa ti yina ti zani tiŋ’ maa gooni dunol’ ni, ka Abimilɛk min’ o niriba maa yiɣisi bɛ sɔɣibu shee maa yina.

english_verse: and Gaal saw them. Zebul was standing there with Gaal, and Gaal remarked, “Zebul, that looks like a crowd of people coming down from the mountaintops.” “No,” Zebul answered, “it's just the shadows of the mountains. It only looks like people moving.”
translation_verse: Gaal ni daa nya niriba maa, ka o ŋmaligi yɛli Zɛbul, “Nyama, niriba n-yiri zoya ŋɔ zuɣu sigirina!” Ka Zɛbul garigi yɛl’ o, “Pa niriba m-bala. Zoya maa shilinshihi ka a nya ka di ŋmani ninsalinim’ maa.”

english_verse: “But Zebul, look over there,” Gaal said. “There's a crowd coming down from the sacred mountain, and another group is coming along the road from the tree where people talk with the spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Ka Gaal lan yɛl’ o yaha, “Nyama, niriba n-yi zoya maa sunsuuni siɣirina ŋɔ, ka shɛb’ mi yi baɣisi oki tia la polo kanna.”

english_verse: Then Zebul replied, “What good is all of your bragging now? You were the one who said Abimelech shouldn't be the ruler of Shechem. Out there is the army that you made fun of. So go out and fight them!”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Zɛbul bɔh’ o, “Ka a noli buɣibuɣi la lee be ya pumpɔŋɔ? Pa nyini n-daa yɛli ni Abimilɛk mi lee nyɛ ŋuni ka ti jɛmd’ o la? Pa bɛna ka a daa ʒiɛm la? To, pumpɔŋɔ cham’ ka a mini ba ti tuhi.”

english_verse: Gaal and the leaders of Shechem went out and fought Abimelech.
translation_verse: Ka Gaal daa gari tooni zaŋ Shɛkɛmnim’ chaŋ, ka bɛ mini Abimilɛk ti tuhi.

english_verse: Soon the people of Shechem turned and ran back into the town. However, Abimelech and his troops were close behind and killed many of them along the way.
translation_verse: Ka Gaal daa ti ŋmaligi guui, ka Abimilɛk kari dol’ o. Ka niriba pam daa nya dansi zaŋ lala hal ti paai tiŋ’ maa gooni dunoli shee.

english_verse: Abimelech stayed at Arumah, and Zebul forced Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem.
translation_verse: Abimilɛk daa bela Aruma, ka Zɛbul daa kari Gaal min’ o dɔɣiriba maa ti bahi ka bɛ ku tooi lan be Shɛkɛm.

english_verse: The next morning, the people of Shechem were getting ready to work in their fields as usual, but someone told Abimelech about it.
translation_verse: N-yi biɛɣu ka Shɛkɛmnim’ daa lo tɔbu chaŋ ti do mɔɣu ni, ka bɛ daa yɛli Abimilɛk di yɛla.

english_verse: Abimelech divided his army into three groups and set up an ambush in the fields near Shechem. When the people came out of the town, he and his army rushed out from their hiding places and attacked.
translation_verse: Ka o daa pir’ o tɔbbihi ʒii buta zuɣu n-zaŋ ba chaŋ mɔɣu maa ni ti sɔɣi do n-gu ba. Ka Abimilɛk daa ti lihi nya ba ka bɛ yi tiŋ’ maa ni kanna, ka o yiɣisi lu bɛ zuɣu ku ba.

english_verse: Abimelech and the troops with him ran to the town gate and took control of it, while two other groups attacked and killed the people who were in the fields.
translation_verse: Abimilɛk min’ o tɔbbihi pirigili yim bɛn daa be o sani daa kab’ chaŋ ti zanila tiŋ’ maa gooni dunol’ ni, ka bɛ pirigili ʒii buyi mi kab’ ti lu bɛn be mɔɣu ni maa zuɣu n-ku bɛ zaa.

english_verse: He and his troops fought in Shechem all day, until they had killed everyone in town. Then he and his men tore down the houses and buildings and scattered salt everywhere.
translation_verse: Ka Abimilɛk daa tuhi bɛn be tiŋ’ maa puuni hal ti luhi wuntaŋa n-daa ŋme n-deei tiŋ’ maa, ka ku niriba bɛn be di ni, ka niŋ yalim bahi tiŋ’ maa tiŋgbani zaa zuɣu.

english_verse: Earlier that day, the leaders of the temple of El Berith at Shechem had heard about the attack. So they went into the temple fortress,
translation_verse: Ka Shɛkɛm zuɣulaannim’ zaa bɛn daa be pii la ni wum lala, ka zo nti kpe Ɛlibɛrit jɛmbu duu ti sɔɣi.

english_verse: He led his troops to Mount Zalmon, where he took an ax and chopped off a tree branch. He lifted the branch onto his shoulder and shouted, “Hurry! Cut off a branch just as I did.”
translation_verse: Ka Abimilɛk min’ o tɔbbihi zaa daa chaŋ ti du Zalimɔn Zoli zuɣu, ka Abimilɛk ti zaŋ lɛhu ŋ-ŋma dabɔbili n-zaŋ li buɣi; ka yɛli bɛn be o sani, “Yi ni nya ka n niŋ shɛm maa, yi gba niŋmiya lala yomyom.”

english_verse: When they all had branches, they followed Abimelech back to Shechem. They piled the branches against the fortress and set them on fire, burning down the fortress and killing about
translation_verse: Di saha ka sokam daa ŋmah’ o dabɔbili n-zaŋ li doli Abimilɛk ti sɔŋ baɣili bɛ sɔɣisili shee maa n-niŋ buɣim nyo li pa bɛ zuɣu, ka ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn zaa daa be di ni kpi. Bɛ kalinli daa nyɛla kaman dɔbba mini paɣiba tuhili.

english_verse: After destroying Shechem, Abimelech went to Thebez. He surrounded the town and captured it.
translation_verse: Ka Abimilɛk daa chaŋ Tɛbiz ti teei gil’ li ŋ-ŋme n-deei li.

english_verse: But there was a tall fortress in the middle of the town, and the town leaders and everyone else went inside. Then they barred the gates and went up to the flat roof.
translation_verse: Amaa ka pii din mali kpiɔŋ daa be tiŋ’ maa ni, ka dɔbba mini paɣiba zaa ni tiŋ’ maa ni nanim’ zaa daa zo nti kpe di ni, ka yo di dunoli n-kpari bɛmaŋ’ niŋ di ni. Ka du pii maa kpaakpaanyom ni ha ti beni.

english_verse: Abimelech and his army rushed to the fortress and tried to force their way inside. Abimelech himself was about to set the heavy wooden doors on fire,
translation_verse: Ka Abimilɛk daa ka pii maa gbinna ni o ti tuhi ba, ka chaŋ ti miri di dunol’ ni ni o niŋ buɣim nyo li.

english_verse: when a woman on the roof dropped a large rock on his head and cracked his skull.
translation_verse: Amaa ka paɣ’ so daa kpuɣ’ nɛkaŋa n-daai li bah’ o zuɣu ni na, ka di ŋma o zuɣuŋmaŋ.

english_verse: The soldier who carried his weapons was nearby, and Abimelech told him, “Take out your sword and kill me. I don't want people to say that I was killed by a woman!” So the soldier ran his sword through Abimelech.
translation_verse: Ka o daa kuhi boli nachimbil’ so ŋun nyɛ o gbaɣino ʒira yomyom yɛl’ o, “Ŋoom’ a takɔbi kuhi ku ma, di yi pa lala, niriba ni yɛli ni paɣa n-ku ma.” Ka o nachimbil’ maa daa shiri zaŋ o takɔbi kuh’ o, ka o kpi.

english_verse: And when the Israelite soldiers saw that their leader was dead, they went back home.
translation_verse: Izraɛlnim’ ni daa nya ka Abimilɛk kpi maa, ka bɛ zaa ŋmaligi kuli bɛ yinsi.

english_verse: That's how God punished Abimelech for killing his brothers and bringing shame on his father's family.
translation_verse: Lala ka Naawuni daa niŋ darigi Abimilɛk tibili o ni daa tum o ba tuumbiɛ’ shɛli din nyɛ o ni daa ku omaŋmaŋ’ ba bidibisi pisopɔin la zuɣu.

english_verse: God also punished the people of Shechem for helping Abimelech. Everything happened just as Jotham's curse said it would.
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa lan chɛ ka Shɛkɛmnim’ gba nya bɛ ninvuɣ’ biɛtali tibidarigibo kaman Gidiɔn bia Jɔtan la ni daa pun yɛli noli ti ba wuhi ni di ni niŋ ba shɛm la.

english_verse: Tola was the next person to rescue Israel. He belonged to the Issachar tribe, but he lived in Shamir, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His father was Puah, and his grandfather was Dodo.
translation_verse: Abimilɛk kum nyaaŋa ka ninvuɣ’ so ŋun daa yɛn fa Izraɛlnim’ bahi yi palo. Lala nir’ maa n-daa nyɛ Pua bia Tola ŋun daa nyɛ Dɔdo yaaŋa la. O daa yila Isaka zuliya ni na, ka be Shamir din be Ifriim tiŋgban’ ni zoya zuɣu la.

english_verse: The next leader of Israel was Jair, who lived in Gilead. He was a leader for
translation_verse: Tola kum nyaaŋa, ka Jair ŋun daa nyɛ Giliad nir’ la gba daa leei Izraɛlnim’ sariakarita yuun’ pisinaayi.

english_verse: When he died, he was buried in the town of Kamon. Israel Is Unfaithful to God
translation_verse: Ka Jair daa ti kpi ka bɛ sɔɣ’ o Kamɔn. Jɛfita yɛla

english_verse: Before long, the Israelites began disobeying the Lord by worshiping Baal, Astarte, and gods from Syria, Sidon, Moab, Ammon, and Philistia.
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka Izraɛlnim’ daa lan tum alahichi Yawɛ sani. Bɛ daa lan ŋmaligi jɛmdila Baal mini Ashitarɔt din nyɛ Sirianim’ mini Sidɔnnim’ ni Mɔabnim’ ni Ammɔnnim’ ni Filistianim’ buɣa la, ka zaɣisi Yawɛ, ka chɛ o jɛmbu.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel and decided to let Philistia and Ammon conquer them.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ suhu daa yiɣisi pam bahi bɛ zuɣu, ka o chɛ ka Filistianim’ mini Ammɔnnim’ kana ti tuhi nyaŋ ba.

english_verse: The leaders of Gilead asked each other, “Who can lead an attack on the Ammonites?” Then they agreed, “If we find someone who can lead the attack, we'll make him the ruler of Gilead.”
translation_verse: Ka Giliad sapashinnim’ daa bɔhi taba, “Ka ŋuni n-lee nyɛ ŋun ni chaŋ ti piligi Ammɔnnim’ ŋɔ tuhibu? Dilan’ ni leei Giliadnim’ zaa zuɣulana.”

english_verse: Then the Ammonites began crossing the Jordan and attacking the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim. Life was miserable for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ka Ammɔnnim’ daa ti gbaai Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili du ni bɛ ti tuhi Juda zuliya niriba mini Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba ni Ifriim zuliya niriba, ka di zuɣu chɛ ka nandahima daa mal’ Izraɛlnim’ pam.

english_verse: They begged the Lord for help and confessed, “We were unfaithful to you, our Lord. We stopped worshiping you and started worshiping idols of Baal.”
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa kum niŋ Yawɛ yɛli, “Ti tum alahichi a sani, dama ti chɛ nyini ŋun nyɛ ti Naawuni ŋɔ jɛmbu, ka jɛmdila buɣa Baalnima.”

english_verse: The Lord answered: In the past when you came crying to me for help, I rescued you. At one time or another I've rescued you from the Egyptians, the Amorites, the Ammonites, the Philistines, the Sidonians, the Amalekites, and the Maonites.
translation_verse: ni Sidɔnnim’ ni Amalɛknim’ ni Maɔnim’ ni daa nahindi ya, ka yi kum niŋ ma la, n daa bi fan ya bɛ nuu ni bahi?

english_verse: But I'm not going to rescue you any more! You've left me and gone off to worship other gods. If you're in such big trouble, go and cry to them for help!
translation_verse: Chamiya ti kum niŋ yi ni pii buɣ’ shɛŋa jɛmdi maa, ka bɛ fan ya bahi yi muɣisigu ŋɔ saha.”

english_verse: “We have been unfaithful to you,” the Israelites admitted. “If we must be punished, do it yourself, but please rescue us from the Ammonites.”
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa yɛli Naawuni, “Ti tum alahichi, amaa ti suhir’ a zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ, fam’ ti bahi; ka niŋ ti a ni bɔri ni a niŋ ti shɛm.”

english_verse: Then the Israelites got rid of the idols of the foreign gods, and they began worshiping only the Lord. Finally, there came a time when the Lord could no longer stand to see them suffer. The Ammonites Invade Gilead
translation_verse: Di saha ka bɛ daa yihi tinzun buɣa maa bɛ kɔbili ni, ka ŋmaligi jɛmdi Yawɛ, ka Izraɛlnim’ nandahima yɛlli maa daa muɣis’ o pam.

english_verse: The rulers of Ammon called their soldiers together and led them to Gilead, where they set up camp. The Israelites gathered at Mizpah and set up camp there.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Ammɔnnim’ tɔbbihi daa lo tɔbu kana ti do Giliad. Ka Izraɛlnim’ gba daa laɣim ti do Mizipa.

english_verse: “Please come back to Gilead! If you lead our army, we will be able to fight off the Ammonites.”
translation_verse: Bɛ daa yɛlila Jɛfita, “Kamina ti leei ti zuɣulana n-zaŋ ti chaŋ ka ti ti tuhi Ammɔnnima.”

english_verse: “Didn't you hate me?” Jephthah replied. “Weren't you the ones who forced me to leave my family? You're only coming to me now because you're in trouble.”
translation_verse: Ka Jɛfita daa bɔhi Giliad kpamba maa, “Pa yinima n-daa je ma hal ka kari ma m ba yiŋ’ la? Ka di chaŋ wula ka yi ti kani n sanna yi wahala nyabu saha?”

english_verse: “But we do want you to come back,” the leaders said. “And if you lead us in battle against the Ammonites, we will make you the ruler of Gilead.”
translation_verse: Ka Giliad kpamba maa yɛli Jɛfita, “Di zuɣu n-chɛ ka ti ka a sanna pumpɔŋɔ maa. Ti bɔrimi ni a kana ti pahi ti zuɣu ka ti chaŋ ti tuhi Ammɔnnima, ka a leei Giliadnim’ zaa zuɣulana.”

english_verse: “All right,” Jephthah said. “If I go back with you and the Lord lets me defeat the Ammonites, will you really make me your ruler?”
translation_verse: Ka Jɛfita lan bɔhi Giliad kpamba maa, “Yi yi zaŋ ma kuli ka ti ti tuhi Ammɔnnima, ka Yawɛ chɛ ka n nyaŋ ba, yi ni saɣi ka n leei yi zuɣulana?”

english_verse: “You have our word,” the leaders answered. “And the Lord is a witness to what we have said.”
translation_verse: Ka Giliad kpamba maa garigi yɛli Jɛfita, “Yɛlimaŋli, ti ni niŋ kaman a ni yɛli shɛm maa, hal Yawɛ n-nyɛ ti min’ a zaa shɛhiralana.”
