english_verse: So Jephthah went back to Mizpah with the leaders of Gilead. The people of Gilead gathered at the place of worship and made Jephthah their ruler. Jephthah also made promises to them.
translation_verse: Ka Jɛfita daa yiɣisi doli Giliad kpamba maa kuli, ka Giliadnim’ ti zaŋ o leei bɛ zuɣulana ni bɛ sapashin’ kpɛma. Ka Jɛfita daa tɔɣis’ o yɛtɔɣa ni nyɛ shɛm zaa Yawɛ sani Mizipa.

english_verse: After the ceremony, Jephthah sent messengers to say to the king of Ammon, “Are you trying to start a war? You have invaded my country, and I want to know why!”
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Jɛfita daa tim tuumba Ammɔnnim’ naa sani ti bɔh’ o, “Taal’ bɔ n-lee be m min’ a sunsuuni, ka a ti kana ni a ti tuhi ma n tiŋgbani zuɣu?”

english_verse: The king of Ammon replied, “Tell Jephthah that the land really belongs to me, all the way from the Arnon River in the south, to the Jabbok River in the north, and west to the Jordan River. When the Israelites came out of Egypt, they stole it. Tell Jephthah to return it to me, and there won't be any war.”
translation_verse: Ka Ammɔn naa daa garigi yɛli Jɛfita tuumba maa, “Izraɛlnim’ ni daa yi Ijipti na saha shɛl’ la ka bɛ daa fa n tiŋgbani, Arinɔn Mɔɣili noli zaŋ ti kpa Jabok Mɔɣili noli m-mali lala hal ti paai Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili noli, dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ labisimiya ti tiŋgbani maa ti ti ka di maha.”

english_verse: Jephthah sent the messengers back to the king of Ammon,
translation_verse: Ka Jɛfita daa lan tim tuumba Ammɔn naa maa sani, ka bɛ chaŋ ti yɛl’ o,

english_verse: and they told him that Jephthah had said: Israel hasn't taken any territory from Moab or Ammon.
translation_verse: “Jɛfita ni yɛli shɛm m-bɔŋɔ: Izraɛlnim’ daa bi fa Mɔabnim’ tiŋgbani bee Ammɔnnim’ tiŋgbani.

english_verse: When the Israelites came from Egypt, they traveled across the desert to the Red Sea and then to Kadesh.
translation_verse: Amaa Izraɛlnim’ ni daa yi Ijipti maa na, bɛ daa kpɛla yɔɣu ni chaŋ na hal ti paai Teeku Ʒiɛɣu n-gbaai li du n-ka Kadɛshi na.

english_verse: They sent messengers to the king of Edom and said, “Please, let us go through your country.” But the king of Edom refused. They also sent messengers to the king of Moab, but he wouldn't let them cross his country either. And so the Israelites stayed at Kadesh.
translation_verse: Di saha maa ka Izraɛlnim’ daa tim tuumba Ɛdom naa sani ti yɛl’ o, ‘Ti suhir’ a, chɛ ka ti kpe a tiŋgbani ŋɔ ni gari;’ amaa ka Ɛdom naa maa daa zaɣisi. Ka bɛ daa lan tim ti yɛli Mɔab naa lala, ka o gba zaɣisi. Dinzuɣu ka Izraɛlnim’ daa kpalim be Kadɛshi.

english_verse: A little later, the Israelites set out into the desert, going east of Edom and Moab, and camping on the eastern side of the Arnon River gorge. The Arnon is the eastern border of Moab, and since the Israelites didn't cross it, they didn't even set foot in Moab.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa ti yiɣisi tim yɔɣu maa ni chani gindi Ɛdomnim’ mini Mɔabnim’ tiŋgbana ni n-daa mali hal ti paai Mɔabnim’ tiŋgbani wulimpuhili polo n-zaŋ bɛ tantinim’ kpa Arinɔn Mɔɣili noli, amaa bɛ daa bi saɣi kpe Mɔabnim’ tiŋgban’ ni, dama Arinɔn Mɔɣili vulo maa n-daa nyɛ Mɔabnim’ tiŋgbani tariga.

english_verse: The Israelites sent messengers to the Amorite King Sihon of Heshbon. “Please,” they said, “let our people go through your country to get to our own land.”
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa lan tim tuumba Amɔrinim’ Naa Sihɔn ŋun daa nyɛ Hɛshibɔn naa la sani ti yɛl’ o, ‘Ti suhir’ a, chɛ ka ti kpe a tiŋgbani ŋɔ ni gari kuli ti ya.’

english_verse: towns between Aroer and Minnith, and others as far as Abel-Keramim. After that, the Ammonites could not invade Israel any more. Jephthah's Daughter
translation_verse: Amaa ka Naa Sihɔn daa bi saɣi ni Izraɛlnim’ kpe o tiŋgbani maa ni gari, ka daa laɣim o tɔbbihi na ti dɔni Jahaz n-tuhi Izraɛlnima.

english_verse: But the Lord God helped Israel defeat Sihon and his army. Israel took over all of the Amorite land where Sihon's people had lived,
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Izraɛl Naawuni ŋɔ daa zaŋ Naa Sihɔn min’ o tɔbbihi maa zaa niŋ Izraɛlnim’ nuu ni, ka bɛ nyaŋ ba. Dina n-chɛ ka Izraɛlnim’ daa deei Amɔrinim’ ni daa be tiŋgban’ shɛl’ ni maa zaa su.

english_verse: from the Arnon River in the south to the Jabbok River in the north, and from the desert in the east to the Jordan River in the west.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa ʒini Amɔrinim’ tiŋgbani maa ni hal ni di tintariga Arinɔn Mɔɣili noli shee la zaŋ hal ti paai Jabok n-yi di yɔɣu maa ni m-mali hal ti paai Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili ni.

english_verse: The messengers also told the king of Ammon that Jephthah had said: The Lord God of Israel helped his nation get rid of the Amorites and take their land. Now do you think you're going to take over that same territory?
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni ŋɔ n-daa fa Amɔrinim’ tiŋgbani maa ti Izraɛlnima, ka a ti bɔri ni a fa li?

english_verse: If Chemosh your god takes over a country and gives it to you, don't you have a right to it? And if the Lord takes over a country and gives it to us, the land is ours!
translation_verse: A ku chɛ ka sula a wuni Chɛmɔshi ni zaŋ tiŋgban’ shɛli ti a ni a su la? Ka Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ ti Naawuni ŋɔ ni zaŋ tiŋgban’ shɛŋa zaa ti ti la, ka ti mi su li.

english_verse: Are you better than Balak the son of Zippor? He was the king of Moab, but he didn't quarrel with Israel or start a war with us.
translation_verse: Ka bee a tɛhiya ni a gari la Mɔab Naa Balak Zipɔr bia la? O daa ŋme Izraɛlnim’ naŋgbankpeeni bee n-lo tɔbu ni o tuhi ba?

english_verse: I haven't done anything to you, but it's certainly wrong of you to start a war. I pray that the Lord will show whether Israel or Ammon is in the right.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu m bi tum a taal’ shɛli, amaa nyini n-lee tum ma taali a ni lo tɔbu na ni a ti tuhi ma maa zuɣu. Ka Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ sariakarita ŋɔ ni woligi yɛlimaŋli ti Izraɛlnim’ mini Ammɔnnim’ zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ.”

english_verse: But the king of Ammon paid no attention to Jephthah's message.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Ammɔn naa maa daa zaɣisi ni o ku wum Jɛfita ni tim na ti yɛl’ o shɛm maa.

english_verse: Then the Lord's Spirit took control of Jephthah, and Jephthah went through Gilead and Manasseh, raising an army. Finally, he arrived at Mizpah in Gilead, where
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yawɛ Shia daa siɣi Jɛfita zuɣu na. Ka o daa yiɣisi chaŋ ti tim Giliad mini Manaasa tiŋgbana ni n-gari chaŋ Mizipa din be Giliad tiŋgban’ ni la n-daa yi Mizipa din be Giliad tiŋgban’ ni maa gari chaŋ Ammɔnnim’ tiŋgban’ ni.

english_verse: he promised the Lord, “If you will let me defeat the Ammonites
translation_verse: Ka Jɛfita daa po pɔri n-lo Yawɛ alikauli yɛli, “A yi ni zaŋ Ammɔnnim’ maa niŋ n nuu ni,

english_verse: From Mizpah, Jephthah attacked the Ammonites, and the Lord helped him defeat them.
translation_verse: Ka Jɛfita daa gbaai mɔɣili du ni o ti tuhi Ammɔnnima, ka Yawɛ daa shiri zaŋ ba niŋ o nuu ni.

english_verse: When Jephthah returned to his home in Mizpah, the first one to meet him was his daughter. She was playing a tambourine and dancing to celebrate his victory, and she was his only child.
translation_verse: Jɛfita ni daa ti labiri kuni yiŋ’ na Mizipa, o bipuɣiŋga n-daa daŋ o soli tuhibu na n-gbib’ chaɣisa chaɣisiri ka wari waa. O kɔŋko mi n-daa kul nyɛ o bia. O daa lan ka bidibiga bee bipuɣiŋga pah’ o zuɣu.

english_verse: “Oh no!” Jephthah cried. Then he tore his clothes in sorrow and said to his daughter, “I made a sacred promise to the Lord, and I must keep it. Your coming out to meet me has broken my heart.”
translation_verse: Ka Jɛfita nin’ ni daa kul nya o bia maa, o dii darigimi cheeg’ omaŋmaŋ’ binyɛrigu ka kuhi yɛli, “Mbaye, m bia! A chɛ ka n suhu saɣim. A leei ŋun ti ma nandahima; dama m pun yaai n noli lo Yawɛ alikauli, ka ku tooi lan yi di nyaaŋa.”

english_verse: “Father,” she said, “you made a sacred promise to the Lord, and he let you defeat the Ammonites. Now, you must do what you promised, even if it means I must die.
translation_verse: Ka bipuɣiŋga maa yɛl’ o, “M ba, a yi pun yaag’ a noli lo Yawɛ alikauli, nyin’ niŋm’ ma kaman a ni pun yɛli shɛm maa, Yawɛ ŋun’ dee ni bɔh’ a dimnim’ Ammɔnnim’ biɛri ti a ŋɔ.”

english_verse: But first, please let me spend two months, wandering in the hill country with my friends. We will cry together, because I can never get married and have children.”
translation_verse: Ka bipuɣiŋga maa lan yɛl’ o ba, “Bin’ yini ka n naɣ’ bɔri ni n suh’ a. Dina n-nyɛ: chɛl’ ma ka n niŋ chira ayi pahi, ka n chɛ ka m mini n tab’ du zoya zuɣu n-fabili n ni yɛn kpi ni m paɣipiɛlital’ ŋɔ zuɣu.”

english_verse: “Yes, you may have two months,” Jephthah said. She and some other girls left, and for two months they wandered in the hill country, crying because she could never get married and have children.
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl’ o, “Chama,” ka daa chɛ ka o chaŋ ni o ti niŋ chira ayi. Ka o daa ŋmaligi ka o min’ o dol’ tab’ chaŋ ti du zoya zuɣu n-fabil’ o ni yɛn kpi ni o paɣipiɛlital’ maa zuɣu.

english_verse: every year, Israelite girls walk around for four days, weeping for Jephthah's daughter.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛl paɣisara chani yuuni kam ti zaŋdi daba anahi fabindi Jɛfita Giliad nir’ la bipuɣiŋga maa zuɣu.

english_verse: The men of the Ephraim tribe got together an army and went across the Jordan River to Zaphon to meet with Jephthah. They said, “Why did you go to war with the Ammonites without asking us to help? Just for that, we're going to burn down your house with you inside!”
translation_verse: Ka Ifriim zuliya niriba daa ti lo tɔbu chaŋ ti gbaai Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili du n-chaŋ Zafɔn ti bɔhi Jɛfita, “Bɔ n-niŋ ka a daa yɛn chaŋ ti tuhi Ammɔnnima, ka bi yɛl’ ti ka ti kana ti pahi yi zuɣu ka ti chaŋ? Ti ni niŋ buɣim nyo a yiŋa ka di di n-kab’ lu a zuɣu.”

english_verse: “But I did ask for your help,” Jephthah answered. “That was back when the people of Gilead and I were having trouble with the Ammonites, and you wouldn't do a thing to help us.
translation_verse: Ka Jɛfita yɛli ba, “M mini n niriba ni Ammɔnnima n-daa mali naŋgbankpeen’ titali, ka n daa ŋme kuŋ’ boli ya, ka yi bi kana ti fa ma bɛ nuu ni bahi.

english_verse: So when we realized you weren't coming, we risked our lives and attacked the Ammonites. And the Lord let us defeat them. There's no reason for you to come here today to attack me.”
translation_verse: Ka n ni daa nya ka yi bi kanna maa, ka n daa zaŋ n nyɛvili pa talima chaŋ bɛ tiŋgbɔŋ ni ti tuhi ba; ka Yawɛ daa zaŋ ba niŋ n nuu ni. Ka di chaŋ wula ka yi ti kana zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ ni yi ti tuhi ma?”

english_verse: But the men from Ephraim said, “You people of Gilead are nothing more than refugees from Ephraim. You even live on land that belongs to the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh.” So Jephthah called together the army of Gilead, then they attacked and defeated the army from Ephraim.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Jɛfita daa laɣim Giliadnima n-chaŋ ti tuhi Ifriim zuliya niriba maa n-nyaŋ ba. Dama Ifriim zuliya niriba maa daa yɛlimi, “Yinim’ Giliadnim’ bɛn be Ifriim zuliya niriba mini Manaasa zuliya niriba sunsuuni ŋɔ nyɛla bɛn daa yi Ifriim zuliya niriba ni zo.

english_verse: The army of Gilead also posted guards at all the places where the soldiers from Ephraim could cross the Jordan River to return to their own land. Whenever one of the men from Ephraim would try to cross the river, the guards would say, “Are you from Ephraim?” “No,” the man would answer, “I'm not from Ephraim.”
translation_verse: Ka Giliadnim’ daa chaŋ ti gu Ifriim zuliya niriba maa soli so’ shɛŋa niriba ni daa yi doli duri Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili la zuɣu. english_verse: The guards would then tell them to say “Shibboleth,” because they knew that people of Ephraim could say “Sibboleth,” but not “Shibboleth.” If the man said “Sibboleth,” the guards would grab him and kill him right there. Altogether,
translation_verse: bɛ yɛr’ o mi, “Dindina yɛlim’ ‘Shibolɛt.’ ” Ka o yɛli, “Sibolɛt”, ka dilan’ ni ku tooi yɛl’ li viɛnyɛliŋga maa zuɣu, bɛ gbaar’ o mi ku o Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili dubu shee maa. Ka bɛ daa ku Ifriim zuliya niriba maa ninvuɣ’ tuhi’ pihinahinaayi di saha maa.

english_verse: Jephthah was a leader of Israel for six years, before he died and was buried in his hometown Mizpah in Gilead. Ibzan
translation_verse: Jɛfita daa niŋ Izraɛlnim’ zuɣulan’ la yuma ayɔbu. Ka ŋun’ Jɛfita ŋun daa nyɛ Giliad nir’ maa daa ti kpi, ka bɛ sɔɣ’ o o ya Giliad maa. Ibizan mini Elɔn ni Abidɔn yɛla

english_verse: Ibzan, the next leader of Israel, came from Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Jɛfita kalinsi nyaaŋa, Ibizan ŋun daa nyɛ Bɛtilihɛm nir’ la n-daa leei Izraɛlnim’ zuɣulana.

english_verse: before he died and was buried in Bethlehem. Elon
translation_verse: Ka Ibizan daa ti kpi ka bɛ sɔɣ’ o Bɛtilihɛm.

english_verse: Elon from the Zebulun tribe was the next leader of Israel. He was a leader for ten years,
translation_verse: Ibizan kalinsi nyaaŋa, Elɔn ŋun daa nyɛ Zɛbulɔn zuliya ni nir’ la n-daa leei Izraɛlnim’ zuɣulana. O daa niŋ bɛ zuɣulan’ la yuun’ pia.

english_verse: before he died and was buried in Aijalon that belonged to the Zebulun tribe. Abdon
translation_verse: Ka Elɔn ŋun daa nyɛ Zɛbulɔn zuliya ni nir’ maa daa ti kpi ka bɛ sɔɣ’ o Aijalɔn Zɛbulɔn tiŋgban’ ni.

english_verse: Once again the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let the Philistines take control of Israel for
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa lan tum alahichi Yawɛ sani, ka o daa zaŋ ba niŋ Filistianim’ nuu ni ka bɛ su ba yuun’ pihinahi.

english_verse: Manoah from the tribe of Dan lived in the town of Zorah. His wife was not able to have children,
translation_verse: Di saha maa, do’ so daa beni n-nyɛ ŋun yi Zɔra na, ka o yuli booni Manɔa. O daa nyɛla Dan zuliya ni nira, ka o paɣ’ nyɛ paɣiŋoo, ka ka bihi.

english_verse: but one day an angel from the Lord appeared to her and said: You have never been able to have any children, but very soon you will be pregnant and have a son. He will belong to God from the day he is born, so his hair must never be cut. And even before he is born, you must not drink any wine or beer or eat any food forbidden by God's laws. Your son will begin to set Israel free from the Philistines.
translation_verse: dama nyama, a shiri ni niŋ pua n-dɔɣi bidibiga. Miri ka a ti chɛ ka bɛ zaŋ piliŋ shih’ o zuɣu ni, dama bia maa ti yɛn nyɛla Nazari nir’ Naawuni sani o dɔɣibu ni zaŋ chana. Ka o ni ti piligi n-fari Izraɛlnim’ Filistianim’ nuu ni bahira.”

english_verse: She went to Manoah and said, “A prophet who looked like an angel of God came and talked to me. I was so frightened, that I didn't even ask where he was from. He didn't tell me his name,
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ maa daa chaŋ ti yɛl’ o yidana, “Naawuni nira n-ka n sanna, o biɛhigu ŋmanila Naawuni malaika, ka o ninni lihibu mali dabiɛm pam. M bi bɔh’ o o ni yi luɣ’ shɛl’ na, ka o mi bi wuhi ma o yuli.

english_verse: but he did say that I'm going to have a baby boy. I'm not supposed to drink any wine or beer or eat any food forbidden by God's laws. Our son will belong to God for as long as he lives.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka o lee yɛli ma, ‘Nyama, a ni niŋ pua n-dɔɣi bidibiga. Dinzuɣu miri ka a nyu wain bee binnyuri kpiɔŋ; a mi miri ka a di binshɛli din chihiri dibu; dama bia maa ti yɛn nyɛla Nazari nir’ Naawuni sani o dɔɣibu dali zaŋ hal ti paag’ o kum dali.’ ”

english_verse: Then Manoah prayed, “Our Lord, please send that prophet again and let him tell us what to do for the son we are going to have.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Manɔa daa balim Yawɛ yɛli, “Yawɛ, n suhir’ a, chɛ ka a ni daa tim do’ so na la lan lab’ ti sanna nti wuhi ti ti ni ti yɛn niŋ bi’ so ti ni yɛn dɔɣi maa shɛm.”

english_verse: God answered Manoah's prayer, and the angel went back to Manoah's wife while she was resting in the fields. Manoah wasn't there at the time,
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa deei Manɔa suhigu maa, ka chɛ ka Naawuni malaika maa lan lab’ paɣ’ maa sanna saha shɛl’ o ni daa yi mɔɣ’ kpaŋ’ ti ʒiya. Amaa o yidan’ Manɔa daa ka o sani.

english_verse: so she found him and said, “That same man is here again! He's the one I saw the other day.”
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ maa daa guui yomyom chaŋ ti yɛl’ o yidana, “Nyama, do’ so ŋun daa ka n sanna la lan yi n zuɣu.”

english_verse: Manoah went with his wife and asked the man, “Are you the one who spoke to my wife?” “Yes, I am,” he answered.
translation_verse: Ka Manɔa daa yiɣisi dol’ o paɣ’ maa chaŋ doo maa sani ti bɔh’ o, “Nyini n-nyɛ ŋun daa tɔɣisi paɣ’ ŋɔ yɛtɔɣa la?” Ka o yɛli, “mani.”

english_verse: Manoah then asked, “When your promise comes true, what rules must he obey and what will be his work?”
translation_verse: Ka Manɔa bɔh’ o, “A yɛligu maa yi ti niŋ pali, bia maa biɛhigu ti yɛn nyɛla wula, ka tuun’ bɔ ka o lee ti yɛn tum?”

english_verse: “Your wife must be careful to do everything I told her,” the Lord's angel answered.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ malaika maa daa yɛli Manɔa, “N ni daa yɛli paɣ’ maa shɛlikam zaa la, di simdi ni o dol’ li viɛnyɛliŋga.

english_verse: “She must not eat or drink anything made from grapes. She must not drink wine or beer or eat anything forbidden by God's laws. I told her exactly what to do.”
translation_verse: O miri ka o di binshɛlikam din yi wain tia zuɣu na bee n-nyu wain bee n-nyu binnyuri kpiɔŋ bee n-di binshɛli din chihiri dibu. Chɛ ka o doli n ni zal’ o shɛlikam maa zaa.”

english_verse: “Please,” Manoah said, “stay here with us for just a little while, and we'll fix a young goat for you to eat.”
translation_verse: Ka Manɔa daa yɛli Yawɛ malaika maa, “N suhir’ a, na di kuli, ka ti gbaai bubil’ polli kɔrigi niŋ bindirigu ti a.”

english_verse: Manoah didn't realize that he was really talking to one of the Lord's angels. The angel answered, “I can stay for a little while, although I won't eat any of your food. But if you would like to offer the goat as a sacrifice to the Lord, that would be fine.”
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ malaika maa yɛli Manɔa, “A yi gooi ma ʒili, n ku di yi bindirigu maa; amaa yi yi niŋ shili ni yi zaŋ li mali sara nyo buɣim, yin’ zaŋmiya li na ti ti Yawɛ.” .

english_verse: Manoah said, “Tell us your name, so we can honor you after our son is born.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Manɔa daa yɛli Yawɛ malaika maa, “Wuhim’ ti a yuli, ka a yɛligu maa ti niŋ pali ka ti ti a jilima.”

english_verse: “No,” the angel replied. “You don't need to know my name. And if you did, you couldn't understand it.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Yawɛ malaika maa bɔh’ o, “Bɔ n-niŋ ka a bɔri ni n wuh’ a n yuli? Dama n yuli maa nyɛla alahiziba yuli.”

english_verse: So Manoah took a young goat over to a large rock he had chosen for an altar, and he built a fire on the rock. Then he killed the goat, and offered it with some grain as a sacrifice to the Lord. But then an amazing thing happened.
translation_verse: Ka Manɔa daa gbaai bubil’ polli kɔrigi m-bo chi pahi di zuɣu n-zaŋ li ti pa sara maligu tampiŋ bimbini zuɣu n-nyo li buɣim mali sara ti Yawɛ ŋun tumd’ alahiziba tuma ŋɔ.

english_verse: The fire blazed up toward the sky, and the Lord's angel went up toward heaven in the fire. Manoah and his wife bowed down low when they saw what happened.
translation_verse: Ka buɣim maa buɣim niɛm daa kpuɣi bimbini maa zuɣu du zuɣusaa, ka Yawɛ malaika maa yiɣi kpe di ni n-dol’ li du zuɣusaa, ka Manɔa min’ o paɣ’ daa nya lala ka teei dɔni n-zaŋ bɛ nina kpa tiŋa.

english_verse: Although the angel didn't appear to them again, they realized he was one of the Lord's angels.
translation_verse: Yawɛ malaika maa ni daa chaŋ ka chɛ Manɔa min’ o paɣ’ saha shɛli maa, ka bɛ daa baŋ ni Yawɛ malaika m-bala.

english_verse: Manoah said, “We have seen an angel. Now we're going to die.”
translation_verse: Ka Manɔa daa yɛl’ o paɣa, “Ti nini nya Naawuni, dinzuɣu biɛhiŋ kani, ti ni kpi.”

english_verse: “The Lord isn't going to kill us,” Manoah's wife responded. “The Lord accepted our sacrifice and grain offering, and he let us see something amazing. Besides, he told us that we're going to have a son.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka o paɣ’ yɛl’ o, “Naawuni yi di bɔri ti kubu, o naan ku deei ti ni zaŋ binshɛŋa nyo buɣim mali sara ti o ŋɔ ti nuu ni bee n-yɛl’ ti o ni yɛl’ ti yɛl’ shɛŋa ŋɔ bee n-wuhi ti o ni wuhi ti binshɛŋa ŋɔ zaa.”

english_verse: Later, Manoah's wife did give birth to a son, and she named him Samson. As the boy grew, the Lord blessed him.
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ maa daa ti dɔɣi bidibiga m-bol’ o yuli Samsin; ka bia maa daa mali ti zooi, ka Yawɛ niŋ alibarika niŋ o ni.

english_verse: Then, while Samson was staying at Dan's Camp between the towns of Zorah and Eshtaol, the Spirit of the Lord took control of him.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ Shia daa piligi tir’ o kpiɔŋ saha shɛl’ o ni daa be Mahanɛdan din be Zɔra mini Ɛshitaol sunsuuni la.

english_verse: One day, Samson went to Timnah, where he saw a Philistine woman.
translation_verse: Dahin shɛli ka Samsin daa ti chaŋ Timna ti nya Filistia do’ so bipuɣiŋga;

english_verse: When he got back home, he told his parents, “I saw a Philistine woman in Timnah, and I want to marry her. Get her for me!”
translation_verse: ka o daa kuli ti yɛl’ o ba min’ o ma, “N nyala Filistia do’ so bipuɣiŋga Timna, dinzuɣu bomiy’ o ti ma ka n niŋ m paɣa.”

english_verse: His parents answered, “There are a lot of women in our clan and even more in the rest of Israel. Those Philistines are pagans. Why would you want to marry one of their women?” “She looks good to me,” Samson answered. “Get her for me!”
translation_verse: Amaa ka o ba min’ o ma bɔh’ o, “Paɣa n-ka a dɔɣiriba bipuɣinsi ni bee ti zuliya ŋɔ zaa ni ka a ni bɔ, ka ti chaŋ ti bɔrila Filistianim’ bɛn bi gundi ŋɔ bipuɣiŋga ni a niŋ a paɣa?” Amaa ka Samsin yɛl’ o ba, “Bom’ o ti ma, dama n suhu yu’ o pam.”

english_verse: At that time, the Philistines were in control of Israel, and the Lord wanted to stir up trouble for them. That's why he made Samson desire that woman.
translation_verse: Samsin ba min’ o ma daa bi mi ni Yawɛ n-wuhi Samsin lala, dama Yawɛ daa bɔrila so’ shɛli o ni yɛn doli tuhi Filistianima. Di saha maa, Filistianima n-daa su Izraɛlnima.

english_verse: As Samson and his parents reached the vineyards near Timnah, a fierce young lion suddenly roared and attacked Samson.
translation_verse: Ka Samsin min’ o ba ni o ma daa yiɣisi chani Timna, ka Samsin daa ti kpe bɛ wain tihi puu ni; ka gbuɣim’ polli nya o ŋumda.

english_verse: But the Lord's Spirit took control of Samson, and with his bare hands he tore the lion apart, as though it had been a young goat. His parents didn't know what he had done, and he didn't tell them.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ Shia daa siɣi Samsin zuɣu na pam, ka o zaŋ o nuzaŋa gbaai gbuɣinli maa n-darigi pirig’ o kaman nir’ ni darigiri pirigiri bubil’ shɛm la. Amaa o daa bi saɣi yɛl’ o ba bee o ma o ni niŋ shɛm maa.

english_verse: When they got to Timnah, Samson talked to the woman, and he was sure that she was the one for him.
translation_verse: Ka Samsin daa chaŋ ka o mini paɣisarili maa ti nya taba, ka Samsin suhu daa yu’ o pam.

english_verse: Later, Samson returned to Timnah for the wedding. And when he came near the place where the lion had attacked, he left the road to see what was left of the lion. He was surprised to see that bees were living in the lion's skeleton, and that they had made some honey.
translation_verse: Ka di daa niŋ daba ayi ha ka Samsin ti labiri ni o ti niŋ paɣisarili maa amiliya, ka o daa ti ŋmaligi birigi ni o lihi nya o ni daa ku gbuɣin’ so sɔŋ la, ka nya ka shihi n-kpe m-pal’ o zaɣ’ woliŋ ni niŋ kpam.

english_verse: He scooped up the honey in his hands and ate some of it as he walked along. When he got back to his parents, he gave them some of the honey, and they ate it too. But he didn't tell them he had found the honey in the skeleton of a lion.
translation_verse: Ka o daa tim ŋmaai shikpam maa niŋ o nuu ni diri chana; ka daa zaŋ di shɛli nti ti o ba min’ o ma, ka bɛ di. Amaa ka Samsin daa bi yɛli ba ni gbuɣin’ kpiɔŋ ni ka o yihi shiri maa na.

english_verse: While Samson's father went to make the final arrangements with the bride and her family, Samson threw a big party, as grooms usually did.
translation_verse: Ka Samsin ba daa chaŋ paɣisarili maa yiŋa, ka Samsin ti chɛ ka bɛ puhi chuɣu nimaani; dama lala ka nachimba daa yi niŋda.

english_verse: When the Philistines saw what Samson was like, they told
translation_verse: Ka niriba daa nya o, ka bo nachimba pihita n-chɛ ka bɛ kana ti be o sani.

english_verse: But if you can't tell me the answer, then each of you will have to give me a shirt and a full change of clothing.” “It's a bet!” the Philistines said. “Tell us the riddle.”
translation_verse: Amaa yi yi ku tooi wuhi ma di gbinni, dindina yi mi ni ti ma silinchi kpar’ suma pihita mini binyɛr’ sun’ shɛŋa din nyɛ chuɣu dali binyɛra” Ka bɛ yɛl’ o, “yɛlim’ ti a ŋahili maa ka ti wum.”

english_verse: Samson said: Once so strong and mighty— now so sweet and tasty! Three days went by, and the Philistine young men had not come up with the right answer.
translation_verse: Ka o yɛli ba, “Ŋun diri ni ka bɛ ni diri shɛli yina; Ŋum mali kpiɔŋ ni ka din nyaɣisi yina.” Ka di daa mali ti paai daba ata, ka bɛ na bi tooi baŋ ŋahili maa gbinni.

english_verse: Finally, on the seventh day of the party they went to Samson's bride and said, “You had better trick your husband into telling you the answer to his riddle. Have you invited us here just to rob us? If you don't find out the answer, we will burn you and your family to death.”
translation_verse: Di daba anahi dali ka bɛ daa ti yɛli Samsin paɣa, “Doli yɛŋkiŋkabina soli n-chɛ ka a yidana wuhi ti o ŋahili maa, di yi pa lala, ti ni nyo a ba yiŋ’ buɣim ka di di li tabili amaŋmaŋa. Yi bol’ ti mi na ni yi ti ti ti samli?”

english_verse: Samson's bride went to him and started crying in his arms. “You must really hate me,” she sobbed. “If you loved me at all, you would have told me the answer to your riddle.” “But I haven't even told my parents the answer!” Samson replied. “Why should I tell you?”
translation_verse: Ka Samsin paɣ’ maa daa chaŋ Samsin sani ti kumdi niŋd’ o yɛra, “A bi yuri ma. A ŋahi n niriba ŋahili, ka bi wuhi ma ŋahili maa gbinni.” Ka Samsin yɛl’ o, “Nyama, hal m bi wuhi m ba bee m ma di gbinni, ka ti wuhiri nyini?”

english_verse: For the entire seven days of the party, she had been whining and trying to get the answer from him. But that seventh day she put so much pressure on Samson that he finally gave in and told her the answer. She went straight to the young men and told them.
translation_verse: Ka o paɣ’ maa daa kum niŋ o bɛ daamiliya chuɣu daba ayopɔin maa ni zaa. Ka paɣ’ maa daa muɣisi Samsin hal ka o ti bahi wuh’ o ŋahili maa gbinni di daba ayopɔin maa dali. Ka paɣ’ maa daa zaŋ li chaŋ ti yɛl’ o niriba maa.

english_verse: Before sunset that day, the men of the town went to Samson with this answer: A lion is the strongest— honey is the sweetest! Samson replied, This answer you have given me doubtless came from my bride-to-be.
translation_verse: Ka tiŋ’ maa ni niriba maa daa ka Samsin sanna daba ayopɔin maa dali, saha shɛli wuntaŋ’ ni daa na bi lu nti yɛl’ o, “Bɔ n-lee beni n-nyaɣisi gari shiri? Ka bɔ n-lee beni m-mali kpiɔŋ gari gbuɣinli?” Ka Samsin yɛli ba, “Yi yi di bi mali n naɣ’ kɔro kɔra, yi naan ku tooi baŋ n ŋahili maa gbinni.

english_verse: The father of the bride made Samson's wife marry one of the
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa zaŋ Samsin paɣ’ maa ti do’ so ŋun daa nyɛ Samsin aŋgo zo.

english_verse: “When you left the way you did, I thought you were divorcing her. So I arranged for her to marry one of the young men who were at your party. But my younger daughter is even prettier, and you can have her as your wife.”
translation_verse: ka yɛli Samsin, “Man’ daa tɛhiya ni a lan je o mi, ka zaŋ o ti a daaŋgo zo la. O tizɔbil’ ŋɔ viɛli gar’ o, dinzuɣu jaande, zaŋm’ o tizɔbil’ maa ka chɛ o.”

english_verse: “This time,” Samson answered, “I have a good reason for really hurting some Philistines.” Samson Takes Revenge
translation_verse: Di saha ka Samsin daa yɛli, “Pumpɔŋɔ dina, n yi lan niŋ Filistianim’ zaɣ’ biɛɣu, di pala n taali.”

english_verse: Then Samson took the foxes into the Philistine wheat fields that were ready to be harvested. He set the rags on fire and let the foxes go. The wheat fields went up in flames, and so did the stacks of wheat that had already been cut. Even the Philistine vineyards and olive orchards burned.
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka o daa niŋ buɣim dab’ li; ka zaŋ ba bahi ka bɛ zo nti kpe Filistianim’ kawana ni. Ka buɣim maa taai bɛ kawaan’ puri maa n-di bɛ ni pun ŋahi luɣ’ shɛŋa mini bɛ ni na bi ŋahi shɛŋa n-tabili bɛ olivi tihi puri.

english_verse: Some of the Philistines started asking around, “Who could have done such a thing?” “It was Samson,” someone told them. “He married the daughter of that man in Timnah, but then the man gave Samson's wife to one of the men at the wedding.” The Philistine leaders went to Timnah and burned to death Samson's wife and her father.
translation_verse: Ka Filistianim’ maa daa bɔhi, “To, ninvuɣ’ ŋuni n-lee tum tuuni ŋɔ?” Ka ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ yɛli ba, “Samsin ŋun deemba nyɛ Timna nir’ la n-tum lala maa. O ni deeg’ o paɣa n-zaŋ o ti o daaŋgo zo la zuɣu.” Ka Filistianim’ maa daa chaŋ ti niŋ buɣim nyo paɣ’ maa min’ o ba.

english_verse: When Samson found out what they had done, he went to them and said, “You killed them! And I won't rest until I get even with you.”
translation_verse: Ka Samsin bɔhi ba, “Yi ni niŋ shɛm ŋɔ zuɣu, M poya ni n ku chɛn ya, faashee ka m bɔhi ya biɛri labisi ka naanyi chɛ.”

english_verse: Then Samson started hacking them to pieces with his sword. Samson left Philistia and went to live in the cave at Etam Rock.
translation_verse: Ka o daa lu bɛ zuɣu ŋ-ŋmɛri kabiri bɛ sakpuri mini bɛ gbalipina n-daa niŋ lala ku ba pam. Di nyaaŋa ka o daa chaŋ Ɛtam ti kpe m-be tampiŋ lɔŋni. Samsin ni tuhi nyaŋ Filistianim’ shɛm

english_verse: But it wasn't long before the Philistines invaded Judah and set up a huge army camp at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Filistianim’ daa kana ti dɔni Juda tiŋgbɔŋ ni n-chaŋ ti liri Lɛhinima.

english_verse: The people of Judah asked, “Why have you invaded our land?” The Philistines answered, “We've come to get Samson. We're going to do the same things to him that he did to our people.”
translation_verse: Ka Judanim’ daa bɔhi ba, “Bɔzuɣu ka yi kana ti liri ti?” Ka bɛ yɛli, “Ti kamina ni ti ti lo Samsin mihi n-zaŋ o chaŋ ti niŋ o o ni niŋ ti shɛm labisi.”

english_verse: Three thousand men from Judah went to the cave at Etam Rock and said to Samson, “Don't you know that the Philistines rule us, and they will punish us for what you did?” “I was only getting even with them,” Samson replied. “They did the same things to me first.”
translation_verse: Ka Judanim’ maa ninvuɣ’ tusaata daa chaŋ Ɛtam tampiŋ lɔŋ maa ni ti bɔhi Samsin, “A bi mi ni Filistianima n-su ti? Ka tuun’ bɔ ka a lee tum ti ŋɔ?” Ka Samsin garigi yɛli ba, “N niŋ ba la bɛ ni niŋ ma shɛm labisi.”

english_verse: “We came here to tie you up and turn you over to them,” said the men of Judah. “I won't put up a fight,” Samson answered, “but you have to promise not to hurt me yourselves.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ yɛli Samsin, “Ti kamina ni ti ti lo a mihi n-zaŋ a ti ti Filistianim’ maa.” Ka Samsin yɛli ba, “Pomiya ni yimaŋmaŋ’ ku ku ma.”

english_verse: “We promise,” the men said. “We will only tie you up and turn you over to the Philistines. We won't kill you.” Then they tied up his hands and arms with two brand-new ropes and led him away from Etam Rock. When the Philistines saw that Samson was being brought to their camp at Jawbone, they started shouting and ran toward him. But the Lord's Spirit took control of Samson, and Samson broke the ropes, as though they were pieces of burnt cloth.
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa zaŋ o ti paai Lɛhi, ka Filistianim’ kul zɔri kani o sanna, ka tahira. Ka Yawɛ Shia daa siɣ’ o zuɣu na pam, ka mi’ shɛŋa din daa lo o maa zaa dii chihichihi; ka di be kaman buɣim ni di gali shɛm la.

english_verse: Samson glanced around and spotted the jawbone of a donkey. The jawbone had not yet dried out, so it was still hard and heavy. Samson grabbed it and started hitting Philistines—he killed
translation_verse: Di saha maa ka Samsin daa nya buŋ yɛno kɔbili kpuɣ’ li n-zaŋ li ku ninvuɣ’ tuhili.

english_verse: After the fighting was over, he made up this poem about what he had done to the Philistines: I used a donkey's jawbone to kill a thousand men; I beat them with this jawbone over and over again.
translation_verse: Ka Samsin daa yɛli, “Buŋ’ yɛno kɔbili ka n zaŋ ku ninvuɣ’ tuhili. Buŋ’ yɛno kɔbili ka n zaŋ ku ba n-laɣim ba sɔŋ gbilligbilli.”

english_verse: Samson tossed the jawbone on the ground and decided to call the place Jawbone Hill. It is still called that today.
translation_verse: O yɛtɔɣa ŋɔ nyaaŋa ka o daa zaŋ buŋ’ yɛno kɔbili maa bahi. Ka bɛ daa bol’ o ni zaŋ li bahi luɣ’ shɛli maa yuli Ramatilɛhi.

english_verse: Samson was so thirsty that he prayed, “Our Lord, you helped me win a battle against a whole army. Please don't let me die of thirst now. Those heathen Philistines will carry off my dead body.”
translation_verse: Ka kɔnyuri daa gbaai Samsin pam, ka o suhi Yawɛ yɛli, “Nyini n-chɛ ka mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ di nasara ŋɔ, ka kɔnyuri ti yɛn ku ma, ka n lu ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn bi gundi ŋɔ nuu ni?”

english_verse: Samson was tired and weary, but God sent water gushing from a rock. Samson drank some and felt strong again. Samson named the place Caller Spring, because he had called out to God for help. The spring is still there at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Ka Naawuni daa chɛ ka Lɛhi tiŋgban’ ni vinvamli tahi bɔɣi, ka kom yi di ni na, ka Samsin nyu ka o ni maai, ka o kpiɔŋ lan labina yaha. Dinzuɣu ka bɛ daa boli kɔbili’ nini maa yuli Ɛnhakɔr. Ka di na kul be Lɛhi hal ni zuŋɔ.

english_verse: years, but the Philistines were still the rulers of Israel.
translation_verse: Samsin daa niŋ Izraɛlnim’ zuɣulana la yuun’ pisi shɛŋa puuni Filistianim’ ni daa su bɛ tiŋgbɔŋ maa la.

english_verse: The people who lived in Gaza found out he was there, and they decided to kill him at sunrise. So they went to the city gate and waited all night in the guardrooms on each side of the gate.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yɛli Gazanim’ ni Samsin be nimaani, ka bɛ laɣimna ti teei gil’ o ni be shɛli maa, ka chaŋ ti gu o tiŋ’ maa gooni dunol’ ni yuŋ zaa. Bɛ daa kul fomi chichi dindali maa yuŋ maa, ka yɛra “Ti ni do n-gul’ o hal ka biɛɣu ti neei ka ti ku o.”

english_verse: Some time later, Samson fell in love with a woman named Delilah, who lived in Sorek Valley.
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka Samsin daa ti bɔri paɣ’ so ŋun be Sɔrɛk Vinvamli ni ka o yuli booni Dilaila.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers went to Delilah and said, “Trick Samson into telling you what makes him so strong and what can make him weak. Then we can tie him up so he can't get away. If you find out his secret, we will each give you
translation_verse: Di saha ka Filistianim’ nanim’ daa ka Dilaila sanna ti yɛl’ o, “Lom’ ania doli yɛŋkiŋkabina soli n-chɛ ka o wuh’ a din chɛ ka o mali kpiɔŋ pam maa, ka wuh’ a ti ni yɛn niŋ shɛm nyaŋ o, ka di chɛ ka ti tooi gbaag’ o n-lo o mihi nyaŋ o. Ka ti zaa yinoyino ni ti a anzinfa laɣibaligu tuhili ni kɔbigakɔbiga.”

english_verse: The next time Samson was at Delilah's house, she asked, “Samson, what makes you so strong? How can I tie you up so you can't get away? Come on, you can tell me.”
translation_verse: Ka Dilaila daa ti yɛli Samsin, “Niŋm’ ania wuhi ma din chɛ ka a mali kpiɔŋ pam maa, ka wuhi ma nir’ ni yɛn niŋ shɛm lo a mihi nyaŋ a.”

english_verse: Samson answered, “If someone ties me up with seven new bowstrings that have never been dried, it will make me just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Ka Samsin yɛl’ o, “Bɛ yi zaŋ tɔbimi’ pala zaɣ’ maha diba ayopɔin lo ma, di ni chɛ ka n gbarigi, ka be kaman sokam ni be shɛm.”

english_verse: The Philistine rulers gave seven new bowstrings to Delilah. They also told some of their soldiers to go to Delilah's house and hide in the room where Samson and Delilah were. If the bowstrings made Samson weak, they would be able to capture him. Delilah tied up Samson with the bowstrings and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson snapped the bowstrings, as though they were pieces of scorched string. The Philistines had not found out why Samson was so strong.
translation_verse: Di saha maa o daa chɛ ka ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ sɔɣ’ bela yil’ maa ni du’ shɛli ni. Ka o daa kuhi yɛl’ o, “Samsin, Filistianim’ kana ni bɛ ti lir’ a.” Ka Samsin daa darigi chihi tɔbimi’ maha maa kaman gali ni yi shihi buɣim di n-chihi shɛm la. Dinzuɣu bɛ daa na bi jɛndi baŋ o kpiɔŋ maa daashili.

english_verse: “You lied and made me look like a fool,” Delilah said. “Now tell me. How can I really tie you up?”
translation_verse: Ka Dilaila yɛl’ o, “A boli ma la jɛrigu, ka ŋma ma ʒiri. Niŋm’ ania, yɛlim’ ma nir’ ni yɛn niŋ shɛm lo a mihi.”

english_verse: Samson answered, “Use some new ropes. If I'm tied up with ropes that have never been used, I'll be just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Ka Samsin yɛl’ o, “Bɛ yi zaŋ mi’ pal’ shɛŋa bɛ ni na bi zaŋ lo binshɛli lo ma, n ni gbarigi, ka be kaman sokam ni be shɛm.”

english_verse: Delilah got new ropes, and again some Philistines hid in the room. Then she tied up Samson's arms and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson snapped the ropes as if they were threads.
translation_verse: Ka Dilaila daa bo mi’ pala lo o, ka kuhi yɛl’ o, “Samsin Filistianim’ kana ni bɛ ti lir’ a.” Ka ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn daa sɔɣi do n-gu’ o maa be yil’ maa ni du’ shɛl’ ni. Ka Samsin daa darigi chihi mihi maa kaman gal’ la.

english_verse: “You're still lying and making a fool of me,” Delilah said. “Tell me how I can tie you up!” “My hair is in seven braids,” Samson replied. “If you weave my braids into the threads on a loom and nail the loom to a wall, then I will be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Ka Dilaila daa lan yɛli Samsin, “A na kul boli ma la jɛrigu, ka ŋmari ma ʒiri hal ni pɔŋɔ. Wuhim’ ma nir’ ni yɛn niŋ shɛm lo a mihi.” Ka o yɛl’ o, “Nir’ yi zaŋ n zab’ kpil’ ayopɔin ŋɔ niŋ kpalu’ dari ni n-wuɣi li, ka bo kpaa shɛbisi di ni vooi li ka di kpaŋ, dindina n ni gbarigi, ka be kaman sokam ni be shɛm.”

english_verse: While Samson was asleep, Delilah wove his braids into the threads on a loom and nailed the loom to a wall. Then she shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson woke up and pulled the loom free from its posts in the ground and from the nails in the wall. Then he pulled his hair free from the woven cloth.
translation_verse: Ka o daa ti gbihiri ka Dilaila gbaag’ o zab’ kpil’ ayopɔin maa niŋ kpalu’ dari ni n-wuɣi li, ka bo kpaa shɛbisi di ni vooi li ka di kpaŋ, ka kuhi yɛl’ o, “Samsin, Filistianim’ kana ni bɛ ti lir’ a.” Ka Samsin daa neei gom ni n-darigi vuɣi kpalu’ dari maa mini kpaa maa ni di wuɣibu maa zaa.

english_verse: “Samson,” Delilah said, “you claim to love me, but you don't mean it! You've made me look like a fool three times now, and you still haven't told me why you are so strong.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dilaila daa bɔhi Samsin, “Wula ka a yɛri ni a yuri ma ka a suhu ka n ni? Siɣimsiɣim buta zaa ka a boli ma jɛrigu, ka bi saɣi yɛli ma a kpiɔŋ din galisi pam maa ni be a luɣ’ shɛli.”

english_verse: Delilah started nagging and pestering him day after day, until he couldn't stand it any longer.
translation_verse: Ka Dilaila daa kul zaŋ di yɛla kaɣili Samsin biɛɣukam, ka kul mal’ li dol’ o hal ka o nyee ti nyɔni pam di zuɣu.

english_verse: Finally, Samson told her the truth. “I have belonged to God ever since I was born, so my hair has never been cut. If it were ever cut off, my strength would leave me, and I would be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Ka o daa kahig’ o daashili zaa wuh’ o ka yɛl’ o, “N nyɛla Nazari nir’ Naawuni sani hal n ni daa na be m ma pul’ ni saha shɛli, ka piliŋ na ʒi n-shihi n zuɣu ni. Ka n yi pini, n kpiɔŋ maa ni yi n ni ka n gbarigi, ka be kaman sokam ni be shɛm.”

english_verse: Delilah realized that he was telling the truth. So she sent someone to tell the Philistine rulers, “Come to my house one more time. Samson has finally told me the truth.” The Philistine rulers went to Delilah's house, and they brought along the silver they had promised her.
translation_verse: Dilaila ni daa baŋ ni Samsin yipa yɛl’ o yɛlimaŋli zaa maa, ka o tim ti yɛli Filistianim’ nanim’ la, “O yipa yɛl’ ma yɛlimaŋli zaa, dinzuɣu kamiyana pumpɔŋɔ.” Ka Filistianim’ nanim’ maa daa bɔ liɣiri ka o sanna.

english_verse: Delilah had lulled Samson to sleep with his head resting in her lap. She signaled to one of the Philistine men as she began cutting off Samson's seven braids. And by the time she was finished, Samson's strength was gone. Delilah tied him up
translation_verse: Ka Dilaila daa chɛ ka Samsin zaŋ o zuɣu pa o naba zuɣu gbihi, ka o bol’ do’ so na ti chɛ ka o pini Samsin zuɣu ni zab’ kpila ayopɔin maa. Ka o daa piligi damdi Samsin, ka o kpiɔŋ maa daa shiri yi o ni.

english_verse: The Philistines grabbed Samson and poked out his eyes. They took him to the prison in Gaza and chained him up. Then they put him to work, turning a millstone to grind grain.
translation_verse: Ka Filistianim’ maa daa gbaag’ o n-kpaɣ’ o nina, ka zaŋ o tahi Gaza ti zaŋ daanya bandi baŋ o, ka chɛ ka o niɛmdi chi sarika ni.

english_verse: But they didn't cut his hair any more, so it started growing back.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Samsin zabiri maa daa ti lan bilina gbaai zoobu o pinibu maa nyaaŋa. Samsin kum yɛla

english_verse: The Philistine rulers threw a big party and sacrificed a lot of animals to their god Dagon. The rulers said: Samson was our enemy, but our god Dagon helped us capture him!
translation_verse: Ka Filistianim’ nanim’ daa ti laɣim ni bɛ mali bɛ buɣili Dagɔn; ka diɛm suhupiɛlli diɛma; dama bɛ daa yɛlimi, “Ti buɣili n-zaŋ ti dim’ Samsin niŋ ti nuu ni maa.”

english_verse: Everyone there was having a good time, and they shouted, “Bring out Samson—he's still good for a few more laughs!” The rulers had Samson brought from the prison, and when the people saw him, this is how they praised their god: Samson ruined our crops and killed our people. He was our enemy, but our god helped us capture him. They made fun of Samson for a while, then they told him to stand near the columns that supported the roof.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ suhuri daa ti paligi pam ka bɛ yɛli, “Bolimiya Samsin na ka o ti diɛm wuhi ti.” Ka bɛ daa chaŋ sarika ni ti zaŋ Samsin na, ka o daa kana ti diɛm wuhi ba. Bɛ daa chɛ ka o ʒiɛla daantalisi sunsuuni.

english_verse: A young man was leading Samson by the hand, and Samson said to him, “I need to lean against something. Take me over to the columns that hold up the roof.”
translation_verse: Ka Samsin daa ti yɛli ninvuɣ’ so ŋun gbib’ o nuu vɔr’ o, “Chɛ ka m bɔbili gbaai duu ŋɔ ni tam daantal’ shɛŋa zuɣu n-zaŋ mmaŋ’ dalim li.”

english_verse: Samson prayed, “Please remember me, Lord God. The Philistines poked out my eyes, but make me strong one last time, so I can take revenge for at least one of my eyes!”
translation_verse: Di saha maa ka Samsin daa suhi Yawɛ yɛli, “Yaa n Duuma Naawuni, n suhir’ a, teemi n yɛla, ka lan ti ma kpiɔŋ yim kɔŋko pahi, yaa n Duuma Naawuni, ka m bɔhi Filistianim’ ŋɔ biɛri labisi n nina ayi ŋɔ zuɣu.”

english_verse: Samson was standing between the two middle columns that held up the roof. He felt around and found one column with his right hand, and the other with his left hand.
translation_verse: Ka Samsin daa zaŋ o nudirigu min’ o nuzaa n-gbaai sunsuuni daantalis’ ayi shɛŋa zuɣu duu maa ni tamya maa;

english_verse: Then he shouted, “Let me die with the Philistines!” He pushed against the columns as hard as he could, and the temple collapsed with the Philistine rulers and everyone else still inside. Samson killed more Philistines when he died than he had killed during his entire life.
translation_verse: ka yɛli, “N Duuma, chɛ ka m mini Filistianim’ ŋɔ laɣim kpi;” ka daai daantalisi maa ni o kpiɔŋ zaa; ka duu maa kab’ lu o mini nanim’ maa ni ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn zaa daa be di ni zuɣu. Dinzuɣu Samsin ni daa ku ninvuɣ’ shɛba o kum dali daa gar’ o ni daa be o nyɛvil’ ni ka ku ninvuɣ’ shɛba.

english_verse: His brothers and the rest of his family went to Gaza and took his body back home. They buried him in his father's tomb, which was located between Zorah and Eshtaol. Samson was a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Samsin mabihi min’ o dɔɣiriba zaa daa chaŋ ti kpuɣ’ o ti sɔɣ’ o ba Manɔa siliga shɛli din daa be Zɔra mini Ɛshitaol sunsuuni la ni. O daa niŋ Izraɛlnim’ zuɣulan’ la yuun’ pisi.

english_verse: Micah returned the silver to his mother, and she said, “I give this silver to the Lord, so my son can use it to make an idol.” Turning to her son, she said, “Micah, now the silver belongs to you.” But Micah handed it back to his mother. She took
translation_verse: O ni daa zaŋ liɣiri maa labisi ti o ma; ka o ma daa yihi di ni anzinfa kpila kɔbisiyi ti anzinfa doora, ka o daa zaŋ li mali anzinfa binnani. Ka bɛ daa zaŋ li zali Maika yiŋa.

english_verse: He had a shrine for worshiping God there at his home, and he had made some idols and a sacred priestly vest. Micah chose one of his own sons to be the priest for his shrine.
translation_verse: Maika daa malila binnana jɛmbu duu; ka daa she mukuru laasabu din nyɛ bɛ ni daa lihiri shɛli ni buɣiri baɣa niŋ di ni, ka daa zaŋ o bidib’ yino leeg’ o maligumaana.

english_verse: This was before kings ruled Israel, so all the Israelites did whatever they thought was right.
translation_verse: Di saha maa Izraɛlnim’ daa ka naa, dinzuɣu sokam daa kul tumdila o suhu ni yu shɛm.

english_verse: One day a young Levite came to Micah's house in the hill country of Ephraim. He had been staying with one of the clans of Judah in Bethlehem, but he had left Bethlehem to find a new place to live where he could be a priest.
translation_verse: O daa yila Bɛtilihɛm din be Juda tiŋgbɔŋ ni maa n-chani bɔri luɣ’ shɛli ni o ʒini. Ka o daa chaŋchaŋ ti kana ti kpɛla Maika ŋun daa be Ifriim tiŋgban’ ni zoya zuɣu maa yiŋa.

english_verse: “Where are you from?” Micah asked. “I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah,” the man answered, “and I'm on my way to find a new place to live.”
translation_verse: Ka Maika daa bɔh’ o, “Tiŋkani ka a yina?” Ka o garigi yɛl’ o, “N nyɛla Lɛvi zuliya nira, ka yi Bɛtilihɛm Juda tiŋgbɔŋ ni na. N chani bɔrila luɣ’ shɛli ni n ʒini.”

english_verse: Micah said, “Why don't you stay here with me? You can be my priest and tell me what God wants me to do. Every year I'll give you ten pieces of silver and one complete set of clothes, and I'll provide all your food.” The young man went for a walk,
translation_verse: Ka Maika yɛl’ o, “Kpalimmi n sani leei m ba ni m maligumaana. N ni tir’ a anzinfa kpila pia yuuni kam, ka tir’ a situra mini bindirigu pahi.”

english_verse: then he agreed to stay with Micah and be his priest. He lived in Micah's house, and Micah treated him like one of his own sons.
translation_verse: Ka Maika daa zaŋ Lɛvi zuliya nachimbil’ maa leeg’ o maligumaana, ka o daa kpalim be ŋun’ Maika yiŋa.

english_verse: Micah said, “I have a Levite as my own priest. Now I know that the Lord will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Maika daa yɛli, “Pumpɔŋɔ m baŋya ni Yawɛ ni chɛ ka n tɔŋ, n ni zaŋ Lɛvi zuliya nira leei m maligumaana ŋɔ zuɣu.”

english_verse: These things happened before kings ruled Israel. The Tribe of Dan Takes Micah's Priest and Idols About this time, the tribe of Dan was looking for a place to live. The other tribes had land, but the people of Dan did not really have any to call their own.
translation_verse: Di ʒiɛmani maa ni naa daa ka Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ni. Di saha maa ka Dan zuliya niriba daa lihiri bɔri luɣ’ shɛli ni bɛ ʒini, dama Izraɛlnim’ ni daa pirigi tiŋgbɔŋ maa ti tab’ la, bɛ daa na bi ti ba bɛ tiŋgbani.

english_verse: The tribe chose five warriors to represent their clans and told them, “Go and find some land where we can live.” The warriors left the area of Zorah and Eshtaol and went into the hill country of Ephraim. One night they stayed at Micah's house,
translation_verse: Ka Dan zuliya niriba maa daa pii bɛ ni niriba anu bɛn mali suhukpeeni n-tim ba ka bɛ yi Zɔra mini Ɛshitaol chaŋ ni bɛ ti sɔɣ’ kaai tiŋgbɔŋ maa n-zahim li nya. Bɛ daa yɛli ba mi, “Chamiya ti sɔɣ’ kaai tiŋgbɔŋ maa nya.” Ka bɛ daa ka Ifriim zuliya niriba zoya zuɣu tiŋ’ maa ni na ti kpe Maika yiŋa.

english_verse: because they heard the young Levite talking, and they knew from his accent that he was from the south. They asked him, “What are you doing here? Who brought you here?”
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa be Maika yiŋ’ maa, ka bɛ nya nachimbil’ ŋun nyɛ Lɛvi zuliya nir’ maa m-baŋ o o yɛtɔɣa puuni, ka bɔh’ o, “Ŋuni n-lee tah’ a kpe na? Ka bɔ ka a lee niŋdi kpe? Bee tuun’ bɔ ka a lee tumdi kpe?”

english_verse: The Levite replied, “Micah hired me as his priest.” Then he told them how well Micah had treated him.
translation_verse: Ka o yɛli ba, “Maika ni chɛ ka n niŋdi shɛm m-bɔŋɔ: O bu ma la paa ka n nyɛ o maligumaana.”

english_verse: “Please talk to God for us,” the men said. “Ask God if we will be successful in what we are trying to do.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ yɛl’ o, “Ti suhir’ a, bɔhim’ Naawuni nya ti ni di nasara ti chandi ŋɔ ni.”

english_verse: “Don't worry,” answered the priest. “The Lord is pleased with what you are doing.”
translation_verse: Ka maligumaana maa daa yɛli ba, “Chamiya ni suhudoo. Yawɛ nuu pa yi zuɣu yi chandi maa ni.”

english_verse: The five men left and went to the town of Laish, whose people were from Sidon, but Sidon was too far away to protect them. Even though their town had no walls, the people thought they were safe from attack. So they had not asked anyone else for protection, which meant that the tribe of Dan could easily take over Laish.
translation_verse: Ka niriba anu maa daa ŋmaligi chaŋ Laishi ti nya ka nimaani niriba bela alaafee biɛhigu. Bɛ daa bemi kaman Sidɔnnima. Bɛ daa nyɛla ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn be baalim ka ka zilisigu. Bɛ daa mali buni, ka dunia ŋɔ ni binshɛli bi pooi ba. Bɛ mini Sidɔnnim’ shee daa wɔɣa, ka bɛ mini so daa ka jina.

english_verse: The five men went back to Zorah and Eshtaol, where their relatives asked, “Did you find any land?”
translation_verse: Niriba anu maa ni daa lab’ Zɔra mini Ɛshitaol bɛ mabihi maa sani, bɛ daa bɔhi ba mi, “Ka lahibal’ bɔ ka yi lee ʒina?”

english_verse: “Let's go!” the five men said. “We saw some very good land with enough room for all of us, and it has everything we will ever need. What are you waiting for? Let's attack and take it. You'll find that the people think they're safe, but God is giving the land to us.”
translation_verse: Yi yi chaŋ, yi ni nya ka niriba maa nyɛla bɛn ka zilisigu. Di nyɛla tiŋgban’ titali, ka nir’ ni bɔri binshɛlikam dunia ŋɔ ni be di ni; yɛlimaŋli, Naawuni mi zaŋ li tin ya.”

english_verse: Six hundred men from the tribe of Dan strapped on their weapons and left Zorah and Eshtaol with their families.
translation_verse: Ka Dan zuliya niriba maa ninvuɣ’ kɔbisiyɔbu daa lo tɔbu yi Zɔra mini Ɛshitaol

english_verse: One night they camped near Kiriath-Jearim in the territory of Judah, and that's why the place just west of Kiriath-Jearim is still known as Dan's Camp.
translation_verse: n-chaŋ ti dɔni sansani Kiriatijiarim Juda tiŋgbɔŋ ni. Ka di zuɣu daa chɛ ka bɛ boli nimaani yuli, Mahanɛdan hal ni zuŋɔ. Di mi bela Kiriatijiarim wulinluhili polo.

english_verse: Then they went into the hill country of Ephraim. When they came close to Micah's house,
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yi nimaani chaŋ Ifriim tiŋgban’ ni zoya zuɣu tiŋ’ maa ni ti kpe Maika yiŋa.

english_verse: the five men who had been spies asked the other warriors, “Did you know that someone in this village has several idols and a sacred priestly vest? What do you think we should do about it?”
translation_verse: Di saha ka niriba anu shɛb’ bɛn daa pun chaŋ ti sɔɣ’ kaai Laishi tiŋgbani maa la daa yɛli bɛ tab’ maa, “Yi mi ni duri ŋɔ ni tan’ shɛli din ŋmani mukuru mini binnan’ bihi ni anzinfa binnani ni dari binnan’ shɛli beni? Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ, baŋmiya yi ni yɛn niŋ shɛm.”

english_verse: “Quiet!” the men said. “Keep your mouth shut and listen. Why don't you come with us and be our priest, so you can tell us what God wants us to do? You could stay here and be a priest for one man's family, but wouldn't you rather be the priest for a clan or even a whole tribe of Israel?”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ yɛl’ o, “Kul shini a noli. Zaŋm’ a nuu pɔb’ a noli, ka dol’ ti ti leei ti ba ni ti maligumaana. A yi nyɛ ninvuɣ’ yino maligumaana ni a yi nyɛ Izraɛl daŋ yini maligumaana, dini n-lee so?”

english_verse: The priest really liked that idea. So he took the vest and the idols and joined the others
translation_verse: Ka di daa niŋ maligumaana maa suhupiɛlli, ka o kpuɣi tan’ shɛli din ŋmani mukuru maa mini binnan’ bihi ni dari binnani maa n-kpe m-be niriba maa sunsuuni ka bɛ chana.

english_verse: from the tribe of Dan. Then they turned and left, after putting their children, their cattle, and the rest of their other possessions in front.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa chɛ ka bɛ bihi mini bɛ niɣi ni bɛn ʒiri bɛ nɛma be tooni, ka bɛ ŋmaligi doli.

english_verse: They had traveled for some time before Micah asked his neighbors to help him get his things back. He and his men caught up with the people of Dan
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa yi Maika yiŋ’ maa chaŋ ha, ka Maika daa kuhi bol’ o ʒiʒiinitaba n-chɛ ka bɛ pah’ o zuɣu ka bɛ kari Dan zuliya niriba maa naba.

english_verse: and shouted for them to stop. They turned to face him and asked, “What's wrong? Why did you bring all these men?”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa kuhi boli Dan zuliya niriba maa, ka bɛ ŋmaligina bɔhi Maika, “Bɔ n-chɛ ka a zaŋ salo ŋɔ tatabo pa amaŋ’ zuɣu na?”

english_verse: Micah answered, “You know what's wrong. You stole the gods I made, and you took my priest. I don't have anything left.”
translation_verse: Ka Maika bɔhi ba, “Bɔzuɣu ka yi bɔhi ma ni bɔ n-chɛ ka n zaŋ niriba ŋɔ pa mmaŋ’ zuɣu na? Yi kpuɣila n wuna, ka zaŋ m maligumaana pahi, ka bɔ ka yi lee chɛ n-ti mani?”

english_verse: “We don't want to hear any more about it,” the people of Dan said. “And if you make us angry, you'll only get yourself and your family killed.”
translation_verse: Ka Dan zuliya niriba maa yɛl’ o, “Miri ka a chɛ ka ti niriba ŋɔ wum a damli, ka bɛ puuni suhuyiɣisilinim’ lu a zuɣu n-ku a min’ a yiŋnima.”

english_verse: After saying this, they turned and left. Micah realized there was no way he could win a fight with them, and so he went back home. The Tribe of Dan Captures Laish
translation_verse: Ka Dan zuliya niriba maa daa ŋmaligi chaŋ. Maika ni daa nya ka bɛ mali kpiɔŋ gar’ o maa, ka o ŋmaligi lab’ kuli.

english_verse: The tribe of Dan took Micah's priest and the things Micah had made, and headed for Laish, which was located in a valley controlled by the town of Beth-Rehob. Laish was defenseless, because it had no walls and was too far from Sidon for the Sidonians to help defend it. The leaders of Laish had not even asked nearby towns to help them in case of an attack. The warriors from Dan made a surprise attack on Laish, killing everyone and burning it down. Then they rebuilt the town and settled there themselves.
translation_verse: Ka so daa kani n-ni fa ba bahi, dama bɛ ya maa mini Sidɔn daa wɔɣ’ pam. Ka bɛ mi mini so daa ka jina ni taba. Bɛ tiŋ’ maa daa bela Bɛtirɛhɔb vinvamli ni. Ka Dan zuliya niriba maa daa lab’ mali tiŋ’ maa me n-ʒini.

english_verse: But they named it Dan, after one of Israel's sons, who was the ancestor of their tribe.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa zaŋ bɛ yabidoo Dan ŋun daa nyɛ Izraɛl bia la yuli m-boli tiŋ’ maa. Amaa tiŋ’ maa yuli daa tuui boonila Laishi.

english_verse: Before kings ruled Israel, a Levite was living deep in the hill country of the Ephraim tribe. He married a woman from Bethlehem in Judah,
translation_verse: Saha shɛli naa ni daa ka Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ni la, ka Lɛvi zuliya do’ so daa zaŋ o mam ŋun yi Bɛtilihɛm Juda tiŋgbɔŋ ni n-kuli Ifriim tiŋgban’ ni zoya zuɣu tinshee din be katiŋa.

english_verse: but she was unfaithful and went back to live with her family in Bethlehem. Four months later
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ maa daa ti je suli niŋ o, ka zo n-kul’ o ba yiŋ’ Bɛtilihɛm Juda tiŋgbɔŋ ni ti niŋ chira anahi nimaani.

english_verse: her husband decided to try and talk her into coming back. So he went to Bethlehem, taking along a servant and two donkeys. He talked with his wife, and she invited him into her family's home. Her father was glad to see him
translation_verse: Ka doo maa daa ti yiɣisi ni o kar’ o naba ti balim o zaŋ o lab’ o yiŋa. Lɛvi zuliya doo maa daa zaŋla o tumtumda pah’ omaŋ’ zuɣu ka bɛ zaŋ buns’ ayi chaŋ. Ka o daa mali ti paari paɣ’ maa ba yiŋa, ka paɣ’ maa ba maa nya o ka chaŋ ti tuh’ o soli ni suhupiɛlli.

english_verse: and did not want him to leave. So the man stayed three days, eating and drinking with his father-in-law.
translation_verse: Ka o deemba ŋun daa nyɛ paɣ’ maa ba yɛli Lɛvi zuliya doo maa ni o kpalimmi gbe, ka o daa kpalim gbe daba ata. Ka bɛ daa laɣindi diri ka nyura, ka o gbɛri nimaani.

english_verse: When everyone got up on the fourth day, the Levite started getting ready to go home. But his father-in-law said, “Don't leave until you have a bite to eat. You'll need strength for your journey.”
translation_verse: Di daba anahi dali ka bɛ daa daŋ yibu asibaasi m-mali shili ni bɛ kuli, amaa ka paɣ’ maa ba maa yɛl’ o deemba maa, “Ʒinimi suug’ a noli n-nya kpiɔŋ ka naanyi chaŋ.”

english_verse: The two men sat down together and ate a big meal. “Come on,” the man's father-in-law said. “Stay tonight and have a good time.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka bɛ niriba ayi maa daa laɣim ʒini di ka nyu. Ka paɣ’ maa ba maa daa yɛli doo maa, “Niŋm’ ania kpalim gbe m-pahi, ka chɛ ka a suhu piɛla.”

english_verse: The Levite tried to leave, but his father-in-law insisted, and he spent one more night there.
translation_verse: Ka doo maa daa ti lan yiɣisi ni o kuli, ka o deemba maa lan balim o hal ka o ti lan gbe yaha.

english_verse: The fifth day, the man got up early to leave, but his wife's father said, “You need to keep up your strength! Why don't you leave right after lunch?” So the two of them started eating.
translation_verse: Di daba anu dali ka o daa ti daŋ yiɣisibu asibaasi ni o kuli, ka paɣ’ maa ba maa lan yɛl’ o, “Niŋm’ suɣilo suug’ a noli, ka chɛ ka di bii na pɔi ka a naanyi chaŋ.” Ka bɛ niriba ayi maa daa laɣim ʒini di.

english_verse: Finally, the Levite got up from the meal, so he and his wife and servant could leave. “Look,” his father-in-law said, “it's already late afternoon, and if you leave now, you won't get very far before dark. Stay with us one more night and enjoy yourself. Then you can get up early tomorrow morning and start home.”
translation_verse: Ka doo maa min’ o mam maa ni o tumtumda la daa ti yiɣisi ni bɛ kuli, ka o deemba ŋun nyɛ paɣ’ maa ba maa yɛl’ o, “Nyama wuntaŋ’ dalimya pam, ka di ku lan yuui ka yuŋ zibi, n suhir’ a, kpalimmi gbe, ka chɛ ka a suhu piɛla. Biɛɣuni ka yi sa daŋ yiɣisibu asibaasi kuli.”

english_verse: They walked on and reached Gibeah in the territory of Benjamin just after sunset.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa gari nimaani n-lan gbaai chandi, zaŋ chaŋ wuntaŋ’ ti yɛn lu ka bɛ paai Gibia din daa be Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba tiŋgban’ ni la.

english_verse: They left the road and went into Gibeah. But the Levite couldn't find a house where anyone would let them spend the night, and they sat down in the open area just inside the town gates.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa ŋmaligi nimaani n-nya luɣ’ shɛli ʒini ni bɛ gbe Gibia, dama so daa bi zaŋ ba ti kpɛh’ o yiŋa ni bɛ gbe.

english_verse: Soon an old man came in through the gates on his way home from working in the fields. Most of the people who lived in Gibeah belonged to the tribe of Benjamin, but this man was originally from the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa be nimaani maa ka ninkur’ so ti yi o puuni na zaawuni. Doo maa daa yila Ifriim zuliya niriba tiŋgban’ ni zoya ni tiŋ’ ni na ti be Gibia maa. Amaa nimaaninim’ daa nyɛla Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba.

english_verse: He noticed that the Levite was just in town to spend the night. “Where are you going?” the old man asked. “Where did you come from?”
translation_verse: Ka o daa ti kpuɣ’ o zuɣu lihi nya sochanda ka o ʒi tiŋ’ maa sokpaŋa; ka ninkurigu maa bɔh’ o, “Ya ka a yina? Bee ya ka a lee chana?”

english_verse: “We've come from Bethlehem in Judah,” the Levite answered. “We went there on a visit. Now we're going to the place where the Lord is worshiped, and later we will return to our home in the hill country of Ephraim. But no one here will let us spend the night in their home.
translation_verse: Ka Lɛvi zuliya doo maa yɛl’ o, “Ti yila Bɛtilihɛm din be Juda tiŋgbɔŋ ni n-gariti kuni Ifriim zuliya niriba tiŋgban’ ni zoya ni tiŋ’ din be katiŋa ka nyɛ n ni yi luɣ’ shɛl’ na la. N daa chaŋla Bɛtilihɛm Juda tiŋgbɔŋ ni, ka labiri kuna, ka so mi bi zaŋ ma ti kpɛh’ o yiŋa.

english_verse: We brought food for our donkeys and bread and wine for ourselves, so we don't need anything except a place to sleep.”
translation_verse: Ti mali mɔri mini difu din ni ti ti bunsi ŋɔ, ka mali m min’ a bipuɣiŋga ŋɔ ni nachimbil’ so ŋun be tinim’ a daba ŋɔ sani ŋɔ bindirigu mini wain. Ti mali ti ni bɔri binshɛlikam.”

english_verse: The old man said, “You are welcome to spend the night in my home and to be my guest, but don't stay out here!”
translation_verse: Ka ninkurigu maa daa yɛl’ o, “Naawuni chɛ ka yi suhuri doya. N ni tin ya yi ni bɔri shɛlikam, amaa lee di gbɛnya palo ŋɔ ni.”

english_verse: The old man brought them into his house and fed their donkeys. Then he and his guests washed their feet and began eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Ka o daa zaŋ ba kul o yiŋa nti chɛ ka bɛ paɣi bɛ naba, ka di ka nyu. Ka o daa bo difu ti bɛ bunsi la gba.

english_verse: They were having a good time, when some worthless men of that town surrounded the house and started banging on the door and shouting, “A man came to your house tonight. Send him out, so we can have sex with him!”
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa ti diri bindirigu saha shɛli, bɛ nini nyabu yim ka tiŋ’ maa ni ninvuɣ’ galima shɛb’ daa ti kana ti teei gili yili maa kpahiri di dunoli ka yɛri ninkurigu ŋun nyɛ yil’ maa lan’ maa, “Zaŋm’ do’ so ŋun kpe a yili ŋɔ na la ti ti ka ti gol’ o!”

english_verse: The old man went outside and said, “My friends, please don't commit such a horrible crime against a man who is a guest in my house.
translation_verse: Ka yil’ maa lana daa yi bɛ sani ti yɛli ba, “M mabihi, doo maa nyɛla n sana, dinzuɣu di tumiya tuun’ biɛɣu ŋɔ bee n-tum vi tuuni ŋɔ.

english_verse: Let me send out my daughter instead. She's a virgin. And I'll even send out the man's wife. You can rape them or do whatever else you want, but please don't do such a horrible thing to this man.”
translation_verse: Nyamiya, m bipuɣiŋga ŋun na ʒi doo mini doo maa mam m-bɔŋɔ; chɛliya ka n zaŋ ba tin ya na pumpɔŋɔ; ka yi niŋ ba yi ni bɔri shɛm, amaa di tumiya doo ŋɔ ŋun’ vi tuun’ shɛli.”

english_verse: The men refused to listen, so the Levite grabbed his wife and shoved her outside. The men raped her and abused her all night long. Finally, they let her go just before sunrise,
translation_verse: Amaa ka niriba maa zaɣisi ni bɛ ku wum o ni yɛli shɛm maa. Ka Lɛvi zuliya doo maa daa zaŋ o mam maa yihi ti ti ba; ka bɛ daa zaŋ o goli yuŋ maa zaa hal ti neei biɛɣu. Ka biɛɣu daa ti neerina ka bɛ zaŋ o bahi ka o chaŋ.

english_verse: and it was almost daybreak when she went back to the house where her husband was staying. She collapsed at the door and lay there until sunrise.
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ maa daa kana ti lu n-dɔni ninkurigu maa yiŋ’ dunol’ ni Lɛvi zuliya doo maa ni daa kpe shɛl’ la biɛkaali saha n-do nimaani hal ka di ti neei.

english_verse: About that time, her husband woke up and got ready to leave. He opened the door and went outside, where he found his wife lying at the door with her hands on the doorstep.
translation_verse: Ka doo maa daa ti yiɣisi asibaasi n-yooi dunoli ni o yina chaŋ, ka nya ka o mam maa dola yil’ maa samban’ dunol’ ni, ka o nuhi teei tiri dunoli polo.

english_verse: “Get up!” he said. “It's time to leave.” But his wife didn't move. He lifted her body onto his donkey and left.
translation_verse: Ka o yɛli paɣ’ maa, “yiɣisim’ ka ti chaŋ.” Amaa ka o bi garigi. Ka o daa kpuɣi paɣ’ maa pa o buŋ’ zuɣu n-zaŋ o kul’ o ya.

english_verse: When he got home, he took a butcher knife and cut her body into twelve pieces. Then he told some messengers, “Take one piece to each tribe of Israel
translation_verse: Ka o daa mal’ ti paai yiŋa m-bo sua pa o mam maa zuɣu ŋ-ŋmah’ o niŋkpil’ pinaayi n-zaŋ o niŋkpil’ yini kam tim ti ti Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ maa yaɣili kam nim’ zaa.

english_verse: and ask everyone if anything like this has ever happened since Israel left Egypt. Tell them to think about it, talk it over, and tell us what should be done.” Everyone who saw a piece of the body said, “This is horrible! Nothing like this has ever happened since the day Israel left Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ka ŋunkam daa nya li yɛli, “yɛlli ŋɔ tatabo na ʒi n-niŋ bee ti nini na ʒi n-nya lala Izraɛlnim’ ni daa yi Ijipti na dahin shɛl’ la hal ni zuŋɔ. Ti tɛhimi di yɛla. Ti gbaamiya saawara baŋ ti ni yɛn yɛli di yɛla shɛm.”

english_verse: The husband of the murdered woman answered: My wife and I went into the town of Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.
translation_verse: Ka Lɛvi zuliya doo ŋun nyɛ bɛ ni daa ku so mam maa yɛli ba, “M mini m mam n-daa chaŋ Gibia din nyɛ Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba tiŋ’ la ni ni ti ti gbe.

english_verse: It was a terrible thing for Israelites to do! So I cut up her body and sent the pieces everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Ka n daa ŋmahiŋmahi m mam maa jilajila n-zaŋ tari Izraɛlnim’ ni su luɣ’ shɛlikam zaa, dama bɛna n-tum din chihiri ŋɔ mini biŋkɔb’ tuuni ŋɔ Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni maa.

english_verse: You are the people of Israel, and you must decide today what to do about the men of Gibeah.
translation_verse: Nyama, yinim’ Izraɛlnim’ zaa bɛn be kpe ŋɔ, zahimmiya yɛlli maa nya ka wuhi ti ni yɛn gbaai li shɛm.”

english_verse: The whole army was in agreement, and they said, “None of us will go home.
translation_verse: Ka niriba maa zaa daa yiɣisi zani naŋgban’ yini yɛli, “Ti ni so ku lab’ kul’ o tanti ni bee o yiŋa.

english_verse: Everyone agreed that Gibeah had to be punished.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Izraɛlnim’ zaa daa laɣim naŋgban’ yini ni bɛ chaŋ ti liri Gibianima.

english_verse: The tribes of Israel sent messengers to every town and village in Benjamin. And wherever the messengers went, they said, “How could those worthless men in Gibeah do such a disgusting thing?
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa tim tuumba Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba maa zaa sani nti bɔhi ba, “Tuumbiɛ’ bɔ ka yi lee tum la?

english_verse: We can't allow such a terrible crime to go unpunished in Israel! Hand the men over to us, and we will put them to death.” But the people of Benjamin refused to listen to the other Israelites.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ yihimiya Gibia ninvuɣ’ galima bɛn tum lala maa na ka ti ku ba, ka lala tuuni maa vuui ka chɛ Izraɛlnima.” Amaa ka Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba maa daa zaɣisi ni bɛ ku wum bɛ mabihi Izraɛlnim’ maa ni yɛli shɛm maa.

english_verse: Men from towns all over Benjamin's territory went to Gibeah and got ready to fight Israel.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba maa daa yi bɛ tinsi ni n-laɣim Gibia na ni bɛ ti lo tɔbu chaŋ ti tuhi Izraɛlnima.

english_verse: The next morning the Israelite army moved its camp to a place near Gibeah.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa yiɣisi asibaasi n-chaŋ ti dɔni sansani miri Gibia.

english_verse: Then they left their camp and got into position to attack the army of Benjamin. The War Between Israel and Benjamin
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa zaŋ bɛ tɔbbihi chaŋ ti zani Gibia ni bɛ liri Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba maa.

english_verse: Benjamin's soldiers came out of Gibeah and attacked, and when the day was over,
translation_verse: Ka Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba maa daa yi Gibia na ti tuhi ku Izraɛlnim’ tɔbbihi tuhi’ pisinaayi dindali maa.

english_verse: The people of Israel went to the place of worship at Bethel, where the sacred chest was being kept. They sat on the ground, crying and not eating for the rest of the day. Then about sunset, they offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing. Phinehas the priest then prayed, “Our Lord, the people of Benjamin are our relatives. Should we stop fighting or attack them again?” “Attack!” the Lord answered. “Tomorrow I will let you defeat them.”
translation_verse: Di saha maa, Naawuni Daalikauli Adaka la daa bela nimaani, ka Ɛliɛza bia Finɛhas ŋun daa nyɛ Aduna yaaŋa la daa su di tuma fukumsi, ka niriba maa daa bɔhi Yawɛ, “Ti cham’ ti lan tuhi ti mabihi bɛn nyɛ Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba la bee ti di chaŋ?” Ka Yawɛ garigi yɛli ba, “Chamiya; dama biɛɣuni n sa ni chɛ ka yi nyaŋ ba.”

english_verse: The Israelites surrounded Gibeah, but stayed where they could not be seen.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa chɛ ka bɛ tɔbbihi chaŋ ti sɔɣ’ dɔni gili Gibia.

english_verse: The men of Benjamin headed down the road toward the desert, trying to escape from the Israelites. But the Israelites stayed right behind them, keeping up their attack. Men even came out of the nearby towns to help kill the men of Benjamin,
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka bɛ daa ŋmaligi Izraɛlnim’ maa tooni guui kpa mɔɣu polo, amaa bɛ daa bi tooi zo n-tiligi. Bɛn daa yi tiŋ’ maa puuni na la daa taɣi ba niŋ sunsuuni n-ku bɛ zaa.

english_verse: who were having to fight on all sides. The Israelite soldiers never let up their attack. They chased and killed the warriors of Benjamin as far as a place directly east of Gibeah,
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa gili Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba maa niŋ sunsuuni n-kari doli ba kuri ba n-zaŋ Nɔha hal ti paai Gibia wulimpuhili polo.

english_verse: Twenty-five thousand soldiers of Benjamin died that day, all of them experienced warriors.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba bɛn daa kpi dindali maa kalinli daa yiɣisila tuhi’ pisinaanu. Ka bɛ zaa daa nyɛla takɔbichɛriba ni tɔbutuhiri’ biinsi.

english_verse: The Israelites turned back and went to every town in Benjamin's territory, killing all the people and animals, and setting the towns on fire.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa ŋmaligi lu Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba bɛn kpalim zuɣu n-zaŋ takɔbi ku ninsalinim’ mini biŋkɔbiri ni bɛ ni daa nya binneen’ shɛb’ zaa; ka daa niŋ buɣim nyo fɔntin’ shɛŋa din daa kpalim zaa.

english_verse: When the Israelites had met at Mizpah before the war with Benjamin, they had made this sacred promise: “None of us will ever let our daughters marry any man from Benjamin.”
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa ti laɣim Mizipa m-po pɔri yɛli, “Ti ni so ku zaŋ o bipuɣiŋga ti Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba ni doo.”

english_verse: After the war with Benjamin, the Israelites went to the place of worship at Bethel and sat there until sunset. They cried loudly and bitterly
translation_verse: Di saha ka Izraɛlnim’ maa daa chaŋ Bɛtɛl ti teei ʒini Naawuni tooni nimaani n-duhi bɛ yee kum pam ka fabili yɛli,

english_verse: and prayed, “Our Lord, you are the God of Israel. Why did you let this happen? Now one of our tribes is almost gone.”
translation_verse: “Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Izraɛl Naawuni ŋɔ, Bɔ n-lee chɛ ka yɛlli ŋɔ tatabo ti niŋ Izraɛlnim’ ni? Di chaŋ wula ka daŋ yini niriba ti ka Izraɛlnim’ kalinli ni?”

english_verse: Early the next morning, the Israelites built an altar and offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing.
translation_verse: Ka biɛɣu daa neei ka niriba maa daŋ yiɣisibu me bimbini zali nimaani, ka mali sara shɛli bɛ ni zaŋdi nyɔri buɣim la mini suhudoo sara.

english_verse: Then they asked each other, “Did any of the tribes of Israel fail to come to the place of worship? We made a sacred promise that anyone who didn't come to the meeting at Mizpah would be put to death.”
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ maa daa bɔhi, “Daŋ shɛli beni ka di niriba bi ka Mizipa na Yawɛ sani laɣiŋgu ŋɔ ni?” Dama bɛ daa pun pola pɔri yɛli ni ninvuɣ’ so ŋun bi ka Mizipa na Yawɛ sani laɣiŋgu maa ni, bɛn’ kum’ o.

english_verse: The Israelites were sad about what had happened to the Benjamin tribe, and they said, “One of our tribes was almost wiped out.
translation_verse: Ka nandahima daa gbaai Izraɛlnima bɛ mabihi Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba maa zuɣu, ka bɛ yɛli, “Daŋ yini niriba ka Izraɛlnim’ kalinli ni zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ.

english_verse: Only a few men of Benjamin weren't killed in the war. We need to get wives for them, so the tribe won't completely disappear. But how can we do that, after promising in the Lord's name that we wouldn't let them marry any of our daughters?”
translation_verse: Ka wula ka ti lee yɛn niŋ nya paɣiba ti bɛ ni shɛb’ bɛn kpalim la? Dama ti pun po Yawɛ sani ni ti ni so di zaŋ o bipuɣiŋga ti ba.”

english_verse: The warriors attacked Jabesh in Gilead, and returned to their camp at Shiloh in Canaan with
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa nya paɣisar’ shɛb’ bɛn nyɛ paɣipiɛlisi kɔbisinahi Jabɛshigiliadnim’ maa ni n-zaŋ ba kuli Shilo sansani din be Keenan tiŋgbɔŋ ni la na.

english_verse: The Israelites met and sent messengers to the men of Benjamin at Rimmon Rock, telling them that the Israelites were willing to make peace with them.
translation_verse: Di saha ka salo maa zaa daa tim tuumba Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba bɛn daa be Rimɔn tampiŋ gbin’ la sani nti yɛli ba ni bɛ ku bɛ mini ba zabili la.

english_verse: So the men of Benjamin came back from Rimmon Rock, and the Israelites let them marry the young women from Jabesh. But there weren't enough women.
translation_verse: Ka Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba maa daa labina, di saha maa ka bɛ daa zaŋ Jabɛshigiliad paɣ’ shɛb’ bɛ ni daa bi kula ti ba. Amaa ka bɛ daa lee bi saɣi ba.

english_verse: The Israelites were very sad, because the Lord had almost wiped out one of their tribes.
translation_verse: Ka nandahima daa gbaai Izraɛlnim’ zaŋ chaŋ Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba maa polo, Yawɛ ni daa chɛ ka Izraɛlnim’ noya woligi la zuɣu.

english_verse: Then their leaders said: All the women of the Benjamin tribe were killed. How can we get wives for the men of Benjamin who are left?
translation_verse: Ka salo maa kpamba daa yɛli, “Ti mi pun ku Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba paɣiba zaa. Ka wula ka ti lee yɛn niŋ nya paɣiba ti bɛ ni bɛn kpalim ŋɔ?”

english_verse: But we can't let the men of Benjamin marry any of our daughters. We made a sacred promise not to do that, and if we break our promise, we will be under our own curse.
translation_verse: Amaa ti mi ku tooi zaŋ ti bipuɣinsi ti ba. Dama tinim’ Izraɛlnim’ pun po n-yɛli ni ti ni so yi zaŋ o bipuɣiŋga n-ti Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba maa, noli din dim’ o.”

english_verse: Then someone suggested, “What about the Lord's Festival that takes place each year in Shiloh? It's held north of Bethel, south of Lebonah, and just east of the road that goes from Bethel to Shechem.”
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka bɛ daa yɛli, “Nyama, Yawɛ chu’ shɛli bɛ ni puhiri yuuni kam la beni, ka bɛ ni puhi li Shilo din be Bɛtɛl nuzaa polo zaŋ lab’ wulimpuhili polo solɔɣu din yi Bɛtɛl kuni Shɛkɛm, ka be Lɛbɔna nudirigu polo la.”

english_verse: The leaders told the men of Benjamin who still did not have wives: Go to Shiloh and hide in the vineyards near the festival.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ yɛli Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba maa, “Chamiya ti sɔɣi do wain tihi pur’ la ni gu.

english_verse: Wait there for the young women of Shiloh to come out and perform their dances. Then rush out and grab one of the young women, then take her home as your wife.
translation_verse: Ka Shilɔnim’ bipuɣinsi yi ti yina ni bɛ ti wa wahi, yin’ yimiya wain tihi puri maa ni na, ka yi zaa yinoyino ti gbaag’ o paɣ’ ni yɛn nyɛ so Shilɔnim’ bipuɣinsi maa ni n-zaŋ ba kuli Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba tiŋgban’ ni.

english_verse: If the fathers or brothers of these women complain about this, we'll say, “Be kind enough to let those men keep your daughter. After all, we couldn't get enough wives for all the men of Benjamin in the battle at Jabesh. And because you didn't give them permission to marry your daughters, you won't be under the curse we earlier agreed on.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ banim’ bee bɛ tizɔdɔbba yi ti kana ti yɛl’ ti di yɛla, ti ni yɛli ba, ‘Pahimiya suɣilo ka chɛ ba ti ba, dama ti bi tuhila tɔbu gbahi ba n-ti bɛ zaa yinoyino ni bɛ niŋ bɛ paɣiba maa, ka di mi pala yinima n-zaŋ ba ti ba, ka ni mali taali di zuɣu.’ ”

english_verse: The men of Benjamin went to Shiloh and hid in the vineyards. The young women soon started dancing, and each man grabbed one of them and carried her off. Then the men of Benjamin went back to their own land and rebuilt their towns and started living in them again.
translation_verse: Ka Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba maa daa shiri niŋ lala n-kpuɣi paɣiba wawariba maa ni saɣisi bɛ kalinli tariga n-ʒi ba lab’ kuli bɛmaŋmaŋ’ tiŋgban’ ni nti lab’ me bɛ tinsi ʒini di ni yaha.

english_verse: Afterwards, the rest of the Israelites returned to their homes and families. Israel Was Not Ruled by a King
translation_verse: Di saha ka Izraɛlnim’ daa wurim nimaani, ka sokam lab’ omaŋmaŋ’ daŋ niriba min’ o malibu sani, ka bɛ daa yi nimaani lab’ bɛ ni su tiŋgban’ shɛŋa ni.

english_verse: In those days Israel wasn't ruled by a king, and everyone did what they thought was right.
translation_verse: Di saha maa, naa daa ka Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ni. Dinzuɣu sokam zaa daa kul tumdila o suhu ni yu shɛm.

english_verse: Before Israel was ruled by kings, Elimelech from the clan of Ephrath lived in the town of Bethlehem. His wife was named Naomi, and their two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. But when their crops failed in Israel, they moved to the country of Moab. And while they were there,
translation_verse: Izraɛlnim’ ni daa na ka naa ka sariakaritiba n-gbib’ ba saha shɛl’ la, ka kum daa ti lu bɛ tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni. Ka do’ so ŋun daa yi Ɛfirat zuliya ni na, ka be Bɛtilihɛm Juda tiŋgbɔŋ ni ka o yuli booni Ɛlimɛlɛk la min’ o paɣ’ Naomi ni o bidibis’ ayi Malɔn mini Kiliɔn daa yiɣisi chaŋ ti ʒini Mɔab tiŋgbɔŋ ni. Bɛ ni daa be nimaani saha shɛli maa,

english_verse: Elimelech died, leaving Naomi with only her two sons.
translation_verse: ka Ɛlimɛlɛk daa ti kpi ka chɛ Naomi min’ o bidibis’ ayi maa kɔŋko.

english_verse: Later, Naomi's sons married Moabite women. One was named Orpah and the other Ruth. About ten years later,
translation_verse: Ka o bidibis’ ayi maa daa kpuɣi Mɔab paɣiba. Paɣiba maa yuya n-daa booni: Opa ni Rut.

english_verse: When Naomi heard that the Lord had given his people a good harvest, she and her two daughters-in-law got ready to leave Moab and go to Judah. As they were on their way there,
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yiɣisi n-laɣim gbaai soli kuni Juda tiŋgbɔŋ ni. Amaa ka bɛ daa ti yi soli ha,

english_verse: Naomi said to them, “Don't you want to go back home to your own mothers? You were kind to my husband and sons, and you've always been kind to me. I pray that the Lord will be just as kind to you.
translation_verse: ka Naomi yɛli ba, “Labimiya kuli yi manim’ sani. Yawɛ ŋɔ niŋmi ya nirilim kaman yi ni niŋ m mini yi yidaannim’ bɛn kpi la nirilim shɛm la.

english_verse: May he give each of you another husband and a home of your own.” Naomi kissed them. They cried
translation_verse: Yawɛ chɛ ka yi zaa yinoyino nya biɛhigu shee yi yidaannim’ yinsi.” Ka Naomi daa chɛbisi ba ka ŋmaligi. Ka paɣiba ayi maa zaa dii kuhiri

english_verse: and said, “We want to go with you and live among your people.”
translation_verse: ka yɛl’ o, “Aai! Ti ni dol’ a kul’ a niriba sani.”
