english_verse: David ran over and pulled out Goliath's sword. Then he used it to cut off Goliath's head. When the Philistines saw what had happened to their hero, they started running away.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda daa dii guui chaŋ ti du n-tam Filistia doo maa zuɣu, ka darigi ŋooi ŋun’ Filistia doo maa maŋmaŋ’ takɔbi di tɔɣu ni n-zaŋ li ku o, ka ŋma o zuɣu. Filistianim’ maa ni daa nya ka bɛ tiyaawumya maa kpi maa, ka bɛ ŋmaligi guui.

english_verse: But the soldiers of Israel and Judah let out a battle cry and went after them as far as Gath and Ekron. The bodies of the Philistines were scattered all along the road from Shaaraim to Gath and Ekron.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ mini Judanim’ daa dii yiɣisi kuhi bahi Filistianim’ maa zuɣu, n-kari dol’ ba hal ti paai Gaat mini Ɛkurɔn dunoya ni, ka di zuɣu daa chɛ ka Filistia tɔbbi’ shɛb’ bɛn nya dansi kul luri soli ni, zaŋ Shaaraim hal ti paai Gaat mini Ɛkurɔn.

english_verse: When the Israelite army returned from chasing the Philistines, they took what they wanted from the enemy camp.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ maa daa kari Filistianim’ maa ti bahi, ka lab’ bɛ suɣa ni ti di nɛma.

english_verse: David took Goliath's head to Jerusalem, but he kept Goliath's weapons in his own tent. David Becomes One of Saul's Officers
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa kpuɣi Filistia doo maa zuɣu maa n-kuli Jɛrusalɛm, amaa ka daa lee zaŋ o tɔbutuhiri’ nɛma ti niŋ ŋun’ Dauda maŋmaŋ’ suɣili ni. Bɛ zaŋ Dauda wuhi Naa Sool

english_verse: After King Saul had watched David go out to fight Goliath, Saul turned to the commander of his army and said, “Abner, who is that young man?” “Your Majesty,” Abner answered, “I swear by your life that I don't know.”
translation_verse: Sool ni daa nya ka Dauda chani ni o ti tuhi Filistia doo maa, ka o bɔhi Abinɛr ŋun daa nyɛ sapashin’ kpɛm’ la, “Ŋun’ bia n-lee nyɛ nachimbil maa?” Ka Abinɛr garigi yɛli, “Naa, nyini ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu, m bi mi.”

english_verse: “Then find out!” Saul told him.
translation_verse: Ka naa daa yɛl’ o, “Bɔhimi nya ŋun’ bia bala.”

english_verse: and Saul asked, “Who are you?” “I am David the son of Jesse, a loyal Israelite from Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: Ka Sool daa bɔh’ o, “Nachimbila, ŋun’ dapala n-lee nyɛ a?” Ka Dauda daa garigi yɛl’ o, “A dabili Jɛsi ŋun nyɛ Bɛtilihɛm nir’ la dapala n-nyɛ ma.”

english_verse: From that time on, Saul kept David in his service and would not let David go back to his own family.
translation_verse: Ka Sool daa zaŋ Dauda ti niŋ o yiŋ’ dindali maa, ka bi saɣi ni o lan kul’ o ba yiŋa.

english_verse: Jonathan liked David so much that they promised to always be loyal friends.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Jɔnatan daa lo Dauda alikauli, dama o daa yur’ o mi kaman o ni yur’ omaŋ’ shɛm la.

english_verse: Jonathan took off the robe that he was wearing and gave it to David. He also gave him his military clothes, his sword, his bow and arrows, and his belt.
translation_verse: Ka Jɔnatan daa yeeg’ omaŋmaŋ’ kparibu shɛli o ni ye n-ti Dauda, ka zaŋ o gbaɣino ti o, hal ka zaŋ o takɔbi min’ o tɔbu ni o gban’ shɛli o ni mali lɔr’ o shee ni ti o pahi.

english_verse: David was a success in everything that Saul sent him to do, and Saul made him a high officer in his army. That pleased everyone, including Saul's other officers. Saul Becomes David's Enemy
translation_verse: Ka Sool daa yi kul tim Dauda luɣ’ shɛlikam zaa, o ti nyarila nasara, lala zuɣu ka Sool daa zaŋ Dauda leei tɔbbihi zuɣulana, ka lala daa tiɣi niriba zaa nini, ka lan tiɣi Sool tumtumdiba zaa nini. Sool leei ŋun zabiri Dauda nyuli

english_verse: David had killed Goliath, the battle was over, and the Israelite army set out for home. As the army went along, women came out of each Israelite town to welcome King Saul. They were celebrating by singing songs and dancing to the music of tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Dauda ni daa ku Filistia doo maa ka labina ka bɛ kuni yiŋa, ka paɣiba daa yi Izraɛl tinsi zaa ni na n-yiini suhupiɛlli yila, ka ŋmɛri biŋkumda ka chaɣisiri chaɣisanim’ wari waa kanna ni bɛ ti tuhi Naa Sool soli.

english_verse: They sang: Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!
translation_verse: Ka paɣiba maa suhuri daa paligi ka bɛ yiini yila yɛri taba, “Sool kula tuhilituhili, ka Dauda mi ku tuhi’ piapia.”

english_verse: This song made Saul very angry, and he thought, “They are saying that David has killed ten times more enemies than I ever did. Next they will want to make him king.”
translation_verse: Ka Sool suhu daa yiɣisi pam, dama yɛtɔɣa maa daa bi niŋ o nyaɣisim ka o yɛli, “Bɛ zaŋ tuhi’ piapia ti Dauda, ka zaŋla tuhilituhili ti m mi, ka bɔ n-lee lan kpalim ka pa ni n nam ŋɔ ka o yɛn deei?”

english_verse: The next day the Lord let an evil spirit take control of Saul, and he began acting like a crazy man inside his house. David came to play the harp for Saul as usual, but this time Saul had a spear in his hand.
translation_verse: N-daa yi biɛɣu ka Naawuni chɛ ka alizin’ biɛɣu siɣi Naa sol zuɣu na, ka o be o yiŋ’ tahira, ka Dauda daa yaa ŋmɛri mɔɣilo niŋd’ o kaman o ni daa yi pun niŋdi shɛm dabisili kam la, ka Sool daa gbib’ o kpani o nuu ni;

english_verse: Saul thought, “I'll pin David to the wall.” He threw the spear at David twice, but David dodged and got away both times.
translation_verse: ka tɛh’ o suhu ni ni o dii zaŋ kpani maa to Dauda tabili dukpini, amaa ka Dauda daa fɔhi li buyi zaa.

english_verse: Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord was helping David and was no longer helping him.
translation_verse: Ka dabiɛm daa gbaai Sool zaŋ chaŋ Dauda polo, dama Yawɛ daa chɛ ŋun’ Sool, ka bela Dauda sani.

english_verse: The Lord helped David, and he and his soldiers always won their battles.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yi kul chaŋ luɣ’ shɛlikam o dirila nasara; dama Yawɛ daa be o sani.

english_verse: But everyone else in Judah and Israel was loyal to David, because he led the army in battle.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Izraɛlnim’ mini Judanim’ zaa daa yuri Dauda, dama ŋuna n-daa yi zaŋdi ba chani tɔb’ ni ka zaŋdi ba labirina. Dauda kpuɣi Sool bipuɣiŋga

english_verse: One day, Saul told David, “If you'll be brave and fight the Lord's battles for me, I'll let you marry my oldest daughter Merab.” But Saul was really thinking, “I don't want to kill David myself, so I'll let the Philistines do it for me.”
translation_verse: Ka Sool daa ti yɛli Dauda. “Nyama, m bipuɣin’ kpɛm’ Mɛrab m-bɔŋɔ, a yi ni mali suhukpeeni m-be n sani tuhiri Yawɛ tɔbu ŋɔ, n ni zaŋ o ti a ka a niŋ a paɣa.” Dama Naa Sool daa tɛhimi ni di bi simdi ni omaŋmaŋ’ ku Dauda, amaa ni o lee ni chɛ ka Filistianim’ ku o.

english_verse: David answered, “How could I possibly marry your daughter? I'm not very important, and neither is my family.”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yɛli Sool, “M mi lee nyɛ ŋuni, ka n daŋ niriba lee nyɛ banima bee m ba zuliya mi lee nyɛ banim’ Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ni ka n ti yɛn leei naa deemba?”

english_verse: But when the time came for David to marry Saul's daughter Merab, Saul told her to marry Adriel from the town of Meholah.
translation_verse: Amaa saha shɛli bɛ ni daa ti yɛn zaŋ Mɛrab ti Dauda, bɛ daa ŋmalig’ o mi ti do’ so ŋun yuli booni Adiriɛl ka o nyɛ Mɛholat nir’ la, ka o niŋ’ o paɣa.

english_verse: Saul had another daughter. Her name was Michal, and Saul found out that she was in love with David. This made Saul happy,
translation_verse: Di saha ka Sool bipuɣiŋga ŋun pah’ ayi ka o yuli daa booni Mikal la suhu daa yu Dauda pam, ka bɛ daa yɛli Sool di yɛla, ka di daa niŋ o nyaɣisim pam.

english_verse: and he thought, “I'll tell David he can marry Michal, but I'll set it up so that the Philistines will kill him.” He told David, “I'm going to give you a second chance to marry one of my daughters.”
translation_verse: Ka Sool daa tɛh’ o suhu ni, “N ni zaŋ o ti Dauda ka o leei tɔŋ gbaag’ o, ka Filistianim’ ku o.” Dinzuɣu ka Sool daa lan yɛli Dauda pahi buyi, “Pumpɔŋɔ a yi pa ni leei n deemba.”

english_verse: Saul ordered his officials to speak to David in private, so they went to David and said, “Look, the king likes you, and all of his officials are loyal to you. Why not ask the king if you can marry his daughter Michal?” “I'm not rich or famous enough to marry princess Michal!” David answered.
translation_verse: Ka Sool tumtumdiba maa daa yɛli Dauda yɛtɔɣa maa. Ka Dauda bɔhi ba, “Yi tɛhiya ni di nyɛla asama ni n leei naa deemba? Dama yi nya ka n nyɛla faralana, ka pa yulilana.”

english_verse: The officials went back to Saul and told him exactly what David had said.
translation_verse: Ka tumtumdiba maa daa chaŋ ti yɛli Sool Dauda ni yɛli shɛm.

english_verse: Saul was hoping that the Philistines would kill David, and he told his officials to tell David, “The king doesn't want any silver or gold. He only wants to get even with his enemies. All you have to do is to bring back proof that you have killed
translation_verse: Di saha ka Sool daa yɛli ba, “Yɛlimiya Dauda, ‘Naa bi bɔri paɣibɔr’ liɣiri a sani n-naɣi pahila Filistianim’ yokol’ gbana kɔbiga din ni chɛ ka ŋun’ naa bɔh’ o dimnim’ maa biɛri.’ ” Sool daa tɛhiya ni lala ni chɛ ka Filistianim’ maa ku Dauda.

english_verse: The officials told David, and David wanted to marry the princess. King Saul had set a time limit, and before it ran out,
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa yɛli Dauda yɛtɔɣa maa, ka di niŋ o nyaɣisim pam o ni yɛn leei naa deemba maa zuɣu. Ka bɛ ni zali saha shɛli maa daa ti yɛn paai,

english_verse: King Saul knew that she loved David, and he also realized that the Lord was helping David.
translation_verse: Amaa Sool ni daa nya ka Yawɛ be Dauda sani, ka o bipuɣiŋga Mikal gba yur’ o maa,

english_verse: But knowing those things made Saul even more afraid of David, and he was David's enemy for the rest of his life.
translation_verse: ka dabiɛm lan gbaag’ o pahi zaŋ chaŋ Dauda polo. Dinzuɣu ka Dauda daa kul nyɛ Sool dima di saha maa zaŋ chana.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers kept coming to fight Israel, but whenever David fought them, he won. He was famous because he won more battles against the Philistines than any of Saul's other officers.
translation_verse: Ka Filistia tɔbbihi daa kul lɔri tɔbu na ti tuhiri ba, amaa bɛ daa yi kul lo tɔb’ na, Dauda n-tuhiri diri nasara gariti Sool sapashinnim’ maa zaa, ka di zuɣu daa chɛ ka Dauda yuli du pam.

english_verse: One day, Saul told his son Jonathan and his officers to kill David. But Jonathan and David were best friends,
translation_verse: Ka Sool daa yɛl’ o bia Jɔnatan min’ o tumtumdiba zaa ni bɛ kum Dauda. Amaa o bia Jɔnatan daa yuri Dauda yɛla pam.

english_verse: and he warned David, “My father is trying to have you killed, so be very careful. Hide in a field tomorrow morning, and I'll bring him there. Then I'll talk to him about you, and if I find out anything, I'll let you know.”
translation_verse: N sa ni doli m ba kana nti zani baɣil’ o a ni sɔɣi luɣ’ shɛli maa ka yɛl’ o a yɛla, ka o yi sa yɛli shɛlikam, n ni yɛl’ a.”

english_verse: The next morning, Jonathan reminded Saul about the many good things David had done for him. Then he said, “Why do you want to kill David? He hasn't done anything to you. He has served in your army and has always done what's best for you. He even risked his life to kill Goliath. The Lord helped Israel win a great victory that day, and it made you happy.”
translation_verse: Dama o daa zaŋ o nyɛvili pa talima ku Filistia doo la, ka Yawɛ daa tum nasara dibu tuun’ kara ti Izraɛlnim’ zaa. A daa nya dimbɔŋɔ ka di’ niŋ a nyaɣisim, ka bɔ n-niŋ ka a bɔri ni a ku Dauda ka di ka daliri, ka di zuɣu chɛ ka a tum alahichi ŋun ka taali ʒim yihibu ni?”

english_verse: Saul agreed and promised, “I swear by the living Lord that I won't have David killed!”
translation_verse: Ka Sool daa wum Jɔnatan ni yɛl’ o shɛm maa zaa, ka po pɔri yɛli, “Hal ka Yawɛ ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu, n ku lan ku o.”

english_verse: Jonathan went to David and told him what Saul had said. Then he brought David to Saul, and David served in Saul's army just as he had done before.
translation_verse: Ka Jɔnatan daa boli Dauda na ti yɛl’ o dimbɔŋɔ zaa, ka zaŋ o tahi Sool sani, ka Dauda ti lan be o sani kaman o ni daa yi pun be o sani shɛm la.

english_verse: The next time there was a war with the Philistines, David fought hard and forced them to retreat. Michal Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Dahin shɛli ka tɔbu daa ti lan lu bɛ mini Filistianim’ sunsuuni, ka Dauda daa chaŋ ti liri ba n-tuhi nyaŋ ba, ka bɛ ŋmaligi guui.

english_verse: One night, David was in Saul's home, playing the harp for him. Saul was sitting there, holding a spear, when an evil spirit from the Lord took control of him. Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but David dodged, and it stuck in the wall. David ran out of the house and escaped.
translation_verse: Ka Sool daa ti zaŋ kpani maa m-bɔr’ ni o to Dauda tabili dukpini, amaa ka Dauda daa fɔhi Sool, ka o zaŋ kpani maa to n-nyɔɣila dukpini. Ka Dauda daa guui n-zo n-tiligi yuŋ maa.

english_verse: Saul sent guards to watch David's house all night and then to kill him in the morning. Michal, David's wife, told him, “If you don't escape tonight, they'll kill you tomorrow!”
translation_verse: Dindali maa ka Sool daa tim ninvuɣ’ shɛba ni bɛ chaŋ ti gu Dauda o yiŋa, o daa lomi ni o ku o asiba. Amaa ka Dauda paɣa Mikal daa yɛl’ o, “A yi bi tilig’ a nyɛvili yuŋ ŋɔ, biɛɣuni bɛ sa ni ku a.”

english_verse: She helped David leave through a window and climb down to the ground. As David ran off,
translation_verse: Ka Mikal daa sɔŋ Dauda ka o doli takɔro ni yi n-zo n-tiligi.

english_verse: Michal put a statue in his bed. She put goat hair on its head and dressed it in some of David's clothes.
translation_verse: Ka Mikal daa zaŋ biŋŋmahindili na ti sɔŋ garo zuɣu n-zaŋ bukɔbiri difiɛli sɔŋ zaŋ di zuɣu kuɣ’ li, ka zaŋ chinchini pil’ li.

english_verse: The next morning, Saul sent guards to arrest David. But Michal told them, “David is sick.”
translation_verse: Ka Sool daa tim tuumba ni bɛ ti zaŋ Dauda na, ka paɣ’ maa yɛli ba, “O biɛrimi.”

english_verse: Saul sent the guards back and told them, “Bring David to me—bed and all—so I can kill him.”
translation_verse: Ka Sool daa tim tuumba ni bɛ chaŋ ti nya Dauda, ka lan yɛli ba “Ʒimiy’ o min’ o garo maa zaa na ka n ti ku o.”

english_verse: When the guards went in, all they found in the bed was the statue with the goat hair on its head.
translation_verse: Ka tuumba maa daa kana ti kpe duu maa ni n-nya ka biŋŋmahindili maa do garo zuɣu, ka di zuɣu kuɣi bukɔbiri difiɛli.

english_verse: “Why have you tricked me this way?” Saul asked Michal. “You helped my enemy get away!” She answered, “He said he would kill me if I didn't help him escape!” Samuel Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Ka Sool daa bɔhi Mikal, “Bɔ n-niŋ ka a yɔhim ma lala n-chɛ ka n dim’ maa zo n-tiligi?” Ka Mikal garigi yɛl’ o, “O yɛli ma mi, ‘Chɛ ka n chaŋ; a yi bi chɛ ka n chaŋ n ni ku a.’ ”

english_verse: Meanwhile, David went to Samuel at Ramah and told him what Saul had done. Then Samuel and David went to Prophets Village and stayed there.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa zo n-chaŋ Samuɛl sani Rama ti yɛl’ o Sool ni niŋ o shɛlikam maa zaa. Ka o mini Samuɛl daa chaŋ ti be Naiɔt.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “David is at Prophets Village in Ramah.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yɛli Sool, “Nyama, Dauda be Naiɔt Rama tiŋgban’ ni.”

english_verse: Saul sent a few soldiers to bring David back. They went to Ramah and found Samuel in charge of a group of prophets who were all prophesying. Then the Spirit of God took control of the soldiers and they started prophesying too.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Sool daa tim tuumba ni bɛ chaŋ ti gbaai Dauda na. Ka bɛ daa paai ti nya anab’ bɔbili, ka bɛ tɔɣisir’ anabitali yɛtɔɣa, ka Samuɛl nyɛ bɛ zuɣulana, ka Naawuni Shia daa siɣi Sool tuumba maa zuɣu na ka bɛ gba tɔɣis’ anabitali yɛtɔɣa.

english_verse: When Saul heard what had happened, he sent some more soldiers, but they prophesied just like the first group. He sent a third group of soldiers, but the same thing happened to them.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yɛli Sool di yɛla ka o lan tim tuun’ shɛba, ka bɛ gba ti tɔɣisi anabitali yɛtɔɣa. Ka Sool daa lan tim tuun’ shɛb’ yaha m-pahi buta, ka bɛ gba daa tɔɣisi anabitali yɛtɔɣa.

english_verse: Finally, Saul left for Ramah himself. He went as far as the deep pit at the town of Secu, and he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” “At Prophets Village in Ramah,” the people answered.
translation_verse: Di saha ka omaŋmaŋ’ daa yiɣisi chaŋ Rama nti chaŋ kɔbil’ titali din be Sɛku la gbini ti bɔhi, “Ya ka Samuɛl mini Dauda lee be la?” Ka so yɛl’ o, “Nyama bɛ be Naiɔt Rama tiŋgban’ ni.”

english_verse: Saul left for Ramah. But as he walked along, the Spirit of God took control of him, and he started prophesying. Then, when he reached Prophets Village,
translation_verse: Di saha ka Sool daa lu soli chani Naiɔt Rama tiŋgban’ ni, ka Naawuni Shia daa siɣ’ o zuɣu na, ka o gba dii gbaai anabitali yɛtɔɣa tɔɣisibu m-mali lala hal ti paai Naiɔt Rama tiŋgbani maa ni.

english_verse: he stripped off his clothes and prophesied in front of Samuel. He dropped to the ground and lay there naked all that day and night. That's how the saying started, “Is Saul now a prophet?”
translation_verse: Ka o gba daa fuɣ’ o situra zaa ka tɔɣisi anabitali yɛtɔɣa Samuɛl tooni, ka daa do o zaɣim dindali maa wuntaŋ’ ni mini yuŋ zaa. Dindali maa ka bɔhigu ŋɔ daa piligi, “Sool gba nyɛla anabi?”

english_verse: David escaped from Prophets Village. Then he ran to see Jonathan and asked, “Why does your father Saul want to kill me? What have I done wrong?”
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka Dauda daa yi Naiɔt din be Rama tiŋgban’ ni maa n-chaŋ Jɔnatan sani ti bɔh’ o, “Bɔ ka n lee niŋ? N taali nyɛ dini? Ka tuumbiɛ’ bɔ ka n lee dii tum a ba, ka o bɔri ni o ku ma?”

english_verse: “My father can't be trying to kill you! He never does anything without telling me about it. Why would he hide this from me? It can't be true!”
translation_verse: Ka Jɔnatan yɛl’ o, “Din’ kariya! A ku kpi. Nyama, m ba na ʒi n-niŋ shɛli ka di nyɛla bin’ titali bee bimbila ka bi yɛli ma. Ka bɔ zuɣu ka m ba ni sɔɣi ma dimbɔŋɔ dina? Pa lala n-nyɛ li.”

english_verse: “Jonathan, I swear it's true! But your father knows how much you like me, and he didn't want to break your heart. That's why he didn't tell you. I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I'm only one step ahead of death.”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa garigi yɛl’ o, “A ba mi ni a yuri ma, ka tɛhi ni di bi simdi ni a baŋ di yɛla, dama a yi baŋ di yɛla, di ni saɣim’ a suhu pam. Amaa yɛlimaŋli, hal ka Yawɛ ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu ni nyin’ ŋumbɔŋɔ gba zuɣu, m mini kum kul chɛla tab’ kpe ni kpe.”

english_verse: Then Jonathan said, “Tell me what to do, and I'll do it.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Jɔnatan daa yɛli Dauda, “A ni bɔri ni n niŋ shɛlikam zaa, n ni niŋ li ti a.”

english_verse: David answered: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and I'm supposed to eat dinner with your father. But instead, I'll hide in a field until the evening of the next day.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yɛli Jɔnatan, “Nyama, biɛɣuni sa nyɛla goli palli dabisili, ka di simdi ni m mini naa sa laɣim ʒini di bindirigu; amaa chɛ ka n chaŋ ti sɔɣi mɔɣu ni hal ti paai daba ata dali zaawuni.

english_verse: If Saul wonders where I am, tell him, “David asked me to let him go to his hometown of Bethlehem, so he could take part in a sacrifice his family makes there every year.”
translation_verse: Ka a ba yi ti bɔri ma ka bi nya ma, nyin’ yɛlim’ o, ‘Dauda suhi ma la soli ni o chaŋ o ya Bɛtilihɛm, dama o yiŋnim’ zaa yɛn malila yuuniyuuni sara.’

english_verse: If your father says it's all right, then I'm safe. But if he gets angry, you'll know he wants to harm me.
translation_verse: O yi yɛli, ‘Di viɛla,’ binshɛli ku lan niŋ mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ; o mi suhu yi yiɣisi, dindina nyin’ baŋmi ni o lo zaɣ’ biɛɣu.

english_verse: Be kind to me. After all, it was your idea to promise the Lord that we would always be loyal friends. If I've done anything wrong, kill me yourself, but don't hand me over to your father.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu niŋmi mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ nirilim ŋɔ, dama a chɛ ka m min’ a lo tab’ alikauli suŋ. Amaa n yi mali taali, amaŋmaŋ’ nyin’ kum’ ma, dama bɔ zuɣu ka a lan yɛn zaŋ ma chaŋ a ba sani yaha?”

english_verse: “Don't worry,” Jonathan said. “If I find out that my father wants to kill you, I'll certainly let you know.”
translation_verse: Ka Jɔnatan daa yɛl’ o, “Din’ kariya, n yi di mi ni m ba lo a zaɣ’ biɛɣu n naan ku yɛl’ a?”

english_verse: “Let's go out to this field, and I'll tell you,” Jonathan answered. When they got there,
translation_verse: Ka Jɔnatan yɛli Dauda, “Kamina ka ti chaŋ mɔɣu ni.” Ka bɛ niriba ayi maa daa yi n-chaŋ mɔɣu ni.

english_verse: Jonathan said: I swear by the Lord God of Israel, that two days from now I'll know what my father is planning. Of course I'll let you know if he's friendly toward you.
translation_verse: Ka Jɔnatan daa ti yɛli Dauda, “Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni ŋɔ di ti shɛhira, biɛɣuni ŋ-ŋɔ tasaha bee dali, n yi daa bɔhi m ba ka o bi lan lo ni o niŋ nyin’ Dauda zaɣ’ biɛɣu, n ku tim na ti yɛl’ a?

english_verse: But if he wants to harm you, I promise to tell you and help you escape. And I ask the Lord to punish me severely if I don't keep my promise. I pray that the Lord will bless you, just as he used to bless my father.
translation_verse: Amaa o suhu yi na kul yumi ni o niŋ a zaɣ’ biɛɣu, ka m bi kana ti yɛl’ a ka a zo n-tiligi ni alaafee, Yawɛ ŋun niŋmi mani Jɔnatan zaɣ’ biɛɣu n-gari m ba ni yɛn niŋ’ a shɛm maa, Yawɛ ni be a sani kaman o ni be m ba sani shɛm la.

english_verse: Someday the Lord will wipe out all of your enemies. Then if I'm still alive, please be as kind to me as the Lord has been. But if I'm dead, be kind to my family.
translation_verse: Di yih’ a ʒiɛyimtali maa n daŋ ni. Ka Yawɛ yi ti kpihim nyin’ Dauda dimnim’ zaa birili dunia ŋɔ ni,

english_verse: Jonathan and David made an agreement that even David's descendants would have to keep. Then Jonathan said, “I pray that the Lord will take revenge on your descendants if they break our promise.”
translation_verse: ŋun’ di kpihim man’ Jɔnatan yuli nyin’ Dauda daŋ ni. Yawɛ bɔhimi nyin’ Dauda dimnim’ biɛri ti a.”

english_verse: Jonathan thought as much of David as he did of himself, so he asked David to promise once more that he would be a loyal friend.
translation_verse: Ka Jɔnatan daa chɛ ka Dauda lan lo o yurilim alikauli yaha, dama o daa yur’ o mi kaman omaŋmaŋ’ la.

english_verse: After this Jonathan said: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and people will wonder where you are, because your place at the table will be empty.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Jɔnatan daa yɛl’ o, “Biɛɣuni sa nyɛla gol’ palli dabisili, ka bɛ sa ni bɔ a kɔŋ, dama a sa ku ʒi a ʒiishee.

english_verse: By the day after tomorrow, everyone will think you've been gone a long time. Then go to the place where you hid before and stay beside Going-Away Rock.
translation_verse: Dali gba bɛ daa ni bɔ a pam kɔŋ, dinzuɣu cham’ yɛla ŋɔ ni daa yiɣisina ka a sɔɣi luɣ’ shɛl’ la nti ŋuni kuɣa din duhiya la lɔŋni.

english_verse: I'll shoot three arrows at a target off to the side of the rock,
translation_verse: Ka n ni ti ka nimaani na nti to piɛma ata kaman n zahimla binshɛli ka tɔr’ la.

english_verse: and send my servant to find the arrows. You'll know if it's safe to come out by what I tell him. If it is safe, I swear by the living Lord that I'll say, “The arrows are on this side of you! Pick them up!”
translation_verse: Nyama, n ni ti tim bi’ so ka yɛl’ o, ‘Cham’ ti bo piɛma maa shee.’ N yi ti yɛl’ o, ‘Nyama, piɛma maa be a luɣili ŋɔ polo, kpuɣimi li na,’ di saha nyin’ yim’ na, dama hal ka Yawɛ ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu binshɛli ku lan niŋ a, ka barina shɛli mi lan kani.

english_verse: But if it isn't safe, I'll say to the boy, “The arrows are farther away!” This will mean that the Lord wants you to leave, and you must go.
translation_verse: Amaa n yi ti yɛli bia maa, ‘Nyama, piɛma maa be a tooni ha;’ dindina nyin’ zoma, dama Yawɛ n-wuh’ a ni a zom’ maa.

english_verse: But he will always watch us to make sure that we keep the promise we made to each other.
translation_verse: Ka di yi nyɛla m min’ a ni daa tɔɣisi yɛtɔɣ’ shɛl’ la dina, Yawɛ ni be m min’ a sunsuuni sahakam.”

english_verse: So David hid there in the field. During the New Moon Festival, Saul sat down to eat
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa sɔɣi mɔɣu maa ni. Ka gol’ palli dali maa daa ti paai, ka naa ʒini ni o di bindirigu.

english_verse: by the wall, just as he always did. Jonathan sat across from him, and Abner sat next to him. But David's place was empty.
translation_verse: Naa daa ʒinila o ʒiishee din tab’ dukpini kaman o ni daa yi pun niŋdi shɛm, ka Jɔnatan ʒiɛya, ka Abinɛr mi ʒini baɣili Sool, amaa ka Dauda ŋun’ ʒiishee daa nyɛ zaɣ’ kuŋ.

english_verse: Saul didn't say anything that day, because he was thinking, “Something must have happened to make David unfit to be at the Festival. Yes, something must have happened.”
translation_verse: Sool daa bi yɛli shɛli dindali maa, dama o daa tɛhimi, “Binshɛli n-niŋ o ka o bi be kasi, biɛhiŋ kani, o shiri bi bela kasi.”

english_verse: The day after the New Moon Festival, when David's place was still empty, Saul asked Jonathan, “Why hasn't that son of Jesse come to eat with us? He wasn't here yesterday, and he still isn't here today!”
translation_verse: N-daa lan yi biɛɣu dabisi’ shɛli din pahir’ ayi goli palli dabisili maa nyaaŋa, ka Dauda ʒiishee maa na kul nyɛla zaɣ’ kuŋ. Di saha ka Sool daa bɔh’ o dapala Jɔnatan, “Bɔ n-niŋ ka Jɛsi dapala ŋɔ bi kana bindirigu dibu shee ŋɔ sɔhila bee zuŋɔ?”

english_verse: Jonathan answered, “The reason David hasn't come to eat with you is that he begged me to let him go to Bethlehem. He said, ‘Please let me go. My family is offering a sacrifice, and my brother told me I have to be there. Do me this favor and let me slip away to see my brothers.’ ”
translation_verse: O yɛli ma mi, ‘Chɛ ka n chaŋ Bɛtilihɛm, dama n yiŋnim’ yɛn malila sara ti ya, ka m biɛli yɛli ni n kana. Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ a yi baŋ ni a nini tiɣi ma, nyin’ chɛ ka n chaŋ ti nya m biɛyanim’ maa.’ Lala zuɣu ka o bi ka nyin’ naa bindirigu ŋɔ dibu shee na maa.”

english_verse: Saul was furious with Jonathan and yelled, “You're no son of mine, you traitor! I know you've chosen to be loyal to that son of Jesse. You should be ashamed of yourself! And your own mother should be ashamed that you were ever born.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Sool suhu daa yiɣisi pam bahi Jɔnatan zuɣu, ka o yɛl’ o, “Nyin’ ŋun nyɛ paɣ’ yoli ŋun bi zani tuhi bia ŋɔ. A tɛhi’ ni m bi mi ni a zaŋ Jɛsi dapala maa kpɛh’ a kɔbili ni ni a dihila amaŋ’ vi, ka lan dih’ a ma gba vi?

english_verse: You'll never be safe, and your kingdom will be in danger as long as that son of Jesse is alive. Turn him over to me now! He deserves to die!”
translation_verse: Jɛsi dapala maa ŋun dee yi be o nyɛvili ni, nyini bee a nam kul ku nya zaashee zani. Dinzuɣu timmi ka bɛ ti zaŋ’ o na, dama di kpala talahi ni o kpi.”

english_verse: “Why do you want to kill David?” Jonathan asked. “What has he done?”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Jɔnatan daa bɔh’ o ba Sool, “Bɔ zuɣu ka a yɛn ku o? Bɔ ka o lee niŋ?”

english_verse: Saul threw his spear at Jonathan and tried to kill him. Then Jonathan was sure that his father really did want to kill David.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Sool daa zaŋ kpani to o ni o ku o; di saha ka Jɔnatan daa baŋ ni o ba shiri loya ni o ku Dauda.

english_verse: Jonathan was angry and hurt that his father had insulted David so terribly. He got up, left the table, and didn't eat anything all that day.
translation_verse: Ka Jɔnatan daa vaai yiɣisi bindirigu maa dibu shee ni suhuyiɣisili pam, ka daa bi di bindirigu goli palli daba ayi dali maa, dama Dauda yɛla daa muɣis’ o pam ni o ba ni daa dih’ o vi shɛm maa zuɣu.

english_verse: In the morning, Jonathan went out to the field to meet David. He took a servant boy along
translation_verse: N-daa yi biɛɣ’ asiba ka Jɔnatan zaŋ bia pa omaŋ’ zuɣu chaŋ mɔɣu ni kaman o mini Dauda ni daa pun tɔɣisi shɛm la.

english_verse: and told him, “When I shoot the arrows, you run and find them for me.” The boy started running, and Jonathan shot an arrow so that it would go beyond him.
translation_verse: Ka o daa ti yɛl’ o bia maa, “Zom’ chaŋ ti pihi n ni yɛn to peen’ shɛŋa ŋɔ na.” Bia maa ni daa zɔri chani maa, ka o to piɛm bah’ o tooni ha.

english_verse: When the boy got near the place where the arrow had landed, Jonathan shouted, “Isn't the arrow on past you?”
translation_verse: Bia maa ni daa ti paai Jɔnatan ni to piɛm maa bahi luɣ’ shɛli maa, ka Jɔnatan bol’ o n-yɛl’ o, “Pa piɛm maa m-be a tooni maa ha?”

english_verse: Jonathan shouted to him again, “Hurry up! Don't stop!” The boy picked up the arrows and brought them back to Jonathan,
translation_verse: O daa lan yɛli bia maa yaha, “Kpaŋmina, niŋmi yomyom, di lan ʒiɛya.” Di saha ka Jɔnatan bia maa daa pih’ o piɛma maa n-zaŋ ka o sanna.

english_verse: but he had no idea about what was going on. Only Jonathan and David knew.
translation_verse: Amaa bia maa ŋun daa bi mi di ni nyɛ shɛm, kulla Jɔnatan mini Dauda n-daa mi di ni nyɛ shɛm.

english_verse: Jonathan gave his weapons to the boy and told him, “Take these back into town.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Jɔnatan daa zaŋ o bidibbina maa ti o bia maa ka yɛl’ o, “Zaŋmi li kuli yiŋa.”

english_verse: After the boy had gone, David got up from beside the mound and bowed very low three times. Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and cried, but David cried louder.
translation_verse: Bia maa ni daa kul ŋmaligi naai, di daa bi yuui ka Dauda yi kuɣa maa lɔŋni na nti lu n-gbani n-zaŋ o nini kpa tiŋa, ka silim o zuɣu buta; ka bɛ va m-bibigi taba, ka kum niŋ taba. Dauda n-daa kum pam gari Jɔnatan.

english_verse: Jonathan said, “Take care of yourself. And remember, we each have asked the Lord to watch and make sure that we and our descendants keep our promise forever.” David left and Jonathan went back to town.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Jɔnatan daa yɛli Dauda, “Cham’ ni suhudoo, man’ dee min’ a ni daa pun lo tab’ alikauli Yawɛ yuli ni, ka yɛli ni Yawɛ be ti sani, ka ni ti lan be ti bihi gba sani sahakam ŋɔ saɣiya.” Ka Dauda daa yiɣisi chaŋ, ka Jɔnatan mi lab’ kuli.

english_verse: David went to see Ahimelech, a priest who lived in the town of Nob. Ahimelech was trembling with fear as he came out to meet David. “Why are you alone?” Ahimelech asked. “Why isn't anyone else with you?”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda daa zo n-chaŋ Nɔb nti chaŋ Ahimɛlɛk ŋun daa nyɛ maligumaana la sani. Ka Ahimɛlɛk daa kana ti tuhi Dauda soli ka o niŋ’ sɔhira; ka o bɔhi Dauda, “Bɔ n-niŋ ka a kɔŋko ka kpe na, ka so bi dol’ a na?”

english_verse: “I'm on a mission for King Saul,” David answered. “He ordered me not to tell anyone what the mission is all about, so I ordered my soldiers to stay somewhere else.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yɛli Ahimɛlɛk ŋun daa nyɛ maligumaana maa, “Naa n-tim ma ni n ti niŋ shɛli ka yɛli ma, ‘Di chɛ ka so baŋ timsim maa yɛla bee n ni tim a ni a ti niŋ shɛli maa.’ Amaa m mini nachimba bɛn chani maa, n wuhi ba bɛ ni yɛn paai ma luɣ’ shɛli;”

english_verse: Do you have any food you can give me? Could you spare five loaves of bread?”
translation_verse: ka bɔh’ o, “Ka bindir’ bɔ ka a lee mali? Tim’ ma bɔrɔbɔro kpila anu bee a ni kul mali bindir’ shɛli kpe.”

english_verse: “The only bread I have is the sacred bread,” the priest told David. “You can have it if your soldiers didn't sleep with women last night.”
translation_verse: Ka maligumaana maa daa garigi yɛli Dauda, “N ka bɔrɔbɔro zim kpe, bɔrɔbɔro kasi n-naɣ’ beni; nachimba maa bɛn’ dee mini paɣiba yi bi dɔni, bɛ ni tooi ŋub’ li.”

english_verse: “Of course we didn't sleep with women,” David answered. “I never let my men do that when we're on a mission. They have to be acceptable to worship God even when we're on a regular mission, and today we're on a special mission.”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yɛli maligumaana maa, “Yɛlimaŋli, hal’ ti yi kul yɛn chaŋ chandi shɛli din bi tibisi gba, ti mini paɣiba bi lan miriti taba din ni chɛ ka bɛ be kasi, bɛ di ti yɛri ti ni chani chandi gahindili shɛli zuŋɔ ŋɔ, dinzuɣu bɛ niŋgbuna zaa bela kasi.”

english_verse: The only bread the priest had was the sacred bread that he had taken from the place of worship after putting out the fresh loaves. So he gave it to David.
translation_verse: Di saha ka maligumaana maa daa zaŋ bɔrɔbɔro kasi maa ti Dauda, dama bɔrɔbɔro shɛli daa ka nimaani n-naɣ’ pahila bɔrɔbɔro shɛli bɛ ni daa zaŋ zali Yawɛ tooni la. Ka bɛ daa kpuɣ’ li ni bɛ ti bo bɔrɔbɔro tula na ti zali di zaashee bɛ ni kpuɣ’ li dahin’ shɛli maa.

english_verse: It so happened that one of Saul's officers was there, worshiping the Lord that day. His name was Doeg the Edomite, and he was the strongest of Saul's shepherds.
translation_verse: Dindali maa Sool tumtumdib’ ni do’ so daa bela nimaani ni o mali maligu shɛli Yawɛ tooni, o daa nyɛla Ɛdom nira ka o yuli booni Doɛg, ŋuna n-daa nyɛ Sool piɛgul’ kpɛma.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech, “Do you have a spear or a sword? I had to leave so quickly on this mission for the king that I didn't bring along my sword or any other weapons.”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa bɔhi Ahimɛlɛk, “A ka takɔbi bee kpani kpe n-zaŋ ti ma? Dama naa tuma maa ni bɔri yomyom shɛm zuɣu chɛ ka m bi tooi zaŋ n takɔbi bee m bidibbin’ shɛli.”

english_verse: The priest answered, “The only sword here is the one that belonged to Goliath the Philistine. You were the one who killed him in Elah Valley, and so you can take his sword if you want to. It's wrapped in a cloth behind the statue.” “It's the best sword there is,” David said. “I'll take it!” David Tries To Find Safety in Gath
translation_verse: Ka maligumaana maa yɛl’ o, “A ni daa ku Filistia do’ so ŋun yuli booni Goliat Ɛla Vinvamli ni la takɔbi la n-naɣ’ beni. Nyama, ti zaŋla tani vil’ li, di be tan’ shɛli din ŋmani mukuru ŋɔ nyaaŋa; a yi ni zaŋ li, nyin’ zaŋm’ li. Dama shɛli lan kani m-pahi di zuɣu.” Ka Dauda daa yɛli, “Din viɛl’ gari li yi kani m-pahi di zuɣu, nyin’ zaŋm’ li ti ma.”

english_verse: David kept on running from Saul that day until he came to Gath, where he met with King Achish.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yiɣisi dindali maa n-zo Sool sani kuli Gaat Naa Akishi sani.

english_verse: The officers of King Achish were also there, and they asked Achish, “Isn't David a king back in his own country? Don't the Israelites dance and sing, ‘Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand’?”
translation_verse: Ka Naa Akishi kpambaliba daa bɔh’ o, “Pa Dauda ŋɔ n-nyɛ o ya naa la? Pa o yɛla ka bɛ daa wari waa ka yiini yila yɛra, ‘Naa Sool kula niriba tuhilituhili, ka Dauda mi ku tuhi’ piapia la?’ ”

english_verse: David thought about what they were saying, and it made him afraid of Achish.
translation_verse: Ka yɛtɔɣa maa daa kpe Dauda suhu ni pam, ka dabiɛm gbaag’ o zaŋ chaŋ Gaat Naa Akishi maa polo.

english_verse: So right there in front of everyone, he pretended to be insane. He acted confused and started making scratches on the doors of the town gate, while drooling in his beard.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Dauda daa taɣ’ o biɛhigu bɛ sani n-niŋdi kaman o nyɛla yinyaa la, ka bo bini n-chihiri dunɔdali punu chiha, ka chɛ ka o nintɔri zɔri dolisir’ o teeŋkɔbiri.

english_verse: “Look at him!” Achish said to his officers. “You can see he's crazy. Why did you bring him to me?
translation_verse: Di saha ka Naa Akishi daa bɔh’ o kpambaliba maa, “Nyamiya, yi nya ka doo ŋɔ nyɛla yinyaa, ka yi zaŋ o kani n sanna?

english_verse: I have enough crazy people without your bringing another one here. Keep him away from my palace!”
translation_verse: N yɛli ya ni yinyahi m-pooi ma, ka yi ti zaŋ doo ŋɔ na ni o ti tumd’ o yinyahili tuma ŋɔ n tooni? Doo ŋɔ ni tooi be n yili ŋɔ?”

english_verse: When David escaped from the town of Gath, he went to Adullam Cave. His brothers and the rest of his family found out where he was, and they followed him there.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yi nimaani zo n-chaŋ Adulam vokabili ni, ka o biɛyanim’ min’ o ba yiŋnim’ zaa daa ti wum o yɛla nimaani ka kahi chaŋ o sani.

english_verse: A lot of other people joined him too. Some were in trouble, others were angry or in debt, and David was soon the leader of
translation_verse: Ka ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn zaa daa be muɣisigu ni mini sama ni daa doli shɛba ni bɛnkam nini daa bi lan tiɣi bɛ biɛhigu zaa daa zo n-chaŋ o sani ka o ti leei bɛ zuɣulana. Ka bɛn daa be o sani maa zaa kalinli daa nyɛla ninvuɣ’ kɔbisinahi.

english_verse: David left Adullam Cave and went to the town of Mizpeh in Moab, where he talked with the king of Moab. “Please,” David said, “let my father and mother stay with you until I find out what God will do with me.”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa lan yi nimaani n-chaŋ Mizipa din be Mɔab tiŋgbɔŋ ni la ti yɛli Mɔab naa, “N suhir’ a ni a chɛ ka m ba mini m ma ʒini a sani hal ka n ti baŋ Naawuni ni yɛn tum tuun’ shɛli ti ma.”

english_verse: So he brought his parents to the king of Moab, and they stayed with him while David was in hiding.
translation_verse: Ka o daa chɛ ba ka bɛ be Mɔab naa maa sani saha shɛli zaa ŋun Dauda ni daa be vokabili maa ni maa.

english_verse: One day the prophet Gad told David, “Don't stay here! Go back to Judah.” David then left and went to Hereth Forest. Saul Kills the Priests of the Lord
translation_verse: Ka anab’ Gaad daa ti yɛli Dauda, “Di kpalim be vokabili ŋɔ ni, yiɣisim’ kpe kuli Juda tiŋgban’ ni.” Ka Dauda daa yi nimaani chaŋ Hɛrɛt yɔɣu ni.

english_verse: Saul was sitting under a small tree on top of the hill at Gibeah when he heard that David and his men had been located. Saul was holding his spear, and his officers were standing in front of him.
translation_verse: Ka Sool daa ti wum ni bɛ nya Dauda mini ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn be o san’ la. Di saha maa ŋun’ Sool daa ʒila ti’ shɛli din yuli booni tamarisik la gbini Gibia Zoli zuɣu, ka o kpani be o nuu ni ka o sapashin’ kpamba zaa ʒe n-gil’ o.

english_verse: He told them: Listen to me! You belong to the Benjamin tribe, so if that son of Jesse ever becomes king, he won't give you fields or vineyards. He won't make you officers in charge of thousands or hundreds as I have done.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Sool daa bɔh’ o sapashin’ kpamba bɛn daa ʒe n-gil’ o maa, “Yinim’ Bɛnjamin zuliya ŋɔ wummiya, yi tɛhiya ni Jɛsi bia ŋɔ ni tooi tila yi zaa yinoyino puri mini wain tihi puri bee o ni tooi chɛ ka yi leei zuɣulaannima n-su niriba tuhilituhili bee kɔbigakɔbiga fukumsi.

english_verse: But you're all plotting against me! Not one of you told me that my own son Jonathan had made an agreement with him. Not one of you cared enough to tell me that Jonathan had helped one of my officers rebel. Now that son of Jesse is trying to ambush me.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu n-chɛ ka yi zaa yi n nyaaŋa bebɔ? Saha shɛli m bia maa mini Jɛsi bia maa ni daa zaŋ bɛ noya naai taba maa, yi ni so daa bi yɛli ma. Yi ni so puu daa bi biɛri n zuɣu bee so ti sɔɣi yɛli ma ni m bia maa piɛlila n dabili bahi n zuɣu ni o sɔɣi do n-gu ma kaman di ni nyɛ shɛm zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ.”

english_verse: Doeg the Edomite was standing with the other officers and spoke up, “When I was in the town of Nob, I saw that son of Jesse. He was visiting the priest Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
translation_verse: Di saha maa ka Doɛg ŋun daa nyɛ Ɛdom nira ka ʒe Sool sapashin’ kpamba maa san’ la daa garigi yɛli Sool, “N daa nya Jɛsi bia maa ka o ka Nɔb na nti chaŋ Ahimɛlɛk ŋun nyɛ Ahitub bia la sani.

english_verse: Ahimelech talked to the Lord for him, then gave him food and the sword that had belonged to Goliath the Philistine.”
translation_verse: Ka o daa ti bɔhi Yawɛ n-nya o yɛla ti o, ka ti o bindirigu, ka lan zaŋ Goliat Filistia doo la takɔb’ la ti o.”

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Ahimelech and his whole family of priests at Nob, ordering them to come to him. When they came,
translation_verse: Di saha ka naa daa tim ti boli Ahimɛlɛk ŋun daa nyɛ Ahitub bia, ka nyɛ maligumaana la min’ o daŋ zaa bɛn daa nyɛ maligumaaniba m-be Nɔb maa na. Ka bɛ zaa daa ka naa sanna.

english_verse: Saul told them, “Listen to me, you son of Ahitub.” “Certainly, Your Majesty,” Ahimelech answered.
translation_verse: Ka Sool daa yɛli, “Nyin’ Ahitub bia ŋɔ wumma.” Ka o garigi yɛli, “N dana, n wumda.”

english_verse: Saul demanded, “Why did you plot against me with that son of Jesse? You helped him rebel against me by giving him food and a sword, and by talking with God for him. Now he's trying to ambush me!”
translation_verse: Ka Sool daa bɔh’ o, “Bɔ n-niŋ ka a mini Jɛsi bia ŋɔ gbiri ma zamba bɔɣa? Bɔzuɣu ka a daa ti o bindirigu ka ti o takɔbi ka lan bɔhi Naawuni n-nya o yɛla ti o ka di zuɣu chɛ ka o yiɣisi lu n zuɣu n-sɔɣi do n-gu ma kaman di ni nyɛ shɛm zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ?”

english_verse: “Your Majesty, none of your officers is more loyal than David!” Ahimelech replied. “He's your son-in-law and the captain of your bodyguard. Everyone in your family respects him.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Ahimɛlɛk daa garigi yɛli, “Naa, a sapashin’ kpamba ŋɔ ni ŋuni n-lee ʒe a yim kaman Dauda ŋun nyɛ nyin’ naa deemba, ka lan nyɛ a tɔbbi’ shɛb’ bɛn gul’ a sapashin’ kpɛma ni ŋun mali jilima a yili ŋɔ n-gari sokam la?

english_verse: This isn't the first time I've talked with God for David, and it's never made you angry before! Please don't accuse me or my family like this. I have no idea what's going on!”
translation_verse: A tɛhiya ni zuŋɔ ka m piligi bɔhiri Naawuni n-nyar’ o yɛla tir’ o? Naa, di zaŋ mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ mini n daŋ zaa so taali, dama mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ bi mi dimbɔŋɔ zaa yɛla hal baabiɛla gba.”

english_verse: “Ahimelech,” Saul said, “you and your whole family are going to die.”
translation_verse: Ka naa yɛl’ o, “Biɛhiŋ kani, n ni ku nyini Ahimɛlɛk min’ a daŋ zaa.”

english_verse: Saul shouted to his bodyguards, “These priests of the Lord helped David! They knew he was running away, but they didn't tell me. Kill them!” But the king's officers would not attack the priests of the Lord.
translation_verse: Di saha ka naa daa yɛli bɛn nyɛ bɛn gul’ o ka ʒe o sani maa, “Kumiya Yawɛ maligumaaniba maa, dama bɛ gba nuu be Dauda yɛla maa ni, bɛ ni daa mi ni o zɔrimi ka bi yɛli ma la zuɣu.” Amaa ka naa sapashin’ kpamba maa ni so daa bi saɣi teeg’ o nuu ni o shihi Yawɛ maligumaaniba maa.

english_verse: Then he attacked the town of Nob, where the priests had lived, and he killed everyone there—men, women, children, and babies. He even killed their cattle, donkeys, and sheep. Only Abiathar Escapes from Nob
translation_verse: Ka o daa lan zaŋ takɔbi chaŋ ti lu Nɔb din daa nyɛ maligumaaniba tiŋ’ la nim’ zuɣu n-ku dɔbba mini paɣiba ni bidibisi mini bipuɣinsi ni biliɛri ni naɣilahi ni bunsi ni piɛri. O daa zaŋla takɔbi ku bɛ zaa.

english_verse: Ahimelech's son Abiathar was the only one who escaped. He ran to David
translation_verse: Amaa ka Ahimɛlɛk ŋun daa nyɛ Ahitub bia maa bidib’ so ŋun yuli booni Abiata la ŋun’ daa zo n-tiligi chaŋ Dauda sani.

english_verse: and told him, “Saul has murdered the Lord's priests at Nob!”
translation_verse: Ka Abiata maa daa yɛli Dauda ni Sool ku Yawɛ maligumaaniba la.

english_verse: David answered, “That day when I saw Doeg, I knew he would tell Saul! Your family died because of me.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yɛli Abiata, “N ni daa kul nya Doɛg Ɛdom nir’ la dindali maa, n daa pun baŋ ni o ni yɛli Sool di yɛla. Mani n-nyɛ ŋun bo kum ti a ba daŋ ŋɔ zaa maa.

english_verse: Stay here. Isn't the same person trying to kill both of us? Don't worry! You'll be safe here with me.”
translation_verse: Kpalimmi be n sani, ka di chɛ ka dabiɛm mal’ a, dama ninvuɣ’ so ŋun bɔri ni o ku ma m-bɔri ni o ku a gba maa; a yi be n sani shɛli ku niŋ a.”

english_verse: One day some people told David, “The Philistines keep attacking the town of Keilah and stealing grain from the threshing place.”
translation_verse: Dahin shɛli ka bɛ daa ti yɛli Dauda, “Nyama, Filistianim’ tuhirila Kɛilanima, ka fari bɛ bindira bɛ puri ni.”

english_verse: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack these Philistines?” “Yes,” the Lord answered. “Attack them and rescue Keilah.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda daa bɔhi Yawɛ, “N cham’ ti liri Filistianim’ maa?” Ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Dauda, “Cham’ ti liri ba n-tiligi Kɛilanim’ maa.”

english_verse: But David's men said, “Look, even here in Judah we're afraid of the Philistines. We will be terrified if we try to fight them at Keilah!”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Dauda niriba maa daa bɔh’ o, “Nyama, ti na be Juda tiŋgbani ŋɔ ni ŋɔ ka dabiɛm mali ti mi, ka ti yi ti chaŋ Kɛila ni ti ti tuhi Filistia tɔbbihi ŋɔ, wula ka di lee yɛn be?”

english_verse: David asked the Lord about it again. “Leave at once,” the Lord answered. “I will give you victory over the Philistines at Keilah.”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa lan bɔhi Yawɛ yaha. Ka Yawɛ daa garigi yɛl’ o, “Yiɣisima, cham’ Kɛila, dama n zaŋ Filistianim’ maa niŋ a nuu ni.”

english_verse: David and his men went there and fiercely attacked the Philistines. They killed many of them, then led away their cattle, and rescued the people of Keilah.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda min’ o niriba maa daa chaŋ Kɛila nti tuhi Filistianim’ maa n-ku ba pam, ka fa bɛ niɣi. Lala ka Dauda daa niŋ fa Kɛilanim’ maa bahi.

english_verse: David heard about Saul's plan to capture him, and he told Abiathar, “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa baŋ ni Sool lo o la zaɣ’ biɛɣu niŋbu, ka daa yɛli Abiata ŋun nyɛ maligumaana maa, “Zaŋmi tan’ la na.”

english_verse: David prayed, “Lord God of Israel, I was told that Saul is planning to come here. What should I do? Suppose he threatens to destroy the town because of me.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda daa yɛli, “Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni ŋɔ, man’ ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ wumya ni Sool ni ka Kɛila ŋɔ na nti wurim li n zuɣu.

english_verse: Would the leaders of Keilah turn me over to Saul? Or is he really coming? Please tell me, Lord.” “Yes, he will come,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: O yi kana, Kɛilanim’ ni gbaai ma ti o? O shiri nyɛla ŋun ni kana kaman mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ ni wum shɛm maa? Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni ŋɔ, n suhir’ a, yɛlim’ mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ.” Ka Yawɛ garigi yɛl’ o, “O ni kana.”

english_verse: David asked, “Would the leaders of Keilah hand me and my soldiers over to Saul?” “Yes, they would,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa lan yɛli, “Ka daɣila Kɛilanim’ ŋɔ ni zaŋ m mini n niriba ŋɔ niŋ ŋun Sool nuu ni?” Ka Yawɛ daa yɛli, “Bɛ shiri ni zaŋ ya niŋ o nuu ni.”

english_verse: David stayed in hideouts in the hill country of Ziph Desert. Saul kept searching, but God never let Saul catch him.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa chaŋ ti kpalim be mɔɣu ni sɔɣisili shee din be Zif mɔɣu ni zoya tiŋgbɔŋ la ni. Ka Sool daa kul lihiri bɔr’ o dabisili kam, amaa ka Naawuni daa bi zaŋ o niŋ o nuu ni.

english_verse: One time, David was at Horesh in Ziph Desert. He was afraid because Saul had come to the area to kill him.
translation_verse: Dauda daa bela Zif mɔɣu ni Hɔrɛshi maa. Di saha ka o daa wum ni Sool kana ni o ti ku o.

english_verse: But Jonathan went to see David, and God helped him encourage David.
translation_verse: Ka Sool bia Jɔnatan daa yiɣisi chaŋ Dauda sani Hɔrɛshi maa nti zaŋ Naawuni yuli kpaŋs’ o suhu.

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Jonathan said. “My father Saul will never get his hands on you. In fact, you're going to be the next king of Israel, and I'll be your highest official. Even my father knows it's true.”
translation_verse: O daa lan yɛl’ o, “Di zɔri dabiɛm, m ba Sool nuu ku shih’ a. Nyini nti yɛn nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ zaa naa, ka m mi nyɛ wulana. M ba Sool gba mi lala.”

english_verse: They both promised the Lord that they would always be loyal to each other. Then Jonathan went home, but David stayed at Horesh. David Escapes from Saul
translation_verse: Ka bɛ niriba ayi maa daa lan lo tab’ alikauli Yawɛ tooni, ka Jɔnatan daa kuli, ka Dauda mi kpalim be Hɔrɛshi.

english_verse: Some people from the town of Ziph went to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Your Majesty, David has a hideout not far from us! It's near Horesh, somewhere on Mount Hachilah south of Jeshimon.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Zifinim’ daa chaŋ Sool sani Gibia ti yɛl’ o, “Dauda sɔɣi bela ti ya Hɔrɛshi sɔɣisili shee din be Hachila zo’ shɛli din labiri Jɛshimɔn nudirigu polo la zuɣu.

english_verse: Saul told them: You've done me a big favor, and I pray that the Lord will bless you.
translation_verse: Ka Sool daa yɛli ba, “Yawɛ niŋmi alibarika niŋ yi ni; dama yi puu biɛri n zuɣu.

english_verse: Now please do just a little more for me. Find out exactly where David is, as well as where he goes, and who has seen him there. I've been told that he's very tricky.
translation_verse: Chamiya ti maan lihi viɛnyɛliŋga n-nya o shiri beni, ka baŋ o ni be luɣ’ shɛli maa, ka lan baŋ ninvuɣ’ so ŋun nya o nimaani maa, dama bɛ yɛli ma ni o neeya pam.

english_verse: Find out where all his hiding places are and come back when you're sure. Then I'll go with you. If he is still in the area, or anywhere among the clans of Judah, I'll find him.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu bomiya nya o ni sɔɣiri luɣ’ shɛŋa zaa ka labina ti yɛli ma yɛlimaŋli, ka m mini ya chaŋ; ŋun dee yi be tiŋgbani maa ni, n ni bɔ o shee Judanim’ zaa niriba tusatusa puuni.”

english_verse: The people from Ziph went back ahead of Saul, and they found out that David and his men were still south of Jeshimon in the Maon Desert.
translation_verse: Ka niriba maa daa yiɣisi daŋ Sool tooni chaŋ Zif. Di saha Dauda min’ o niriba daa bela Maɔn yɔɣu ni luɣ’ shɛli din yuli booni Araba, ka di be Jɛshimɔn nudirigu polo la.

english_verse: Saul and his army set out to find David. But David heard that Saul was coming, and he went to a place called The Rock, one of his hideouts in Maon Desert. Saul found out where David was and started closing in on him.
translation_verse: Ka Sool min’ o niriba daa chaŋ ni bɛ ti bɔ Dauda shee. Ka bɛ daa yɛli Dauda, ka o zo n-chaŋ tampima zo’ shɛli din daa be Maɔn yɔɣu ni la zuɣu. Ka Sool daa wum lala ka kari Dauda naba Maɔn yɔɣu maa ni.

english_verse: Saul was going around a hill on one side, and David and his men were on the other side, trying to get away. Saul and his soldiers were just about to capture David and his men,
translation_verse: Sool daa bela zoli maa yaɣi yini polo, ka Dauda min’ o niriba mi be yaɣi din’ la polo, ka Dauda daa kpaŋ zɔri yomyom ni o yi Sool nuu ni saha shɛli Sool ni daa ti chɛ ŋun’ Dauda min’ o niriba maa kpe ni kpe ni o gbahi ba la.

english_verse: when a messenger came to Saul and said, “Come quickly! The Philistines are attacking Israel and taking everything.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka tumo daa kana ti yɛli Sool, “Kulimina yomyom, dama Filistianim’ kana ti liri ti.”

english_verse: Saul stopped going after David and went back to fight the Philistines. That's why the place is called “Escape Rock.”
translation_verse: Ka Sool daa chɛ Dauda kari doli ka lab’ kuli ni o ti tuhi Filistianim’ maa. Dinzuɣu ka bɛ daa boli nimaani zo n-tiligi tampiŋ.

english_verse: David left and went to live in the hideouts at En-Gedi.
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Dauda daa yi nimaani n-chaŋ ti be Ɛngɛdi sɔɣisili shee.

english_verse: When Saul got back from fighting off the Philistines, he heard that David was in the desert around En-Gedi.
translation_verse: Sool ni daa kuli ti tuhi Filistianim’ maa ka labina ka bɛ yɛl’ o, “Nyama Dauda be Ɛngɛdi.”

english_verse: There were some sheep pens along the side of the road, and one of them was built around the entrance to a cave. Saul went into the cave to relieve himself. David and his men were hiding at the back of the cave.
translation_verse: Ka o daa kana ti paai piɛri biɛhigu shee ka tampiŋ voli daa be nimaani so’ naŋgbanyee; ka Sool daa kpe di puuni ni o ti damdi yɔɣu ni ka Dauda min’ o niriba gba daa be voli maa puuni ha.

english_verse: They whispered to David, “The Lord told you he was going to let you defeat your enemies and do whatever you want with them. This must be the day the Lord was talking about.” David sneaked over and cut off a small piece of Saul's robe, but Saul didn't notice a thing.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda niriba maa daa yɛl’ o, “Zuŋɔ n-nyɛ dabisi’ shɛli Yawɛ ni daa yɛl’ a, ‘Nyama, n zaŋ a dim’ niŋ a nuu ni, niŋm’ o a ni bɔri shɛm la.’ ” Di saha ka Dauda daa puɣisi chaŋ ti sɔɣi ŋmaai Naa Sool kparibu naŋgbambili.

english_verse: Afterwards, David was sorry that he had even done that,
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka di daa muɣisi Dauda pam, o ni daa ŋmaai Sool binyɛrigu maa zuɣu.

english_verse: and he told his men, “Stop talking foolishly. We're not going to attack Saul. He's my king, and I pray that the Lord will keep me from doing anything to harm his chosen king.” Saul left the cave and started down the road.
translation_verse: Yɛtɔɣa ŋɔ ka Dauda daa zaŋ yɛl’ o niriba maa, ka daa bi saɣi ni bɛ chaŋ ti liri Sool. Ka Sool daa ti yiɣisi voli maa ni yina chaŋ o chandi.

english_verse: Soon, David also got up and left the cave. “Your Majesty!” he shouted from a distance. Saul turned around to look. David bowed down very low
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Dauda gba daa yiɣisi voli maa ni yina nti kuhi boli Naa Sool, “N dan’ naa!” Ka Sool daa ŋmaligi lih’ o nyaaŋa, ka Dauda damdi zaŋ o zuɣu silim tiŋa n-lu o sizuura,

english_verse: and said: Your Majesty, why do you listen to people who say that I'm trying to harm you?
translation_verse: ka bɔh’ o, “Bɔ n-niŋ ka a wumdi ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn yɛr’ a, ‘Nyama, Dauda lo a zaɣ’ biɛɣu la yɛtɔɣa?’

english_verse: You can see for yourself that the Lord gave me the chance to catch you in the cave today. Some of my men wanted to kill you, but I wouldn't let them do it. I told them, “I will not harm the Lord's chosen king!”
translation_verse: Nyama, a nya Yawɛ ni zaŋ a niŋ n nuu ni shɛm vol’ la ni zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ, ka n niriba shɛb’ di yɛli ni n kum’ a, amaa ka man’ lee tilig’ a. N di yɛlimi, ‘Man’ ku zaŋ n nuu shihi n dana, dama o nyɛla Yawɛ ni booi kpam bahi so zuɣu ni.’

english_verse: Your Majesty, look at what I'm holding. You can see that it's a piece of your robe. If I could cut off a piece of your robe, I could have killed you. But I let you live, and that should prove I'm not trying to harm you or to rebel. I haven't done anything to you, and yet you keep trying to ambush and kill me.
translation_verse: M ba, nyam’ a binyɛrigu naŋgbambili n nuu ni. Yɛlimaŋli, n ni ŋmaag’ a binyɛrigu naŋgbambili ka bi ku a ŋɔ, di simdi ni a baŋ ni taali bee zaɣ’ biɛ’ shɛli ka n sani ni nyini. M bi tum a taal’ shɛli, hal a ni kul kariti dol’ ma ni a ku ma maa zaa yoli.

english_verse: I'll let the Lord decide which one of us has done right. I pray that the Lord will punish you for what you're doing to me, but I won't do anything to you.
translation_verse: Yawɛ ni woligi ti m min’ a, Yawɛ ni bɔh’ a biɛri ti ma, amaa man’ ku zaŋ n nuu shih’ a.

english_verse: An old proverb says, “Only evil people do evil things,” and so I won't harm you.
translation_verse: Kaman kurimbuni ha yɛtɔɣ’ ŋahili ni yɛli shɛm la, ‘Ninvuɣ’ biɛɣu kɔbili ni ka ninvuɣ’ biɛtali yirina.’ Amaa man’ ku zaŋ n nuu shih’ a.

english_verse: Why should the king of Israel be out chasing me, anyway? I'm as worthless as a dead dog or a flea.
translation_verse: Ŋuni ka Izraɛl naa lee yina kariti doli ŋɔ? Ŋuni ka a lee kariti doli ni a ku ŋɔ? A kariti dolila ba’ kpiŋ! A kariti dolila buduli zaɣ’ bila.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord will help me escape and show that I am in the right.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu Yawɛ ni leei ti sariakarita, o ni woligi ti m min’ a. O ni lihi ti yɛtɔɣa ŋɔ zuɣu, ka zani n nyaaŋa n-fa ma a nuu ni bahi.”

english_verse: and said: David, you're a better person than I am. You treated me with kindness, even though I've been cruel to you.
translation_verse: ka yɛli Dauda, “A nyɛla wuntizɔra pam gari ma, dama a tum ma din viɛla, ka man’ zaŋla zaɣ’ biɛɣu yo a samli.

english_verse: You've told me how you were kind enough not to kill me when the Lord gave you the chance.
translation_verse: Ka zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ, a kahigi wuhi ma a ni niŋ ma zaɣ’ viɛlli shɛm, ka bi ku ma saha shɛli Yawɛ ni di zaŋ ma niŋ a nuu ni la.

english_verse: If you really were my enemy, you wouldn't have let me leave here alive. I pray that the Lord will give you a big reward for what you did today.
translation_verse: Dama nir’ yi nya o dindana ŋ-ŋɔ, o ni chɛ o ni alaafee? Dinzuɣu a ni niŋ ma shɛm zuŋɔ ŋɔ, Yawɛ ni yo a sam’ viɛlli.

english_verse: I realize now that you will be the next king, and a powerful king at that.
translation_verse: Pumpɔŋɔ nyama, biɛhiŋ kani, m mi ni a ni leei naa, ka Izraɛl nam ti nya zaashee zani a kɔbili ni.

english_verse: Promise me with the Lord as your witness, that you won't wipe out my descendants. Let them live to keep my family name alive.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pom’ Yawɛ ni a ti ku ku n zuliya n kalinsi nyaaŋa bee n-kpihim n daŋ birili.”

english_verse: So David promised, and Saul went home. David and his men returned to their hideout.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa po lala pɔri maa Sool sani. Di saha ka Sool daa kuli, ka Dauda min’ o niriba maa mi labi bɛ sɔɣisili maa shee.

english_verse: One day, Nabal was in Carmel where his servants were cutting the wool from his sheep. David was in the desert when he heard about it.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa be mɔɣu maa ni ka wum ni Nabal chɛrila o piɛri kɔbiri.

english_verse: So he sent ten men to Carmel with this message for Nabal: I hope that you and your family are healthy and that all is going well for you.
translation_verse: Yi ni ti yɛn puh’ o shɛm m-bɔŋɔ: Naawuni tim a suhudoo, ka ti a malibu suhudoo, ka chɛ ka suhudoo be a ni su shɛlikam zaa ni.

english_verse: I've heard that you are cutting the wool from your sheep. When your shepherds were with us in Carmel, we didn't harm them, and nothing was ever stolen from them.
translation_verse: Yɛlimiy’ o ni n wumya ni o chɛrila o piɛri kɔbiri ni o piɛguliba maa mi yi kul bela ti sani, ka ti bi niŋ ba zaɣ’ biɛ’ shɛli, bɛ mi binshɛli daa bi bɔrigi bɛ ni daa be ti sani Kamɛl saha shɛli maa.

english_verse: Ask your shepherds, and they'll tell you the same thing. My servants are your servants, and you are like a father to me. This is a day for celebrating, so please be kind and share some of your food with us.
translation_verse: Ni o bɔhim’ o nachimba maa, bɛ ni yɛl’ o. Dinzuɣu n suhir’ o mi ni o niŋmi n nachimba ŋɔ nirilim, dama chuɣu dali ka ti kana maa. N suhir’ o mi, din kul be o nuu ni, ŋun’ zaŋ ti yinim’ bɛn nyɛ o tumtumdiba ŋɔ ka yi zaŋ na ti ti o bia Dauda.”

english_verse: David's men went to Nabal and gave him David's message, then they waited for Nabal's answer.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda nachimba maa daa chaŋ ti zaŋ Dauda yuli yɛli Nabal yɛtɔɣa maa zaa, ka kpalim ʒiɛya guhira.

english_verse: This is what he said: Who does this David think he is? That son of Jesse is just one more slave on the run from his master, and there are too many of them these days.
translation_verse: Ka Nabal daa garigi bɔhi Dauda tuumba maa, “Ŋuni n-lee nyɛ Dauda? Ka ŋuni mi n-lee nyɛ Jɛsi bia? Pumpɔŋɔ daba pam kul zɔrimi ka chɛri bɛ laamba.

english_verse: What makes you think I would take my bread, my water, and the meat that I've had cooked for my own servants and give it to you? Besides, I'm not sure that David sent you!
translation_verse: N zaŋmi m bɔrɔbɔro mini ko’ shɛli ni nim’ shɛli n ni ku n-zali bɛn chɛri m piɛri kɔbiri maa ti ninvuɣ’ shɛba n ni bi mi bɛ ni yi shɛl’ na?”

english_verse: The men returned to their camp and told David everything Nabal had said.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda nachimba maa ŋmaligi labi ti yɛl’ o dimbɔŋɔ zaa.

english_verse: “Everybody get your swords!” David ordered. They all strapped on their swords. Two hundred men stayed behind to guard the camp, but the other
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yɛl’ o niriba maa, “Sokam nyaɣim’ o takɔbi!” Ka Dauda gba daa nyaɣ’ o takɔbi; ka niriba kɔbisinahi daa pah’ o zuɣu ka bɛ chaŋ, ka chɛ niriba kɔbisiyi ka bɛ mi kpalim guli bɛ nɛma.

english_verse: He's a bully who won't listen to anyone. Isn't there something you can do? Please think of something! Or else our master and his family and everyone who works for him are all doomed.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ zahimmi yɛlli maa ka baŋ a ni yɛn niŋ shɛm; dama dimbɔŋɔ ni tooi tahi zaɣ’ biɛɣu ti kpɛm’ maa sanna n-tabil’ o yiŋnim’ zaa, ka o mi yɛla kpɛm’ pam ka nir’ ku tooi tɔɣis’ o yɛtɔɣa.”

english_verse: and told her servants, “Take this on ahead, and I'll catch up with you.” She didn't tell her husband Nabal what she was doing.
translation_verse: ka yɛli nachimba maa, “Chamiya n tooni ka n doli yi nyaaŋa na.” Amaa o daa bi saɣi yɛl’ o yidan’ Nabal.

english_verse: Abigail was riding her donkey on the path that led around the hillside, when suddenly she met David and his men heading straight at her.
translation_verse: Ka o daa ba buŋa chaŋ ti ŋmaligi zolɔŋni n-tuhi Dauda min’ o niriba maa soli ka bɛ kanna.

english_verse: David had just been saying, “I surely wasted my time guarding Nabal's things in the desert and keeping them from being stolen! I was good to him, and now he pays me back with insults.
translation_verse: Dauda daa yɛlimi, “Yɛlimaŋli, yoli ka n daa kul guli doo ŋɔ binyara ŋɔ mɔɣu ŋɔ ni ka bi chɛ ka o binshɛli bɔrigi ŋɔ, ka ŋun’ ti zaŋla zaɣ’ biɛɣu yo ma samli.

english_verse: I swear that by morning, there won't be a man or boy left from his family or his servants' families. I pray that God will punish me if I don't do it!”
translation_verse: Zaŋ chaŋ biɛɣu sa ti yɛn neei ka n yi chɛ ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn be o sani maa, hal do’ yino gba, Naawuni ŋun niŋm’ ma n ni yɛn niŋ’ o shɛm maa, hal ŋun’ niŋm’ ma gari lala gba.”

english_verse: Abigail quickly got off her donkey and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: Abigeel ni daa ti kul nya Dauda, o dii sheela o buŋ’ maa zuɣu na yom lu n-gbani Dauda tooni, ka zaŋ o zuɣu silim tiŋa.

english_verse: Please forgive me if I say a little more. The Lord will always protect you and your family, because you fight for him. I pray that you won't ever do anything evil as long as you live.
translation_verse: N suhir’ a mi, chɛli mani ŋun nyɛ a dabipaɣ’ ŋɔ taali. Dama biɛhiŋ kani, Yawɛ ni me a yili a ni tuhiri ŋun’ Yawɛ tɔb’ shɛli ŋɔ zuɣu; ka a ku tum zaɣ’ biɛɣu hal ni a nyɛvili tariga.

english_verse: The Lord your God will keep you safe when your enemies try to kill you. But he will snatch away their lives quicker than you can throw a rock from a sling.
translation_verse: N dana, ka so yi ti dol’ a ni o ku a, Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ a Naawuni ŋɔ ŋun’ zaŋm’ a nyɛvili ŋɔ pahi nyɛviya pam zuɣu n-gul’ li, amaa o ni ti zaŋ a dimnim’ nyɛviya labi kaman kuɣilɔŋ kuɣili ka bɛ labi la.

english_verse: The Lord has promised to do many good things for you, even to make you the ruler of Israel. The Lord will keep his promises to you,
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ yi ti niŋ nyini n dana zaɣ’ viɛl’ shɛlikam zaa o ni yɛli ni o ni niŋ a la, ka chɛ ka a leei Izraɛl naa,

english_verse: and now your conscience will be clear, because you won't be guilty of taking revenge and killing innocent people. When the Lord does all those good things for you, please remember me.
translation_verse: a ti ku mali suhugarigu a ni daa ku so ka di ka daliri zuɣu bee amaŋmaŋ’ ni daa bɔhi biɛri zuɣu. N dana, ka Yawɛ yi ti chɛ ka binshɛɣukam niŋ viɛnyɛliŋga a sani, nyin’ di ti tam mani ŋun nyɛ a dabipaɣ’ ŋɔ yɛla.”

english_verse: David told her: I praise the Lord God of Israel! He must have sent you to meet me today.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yɛli Abigeel, “Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Izraɛl Naawuni ŋun tim a na ka a ti tuhi ma soli ŋɔ mali alibarika!

english_verse: And you should also be praised. Your good sense kept me from taking revenge and killing innocent people.
translation_verse: Ka a ni tɛhi tɛhi viɛl’ shɛŋa ka taɣ’ ma zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ ka m bi tum taali so ʒim yihibu puuni bee n-zaŋ mmaŋmaŋ’ nuhi ŋɔ bɔhi biɛri ŋɔ zuɣu, a mali alibarika.

english_verse: If you hadn't come to meet me so quickly, every man and boy in Nabal's family and in his servants' families would have been killed by morning. I swear by the living Lord God of Israel who protected you that this is the truth.
translation_verse: Dama hal ka Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni ŋun be ka nyɛ ŋun taɣ’ ma ka m bi niŋ ya zaɣ’ biɛɣu ŋɔ zuɣu, a yi di bi kana yomyom ti nya ma, biɛɣuni asiba doo zaɣ’ yino gba sa naan ku lan guui Nabal yiŋa.”

english_verse: David accepted the food Abigail had brought. “Don't worry,” he said. “You can go home now. I'll do what you asked.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda daa deei paɣ’ maa ni ʒi pin’ shɛŋa na maa ka yɛl’ o, “Kulim’ a yiŋ’ ni suhudoo, nyama, n wum a yɛligu maa, ka ni niŋ a ni fabili niŋ ma ni n niŋ shɛm maa.”

english_verse: Abigail went back home and found Nabal throwing a party fit for a king. He was very drunk and feeling good, so she didn't tell him anything that night.
translation_verse: Ka Abigeel daa kuli Nabal sani nti nya ka o puhirila chuɣu o yiŋa, ka di ŋmanila naa m-puhiri chuɣu. Ka ŋun’ Nabal daa kul mali suhupiɛlli, dama o daa nyula dam buɣi. Ka o paɣ’ maa daa bi yɛl’ o shɛli dindali maa hal ka biɛɣu ti neei.

english_verse: But when he sobered up the next morning, Abigail told him everything that had happened. Nabal had a heart attack, and he lay in bed as still as a stone.
translation_verse: Biɛɣu ni daa neeg’ asiba ka dam maa yi o ninni, ka o paɣ’ maa yɛl’ o binshɛɣukam zaa, ka o suhu kabi, ka o be kaman kuɣili la.

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Zaŋ chaŋ kaman biɛɣu pia dali, ka Yawɛ daa ku Nabal.

english_verse: She bowed down and said, “I would willingly be David's slave and wash his servants' feet.”
translation_verse: Ka Abigeel daa yiɣisi gbani n-zaŋ o zuɣu silim tiŋa ka yɛli, “Nyamiya, man’ ŋun nyɛ yi dabipaɣ’ ŋɔ nyɛla ŋun ni paɣi n dan’ tumtumdiba naba.”

english_verse: Abigail quickly got ready and went back with David's messengers. She rode on her donkey, while five of her servant women walked alongside. She and David were married as soon as she arrived.
translation_verse: Ka Abigeel daa yiɣisi niŋ yomyom m-ba buŋa, ka o paɣisara anu bɛn daa be o sani n-tumd’ o tuma pah’ o zuɣu ka bɛ doli Dauda tuumba maa chaŋ, ka o ti leei Dauda paɣa.

english_verse: David had earlier married Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel, so both she and Abigail were now David's wives.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa lan kpuɣi Ahinɔam ŋun nyɛ Jɛziriil nir’ la pahi, ka bɛ niriba ayi maa daa leeg’ o paɣiba.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Saul had arranged for Michal to marry Palti the son of Laish, who came from the town of Gallim.
translation_verse: Di saha Sool daa pun zaŋla o bipuɣiŋga Mikal ŋun daa nyɛ Dauda paɣ’ la n-ti do’ so ŋun yuli booni Paliti ka o nyɛ Laishi Gallim nir’ bia la.

english_verse: Once again, some people from Ziph went to Gibeah to talk with Saul. “David has a hideout on Mount Hachilah near Jeshimon out in the desert,” they told him.
translation_verse: Ka Zifinim’ daa ti ka Sool sanna Gibia nti yɛl’ o, “Dauda sɔɣi bela Hachila Zoli din mini Jɛshimɔn nin’ tuhi tab’ la zuɣu.”

english_verse: Saul set up camp on Mount Hachilah, which is across the road from Jeshimon. But David was hiding out in the desert. When David heard that Saul was following him,
translation_verse: Ka Sool min’ o niriba maa daa ti paai Hachila zolɔŋni zaŋ labi Jɛshimɔn wulimpuhili polo nti ti bɛ suɣa do nimaani palli noli. Amaa Dauda daa na bela mɔɣu maa ni. O ni daa ti wum ni Sool kar’ o naba na mɔɣu maa ni,

english_verse: he sent some spies to find out if it was true.
translation_verse: ka o tim puɣisiriba ka bɛ chaŋ ti nya ka Sool shiri be ni.

english_verse: Then he sneaked up to Saul's camp. He noticed that Saul and his army commander Abner the son of Ner were sleeping in the middle of the camp, with soldiers sleeping all around them.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda daa yiɣisi chaŋ Sool ni be luɣ’ shɛli maa ti nya o ni do luɣ’ shɛli polo, ka Nɛr bia Abinɛr ŋun daa nyɛ o tɔbbihi zuɣulan’ la do o sani. Sool daa dola suɣa maa sunsuuni, ka tɔbbihi maa do n-gil’ o.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Joab's brother Abishai, “Which one of you will go with me into Saul's camp?” “I will!” Abishai answered.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda bɔhi Ahimɛlɛk ŋun daa nyɛ Hiti nir’ la mini Zɛruya bia Abishai ŋun daa nyɛ Jɔab mabia la, “Ŋuni n-lee ni doli ma chaŋ Sool sansan’ ni?” Ka Abishai daa yɛli, “Man’ ni dol’ a chaŋ.”

english_verse: That same night, David and Abishai crept into the camp. Saul was sleeping, and his spear was stuck in the ground not far from his head. Abner and the soldiers were sound asleep all around him.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda mini Abishai daa chaŋ tɔbbihi maa sani yuŋ, ka Sool ti dola sansani maa sunsuuni gbihiri ka o kpani sa o zuɣusaa, ka Abinɛr mini tɔbbihi maa do n-gil’ o.

english_verse: Abishai whispered, “This time God has let you get your hands on your enemy! I'll pin him to the ground with one thrust of his own spear.”
translation_verse: Ka Abishai daa yɛli Dauda, “Naawuni zaŋ a dim’ maa niŋ a nuu ni zuŋɔ; dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ chɛ ka n kul zaŋ kpani ŋɔ kuh’ o yim tabili tiŋa, m bi yɛn kuh’ o buyi.”

english_verse: “Don't kill him!” David whispered back. “The Lord will punish anyone who kills his chosen king.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yɛli Abishai, “Di ku o, dama ŋuni n-lee ni tooi zaŋ o nuu shihi Yawɛ ni booi kpam bahi ninvuɣ’ so zuɣu ni, ka ku mali taali?”

english_verse: As surely as the Lord lives, the Lord will kill Saul, or Saul will die a natural death or be killed in battle.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa lan yɛli, “Hal ka Yawɛ ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu, ŋun’ Yawɛ ni ku o bee o kum dali yi paai, o ni kpi bee ŋun chaŋ tɔb’ ni ka bɛ ti ku o.

english_verse: But I pray that the Lord will keep me from harming his chosen king. Let's grab his spear and his water jar and get out of here!”
translation_verse: Yawɛ di saɣi ka n zaŋ n nuu shihi ŋun’ Yawɛ ni booi kpam bahi ninvuɣ’ so zuɣu ni maa, amaa lee saami kpan’ shɛli din sa o zuɣusaa ŋɔ ka kpuɣ’ o ko’ gaɣili ŋɔ ka ti chaŋ.”

english_verse: David took the spear and the water jar, then left the camp. None of Saul's soldiers knew what had happened or even woke up—the Lord had made all of them fall sound asleep.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda daa saai kpani maa ka kpuɣi ko’ gaɣili maa Sool zuɣusaa ka bɛ chaŋ. So daa bi nya ba bee m-baŋ di yɛla bee so ti neei, bɛ zaa daa gbihirimi, dama Yawɛ n-daa chɛ ka go’ titali gbahi ba.

english_verse: David and Abishai crossed the valley and went to the top of the next hill, where they were at a safe distance.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa zo n-chaŋ yaɣ’ shɛli polo katiŋa nti du n-tam zoli zuɣu ka o mini ba daa danigi tab’ pam.

english_verse: “Abner!” David shouted toward Saul's army. “Can you hear me?” Abner shouted back. “Who dares disturb the king?”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa duh’ o yee bɔhi tɔbbihi maa mini Nɛr bia Abinɛr la, “Abinɛr, a ku garigi ma?” Ka Abinɛr garigi bɔhi, “Nyin’ ŋuni n-lee booni naa maa?”

english_verse: “Abner, what kind of a man are you?” David replied. “Aren't you supposed to be the best soldier in Israel? Then why didn't you protect your king? Anyone who went into your camp could have killed him tonight.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa bɔh’ o, “Pa doo n-nya a? A kpee be Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ni? Ka bɔ n-niŋ ka a bi ʒiɛya gul’ a dan’ naa? Dama ninvuɣ’ so kana ni o ti ku a dan’ naa maa.

english_verse: You're a complete failure! I swear by the living Lord that you and your men deserve to die for not protecting the Lord's chosen king. Look and see if you can find the king's spear and the water jar that were near his head.”
translation_verse: A ni niŋ shɛm maa bi viɛla. Hal ka Yawɛ ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu, yi simdila kubu, dama yi bi gul’ yi dan’ naa ŋun nyɛ Yawɛ ni booi kpam bahi ninvuɣ’ so zuɣu ni maa. Ka pumpɔŋɔ nyam’ naa kpan’ la min’ o ko’ gaɣili din ʒe o zuɣusaa la ni be luɣ’ shɛli.”

english_verse: Saul could tell it was David's voice, and he called out, “David, my son! Is that you?” “Yes it is, Your Majesty.
translation_verse: Ka Sool daa baŋ Dauda kukoli maa ka bɔh’ o, “M bia Dauda, a kukoli m-bala?” Ka Dauda garigi yɛli, “N dan’ naa, n kukoli m-bala.”

english_verse: Why are you hunting me down? Have I done something wrong, or have I committed a crime?
translation_verse: Ka Dauda mi bɔh’ o, “Ka bɔ n-niŋ ka n dan’ ti kariti doli man’ ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ lala? Bɔ ka n lee niŋ? Taal’ bɔ ka n lee tum?

english_verse: Please listen to what I have to say. If the Lord has turned you against me, maybe a sacrifice will make him change his mind. But if some people have turned you against me, I hope the Lord will punish them! They have forced me to leave the land that belongs to the Lord and have told me to worship foreign gods.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu n dan’ naa, pumpɔŋɔ wummi man’ ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ ni mali yɛtɔɣ’ shɛli ni n yɛl’ a. Di yi nyɛla Yawɛ m-piɛl’ a bahi n zuɣu ŋɔ, nyin’ malimi sara ti o, o ni deei li, amaa di yi nyɛla ninsalinima, Yawɛ ŋun bahim’ ba yoli, dama bɛ kari ma bahi zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ ni n di deei n tarili Yawɛ tiŋgbani ŋɔ ni ka yɛli ma, ‘Cham’ ti jɛm wun’ shɛba.’

english_verse: Don't let me die in a land far away from the Lord. I'm no more important than a flea! Why should the king of Israel hunt me down as if I were a bird in the mountains?”
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ di chɛ ka n ʒim yi n-lu tiŋa tiŋgban’ shɛli din mini Yawɛ shee wɔɣa ni taba ŋɔ ni, dama Izraɛl naa kana ti kariti doli ma kaman nir’ ni kariti doli kɔriŋga zoya zuɣu shɛm la.”

english_verse: “David, you had the chance to kill me today. But you didn't. I was very wrong about you. It was a terrible mistake for me to try to kill you. I've acted like a fool, but I'll never try to harm you again. You're like a son to me, so please come back.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Sool daa yɛli, “N tum taali, m bia Dauda, labimina, n ku lan niŋ a zaɣ’ biɛɣu yaha, dama a lihi n nyɛvili ka di nyɛ binsuŋ a sani zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ; nyama, n tum jɛrilim ka birigi pam.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty, here's your spear! Let one of your soldiers come and get it.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa garigi yɛl’ o, “N dan’ naa, a kpani maa m-bɔŋɔ, chɛ ka nachimba maa ni yino kana ti zaŋ li.”

english_verse: The Lord put you in my power today, but you are his chosen king and I wouldn't harm you. The Lord rewards people who are faithful and live right.
translation_verse: Dauda daa lan yɛli, “Yawɛ tim ninsal’ kam laara o wuntitali min’ o ʒiɛyimtali zuɣu; dama Yawɛ zaŋ a niŋ n nuu ni zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ, ka man’ lee bi saɣi teegi n nuu shihi ŋun’ Yawɛ ni booi kpam bahi nyin’ ninvuɣ’ so zuɣu ni ŋɔ.

english_verse: I spared your life today, and I pray that the Lord will spare my life and keep me safe.”
translation_verse: Nyama, n ni lihi a nyɛvili ka di nyɛ binsuŋ shɛm zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ, lala ka Naawuni gba ni lihi n nyɛvili ka di nyɛ binsuŋ, ka o ni tiligi ma nahiŋgu kam zaa ni.”

english_verse: “David, my son, I pray that the Lord will bless you and make you successful!” David in Philistia Saul went back home. David also left,
translation_verse: Di saha ka Sool daa yɛli Dauda, “M bia Dauda, Naawuni niŋm’ alibarika niŋ a ni. A ni ti tum’ tuma pam, ka di nasara di tumbu ni.” Ka Dauda daa chaŋ o chandi, ka Sool mi ŋmaligi kuli.

english_verse: but he thought to himself, “One of these days, Saul is going to kill me. The only way to escape from him is to go to Philistia. Then I'll be outside of Israel, and Saul will give up trying to catch me.”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yɛl’ o suhu ni, “Pumpɔŋɔ Sool ni ti bahi ku ma dahin’ shɛli. N lan ka n ni yɛn niŋ shɛm pahila n zo n-kuli Filistianim’ tiŋgbɔŋ ni din ni chɛ ka Sool yihi n shee bɔbu tahima Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni, ka n yi o nuu ni”

english_verse: When Saul found out that David had run off to Gath, he stopped trying to catch him.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yɛli Sool ni Dauda zo n-kuli Gaat, ka o daa chɛ o shee bɔbu.

english_verse: One day, David was talking with Achish and said, “If you are happy with me, then let me live in one of the towns in the countryside. I'm not important enough to live here with you in the royal city.”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa ti yɛli Akishi, “A suhu yi yu ma, nyin’ tim ma a tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni tinsi ŋɔ ni luɣ’ shɛli ka n ʒini, dama wula ka man’ ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ min’ a lee yɛn laɣim ʒi na’ tiŋ’ ŋɔ ni?”

english_verse: Achish gave David the town of Ziklag that same day, and Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah ever since.
translation_verse: Ka Akishi daa zaŋ Zikilag ti o dindali maa, dinzuɣu ka Juda nanim’ na kul su Zikilag hal ni zuŋɔ.

english_verse: David was in Philistia for a year and four months.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa be Filistianim’ maa sani yuuni ni chira anahi.

english_verse: The Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites lived in the area from Telam to Shur and on as far as Egypt, and David often attacked their towns.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda min’ o niriba maa daa yiri chani ti liriti Gɛshurinim’ mini Gɛrizinim’ ni Amalɛknima n-tuhiri ba ka fari bɛ nɛma; dama bɛna n-daa nyɛ tiŋ’ maa tiŋbihi kurimbuni ha. Dauda min’ o niriba maa daa yi chanimi hal ti paai Shur n-zaŋ hal ni Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ni.

english_verse: Whenever David and his men attacked a town, they took the sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and the clothing, and killed everyone who lived there. After he returned from a raid, David always went to see Achish,
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa ku tinsi maa niriba zaa, ka bi chɛ ka paɣa bee doo kpalim; ka daa gbahi bɛ piɛri mini niɣi, ni bunsi ni laakumnima, ka va bɛ situra pahi n-lab’ Akishi sanna.

english_verse: who would ask, “Where did you attack today?” David would answer, “Oh, we attacked some desert town that belonged to the Judah tribe.” Sometimes David would say, “Oh, we attacked a town in the desert where the Jerahmeel clan lives” or “We attacked a town in the desert where the Kenites live.”
translation_verse: Ka Akishi daa yi bɔh’ o, “Banim’ ka a lee liri zuŋɔ?” Dauda yɛr’ o mi, “Nɛgɛb’ din be Juda tiŋgban’ ni la nim’ ka n liri.” Bee ŋun yɛli, “Nɛgɛb din be Jɛramiil polo la nim’ ka n liri bee Nɛgɛb din be Kɛn tiŋgban’ ni la nim’ ka n liri.”

english_verse: That's why David killed everyone in the towns he attacked. He thought, “If I let any of them live, they might come to Gath and tell what I've really been doing.” David made these raids all the time he was in Philistia.
translation_verse: Dauda daa na ʒi n-chɛ doo bee paɣa, bɛ ti chaŋ Gaat ti yɛli ba zuɣu. O daa tɛhimi, “Di yi pa lala, bɛ ni chaŋ Gaat ti yɛli ti yɛla.” ka yɛli, “Dauda n-tum shɛm maa.” Lala ka Dauda min’ o niriba maa daa kul niŋdi saha shɛli zaa bɛ ni daa be Filistianim’ sani maa.

english_verse: But Achish trusted David and thought, “David's people must be furious with him. From now on he will have to take orders from me.”
translation_verse: Ka Akishi daa niŋ Dauda naani pam ka yɛli, “O chɛ ka o niriba Izraɛlnim’ bi lan bɔr’ o yɛlli zaa, dinzuɣu o kul ni nyɛ n tumtumda sahakam.”

english_verse: The Philistines went to Shunem and set up camp. Saul called the army of Israel together, and they set up their camp in Gilboa.
translation_verse: Ka Filistianim’ maa daa laɣim ka Shunɛm na nti ti bɛ suɣa do nimaani; ka Sool gba daa laɣim Izraɛlnim’ zaa ka bɛ mi ti bɛ suɣa do Gilibɔa.

english_verse: Saul took one look at the Philistine army and started shaking with fear.
translation_verse: Sool ni daa nya Filistia tɔbbihi maa, ka dabiɛm gbaag’ o ka o suhu fuŋ pam.

english_verse: So he asked the Lord what to do. But the Lord would not answer, either in a dream or by a priest or a prophet.
