translation_verse: Sool ni daa bɔhi Yawɛ ni o baŋ yɛlli maa ni nyɛ shɛm, Yawɛ daa bi garig’ o zahindi puuni bee Urim puuni bee n-chɛ ka anab’ so yɛl’ o shɛli.

english_verse: Then Saul told his officers, “Find me a woman who can talk to the spirits of the dead. I'll go to her and find out what's going to happen.” His servants told him, “There's a woman at Endor who can talk to spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Sool daa yɛl’ o tumtumdiba, “Chamiya ti bo n-nya paɣ’ so ŋun nyɛ jinwara ni be luɣ’ shɛli, ka n chaŋ o sani ti kari saria.” Ka o tumtumdiba maa daa yɛl’ o, “Nyama, jinwara be Ɛndo.”

english_verse: That night, Saul put on different clothing so nobody would recognize him. Then he and two of his men went to the woman, and asked, “Will you bring up the ghost of someone for us?”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Sool daa taɣ’ omaŋ’ biɛhigu, ka taɣi binyɛr’ shɛŋa ye n-zaŋ niriba ayi pa omaŋ’ zuɣu ka bɛ chaŋ paɣ’ maa sani yuŋ, ka o ti yɛl’ o, “Vihim’ nya n-ti ma, ka chɛ ka n ni yɛn boli ninvuɣ’ so yuli ŋɔ shia yina.”

english_verse: The woman said, “Why are you trying to trick me and get me killed? You know King Saul has killed everyone who talks to the spirits of the dead!”
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ maa daa yɛl’ o, “Yɛlimaŋli, a mi Sool ni niŋ shɛm, o kari bukpahinim’ mini jinwariba tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni, ka wula ka a ti kana ti bari n nyɛvili tɔŋ ni a chɛ ka n kpi?”

english_verse: Saul replied, “I swear by the living Lord that nothing will happen to you because of this.”
translation_verse: Ka Sool daa po Yawɛ yɛli, “Hal ka Naawuni ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu, a ku nya tibidarigibo shɛli dimbɔŋɔ zuɣu.”

english_verse: “Who do you want me to bring up?” she asked. “Bring up the ghost of Samuel,” he answered.
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ maa daa bɔh’ o, “Ŋuni ka a lee bɔri ni n chɛ ka o yina?” Ka o yɛl’ o, “M bɔri ni a chɛ ka Samuɛl n-yina.”

english_verse: When the woman saw Samuel, she screamed. Then she turned to Saul and said, “You've tricked me! You're the king!”
translation_verse: Paɣ’ maa nini ni daa ti nya Samuɛl, o daa ŋmɛla kuŋ’ pam ka bɔhi Sool, “Bɔ n-niŋ ka a yɔhim ma? Nyini n-nyɛ Sool!”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Saul replied. “Just tell me what you see.” She answered, “I see a spirit rising up out of the ground.”
translation_verse: Ka naa daa yɛl’ o, “Di zɔri dabiɛm, bɔ ka a lee nya?” Ka paɣ’ maa yɛl’ o, “N nyala so shia ka di yiri tiŋgban’ ni na.”

english_verse: “What does it look like?” “It looks like an old man wearing a robe.” Saul knew it was Samuel, so he bowed down low.
translation_verse: Ka o bɔh’ o, “O biɛhigu lee nyɛla wula?” Ka o yɛl’ o, “Do’ kurili n-zaŋ kparibu pɔb’ omaŋa n-yirina.” Di saha ka Sool daa baŋ ni Samuɛl m-bala, ka damdi zaŋ o nina kpa tiŋa n-lu o sizuura.

english_verse: “Why are you bothering me by bringing me up like this?” Samuel asked. “I'm terribly worried,” Saul answered. “The Philistines are about to attack me. God has turned his back on me and won't answer any more by prophets or by dreams. What should I do?”
translation_verse: Ka Samuɛl daa bɔhi Sool, “Bɔ n-niŋ ka a nahim ma n-chɛ ka n yina.?” Ka Sool garigi yɛl’ o, “Muɣisigu titali m-paa’ ma, dama Filistianima n-yɛn tuhi ma, ka Naawuni chɛ ma, ka bi lan garigiri ma. O bi lan chɛ ka anabinim’ garigiri ma bee n-chɛ ka n nyari shɛli zahindi ni. Dinzuɣu ka m bol’ a na ni a ti wuhi ma n ni yɛn niŋ shɛm.”

english_verse: Samuel said: If the Lord has turned away from you and is now your enemy, don't ask me what to do.
translation_verse: Ka Samuɛl yɛl’ o, “Yawɛ zaɣis’ a ka leeg’ a dima, ka wula a lan bɔhiri ma?

english_verse: I've already told you: The Lord has sworn to take the kingdom from you and give it to David. And that's just what he's doing!
translation_verse: Yawɛ ni daa yɛli ma ni n yɛl’ a ni o ni niŋ a shɛm la ka o niŋ a maa, dama o darigi deei nam maa a nuu ni n-zaŋ ti Dauda ŋun nyɛ a kpee la.

english_verse: When the Lord was angry with the Amalekites, he told you to destroy them, but you didn't do it. That's why the Lord is doing this to you.
translation_verse: A ni daa zaɣisi Yawɛ noli ka bi ku Amalɛknim’ zaa, ka saɣim bɛ ni mali shɛlikam zaa la zuɣu ka Yawɛ niŋ a o ni niŋ a shɛm zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ.

english_verse: Tomorrow the Lord will let the Philistines defeat Israel's army, then you and your sons will join me down here in the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Din pahi nyɛla, Yawɛ ni zaŋ a mini Izraɛlnim’ niŋ Filistianim’ nuu ni, dinzuɣu biɛɣuni a min’ a bidibisi sa ni be n sani, dama Yawɛ ni zaŋ Izraɛl tɔbbihi niŋ Filistianim’ nuu ni.”

english_verse: At once, Saul collapsed and lay stretched out on the floor, terrified at what Samuel had said. He was weak because he had not eaten anything since the day before.
translation_verse: Di saha ka dabiɛm daa gbaai Sool ka o lu n-teei dɔni tiŋa, Samuɛl ni daa yɛl’ o yɛtɔɣ’ shɛŋa maa zuɣu. O daa lan ka yaa, dama o daa bi di binshɛli dindali maa wuntaŋ’ ni mini yuŋ zaa.

english_verse: The woman came over to Saul, and when she saw that he was completely terrified, she said, “Your Majesty, I listened to you and risked my life to do what you asked.
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ maa daa chaŋ Sool sani nti nya ka dabiɛm gbaai Sool pam ka o yɛl’ o, “Nyama, mani ŋun nyɛ a dabipaɣ’ ŋɔ niŋ a ni yɛli ma ni n niŋ shɛli maa, m mi zaŋla n nyɛvili pa talima, ka niŋ a ni yɛli ma ni n niŋ shɛm maa.

english_verse: Now please listen to me. Let me get you a little something to eat. It will give you strength for your walk back to camp.”
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ di simdi ka a gba niŋ mani ŋun nyɛ a dabipaɣ’ ŋɔ ni yɛn yɛl’ a ni a niŋ shɛm ŋɔ. Chɛ ka n niŋ bindirigu ti a ka a di ka nya yaa lab’ yiŋa.”

english_verse: “No, I won't eat!” But his officers and the woman kept on urging Saul, until he finally agreed. He got up off the floor and sat on the bed.
translation_verse: Ka o daa zaɣisi ka yɛli, “N ku di.” Amaa ka o tumtumdiba la mini paɣ’ maa daa kpaŋ bɛmaŋa m-balim o hal ka o ti saɣi, ka daa yiɣisi tiŋa n-ʒini garo zuɣu.

english_verse: At once the woman killed a calf that she had been fattening up. She cooked part of the meat and baked some thin bread.
translation_verse: Paɣ’ maa mi daa mali naɣipol’ kpabili o yiŋa, ka o daa dii yiɣisi yomyom chɛ ka bɛ kɔrigi naɣipolli maa, ka o niŋ zim ŋɔri mali bɔrɔbɔro din ka dabindi

english_verse: Then she served the food to Saul and his officers, who ate and left before daylight.
translation_verse: n-zaŋ li na ti zali Sool min’ o tumtumdiba maa tooni ka bɛ di, ka daa yiɣisi kuli yuŋ maa.

english_verse: The Philistine army commanders were angry and shouted: Send David back to the town you gave him. We won't have him going into the battle with us. He could turn and fight against us! Saul would take David back as an officer if David brought him the heads of our soldiers.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Filistia sapashinnim’ maa daa je suli niŋ Akishi ka yɛl’ o, “Chɛ ka o lab’ kuli ti be a ni zaŋ tiŋ’ shɛli ti o la ni, o ku dol’ ti chaŋ tɔb’ ni, di pa shɛli ka o ti leei ti dima nimaani. Dama wula ka o yɛn niŋ ka o naa maa lan deeg’ o, ka di pala o ŋmala ti niriba ŋɔ zuɣuri ti o.

english_verse: The Israelites even dance and sing, “Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!”
translation_verse: Pa Dauda so yɛla bɛ ni wari waa ka yiini yila yɛra, ‘Sool kula niriba tuhilituhili, ka Dauda mi ku niriba tuhi’ piapia la m-bala?’ ”

english_verse: Achish called David over and said: I swear by the living Lord that you've been honest with me, and I want you to fight by my side. I don't think you've done anything wrong from the day you joined me until this very moment. But the other Philistine rulers don't want you to come along.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Akishi daa boli Dauda ti yɛl’ o, “Hal ka Yawɛ ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu, a nyɛla ŋun ʒe ma yim, ka man’ sani, di simdi ni a pahi dol’ ti chaŋ tɔb’ maa ni, dama dahin’ shɛli a ni kuli n sanna hal ni zuŋɔ, n na bi nya a galimi. Amaa di zaa yoli, nanim’ maa bi saɣi ni a dol’ ti chaŋ.

english_verse: Go on back home and try not to upset them.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ labimi kuli ni suhudoo, ka miri ka a chɛ ka Filistia nanim’ suhuri ti miligi a zuɣu.”

english_verse: Achish said: I believe that you're as good as an angel of God, but our army commanders have decided that you can't fight in this battle.
translation_verse: Ka Akishi daa garigi yɛli Dauda, “M mi ni a ka galimi shɛli kaman Naawuni malaika ni ka galimi shɛm la, amaa di zaa yoli, Filistia sapashinnim’ maa yɛliya ni a di dol’ ti chaŋ tɔb’ maa ni.

english_verse: You and your troops will have to go back to the town I gave you. Get up and leave tomorrow morning as soon as it's light. I'm pleased with you, so don't let any of this bother you.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu biɛɣuni asiba di yi sa kul neerina, a min’ a niriba bɛn doli ma kana maa yin’ daŋmiya yiɣisibu n-labi yiŋ’ yomyom.”

english_verse: David and his men got up early in the morning and headed back toward Philistia, while the Philistines left for Jezreel.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda min’ o niriba maa daa daŋ yibu asiba n-labi Filistianim’ tiŋgbɔŋ maa ni, ka Filistianim’ maa daa chaŋ Jɛziriil.

english_verse: It took David and his men three days to reach Ziklag. But while they had been away, the Amalekites had been raiding in the desert around there. They had attacked Ziklag, burned it to the ground,
translation_verse: Ka Dauda min’ o niriba maa daa ti paai Zikilag daba ata dali n-nya ka Amalɛknim’ kamina ti liri Nɛgɛbinim’ mini Zikilagnima n-nyaŋ Zikilagnim’ maa, ka nyo tiŋ’ maa buɣim.

english_verse: When David and his men came to Ziklag, they saw the burned-out ruins and learned that their families had been taken captive.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda min’ o niriba maa daa ti paai tiŋ’ maa ni n-nya ka bɛ nyo li la buɣim, ka gbahi bɛ paɣiba mini bɛ bidibisi ni bipuɣinsi zaa chaŋ.

english_verse: They started crying and kept it up until they were too weak to cry any more.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda mini ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn daa be o sani maa duhi bɛ yɛhi n-kum hal ti lan ka yaa din ni kum.

english_verse: David's two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail, had been taken captive with everyone else.
translation_verse: Bɛ daa gbahi Dauda paɣiba ayi la gba chaŋ; Ahinɔam ŋun daa yi Jɛziriil na la mini Abigeel Nabal pakoli ŋun daa yi Kamɛl na la.

english_verse: David was desperate. His soldiers were so upset over what had happened to their sons and daughters that they were thinking about stoning David to death. But he felt the Lord God giving him strength,
translation_verse: Ka Dauda suhu daa saɣim pam, dama o niriba maa suhuri daa yiɣisimi, ka bɛ yɛli ni bɛ ni lab’ o kuɣa. Dama sokam daa kul fabindila o bidibisi min’ o bipuɣinsi zuɣu. Amaa ka Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Dauda Naawuni ŋɔ daa kpaŋs’ o suhu.

english_verse: and he said to the priest, “Abiathar, let's ask God what to do.” Abiathar brought everything he needed to get answers from God, and he went over to David.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yɛli Ahimɛlɛk bia Abiata ŋun daa nyɛ maligumaana la, “Zaŋmi tan’ shɛli din ŋmani mukuru la ti ma na.” Ka Abiata daa zaŋ tan’ shɛli din ŋmani mukuru maa na ti ti Dauda.

english_verse: Then David asked the Lord, “Should I go after the people who raided our town? Can I catch up with them?” “Go after them,” the Lord answered. “You will catch up with them, and you will rescue your families.”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa bɔhi Yawɛ, “M biɛhimi ŋmɛnditoya ŋɔ naba? N ni paai ba?” Ka o garigi yɛl’ o, “Biɛhimi bɛ naba, a ni paa’ ba n-fa a niriba maa.”

english_verse: Some of David's men found an Egyptian out in a field and took him to David. They gave the Egyptian some bread, and he ate it. Then they gave him a drink of water,
translation_verse: Ka Dauda niriba maa daa ti nya Ijipti nachimbil’ so mɔɣu maa ni n-zaŋ o ka Dauda sanna nti ti o bɔrɔbɔro ka o ŋubi, ka ti o kom ka o nyu.

english_verse: some dried figs, and two handfuls of raisins. This was the first time in three days he had tasted food or water. Now he felt much better.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa lan ti o bɛ ni zaŋ fiig tihi wala m-pahi mali mahi’ shɛŋa mini wain wal’ kuma yila ayi. O ni daa di n-naai ka o nini neei, dama o daa bi di shɛli bee n-nyu kom wuntaŋ’ ni mini yuŋ dabisi’ muna ata.

english_verse: “Who is your master?” David asked. “And where do you come from?” “I'm from Egypt,” the young man answered. “I'm the servant of an Amalekite, but he left me here three days ago because I was sick.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa bɔh’ o, “Tiŋ’ kani ka a lee yina? Ŋuni n-lee su a?” Ka o garigi yɛli, “N nyɛla Ijipti nachimbila, ka nyɛ ŋun tumdi Amalɛk do’ so tuma. N daa kala alaafee, ka ŋun su ma maa chɛ ma bahi ka chaŋ, di zuŋɔ daba ata m-bɔŋɔ.

english_verse: We had attacked some towns in the desert where the Cherethites live, in the area that belongs to Judah, and in the desert where the Caleb clan lives. And we burned down Ziklag.”
translation_verse: Ti daa chaŋmi ti ŋme Nɛgɛb din nyɛ Chɛrɛtinim’ tiŋ’ ka be Juda tiŋgban’ ni la, ka di bɛ nɛma. Ka ti daa lan chaŋ ti ŋme Nɛgɛb shɛli din nyɛ Kalɛb daŋ niriba tiŋ’ la gba ka di bɛ nɛma; ka nyo Zikilag yiya zaa buɣim.”

english_verse: “Will you take me to those Amalekites?” David asked. “Yes, I will, if you promise with God as a witness that you won't kill me or hand me over to my master.”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa bɔh’ o, “A ni saɣi tahi ma ŋmɛnditoya maa sani?” Ka o garigi yɛli Dauda, “Pom’ Naawuni ni a ku ku ma bee n-zaŋ ma niŋ n dan’ maa nuu ni pɔi, ka n naanyi zaŋ a tahi bɛ sani.”

english_verse: He led David to the Amalekites. They were eating and drinking everywhere, celebrating because of what they had taken from Philistia and Judah.
translation_verse: O ni daa zaŋ o tahi bɛ sani, ŋmɛnditoya maa daa woliwolila taba ʒiya diri ka nyura, ka wari wahi, bɛ ni ŋme n-di neen’ shɛŋa Filistia mini Juda tiŋgbana ni maa zuɣu.

english_verse: David attacked just before sunrise the next day and fought until sunset. Four hundred Amalekites rode away on camels, but they were the only ones who escaped.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa daŋ yibu asibaasi n-liri ba n-tuhi ba hal ni zaawuni, ka do’ so daa bi zo n-tiligi naɣila nachimba kɔbisinahi n-daa ba laakumnim’ zo n-tiligi.

english_verse: David rescued his two wives and everyone else the Amalekites had taken from Ziklag.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa lan fa Amalɛknim’ maa ni daa ŋme n-di binshɛŋa maa zaa, ka lan fa o paɣiba ayi la gba.

english_verse: including their livestock. David also took the sheep and cattle that the Amalekites had with them, but he kept these separate from the others. Everyone agreed that these would be David's reward.
translation_verse: Dauda daa lan tuhi fa piɛri mini niɣi, ka o niriba maa daa taɣiri niɣi maa be tooni ka yɛra, “Dauda ni tuhi fa neen’ shɛŋa m-bɔŋɔ.”

english_verse: Some of David's men were good-for-nothings, and they said, “Those men didn't go with us to the battle, so they don't get any of the things we took back from the Amalekites. Let them take their wives and children and go!”
translation_verse: Amaa ka putɔɣulaannim’ mini ninvuɣ’ yoya bɛn daa pahi doli Dauda chaŋ maa yɛli, “Ti bi yɛn ti ba ti ni tuhi fa neen’ shɛŋa ŋɔ shɛli, naɣila bɛ paɣiba mini bɛ bihi ka ti ni zaŋ ti ba ka bɛ chaŋ, dama bɛ daa bi dol’ ti chaŋ.”

english_verse: But David said: My friends, don't be so greedy with what the Lord has given us! The Lord protected us and gave us victory over the people who attacked.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Dauda daa yɛli, “M mabihi, di bi simdi ni yi niŋ Yawɛ ni ti ti binshɛŋa maa lala, dama ŋuna n-daa gul’ ti ka zaŋ ŋmɛnditoya bɛn daa kana ti liri ti maa niŋ ti nuu ni.

english_verse: Who would pay attention to you, anyway? Soldiers who stay behind to guard the camp get as much as those who go into battle.
translation_verse: Ŋuni n-lee ni saɣi yi ni yɛli shɛm maa yɛlli ŋɔ puuni? Ŋun chaŋ tɔb’ maa tuhibu shee tarili ni nyɛ shɛm, ŋun ʒiya guli nɛma gba tarili yɛn nyɛla lala. Bɛ zaa tarili yɛn nyɛla yim.”

english_verse: David made this a law for Israel, and it has been the same ever since.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa zaŋ li lee kali ni zaligu Izraɛlnim’ zaa sani, ka bɛ dol’ li hal ni zuŋɔ.

english_verse: David went back to Ziklag with everything they had taken from the Amalekites. He sent some of these things as gifts to his friends who were leaders of Judah, and he told them, “We took these things from the Lord's enemies. Please accept them as a gift.”
translation_verse: Dauda ni daa labi Zikilag, o daa piila o ni tuhi di neen’ shɛŋa maa shɛli nti ti o zɔnim’ bɛn daa nyɛ Juda kpamba la ka yɛli ba, “N ni tuhi Yawɛ dimnim’ ka di neen’ shɛŋa ka m pii tin ya na maa.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Philistines were fighting Israel at Mount Gilboa. Israel's soldiers ran from the Philistines, and many of them were killed.
translation_verse: Filistianim’ mini Izraɛlnim’ daa ti tuhiri tɔbu, ka Izraɛlnim’ daa ŋmaligi guui ka chɛ Filistianim’ maa; ka Filistianim’ maa daa dol’ ba ti ku ba Gilibɔa Zoli zuɣu.

english_verse: The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons, and they killed his sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
translation_verse: Ka Filistianim’ maa daa kari ti paai Sool min’ o bidibisi n-ku o bidibisi bɛn daa nyɛ Jɔnatan mini Abinadab ni Malikishua.

english_verse: The fighting was fierce around Saul, and he was badly wounded by enemy arrows.
translation_verse: Ka tɔb’ maa daa kpaɣi mii Sool, ka peentɔriba daa nya o n-to o piɛm ti o daŋ pam.

english_verse: Saul told the soldier who carried his weapons, “Kill me with your sword! I don't want these worthless Philistines to torture and make fun of me.” But the soldier was afraid to kill him. Saul then took out his own sword; he stuck the blade into his stomach, and fell on it.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Sool daa yɛl’ o gbaɣinɔʒira, “Ŋoom’ a takɔbi n-kuhi ku ma, di so ka bɛn bi gundi ŋɔ ti kana ti zaŋ bɛ takɔbiri kuhi ku ma, ka zaŋ ma diɛm.” Amaa ka dabiɛm daa gbaag’ o gbaɣinɔʒira maa pam ka o bi saɣi ku o. Dinzuɣu ka Sool daa zaŋ omaŋmaŋ’ takɔbi zali n-lu di zuɣu.

english_verse: When the soldier knew that Saul was dead, he killed himself in the same way.
translation_verse: Sool gbaɣinɔʒiri maa ni daa nya ka Sool kpi maa, ka o gba lu o takɔbi zuɣu kpi m-pah’ o zuɣu.

english_verse: Saul was dead, his three sons were dead, and the soldier who carried his weapons was dead. They and all his soldiers died on that same day.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu Sool min’ o bidibis’ ata ni o gbaɣinɔʒira ni o niriba zaa ni daa laɣim kpi dahin yini shɛm m-bala.

english_verse: The Israelites on the other side of Jezreel Valley and the other side of the Jordan learned that Saul and his sons were dead. They saw that the Israelite army had run away. So they ran away too, and the Philistines moved into the towns the Israelites had left behind.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ bɛn daa be vinvamli maa yaɣ’ din’ la mini bɛn daa be Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili dul’ la daa nya ka Izraɛlnim’ ŋmaligi guui, ka Sool min’ o bidibisi kpi, ka bɛ daa yi n-zo ka chɛ bɛ tinsi, ka Filistianim’ maa daa kana ti be di ni.

english_verse: The day after the battle, when the Philistines returned to the battlefield to take the weapons of the dead Israelite soldiers, they found Saul and his three sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa.
translation_verse: N-daa yi biɛɣu ka Filistianim’ maa chaŋ ni bɛ ti yeei bɛ ni ku shɛb’ maa nɛma, ka daa nya ka Sool min’ o bidibis’ ata maa lu n-dola Gilibɔa Zoli zuɣu.

english_verse: The people who lived in Jabesh in Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul's body.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Jabɛshigiliadnim’ daa wum Filistianim’ ni niŋ Sool shɛm maa,

english_verse: So one night, some brave men from Jabesh went to Beth-Shan. They took down the bodies of Saul and his sons, then brought them back to Jabesh and burned them.
translation_verse: ka bɛ dɔbba bɛn zaa mali suhukpeeni daa yi n-chaŋ yuŋ ti yihi Sool min’ o bidibisi maa Bɛtishan gooni maa zuɣu n-zaŋ ba chaŋ Jabɛshi ti nyo ba buɣim nimaani.

english_verse: They buried the bones under a small tree in Jabesh, and for seven days, they went without eating to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa va bɛ kɔba ti sɔɣi Jabɛshi tiŋ’ puuni tamarisik tia gbini, ka lo noli daba ayopɔin.

english_verse: Saul was dead. Meanwhile, David had defeated the Amalekites and returned to Ziklag.
translation_verse: Dauda ni daa tuhi Amalɛknim’ maa ka labina Naa Sool kum maa nyaaŋa, o daa kpalimla Zikilag daba ayi.

english_verse: Three days later, a soldier came from Saul's army. His clothes were torn, and dirt was on his head. He went to David and knelt down in front of him.
translation_verse: Nyama di daba ata dali ka do’ so daa ti yi Sool sansan’ ni n-zo m-paana ka o binyɛra chahi, ka taŋkpaɣu puɣ’ o zuɣu. O ni daa ti paai Dauda sani, o daa lumi gbani Dauda tooni lu o sizuura.

english_verse: David asked, “Where did you come from?” The man answered, “From Israel's army. I barely escaped with my life.”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa bɔh’ o, “Ya ka a yina?” Ka o garigi yɛl’ o, “Izraɛlnim’ sansan’ ni ka n yi n-zo na maa.”

english_verse: “Who won the battle?” David asked. The man said, “Our army turned and ran, but many were wounded and died. Even King Saul and his son Jonathan are dead.”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda yɛl’ o, “Yɛlim’ ma din niŋ.” Ka o yɛl’ o, “Tɔbbihi maa ŋmaligimi guui, ka bɛ pam lu tɔb’ maa ni, ka Sool min’ o bia Jɔnatan gba lu tɔb’ maa ni.”

english_verse: The young man replied: I was on Mount Gilboa and saw King Saul leaning on his spear. The enemy's war chariots and cavalry were closing in on him.
translation_verse: Ka nachimbil’ so ŋun daa yɛl’ o li maa yɛli, “Di daa niŋla daliri ka n chaŋ Gilibɔa Zoli zuɣu nti chirigi Sool ka o zaŋ omaŋ’ dalim’ o kpani, ka chɛchɛbunsi mini wɔribariba daa kabiri kani o sanna.

english_verse: When he turned around and saw me, he called me over. I went and asked what he wanted.
translation_verse: Ka o daa ŋmaligi lih’ o nyaaŋa nya ma ka boli ma, ka n garigi yɛl’ o, ‘N-nyɛ ma.’

english_verse: Saul asked me, “Who are you?” “An Amalekite,” I answered.
translation_verse: Ka o bɔhi n ni nyɛ ninvuɣ’ so, ka n yɛl’ o, ‘N nyɛla Amalɛk nira.’

english_verse: Then he said, “Kill me! I'm dying, and I'm in terrible pain.”
translation_verse: Ka o yɛli ma, ‘Kamina ti zani baɣili ma n-ku ma, dama n nya daŋ pam, ka m mi shia na bi siɣi.’

english_verse: So I killed him. I knew he was too badly wounded to live much longer. Then I took his crown and his arm-band, and I brought them to you, Your Majesty. Here they are.
translation_verse: Di saha ka n daa chaŋ ti zani baɣil’ o n-ku o, ka pilig’ o zuɣupiligu din be o zuɣu ni, ka lan pirigi baŋ’ din be o nuu ni na, dama n daa baŋya ni o ni lu n-doya shɛm maa, o ku lan gali. Dinzuɣu ka n zaŋ o nɛma maa na ni n ti ti nyini n dana.”

english_verse: At once, David and his soldiers tore their clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda daa gbaag’ omaŋmaŋ’ binyɛra n-dar’ chahi li, ka bɛnkam daa be o sani gba daa niŋ lala.

english_verse: They cried all day long and would not eat anything. Everyone was sad because Saul, his son Jonathan, and many of the Lord's people had been killed in the battle.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa kum ka fabili pam, ka lo noli Sool min’ o bia Jɔnatan ni Yawɛ niriba Izraɛlnim’ zuɣu dindali hal ni zaawuni, bɛ ni daa zaŋ takɔbiri ku ba maa zuɣu.

english_verse: David asked the young man, “Where is your home?” The man replied, “My father is an Amalekite, but we live in Israel.”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa bɔhi nachimbil’ so ŋun daa yɛl’ o li maa, “Tiŋ’ kani ka a lee yina?” Ka o garigi yɛl’ o, “N nyɛla Amalɛk saan’ so ŋun be a tiŋgbani ŋɔ ni bia.”

english_verse: David said to him, “Why weren't you afraid to kill the Lord's chosen king? And you even told what you did. It's your own fault that you're going to die!” Then David told one of his soldiers, “Come here and kill this man!” David Sings in Memory of Saul
translation_verse: Ka Dauda yɛl’ o, “A ʒim yihibu taali ʒi a zuɣu, dama amaŋmaŋ’ noli n-di a shɛhira yɛli, ‘Mani n-ku Yawɛ ni pii ninvuɣ’ so maa.’ ” Dauda fabili Naa Sool mini Jɔnatan zuɣu

english_verse: David sang a song in memory of Saul and Jonathan,
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa fabili fabila ŋɔ Sool min’ o bia Jɔnatan zuɣu,

english_verse: Israel, your famous hero lies dead on the hills, and your mighty warriors have fallen!
translation_verse: Bɛ ku Izraɛl jilima zoya din du pam zuɣu, ka wɔɣira lu.

english_verse: Don't tell it in Gath or spread the news on the streets of Ashkelon. The godless Philistine women will be happy and jump for joy.
translation_verse: Di moliya di yɛla gili Gaat fɔŋ ni; yi mi di moliya di yɛla doli Ashikɛlɔn solɔri, ka di zuɣu chɛ ka Filistia bipuɣinsi yiɣi jam, bee n-chɛ ka bɛn bi gundi ŋɔ bipuɣinsi suhuri paligi.

english_verse: Don't let dew or rain fall on the hills of Gilboa. Don't let its fields grow offerings for God. There the warriors' shields were smeared with mud, and Saul's own shield was left unpolished.
translation_verse: “Yinim’ Gilibɔa zoya, maligim bee saa ku lan lu yi zuɣu na bee bimbilima ti lan bili yi zolɔna ni. Dama nimaani ka kpiɔŋlaannim’ bidibbina nya filiŋ. Ka Sool nyɔtaɣirigu bi lan nya kpam ʒe.

english_verse: The arrows of Jonathan struck, and warriors died. The sword of Saul cut the enemy apart.
translation_verse: Jɔnatan tɔbu daa ʒi n-lab’ kuli ka pa ni o ni ku ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ ʒim mini kpiɔŋlaannim’ kpam n-varim li. Ka Sool mi takɔbi na ʒi n-chɛ n-ziŋ.

english_verse: It was easy to love Saul and Jonathan. Together in life, together in death, they were faster than eagles and stronger than lions.
translation_verse: Sool mini Jɔnatan, n yurinima bɛn veeni yurilim. Bɛ daa bi woligi taba bɛ nyɛviya ni mini bɛ kum ni. Bɛ daa valim gari tɔrili. Bɛ daa mali kpiɔŋ gari gbuɣima.

english_verse: Women of Israel, cry for Saul. He brought you fine red cloth and jewelry made of gold.
translation_verse: Yinim’ Izraɛl bipuɣinsi, kummiya Sool zuɣu. Ŋuna n-zaŋ mulifu viɛlli soli ya. Ŋuna n-zaŋ salima yɛri yɛli ya.

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen in the heat of battle, and Jonathan lies dead on the hills of Gilboa.
translation_verse: Nyam’ kpiɔŋlaannim’ ni lu tɔb’ sunsuuni shɛm! Bɛ ku Jɔnatan sɔŋ zoya zuɣu!

english_verse: Jonathan, I miss you most! I loved you like a brother. You were truly loyal to me, more faithful than a wife to her husband.
translation_verse: M mabia Jɔnatan, n suhu saɣimya pam a zuɣu. M min’ a biɛhigu daa lu n-taɣili tab’ pam. A yurilim zaŋ chaŋ n sani daa mali alahiziba, ka galisi pam gari paɣ’ ni mali yurilim shɛm.

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen, and their weapons are destroyed.
translation_verse: Nyam’ kpiɔŋlaannim’ ni lu tɔb’ sunsuuni shɛm, ka bɛ bidibbina bahi yoli!

english_verse: Later, David asked the Lord, “Should I go back to one of the towns of Judah?” The Lord answered, “Yes.” David asked, “Which town should I go to?” “Go to Hebron,” the Lord replied.
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka Dauda daa bɔhi Yawɛ, “N cham’ Juda tin’ shɛl’ ni ti ʒini?” Ka Yawɛ yɛl’ o, “Chama.” Ka Dauda lan bɔhi, “N cham’ tiŋ’ kani?” Ka o yɛl’ o, “Cham’ Hiburɔn.”

english_verse: David went to Hebron with his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail. Ahinoam was from Jezreel, and Abigail was the widow of Nabal from Carmel.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda daa zaŋ o paɣiba ayi la Ahinɔam ŋun daa yi Jɛziriil na la mini Abigeel Nabal pakoli ŋun mi daa yi Kamɛl na la chaŋ Hiburɔn.

english_verse: David also told his men and their families to come and live in the villages near Hebron.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa zaŋ ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn zaa be o sani mini bɛ malibu na ka bɛ ti ʒini Hiburɔn fɔndi ni.

english_verse: The people of Judah met with David at Hebron and poured olive oil on his head to show that he was their new king. Then they told David, “The people from Jabesh in Gilead buried Saul.”
translation_verse: Ka Judanim’ daa kana ti booi kpam bahi Dauda zuɣu ni nimaani n-zaŋ o leei Judanim’ naa. Ka bɛ daa yɛli Dauda ni Jabɛshigiliadnima n-daa sɔɣi Sool.

english_verse: David sent messengers to tell them: The Lord bless you! You were kind enough to bury Saul your ruler,
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa tim tuumba Jabɛshigiliadnim’ maa sani ti yɛli ba, “Yawɛ niŋmi alibarika niŋ yi ni yi ni daa wuhi yi ʒiɛyimtali ni nyɛ shɛm zaŋ chaŋ yi dan’ Naa Sool sani, ka sɔɣ’ o la zuɣu.

english_verse: and I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you. I will be your friend because of what you have done.
translation_verse: Pumpɔŋɔ Yawɛ ni wuhi ya o yurilim min’ o ʒiɛyimtali ni nyɛ shɛm zaŋ chaŋ yi sani; ka man’ gba ni niŋ ya zaɣ’ viɛlli yi ni daa tum tuun’ shɛli maa zuɣu.

english_verse: Saul is dead, but the tribe of Judah has made me their king. So be strong and have courage. Ishbosheth Becomes King of Israel
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ kpaŋsimiya yimaŋa ka mali suhukpeeni, dama yi dan’ Sool kpiya ka Judanim’ mi zaŋ ma leei bɛ naa.” Bɛ zaŋ Ishibɔshɛt leei Izraɛlnim’ naa

english_verse: Abner the son of Ner had been the general of Saul's army. He took Saul's son Ishbosheth across the Jordan River to Mahanaim
translation_verse: Ka Sool tɔbbihi sapashin’ kpɛm’ Abinɛr ŋun daa nyɛ Nɛr bia la daa zaŋ Sool bia Ishibɔshɛt n-zo chaŋ Mahanaim

english_verse: and made him king of Israel, including the areas of Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, and Benjamin.
translation_verse: nti zaŋ o leei naa ni o su Giliad mini Ashur ni Jɛziriil ni Ifriim ni Bɛnjamin tiŋgbana ni Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ zaa.

english_verse: and he ruled from Hebron for seven and a half years. The War between David and Ishbosheth
translation_verse: Saha shɛli Dauda ni daa di nam ʒi Hiburɔn n-su Judanim’ maa yuma daa nyɛla yuma ayopɔin ni chira ayɔbu. Tɔb’ lu Judanim’ mini Izraɛlnim’ sunsuuni

english_verse: One day, Abner and the soldiers of Ishbosheth left Mahanaim and went to Gibeon.
translation_verse: Ka Abinɛr ŋun daa nyɛ Nɛr bia la mini Sool bia Ishibɔshɛt la tɔbbihi daa yi Mahanaim chaŋ Gibiɔn.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab the son of Zeruiah was leading David's soldiers, and the two groups met at the pool in Gibeon. Abner and his men sat down on one side of the pool, while Joab and his men sat on the other side.
translation_verse: Ka Jɔab ŋun daa nyɛ Zɛruya bia la mini Dauda tɔbbihi mi daa yi n-chaŋ ti paai ba Gibiɔn biaŋ ni n-chaŋ ti ʒini biaŋ maa yaɣ’ yini polo ka bɛn’ la mi chaŋ ti ʒini biaŋ maa yaɣ’ din’ la polo.

english_verse: Abner yelled to Joab, “Let's get some of our best soldiers to stand up and fight each other!” Joab agreed,
translation_verse: Ka Abinɛr daa yɛli Jɔab, “Chɛ ka nachimba maa yiɣisi diɛm ka ti nya.” Ka Jɔab yɛli, “Chɛ ka bɛ yiɣisi.”

english_verse: and twelve of Ishbosheth's men from the tribe of Benjamin got up to fight twelve of David's men.
translation_verse: Di saha ka bɛ daa yiɣisi kaman bɛ kalinli ni nyɛ shɛm, ka ninvuɣ’ pinaayi daa yi Bɛnjamin mini Ishibɔshɛt Sool bia maa polo na, ka ninvuɣ’ pinaayi mi yi Dauda tɔbbihi maa polo na.

english_verse: They grabbed each other by the hair and stabbed each other in the side with their daggers. They all died right there! That's why the place in Gibeon is called “Field of Daggers.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ zaa ti gbahi tab’ zuɣuri, ka zaŋ takɔbiri kuhi tab’ puluɣa ni, ka bɛ zaa laɣim lu n-kpi. Dinzuɣu ka bɛ daa boli nimaani Hɛlikatihazurim, ka di be Gibiɔn.

english_verse: Then everyone started fighting. Both sides fought very hard, but David's soldiers defeated Abner and the soldiers of Israel.
translation_verse: Ka nimmoo tɔb’ daa bili dindali maa, ka Naa Dauda tɔbbihi maa daa tuhi nyaŋ Abinɛr mini Izraɛlnim’ maa.

english_verse: Zeruiah's three sons were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel could run as fast as a deer in an open field,
translation_verse: Ka Zɛruya bidibis’ ata daa be nimaani, bɛna n-nyɛ Jɔab mini Abishai ni Asahɛl. Asahɛl daa guurimi kaman molifu la.

english_verse: When Abner turned and saw him, he said, “Is that you, Asahel?” Asahel answered, “Yes it is.”
translation_verse: Ka Abinɛr daa ti ŋmaligi lih’ o nyaaŋa nya o ka bɔh’ o, “Asahɛl, nyini m-bala?” Ka o yɛli, “Mani m-bala.”

english_verse: Abner said, “There are soldiers all around. Stop chasing me and fight one of them! Kill him and take his clothes and weapons for yourself.” But Asahel refused to stop.
translation_verse: Ka Abinɛr yɛl’ o, “Ŋmaligim’ a nudirigu bee a nuzaa polo n-gbaai nachimba ŋɔ ni yino n-fa o ni mali shɛli.” Amaa ka Asahɛl bi ŋmaligi ka chɛ o dolibu.

english_verse: Abner said, “If you don't turn back, I'll have to kill you! Then I could never face your brother Joab again.”
translation_verse: Ka Abinɛr ti lan yɛl’ o, “Ŋmaligim’ ka chɛ ma dolibu; bɔ n-niŋ ka a yɛn chɛ ka n ku a? N yi ku a wula ka n lee yɛn niŋ lih’ a biɛli Jɔab ninni?”

english_verse: But Asahel would not turn back, so Abner struck him in the stomach with the back end of his spear. The spear went all the way through and came out of his back. Asahel fell down and died. Everyone who saw Asahel lying dead just stopped and stood still.
translation_verse: Amaa ka o daa zaɣisi ni o ku ŋmaligi; dinzuɣu ka Abinɛr daa zaŋ o kpani zuɣu polo to o pul’ ni ka di pili yi o yaaŋa zuɣu, ka o daa lu nimaani kpi. Ka bɛn zaa daa paai Asahɛl ni lu luɣ’ shɛli kpi maa kpalim zani baalim.

english_verse: But Joab and Abishai went after Abner. Finally, about sunset, they came to the hill of Ammah, not far from Giah on the road to Gibeon Desert.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Jɔab mini Abishai bɛn’ daa kari doli Abinɛr, zaŋ chaŋ wuntan’ luhili saha ka bɛ daa paai Amma Zoli din be Gia polo Gibiɔn mɔɣu ni soli zuɣu la gbini.

english_verse: Abner brought the men of Benjamin together in one group on top of a hill, and they got ready to fight.
translation_verse: Ka Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba daa ti laɣim zaŋ bɛ noya naai Abinɛr ka bɛ min’ o leei zaɣ’ yini n-du zoli maa zuɣu ti zani.

english_verse: Abner shouted to Joab, “Aren't we ever going to stop killing each other? Don't you know that the longer we keep on doing this, the worse it's going to be when it's all over? When are you going to order your men to stop chasing their own relatives?”
translation_verse: Ka Abinɛr daa ti kuhi bahi Jɔab ha bɔh’ o, “Ti kul yɛn zaŋla takɔbiri ŋɔ n-kuri tab’ hal ni saha din ka bahigu? A bi mi ni di bahigu ti yɛn nyɛla dimdi din ku naai? Bɔ saha ka a yɛn yɛl’ a niriba maa ka bɛ chɛ bɛ mabihi ŋɔ kari doli?”

english_verse: Joab shouted back, “I swear by the living God, if you hadn't spoken, my men would have chased their relatives all night!”
translation_verse: Ka Jɔab daa yɛli, “Hal ka Naawuni ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu, a yi di bi yɛli shɛli, biɛhiŋ kani, n niriba ŋɔ naan kari doli bɛ mabihi maa hal ni biɛɣuni asiba.”

english_verse: Joab took his trumpet and blew the signal for his soldiers to stop chasing the soldiers of Israel. At once, the fighting stopped.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Jɔab daa piɛbi kikaa, ka niriba maa kpalim zani ka bi lan kariti doli Izraɛlnim’ maa bee n-lan tuhiri ba.

english_verse: Abner and his troops marched through the Jordan River valley all that night. Then they crossed the river and marched all morning until they arrived back at Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Ka Abinɛr min’ o niriba maa daa chaŋ yuŋ maa zaa n-gari Araba ti gbaai Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili du, zaŋ chaŋ wuntaŋ’ daa ti yɛn zani zuɣu ni ka bɛ paai Mahanaim.

english_verse: As soon as Joab stopped chasing Abner, he got David's troops together and counted them. There were
translation_verse: Ka Jɔab daa yi Abinɛr karibu maa yɔɣu labina nti laɣim Dauda tɔbbihi maa zali ka bɛ ni ninvuɣ’ pisiyinika daa kani m-pahi Asahɛl zuɣu.

english_verse: Joab and his troops carried Asahel's body to Bethlehem and buried him in the family burial place. Then they marched all night and reached Hebron before sunrise.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa zaŋ Asahɛl chaŋ Bɛtilihɛm ti sɔɣ’ o o ba siliga din daa be nimaani la puuni. Ka Jɔab min’ o niriba maa daa ŋmaligi doli tab’ yuŋ labi, zaŋ chaŋ biɛɣu daa ti yɛn neei, ka bɛ paai Hiburɔn.

english_verse: As the war went on between the families of David and Saul, Abner was gaining more power than ever in Saul's family.
translation_verse: Tɔb’ daa yi ti lu Naa Sool niriba mini Dauda niriba sunsuuni saha shɛlikam, di saha Abinɛr nyarila yaa Sool niriba maa sani.

english_verse: He had even slept with a wife of Saul by the name of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah. But Saul's son Ishbosheth told Abner, “You shouldn't have slept with one of my father's wives!”
translation_verse: Sool mam daa beni ka o yuli booni Rizipa. O daa nyɛla Aiya bipuɣiŋga, ka Ishibɔshɛt daa ti bɔhi Abinɛr, “Bɔ n-niŋ ka a zaŋ m ba mam maa dɔni?”

english_verse: Abner was very angry because of what Ishbosheth had said, and he told Ishbosheth: Am I some kind of worthless dog from Judah? I've always been loyal to your father's family and to his relatives and friends. I haven't turned you over to David. And yet you talk to me as if I've committed a crime with this woman.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Abinɛr suhu daa yiɣisi pam Ishibɔshɛt yɛtɔɣa maa zuɣu, ka o daa bɔh’ o, “Judanim’ baa n-nyɛ ma? N kul ʒiɛla a ba Sool min’ o mabihi ni o zɔnim’ zaa yim hal ni zuŋɔ, ka bi saɣi zaŋ a niŋ Dauda nuu ni, di zaa yoli ka a ti zaŋ ma taali paɣ’ zuɣu!”

english_verse: I ask God to punish me if I don't help David get what the Lord promised him!
translation_verse: O daa lan yɛli, “N yi bi chɛ ka Naawuni ni daa lo Dauda alikauli yɛli

english_verse: God said that he wouldn't let anyone in Saul's family ever be king again and that David would be king instead. He also said that David would rule both Israel and Judah, all the way from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south.
translation_verse: ni o ni yihi Sool nam ni ka zaŋ ŋun’ Dauda ʒili nam gbandi maa zuɣu, ka o su Judanim’ mini Izraɛlnim’ zaa, zaŋ Dan hal ti kpa Bɛrishiiba la niŋ pali, Naawuni ŋun darigim n tibili, hal ŋun darigim n tibili pam gba.”

english_verse: Ishbosheth was so afraid of Abner that he could not even answer.
translation_verse: Ka Ishibɔshɛt daa kɔŋ o ni yɛn yɛli Abinɛr shɛm, dama o daa zɔr’ o mi.

english_verse: Abner sent some of his men to David with this message: “You should be the ruler of the whole nation. If you make an agreement with me, I will persuade everyone in Israel to make you their king.”
translation_verse: Ka Abinɛr daa tim tuumba Dauda sani Hiburɔn ni bɛ ti yɛl’ o, “Ŋuni n-lee lan su tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ? Chɛ ka m min’ a lo tab’ alikauli, ka n sɔŋ a n-zaŋ Izraɛlnim’ zaa na ti ti a.”

english_verse: David sent this message back: “Good! I'll make an agreement with you. But before I will even talk with you about it, you must get Saul's daughter Michal back for me.”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yɛli, “Di viɛla, n ni lo a alikauli; amaa bin’ yini ka n naɣ’ bɔri ni a niŋ, dina n-nyɛ: a yi ti yɛn kana ti nya ma nyin’ zaŋm’ Mikal Sool bipuɣiŋga la mali na, di yi pa lala a yi ti kana a ku nya n ninni.”

english_verse: David sent a few of his officials to Ishbosheth to give him this message: “Give me back my wife Michal! I killed
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda daa lan tim tuumba Sool bia Ishibɔshɛt sani ti yɛl’ o, “Zaŋmi m paɣ’ Mikal ŋun nyɛ n ni daa zaŋ Filistianim’ yokol’ gbana kɔbiga yo so zuɣu la ti ma na.”

english_verse: Ishbosheth sent some of his men to take Michal away from her new husband, Paltiel the son of Laish.
translation_verse: Ka Ishibɔshɛt daa tim ti deeg’ o o yidan’ Palitiɛl ŋun daa nyɛ Laishi bia la sanna.

english_verse: Paltiel followed Michal and the men all the way to Bahurim, crying as he walked. But he went back home after Abner ordered him to leave.
translation_verse: Amaa ka o yidan’ maa daa dol’ o kuhiri hal ni Bahurim. Ka Abinɛr daa ti yɛl’ o, “Ŋmaligi lab’ kuli,” ka o daa lab’ kuli.

english_verse: Abner talked with the leaders of the tribes of Israel and told them, “You've wanted to make David your king for a long time now.
translation_verse: Ka Abinɛr daa laɣim Izraɛl kpamba na ti yɛli ba, “Saha shɛli din gari la puuni, yi daa kul bɔri ni Naa Dauda n-leei yi naa.

english_verse: So do it! After all, God said he would use his servant David to rescue his people Israel from their enemies, especially from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ, chɛliya ka lala niŋ; dama Yawɛ daa lo Naa Dauda alikauli yɛli, ‘N dabili Dauda nuu ka n ti yɛn zaŋ fa n niriba Izraɛlnim’ Filistianim’ mini bɛ dimnim’ zaa nuu ni bahi.’ ”

english_verse: Finally, Abner talked with the tribe of Benjamin. Then he left for Hebron to tell David everything that the tribe of Benjamin and the rest of the people of Israel wanted to do.
translation_verse: Ka Abinɛr daa lan yɛli Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba gba di yɛla, di nyaaŋa ka o daa chaŋ Dauda sani Hiburɔn ni o ti yɛl’ o Izraɛlnim’ mini Bɛnjamin zuliya niriba ni lo ni bɛ niŋ zaɣ’ viɛl’ shɛli zaa yɛla.

english_verse: After the feast, Abner said, “Your Majesty, let me leave now and bring Israel here to make an agreement with you. You'll be king of the whole nation, just as you've been wanting.” David told Abner he could leave, and he left without causing any trouble. Joab Kills Abner
translation_verse: Ka Abinɛr daa yɛli Dauda, “N ni yiɣisi chaŋ ti laɣim Izraɛlnim’ zaa n-ka n dan’ naa sanna ka bɛ ti lo a alikauli, ka di chɛ ka a su a suhu ni bɔri shɛb’ zaa.” Di saha ka Dauda daa chɛbisi Abinɛr ka o kuli ni suhudoo. Bɛ ku Abinɛr

english_verse: Soon after Abner had left Hebron, Joab and some of David's soldiers came back, bringing a lot of things they had taken from an enemy village.
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Dauda tɔbbihi mini Jɔab daa yi ŋmɛnditoli yɔɣu paana ni nɛma pam. Amaa di saha maa Abinɛr daa lan ka Dauda sani Hiburɔn. Dauda daa pun chɛbis’ o mi ka o chaŋ ni suhudoo.

english_verse: Right after they arrived, someone told Joab, “Abner visited the king, and the king let him go. Abner even left without causing any trouble.”
translation_verse: Jɔab mini tɔbbi’ shɛb’ bɛn zaa daa be o sani maa ni daa kuna ka bɛ daa yɛl’ o, “Nɛr bia Abinɛr la kala naa sanna ka o bah’ o ka o chaŋ ni suhudoo.”

english_verse: Joab went to David and said, “What have you done? Abner came to you, and you let him go. Now he's long gone!
translation_verse: Di saha ka Jɔab daa chaŋ naa sani ti bɔh’ o, “Bɔ n-niŋ ka a niŋ lala? Nyama, Abinɛr kala a sanna, ka bɔ niŋ ka a bah’ o ka o chaŋ?

english_verse: You know Abner—he came to trick you. He wants to find out how strong your army is and to know everything you're doing.”
translation_verse: A mi ni Nɛr bia Abinɛr maa kamina ni o ti yɔhim’ a baŋ a ni doli so’ shɛli yiri min’ a ni doli so’ shɛli kpɛra; ka lan baŋ a ni niŋdi shɛlikam zaa.”

english_verse: Joab left David, then he sent some messengers to catch up with Abner. They brought him back from the well at Sirah, but David did not know anything about it.
translation_verse: Ka Jɔab daa ŋmaligi Dauda sani yi nti tim ni bɛ cham’ ti gɔŋ Abinɛr labisina. Ka bɛ daa chaŋ ti paag’ o Sira kɔbiliga gbini n-gɔŋ o labisina, amaa Dauda daa bi mi di yɛla.

english_verse: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab pretended he wanted to talk privately with him. So he took Abner into one of the small rooms that were part of the town gate and stabbed him in the stomach. Joab killed him because Abner had killed Joab's brother Asahel. Abner's Funeral

translation_verse: di saha ka naa daa yɛli anab’ Neetan, “Nyama, m bela sida dari yil’ ni, amaa ka Naawuni Daalikauli Adaka ŋɔ dim be suɣili ni.”

english_verse: Nathan replied, “The Lord is with you, so do what you want!”
translation_verse: Ka Neetan daa yɛli naa, “Cham’ ti niŋ a ni lo a suhu ni ni a niŋ shɛm, Yawɛ ʒe a nyaaŋa.”

english_verse: That night, the Lord told Nathan
translation_verse: Amaa dindali maa yuŋ ka Yawɛ daa yɛli Neetan,

english_verse: to go to David and give him this message: David, you are my servant, so listen to what I say. Why should you build a temple for me?
translation_verse: “Cham’ ti yɛli n dabili Dauda ni man’ Yawɛ bɔhir’ o, ‘A yɛn mɛla duu ti ma ka m be di ni?’

english_verse: I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them.
translation_verse: Saha shɛli n ni daa yihi Izraɛlnim’ Ijipti tiŋgbɔŋ ni na la hal ni zuŋɔ n na ʒi m be duu, amaa suɣili ni ka n kul be ka yi mali ma ginda.

english_verse: I chose leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
translation_verse: Luɣ’ shɛlikam zaa m mini n niriba Izraɛlnim’ maa ni daa chaŋ, n daa na mi m-bɔhi sariakaritib’ shɛb’ n ni daa pii zali ni bɛ su n niriba Izraɛlnim’ la, ‘Bɔ n-niŋ ka yi bi zaŋ sida dari me duu ti ma?’ ”

english_verse: David, this is what I, the Lord All-Powerful, say to you. I brought you in from the fields where you took care of sheep, and I made you the leader of my people.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ yɛlimi n dabili Dauda ni man’ Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ tɔbbihi zaa naa ŋɔ yɛliya, “Mani n-daa yih’ a mɔɣu ni piɛgulibo ni na ni a ti leegi n niriba Izraɛlnim’ toondana n-su ba.

english_verse: Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
translation_verse: Ka a daa yi kul chani luɣ’ shɛlikam, m bela a sani, ka nyaŋ a dimnim’ zaa ti a, ka duh’ a yuli kaman dunia ŋɔ ninvuɣ’ kara yuya ni du shɛm.

english_verse: I have given my people Israel a land of their own where they can live in peace, and they won't have to tremble with fear any more. Evil nations won't bother them, as they did
translation_verse: N ni bo biɛhigu shee ti n niriba Izraɛlnima, ka zaŋ ba ʒili nimaani ka bɛ be bɛ dahalali tiŋgbɔŋ ni ka so ku lan dam ba yaha; ka ninvuɣ’ galima ku lan nahim ba kaman bɛ ni daa yi niŋdi ba shɛm

english_verse: when I let judges rule my people. And I have kept your enemies from attacking you. Now I promise that you and your descendants will be kings.
translation_verse: saha shɛli n ni daa pii zuɣulaannim’ zali ka bɛ su n niriba Izraɛlnim’ maa la. N ni chɛ ka a nya nyee vuhi a dimnim’ zaa sani. M-pahi, man’ Yawɛ lan yɛl’ a ni n ni me yili ti a,

english_verse: I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried in the tomb of your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler,
translation_verse: ka a dabisa yi ti pali ka a dɔni a yaannim’ tooni, n ni piig’ a bihi ni yino ŋun nyɛ a dahalali bia n-chɛ ka o nam nya zaashee zani.

english_verse: and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: Ŋuna n-ni ti me yili ti n yuli jilima, ka n ti chɛ ka o nam zani hal ni saha din ka bahigu.

english_verse: I will be his father, and he will be my son. When he does wrong, I'll see that he is corrected, just as children are corrected by their parents.
translation_verse: Mani n-ni ti nyɛ o ba ka o mi nyɛ m bia, ka o yi ti tum taali, n ni zaŋ fiɛbiga fiɛb’ o n-saɣis’ o kaman ninsalinim’ ni saɣisiri bɛ bihi shɛm.

english_verse: After all, you really are Israel's God, the Lord All-Powerful. You've told me that you will let my descendants be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
translation_verse: Dama nyini Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Tɔbbihi Naa, ka nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni ŋɔ n-kahigi dimbɔŋɔ wuhi mani a dabili ŋɔ ka yɛli, ‘N ni me a yili ti a,’ dinzuɣu ka mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ mali suhukpeeni n-suhir’ a suhigu ŋɔ.

english_verse: David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. Then he sat there and prayed: Lord All-Powerful, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us,
translation_verse: Di saha ka Naa Dauda daa kpe nti ʒini Yawɛ tooni ka yɛli, “Yaa n Duuma NAAWUNI, m mi lee nyɛ ŋuni, ka n daŋ lee nyɛ dini, ka a ti zaŋ ma zali zaashee ŋɔ tatabo ni?

english_verse: I am your servant, and you know my thoughts, so there is nothing more that I need to say.
translation_verse: Yaa n Duuma NAAWUNI, bɔ yɛla ka man’ Dauda lee lan yɛn yɛl’ a yaha? Dama a mi man’ a dabili Dauda.

english_verse: You have done this wonderful thing, and you have let me know about it, because you wanted to keep your promise.
translation_verse: A daalikauli min’ a suhu yubu zuɣu, ka a tum tuun’ kara ŋɔ zaa ni a chɛ ka man’ ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ baŋ li.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are greater than all others. No one is like you, and you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu, Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Naawuni ŋɔ, nyini n-nyɛ ŋun galisi, dama so kani m-be ka nyini, ka Naawuni so mi lan kani m-pah’ a zuɣu kaman ti ni wum shɛm ti tiba ni.

english_verse: And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so your people could live here.
translation_verse: Zuliya shɛli lan be dunia ŋɔ ni ŋ-ŋman’ a niriba Izraɛlnima? Bee nyin’ Naawuni na mi n-tiligi zuliya shɛba n-zaŋ ba leeg’ a dahalali niriba, ka tum tuun’ kara din mali dabiɛm bɛ sani? Bee n-kari zuliya shɛb’ mini bɛ buɣa zaa kpɛhi yɔɣu ka chɛ a niriba maa ni di chɛ ka a yuli du?

english_verse: You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
translation_verse: Yawɛ, nyini n-daa zaŋ a niriba Izraɛlnim’ leeg’ a dahalali niriba ʒiɛmani kam ni, ka leei bɛ Naawuni.

english_verse: Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord God All-Powerful rules Israel, and David's descendants are his chosen kings.”
translation_verse: din ni chɛ ka bɛ tibig’ a yuli ʒiɛmani kam ni ka yɛra, ‘Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Tɔbbihi Naa ŋɔ n-nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni,’ ka a chɛ ka mani a dabili Dauda zuliya nya zaashee zani a tooni.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are God. You have promised me some very good things, and you can be trusted to do what you promise.
translation_verse: “Ka pumpɔŋɔ, yaa n Duuma NAAWUNI, nyini n-nyɛ Naawuni, ka a yɛligu nyɛ yɛlimaŋli, ka a lo a dabili bin’ suŋ ŋɔ.

english_verse: Please bless my descendants and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already promised, and I'm sure that you will bless my family forever.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ n suhir’ a ni a niŋ alibarika niŋ man’ a dabili ŋɔ daŋ ni din ni chɛ ka n daŋ kul ʒiɛya ʒiɛmani kam ni nyin’ Naawuni sani; dama nyini Yawɛ n-daa yɛli lala, ka a daalibarika kul ni be man’ a dabili ŋɔ daŋ ni ʒiɛmani kam ni.”

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard. David's sons were priests.
translation_verse: Ka Jɛhɔiada bia Bɛnaaya su tɔbbi’ shɛb’ bɛ ni daa booni Chɛrɛtinim’ mini Pɛlɛtinim’ la fukumsi. Ka Dauda bidibisi gba daa nyɛ maligumaaniba.

english_verse: David also defeated the Moabites. Then he made their soldiers lie down on the ground, and he measured them off with a rope. He would measure off two lengths of the rope and have those men killed, then he would measure off one length and let those men live. The people of Moab had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
translation_verse: Ka o daa lan chaŋ ti tuhi nyaŋ Mɔabnima, ka chɛ ka bɛ dɔni tiŋa m-pie taba ʒii buta zuɣu, ka o chɛ ka bɛ ku ʒii buyi zuɣu niriba zaa ka chɛ yim zuɣu niriba. Ka Mɔabnim’ maa daa leei Dauda daba, ka yɔri farigu o sani.

english_verse: David set out for the Euphrates River to build a monument there. On his way, he defeated the king of Zobah, whose name was Hadadezer the son of Rehob.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa lan chaŋ ti tuhi nyaŋ Hadadɛza ŋun daa nyɛ Rɛhɔb bia ka nyɛ Zɔba naa la, saha shɛli ŋun Hadadɛza ni daa chaŋ ni o ti tuhi deei Yufretiiz Mɔɣili polo la.

english_verse: He left some of his soldiers in Damascus, and the Arameans had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him. Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda daa tahi tɔbbihi ti ʒili Damaskus ka Sirianim’ maa daa leei Dauda ni su shɛba, ka bɛ yɔri farigu o sani. Ka Yawɛ daa chɛ ka Dauda kul diri nasara o ni chaŋ luɣ’ shɛlikam.

english_verse: Hadadezer's officers had carried their arrows in gold cases hung over their shoulders, but David took these cases and brought them to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa fa Hadadɛza sapashin’ kpamba ni daa mali salima nyɔtaɣiri’ shɛŋa n-zaŋ li kuli Jɛrusalɛm.

english_verse: He also took a lot of bronze from the cities of Betah and Berothai, which had belonged to Hadadezer.
translation_verse: Ka Naa Dauda daa lan kpuɣi daanya pam Bɛta mini Bɛrɔtai din daa nyɛ Hadadɛza ni su fɔntin’ shɛŋa la ni.

english_verse: King Toi of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Toi heard that David had attacked and defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Joram to praise and congratulate David. Joram also brought him gifts made of silver, gold, and bronze.
translation_verse: ka o daa tim o bia Jɔram ni o cham’ ti puhi Naa Dauda ni o zuɣusuŋ, o ni daa tuhi nyaŋ Hadadɛza ka di nasara maa zuɣu. Dama ŋun’ Tɔi mini Hadadɛza daa kul tuhirila tab’ waawaayili. Ka Jɔram daa zaŋ pina din nyɛ salima mini anzinfa ni daanya n-chaŋ ti ti Naa Dauda.

english_verse: David gave these to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold that he had captured from
translation_verse: Ka Naa Dauda daa zaŋ o ni daa tuhi nyaŋ zuliya shɛb’ zaa ka va anzinfa mini salim’ shɛŋa la pahi di zuɣu ti Yawɛ.

english_verse: Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Abiathar the son of Ahimelech, were the priests. Seraiah was the secretary.
translation_verse: Ka Ahitub bia Zadok mini Abiata bia Ahimɛlɛk nyɛ maligumaaniba, ka Sɛraya nyɛ gbansabira.

english_verse: Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
translation_verse: Ka Zɛruya bia Jɔab la daa su tɔbbihi fukumsi ka Jɛhɔshafat Ahilud bia la nyɛ gbansabira wulana.

english_verse: One day, David thought, “I wonder if any of Saul's family are still alive. If they are, I will be kind to them, because I made a promise to Jonathan.”
translation_verse: Dahin shɛli ka Dauda daa ti bɔhi, “Sool daŋ ni ninvuɣ’ so na beni ka n ni niŋ o nirilim Jɔnatan zuɣu?”

english_verse: David called in Ziba, one of the servants of Saul's family. David said, “So you are Ziba.” “Yes, Your Majesty, I am.”
translation_verse: Ka ninvuɣ’ so ŋun daa nyɛ Sool tumtumda ka o yuli booni Ziba la daa be nimaani, ka bɛ daa bol’ o ti Naa Dauda ka o ti bɔh’ o, “Nyini n-nyɛ Ziba?” Ka o garigi yɛli’, “Naa, mani.”

english_verse: David asked, “Are any of Saul's family still alive? If there are, I want to be kind to them.” Ziba answered, “One of Jonathan's sons is still alive, but he can't walk.”
translation_verse: Ka naa daa bɔh’ o “So na be Sool daŋ ni ka n ni niŋ o nirilim kaman Naawuni ni bɔri shɛm?” Ka Ziba daa yɛli naa, “Jɔnatan bidibiga na beni, o mi nyɛla gbarigu.”

english_verse: “Where is he?” David asked. Ziba replied, “He lives in Lo-Debar with Machir the son of Ammiel.”
translation_verse: Ka naa bɔh’ o, “O be ya?” Ka Ziba daa yɛli naa, “O be Ammiɛl bia Makiri la yiŋa Lɔdɛba.”

english_verse: David sent some servants to bring Jonathan's son from Lo-Debar. His name was Mephibosheth, and he was the grandson of Saul. He came to David and knelt down. David asked, “Are you Mephibosheth?” “Yes, I am, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Ka Sool yaaŋa Mɛfibɔshɛt ŋun daa nyɛ Jɔnatan bia maa daa ka Naa Dauda sanna nti lu n-gbani Dauda tooni lu o sizuura. Ka Dauda bol’ o, “Mɛfibɔshɛt.” Ka o garigi yɛli, “N-nyɛ mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili maa.”

english_verse: David said, “Don't be afraid. I'll be kind to you because Jonathan was your father. I'm going to give you back the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul. Besides that, you will always eat with me at my table.”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yɛl’ o, “Di zɔri dabiɛm, dama n ni niŋ a nirilim a ba Jɔnatan zuɣu, ka zaŋ a yab’ Sool ni daa su tiŋgban’ shɛli zaa ti a, ka lan chɛ ka m min’ a laɣindi ʒiini diri sahakam.”

english_verse: Mephibosheth knelt down again and said, “Why should you care about me? I'm worth no more than a dead dog.”
translation_verse: Ka o daa lan lu Dauda sizuura ka yɛli, “Ka mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ mi lee nyɛ ŋuni, ka a ti lihi nya mani ŋun nyɛ ba’ kpiŋ ŋɔ lala.”

english_verse: David called in Ziba, Saul's chief servant, and told him, “Since Mephibosheth is Saul's grandson, I've given him back everything that belonged to your master Saul and his family.
translation_verse: Di saha ka naa daa boli Ziba ŋun daa nyɛ Sool tumtumda la na ti yɛl’ o, “Sool min’ o daŋ zaa ni daa su shɛlikam zaa n ni zaŋ li ti a dan’ yaaŋa ŋɔ.

english_verse: When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had beaten them, they made peace with Israel and accepted David as their ruler. The Arameans were afraid to help Ammon any more.
translation_verse: Ka na’ shɛb’ zaa bɛn daa be Hadadɛza sulinsi ni nya Izraɛlnim’ ni tuhi nyaŋ ba maa, ka bɛ daa kana ti tim sandaani niŋ Izraɛlnim’ maa ka zaŋ bɛmaŋ’ ti ba. Di saha zaŋ chana ka Sirianim’ maa daa zɔri dabiɛm ni bɛ lan sɔŋ Ammɔnnim’ yaha.

english_verse: David said, “Nahash was kind to me, and I will be kind to his son.” So he sent some officials to the country of Ammon to tell Hanun how sorry he was that his father had died.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yɛli, “N ni be Hanun Nahash bia ŋɔ yɛlimaŋli biɛhigu kaman o ba ni daa be ma yɛlimaŋli biɛhigu shɛm la.” Dinzuɣu ka o daa tim tuumba ni bɛ chaŋ ti sɔɣi Nahash kuli maa ti o. Ka Dauda tuumba maa daa ti paai Ammɔnnim’ maa tiŋgbɔŋ ni,

english_verse: But Hanun's officials told him, “Do you really believe David is honoring your father by sending these people to comfort you? He probably sent them to spy on our city, so he can destroy it.”
translation_verse: amaa ka Ammɔn nabihi daa yɛli bɛ dan’ Hanun, “A tɛhiya ni Dauda ni tim tuumba na ka bɛ ti sɔɣi kuli maa wuhiri ni yɛlimaŋli biɛhigu ka o be a maa? Dauda timla niriba ŋɔ na ni bɛ ti vihi baŋ yaŋɔ daashili zaa ka tuhi nyaŋ ti.”

english_verse: Hanun arrested David's officials and had their beards shaved off on one side of their faces. He had their robes cut off just below the waist, and then he sent them away.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Hanun daa chɛ ka bɛ gbahi Dauda tuumba maa m-pini bɛ zaa teensi pirigilipirigili bahi ka chɛ pirigilipirigili, ka daa lan ŋmahi bɛ binyɛra bɛ sakpuɣa zuɣu bahi ka chɛ ka bɛ chaŋ.

english_verse: They were terribly ashamed. When David found out what had happened to his officials, he sent a message and told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then you can come home.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yɛli Dauda, ka o tim ni bɛ ti tuhi ba soli, dama vi daa mali tuumba maa pam. Ka naa daa yɛli ba, “Kpalimmiya be Jɛriko hal ka yi teensi maa ti bili, ka yi naanyi kuna.”

english_verse: The Ammonites realized that they had made David very angry, so they hired more foreign soldiers. Twenty thousand of them were foot soldiers from the Aramean cities of Beth-Rehob and Zobah,
translation_verse: Ammɔnnim’ ni daa baŋ ni bɛ leei Dauda dimnim’ maa, ka bɛ daa chaŋ Sirianim’ tinsi ni Bɛtirɛhɔb mini Zɔba nti da Sirianim’ tɔbbi’ shɛb’ bɛn’ nyɛ tinchandiba tuhi’ pisi, ka Maaka naa daa yina ni tɔbbihi tuhili, ka Tɔbinim’ gba daa yina ni tɔbbihi tuhi’ pinaayi.

english_verse: Be brave and fight hard to protect our people and the cities of our God. I pray that the Lord will do whatever pleases him.”
translation_verse: Maliya suhukpeeni ka ti zabi ti niriba mini ti Naawuni tinsi ŋɔ zuɣu, ka chɛ ka ŋun’ Yawɛ niŋ o ni nya ka shɛli viɛl’ o sani.”

english_verse: David heard what they had done, and he sent out Joab with all of his well-trained soldiers.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa wum lala ka chɛ ka Jɔab zaŋ o tɔbbi’ kpɛma zaa chaŋ bɛ tuhibu.

english_verse: The Ammonite troops came out and got ready to fight in front of the gate to their city. The Arameans from Zobah and Rehob and the soldiers from Tob and Maacah formed a separate group in the nearby fields.
translation_verse: Ka Ammɔnnim’ maa daa yina nti teei zani tiŋ’ maa dunol’ ni, ka Siria tɔbbihi bɛn daa yi Zɔba mini Rɛhɔb ni Tɔb ni Maaka na la mi laɣim ʒe mɔɣu ni mɔɣu ni.

english_verse: Joab saw that he had to fight in front and behind at the same time, and he picked some of the best Israelite soldiers to fight the Arameans.
translation_verse: Jɔab ni daa nya ka tɔb’ maa be n-gil’ o tooni ni o nyaaŋa zaa maa, ka o pii Izraɛl tɔbutuhiri’ biinsi ni bɛ chaŋ ti tuhi Sirianim’ maa.

english_verse: He put his brother Abishai in command of the rest of the army and gave them orders to fight the Ammonites.
translation_verse: Ka o daa zaŋ tɔbbi’ shɛb’ bɛn kpalim maa niŋ o mabia Abishai nuu ni ni bɛ chaŋ ti tuhi Ammɔnnim’ maa.

english_verse: Joab told his brother, “If the Arameans are too much for me to handle, you can come and help me. If the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come and help you.
translation_verse: Ka o daa yɛli ba, “Yi yi ti nya ka Sirianim’ maa yɛn nyaŋ ma, yin’ zomiya n kuŋa, ka m mi yi ti nya ka Ammɔnnim’ maa yɛn nyaŋ ya, n ni zo yi kuŋa.

english_verse: Joab and his soldiers attacked the Arameans, and the Arameans ran from them.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Jɔab mini ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn daa be o sani daa vu m-miri ni bɛ ti tuhi Sirianim’ maa, ka bɛ daa ŋmaligi guui.

english_verse: When the Ammonite soldiers saw that the Arameans had run away, they ran from Abishai's soldiers and went back into their own city. Joab stopped fighting the Ammonites and returned to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ammɔnnim’ ni daa nya ka Sirianim’ maa ŋmaligi guui maa, ka bɛ gba daa ŋmaligi Abishai tooni guui ti kpe bɛ tiŋ’ maa puuni. Di saha ka Jɔab daa yi Ammɔnnim’ maa tuhibu yɔɣu n-lab’ Jɛrusalɛm.

english_verse: The Arameans realized they had lost the battle, so they brought all their troops together again.
translation_verse: Amaa Sirianim’ maa ni daa nya ka Izraɛlnim’ tuhi nyaŋ ba maa, ka bɛ laɣim taba.

english_verse: Hadadezer sent messengers to call in the Arameans who were on the other side of the Euphrates River. Then Shobach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led them to the town of Helam.
translation_verse: Ka Hadadɛza daa tim ti zaŋ Sirianim’ bɛn be Yufretiiz Mɔɣili dul’ la n-ka Hɛlam na, ka Shɔbak ŋun daa nyɛ Hadadɛza kamɔna’ kpɛm’ la leei bɛ zuɣulana.

english_verse: David found out what the Arameans were doing, and he brought Israel's whole army together. They crossed the Jordan River and went to Helam, where the Arameans were ready to meet them.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yɛli Dauda di yɛla, ka o laɣim Izraɛlnim’ zaa ka bɛ chaŋ ti gbaai Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili du n-ka Hɛlam na. Ka Sirianim’ maa daa niŋ shili yina ti liri Dauda ka bɛ min’ o zaŋ nya taba.

english_verse: It was now spring, the time when kings go to war. David sent out the whole Israelite army under the command of Joab and his officers. They destroyed the Ammonite army and surrounded the capital city of Rabbah, but David stayed in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ka siɣili saha din nyɛ nanim’ ni daa yi tuhiri tɔbu saha shɛli la daa ti paai, ka Dauda daa tim Jɔab mini sapashin’ kpamba ni Izraɛl tɔbbihi zaa ka bɛ chaŋ ti tuhi nyaŋ Ammɔnnima, ka chaŋ ti teei gili Raba. Amaa ka Dauda ŋun’ daa kpalim be Jɛrusalɛm.

english_verse: he may get angry and ask, “Why did you go so near the city to fight? Didn't you know they would shoot arrows from the wall?
translation_verse: ka o suhu yiɣisi ka o bɔh’ a, ‘Bɔ n-niŋ ka yi chaŋ miri tiŋ’ maa ni yi ti tuhi ba? Yi bi mi ni bɛ ni tɔn ya piɛma goma zuɣu na?

english_verse: But later, when she found out that she was going to have a baby, she sent someone to David with this message: “I'm pregnant!”
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ maa daa niŋ pua, ka tim na ti yɛli Dauda ni o malila pua.

english_verse: David sent a message to Joab: “Send Uriah the Hittite to me.” Joab sent Uriah
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda daa tim ti yɛli Jɔab, “Chɛ ka Yuria ŋun nyɛ Hiti nir’ la kuna.” Ka Jɔab daa chɛ ka Yuria kuli Dauda sani.

english_verse: to David's palace, and David asked him, “Is Joab well? How is the army doing? And how about the war?”
translation_verse: Yuria ni daa ka Dauda sanna, ka o ti puh’ o bɔhi Jɔab mini tɔbbihi maa zaa yɛla ni tɔb’ maa ni chani shɛm.

english_verse: Then David told Uriah, “Go home and clean up.” Uriah left the king's palace, and David had dinner sent to Uriah's house.
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Dauda yɛli Yuria, “Kulimi yiŋ’ ti paɣ’ a naba.” Ka Yuria daa yiɣisi nayili maa yi, ka naa daa chɛ ka bɛ zaŋ pini dol’ o nyaaŋa ni bɛ ti ti o.

english_verse: But Uriah didn't go home. Instead, he slept outside the entrance to the royal palace, where the king's guards slept.
translation_verse: Amaa Yuria daa bi kul’ o yiŋa, ka daa yi nti dɔnila nayili samban’ dunol’ ni tɔbbi’ shɛb’ bɛn daa guli nayili maa sani.

english_verse: Someone told David that Uriah had not gone home. So the next morning David asked him, “Why didn't you go home? Haven't you been away for a long time?”
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa yɛli Dauda, “Yuria bi kul’ o yiŋa.” Ka Dauda daa bɔhi Yuria, “Pa gɔrim yɔɣu ka a yina maa? Ka bɔ n-niŋ ka a bi kuli yiŋa?”

english_verse: Uriah answered, “The sacred chest and the armies of Israel and Judah are camping out somewhere in the fields with our commander Joab and his officers and troops. Do you really think I would go home to eat and drink and sleep with my wife? I swear by your life that I would not!”
translation_verse: Ka Yuria daa garigi yɛli Dauda, “Alikauli Adaka la mini Izraɛlnim’ ni Judanim’ zaa bela tɔb’ tuhibu yɔɣu, ka n dan’ Jɔab mini n dan’ naa sapashinnim’ zaa do mɔɣu ni, ka man’ ti yɛn kuli yiŋa nti di ka nyu ka m mini m paɣ’ doya? Hal ka nyin’ naa ŋun be ŋɔ min’ a shia din be ŋɔ zuɣu, n kul ku niŋ lala.”

english_verse: Then David said, “Stay here in Jerusalem today, and I will send you back tomorrow.” Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day. Then the next day,
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda daa yɛl’ o, “Kpalimmi kpe zuŋɔ yaha, ka n sa bah’ a ka a lab’ biɛɣuni.” Ka Yuria daa kpalim Jɛrusalɛm dindali maa neei biɛɣu.

english_verse: David invited him for dinner. Uriah ate with David, who gave him so much to drink that he got drunk. But Uriah still did not go home. He went out and slept on his mat near the palace guards.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa bol’ o na ka o min’ o ti di ka nyu, ka Dauda daa chɛ ka o nyu dam kuli, ka di daa ti niŋ yuŋ ka o yi samban’ ni nayili guliba maa sani nti dɔni o bindoo zuɣu, ka daa bi kul’ o yiŋa.

english_verse: Early the next morning, David wrote a letter and told Uriah to deliver it to Joab.
translation_verse: Ka biɛɣ’ daa neei asiba ka Dauda sabi gbaŋ ti o ni o zaŋ mali chaŋ ti ti Jɔab.

english_verse: The letter said: “Put Uriah on the front line where the fighting is the worst. Then pull the troops back from him, so that he will be wounded and die.”
translation_verse: O daa sabila gbaŋ maa yɛli Jɔab, “Zaŋmi Yuria zali tooni tɔb’ maa ni mali kpiɔŋ luɣ’ shɛli polo, ka miligi ka chɛ o ka bɛ ku o.”

english_verse: Joab had been carefully watching the city of Rabbah, and he put Uriah in a place where he knew there were some of the enemy's best soldiers.
translation_verse: Jɔab ni daa chɛ ka bɛ teei gili tiŋ’ maa, ka o zaŋ Yuria zali o ni mi ni tɔbutuhiri’ biinsi be shɛli polo,

english_verse: When the men of the city came out, they fought and killed some of David's soldiers—Uriah the Hittite was one of them.
translation_verse: Ka tiŋ’ maa nim’ daa yina ka bɛ mini Jɔab ti zaŋ nya taba, ka Dauda tɔbbihi maa shɛb’ daa lu nimaani, ka bɛ daa ku Yuria ŋun nyɛ Hiti nir’ la gba nimaani.

english_verse: Joab sent a messenger to tell David everything that was happening in the war.
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Jɔab daa tim ni bɛ kuli ti yɛli Dauda tɔb’ maa lahibali ni nyɛ shɛm.

english_verse: He gave the messenger these orders: When you finish telling the king everything that has happened,
translation_verse: O daa wuhila tumo maa, “A yi kuli ti yɛli naa tɔb’ maa lahibali naai,

english_verse: Don't you know how Abimelech the son of Gideon was killed at Thebez? Didn't a woman kill him by dropping a large rock from the top of the city wall? Why did you go so close to the city walls?” Then tell him, “One of your soldiers who was killed was Uriah the Hittite.”
translation_verse: Ŋuni n-daa lee ku Abimilɛk Jɛrubɛshɛt bia la? Pa nɛkaŋ’ ka paɣ’ daa zani gooni zuɣu ka zaŋ bah’ o zuɣu na ka o kpi tin’ shɛli din yuli booni Tɛbiz la? Ka bɔ n-niŋ ka yi chaŋ miri bɛ gooni maa gbini?’ Di saha nyin’ yɛlim’ o, ‘A dabili Yuria ŋun nyɛ Hiti nir’ la gba kpiya.’ ”

english_verse: The messenger went to David and reported everything Joab had told him.
translation_verse: Ka tumo maa daa chaŋ ti yɛli Dauda Jɔab ni daa yɛl’ o ni o ti yɛli shɛm zaa.

english_verse: He added, “The enemy chased us from the wall and out into the open fields. But we pushed them back as far as the city gate.
translation_verse: Tumo maa daa yɛlila Dauda, “Ti dimnim’ maa daa gari ti la yaa ka yina ni bɛ ti tuhi ti polo ni, amaa ka ti daa lan daai ba labisi bɛ tiŋ’ maa dunɔdal’ ni.”

english_verse: Then they shot arrows at us from the top of the wall. Some of your soldiers were killed, and one of them was Uriah the Hittite.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka peentɔriba daa tam gooni zuɣu ka tɔri ti piɛma na. Bɛ daa ku naa tɔbbihi maa shɛba, hal naa tɔbbia Yuria ŋun nyɛ Hiti nir’ la gba kpiya.

english_verse: David replied, “Tell Joab to cheer up and not to be upset about what happened. You never know who will be killed in a war. Tell him to strengthen his attack against the city and break through its walls.”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yɛli tumo maa, “A ni yɛn chaŋ ti yɛli Jɔab shɛm m-bɔŋɔ kpaŋs’ o suhu, ‘Di chɛ ka yɛlli ŋɔ muɣis’ a, dama takɔb’ bi chihiri so kubu, mali suhukpeeni ka liri tiŋ’ maa nim’ ni nimmoo n-nyaŋ ba.’ ”

english_verse: When Bathsheba heard that her husband was dead, she mourned for him.
translation_verse: Yuria paɣa Batishiiba ni daa wum ni o yidan’ kpiya, o daa kum o zuɣu.

english_verse: Then after the time for mourning was over, David sent someone to bring her to the palace. She became David's wife, and they had a son. The Lord's Message for David The Lord was angry because of what David had done,
translation_verse: O ni daa kum o yidan’ kuli maa naai, ka Dauda daa tim ka bɛ ti zaŋ o kul’ o yiŋ’ na ka o ti zaŋ o leeg’ o paɣa, ka o daa ti dɔɣi bidibiga. Amaa ka Dauda ni daa niŋ shɛm maa daa bi niŋ Yawɛ nyaɣisim.

english_verse: The rich man owned a lot of sheep and cattle,
translation_verse: Bundan’ maa daa mali piɛri mini niɣi pam,

english_verse: One day someone came to visit the rich man, but the rich man didn't want to kill any of his own sheep or cattle and serve it to the visitor. So he stole the poor man's lamb and served it instead.
translation_verse: Ka sana daa ti paai bundana maa, ka o je ni o piig’ o piɛri maa ni bee o niɣi maa yino n-niŋ o saani, amaa ka daa chaŋ ti gbaala faralan’ maa piɛsaa la na nti niŋ o san’ maa saani.”

english_verse: David was furious with the rich man and said to Nathan, “I swear by the living Lord that the man who did this deserves to die!
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda suhu daa yiɣisi pam bahi ninvuɣ’ so ŋun niŋ lala maa zuɣu, ka o yɛli Neetan, “Hal ka Yawɛ ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu, ninvuɣ’ so ŋun niŋ lala maa simdila kubu.

english_verse: And because he didn't have pity on the poor man, he will have to pay four times what the lamb was worth.”
translation_verse: Ka di simdi ka o yo faralan’ maa piɛr’ anahi, o ni tum shɛm maa min’ o ni bi zɔri nambɔɣu la zuɣu.”

english_verse: Then Nathan told David: You are that rich man! Now listen to what the Lord God of Israel says to you: “I chose you to be the king of Israel. I kept you safe from Saul
translation_verse: Ka Neetan daa yɛli Dauda, “Nyini n-nyɛ lala nir’ maa. Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ Naawuni ŋɔ ni yɛli shɛm m-bɔŋɔ: ‘Mani n-daa piig’ a leei Izraɛlnim’ naa, ka daa fa a Sool nuu ni bahi,

english_verse: and even gave you his house and his wives. I let you rule Israel and Judah, and if that had not been enough, I would have given you much more.
translation_verse: ka daa zaŋ a dan’ maa yili ti a, ka zaŋ o paɣiba ti a, ka zaŋ Izraɛl mini Juda ti a pahi. Ka dimbɔŋɔ yi di pɔra, n naan ti a din gari lala pahi.

english_verse: Why did you disobey me and do such a horrible thing? You murdered Uriah the Hittite by letting the Ammonites kill him, so you could take his wife.
translation_verse: Ka bɔ n-niŋ ka a lihi ʒiɛm man’ Yawɛ yɛligu ka tum zaɣ’ biɛɣu ŋɔ man’ Yawɛ ninni? Nyini n-ku Yuria ŋun nyɛ Hiti nir’ la. Nyini n-daa chɛ ka Ammɔnnim’ zaŋ takɔbi ku o, ka a kpuɣ’ o paɣa n-leeg’ a paɣa.

english_verse: “Because you wouldn't obey me and took Uriah's wife for yourself, your family will never live in peace.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ a ni lihi ʒiɛm ma ka kpuɣi Yuria ŋun nyɛ Hiti nir’ la paɣa maa zuɣu, ninvuɣ’ kubo kul ku milig’ a yili ŋɔ.’

english_verse: Someone from your own family will cause you a lot of trouble, and I will take your wives and give them to another man before your very eyes. He will go to bed with them while everyone looks on.
translation_verse: Yawɛ yɛliya, ‘Nyama, n ni chɛ ka zaɣ’ biɛɣu yi a yiŋ’ dundɔŋ ni na n-lu a zuɣu; ka n ti zaŋ a paɣiba ti a ʒiʒiinikpee ka o zaŋ ba dɔni palo ni wuntaŋ’ ni a ninni.

english_verse: What you did was in secret, but I will do this in the open for everyone in Israel to see.”
translation_verse: Dama nyin’ daa niŋ li la ashilɔni, amaa man’ yɛn niŋ li la palɔni wuntaŋ’ ni Izraɛlnim’ zaa ninni.’ ”

english_verse: David said, “I have disobeyed the Lord.” “Yes, you have!” Nathan answered. “You showed you didn't care what the Lord wanted. He has forgiven you, and you won't die. But your newborn son will.”
translation_verse: Amaa di zaa yoli, a ni bi lihi nya Yawɛ ka tum tuun’ shɛli ŋɔ zuɣu, paɣ’ maa ni yɛn dɔɣi bi’ so ti a maa ni kpi.”

english_verse: Then Nathan went back home. David's Young Son Dies The Lord made David's young son very sick.
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Neetan daa yiɣisi kul’ o yiŋa. Naa Dauda bidibiga kpiya Ka Yawɛ daa chɛ ka dɔro gbaai Yuria paɣ’ ni dɔɣi bidib’ so ti Dauda maa.

english_verse: So David went without eating to show his sorrow, and he begged God to make the boy well. David would not sleep on his bed, but spent each night lying on the floor.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa lo noli, ka kpe duu nti teei dɔni tiŋgban’ ni suhiri Naawuni bia maa zuɣu din dali maa yuŋ zaa.

english_verse: His officials stood beside him and tried to talk him into getting up. But he would not get up or eat with them.
translation_verse: Ka kpambaliba bɛn daa be o yiŋa kana ti zan’ o sani ni bɛ kpuɣ’ o yiɣisi, amaa ka o bi saɣi bee n-chɛ ka o mini ba laɣim ʒini di bindirigu.

english_verse: After the child had been sick for seven days, he died, but the officials were afraid to tell David. They said to each other, “Even when the boy was alive, David wouldn't listen to us. How can we tell him his son is dead? He might do something terrible!”
translation_verse: Di daba ayopɔin dali ka bia maa daa kpi. Ka kpambaliba maa daa zɔri ni bɛ garigi Dauda o bia maa kuli; dama bɛ daa yɛlimi, “Nyama, bia ŋɔ daa na nɛmi ka ti tɔɣis’ o yɛtɔɣa ka o zaɣisi wumbu la, ka wula ka ti lee yɛn tooi yɛl’ o ni bia maa kpiya? Di pa shɛli ka o ti tum omaŋ’ barina.”

english_verse: David noticed his servants whispering, and he knew the boy was dead. “Did my son die?” he asked his servants. “Yes, he did,” they answered.
translation_verse: Amaa Dauda ni daa nya ka o kpambaliba maa sɔɣiri yɛri tab’ maa ka o baŋ ni bia maa kpiya; ka bɔh’ o kpamba maa, “Bia maa kpiya?” Ka bɛ yɛl’ o, “O kpiya.”

english_verse: His officials said, “What are you doing? You went without eating and cried for your son while he was alive! But now that he's dead, you're up and eating.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka o kpamba maa daa bɔh’ o, “Wula ka a lee niŋ shɛm maa? Bia maa ni daa na ne, a daa lola noli ka kum o zuɣu pam, amaa ka o ti lee kpi ka a yiɣisi di bindirigu?”

english_verse: David answered: While he was still alive, I went without food and cried because there was still hope. I said to myself, “Who knows? Maybe the Lord will have pity on me and let the child live.”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa garigi yɛli ba, “O ni daa na ne ka n lo noli ka kumd’ o zuɣu maa, n daa yɛlimi, ‘Di pa shɛli Yawɛ ni zo ma nambɔɣu ka chɛ ka o ku kpi.

english_verse: But now that he's dead, why should I go without eating? I can't bring him back! Someday I will join him in death, but he can't return to me. Solomon Is Born
translation_verse: Amaa pumpɔŋɔ o kpiya, ka bɔ zuɣu ka n lee lan yɛn lo noli yaha? N ni tooi lan chɛ ka o labina? Mani n-naɣi ni ti chaŋ o sani, amaa ŋun’ ku lan labi n sanna.’ ” Bɛ dɔɣi Sulemaana

english_verse: David comforted his wife Bathsheba and slept with her. Later on, she gave birth to another son and named him Solomon. The Lord loved Solomon
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Dauda daa maag’ o paɣa Batishiiba suhu, ka o min’ o daa lan dɔni ka o dɔɣi bidibiga, ka o bol’ o yuli Sulemaana. Ka Yawɛ daa yur’ o pam,

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab had been in the country of Ammon, attacking the city of Rabbah. He captured the royal fortress
translation_verse: Di saha maa Jɔab daa na kul tuhirila Ammɔnnim’ bɛ tin’ zuɣu din nyɛ Raba la ni.

english_verse: and sent a messenger to tell David: I have attacked Rabbah and captured the fortress guarding the city water supply.
translation_verse: Ka o daa ti tim ti yɛli Dauda, “N tuhi nyaŋ Rabanim’ maa hal ka fa bɛ tin’ shɛli din mali kom la gba.

english_verse: Call the rest of the army together. Then surround the city, and capture it yourself. If you don't, everyone will remember that I captured the city.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ laɣimmi ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn kpalim la na nti tuhi deei tiŋ’ maa amaŋmaŋa, di yi pa lala n yi tuhi deei tiŋ’ maa, bɛ ni zaŋ n yuli bol’ li.”

english_verse: David called the rest of the army together and attacked Rabbah. He captured the city
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda daa laɣim niriba maa zaa chaŋ Raba ti tuhi deei li.

english_verse: David made the people of Rabbah tear down the city walls with iron picks and axes, and then he put them to work making bricks. He did the same thing with all the other Ammonite cities. David went back to Jerusalem, and the people of Israel returned to their homes.
translation_verse: Ka o daa chɛ ka tiŋ’ maa niriba zaŋ suhi din mali nyina mini kuriti kuya ni kuriti lɛri n-tumd’ o tuma, ka ŋmar’ o bilichiisi; lala ka o daa niŋ Ammɔnnim’ tinsi maa zaa. Di nyaaŋa ka Dauda min’ o niriba maa zaa daa lab’ Jɛrusalɛm.

english_verse: David had a beautiful daughter named Tamar, who was the sister of Absalom. She was also the half sister of Amnon, who fell in love with her.
translation_verse: Dauda bia Absalom daa mali tizɔpaɣ’ viɛlli ka o yuli booni Tama. Dahin shɛli ka Dauda bia Amnɔn kɔre daa ti kpe o ni.

english_verse: But Tamar was a virgin, and Amnon could not think of a way to be alone with her. He was so upset about it that he made himself sick.
translation_verse: Ka Amnɔn daa zaŋ di yɛla muɣis’ omaŋ’ hal ti gbaai dɔro o tizɔpaɣ’ Tama maa zuɣu. Dama Tama daa na ʒi doo, ka di zuɣu daa chɛ ka Amnɔn kɔŋ o ni yɛn niŋ o shɛm.

english_verse: Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, who was the son of David's brother Shimeah. Jonadab always knew how to get what he wanted,
translation_verse: Amaa Amnɔn daa mal’ o zo so ka o yuli booni Jɔnadab, o daa nyɛla Dauda mabia Shamma dapala, ka daa mali yɛm pam.

english_verse: and he said to Amnon, “What's the matter? You're the king's son! You shouldn't have to go around feeling sorry for yourself every morning.” Amnon said, “I'm in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.”
translation_verse: Ka Jɔnadab daa bɔhi Amnɔn, “Nabia, bɔ n-niŋ ka a kpalim mali suhugarigu biɛɣukam lala? Yɛlim’ ma din muɣis’ a. Ka Amnɔn daa yɛl’ o, “N kɔre n-kpe m mabia Absalom tizɔpaɣ’ Tama ni.”
