english_verse: Jonadab told him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, ask him to send Tamar, so you can watch her cook something for you. Then she can serve you the food.”
translation_verse: Ka Jɔnadab daa yɛli Amnɔn, “Dɔnim’ a garo zuɣu n-niŋ kaman a biɛrimi la, ka a ba yi ti kana ni o ti kaag’ a, nyin’ yɛlim’ o, ‘Chɛ ka n tizɔpaɣ’ Tama kana ti mali bɔrɔbɔro ti ma ka n ŋubi, ka yuun’ o ka o duɣi bindirigu kpe n-zaŋ li na ti gbib’ o nuu ni ka n di.’ ”

english_verse: So Amnon went to bed and pretended to be sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please, ask Tamar to come over. She can make some special bread while I watch, and then she can serve it to me.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Amnɔn daa dɔni n-shiri niŋ kaman o biɛrimi la. Ka naa daa ti kana ni o ti kaag’ o, ka Amnɔn yɛl’ o, “Naa, chɛ ka Tama kana ti mali maha ti ma n ninni, ka zaŋ li na ti gbib’ o nuu ni ka n ŋubi.”

english_verse: David told Tamar, “Go over to Amnon's house and fix him some food.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda daa tim ti yɛli Tama, “Cham’ a tizɔdoo Amnɔn yiŋa nti niŋ bindirigu ti o.”

english_verse: When she got there, he was lying in bed. She mixed the dough, made the loaves, and baked them while he watched.
translation_verse: Ka Tama daa chaŋ o tizɔdoo Amnɔn yiŋa ka o ti domi. Ka o daa niŋ zim ŋɔri mahibiɛli m-mali maha o nini maa ni

english_verse: Then she took the bread out of the pan and put it on his plate, but he refused to eat it. Amnon said, “Send the servants out of the house.” After they had gone,
translation_verse: n-yaai li mahilaa ni ti zal’ o tooni, ka o zaɣisi li ŋubbu, ka yɛl’ o, “Karimi sokam ka bɛ yi ka chɛ ma,” ka bɛ zaa daa yi.

english_verse: he said to Tamar, “Serve the food in my bedroom.” Tamar picked up the bread that she had made and brought it into Amnon's bedroom.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Amnɔn daa yɛli Tama, “Zaŋmi bindirigu maa kpɛhi n dugbɛrili puuni nti gbib’ li a nuu ni ka n di.” Ka Tama daa zaŋ o ni mali mahi’ shɛŋa maa kpɛh’ o tizɔdoo Amnɔn dugbɛrili maa ni.

english_verse: But as she was taking it over to him, he grabbed her and said, “Come to bed with me!”
translation_verse: Amaa o ni daa ti zaŋ li mir’ o na ni o di ka o dii gɔh’ o nuu ni ka yɛl’ o, “N tizɔpaɣa, chɛ ka m min’ a dɔni.”

english_verse: She answered, “No! Please don't force me! This sort of thing isn't done in Israel. It's disgusting!
translation_verse: Ka o daa garigi yɛl’ o, “Aai, m biɛli, di zaŋ kiŋkansi doli ma, dama tuuni ŋɔ na ʒi n-tum Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni, di tum jɛrilim tuuni ŋɔ.

english_verse: Think of me. I'll be disgraced forever! And think of yourself. Everyone in Israel will say you're nothing but trash! Just ask the king, and he will let you marry me.”
translation_verse: Ka ya polo ka n lee yɛn zaŋ vi ŋɔ kpe? Ka sokam ni bol’ a jɛrigu Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ni, dinzuɣu jaande, yɛlim’ naa, o ni zaŋ ma ti a.”

english_verse: But Amnon would not listen to what she said. He was stronger than she was, so he overpowered her and raped her.
translation_verse: Amaa ka o daa zaɣisi wumbu. Ka o ni daa mali yaa gari Tama maa zuɣu, ka o zaŋ kpeengarigu dɔn’ o.

english_verse: Then Amnon hated her even more than he had loved her before. So he told her, “Get up and get out!”
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Amnɔn daa kul lan je Tama yɛlli zaa, hal ka o ni daa je o shɛm maa gar’ o ni daa yur’ o shɛm la gba. Di saha ka Amnɔn daa yɛl’ o, “Yiɣisim’ yi.”

english_verse: She said, “Don't send me away! That would be worse than what you have already done.” But Amnon would not listen.
translation_verse: Amaa ka o daa garigi yɛl’ o, “Aai, m biɛli, a ni kariti ma shɛm ŋɔ n-lee bie n-gari a ni niŋ ma shɛm maa gba.” Amaa ka Amnɔn daa zaɣis’ o yɛligu maa wumbu;

english_verse: He called in his servant and said, “Throw this woman out and lock the door!”
translation_verse: ka daa boli nachimbil’ so ŋun daa tumd’ o tuma na ti yɛl’ o, “Zaŋm’ paɣ’ ŋɔ yihi ka kpari dunoli.”

english_verse: The servant made her leave, and he locked the door behind her. The king's unmarried daughters used to wear long robes with sleeves.
translation_verse: Di saha o daa yɛla saalo’ bɔɣiwɔɣila, dama di saha maa nabipuɣinsi bɛn daa na ʒi dɔbba ni daa yi yɛri saalo’ shɛŋa m-bala. Ka o tumtumda maa daa daag’ o yihi ka kpari dunoli.

english_verse: Tamar tore the robe she was wearing and put ashes on her head. Then she covered her face with her hands and cried loudly as she walked away. Absalom Kills Amnon
translation_verse: Ka Tama daa niŋ tampiligim buɣ’ o zuɣu ka darigi cheeg’ o ni daa ye saalo’ shɛli maa, ka kah’ o nuhi pa o zuɣu ni n-kuhiri pampam chana.

english_verse: Tamar's brother Absalom said to her, “How could Amnon have done such a terrible thing to you! But since he's your brother, don't tell anyone what happened. Just try not to think about it.” Tamar soon moved into Absalom's house, but she was always sad and lonely.
translation_verse: Ka o tizɔdoo Absalom daa nya o ka bɔh’ o, “A tizɔdoo Amnɔn zaŋ a mi dɔni yɔɣu?” Ka daa yɛl’ o, “N tizɔpaɣa niŋmi suɣilo, a tizɔdoo m-bala, di chɛ ka di muɣis’ a.” Di saha ka Tama daa leei bɛ ni ku lan bo paɣ’ so, ka o kpalim ʒi o tizɔdoo Absalom yiŋa.

english_verse: Absalom treated Amnon as though nothing had happened, but he hated Amnon for what he had done to his sister Tamar.
translation_verse: Amaa Absalom daa bi yɛli Amnɔn zaɣ’ biɛɣu bee zaɣ’ viɛlli, dama o daa lan je Amnɔn yɛlli o ni daa zaŋ kiŋkansi niŋ o tizɔpaɣ’ Tama shɛm maa zuɣu. Absalom bɔhi Amnɔn biɛri

english_verse: Two years later, Absalom's servants were cutting wool from his sheep in Baal-Hazor near the town of Ephraim, and Absalom invited all of the king's sons to be there.
translation_verse: Di yuma ayi nyaaŋa ka Absalom daa ti yɛn chɛ o piɛri kɔbiri Baalihazɔr din mini Ifriim bi wɔɣ’ ni tab’ la, ka daa boli nabihi zaa ni bɛ kana.

english_verse: Then he went to David and said, “My servants are cutting the wool from my sheep. Please come and join us!”
translation_verse: Ka Absalom daa chaŋ naa sani ti yɛl’ o, “Naa nyama, a dabili yɛn chɛla o piɛri kɔbiri, ka bɔri ni naa min’ o kpamba zaa kana.”

english_verse: David answered, “No, my son, we won't go. It would be too expensive for you.” Absalom tried to get him to change his mind, but David did not want to go. He only said that he hoped they would have a good time.
translation_verse: Amaa ka naa daa yɛli Absalom, “Aai, m bia, di chɛ ka ti zaa kana, di yi nyɛ lala, ti yɛla ni ti muɣis’ a pam.” Ka Absalom daa kpaŋ omaŋa ni o chɛ ka o chaŋ, amaa ka o daa zaɣisi, ka naɣ’ suhila alibarika niŋ o ni.

english_verse: Absalom said, “If you won't go, at least let my brother Amnon come with us.” David asked, “Why should he go with you?”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Absalom daa yɛli naa, “ N suhir’ a mi, a yi ku chaŋ, nyin’ lee chɛ ka ti mini m mabia Amnɔn chaŋ.” Ka naa daa bɔh’ o, “Bɔzuɣu ka a lee bɔri ni yi min’ o chaŋ?”

english_verse: But Absalom kept on insisting, and finally David let Amnon and all his other sons go with Absalom. Absalom prepared a banquet fit for a king.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Absalom daa kpaŋ omaŋ’ hal ka o ti saɣi ka Amnɔn mini nabihi maa zaa daa dol’ o chaŋ.

english_verse: But he told his servants, “Keep an eye on Amnon. When he gets a little drunk from the wine and is feeling relaxed, I'll give the signal. Then kill him! I've commanded you to do it, so don't be afraid. Be strong and brave.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Absalom daa yɛl’ o tumtumdiba, “Lihimiya, yi yi ti nya ka Amnɔn nyu wain kuli ka n yɛli ya, ‘Kumiya Amnɔn,’ yin’ kumiy’ o. Di zɔriya dabiɛm, mani m-puhi ya. Maliya suhukpeeni ka tum bidibilim tuma.”

english_verse: Absalom's servants killed Amnon, just as Absalom had told them. The rest of the king's sons quickly rode away on their mules to escape from Absalom.
translation_verse: Ka Absalom tumtumdiba maa daa shiri niŋ Amnɔn kaman Absalom ni wuhi ba ni bɛ niŋ o shɛm maa. Di saha ka nabihi maa zaa daa dii yiɣisi ba bɛ buntaansi zo.

english_verse: While they were on their way to Jerusalem, someone told David, “Absalom has killed all of your sons! Not even one is left.”
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa na be soli kuna ka lahibali ti nti to Dauda, “Absalom ku nabihi la zaa, hal bɛ yino bi lan kpalim.”

english_verse: David got up, and in his sorrow he tore his clothes and lay down on the ground. His servants remained standing, but they tore their clothes too.
translation_verse: Di saha ka naa daa yiɣisi dari chah’ o binyɛra, ka teei dɔni tiŋgban’ ni ka kpambaliba bɛn daa be o sani gba dari chahi bɛ binyɛra.

english_verse: Then David's nephew Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, not all of your sons were killed! Only Amnon is dead. On the day that Amnon raped Tamar, Absalom decided to kill him.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Dauda mabia Shamma dapala Jɔnadab daa yɛli, “N dana, di tɛhi ni bɛ ku nabihi maa zaa, Amnɔn kɔŋko n-kpi. Absalom n-chɛ ka bɛ ku o, ka dimbɔŋɔ maa nyɛla o ni pun lo shɛli dahin’ shɛli o ni daa zaŋ kiŋkansi dɔn’ o tizɔpaɣa Tama la zuɣu.

english_verse: Don't worry about the report that all your sons were killed. Only Amnon is dead,
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ n dan’ naa, di chɛ ka di muɣis’ a kaman a bihi maa zaa n-shiri kpi la, dama Amnɔn kɔŋko n-kpi.”

english_verse: and Absalom has run away.” One of the guards noticed a lot of people coming along the hillside on the road to Horonaim. He went and told the king, “I saw some men coming along Horonaim Road.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Absalom daa zo. Ka nachimbil’ so ŋun daa guli nayili maa daa ti kpuɣ’ o zuɣu lihi nya niriba pam ni doli Hɔrɔnaim soli m-baɣisiri zoli kanna.

english_verse: Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, look! Here come your sons now, just as I told you.”
translation_verse: Ka Jɔnadab daa yɛli naa, “Nyama, nabihi maa kunna kaman mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ ni pun yɛl’ a shɛm la.”

english_verse: No sooner had he said it, than David's sons came in. They were weeping out loud, and David and all his officials cried just as loudly.
translation_verse: Nyama, o ni daa kul yɛri maa o noli daa na bi lu tiŋa, ka nabihi maa dii kpɛna nti duhi bɛ yee kumda, ka naa min’ o kpamba zaa gba daa kum pam.

english_verse: David still felt so sad over the loss of Amnon that he wanted to take his army there and capture Absalom.
translation_verse: Ka naa suhu daa ti giri zaŋ chaŋ Amnɔn kum maa polo, o ni daa nya ka o lan kani maa zuɣu, ka o suhu lan yu ni o kari Absalom naba.

english_verse: Joab knew that David couldn't stop thinking about Absalom,
translation_verse: Ka Zɛruya bia Jɔab ni daa ti baŋ ni Naa Dauda suhu lu Absalom ni,

english_verse: The woman from Tekoa went to David. She bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, please help me!”
translation_verse: Tɛkɔa paɣ’ maa ni daa ti paai naa tooni, o daa lumi gbani zaŋ o nini kpa tiŋa n-lu naa sizuura ka yɛli, “Naa, fam ma bahi.”

english_verse: David asked, “What's the matter?” She replied: My husband is dead, and I'm a widow.
translation_verse: Ka naa daa bɔh’ o, “Bɔ n-lee muɣis’ a?” Ka o garigi yɛli, “Mbaye, n yidan’ kpimi ka n kpalim pakoli.

english_verse: I had two sons, but they got into a fight out in a field where there was no one to pull them apart, and one of them killed the other.
translation_verse: Mani ŋun nyɛ a dabipaɣ’ ŋɔ daa malila bidibis’ ayi, ka bɛ daa ti chaŋ puu ni ti zabi, ka so kani ŋun ni goo’ ba, ka yino daa ŋme n-ku ŋun’ la.

english_verse: Now all of my relatives have come to me and said, “Hand over your son! We're going to put him to death for killing his brother.” But what they really want is to get rid of him, so they can take over our land. Please don't let them put out my only flame of hope! There won't be anyone left on this earth to carry on my husband's name.
translation_verse: Ka pumpɔŋɔ bɛ dɔɣiriba zaa suhuri yiɣisimi bahi mani ŋun nyɛ a dabipaɣ’ ŋɔ zuɣu ka yɛli, “Zaŋm’ ŋun ku o mabia maa ti ti ka ti ku o, o ni ku o mabia maa zuɣu din ni chɛ ka bɛ ku falidir’ maa gba. Lala n-ni chɛ ka bɛ kpihi buɣimsal’ shɛli din kpalim maa din ni chɛ ka bɛ kpihim n yidan’ maa zuliya min’ o yuli dunia yili.”

english_verse: “Go on home,” David told her. “I'll take care of this matter for you.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka naa daa yɛli paɣ’ maa, “Lab’ kuli, ka n lihi a yɛlli maa zuɣu.”

english_verse: The woman said, “I hope your decision doesn't cause any problems for you. But if it does, you can blame me.”
translation_verse: Ka Tɛkɔa paɣ’ maa daa yɛli, “N dana, chɛ ka a ni yɛn niŋ shɛlikam zambu ʒi m mini n daŋ zaa zuɣu, ka a min’ a nam ʒiishee ŋɔ ku mali taali di puuni.”

english_verse: He said, “If anyone gives you trouble, bring them to me, and it won't happen again!”
translation_verse: Ka naa daa yɛl’ o, “So yi lan yɛl’ a shɛli, nyin’ tahim’ o n sanna, ka o ku lan tooi niŋ a shɛli yaha.”

english_verse: “Please,” she replied, “swear by the Lord your God that no one will be allowed to kill my son!” He said, “I swear by the living Lord that no one will touch even a hair on his head!”
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ maa daa yɛli, “Naa, n suhir’ a mi, pom’ Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ a Naawuni ŋɔ ni a ku chɛ ka ŋun yɛn bɔhi ʒim yihibu biɛri maa ku o din ni chɛ ka bɛ ku ku m bia maa.” Ka naa daa yɛl’ o, “Hal ka Yawɛ ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu, a bia maa zabigu zaɣ’ yini gba ku yi o zuɣu ni lu tiŋa.”

english_verse: Then she asked, “Your Majesty, may I say something?” “Yes,” he answered.
translation_verse: Ka paɣa maa daa lan yɛli, “N dan’ naa, n suhir’ a, chɛ ka n yɛl’ a yɛtɔɣili ŋɔ.” Ka o yɛl’ o, “Yɛlima.”

english_verse: The woman said: Haven't you been hurting God's people? Your own son had to leave the country. And when you judged in my favor, it was the same as admitting that you should have let him come back.
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ maa daa yɛl’ o, “Ka bɔ n-niŋ ka a lo ni a niŋ Naawuni niriba zaɣ’ biɛɣu? Dama naa yi bi chɛ ka o bia ŋun be yɔɣu la labina yaha, dindina naa yɛtɔɣa ŋɔ nyɛla din gbaag’ omaŋmaŋa.

english_verse: We each must die and disappear like water poured out on the ground. But God doesn't take our lives. Instead, he figures out ways of bringing us back when we run away.
translation_verse: Di kpala talahi ni ti zaa kpi; ti ŋmanila kom din kpaai bahi tiŋa ka nir’ ku lan tooi va li la. Amaa Naawuni ni tiligi ninvuɣ’ so ŋun bi yih’ o bia ŋun zo n-kpe yɔɣu o daŋ ni.

english_verse: Your Majesty, I came here to tell you about my problem, because I was afraid of what someone might do to me. I decided to come to you, because I thought you could help.
translation_verse: Pumpɔŋɔ n kamina ni n ti yɛli nyini n dan’ naa dimbɔŋɔ, dama niriba maa chɛmi ka dabiɛm gbaai ma pam ka n tɛhi ni n yi yɛli nyin’ naa, di pa shɛli a ni niŋ man’ ŋun nyɛ o dabipaɣ’ ŋɔ ni bɔr’ shɛm maa.

english_verse: In fact, I knew that you would listen and save my son and me from those who want to take the land that God gave us.
translation_verse: Dama naa ni wum n fabila maa ka fa m mini m bia ŋun nyɛ a dabili maa ninvuɣ’ so ŋun bɔr’ ni o ku ti n-kpihim ti birili Naawuni ni zaŋ tiŋgbɔn shɛli ti ti ŋɔ ni la nuu ni bahi.

english_verse: I can rest easy now that you have given your decision. You know the difference between right and wrong just like an angel of God, and I pray that the Lord your God will be with you.
translation_verse: Man’ ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ daa lan tɛhimi ni nyin’ naa yɛligu nyɛla din ni ti ma vuhim, dama nyini n dan’ naa ŋmanila Naawuni malaika ŋun mi zaɣ’ suŋ ni zaɣ’ biɛɣu. Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ a Naawuni ŋɔ ni be a sani.”

english_verse: Then David said to the woman, “Now I'm going to ask you a question, and don't try to hide the truth!” The woman replied, “Please go ahead, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka naa daa garigi yɛli paɣ’ maa, “N yi bɔh’ a bɔhigu nyin’ di sɔɣi ma shɛli.” Ka paɣ’ maa yɛl’ o, N dan’ naa, bɔhim’ ma.

english_verse: but only to show you the other side of this problem. You must be as wise as the angel of God to know everything that goes on in this country.”
translation_verse: A dabili Jɔab bɔrimi ni o mali yɛla zali dɛde, dina n-chɛ ka o niŋ lala maa. Amaa n dan’ mali yɛm kaman Naawuni malaika ni mali yɛm shɛm la din ni tooi baŋ binshɛɣukam din be dunia ŋɔ ni.”

english_verse: David turned to Joab and said, “It seems that I have already given my decision. Go and bring Absalom back.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka naa daa yɛli Jɔab, “Nyama, pumpɔŋɔ n saɣ’ a ni bɔri shɛm maa, cham’ ti zaŋ Absalom na.”

english_verse: Joab went to Geshur to get Absalom. But when they came back to Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Di saha ka Jɔab daa yiɣisi chaŋ Gɛshur nti zaŋ Absalom kuli Jɛrusalɛm na.

english_verse: David told Joab, “I don't want to see my son Absalom. Tell him to stay away from me.” So Absalom went to his own house without seeing his father. Absalom Was Handsome
translation_verse: Ka naa daa yɛl’ o, “Chɛ ka o be omaŋmaŋ’ yiŋa, o di chɛ ka n nini nya o. Dinzuɣu ka Absalom daa be omaŋmaŋ’ yiŋa, ka bi chani naa sani.” Absalom mini Naa Dauda tɔɣisiya

english_verse: No one in all Israel was as handsome and well-built as Absalom.
translation_verse: So daa ka Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ zaa ni n-viɛli paai Absalom. O daa ka dalinli o napɔnvari ni zaŋ hal ni o zuɣu ni.

english_verse: His hair grew so thick and heavy that when he got it cut once a year, it weighed over two kilograms.
translation_verse: O daa yi chɛ o zabiri o zaŋdila nayili sania zahim li ka di tibisim nyɛ kaman kilɔgiram ayi.

english_verse: Absalom had three sons. He also had a daughter named Tamar, who grew up to be very beautiful. Absalom Finally Sees David
translation_verse: Absalom daa dɔɣila bidibis’ ata ni bipuɣin’ yino ŋun yuli daa booni Tama, o daa nyɛla paɣisar’ viɛlli.

english_verse: Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years without seeing his father.
translation_verse: Absalom daa niŋ yuma ayi Jɛrusalɛm ka o nini bi nya naa.

english_verse: He wanted Joab to talk to David for him. So one day he sent a message asking Joab to come over, but Joab refused. Absalom sent another message, but Joab still refused.
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Absalom daa tim ti boli Jɔab ni o kana ka o tim o naa sani, amaa ka Jɔab daa zaɣisi kandina. Ka o lan tim pahi buyi, amaa ka Jɔab kul bahi zaɣisi kandina.

english_verse: Finally, Absalom told his servants, “Joab's barley field is right next to mine. Go set it on fire!” And they did.
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Absalom daa yɛl’ o tumtumdiba, “Nyamiya, Jɔab puu m-baɣi m puu ka siŋkaafa be di ni la, chamiya ti niŋ buɣim nyo li. Ka Absalom tumtumdiba maa daa shiri chaŋ ti niŋ buɣim nyo puu maa.”

english_verse: Joab went to Absalom's house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Jɔab daa yiɣisi chaŋ Absalom yiŋa nti bɔh’ o, “Bɔ zuɣu ka a chɛ ka a tumtumdiba nyo m puu buɣim?”

english_verse: Absalom answered, “You didn't pay any attention when I sent for you. I want you to ask my father why he told me to come back from Geshur. I was better off there. I want to see my father now! If I'm guilty, let him kill me.”
translation_verse: Ka Absalom daa garigi yɛli Jɔab, “Nyama, n daa tim na ti bol’ a ni a kana ka n tim a naa sani ka a ti bɔh’ o “Bɔzuɣu ka n lee yi Gɛshur n-kul’ kpɛna? N yi di na kpalim be nimaani di di so. Dinzuɣu, pumpɔŋɔ zaŋm’ ma chaŋ naa sani, n yi mali taali, ŋun’ kum’ ma.”

english_verse: Joab went to David and told him what Absalom had said. David sent for Absalom, and Absalom came. He bowed very low, and David leaned over and kissed him.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Jɔab daa chaŋ naa sani ti yɛl’ o, ka naa daa chɛ ka bɛ boli Absalom, ka o kana ti damdi naa tooni, ka naa daa mɔɣis’ o kpariŋ.

english_verse: Some time later, Absalom got himself a chariot with horses to pull it, and he had
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka Absalom daa bo chɛchɛbuŋ’ mini yuri ka zaŋ ninvuɣ’ pihinu bah’ o tooni.

english_verse: He would get up early each morning and wait by the side of the road that led to the city gate. Anyone who had a complaint to bring to King David would have to go that way, and Absalom would ask each of them, “Where are you from?” If they said, “I'm from a tribe in the north,”
translation_verse: Absalom daa yi daŋdi la yibu n-chani ti zaani tiŋ’ maa dunoli sokpaŋa, ka so daa yi ti mali yɛlli chani naa sani ni o ti mal’ li, o boon’ o mi na ti bɔh’ o, “Tiŋ’ kani ka a lee yina?” Ka dilan’ yi yɛli, “Mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ nyɛla Izraɛl zuliya yaakaza nira.”

english_verse: Absalom would say, “You deserve to win your case. It's too bad the king doesn't have anyone to hear complaints like yours.
translation_verse: Absalom dii yɛrila dilana, “Nyama, a yɛtɔɣa viɛla ka tuhi, amaa naa bi bo so zal’ o zaani ni o wum a ni mali shɛli.”

english_verse: Whenever anyone came to Absalom and started bowing down, he would reach out and hug and kiss them.
translation_verse: Ka ŋunkam daa yi mir’ o ni o damd’ o tiŋa n-lu o sizuura, o teerila o nuu gbaai dilana m-mɔɣis’ o kpariŋ.

english_verse: That's how he treated everyone from Israel who brought a complaint to the king. Soon everyone in Israel liked Absalom better than they liked David.
translation_verse: Lala ka Absalom daa yi niŋdi Izraɛlnim’ bɛn zaa kani naa sanna ni o ti kari bɛ yɛtɔɣa saria ti ba, ka di zuɣu daa chɛ ka Izraɛlnim’ suhuri lɛbigi ŋun’ Absalom polo.

english_verse: Four years later, Absalom said to David, “Please, let me go to Hebron. I have to keep a promise that I made to the Lord,
translation_verse: Di yuma anahi nyaaŋa ka Absalom daa chaŋ ti yɛli naa, “Naa, n suhir’ a mi, chɛ ka n chaŋ Hiburɔn nti pali n ni daa lo Yawɛ alikauli shɛli nimaani.

english_verse: when I was living with the Arameans in Geshur. I promised that if the Lord would bring me back to live in Jerusalem, I would worship him in Hebron.”
translation_verse: Dama mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ ni daa be Gɛshur Aram tiŋgbɔŋ ni la, ka n daa lo alikauli yɛli, ‘Yawɛ yi ti chɛ ka n labi Jɛrusalɛm, n ni jɛm o Hiburɔn.’ ”

english_verse: David gave his permission, and Absalom went to Hebron.
translation_verse: Ka naa daa yɛl’ o, “Cham’ ni suhudoo.” Ka o daa yiɣisi chaŋ Hiburɔn.

english_verse: A messenger came and told David, “Everyone in Israel is on Absalom's side!”
translation_verse: Ka so daa kana ti yɛli Dauda, “Izraɛlnim’ suhuri lɛbigila Absalom polo.”

english_verse: David's officials were in Jerusalem with him, and he told them, “Let's get out of here! We'll have to leave soon, or none of us will escape from Absalom. Hurry! If he moves fast, he could catch us while we're still here. Then he will kill us and everyone else in the city.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda daa yɛl’ o kpamba bɛn be o sani zaa, “Yiɣisimiya ka ti zo, di yi pa lala ti ti ku tooi lan zo n-yi Absalom nuu ni. Ti zomiya yomyom, di yi pa lala o ni gbahi ti pumpɔŋɔ n-niŋ ti zaɣ’ biɛɣu, ka zaŋ takɔbi ku ya ŋɔ nima.”

english_verse: David left behind ten of his wives to take care of the palace, but the rest of his family and his officials and soldiers went with him. They stopped at the last house at the edge of the city.
translation_verse: Naa min’ o niriba maa zaa ni daa yiri tiŋ’ maa ni, bɛ daa zanila yili shɛli din’ bahindi nyaaŋa.

english_verse: Then David stood there and watched while his regular troops and his bodyguards marched past. The last group was the
translation_verse: Ka o kpamba maa zaa daa kana ti gar’ o zuɣu, ka Chɛrɛtinim’ mini Pɛlɛtinim’ ni Gaatinim’ ninvuɣ’ kɔbisiyɔbu bɛn daa doli naa yi Gaat la na zaa daa gar’ o tooni.

english_verse: David spoke to Ittai and said, “You're a foreigner from the town of Gath. You don't have to leave with us. Go back and join the new king!
translation_verse: Di saha ka naa daa yɛli Itai ŋun daa nyɛ Gaat nir’ la, “Bɔzuɣu ka yi mi dol’ ti chana? Labimiya ka yi mini naa maa ti be, dama yinim’ nyɛla tinzunnima, ka lan nyɛ yi yanim’ ni kari shɛb’ bahi na.

english_verse: You haven't been with me very long, so why should you have to follow me, when I don't even know where I'm going? Take your soldiers and go back. I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you.”
translation_verse: Kulla sɔhila ka yi paai kpe na; ka n chɛ ka yi doli ma chani gindi ka m bi mi n ni kuni luɣ’ shɛli polo gba? Zaŋm’ a mabihi maa ka yi labi. Yawɛ ni wuhi ya o yurilim din bi naari min’ o ʒiɛyimtali.”

english_verse: Ittai answered, “Your Majesty, just as surely as you and the Lord live, I will go where you go, no matter if it costs me my life.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Itai daa garigi yɛli naa, “Hal ka Yawɛ ŋun be ŋɔ mini nyini n dan’ naa ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu, nyini n dan’ ni yɛn kpe luɣ’ shɛlikam zaa, di yi nyɛla kum shee bee nyɛvili shee, nimaani ka man’ ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ yɛn kpe.”

english_verse: “Then come on!” David said. So Ittai and all his men and their families walked on past David. David Sends the Sacred Chest Back to Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yɛli Itai, “Dindina garim’ ka ti chaŋ.” Di saha ka Itai ŋun daa nyɛ Gaat nir’ maa min’ o niriba zaa ni bibihi bɛn daa be o sani zaa gari tooni.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem were crying and moaning as David and everyone with him passed by. He led them across Kidron Valley and along the road toward the desert.
translation_verse: Naa min’ o niriba maa ni daa yiri maa, tiŋ’ maa nim’ zaa daa duhila kuŋa n-kum pam. Ka Naa daa chaŋ ti gbaai Kidirɔn kulibɔŋ du, ka o min’ o niriba maa zaa daa zaŋ kpa mɔɣu polo.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests were there along with several men from the tribe of Levi who were carrying the sacred chest. They set the chest down, and left it there until David and his followers had gone out of the city.
translation_verse: Ka Abiata daa yina, nyama, ka Zadok gba mini Lɛvinim’ zaa daa kpuɣi Naawuni Daalikauli Adaka la na ti zaŋ li zali hal ka niriba maa zaa ti yi tiŋ’ maa ni na.

english_verse: Then David said: Zadok, take the sacred chest back to Jerusalem. If the Lord is pleased with me, he will bring me back and let me see it and his tent again.
translation_verse: Di saha ka naa daa yɛli Zadok, “Zaŋmi Naawuni Daalikauli Adaka maa labisi tiŋ’ maa puuni ti zali, Yawɛ nini yi tiɣi ma, o ni lan zaŋ ma labisina ka n nini ti nya di min’ o biɛhigu shee.

english_verse: But if he says he isn't pleased with me, then let him do what he knows is best.
translation_verse: Amaa o yi yɛli ma, ‘N nini bi lan tiɣ’ a.’ Nyama, mani m-bɔŋɔ, O niŋmi ma kaman o ni nya ka shɛli viɛl’ o sani.”

english_verse: Zadok, you are a good judge of things, so return to the city and don't cause any trouble. Take your son Ahimaaz with you. Abiathar and his son Jonathan will also go back.
translation_verse: Ka naa daa lan yɛli Zadok ŋun daa nyɛ maligumaana maa, “Nyama, a mini Abiata zaŋmiya yi bidibis’ ayi bɛn nyɛ a bia Ahimaaz mini Abiata bia Jɔnatan n-labi tiŋ’ maa puuni ni suhudoo.

english_verse: I'll wait at the river crossing in the desert until I hear from you.
translation_verse: Nyamiya, n ni gbaai kulibɔŋ ŋɔ du nti guhiri mɔɣu ni hal ka yi ti tim na ti yɛli ma lahibali din beni.”

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar took the sacred chest back into Jerusalem and stayed there.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Zadok mini Abiata daa zaŋ Naawuni Daalikauli Adaka maa labisi Jɛrusalɛm, ka daa kpalim be nimaani.

english_verse: David went on up the slope of the Mount of Olives. He was barefoot and crying, and he covered his head to show his sorrow. Everyone with him was crying, and they covered their heads too.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Dauda daa chaŋ ti du Olivi tihi Zoli n-chani ka kumda. O daa zaŋla bini pil’ o zuɣu, ka chani napɔn’ zaŋa. Ka ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn zaa daa be o sani gba zaŋ bina pil’ bɛ zuɣuri n-kumdi dol’ o chana.

english_verse: Someone told David, “Ahithophel is helping Absalom plot against you!” David said, “Please, Lord, keep Ahithophel's plans from working!” David Sends Hushai Back as a Spy
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yɛli Dauda ni Ahitɔfɛl gba pahila Absalom zuɣu. Ka Dauda yɛli, “Yawɛ, n suhir’ a mi, chɛ ka Ahitɔfɛl ni yɛn wuhi yikombiɛlim yɛtɔɣ’ shɛŋa zaa leei jɛrilim.”

english_verse: When David reached the top of the Mount of Olives, he met Hushai the Archite at a place of worship. Hushai's robe was torn, and dust was on his head.
translation_verse: Dauda ni daa ti paai zoli maa zuɣu luɣ’ shɛli bɛ ni daa yi jɛmdi Naawuni la, nyama, ka Hushai ŋun nyɛ Ariki nir’ la daa chɛh’ omaŋmaŋ’ binyɛrigu ka kɔri taŋkpaɣu puɣ’ o zuɣu n-ka Naa Dauda sanna.

english_verse: David told him: If you come with me, you might slow us down.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yɛl’ o, “A yi doli ma, a yɛla ni ti muɣisi ma.

english_verse: Go back into the city and tell Absalom, “Your Majesty, I am your servant. I will serve you now, just as I served your father in the past.” Hushai, if you do that, you can help me ruin Ahithophel's plans.
translation_verse: Amaa a yi labi tiŋ’ maa puuni nti yɛli Absalom, ‘N dan’ naa, n ni leeg’ a kpambala. Kaman n ni yi kul nyɛ a ba kpambala shɛm, lala ka n yɛn nyɛ a gba kpambala, dina n-ni chɛ ka a nyaŋ Ahitɔfɛl yikombiɛlim maa ti ma.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests will be there with you, and you can tell them everything you hear in the palace.
translation_verse: Zadok mini Abiata bɛn nyɛ maligumaaniba la be nimaani. Dinzuɣu a yi ti kul wum shɛlikam nayili maa, nyin’ yɛlim’ Zadok mini Abiata bɛn nyɛ maligumaaniba maa.

english_verse: David's advisor Hushai slipped back into Jerusalem, at just about the same time Absalom was coming in.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda zɔsimo Hushai daa labi tiŋ’ puuni ti saɣisi saha shɛli Absalom ni kpɛri Jɛrusalɛm na.

english_verse: David had started down the other side of the Mount of Olives, when he was met by Ziba, the chief servant of Mephibosheth. Ziba had two donkeys that were carrying
translation_verse: Dauda ni daa yiɣisi zoli maa zuɣu n-tirisi tooni biɛla ha, ka Ziba ŋun daa nyɛ Mɛfibɔshɛt tumtumda la daa taɣi bɛ ni pa bun’ shɛb’ gaya kana ti tuhi ba soli. Bunsi maa daa ʒirila bɔrɔbɔro kpil’ kɔbiga mini wain tiwala din kuui zaza yila kɔbiga ni tiwal’ moma bini kɔbiga ni wain koligu pali.

english_verse: “What's all this?” David asked. Ziba said, “The donkeys are for your family to ride. The bread and fruit are for the people to eat, and the wine is for them to drink in the desert when they are tired out.”
translation_verse: Ka naa daa bɔhi Ziba, “Bɔzuɣu ka a ʒi dimbɔŋɔnim’ zaa na?” Ka Ziba garigi yɛl’ o, “Bunsi ŋɔ nyɛla naa min’ o malibu ni yɛn ba shɛba, ka bɔrɔbɔro ŋɔ mini tiwal’ moma ŋɔ nyɛ nachimba bindirigu. Ka wain ŋɔ mi nyɛ bɛ ni shɛb’ bɛn ti tarigi yɔɣu ŋɔ ni ni yɛn nyu shɛli.”

english_verse: “And where is Mephibosheth?” David asked. Ziba answered, “He stayed in Jerusalem, because he thinks the people of Israel want him to rule the kingdom of his grandfather Saul.”
translation_verse: Ka naa daa bɔhi Ziba, “Ka a dan’ bia la lee be ya polo?” Ka Ziba garigi yɛli naa, “Nyama, o kpalim Jɛrusalɛm, dama o yɛlimi, ‘Pumpɔŋɔ Izraɛlnim’ ni zaŋ n yab’ nam ŋɔ ti ma.’ ”

english_verse: David then told him, “Everything that used to belong to Mephibosheth is now yours.” Ziba said, “Your Majesty, I am your humble servant, and I hope you will be pleased with me.” Shimei Curses David
translation_verse: Di saha ka naa daa yɛli Ziba, “Nyama, Mɛfibɔshɛt ni daa su shɛlikam zaa leeg’ a dini pumpɔŋɔ.” Ka Ziba garigi yɛli, “N nyɛla ŋun luri n dan’ sizuura. Chɛ ka nyini n dan’ naa nini kul tiɣiri ma sahakam.” Naa Dauda mini Shimɛi

english_verse: David was near the town of Bahurim when a man came out and started cursing him. The man was Shimei the son of Gera, and he was one of Saul's distant relatives.
translation_verse: Naa Dauda ni daa ti paai Bahurim, ka Sool daŋ ni do’ so ŋun daa nyɛ Gɛra bia ka o yuli booni Shimɛi la daa yina ti turi ba.

english_verse: He threw stones at David, at his soldiers, and at everyone else, including the bodyguards who walked on each side of David.
translation_verse: Hal Naa Dauda kpambaliba zaa mini ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn mali kpiɔŋ ni daa be o nudirigu min’ o nuzaa polo maa zaa yoli, doo maa daa pihila kuɣa labiri Dauda mini ba zaa.

english_verse: Shimei was yelling at David, “Get out of here, you murderer! You good-for-nothing,
translation_verse: Ka Shimɛi daa kul turi ba ka yɛra, “Wara, wara, nyin’ ninvuɣ’ kur’ ŋɔ, nyin’ ninvuɣ’ yoli ŋɔ.

english_verse: the Lord is paying you back for killing so many in Saul's family. You stole his kingdom, but now the Lord has given it to your son Absalom. You're a murderer, and that's why you're in such big trouble!”
translation_verse: A ni daa ku Sool so min’ o yiŋnim’ shɛba, ka di nam zan’ o zaani la biɛri ka Yawɛ bɔhir’ a, ka fa a nam maa ti a bia Absalom maa. Nyama a bahila yoli maa, dama a nyɛla ninvuɣ’ kura.”

english_verse: Abishai said, “Your Majesty, this man is as useless as a dead dog! He shouldn't be allowed to curse you. Let me go over and chop off his head.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Abishai ŋun daa nyɛ Zɛruya bia la daa yɛli naa “Bɔ n-niŋ ka ba’ kpiŋ ŋɔ doli yɛri n dan’ naa zilima lala? Chɛ ka n chaŋ ti ŋma o zuɣu.”

english_verse: David replied, “What will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? If Shimei is cursing me because the Lord has told him to, then who are you to tell him to stop?”
translation_verse: Amaa ka naa daa yɛli, “Yinim’ Zɛruya bihi ŋɔ, wula ka n yɛn niŋ ya? Di yi nyɛla Yawɛ n-yɛl’ o, ‘Tum’ Dauda,’ ŋuni n-lee ni tooi bɔh’ o, “Bɔ n-niŋ ka a niŋdi lala?”

english_verse: Then David said to Abishai and all his soldiers: My own son is trying to kill me! Why shouldn't this man from the tribe of Benjamin want me dead even more? Let him curse all he wants. Maybe the Lord did tell him to curse me.
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yɛli Abishai min’ o kpamba maa, “Nyamiya, mmaŋmaŋ’ bia m-bɔri ni o ku ma la, di ni ti be ka Bɛnjamin zuliya ni nir’ ŋɔ? Chɛliy’ o ka o tu ma, dama Yawɛ n-zal’ o lala.

english_verse: But if the Lord hears these curses and sees the trouble I'm in, maybe he will have pity on me instead.
translation_verse: Di pa shɛli o turi ŋɔ zuɣu ni chɛ ka Yawɛ lihi n wahala ŋɔ ka niŋ ma din viɛli zuŋɔ.”

english_verse: David and the others went on down the road. Shimei went along the hillside by the road, cursing and throwing rocks and dirt at them.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda min’ o niriba maa daa lu solɔɣu chana, ka Shimɛi daa be zolɔŋni m-baɣisir’ o luɣili polo dol’ o chani tur’ o, ka labir’ o kuɣa, ka toori taŋkpaɣu chɛr’ o.

english_verse: When David and those with him came to the Jordan River, they were tired out. But after they rested, they felt much better. Hushai Meets Absalom
translation_verse: Ka naa mini ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn zaa daa be o sani maa daa mali ti paai Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili ni ka di wum ba pam, ka o zani nimaani vuhi.

english_verse: By this time, Absalom, Ahithophel, and the others had reached Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ka Absalom min’ o niriba zaa ni Izraɛlnim’ daa chaŋ ti kpe Jɛrusalɛm, ka Ahitɔfɛl gba daa be o sani.

english_verse: David's friend Hushai came to Absalom and said, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Ka Hushai ŋun daa nyɛ Ariki nir’ ka nyɛ Dauda zɔsimo la daa chaŋ Absalom sani ti yɛl’ o, “Naawuni dolimi naa nyɛvili! Naawuni dolimi naa nyɛvili!”

english_verse: But Absalom asked Hushai, “Is this how you show loyalty to your friend David? Why didn't you go with him?”
translation_verse: Ka Absalom daa bɔhi Hushai, “A ʒiɛyimtali zaŋ chaŋ a zo maa sani ni bahindi shɛm m-bala? Bɔ n-niŋ ka a bi dol’ a zo maa chaŋ?”

english_verse: Hushai answered, “The Lord and the people of Israel have chosen you to be king. I can't leave. I have to stay and serve the one they've chosen.
translation_verse: Ka Hushai daa garigi yɛli Absalom, “Aai Yawɛ min’ o niriba ŋɔ ni Izraɛlnim’ ni pii ninvuɣ’ so, o sani ka n yɛn be ka o su ma.

english_verse: Besides, it seems right for me to serve you, just as I served your father.” Ahithophel's Advice
translation_verse: M-pahi, ŋuni ka n lan yɛn jɛm ka pa ni n dan’ Dauda bia? N ni daa kul jɛmd’ a ba shɛm, lala ka n yɛn jɛm a gba.”

english_verse: Absalom turned to Ahithophel and said, “Give us your advice! What should we do?”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Absalom daa bɔhi Ahitɔfɛl, “Wuhim’ ti ti ni yɛn niŋ shɛm.”

english_verse: Ahithophel answered, “Some of your father's wives were left here to take care of the palace. You should have sex with them. Then everyone will find out that you have publicly disgraced your father. This will make you and your followers even more powerful.”
translation_verse: Ka Ahitɔfɛl daa yɛl’ o, “Cham’ ti zaŋ a ba mamanim’ shɛb’ o ni chɛ n-niŋ nayili ni bɛ maani li la dɔni, ka di chɛ ka Izraɛlnim’ zaa baŋ ni a leeg’ a ba dataa, ka bɛnkam zaa be a polo ni kpaŋsi bɛmaŋa.”

english_verse: Absalom had a tent set up on the flat roof of the palace, and everyone watched as he went into the tent with his father's wives.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka bɛ daa du nayili dufahirili zuɣusaa nti ti suɣili zali Absalom, ka Absalom daa mal’ o ba mamanim’ maa dooni nimaani Izraɛlnim’ zaa ninni.

english_verse: Ahithophel gave such good advice in those days that both Absalom and David thought it came straight from God.
translation_verse: Di ʒiɛman’ maa ni Ahitɔfɛl daa yi kul yɛli yɛtɔɣ’ shɛli, di ŋmanila Naawuni maŋmaŋ’ yɛligu n-nyɛ li. Ka Dauda min’ o bia Absalom zaa daa yi bi zaŋd’ o yɛligu niŋd’ asahi.

english_verse: and we will all go to fight David wherever he is. We will fall on him just as dew falls and covers the ground. He and all his soldiers will die!
translation_verse: Ka lala ni chɛ ka ti lir’ o o ni be luɣ’ shɛli maa n-lu o zuɣu kaman maligim ni luri tiŋgbani zuɣu shɛm la, ka o mini ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn be o sani maa zaa so ku tiligi.

english_verse: while he is tired and discouraged. He will panic, and everyone with him will run away. I won't kill anyone except David,
translation_verse: Di yi ti wum o ka o suhu zɔhira saha shɛli, ka n dii lir’ o n-kpɛh’ o dabiɛm ka ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn be o sani maa zaa zo ka chɛ o, ka n ku ŋun’ naa maa kɔŋko,

english_verse: since he's the one you want to get rid of. Then I'll bring the whole nation back to you like a bride coming home to her husband. This way there won't be a civil war. Hushai Fools Absalom
translation_verse: ka zaŋ niriba maa zaa labina ti ti a kaman amiliya n-kul’ o yidan’ yili la. Ninvuɣ’ yino kɔŋko ka a bɔr’ ni a ku ka chɛ bɛnkam kpalim zaa ka bɛ suhu doya.”

english_verse: Absalom and all the leaders of the tribes of Israel agreed that Ahithophel had a good plan.
translation_verse: Ka o yɛtɔɣa maa daa paligi Absalom mini Izraɛl kpamba zaa suhuri.

english_verse: Then Absalom said, “Bring in Hushai the Archite. Let's hear what he has to say.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Absalom daa yɛli “Bolimiya Hushai ŋun nyɛ Ariki nir’ la gba na ka ti ti wum o mi ni mali shɛli ni o yɛli.”

english_verse: Hushai came in, and Absalom told him what Ahithophel had planned. Then Absalom said, “Should we do what he says? And if we shouldn't, can you come up with anything better?”
translation_verse: Ka Hushai daa kana, ka Absalom ti yɛl’ o, “Ahitɔfɛl ni yɛl’ ni ti niŋ shɛm m-bɔŋɔ, ti niŋm’ o ni yɛli shɛm maa? Di yi pa lala, nyin’ yɛlim’ ti.”

english_verse: Hushai said: This time Ahithophel's advice isn't so good.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Hushai daa yɛli Absalom, “Ahitɔfɛl ni yɛli shɛm pumpɔŋɔ ŋɔ din bi viɛla;”

english_verse: You know that your father and his followers are real warriors. Now they are as fierce as a mother bear whose cubs have just been killed. Besides, your father has a lot of experience in fighting wars, and he won't be spending the night with the others.
translation_verse: Ka Hushai lan yɛli yaha, “A mi ni a ba min’ o niriba maa nyɛla tɔbutuhiri’ biinsi, ka pumpɔŋɔ bɛ kul taami kaman bɛ ni yi gbaai jaŋgbimbil’ ka chɛ o ma mɔɣu ni ka o taai shɛm la, ka din pahi nyɛla, a ba mi tɔb’ tuhibu looloochi pam, o ku saɣi dɔni niriba maa sani yuŋ.

english_verse: He has probably already found a hiding place in a cave or somewhere else. As soon as anyone hears that some of your soldiers have been killed, everyone will think your whole army has been destroyed.
translation_verse: Nyama pumpɔŋɔ ŋ-ŋɔ o sɔɣi vol’ shɛl’ ni bee luɣ’ shɛli polo. Ka niriba maa shɛb’ yi chaŋ ti lir’ o tuuli liribu ŋɔ ka o ku ba, ŋunkam wum di yɛla ni yɛli ni bɛ ku Absalom niriba pam.

english_verse: Then even those who are as brave as a lion will lose their courage. All Israel knows what a great warrior your father is and what brave soldiers he has.
translation_verse: Di saha hal ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn mali suhukpeeni kaman gbuɣinli la suhuri ni fuŋ dabiɛm zuɣu, dama Izraɛlnim’ zaa mi ni a ba mali kpiɔŋ. Ka ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn zaa be o sani maa nyɛla bɛn mali suhukpeeni.

english_verse: My advice is to gather all the fighting men of Israel from the town of Dan in the north down to the town of Beersheba in the south. You will have more soldiers than there are grains of sand on the seashore. Absalom, you should lead them yourself,
translation_verse: Amaa man’ ni mali shɛli nyɛla, a chɛ ka Izraɛlnim’ zaa bɛn be Dan zaŋ hal ni Bɛrishiiba zaa laɣim a sanna kaman teeku noli bihigu la, ka a maŋmaŋ’ yina n-gari tooni zaŋ ba chaŋ.

english_verse: If they go into a walled town, we will put ropes around that town and drag it into the river. We won't leave even one small piece of a stone.
translation_verse: Ka di yi nyɛla o yila nimaani n-kpe fɔntin’ shɛli ni, di saha Izraɛlnim’ zaa ni bo gabisi yina nti vo tiŋ’ maa ti bahi zolɔŋni hal ka nir’ ti ku lan nya di kuɣibil’ nimaani gba.”

english_verse: Absalom and the others liked Hushai's plan better than Ahithophel's plan. This was because the Lord had decided to keep Ahithophel's plan from working and to cause trouble for Absalom. Jonathan and Ahimaaz Tell David the News
translation_verse: Ka Absalom mini Izraɛlnim’ zaa daa yɛli, “Hushai ŋun nyɛ Ariki nir’ ŋɔ ni yɛli shɛm ŋɔ ne nini gari Ahitɔfɛl ni yɛli shɛm la.” Dama Yawɛ daa zaliya ni Ahitɔfɛl ni yɛli shɛm maa di nya nasara, ka di chɛ ka ŋun’ Yawɛ chɛ ka zaɣ’ biɛɣu paai Absalom. Bɛ nyihi Naa Dauda ka o zo

english_verse: At once, Hushai went to Zadok and Abiathar. He told them what advice Ahithophel had given to Absalom and to the leaders of Israel. He also told them about the advice he had given.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Hushai daa yɛli Zadok mini Abiata bɛn daa nyɛ maligumaaniba la, “Ahitɔfɛl ni yɛli Absalom mini Izraɛl kpamba shɛm m-bɔŋɔ, ka m mi yɛli ba shɛm m-bɔŋɔ.

english_verse: Then he said, “Hurry! Send someone to warn David not to spend the night on this side of the Jordan. He must get across the river, so he and the others won't be wiped out!”
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ timmiya yomyom ka bɛ ti yɛli Dauda ni o di gbe kulibɔŋ duli maa yuŋ ŋɔ, amaa ni o chɛ ka o min’ o niriba maa tirisi tooni, di yi pa lala bɛ ni kpimsi ŋun’ naa mini niriba bɛn be o sani maa birili zaa.”

english_verse: Jonathan and Ahimaaz had been waiting at Rogel Spring because they did not want to be seen in Jerusalem. A servant girl went to the spring and gave them the message for David.
translation_verse: Di saha maa Abiata bia Jɔnatan mini Zadok bia Ahimaaz daa sɔɣila Ɛnrɔgɛl, ka bipuɣimbil’ so chani ti yɛri ba dinkam beni, ka bɛ mi zaŋdi li chani ti yɛri Naa Dauda, dama bɛ daa bi bɔr’ ni bɛ kpe tiŋ’ puuni ka so nya ba.

english_verse: But a young man saw them and went to tell Absalom. So Jonathan and Ahimaaz left and hurried to the house of a man who lived in Bahurim. Then they climbed down into a well in the courtyard.
translation_verse: Amaa ka bidibbil’ so daa ti nya ba ka chaŋ ti yɛli Absalom, ka bɛ niriba ayi maa zaa daa zo yomyom ti kpe Bahurim do’ so yiŋa, doo maa daa malila kɔbiliga o yiŋa ka bɛ siɣi di puuni.

english_verse: The man's wife put the cover on the well and poured grain on top of it, so the well could not be seen.
translation_verse: Ka yili maa ni paɣa daa zaŋ bini pa kɔbiliga maa noli n-yɛrigi chi diɛli di zuɣu, ka so daa bi baŋ ni shɛli be nimaani.

english_verse: Absalom's soldiers came to the woman and demanded, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” The woman answered, “They went across that stream.” The soldiers went off to look for the two men. But when they did not find the men, they went back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ka Absalom sapashinnim’ daa kana yili maa ni nti bɔhi paɣ’ maa, “Ahimaaz mini Jɔnatan be ya?” Ka paɣ’ maa garigi yɛli ba, “Bɛ du kulibɔŋ ŋɔ ha.” Ka bɛ lihilihi ka bi nya ba, ka labi Jɛrusalɛm.

english_verse: After the soldiers had gone, Jonathan and Ahimaaz climbed out of the well. They went to David and said, “Hurry! Get ready to cross the river!” Then they told him about Ahithophel's plan.
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa ŋmaligi chaŋ naai ka niriba maa yi kɔbiliga maa ni na n-chaŋ ti yɛli Naa Dauda, bɛ daa yɛl’ o mi, “Yiɣisim yomyom gbaai kulibɔŋ ŋɔ du, dama n-nyɛ Ahitɔfɛl ni wuhi yikombiɛlim shɛm zaŋ chaŋ a polo.”

english_verse: David and the others got ready and started crossing the Jordan River. By sunrise all of them were on the other side. Ahithophel Kills Himself
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda mini ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn zaa daa be o sani maa yiɣisi, zaŋ chaŋ biɛɣu ti yɛn neei la ka bɛ zaa gbaai Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili du, ka bɛ yino bi kpalim ka bi du.

english_verse: When Ahithophel saw that Absalom and the leaders of Israel were not going to follow his advice, he saddled his donkey and rode back to his home in Gilo. He told his family and servants what to do. Then he hanged himself, and they buried him in his family's burial place. Absalom Puts Amasa in Charge of the Army
translation_verse: Ahitɔfɛl ni daa nya ka bɛ bi deeg’ o yikombiɛlim soli maa, ka o dii pa o buŋ’ gali n-kul’ o ya nti malimal’ o yiŋ’ binshɛɣukam zali dɛde ka yil’ omaŋ’ mia kpi, ka bɛ daa zaŋ o sɔɣ’ o yaannim’ siliga ni.

english_verse: David went to the town of Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan River with the army of Israel.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Dauda daa paai Mahanaim. Ka Absalom mini Izraɛlnim’ zaa mi gbaai Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili du.

english_verse: Absalom put Amasa in Joab's place as commander of the army. Amasa's father was Ithra from the family of Ishmael, and his mother was Abigal, the daughter of Nahash and the sister of Joab's mother Zeruiah.
translation_verse: Absalom daa zaŋla Amasa leeg’ o tɔbbihi sapashin’ kpɛma n-zali Jɔab zaani. Amasa daa nyɛla do’ so ŋun yuli booni Itira, ka o nyɛ Ishimail zuliya ni nir’ la dapala. Itira maa daa kpuɣila Jɔab ma Zɛruya tizo Abigeel Nahash bipuɣiŋga.

english_verse: The Israelites under Absalom's command set up camp in the region of Gilead. Friends Bring Supplies to David
translation_verse: Ka Absalom mini Izraɛlnim’ daa dɔni sansani Giliad tiŋgban’ ni.

english_verse: After David came to the town of Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash came from Rabbah in Ammon, Machir the son of Ammiel came from Lo-Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite came from Rogelim.
translation_verse: Dauda min’ o niriba maa ni daa mali ti paai Mahanaim, ka Nahash bia Shɔbi ŋun daa yi Raba din be Ammɔn tiŋgban’ ni la na mini Makiri Amiɛl bia ŋun daa yi Lɔdɛba na la ni Barizillai ŋun daa nyɛ Giliad nira ka yi Rɔgɛlim na la

english_verse: Here is a list of what they brought: sleeping mats, blankets, bowls, pottery jars, wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, honey, yogurt, sheep, and cheese. They brought the food for David and the others because they knew that everyone would be hungry, tired, and thirsty from being out in the desert.
translation_verse: m-pahi shiri mini bihikpam ni piɛri ni waagasi zuɣu na nti ti Dauda mini ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn daa be o sani maa ni bɛ di, dama bɛ daa yɛlimi, “Ŋ-ŋɔ kum mini kɔnyuri wum niriba maa ka bɛ tarigi yɔɣu maa ni.”

english_verse: He sent out one third of his army under the command of Joab, another third under the command of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, and the rest under the command of Ittai from Gath. He told the soldiers, “I'm going into battle with you.”
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa piri tɔbbihi maa ʒii buta zuɣu, ka chɛ ka Jɔab su yim zuɣu, ka Abishai Zɛruya bia ŋun daa nyɛ Jɔab tizo la su yim zuɣu, ka Itai Gaat nir’ la mi daa su bɛn kpalim la. Ka naa daa yɛli niriba maa, “Mmaŋmaŋ’ gba ni yina pahi yi zuɣu ka ti chaŋ.”

english_verse: But the soldiers said, “No, don't go into battle with us! It won't matter to our enemies if they make us all run away, or even if they kill half of us. But you are worth
translation_verse: Amaa ka niriba maa daa yɛl’ o, “Di bi simdi ni a dol’ ti chaŋ. Dama tinim’ yi ŋmaligi guui bɛ baɣa ku be ti ni, ka ti pirigili yi kpi, bɛ baɣa ku be ti ni, a kɔŋko saɣi ti niriba tuhi’ pia, dinzuɣu di simdi ka a kpalim yiŋ’ ŋɔ, ka lee tir’ ti sɔŋsim na.”

english_verse: and one of them went and told Joab, “I saw Absalom hanging in a tree!”
translation_verse: Ka do’ so daa nya o ka yɛli Jɔab, “Nyama, n nyala Absalom ka o yili oki tia zuɣu.”

english_verse: David said, “All right, if you think I should.” Then in a voice loud enough for everyone to hear, he said, “Joab! Abishai! Ittai! For my sake, be sure that Absalom comes back unharmed.” David stood beside the town gate as his army marched past in groups of
translation_verse: Di saha ka tɔbbihi maa daa yi n-kpe yɔɣu ni bɛ ti tuhi Izraɛlnima. Bɛ daa tuhi tab’ la Ifriim tiŋgban’ ni yɔɣu sunsuuni.

english_verse: Battles were being fought all over the forest, and David's soldiers were winning. Twenty thousand soldiers were killed that day, and more of them died from the dangers of the forest than from the fighting itself.
translation_verse: Ka bɛn kpalim daa wurim kpe yɔɣu ʒiizaa, ka bɛ doli ba, ka bɛn daa kpi yɔɣu maa ni daa gari bɛ ni zaŋ takɔbiri ku shɛba.

english_verse: Absalom was riding his mule under a huge tree when his head caught in the branches. The mule ran off and left Absalom hanging in midair. Some of David's soldiers happened by,
translation_verse: Ka Dauda tɔbbihi maa daa chirigi Absalom ka o ba o buntaaŋa zɔra, ka buntaaŋa maa daa ti yɛn zaŋ o gari oki ti’ titali gbini, ka o zuɣu kpe n-shɛbisi oki tia maa wula ni ka o yili zuɣusaa, ka buntaaŋa maa zo ka chɛ o ka o kpalim yiliya.

english_verse: Joab said, “You saw Absalom? Why didn't you kill him? I would have given you ten pieces of silver and a special belt.”
translation_verse: Ka Jɔab daa bɔhi ninvuɣ’ so ŋun daa yɛl’ o maa, “A shiri nya o? Ka bɔ n-niŋ ka a di bi chɛ o sua luhi tiŋ’ na nimaani? N suhu naan paligi ka n ti a anzinfa laɣibaligu pia mini gbaŋ din lɔr’ sheeni.”

english_verse: He always finds out what's going on. I would have been risking my life to kill Absalom, because you would have let me take the blame.”
translation_verse: Ka di yi di nyɛla n niŋ o la zaɣ’ biɛɣu ka binshɛli mi bi sɔɣiri naa sani, di saha a ku zani n nyaaŋa.”

english_verse: Joab said, “I'm not going to waste any more time on you!” Absalom was still alive, so Joab took three spears and stuck them through Absalom's chest.
translation_verse: Ka Jɔab daa yɛl’ o, “Man’ bi lan yɛn ku saha a sani yaha,” ka daa dii zaŋ kpana ata chaŋ ti kuhi Absalom suhu dɛde saha shɛl’ o ni daa na ne n-yili oki tia maa zuɣu maa.

english_verse: Ten of Joab's bodyguards came over and finished him off.
translation_verse: Ka nachimba pia bɛn daa nyɛ Jɔab gbaɣino ʒiriba daa laɣim gili Absalom m-bahi jɛh’ o.

english_verse: Then Joab blew a trumpet to signal his troops to stop chasing Israel's soldiers.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Jɔab daa piɛbi kikaa n-gooi tɔbbihi maa ka bɛ daa chɛ Izraɛlnim’ maa kari doli ka labina.

english_verse: They threw Absalom's body into a deep pit in the forest and put a big pile of rocks over it. Meanwhile, the people of Israel had all run back to their own homes.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa zaŋ Absalom ti bahi bɔɣ’ zilinli ni mɔɣu maa ni, ka kahi kuɣa na ti pa o zuɣu, ka di du pam. Ka Izraɛlnim’ maa zaa yinoyino daa zo n-kul’ o yiŋa.

english_verse: When Absalom was alive, he had set up a stone monument for himself in King's Valley. He explained, “I don't have any sons to keep my name alive.” He called it Absalom's Monument, and that is the name it still has today. Ahimaaz Wants To Tell David
translation_verse: Absalom ni daa na be o nyɛvili ni, o daa mɛla binwɔɣinli zali nayili vinvamli ni ni bɛ ti mal’ li teer’ o yɛla, dama o daa yɛlimi, “N ka bidibiga ŋun ni ti chɛ ka n yuli ku kpi,” Ka o daa zaŋ o yuli boli bini maa. Ka hal ni zuŋɔ bɛ na kul boonila binwɔɣinli maa Absalom binwɔɣinli. Bɛ garigi Naa Dauda Absalom kuli

english_verse: Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, “Joab, let me run and tell King David that the Lord has rescued him from his enemies.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Zadok bia Ahimaaz daa yɛli, “Chɛ ka man’ guui kuli nti ti naa lahibali ni Yawɛ fa o o dimnim’ nuu ni bahi.”

english_verse: Joab answered, “You're not the one to tell the king that his son is dead. You can take him a message some other time, but not today.”
translation_verse: Ka Jɔab daa yɛl’ o, “Pa nyini n-yɛn ʒi lahibali maa kuli zuŋɔ, dahin’ shɛli ka a ni ti ʒi lahibali maa kuli, amaa zuŋɔ dina a ku ʒi lahibali maa kuli, dama nabia maa kpiya.”

english_verse: Someone from Ethiopia was standing there, and Joab told him, “Go and tell the king what you have seen.” The man knelt down in front of Joab, then got up and started running.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Jɔab daa yɛli Kushi nir’ ŋun daa be o san’ la, “Cham’ ti yɛli naa a nini ni nya shɛm.” Ka Kush nir’ maa daa zaŋ o zuɣu silim tiŋ’ Jɔab tooni lu o sizuura ka ŋmaligi guui.

english_verse: Ahimaaz spoke to Joab again, “No matter what happens, I still want to go. And besides, the Ethiopian has already left.” Joab said, “Why should you go? You won't get a reward for the news you have!”
translation_verse: Ka Zadok bia Ahimaaz daa lan yɛli, “Di yi kul nyɛ shɛlikam, nyin’ chɛ ka n gba zo n-doli Kush nir’ maa nyaaŋa.” Ka Jɔab yɛl’ o, “M bia, bɔzuɣu ka a lee bɔr’ ni a zo n-kuli nti ti lahibal’ maa, dama a mi ni a bi yɛn nya shɛli di zuɣu?”

english_verse: “I'll run no matter what!” Ahimaaz insisted. “All right then, run!” Joab said. Ahimaaz took the road through the Jordan Valley and outran the Ethiopian.
translation_verse: Ka Ahimaaz daa lan yɛli, “Di yi kul nyɛ shɛlikam, man’ ni zo n-kuli.” Ka Jɔab daa yɛl’ o, “Zom’ kuli.” Di saha ka Ahimaaz daa ŋmaligi guui n-zo n-doli bɔpiɛligu polo nti gari Kush nir’ maa zuɣu.

english_verse: Meanwhile, David was sitting between the inner and outer gates in the city wall. One of his soldiers was watching from the roof of the gate-tower. He saw a man running toward the town
translation_verse: Di saha maa Dauda daa ʒila tiŋ’ maa dunoya ayi sunsuuni, ka tiŋgula daa ti du n-tam dunɔdali dufahirili zuɣusaa n-lihi ha nya do’ so ni zɔrina o kɔŋko.

english_verse: and shouted down to tell David. David answered, “If he's alone, he must have some news.” The runner was getting closer,
translation_verse: Ka tiŋgul’ maa daa boli naa n-yɛl’ o. Ka naa daa yɛli, “Di yi nyɛ o kɔŋko n-zɔrina maa dindina o ʒirila lahibali na.” Ka o daa ti zo m-mirina.

english_verse: when the soldier saw someone else running. He shouted down to the gate, “Look! There's another runner!” David said, “He must have some news too.”
translation_verse: Ka tiŋgul’ maa daa lan nya ka do’ so zɔrina ka o boli dunɔgula n-yɛl’ o, “Nyama, do’ so lan zɔrina o kɔŋko.” Ka naa yɛli, o gba ʒirila lahibali na.

english_verse: The soldier on the roof shouted, “The first one runs just like Ahimaaz the son of Zadok.” This time David said, “He's a good man. He must have some good news.”
translation_verse: Ka tiŋgul’ maa daa yɛli, “Ŋun be tooni zɔrina maa ŋmanila Zadok bia Ahimaaz.” Ka naa daa yɛli, “O nyɛla ninvuɣ’ suŋ, dinzuɣu lahibali suŋ ka o ʒirina maa.”

english_verse: Ahimaaz called out, “We won! We won!” Then he bowed low to David and said, “Your Majesty, praise the Lord your God! He has given you victory over your enemies.”
translation_verse: Ka Ahimaaz daa ti paana yɛli naa, “Bɛ zaa mal’ alaafee,” Ka silim o zuɣu n-zaŋ o nini kpa tiŋa ka yɛli, “Naa, Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ a Naawuni ŋun zaŋ ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn je nyini n dan’ naa niŋ ti nuu ni ŋɔ simdi paɣibu.”

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. Ahimaaz said, “When Joab sent your personal servant and me, I saw a noisy crowd. But I don't know what it was all about.”
translation_verse: Ka naa daa bɔhi, “Nachimbil’ Absalom mal’ alaafee?” Ka Ahimaaz daa garigi yɛl’ o, “Jɔab ni di tim ma saha shɛli na maa, n di nya zama ni laɣim yo vuri, amaa n di bi baŋ di ni nyɛ shɛli.”

english_verse: David told him, “Stand over there and wait.” Ahimaaz went over and stood there.
translation_verse: Ka naa yɛl’ o, “Ŋmaligim’ zani kpaŋ’ kpe.” Ka o daa ŋmaligi zani kpaŋa.

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. The Ethiopian replied, “I wish that all Your Majesty's enemies and everyone who tries to harm you would end up like him!” David Cries for Absalom
translation_verse: Ka naa daa bɔh’ o, “Ka daɣila nachimbil’ Absalom mal’ alaafee?” Ka Kush nir’ maa daa garigi yɛl’ o, “Naawuni chɛ ka din niŋ nachimbil’ maa niŋ nyini n dan’ naa dimnim’ mini ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn zaa yiɣisi wuɣil’ a zuɣu ni bɛ niŋ a zaɣ’ biɛɣu la.”

english_verse: David started trembling. Then he went up to the room above the city gate to cry. As he went, he kept saying, “My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! I wish I could have died instead of you! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Ka naa suhu daa saɣim pam, ka o yiɣisi kpɛri dunoli maa zuɣusaa duu puuni ka kumda. O ni daa chani ni o ti kpe maa o daa yɛrimi, “Mbaye, m bia Absalom, m bia, m bia Absalom! Mani n-yi di kpi ka chɛ a ŋɔ, di di so. Mbaye, Absalom. M bia, m bia!”

english_verse: Someone told Joab, “The king is crying because Absalom is dead.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yɛli Jɔab, “Nyama, naa kumdimi ka fabindi Absalom zuɣu.”

english_verse: David's army found out he was crying because his son had died, and their day of victory suddenly turned into a day of sadness.
translation_verse: Ka dindali maa nasara dibu suhupiɛlli maa daa leela suhugarigu dabisili Naa Dauda tɔbbihi maa sani; dama bɛ daa wumya ni naa kumdila o bia maa kuli.

english_verse: The troops were sneaking into Mahanaim, just as if they had run away from a battle and were ashamed.
translation_verse: Ka tɔbbihi maa daa chaŋ na sɔasɔa ti kpe tiŋ’ maa puuni dindali maa kaman tɔbbi’ shɛb’ bɛn ŋmaligi guui tɔbu ni n-kuli ti kpɛri bɛ ya ni vi la.

english_verse: David covered his face with his hands and kept on crying loudly, “My son, Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Ka naa daa zaŋ bini pɔb’ o ninni ka kuhiri pampam yɛra, Mbaye m bia Absalom, mbaye Absalom, m bia, m bia!

english_verse: Joab went to the house where David was staying and told him: You've made your soldiers ashamed! Not only did they save your life, they saved your sons and daughters and wives as well.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Jɔab daa kpe nayili maa nti yɛli naa, “Zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ, a dihi a tɔbbihi bɛn zaa tilig’ a nyɛvili ka tilig’ a bidibisi min’ a bipuɣinsi ni a paɣiba ni a mamanim’ zaa nyɛviya ŋɔ vi,

english_verse: You're more loyal to your enemies than to your friends. What you've done today has shown your officers and soldiers that they don't mean a thing to you. You would be happy if Absalom was still alive, even if the rest of us were dead.
translation_verse: dama a yurila ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn je a, ka je ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn yur’ a. Zuŋɔ a kahigi wuhi ni sapashin’ kpamba mini tɔbbihi pa shɛli a sani. Zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ m baŋya ni Absalom yi di ne ka tinim’ zaa kpi, a naam paɣ’ lala.

english_verse: Now get up! Go out there and thank them for what they did. If you don't, I swear by the Lord that you won't even have one man left on your side tomorrow morning. You may have had a lot of troubles in the past, but this will be the worst thing that has ever happened to you!
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ yiɣisima n-chaŋ ti tɔɣisi tɔbbihi maa suhumahili yɛtɔɣa; dama m po Yawɛ, a yi bi chaŋ, so ku kpalim’ a sani yuŋ ŋɔ, ka dimbɔŋɔ maa ni bie n-gari zaɣ’ biɛ’ shɛŋa din pun niŋ a a nachimbilim ni zaŋ na hal ni pɔŋɔ!”

english_verse: David got up and went to the town gate and sat down. When the people heard that he was sitting there, they came to see him. Israel and Judah Want David Back After Israel's soldiers had all returned home,
translation_verse: Di saha ka naa daa yiɣisi chaŋ ti ʒin’ o ʒiishee dunɔdali gbini. Ka bɛ daa yɛli niriba maa, “Nyamiya, naa ʒin’ o ʒiishee dunɔdal’ la gbini. Ka bɛ zaa daa ka naa tooni na. Naa Dauda lab’ Jɛrusalɛm Di saha maa Izraɛlnim’ zaa yinoyino daa pun zomi kuli bɛ yinsi.

english_verse: everyone in Israel started arguing. They were saying to each other, “King David rescued us from the Philistines and from our other enemies. But then we chose Absalom to be our new leader, and David had to leave the country to get away. Absalom died in battle, so why hasn't something been done to bring David back?”
translation_verse: Amaa ti ni daa zaŋ Absalom so leei ti naa maa kpi tɔb’ ni. Ka pumpɔŋɔ bɔ n-niŋ ka yi bi yɛli shɛli zaŋ chaŋ naa maa zaŋbuna polo?”

english_verse: When David found out what they were saying, he sent a message to Zadok and Abiathar the priests. It said: Say to the leaders of Judah, “Why are you the last tribe to think about bringing King David back home?
translation_verse: Ka Naa Dauda daa tim ti yɛli Zadok mini Abiata bɛn daa nyɛ maligumaaniba la, “Bɔhimiya Juda kpamba, ‘Bɔzuɣu ka yinim’ nyɛ bɛn ti yɛn bahindi nyaaŋa naa zaŋ kulis’ o yiŋa, hal ka Izraɛlnim’ zaa yɛtɔɣa ti paai man’ naa?

english_verse: He is your brother, your own relative! Why haven't you done anything to bring him back?”
translation_verse: Yinima n-nyɛ n dɔɣiriba, yi nyɛla n niŋgbuŋ mini n ʒim, ka bɔ n-niŋ ka yinim’ ti yɛn bahindi nyaaŋa n-zaŋ man’ naa labisi?”

english_verse: And tell Amasa, “You're my nephew, and with God as a witness, I swear I'll make you commander of my army instead of Joab.”
translation_verse: Yɛlimiya Amasa, ‘A nyɛla n niŋgbuŋ mini n ʒim, zuŋɔ zaŋ chana, n yi bi zaŋ a leei n tɔbbihi sapashin’ kpɛma n-zali Jɔab zaani, Naawuni ŋun niŋmi ma zaɣ’ biɛɣu, hal ŋun niŋmi ma zaɣ’ biɛɣu pam gba.’ ”

english_verse: Soon the tribe of Judah again became followers of David, and they sent him this message: “Come back, and bring your soldiers with you.” David Starts Back for Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ka Amasa daa zaŋ Judanim’ maa zaa suhuri laɣim taba ka bɛ be kaman ninvuɣ’ yino la, ka daa tim ti yɛli Naa “A min’ a kpamba zaa labimina.”

english_verse: Shimei the son of Gera was there with them. He had hurried from Bahurim to meet David. Shimei was from the tribe of Benjamin, and
translation_verse: Ka Gɛra bia Shimɛi ŋun daa nyɛ Bɛnjamin zuliya ni nir’ la daa yi Bahurim kana yomyom ti pahi Judanim’ maa zuɣu ni bɛ tuhi Naa Dauda soli.

english_verse: I know I was wrong. That's why I wanted to be the first one from the northern tribes to meet you.”
translation_verse: Dama nyama, mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ mi ni n daa tum taali, dinzuɣu ka mani n-nyɛ ŋun daŋ yi Yisifu zuliya ni kana ni n ti tuhi nyini n dan’ naa soli maa.”

english_verse: Then they brought David's family and servants back across the river, and they did everything he wanted them to do. Shimei Meets with David Shimei crossed the Jordan River and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa du mɔɣili maa ni bɛ ti zaŋ naa malibu duhi na, ka niŋ o ni bɔri shɛm. Naa Dauda niŋ Shimɛi nirilim Naa ni daa ti yɛn du mɔɣili maa saha shɛli, ka Shimɛi Gɛra bia maa daa kana ti damdi naa tooni,

english_verse: He said, “Your Majesty, I beg you not to punish me! Please, forget what I did when you were leaving Jerusalem. Don't even think about it.
translation_verse: ka yɛl’ o, “N dana, di zaŋ man’ ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ taali bee n-lan teei n ni daa tum gala shɛm dahin’ shɛli nyini n dan’ ni daa yi Jɛrusalɛm n-zɔrila yɛla. Naa, di zaŋ li niŋ a suhu ni.

english_verse: But Abishai shouted, “You should be killed for cursing the Lord's chosen king!”
translation_verse: Ka Abishai Zɛruya bia la daa yɛli, “Di simdi ni ti ku Shimɛi o ni daa tu Yawɛ ninvuɣ’ gahindili ŋɔ zuɣu.”

english_verse: David said, “Abishai, what will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? Is it your job to tell me who has done wrong? I've been made king of all Israel today, and no one will be put to death!”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Dauda daa yɛli, “Wula ka n yɛn niŋ yinim’ Zɛruya bihi bɛn be kaman yi leela n dimnim’ zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ? Di simdi ni ti ku nira Izraɛl tiŋgban’ ni zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ? Pa mani n-nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ naa zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ?

english_verse: Then David promised Shimei that he would not be killed. Mephibosheth Meets with David
translation_verse: Ka naa daa po pɔri yɛli Shimɛi, A ku kpi.” Naa Dauda niŋ Mɛfibɔshɛt nirilim

english_verse: Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul, also came to meet David. He had missed David so much that he had not taken a bath or trimmed his beard or washed his clothes the whole time David was gone. David asked him, “Why didn't you go with me?”
translation_verse: O ni daa yi Jɛrusalɛm kana ni o ti tuhi Naa Dauda soli maa, ka naa bɔh’ o, “Mɛfibɔshɛt, bɔzuɣu ka a daa bi doli ma chaŋ?”

english_verse: He answered, “Your Majesty, you know I can't walk. I told my servant to saddle a donkey for me so I could go with you. But my servant left without me, and
translation_verse: Ka o garigi yɛli, “N dan’ naa, n tumtumda n-daa yɔhim’ ma, man’ ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ daa yɛl’ o mi, ‘Pam’ m buŋ’ ŋɔ gali ti ma ka m ba n-doli naa chaŋ,’ dama a mi ni mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ nyɛla wɔbiga.

english_verse: then he lied about me. You're as wise as an angel of God, so do what you think is right.
translation_verse: Ka o daa yi n nyaaŋa n-kana ti ŋma ʒiri pa ma nyini n dan’ naa sani. Amaa nyini n dan’ naa ŋmanila Naawuni malaika, dinzuɣu niŋm’ a ni nya ka shɛli viɛl’ a sani.

english_verse: After all, you could have killed my whole family and me. But instead, you let me eat at your own table. Your Majesty, what more could I ask?”
translation_verse: Dama di daa simdi ni nyini n dan’ naa ku m ba daŋ niriba zaa, amaa ka a daa zaŋ mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ m-pah’ a mini ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn laɣindi diri zuɣu. N lan malila n ni yɛn niŋ shɛm n-naɣ’ pahila n kum niŋ nyin’ naa?”

english_verse: David answered, “You've said enough! I've decided to divide the property between you and Ziba.”
translation_verse: Ka naa daa yɛl’ o, “Di lan yɛli shɛli zaŋ chaŋ amaŋmaŋ’ polo yaha. M pun zali ni a mini Ziba pirigim’ tiŋgbani maa ti taba.”

english_verse: Mephibosheth replied, “He can have it all! I'm just glad you've come home safely.” Barzillai Returns Home
translation_verse: Ka Mɛfibɔshɛt daa yɛli naa, “Nyini n dan’ naa ni kul lab’ yiŋ’ na ni alaafee ŋɔ, chɛ ka o zaŋ di zaa.” Naa Dauda niŋ Barizillai nirilim

english_verse: Barzillai came from Rogelim in Gilead to meet David at the Jordan River and go across with him.
translation_verse: Ka Barizillai ŋun daa nyɛ Giliad nir’ la daa yi Rɔgɛlim n-chaŋ naa sani Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili maa ni ni o ti doli naa du Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili maa.

english_verse: David said to him, “Cross the river and go to Jerusalem with me. I will take care of you.”
translation_verse: Ka Naa Dauda daa yɛl’ o, “Doli ma kuli Jɛrusalɛm ka n ti gbib’ a.”

english_verse: Barzillai answered: Your Majesty, why should I go to Jerusalem? I don't have much longer to live.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Barizillai daa yɛli, “Yuma ala ka n lee lan yɛn niŋ dunia yili ŋɔ, ka lan doli nyin’ naa kuni Jɛrusalɛm?

english_verse: I'll cross the river with you, but I'll only go a little way on the other side. You don't have to be so kind to me.
translation_verse: Man’ a dabili ŋɔ kul ni dolila nyini naa du Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili ŋɔ n-chaŋ biɛla ha. Bɔzuɣu ka nyini naa ti yɛn yo ma san’ titali ŋɔ?

english_verse: Just let me return to my hometown, where I can someday be buried near my father and mother. My servant Chimham can go with you, and you can treat him as your own.
translation_verse: Jaande chɛ ka n labi n ya ti kpi ka bɛ sɔɣi ma baɣili m ba mini m ma gbala. Amaa a dabili Chimham m-bɔŋɔ, chɛ ka o doli nyini n dan’ naa kuli ka a ti niŋ o a ni nya ka shɛli viɛl’ a sani.”

english_verse: David said, “I'll take Chimham with me, and whatever you ask me to do for him, I'll do. And if there's anything else you want, I'll also do that.”
translation_verse: Ka naa daa yɛli, “Chimham ni doli ma kuli ka n ti niŋ o a ni nya ka shɛli viɛl’ a sani, ka a suhu ni kul yu ni n niŋ shɛlikam zaa, n ni niŋ li ti a.”

english_verse: David's soldiers went on across the river, while he stayed behind to tell Barzillai goodbye and to wish him well. Barzillai returned home, but
translation_verse: Di saha ka naa daa mɔɣisi Barizillai kpariŋ, ka suhi alibarika niŋ o ni, ka Barizillai daa labi kul’ o yiŋa, ka naa mini niriba maa zaa daa gbaai Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili maa du. Judanim’ mini Izraɛlnim’ ŋme tab’ naŋgbankpeeni zaŋ chaŋ naa polo

english_verse: Chimham crossed the river with David. Israel and Judah Argue All of Judah's army and half of Israel's army were there to help David cross the river.
translation_verse: Ka naa daa chaŋ Giligal, ka Chimham daa dol’ o chaŋ; ka Judanim’ zaa mini Izraɛlnim’ pirigili gba daa zaŋ naa lu soli.

english_verse: The soldiers from Israel came to him and said, “Why did our relatives from Judah secretly take you and your family and your soldiers across the Jordan?”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Izraɛlnim’ zaa daa kana ti bɔhi naa, “Wula ka ti mabihi Judanim’ ŋɔ lee sɔɣi zaŋ a min’ a malibu ni a niriba ŋɔ zaa baai du Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili na?”

english_verse: The people of Judah answered, “Why are you so angry? We are the king's relatives. He didn't give us any food, and we didn't take anything for ourselves!”
translation_verse: Ka Judanim’ maa zaa daa garigi yɛli Izraɛlnim’ maa, “Naa ni nyɛ ti daŋ ni nir’ zuɣu. Ka wula ka yi suhuri yiɣisi yɛlli ŋɔ zuɣu? Yi nya ka ti dila naa binshɛli? Bee o ti ti la pini?”

english_verse: Those from Israel said, “King David belongs to us ten times more than he belongs to you. Why didn't you think we were good enough to help you? After all, we were the first ones to think of bringing him back!” The people of Judah argued more strongly than the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ maa daa garigi yɛli Judanim’ maa, “Ti mali soli zaŋ chaŋ naa sani ʒii bupia zuɣu gari ya, hal Dauda sani gba, ti mali soli gari ya. Ka wula ka yi yuli ʒiɛm ti? Pa tinima n-daa daŋ yɛli ti naa maa zaŋbuna yɛla?” Amaa ka Judanim’ daa zaŋ suhuyiɣisili tahi nyaŋ Izraɛlnim’ maa.

english_verse: A troublemaker from the tribe of Benjamin was there. His name was Sheba the son of Bichri, and he blew a trumpet to get everyone's attention. Then he said, “People of Israel, David the son of Jesse doesn't belong to us! Let's go home.”
translation_verse: Di saha maa ka ninvuɣ’ galiŋ so daa beni ka o yuli booni Shiiba, o daa nyɛla Bikiri bia, ka yi Bɛnjamin zuliya ni na. Ŋuna n-daa zaŋ kikaa piɛbi ka yɛli, “Ti nuu ka Dauda nam maa yɛla ni, ti pala bɛn diri Jɛsi bia maa fali, dinzuɣu Izraɛlnima, sokam kulim’ o yiŋa.”

english_verse: So they stopped following David and went off with Sheba. But the people of Judah stayed close to David all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem. David's Ten Wives
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ maa zaa daa zo Dauda sani n-chaŋ ti doli Shiiba Bikiri bia maa, amaa ka Judanim’ daa doli bɛ naa maa ni ʒiɛyimtali n-yi Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili maa ni kuli Jɛrusalɛm.

english_verse: David had left ten of his wives in Jerusalem to take care of his palace. But when he came back, he had them taken to another house, and he placed soldiers there to guard them. He gave them whatever they needed, but he never slept with any of them again. They had to live there for the rest of their lives as if they were widows. The Army Goes after Sheba
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa ti paag’ o yiŋ’ Jɛrusalɛm n-yih’ o mamanim’ pia shɛb’ o ni daa chɛ n-niŋ nayili maa ni bɛ maani li la n-zaŋ ba ti niŋ yili shɛl’ ni, ka chɛ ka bɛ guli ba, ka o dihiri ba ka sooni ba, amaa o daa bi lan chɛ ka o mini ba dɔni yaha. Dinzuɣu bɛ daa kul bela yili maa ni kaman pakoya la hal ni bɛ nyɛviya tariga.

english_verse: David said to Amasa, “Three days from now I want you and all of Judah's army to be here!”
translation_verse: Ka naa daa yɛli Amasa, “Cham’ ti boli Judanim’ zaa ka bɛ laɣim n sanna daba ata sunsuuni, ka a gba beni pahi.”

english_verse: Amasa started bringing the army together, but it was taking him more than three days.
translation_verse: Ka Amasa daa yi n-chaŋ ni o ti boli Judanim’ maa na, amaa ka o daa yuui hal ka bɛ ni daa zal’ o dabisi shɛli maa ti gari.

english_verse: So David said to Abishai, “Sheba will hurt us more than Absalom ever did. Take my best soldiers and go after him. We don't want him to take over any walled cities and get away from us.” Joab Kills Amasa
translation_verse: Ka Dauda daa yɛli Abishai, “Pumpɔŋɔ Shiiba Bikiri bia ŋɔ ni niŋ ti barina pam n-gari Absalom ni daa niŋ ti shɛm la, dinzuɣu zaŋm’ a dan’ tɔbbihi ŋɔ m-biɛh’ o naba, di yi pa lala o ni ti kpe tiŋ’ shɛŋa bɛ ni me goondahi gili ni, ka muɣisi ti.”

english_verse: Abishai left Jerusalem to try and capture Sheba. He took along Joab and his soldiers, as well as David's bodyguard and best troops.
translation_verse: Ka Jɔab mini Chɛrɛtinim’ ni Pɛlɛtinim’ ni wɔɣira zaa daa pahi Abishai zuɣu ka bɛ yi Jɛrusalɛm chaŋ ni bɛ ti biɛhi Bikiri bia Shiiba maa naba.

english_verse: They had gone as far as the big rock at Gibeon when Amasa caught up with them. Joab had a dagger strapped around his waist over his military uniform, but it fell out as he started toward Amasa.
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa ti paai kuɣ’ titali din daa do Gibiɔn la gbini, ka Amasa daa tuhi ba soli nimaani, di saha maa Jɔab daa yɛla tɔbutuhiri’ nɛma, ka takɔbi daa su di tɔɣu ni ka o zaŋ li nyaɣi pa o nɛma maa zuɣu n-gbaai li lo o shee ni. O ni daa gari zani tooni ka takɔbi maa ŋooi yina.

english_verse: Joab said, “Amasa, my cousin, how are you?” Then Joab took hold of Amasa's beard with his right hand, so that he could greet him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Ka Jɔab daa bɔhi Amasa, “M mabia, a mal’ alaafee?” Ka daa zaŋ o nudirigu gbaai Amasa teeŋa n-niŋ kaman o yɛn mɔɣisila o kpariŋ la.

english_verse: Amasa did not see the dagger in Joab's other hand. Joab stuck it in Amasa's stomach, and his insides spilled out on the ground. Joab only struck him once, but Amasa was dying. Joab and his brother Abishai went off to chase Sheba.
translation_verse: Amaa Amasa daa bi nya takɔbi maa Jɔab nuu ni, di saha ka Jɔab zaŋ takɔbi maa kuh’ o pul’ ni, ka o nyɔri daa yina ka o kpi. O daa bi lan kuh’ o pahi buyi. Di saha ka Jɔab min’ o mabia Abishai daa lan gbaai Bikiri bia Shiiba la naba biɛhibu.

english_verse: One of Joab's soldiers stood by Amasa and shouted, “If any of you are for Joab and David, then follow Joab!”
translation_verse: Ka Jɔab niriba maa ni yino daa chaŋ ti zani Amasa sani ka yɛli, “Ŋunkam bɔr’ Jɔab ka nyɛ ŋun be Naa Dauda polo, ŋun’ doli Jɔab.”

english_verse: Amasa was still rolling in his own blood in the middle of the road. The soldier who had shouted noticed that everyone who passed by would stop, so he dragged Amasa off the road and covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Ka Amasa daa kpi n-do o ʒim ni solɔɣu maa zuɣu. Ka ŋunkam daa yi kana ti nya o, dilan’ kpalindimi zani. Ka doo maa ni daa nya ka niriba kanna ti kpalindi zaani maa, ka o daa vuui Amasa solɔɣu maa zuɣu nti sɔŋ mɔri ni, ka zaŋ binyɛrigu pa o zuɣu.

english_verse: After this, no one else stopped. They all walked straight past him on their way to help Joab capture Sheba. Sheba Hides Out in the Town of Abel
translation_verse: O ni daa vuui Amasa niŋgbuŋ solɔɣu maa zuɣu maa nyaaŋa ka niriba maa daa naanyi doli Jɔab n-lan gbaai Bikiri bia Shiiba la naba biɛhibu.

english_verse: Sheba had gone through all of the tribes of Israel when he came to the town of Abel Beth-Maacah. All of his best soldiers met him there and followed him into the town.
translation_verse: Ka Shiiba daa chaŋ yaɣi Izraɛl tinsi zaa zuɣu n-chaŋ ti kpe Ɛbɛl fɔŋ din be Bɛtimaaka la ni. Ka Bikiri daŋ ni niriba zaa daa laɣim dol’ o kpe tiŋ’ maa ni.

english_verse: Joab and his troops came and surrounded Abel, so that no one could go in or come out. They made a dirt ramp up to the town wall and then started to use a battering ram to knock the wall down. A Wise Woman Saves the Town
translation_verse: Ka Jɔab min’ o niriba zaa daa kana ti teei gili Ɛbɛl Bɛtimaaka n-kɔri taŋkpaɣu duhiduhi gili tiŋ’ maa ka di du nti saɣisi di gooni zuɣusaa, ka gbiri di gbinni ni bɛ daai li luhi.

english_verse: A wise woman shouted from the top of the wall, “Listen to me! Listen to me! I have to talk to Joab! Tell him to come here!”
translation_verse: Di saha ka paɣ’ yɛndaan’ so daa be tiŋ’ maa ni ka kuhi yɛl’ ba na, “Wummiya! Wummiya! Yɛlimiya Jɔab ni o kana ka n ti yɛl’ o yɛtɔɣ’ shɛli.”

english_verse: When he came, the woman said, “Are you Joab?” “Yes, I am,” he answered. She said, “Please, listen to what I have to say.” “All right,” he said. “I'll listen.”
translation_verse: Ka Jɔab daa chaŋ o sani, ka paɣ’ maa ti bɔh’ o, “Nyini n-nyɛ Jɔab maa?” Ka Jɔab saɣi, “Iin mani.” Ka paɣ’ maa yɛl’ o, “Wummi mani ŋun nyɛ a dabipaɣ’ ŋɔ ni yɛn yɛl’ a shɛm ŋɔ.” Ka Jɔab yɛl’ o, “N wumda.”

english_verse: She said, “Long ago people used to say, ‘If you want good advice, go to the town of Abel to get it.’ The answers they got here were all that was needed to settle any problem.
translation_verse: Di saha ka paɣ’ maa daa yɛl’ o, “Kurimbuni ha bɛ daa yi yɛrila niriba, ‘Chamiya Ɛbɛl n-ti bɔhi ka bɛ wuhi ya.’ Lala ka bɛ daa yi niŋdi maani yɛla.

english_verse: We are Israelites, and we want peace! You can trust us. Why are you trying to destroy a town that's like a mother in Israel? Why do you want to wipe out the Lord's people?”
translation_verse: N nyɛla bɛn mali suhudoo ka ʒe yim Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni yino. Ka yi ti bɔri ni yi wurim tin’ shɛli din nyɛ Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni tinsi ma? Bɔzuɣu ka a bɔri ni a saɣim Yawɛ ni su binshɛli?”

english_verse: Joab answered, “No, no! I'm not trying to wipe you out or destroy your town!
translation_verse: Ka Jɔab daa garigi yɛl’ o, “Din’ kariya, din’ kariya ka n saɣim bee n-wurim ya ŋɔ.

english_verse: That's not it at all. There's a man in your town from the hill country of Ephraim. His name is Sheba, and he is the leader of a rebellion against King David. Turn him over to me, and we will leave your town alone.” The woman told Joab, “We will throw his head over the wall.”
translation_verse: Di pala yɛlimaŋli. Amaa ti bɔrila do’ so ŋun yi Ifriim zoya ni tiŋ’ la ni na ka o yuli booni Bikiri ŋun nyɛ Shiiba bia la, ka nyɛ ŋun daa yi Naa Dauda nyaaŋa la. Zaŋmiy’ o kɔŋko ti ma ka n zo ka chɛ yi ya ŋɔ.” Ka paɣ’ maa daa yɛli Jɔab, “Nyama, ti ni ŋmaag’ o zuɣu bahi ya gooni na.”

english_verse: She went to the people of the town and talked them into doing it. They cut off Sheba's head and threw it to Joab. Joab blew a signal on his trumpet, and the soldiers returned to their homes. Joab went back to David in Jerusalem. Another List of David's Officials
translation_verse: Di saha ka paɣ’ maa daa zaŋ o ni niŋ yɛn shɛli maa chaŋ tiŋ’ maa nim’ zaa sani, ka bɛ daa ŋmaai Bikiri bia Shiiba maa zuɣu n-zaŋ li bahi Jɔab na. Ka o daa piɛbi kikaa ka sokam wurim kul’ o yiŋa, ka Jɔab mi daa labi naa sani Jɛrusalɛm. Naa Dauda tumtumdi’ kpamba

english_verse: Joab was the commander of Israel's entire army. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was in command of David's bodyguard.
translation_verse: Jɔab n-daa nyɛ Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ni zaa tɔbbihi sapashin’ kpɛma, ka Jɛhɔiada bia Bɛnaaya la mi daa su Chɛrɛtinim’ mini Pɛlɛtinim’ fukumsi.

english_verse: Adoram was in charge of the slave-labor force. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept government records.
translation_verse: Ka Adɔram daa nyɛ ŋun su tumtumdiba fukumsi; ka Ahilud bia Jɛhɔshafat daa nyɛ ŋun su gbana sabbu fukumsi.

english_verse: Sheva was the secretary. Zadok and Abiathar were the priests.
translation_verse: Ka Shɛva daa nyɛ gbaŋŋmara. Ka Zadok mini Abiata daa nyɛ maligumaaniba,
