english_verse: Elijah told Ahab, “Get something to eat and drink. I hear a heavy rain coming.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Ilaija daa yɛli Ɛhab, “Cham’ ti di ka nyu, dama saa vura.”

english_verse: Ahab left, but Elijah climbed back to the top of Mount Carmel. Then he stooped down with his face almost to the ground
translation_verse: Ka Ɛhab ni daa chaŋ ni o ti di ka nyu saha shɛli maa, ka Ilaija daa du Kamɛl Zoli zuɣu nti kurim n-zaŋ o nini kpa o duna;

english_verse: and said to his servant, “Look toward the sea.” The servant left. And when he came back, he said, “I looked, but I didn't see anything.” Elijah told him to look seven more times.
translation_verse: ka yɛl’ o tumo, “Cham’ ti lihi teeku polo.” Ka o daa chaŋ ti lihi ka yɛli, “M bi nya shɛli.” Ka Ilaija yɛl’ o, “Labimi yaha n-niŋ lala hal ti paai siɣimsiɣim buyopɔin.”

english_verse: After the seventh time the servant replied, “I see a small cloud coming this way. But it's no bigger than a fist.” Elijah told him, “Tell Ahab to get his chariot ready and start home now. Otherwise, the rain will stop him.”
translation_verse: Napɔŋ din pahir’ ayopɔin maa ni, ka o daa ti yɛli, “N nya sagban’ bila ka di be kaman ninsal’ nuu la n-yi teeku polo na.” Ka o yɛl’ o, “Cham’ ti yɛli Ɛhab, ‘Malim’ a chɛchɛbuŋ’ shili n-yiɣisi kuli, di yi pa lala saa ni taɣ’ a sɔŋ.’ ”

english_verse: A few minutes later, it got very cloudy and windy, and rain started pouring down. So Elijah wrapped his coat around himself, and the Lord gave him strength to run all the way to Jezreel. Ahab followed in his chariot.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ yiko daa kpe Ilaija ni, ka o voog’ o shɛlɔrigu lo n-zo n-daŋ Ɛhab tooni ti paai Jɛziriil dunɔdali gbini.

english_verse: Ahab told his wife Jezebel what Elijah had done and that he had killed the prophets.
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka Ɛhab daa yɛl’ o paɣ’ Jɛzibɛl Ilaija ni niŋ shɛlikam zaa min’ o ni zaŋ takɔbi ku Baal daanabinim’ zaa shɛm yɛla.

english_verse: She sent a message to Elijah: “You killed my prophets. Now I'm going to kill you! I pray that the gods will punish me even more severely if I don't do it by this time tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Ka Jɛzibɛl daa tim ti yɛli Ilaija, “Biɛɣuni ŋ-ŋɔ tasaha n yi sa bi ku a kaman a ni ku anabinim’ ŋɔ shɛm maa, n wuna bɛn’ kum’ ma.”

english_verse: Elijah was afraid when he got her message, and he ran to the town of Beersheba in Judah. He left his servant there,
translation_verse: Ka dabiɛm daa gbaai Ilaija, ka o yiɣisi zo ni o tilig’ o nyɛvili. O daa zaŋla o tumo la n-zo n-kuli Bɛrishiiba din be Juda tiŋgbɔŋ ni la nti chɛ o nimaani.

english_verse: then walked another whole day into the desert. Finally, he came to a large bush and sat down in its shade. He begged the Lord, “I've had enough. Just let me die! I'm no better off than my ancestors.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka ŋun’ maŋmaŋ’ daa kpe mɔɣu chaŋ dabisi’ muni chandi nti teei ʒini ti’ shɛli gbini n-suhiri Naawuni bɔri ni o kpi. O daa yɛlimi, “Yawɛ, di saɣiya, deemi n nyɛvili pumpɔŋɔ, dama m bi so n yaannima.”

english_verse: Then he lay down in the shade and fell asleep. Suddenly an angel woke him up and said, “Get up and eat.”
translation_verse: Ka o daa dɔni tia maa gbini gbihi. Ka malaika daa shih’ o ka yɛl’ o, “Yiɣisim’ di bindirigu.”

english_verse: Elijah looked around, and by his head was a jar of water and some baked bread. He sat up, ate and drank, then lay down and went back to sleep.
translation_verse: Ka o yiɣisi lihi nya ka bɛ ni she mahi’ kpil’ shɛli kuɣ’ tula zuɣu mini kɔgaɣili n-ʒe o zuɣu polo. Ka o daa di ka nyu, ka lan lab’ dɔni.

english_verse: So Elijah sat up and ate and drank. The food and water made him strong enough to walk
translation_verse: Ka Ilaija daa yiɣisi di ka nyu, ka bindirigu maa daa ti o kpiɔŋ wuntaŋ’ ni mini yuŋ biɛɣ’ pihinahi, ka o chaŋ hal ti paai Sinai Zoli din nyɛ Naawuni zol’ la zuɣu.

english_verse: and he spent the night there in a cave. The Lord Appears to Elijah While Elijah was on Mount Sinai, the Lord asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
translation_verse: Ka o daa kpe vokabili puuni zoli maa zuɣu nti gbe nimaani. Ka Yawɛ daa bɔh’ o, “Ilaija, bɔ ka a lee niŋdi kpe?”

english_verse: He answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaija garigi yɛli, “N zabirila nyuli tiri nyin’ Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Tɔbbihi Naawuni ŋɔ; dama Izraɛlnim’ yi a mini ba daalikauli la nyaaŋa; ka daag’ a sara maligu bimbina luhi; ka zaŋ takɔbi ku a daanabinima; ka n kɔŋko nti kpalim, ka bɛ bɔri ni bɛ ku man’ gba.”

english_verse: “Go out and stand on the mountain,” the Lord replied. “I want you to be there when I pass by.” All at once, a strong wind shook the mountain and shattered the rocks. But the Lord was not in the wind. Next, there was an earthquake, but the Lord was not in the earthquake.
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl’ o, “Cham’ ti du n-tam zoli din do man’ Yawɛ tooni ŋɔ zuɣu. Dama Yawɛ yɛn garila nimaani.” Ka sanʒiɛ’ titali din mali kpiɔŋ daa yiɣisi ʒiɛri wurindi zoli maa, ka ŋmari kuɣa sɔŋdi Yawɛ tooni, amaa ka Yawɛ daa ka di ni. Ka tiŋgbani dambu daa doli sanʒiɛɣu maa nyaaŋa na, amaa ka Yawɛ ka tiŋgbani dambu maa ni.

english_verse: Then there was a fire, but the Lord was not in the fire. Finally, there was a gentle breeze,
translation_verse: Ka buɣim daa doli tiŋgbani dambu maa nyaaŋa na, amaa ka Yawɛ daa ka buɣim maa gba ni. Ka kukol’ balli zaɣ’ bilifu daa ti doli buɣim maa dibu nyaaŋa na.

english_verse: and when Elijah heard it, he covered his face with his coat. He went out and stood at the entrance to the cave. A voice asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
translation_verse: Ilaija ni daa wum li saha shɛli, o daa zaŋla o binyɛrigu pɔb’ o nina yi nti ʒe vokabili maa dunol’ ni. Nyama, ka kukoli maa daa bɔh’ o, “Ilaija, bɔ ka a lee niŋdi kpe?”

english_verse: Elijah answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
translation_verse: Ka o garigi yɛli, “N zabirila nyuli tiri nyin’ ŋun nyɛ Tɔbbihi Naawuni ŋɔ, dama Izraɛlnim’ yi a mini ba daalikauli la nyaaŋa, ka daag’ a sara maligu bimbina luhi, ka zaŋ takɔbi ku a daanabinim’ zaa, ka n kɔŋko nti kpalim, ka bɛ bɔri ni bɛ ku man’ gba.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Elijah, you can go back to the desert near Damascus. And when you get there, appoint Hazael to be king of Syria.
translation_verse: Ka Yawɛ daa yɛl’ o, “Labimi mɔɣu ni luɣ’ shɛli din miri Damaskus la. A yi paai nimaani, nyin’ boom’ kpam bahi Hazaɛl zuɣu ni ka o leei Siria naa;

english_verse: Then appoint Jehu son of Nimshi to be king of Israel, and Elisha son of Shaphat to take your place as my prophet.
translation_verse: ka booi kpam bahi Nimshi bia Jɛhu zuɣu ni ka o leei Izraɛl naa; ka lan booi kpam bahi Shafat ŋun nyɛ Ɛbɛlimɛhola nir’ la bia Ilaisha zuɣu ni, ka o mi leeg’ anabi zani a zaani.

english_verse: Hazael will start killing the people who worship Baal. Jehu will kill those who escape from Hazael, and Elisha will kill those who escape from Jehu.
translation_verse: Ka ninvuɣ’ so ŋun ti zo n-yi Hazaɛl takɔbi kubu ni, Jɛhu ŋun’ kum’ o; ka ŋun ti zo n-yi Jɛhu takɔbi kubu ni, Ilaisha mi ŋun’ kum’ o.

english_verse: Elijah left and found Elisha plowing a field with a pair of oxen. There were eleven other men in front of him, and each one was also plowing with a pair of oxen. Elijah went over and put his own coat on Elisha.
translation_verse: Ka Ilaija daa ŋmaligi nimaani chaŋ ti nya Shafat bia Ilaisha maa ka o malila naɣikɔra siɣimsiɣim bupinaayi zuɣu ka bɛ be o tooni kɔra; omaŋmaŋ’ n-daa mali bɛn pahiri bupinaayi maa kɔra. Ka Ilaija daa chaŋ ti gar’ o sani ka pirig’ o binyɛrigu pa o zuɣu.

english_verse: Elisha stopped plowing and ran after him. “Let me kiss my parents goodbye, then I'll go with you,” he said. “You can go,” Elijah said. “But remember what I've done for you.”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha daa chɛ naɣikɔra maa, ka guui doli Ilaija nti yɛl’ o, “Chɛ ka n chɛbisi m ba mini m ma pɔi ka naanyi dol’ a.” Ka Ilaija yɛl’ o, “Labima, ka n yɛl’ a la wula?

english_verse: Elisha left and took his oxen with him. He killed them and boiled them over a fire he had made with the wood from his plow. He gave the meat to the people who were with him, and they ate it. Then he left with Elijah and became his assistant.
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha daa lab’ o naɣikɔra maa sani nti zaŋ ba kɔrigi, ka zaŋ bɛ dapuhi m-mali buɣim duɣi ba n-zaŋ ti niriba ka bɛ ŋubi. Di nyaaŋa ka o daa chaŋ ti doli Ilaija n-sɔŋd’ o.

english_verse: They dressed in sackcloth and put ropes on their heads, then they went to Ahab and said, “Your servant Benhadad asks you to let him live.” “Is he still alive?” Ahab asked. “Benhadad is like a brother to me.”

translation_verse: Ka o daa tim tuumba tiŋ’ maa puuni Izraɛl Naa Ɛhab sani nti yɛl’ o, “Bɛnhadad

english_verse: Later, Benhadad sent another messenger to say to Ahab, “I already told you to give me your silver and gold, your wives, and your children.
translation_verse: Ka tuumba maa daa ti lan labina nti yɛl’ o, “Bɛnhadad ni yɛli shɛm m-bɔŋɔ, ‘N daa timna ti yɛl’ a ni a zaŋ a daanzinfa min’ a salima ni a paɣiba ni a bihi ti ma na,

translation_verse: amaa biɛɣuni ŋ-ŋɔ tasaha n sa ni tim n tuumba na ka bɛ ti kpe a min’ a kpambaliba yinsi nti vihi, ka bɛ yi kul nya binshɛlikam ka di tiɣi bɛ nini, bɛn’ kpuɣim’ li.’ ”

english_verse: “Don't listen to him!” they answered. “You don't have to do what he says.”
translation_verse: Ka kpamba maa mini niriba maa zaa daa yɛl’ o, “Di garig’ o shɛli bee n-saɣ’ o ni yɛli shɛm maa.”

english_verse: So Ahab sent someone to tell Benhadad, “Your Majesty, I'll give you my silver and gold, and even my wives and children. But I won't let you have anything else.” When Benhadad got his answer,
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka o daa yɛli Bɛnhadad tuumba maa, “Yɛlimiya n dan’ naa, ‘A ni daa daŋ bɔri ni man’ ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ niŋ shɛlikam zaa la, n saɣiya ni n ni niŋ li, amaa dimbɔŋɔ dindina, n ku tooi niŋ li.’ ” Ka tuumba maa daa ŋmaligi kuli nti lan ʒi yɛtɔɣ’ shɛli labina yaha.

english_verse: he replied, “I'll completely destroy Samaria! There won't even be enough of it left for my soldiers to carry back in their hands. If I don't do it, I pray that the gods will punish me terribly.”
translation_verse: Naa Bɛnhadad daa timmina nti yɛl’ o, “Samaria taŋkpaɣu yi ni tooi pali n niriba bɛn doli ma zaa nukurigu yimyim, m buɣa bɛn niŋm’ ma zaɣ’ biɛɣu, hal n niŋ ma zaɣ’ biɛɣu pam gba.”

english_verse: Ahab then answered, “Benhadad, don't brag before the fighting even begins. Wait and see if you live through it.”
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛl Naa daa garigi yɛli, “Yɛlimiy’ o, ‘Tɔbbi’ so ŋun na lɔri kpara bi simdi ka o nyuri bara kaman tɔbbi’ so ŋun lɔrigi kpara ni nyuri bara shɛm.’ ”

english_verse: Meanwhile, Benhadad and the other kings had been drinking in their tents. But when Ahab's reply came, he ordered his soldiers to prepare to attack Samaria, and they all got ready.
translation_verse: Bɛnhadad min’ o natab’ bɛn daa ʒe o nyaaŋa la daa bela bɛ suɣa ni nyuri dam, ka bɛ zaŋ o ni daa yɛli shɛm maa na ti yɛli Bɛnhadad. Ka o daa yɛl’ o tɔbbihi ni bɛ malim’ shili n-chaŋ ti liri Samarianim’ maa, ka bɛ daa teei zani.

english_verse: At that very moment, a prophet ran up to Ahab and said, “You can see that Benhadad's army is very strong. But the Lord has promised to help you defeat them today. Then you will know that the Lord is in control.”
translation_verse: Nyama, ka anabi so daa kana ti yɛli Izraɛl Naa Ɛhab, “Yawɛ ni yɛli shɛm m-bɔŋɔ, ‘Yi nya ninvuɣ’ gbaliŋ ŋɔ zaa bebɔ? Nyama, n ni zaŋ ba niŋ a nuu ni zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ, ka a baŋ ni mani n-shiri nyɛ Yawɛ.’ ”

english_verse: “Who will fight the battle?” Ahab asked. The prophet answered, “The young bodyguards who serve the district officials.” “But who will lead them into battle?” Ahab asked. “You will!” the prophet replied.

translation_verse: Sapashinnim’ maa ni daa ti nya Jɛhɔshafat bɛ daa yɛlimi, “Biɛhiŋ kani, Izraɛl naa maa m-bala.” Ka bɛ daa chaŋ ni bɛ ti tuh’ o; ka Jɛhɔshafat daa kuhi pam.

english_verse: As the sun was going down, someone in Israel's army shouted to the others, “Retreat! Go back home!”
translation_verse: Ka wuntaŋ’ daa ti miri lubu ka bɛ ŋme kuŋ’ yɛli Izraɛl tɔbbihi, “Sokam lab’ kul’ o ya o tiŋgbɔŋ ni!”

english_verse: Ahab's body was taken to Samaria and buried there.
translation_verse: Lala ka naa maa daa kpi; ka bɛ daa zaŋ o kuli Samaria ti sɔɣi.

english_verse: Some workers washed his chariot near a spring in Samaria, and prostitutes washed themselves in his blood. Dogs licked Ahab's blood off the ground, just as the Lord had warned.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa paɣ’ o chɛchɛbuŋ’ maa sɔŋ miri Samaria biaŋ, ka bahi daa kana ti lɛl’ o ʒim; ka pagɔra gba kana nti su di kom kaman Yawɛ ni daa pun yɛli shɛm la.

english_verse: Everything else Ahab did while he was king, including the towns he strengthened and the palace he built and furnished with ivory, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Jehoram became king. King Ahaziah of Israel
translation_verse: Ka Jɛhɔshafat daa ti kani, ka bɛ sɔɣ’ o o yab’ Dauda tiŋ’ la ni; ka o bia Jɛhɔram daa di nam zan’ o zaani. Izraɛl Naa Ahazia yɛla

english_verse: Ahaziah son of Ahab became king of Israel in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat's rule in Judah, and he ruled two years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Juda Naa Jɛhɔshafat ni daa di nam zaŋ chaŋ yuun’ pinaayopɔin saha ka Ɛhab bia Ahazia daa di Izraɛl nam ʒi Samaria. O daa diya n-sula Izraɛlnim’ yuma ayi.

english_verse: Ahaziah disobeyed the Lord, just as his father, his mother, and Jeroboam had done. They all led Israel to sin.
translation_verse: O daa tum alahichi Yawɛ sani, ka dol’ o ba min’ o ma ni Nɛbat bia Jɛrɔbɔam bɛn daa chɛ ka Izraɛlnim’ tum alahichi la naba.

english_verse: Ahaziah worshiped Baal and made the Lord God of Israel very angry, just as his father had done.
translation_verse: O daa jɛmdila Baal, ka dol’ o ba ni daa niŋ shɛlikam la soli n-chɛ ka Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Izraɛl Naawuni suhu yiɣisi pam.

english_verse: Soon after King Ahab of Israel died, the country of Moab rebelled against his son King Ahaziah. One day, Ahaziah fell through the wooden slats around the porch on the flat roof of his palace in Samaria, and he was badly injured. So he sent some messengers to the town of Ekron with orders to ask the god Baalzebub if he would get well.
translation_verse: Di saha maa Ahazia daa yila o yiŋ’ jirambisa zuɣusaa duu luɣili ni dunɔdura zuɣu lu tiŋa o ya Samaria m-biɛri doya, ka daa tim tuumba ka yɛli ba, “Chamiya Baalizibub ŋun nyɛ Ɛkurɔn buɣili la sani nti bɔh’ o nya n ni nya alaafee dɔro ŋɔ ni, bee?”

english_verse: About the same time, an angel from the Lord sent Elijah the prophet from Tishbe to say to the king's messengers, “Ahaziah has rejected Israel's own God by sending you to ask Baalzebub about his injury.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Yawɛ malaika daa yɛli Ilaija, Tishibi nir’ la, “Yiɣisim’ chaŋ ti tuhi Samaria naa tuumba ŋɔ soli m-bɔhi ba, ‘Naawuni n-lee ka Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni bee di chaŋ wula ka yi ti chanila Baalizibub ŋun nyɛ Ɛkurɔn buɣili la sani ni a ti bɔh’ o nya?’

english_verse: Tell him that because he has done this, he's on his deathbed!” And Elijah did what he was told.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ Yawɛ yɛliya, ‘A ku lan yiɣis’ a ni do bindo’ shɛli zuɣu ŋɔ, amaa biɛhiŋ kani, a ni kpi.’ ” Ka Ilaija daa chaŋ.

english_verse: When the messengers returned to Ahaziah, he asked, “Why are you back so soon?”
translation_verse: Ka tuumba maa daa lab’ kuli, ka naa maa ti bɔhi ba, “Ka wula ka yi ŋmaligi labina?”

english_verse: “A man met us along the road with a message for you from the Lord,” they answered. “The Lord wants to know why you sent us to ask Baalzebub about your injury and why you don't believe there's a God in Israel. The man also told us that the Lord says you're going to die.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa garigi yɛl’ o. “Do so n-tuhi ti soli yɛl’ ti, ‘Labimiya na’ so ŋun tim ya maa sani nti yɛl’ o, Yawɛ ni yɛli shɛm m-bɔŋɔ, Naawuni n-lee ka Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ni bee di chaŋ wula ka a ti timdi ni bɛ cham’ ti bɔhila Baalizibub ŋun nyɛ Ɛkurɔn buɣili la nya? Dinzuɣu a ku lan yiɣis’ a ni do bindo’ shɛli zuɣu ŋɔ, amaa biɛhiŋ kani, a ni kpi.’ ”

english_verse: “What did the man look like?” Ahaziah asked.
translation_verse: Ka o bɔhi ba, “Ninvuɣ’ bɔ n-lee tuhi ya soli n-yɛli ya lala maa?”

english_verse: “He was hairy and had a leather belt around his waist,” they answered. “It must be Elijah!” replied Ahaziah.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ garigi yɛl’ o, “Do so ŋun yɛl’ ti lala maa yɛla biŋkɔbigu kɔbiri binyɛrigu, ka zaŋ gbaŋ lo o shee ni.” Ka o yɛli, “Ilaija ŋun nyɛ Tishibi nir’ la m-bala.”

english_verse: Fire has already wiped out the other officers and their soldiers. Please don't let it happen to me.”
translation_verse: Nyama, buɣim pun yi zuɣusaa na ti di n-ku sapashinnima ayi la mini bɛ tɔbbihi pihinunu, amaa tiligim’ man’ nyɛvili.”

english_verse: The angel from the Lord said to Elijah, “Go with him and don't be afraid.” So Elijah got up and went with the officer.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Yawɛ malaika daa yɛli Ilaija, “Dol’ o chaŋ ka di zɔr’ o dabiɛm.” Ka Ilaija daa yiɣisi dol’ o chaŋ naa sani ti yɛl’ o,

english_verse: When Elijah arrived, he told Ahaziah, “The Lord wants to know why you sent messengers to Ekron to ask Baalzebub about your injury. Don't you believe there's a God in Israel? Ahaziah, because you did that, the Lord says you will die.”
translation_verse: “Yawɛ yɛliya, Naawuni n-lee ka Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ni bee di chaŋ wula ka a ti timdi ni bɛ cham’ ti bɔhi Baalizibub ŋun nyɛ Ɛkurɔn buɣili la nya a ni kpaŋ bee a ku kpaŋ? Dinzuɣu a ku yiɣis’ a bariŋ bindo’ shɛli zuɣu a ni doya ŋɔ, amaa biɛhiŋ kani a ni kpi.”

english_verse: Ahaziah died, just as the Lord had said. But since Ahaziah had no sons, Joram his brother then became king. This happened in the second year that Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.
translation_verse: Ka o daa shiri kpi kaman Yawɛ ni daa chɛ ka Ilaija yɛli shɛm maa. Ka o tizo Jɔram daa di nam zan’ o zaani, Juda Naa Jɛhɔram ŋun daa nyɛ Jɛhɔshafat bia la nam dibu yuma ayi saha, dama Ahazia daa ka bidibiga.

english_verse: Everything else Ahaziah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Ka Ahazia ni daa tum shɛlikam zaa pahi, bɛ sab’ di yɛla niŋ Izraɛl nanim’ litaafi shɛli bɛ ni booni Yɛlikura litaafi la ni.

english_verse: Not long before the Lord took Elijah up into heaven in a strong wind, Elijah and Elisha were leaving Gilgal.
translation_verse: Yawɛ ni daa yɛn chɛ ka pɔhim din mali kpiɔŋ kpuɣi Ilaija chaŋ alizanda ni saha shɛli, o mini Ilaisha daa yila Giligal m-be soli zuɣu chana.

english_verse: Elijah said to Elisha, “The Lord wants me to go to Bethel, but you must stay here.” Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I will stay with you no matter what!” And he went with Elijah to Bethel.
translation_verse: Ka Ilaija daa yɛli Ilaisha, “N suhir’ a, kpalimmi kpe; Yawɛ n-tim ma Bɛtɛl.” Amaa ka Ilaisha yɛl’ o, “Yawɛ ŋun be ŋɔ mini nyini ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu, n kul ku chɛ a dolibu.” Ka bɛ daa laɣim doli chaŋ Bɛtɛl.

english_verse: A group of prophets who lived there asked Elisha, “Do you know that today the Lord is going to take away your master?” “Yes, I do,” Elisha answered. “But don't remind me of it.”
translation_verse: Ka anabinim’ shɛb’ bɛn daa be Bɛtɛl daa yina ti bɔhi Ilaisha, “A mi ni Yawɛ ni kpuɣ’ a zuɣulan’ maa zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ n-chaŋ ka chɛ a bebɔ?” Ka Ilaisha garigi yɛli ba, “Iin, m mi. Amaa shiniya yi noli.”

english_verse: Elijah then said, “Elisha, now the Lord wants me to go to Jericho, but you must stay here.” Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life, that I will stay with you no matter what!” And he went with Elijah to Jericho.
translation_verse: Ka Ilaija daa lan yɛl’ o, “Ilaisha, n suhir’ a, kpalimmi kpe; Yawɛ n-tim ma Jɛriko.” Amaa ka Ilaisha yɛl’ o, “Yawɛ ŋun be ŋɔ mini nyini ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu, n kul ku chɛ a dolibu.” Ka bɛ daa laɣim doli chaŋ Jɛriko.

english_verse: A group of prophets who lived there asked Elisha, “Do you know that today the Lord is going to take away your master?” “Yes, I do,” Elisha answered. “But don't remind me of it.”
translation_verse: Ka anabinim’ bɛn daa be Jɛriko maa daa chaŋ Ilaisha sani ti bɔh’ o, “A mi ni Yawɛ ni kpuɣ’ a zuɣulan’ maa zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ n-chaŋ ka chɛ a bebɔ?” Ka Ilaisha garigi yɛli ba, “Iin, m mi. Amaa shiniya yi noli.”

english_verse: Elijah then said to Elisha, “Now the Lord wants me to go to the Jordan River, but you must stay here.” Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I will never leave you!” So the two of them walked on together.
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka Ilaija daa lan yɛl’ o, “N suhir’ a, kpalimmi kpe; dama Yawɛ n-tim ma Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili ni.” Amaa ka Ilaisha gba lan yɛl’ o, “Yawɛ ŋun be ŋɔ mini nyini ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu, n kul ku chɛ a dolibu.” Ka bɛ niriba ayi maa daa doli chana.

english_verse: Fifty prophets followed Elijah and Elisha from Jericho, then stood at a distance and watched as the two men walked toward the river.
translation_verse: Ka anabinim’ maa pihinu daa doli ba chaŋ ti kaɣ’ ʒe kpaŋ’ ha ka chɛ ba.

english_verse: When they got there, Elijah took off his coat, then he rolled it up and struck the water with it. At once a path opened up through the river, and the two of them walked across on dry ground.
translation_verse: Ka Ilaija daa pirig’ o binyɛrigu m-pɔripɔri li zaŋ fiɛb’ kom maa, ka kom maa daa pirigi buyi n-daai ti dɔni di yaɣ’ ayi maa zaa hal ka bɛ niriba ayi maa zaa ti doli tiŋgban’ kuŋ zuɣu du duli.

english_verse: After they had reached the other side, Elijah said, “Elisha, the Lord will soon take me away. What can I do for you before that happens?” Elisha answered, “Please give me twice as much of your power as you give the other prophets, so I can be the one who takes your place as their leader.”
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa du duli maa ha, ka Ilaija yɛli Ilaisha, “Yɛlim’ ma a ni bɔri ni n niŋ shɛli ti a pɔi ka bɛ naanyi kpuɣ’ ma chaŋ ka chɛ a.” Ka Ilaisha yɛl’ o, “N suhir’ a, chɛ ka a shia ŋun be a ni ŋɔ ʒiibuyi zuɣu be n ni.”

english_verse: Elijah and Elisha were walking along and talking, when suddenly there appeared between them a flaming chariot pulled by fiery horses. At once, a strong wind took Elijah up into heaven.
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa kul yɛri lala chani maa, yim, ka chɛchɛbuŋ’ din mali buɣim mini di yuri din mali buɣim dii kana ti kpe bɛ niriba ayi maa sunsuuni n-woligi ba, ka pɔhim din mali kpiɔŋ dii kpuɣi Ilaija du zuɣusaa.

english_verse: Elisha saw this and shouted, “Israel's cavalry and chariots have taken my master away!” After Elijah had gone, Elisha tore his clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Ilaisha ni daa nya lala maa, ka o kuhi yɛli, “M ba, m ba! Izraɛl chɛchɛbunsi mini di wɔribariba.” Ka o daa bi lan nya Ilaija yaha. Di saha ka o daa gbaag’ omaŋmaŋ’ binyɛrigu darigi tooi li buyi.

english_verse: Elijah's coat had fallen off, so Elisha picked it up and walked back to the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Ka o daa kpuɣi Ilaija binyɛr’ shɛli din daa yi o sani luna n-lab’ ti zani Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili naŋgbaŋgbiriŋ.

english_verse: He struck the water with the coat and wondered, “Will the Lord perform miracles for me as he did for Elijah?” As soon as Elisha did this, a dry path opened up through the water, and he walked across.
translation_verse: Di saha ka o daa zaŋ Ilaija binyɛr’ shɛli din daa yi o sani luna maa n-fiɛb’ kom maa ka bɔhi, “Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ Ilaija Naawuni la lee be ya?” O ni daa fiɛb’ kom maa, ka di dii pirigi buyi n-daai ti dɔni di yaɣa ayi maa zaa, ka Ilaisha daa doli nimaani du duli.

english_verse: When the prophets from Jericho saw what happened, they said to each other, “Elisha now has Elijah's power.” They walked over to him, bowed down,
translation_verse: Anab’ shɛb’ bɛn daa be Jɛriko la ni daa nya Ilaisha ka o miri ba na ka bɛ yɛli, “Ilaija shia la shiri be Ilaisha ni.” Ka bɛ daa chaŋ ti tuh’ o soli n-damd’ o tiŋa,

english_verse: They kept begging until he was embarrassed to say no. He finally agreed, and the prophets sent the men out. They looked three days for Elijah but never found him.
translation_verse: Amaa ka bɛ daa kaɣil’ o hal ka di ti niŋ o vi, ka o bahi ba noli ni bɛ timma. Dinzuɣu ka bɛ daa tim ninvuɣ’ pihinu ka bɛ chaŋ ti lihi bɔ o dabisi’ muna ata zaa ka bi nya o.

english_verse: They returned to Jericho, and Elisha said, “I told you that you wouldn't find him.” Elisha Makes the Water Pure at Jericho
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa lab’ Ilaisha sanna Jɛriko o ni daa be luɣ’ shɛli, ka o bɔhi ba, “N daa pun bi yɛli ya ni yi di chaŋ?” Ilaisha tum alahiziba tuma

english_verse: One day the people of Jericho said, “Elisha, you can see that our city is in a good spot. But the water from our spring is so bad that it even keeps our crops from growing.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Jɛrikɔnim’ daa kana ti yɛli Ilaisha, “Ti dana, yiya ŋɔ ni ʒe luɣ’ shɛli ŋɔ viɛli pam kaman a gba ni nya li shɛm, amaa di kom nyɛla ko’ biɛɣu, ka di zuɣu chɛ ka paɣiba zaŋdi bahira.”

english_verse: He replied, “Put some salt in a new bowl and bring it to me.” They brought him the bowl of salt,
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha yɛli ba, “Bomiya la’ palli n-niŋ yalim niŋ di ni ti ma na.” Ka bɛ daa bo li na ti ti o.

english_verse: and he carried it to the spring. He threw the salt into the water and said, “The Lord has made this water pure again. From now on you'll be able to grow crops, and no one will starve.”
translation_verse: Ka o daa chaŋ kuliga ni nti kpaai yalim maa bahi kom maa ni ka yɛli, “Yawɛ yɛliya, n chɛ ka kom maa leei ko’ viɛlli; ka pumpɔŋɔ zaŋ chana, di ku lan ku so bee n-chɛ ka paɣiba zaŋdi bahira.”

english_verse: The water has been fine ever since, just as Elisha said. Some Boys Make Fun of Elisha
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu kom maa na kul nyɛla ko’ viɛlli hal ni zuŋɔ kaman Ilaisha ni daa yɛli shɛm maa.

english_verse: Elisha left and headed toward Bethel. Along the way some boys started making fun of him by shouting, “Go away, baldy! Get out of here!”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha daa ti yi nimaani n-chani Bɛtɛl. O ni daa yi soli n-chani ha, ka bidibbihi nya o m-maani o ansarisi yɛra, “Zuɣupalo ŋɔ lana, chama! Zuɣupalo ŋɔ lana, chama!”

english_verse: Elisha turned around and stared at the boys. Then he cursed them in the name of the Lord. At once two bears ran out of the woods and ripped to pieces
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha daa ŋmaligi nya ba, ka zaŋ Yawɛ yuli yɛli ba noli. Ka gbuɣin’ nyama ayi daa yi tibɔŋ ni na nti dim ku bidibbihi pihinahinaayi.

english_verse: Elisha went up to Mount Carmel, then returned to Samaria.
translation_verse: Ka o daa yi nimaani chaŋ Kamɛl Zoli zuɣu, ka daa ti yi nimaani lab’ Samaria.

english_verse: Joram son of Ahab became king of Israel in Jehoshaphat's eighteenth year as king of Judah. Joram ruled twelve years from Samaria
translation_verse: Juda Naa Jɛhɔshafat ni daa di nam zaŋ chaŋ yuun’ pisaayika saha, ka Ɛhab bia Jɛhɔram daa di Izraɛl nam Samaria. O daa niŋ la o nam maa ni yuun’ pinaayi.

english_verse: and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He tore down the stone image his father had made to honor Baal, and so he wasn't as sinful as his parents.
translation_verse: O daa tum alahichi Yawɛ sani. Amaa o daa lee bi tummi kaman o ba min’ o ma ni daa tum shɛm la; dama o daa wurim o ba ni daa me Baal binwɔɣinli shɛli zal’ la.

english_verse: But he kept doing the sinful things that Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel to do. The Country of Moab Rebels against Israel
translation_verse: Amaa o daa tum Nɛbat bia Jɛrɔbɔam ni daa tum alahichi shɛli n-chɛ ka Izraɛlnim’ tum alahichi la tatabo. O daa bi lɔɣ’ li.

english_verse: For many years the country of Moab had been controlled by Israel and was forced to pay taxes to the kings of Israel. King Mesha of Moab raised sheep, so he paid the king of Israel
translation_verse: Mɔab Naa Mɛsha daa wumsirila piɛri, ka di daa kpala talahi ni o tahiri piɛbihi polo tuhi’ kɔbiga mini piɛlahi tuhi’ kɔbiga kɔbiri yuuni kam nti tiri Izraɛl naa.

english_verse: But soon after the death of Ahab, Mesha rebelled against Israel.
translation_verse: Amaa Ɛhab kum nyaaŋa, ka Mɔab naa maa daa zaɣisi ni o ku lan niŋ lala ti Izraɛl naa.

english_verse: One day, Joram left Samaria and called together Israel's army.
translation_verse: Ka Naa Jɛhɔram daa dii yiɣisi Samaria di saha maa n-chaŋ ti laɣim Izraɛl tɔbbihi zaa.

english_verse: He sent this message to King Jehoshaphat of Judah, “The king of Moab has rebelled. Will you go with me to attack him?” “Yes, I will,” Jehoshaphat answered. “I'm on your side, and my soldiers and horses are at your command.
translation_verse: Di saha maa ka o daa tim Juda Naa Jɛhɔshafat sani ti yɛl’ o, “Mɔab naa zaɣisi ma jɛmbu. A ni pahi n zuɣu ka ti chaŋ ti tuh’ o?” Ka o garigi yɛl’ o, “N ni chaŋ. A ni be shɛm lala n-nyɛ ma. N niriba bemi ka a niriba, ka n yuri be ka a yuri.”

english_verse: So Joram, Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom led their troops out. But seven days later, there was no drinking water left for them or their animals.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛl naa mini Juda naa ni Ɛdom naa daa laɣim chaŋ. Ka bɛ daa chaŋ ti paai daba ayopɔin chandi tariga ka kom pooi ba, hal ka shɛli kani ka bɛ tɔbbihi mini bɛ ni daa ʒiri biŋkɔb’ shɛb’ chani ni nyu.

english_verse: Joram cried out, “This is terrible! The Lord must have led us out here to be captured by Moab's army.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka Izraɛl naa daa yɛli, “Mbaye! Yawɛ zaŋla ti nanima ata ŋɔ na ni o ti niŋ Mɔabnim’ nuu ni!”

english_verse: Jehoshaphat said, “Which of the Lord's prophets is with us? We can find out from him what the Lord wants us to do.” One of Joram's officers answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He was one of Elijah's closest followers.”
translation_verse: Ka Jɛhɔshafat bɔh’ o, “Yawɛ anab’ so ka kpe ka ti ni bɔh’ o baŋ Yawɛ ni yɛli shɛm?” Di saha ka Izraɛl naa sapashinnim’ ni yino daa garigi yɛli, “Shafat bia Ilaisha, ŋun daa nyɛ Ilaija sɔŋda la be kpe.”

english_verse: Jehoshaphat replied, “He can give us the Lord's message.” The three kings went over to Elisha,
translation_verse: Ka Jɛhɔshafat yɛli, “Yawɛ yɛligu be o ni.” Dinzuɣu ka Izraɛl naa mini Jɛhɔshafat ni Ɛdom naa daa chaŋ o sani.

english_verse: and he asked Joram, “Why did you come to me? Go talk to the prophets of the foreign gods your parents worshiped.” “No,” Joram answered. “It was the Lord who led us out here, so that Moab's army could capture us.”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha daa ti bɔhi Izraɛl naa, “M min’ a yɛla bi kpa. Cham’ a ba min’ a ma daanabinim’ la sani.” Amaa ka Izraɛl naa maa yɛl’ o, “Aai, Yawɛ n-zaŋ ti nanima ata ŋɔ na ni o ti niŋ Mɔabnim’ nuu ni.”

english_verse: Elisha said to him, “I serve the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as he lives, I swear I wouldn't even look at you if I didn't respect King Jehoshaphat.”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha yɛli, “N ni jɛmdi Yawɛ so ŋun nyɛ Tɔbbihi Naa ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu, di yi di pala n ni ti Juda Naa Jɛhɔshafat jilima zuɣu, n naan ku ŋmaligi lih’ a bee nti nya a.

english_verse: Then Elisha said, “Send for someone who can play the harp.” The harpist began playing, and the Lord gave Elisha this message for Joram:
translation_verse: Amaa bomiya baaŋa ti ma na pumpɔŋɔ.” Baaŋa maa ni daa ti yiini yila saha shɛli, ka Yawɛ yiko siɣi Ilaisha zuɣu na,

english_verse: The Lord says that this dry riverbed will be filled with water.
translation_verse: ka o yɛli, “Yawɛ ni yɛli shɛm m-bɔŋɔ, ‘N ni chɛ ka kom tɛli baa din kuui ŋɔ ni zaa.’

english_verse: You won't feel any wind or see any rain, but there will be plenty of water for you and your animals.
translation_verse: Yawɛ lan yɛli, ‘Yi ku nya pɔhim bee saa, amaa kom ni tɛli baa ŋɔ ni ka yi mini yi niɣi ni yi biŋkɔbiri nyu.’ ”

english_verse: That simple thing isn't all the Lord is going to do. He will also help you defeat Moab's army.
translation_verse: Ka dimbɔŋɔ nyɛla yɛl’ bila Yawɛ sani. O ni lan zaŋ Mɔabnim’ niŋ yi nuu ni;

english_verse: You will capture all their walled cities and important towns. You will chop down every good tree and stop up every spring of water, then ruin their fertile fields by covering them with rocks.
translation_verse: ka yi ŋme n-nyaŋ bɛ ni me birininim’ gili bɛ tin’ shɛŋa la nim’ mini tiŋ’ gahinda la, ka ŋma bɛ ti’ suŋ kam zaa luhi; ka ŋari bɛ kɔbil’ nina zaa, ka kahi kuɣa sɔŋ luɣ’ shɛŋa din tam vuhiri shee zaa n-saɣim li.

english_verse: The next morning, while the sacrifice was being offered, water suddenly started flowing from the direction of Edom, and it flooded the land.
translation_verse: Dindali maa kaai biɛɣ’ asibaasi sara maligu saha, ka kom daa yi Ɛdom polo n-zo na ti tɛli tiŋgbani zaa.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the people of Moab had heard that the three kings were coming to attack them. They had called together all of their fighting men, from the youngest to the oldest, and these troops were now standing at their border, ready for battle.
translation_verse: Mɔabnim’ zaa ni daa wum ni nanim’ shɛb’ kana ni bɛ ti tuhi ba, bɛ daa laɣimla bipola zaŋ tabili ninkura zaa bɛn ni tooi ye gbaɣinɔnim’ na nti sɔŋ bɛ tintariga.

english_verse: When they got up that morning, the sun was shining across the water, making it look red. The Moabite troops took one look
translation_verse: Ka Mɔabnim’ maa daa yiɣis’ asibaasi, ka wuntaŋ’ nyeei kpe kom maa, ka bɛ nya ka di do bɛ tooni ha m-mɔhi kaman ʒim la.

english_verse: and shouted, “Look at that blood! The armies of those kings must have fought and killed each other. Come on, let's go take what's left in their camp.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa yɛli, “Ʒim m-bala. Nanim’ maa ŋ-ŋmaligi zabi n-ku tab’ maa! Dinzuɣu Mɔabnima, chamiya ti di nɛma!”

english_verse: But when they arrived at Israel's camp, the Israelite soldiers came out and attacked them, until they turned and ran away. Israel's army chased them all the way back to Moab, and even there they kept up the attack.
translation_verse: Amaa ka bɛ daa mali ti paai Izraɛlnim’ sansan ni, ka Izraɛlnim’ maa daa yiɣisi lu bɛ zuɣu, ka Mɔabnim’ maa ŋmaligi guui, ka Izraɛlnim’ kari doli ba ŋ-ŋmɛri kuri ba chana.

english_verse: The Israelites destroyed the Moabite towns. They chopped down the good trees and stopped up the springs of water, then covered the fertile fields with rocks. Finally, the only city left standing was Kir-Hareseth, but soldiers armed with slings surrounded and attacked it.
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛlnim’ daa saɣim Mɔabnim’ maa tinsi; ka sokam daa kahi kuɣa nti bahi bɛ tiŋgbani maa luɣ’ shɛŋa din vuhiri shee hal ka di zaa ti nyɛla kuɣa noli; ka ŋari bɛ kɔbil’ nina; ka ŋma bɛ ti’ suŋ kam zaa luhi. Ka bɛ tin’ titali din yuli booni Kiriharɛsɛt la kɔŋko n-daa ti kpalim, ka kuɣilɔnlabiriba daa chaŋ ti teei gil’ li ŋ-ŋme n-nyaŋ ba.

english_verse: He then grabbed his oldest son who was to be the next king and sacrificed him as an offering on the city wall. The Israelite troops were so horrified that they left the city and went back home.
translation_verse: Di saha ka o daa zaŋ o zuu ŋun ti yɛn di nam zan’ o zaani mali maligu gooni zuɣu n-zaŋ o nyo buɣim. Ka suli daa gbaai Izraɛlnima, ka bɛ ŋmaligi lab’ bɛ ya ka chɛ o.

english_verse: One day the widow of one of the Lord's prophets said to Elisha, “You know that before my husband died, he was a follower of yours and a worshiper of the Lord. But he owed a man some money, and now that man is on his way to take my two sons as his slaves.”
translation_verse: Anab’ so pakoli daa ti yɛli Ilaisha, “A dab’ so ŋun yi nyɛ n yidan’ la kpiya. Ka a mi mi ni a dabili maa daa nyɛla ŋun zɔri Yawɛ, amaa ka o sandana kana ni o ti zaŋ m bidibis’ ayi nti leeg’ o daba.”

english_verse: “Maybe there's something I can do to help,” Elisha said. “What do you have in your house?” “Sir, I have nothing but a small bottle of olive oil.”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha bɔh’ o, “Ka bɔ ka a lee bɔri ni n niŋ ti a? Yɛlim’ ma a ni mali shɛl’ a yiŋa.” Ka o yɛl’ o, “A dabipaɣa ka shɛli; kulla kpaŋman’ yini kɔŋko ka m mali.”

english_verse: Elisha told her, “Ask your neighbors for their empty jars. And after you've borrowed as many as you can,
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha yɛl’ o, “Cham’ a ʒiʒiinitab’ sani nti suhi kpaŋman’ kuma pam na, pa biɛla.

english_verse: go home and shut the door behind you and your sons. Then begin filling the jars with oil and set each one aside as you fill it.”
translation_verse: Ka a chɛ ka a min’ a bidibisi maa kpe yi duu ka yo yimaŋ’ niŋ di puuni, ka zaŋ kpam maa m-boori niŋdi ŋmana maa ni; ŋman’ yini yi ti pali, ka yi vuui li zali kpaŋa.”

english_verse: The woman left. Later, when she and her sons were back inside their house, the two sons brought her the jars, and she began filling them.
translation_verse: Ka pakoli maa daa yi o sani kuli nti chɛ ka o min’ o bihi maa kpe duu ka yo bɛmaŋ’ niŋ di puuni; ka o bihi maa zaŋdi ŋmana n-zaan’ o, ka o boori kpam maa niŋdi di ni.

english_verse: At last, she said to one of her sons, “Bring me another jar.” “We don't have any more,” he answered, and the oil stopped flowing from the small bottle.
translation_verse: Ka ŋmana maa zaa daa ti pali; ka o yɛl’ o bidibisi maa ni yino, “Zaŋm’ ŋman’ shɛl’ na.” Ka o yɛl’ o, “Ŋman’ shɛl’ lan kani.” Ka kpam maa mi dii ŋmaai, ka bi lan yirina.

english_verse: After she told Elisha what had happened, he said, “Sell the oil and use part of the money to pay what you owe the man. You and your sons can live on what is left.” Elisha Brings a Rich Woman's Son Back to Life
translation_verse: Ka pakoli maa daa lab’ ti yɛli Naawuni daanab’ maa. Ka Ilaisha yɛl’ o, “Cham’ ti zaŋ kpam maa kɔhi n-yo yi samli maa, ka chɛ din kpalim ka a min’ a bidibisi maa dira.” Ilaisha mini Shunɛm paɣ’ bundan’ yɛla

english_verse: Once, while Elisha was in the town of Shunem, he met a rich woman who invited him to her home for dinner. After that, whenever he was in Shunem, he would have a meal there with her and her husband.
translation_verse: Dahin shɛli ka Ilaisha daa ti chaŋ Shunɛm ka paɣ’ bundaan’ so daa be nimaani m-balim o ni o dim’ bindirigu. Dinzuɣu o daa yi ti doli nimaani polo saha shɛlikam, o kpɛrila yili maa ni ti diri bindirigu.

english_verse: Some time later the woman said to her husband, “I'm sure the man who comes here so often is a prophet of God.
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ bundan’ maa daa ti yɛl’ o yidana, “Nyama, pumpɔŋɔ m baŋya ni do’ so ŋun doli yiri ti sanna waawaayili ŋɔ nyɛla Naawuni ninvuɣ’ gahindili.

english_verse: Why don't we build him a small room on the flat roof of our house? We can put a bed, a table and chair, and an oil lamp in it. Then whenever he comes, he can stay with us.”
translation_verse: Chɛ ka ti me dubil’ tam ti yil’ ŋɔ zuɣusaa, ka bo garo mini teebuli ni kuɣa ni firila zali di ni, o yi ti lan ka ti sanna ka o kpe nimaani.”

english_verse: The next time Elisha was in Shunem, he stopped at their house and went up to his room to rest.
translation_verse: Dahin’ shɛli ka Ilaisha daa ti chaŋ nimaani n-kpe duu maa ni ni o ti vuhi.

english_verse: He said to his servant Gehazi, “This woman has been very helpful. Have her come up here to the roof for a moment.” She came, and Elisha told Gehazi to say to her, “You've gone to a lot of trouble for us, and we want to help you. Is there something we can request the king or army commander to do?” The woman answered, “With my relatives nearby, I have everything I need.”
translation_verse: Ka o yɛli Gɛhaazi, “Yɛlim’ o, ‘Nyama, a niŋ wahala pam sɔŋ ti; ka bɔ ka a lee bɔri ni ti niŋ ti a? A bɔri ni ti yɛli naa bee sapashin’ kpɛm’ yɛtɔɣ’ shɛli ti a?’ ” Ka paɣ’ maa garigi yɛli, “Mmaŋmaŋ’ niriba ni ka m be maa.”

english_verse: “Then what can we do for her?” Elisha asked Gehazi. Gehazi replied, “I do know that her husband is old, and that she doesn't have a son.”
translation_verse: Ka o bɔhi, “Ka bɔ ka ti lee yɛn niŋ ti paɣa maa?” Ka Gɛhaazi garigi yɛl’ o, “To, paɣ’ maa ka bidibiga, ka o yidana mi kurigi.”

english_verse: “Ask her to come here again,” Elisha told his servant. He called for her, and she came and stood in the doorway of Elisha's room.
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha yɛli, “Bolim’ o na.” Ka o daa boli paɣ’ maa, ka o kana ti zani dunol’ ni.

english_verse: Elisha said to her, “Next year at this time, you'll be holding your own baby son in your arms.” “You're a man of God,” the woman replied. “Please don't lie to me.”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha yɛl’ o, “Zaŋ chaŋ yuuni na ŋ-ŋɔ tasaha a ni gbib’ bidibiga a nuu ni.” Ka paɣ’ maa yɛli, “Aai. Wɛi, n dana, a nyɛla Naawuni nira, di yɔhim’ man’ ŋun nyɛ a dab’ paɣ’ ŋɔ!”

english_verse: But a few months later, the woman got pregnant. She gave birth to a son, just as Elisha had promised.
translation_verse: Amaa ka paɣ’ maa daa shiri niŋ pua n-dɔɣi bidibiga shɛɣuni kaman Ilaisha ni daa yɛl’ o ni o ni dɔɣi saha shɛli maa.

english_verse: One day while the boy was still young, he was out in the fields with his father, where the workers were harvesting the crops.
translation_verse: Ka bia maa daa mali ti zooi. Dahin shɛli ka o daa ti dol’ o ba chaŋ puu ni kachɛriba sani.

english_verse: Suddenly he shouted, “My head hurts. It hurts a lot!” “Carry him back to his mother,” the father said to his servant.
translation_verse: Ka o daa ti yɛl’ o ba, “Wɛi, n zuɣu n-yaara, n zuɣu n-yaara!” Ka bia maa ba yɛl’ o tumtumdi so, “Zaŋm’ bia maa kuli ti ti o ma.”

english_verse: loaves of bread made from the first barley that was harvested. Elisha said, “Give it to the people so they can eat.”
translation_verse: Ka doo maa daa zaŋ bia maa nti ti o ma; ka o zaŋ o ʒil’ o naba zuɣu n-gbib’ o hal ti paai wuntaŋ’ zuɣusaa saha, ka o leei Naawuni dini.

english_verse: She carried him upstairs to Elisha's room and laid him across the bed. Then she walked out and shut the door behind her.
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ maa daa zaŋ bia maa n-du n-kpɛhi ti sɔŋ Naawuni nir’ maa garo zuɣu; ka yina n-vooi dunoli yo.

english_verse: The woman called to her husband, “I need to see the prophet. Let me use one of the donkeys. Send a servant along with me, and let me leave now, so I can get back quickly.”
translation_verse: Ka o daa bol’ o yidana n-yɛl’ o, “Chɛ ka tumtumdi’ yino zaŋ bun’ yino ti ma na, ka n chaŋ yomyom ti nya Naawuni nir’ ŋɔ ka labina.”

english_verse: “Why do you need to see him today?” her husband asked. “It's not the Sabbath or time for the New Moon Festival.” “That's all right,” she answered.
translation_verse: Ka o yidan’ maa bɔh’ o, “Bɔzuɣu ka a bɔri ni a chaŋ o sani zuŋɔ? Zuŋɔ pala gol’ palli dabisili bee Vuhim Dabisili.” Ka paɣ’ maa yɛli, “Di bi galim.”

english_verse: She left at once for Mount Carmel to talk with Elisha. When Elisha saw her coming, he said, “Gehazi, look! It's the woman from Shunem.
translation_verse: Ka o daa yiɣisi n-chaŋ Naawuni nir’ maa sani Kamɛl Zoli zuɣu. Naawuni Nir’ maa ni daa nya paɣ’ maa ka o kanna ka o yɛl’ o sɔŋda Gɛhaazi, “Nyama, Shunɛm paɣ’ la m-be katiŋ’ kanna ŋɔ.

english_verse: Run and meet her. And ask her if everything is all right with her and her family.” “Everything is fine,” she answered Gehazi.
translation_verse: Guum’ yomyom tuh’ o soli ti bɔh’ o, ‘A min’ a yidan’ ni yi bia la mal’ alaafee?’ ” Ka o garigi yɛli Gɛhaazi, “Ti mal’ alaafee.”

english_verse: But as soon as she got to the top of the mountain, she went over and grabbed Elisha by the feet. Gehazi started toward her to push her away, when Elisha said, “Leave her alone! Don't you see how sad she is? But the Lord hasn't told me why.”
translation_verse: O ni daa mali ti paai Naawuni nir’ maa sani zoli maa zuɣu, o daa gbaala o napɔŋ, ka Gɛhaazi kana ni o ti daag’ o bahi, ka Naawuni nir’ maa yɛl’ o, “Chɛl’ o. O malila yɛli muɣisirili ka Yawɛ zaŋ li sɔɣi ma ka bi kahigi li wuhi ma.”

english_verse: The woman said, “Sir, I begged you not to get my hopes up, and I didn't even ask you for a son.”
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ maa bɔhi Ilaisha, “N daa yɛli nyini n dana ni a tim ma bia? N daa pun bi yɛl’ a ni a di yɔhim ma?”

english_verse: “Gehazi, get ready and go to her house,” Elisha said. “Take along my walking stick, and when you get there, lay it on the boy's face. Don't stop to talk to anyone, even if they try to talk to you.”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha daa yɛli Gɛhaazi, “Malim’ shili kpuɣi n jaaŋgbee ŋɔ chaŋ. A yi ti nya so sol’ ni, nyin’ di puh’ o; ka so yi puh’ a, nyin’ di saɣi. A yi ti paai, nyin’ zaŋmi n jaaŋgbee maa pa bia maa ninni.”

english_verse: But the boy's mother said to Elisha, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I won't leave without you.” So Elisha got up and went with them.
translation_verse: Ka bia maa ma maa daa yɛli Ilaisha, “Yawɛ ŋun be ŋɔ mini nyin’ ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu, n ku chaŋ ka chɛ a.” Ka Ilaisha daa yiɣisi dol’ o.

english_verse: Gehazi ran on ahead and laid Elisha's walking stick on the boy's face, but the boy didn't move or make a sound. Gehazi ran back to Elisha and said, “The boy didn't wake up.”
translation_verse: Ka Gɛhaazi daa daŋ tooni nti zaŋ jaaŋgbee maa pa bia maa ninni, amaa ka vuhim bee nyɛvili shɛhirili kani. Dinzuɣu ka o daa ŋmaligi labina ti tuhi Ilaisha soli n-yɛl’ o, “Bia maa bi neei.”

english_verse: Elisha arrived at the woman's house and went straight to his room, where he saw the boy's body on his bed.
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha daa paai yili maa ni nti nya ka bia maa kpi n-dola o garo zuɣu.

english_verse: He walked in, shut the door, and prayed to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ka o daa kpe duu maa ni, ka vooi dunoli yo bɛ niriba ayi maa niŋ, ka suhi Yawɛ.

english_verse: Then he got on the bed and stretched out over the dead body, with his mouth on the boy's mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hand on his hands. As he lay there, the boy's body became warm.
translation_verse: Di nyaaŋa ka o daa chaŋ ti teei dɔni bia maa zuɣu n-zaŋ o noli min’ o nina kpa bia maa noli ni o nina, ka zaŋ o nuhi pa o nuhi zuɣu; ka teeg’ omaŋ’ dolisi bia maa, ka o niŋgbuna piligi biibu.

english_verse: Elisha got up and walked back and forth in the room, then he went back and leaned over the boy's body. The boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha daa yiɣisi chaŋchaŋ gili duu maa ni, ka ti lan lab’ ti teei dɔni bia maa zuɣu yaha. Ka bia maa daa tihim siɣimsiɣim buyopɔin, ka neeg’ o nina.

english_verse: Elisha called out to Gehazi, “Ask the boy's mother to come here.” Gehazi did, and when she was at the door, Elisha said, “You can take your son.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka o daa boli Gɛhaazi na ti yɛl’ o, “Bolim’ Shunɛm paɣ’ maa na.” Ka o bol’ o. Ka paɣ’ maa kana, ka o ti yɛl’ o, “Kpuɣim’ a bia.”

english_verse: She came in and bowed down at Elisha's feet. Then she picked up her son and left. Elisha Makes Some Stew Taste Better
translation_verse: Ka paɣ’ maa daa kana ti lu n-gbani Ilaisha naba ni n-zaŋ o zuɣu silim tiŋa, ka kpuɣ’ o bia maa yi. Alahiziba tumtumsa ayi din pahi

english_verse: Later, Elisha went back to Gilgal, where there was almost nothing to eat, because the crops had failed. One day while the prophets who lived there were meeting with Elisha, he said to his servant, “Prepare a big pot of stew for these prophets.”
translation_verse: Ka kum daa ti lu, ka Ilaisha lab’ Giligal na. Ka anabinim’ daa ti ʒi o sani, ka o yɛl’ o sɔŋda, “Zaŋm’ duɣ’ titali tam n-duɣi ʒiɛri ti anabinim’ ŋɔ.”

english_verse: One of them went out into the woods to gather some herbs. He found a wild vine and picked as much of its fruit as he could carry, but he didn't know that the fruit was very sour. When he got back, he cut up the fruit and put it in the stew.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ ni yino daa yi n-chaŋ ni o ti bo ʒiɛvari na nti nya mɔɣu ni yɔɣili m-pɔhi li buɣi na nti ŋmahiŋmahi li niŋ ʒɛduɣu maa ni, ka bi mi di ni nyɛ shɛli.

english_verse: The stew was served, and when the prophets started eating it, they shouted, “Elisha, this stew tastes terrible! We can't eat it.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa ti tooi li ti niriba maa ni bɛ piɛbi. Bɛ ni daa piɛbiri ʒiɛri maa ka bɛ ti kuhi yɛli, “Wɛi, Naawuni nira, Lɔɣu be duɣu maa ni!” Ka bɛ daa kɔŋ li piɛbbu.

english_verse: “Bring me some flour,” Elisha said. He sprinkled the flour in the stew and said, “Now serve it to them.” And the stew tasted fine. Elisha Feeds One Hundred People
translation_verse: Ka o daa yɛli, “Dindina niŋmiya zim ti ma na.” Ka o daa zaŋ zim maa yuɣisi ʒiɛri maa ni ka yɛli ba, “Toomiya li ti niriba maa ka bɛ piɛbi.” Ka barina shɛli daa lan ka di ni yaha.

english_verse: So the servant served the bread and grain to the people. They ate and still had some left over, just as the Lord had promised.
translation_verse: Ka o sɔŋda maa daa zaŋ li ti ba. Ka bɛ daa shiri ŋub’ li ka guui kaman Yawɛ ni daa pun yɛli shɛm maa.

english_verse: Naaman was the commander of the Syrian army. The Lord had helped him and his troops defeat their enemies, so the king of Syria respected Naaman very much. Naaman was a brave soldier, but he had leprosy.
translation_verse: Naaman ŋun daa nyɛ Siria naa sapashin’ kpɛma daa nyɛla ninvuɣ’ titali, ka mali jilima pam o naa maa sani, dama o zuɣu ka Yawɛ daa tiri Sirianim’ nasara. O daa mali kpiɔŋ pam, ka lan nyɛ tɔbutuhir’ biiŋa; amaa ka kɔŋ’ lee mal’ o.

english_verse: One day while the Syrian troops were raiding Israel, they captured a girl, and she became a servant of Naaman's wife.
translation_verse: Sirianim’ daa ti chaŋ ti tuhi Izraɛlnima, ka gbaai bipuɣimbil’ so kuli ka o ti tumdi tuma sɔŋdi Naaman paɣa.

english_verse: When Naaman told the king what the girl had said,
translation_verse: Ka Naaman daa chaŋ o naa sani nti yɛl’ o, “Izraɛl bipuɣimbil’ la ni yɛli shɛm m-bɔŋɔ.”

english_verse: the king replied, “Go ahead! I will give you a letter to take to the king of Israel.” Naaman left and took along
translation_verse: Ka Siria naa maa daa yɛl’ o, “Cham’ pumpɔŋɔ! N ni sab’ gbaŋ ti a ka a mali ti ti Izraɛl naa.” Ka Naaman daa bo anzinfa laɣibaligu tuhi’ pia mini salima laɣibaligu tusaayɔbu ni binyɛr’ suma din nyɛ chuɣu binyɛra pia chaŋ.

english_verse: He also carried the letter to the king of Israel. It said, “I am sending my servant Naaman to you. Would you cure him of his leprosy?”
translation_verse: Ka o daa zaŋ gbaŋ maa nti ti Izraɛl naa. O ni daa sabi gbaŋ maa n-yɛli shɛm m-bɔŋɔ: “Gbaŋ ŋɔ yi paag’ a, nyin’ baŋmi ni mani n-chɛ ka Naaman ŋun nyɛ n tumtumda ŋɔ ka a sanna ni a ti tib’ o kɔŋ’ ŋɔ.”

english_verse: Elisha sent someone outside to say to him, “Go wash seven times in the Jordan River. Then you'll be completely cured.”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha daa tim tumo ni o yim’ na ti yɛli Naaman ni o cham’ Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili ni nti mim di ni siɣimsiɣim buyopɔin ka o niŋgbuna lab’ dimaŋ’ ni ka o nya alaafee.

english_verse: When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes in fear and shouted, “That Syrian king believes I can cure this man of leprosy! Does he think I'm God with power over life and death? He must be trying to pick a fight with me.”
translation_verse: Izraɛl naa maa ni daa ti karim gbaŋ maa, o daa darigimi toog’ o binyɛrigu ka yɛli, “N nyɛla Naawuni ka ni tooi ku nir’ ka lan neeg’ o, ka doo ŋɔ ti yɛri ma ni n tibimi nir’ kɔŋa? Nir’ yi kpahim yɛlli maa, a ni baŋ ni vuri ka o bɔri ma maa!”

english_verse: As soon as Elisha the prophet heard what had happened, he sent the Israelite king this message: “Why are you so afraid? Send the man to me, so that he will know there is a prophet in Israel.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Ilaisha ŋun nyɛ Naawuni nir’ maa daa wum Izraɛl naa ni darigi toog’ o binyɛrigu shɛm maa yɛla, ka tim ti bɔhi naa maa, “Bɔ n-niŋ ka a darigi toog’ a binyɛrigu? Chɛ ka doo maa ka n sanna nti baŋ ni anabi be Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni.”

english_verse: Naaman left with his horses and chariots and stopped at the door of Elisha's house.
translation_verse: Ka Naaman daa zaŋ o yuri min’ o chɛchɛbuŋa ŋ-ŋmaligi chaŋ ti zani Ilaisha yiŋ’ dunol’ ni.

english_verse: But Naaman stormed off, grumbling, “Why couldn't he come out and talk to me? I thought for sure he would stand in front of me and pray to the Lord his God, then wave his hand over my skin and cure me.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Naaman daa je suli ŋ-ŋmaligi chani ka yɛra, “Man’ di mi ni o yɛn yimina nti zani n-suhi Yawɛ ŋun nyɛ o Naawuni maa, ka zaŋ o nuu gahigahi kpe, ka chɛ ka n kɔŋ’ maa naai.

english_verse: What about the Abana River or the Pharpar River? Those rivers in Damascus are just as good as any river in Israel. I could have washed in them and been cured.”
translation_verse: Abana mini Faaripa mɔɣa din be Damaskus la bi so koma zaa din be Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni? N naan dii ku chaŋ nimaani nti mim ka nya alaafee?” Dinzuɣu ka o suhu daa yiɣisi pam ka o ŋmaligi chaŋ.

english_verse: His servants went over to him and said, “Sir, if the prophet had told you to do something difficult, you would have done it. So why don't you do what he said? Go wash and be cured.”
translation_verse: Ka o tumtumdiba daa chaŋ o sani nti yɛl’ o, “Ti ba, anab’ maa yi di yɛl’ a ni a niŋm’ binshɛli din to pam, a naan ku niŋ li? Di ni ti be ka o ni yɛl’ a mi, ‘Cham’ ti mim kom ni ka nya alaafee ŋɔ?’ ”

english_verse: Naaman walked down to the Jordan; he waded out into the water and stooped down in it seven times, just as Elisha had told him. At once, he was cured, and his skin became as smooth as a child's.
translation_verse: Ka Naaman daa saɣi, ka chaŋ ti mim Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili ni siɣimsiɣim buyopɔin kaman Naawuni nir’ maa ni daa yɛl’ o shɛm maa, ka nya alaafee zaa. Ka o niŋgbuna lab’ dimaŋ’ ni m-be kaman bibil’ niŋgbuna la.

english_verse: Naaman and his officials went back to Elisha. Naaman stood in front of him and announced, “Now I know that the God of Israel is the only God in the whole world. Sir, would you please accept a gift from me?”
translation_verse: Ka o mini bɛn daa dol’ o chaŋ maa zaa daa lab’ Naawuni nir’ maa sani ka o ti chaŋ ti zan’ o tooni ka yɛli, “M baŋya pumpɔŋɔ ni Naawuni ka dunia ŋɔ ni luɣ’ shɛli m-pahi Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ŋɔ ni zuɣu; dinzuɣu deem’ pin’ shɛli man’ ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ ni yɛn ti a ŋɔ.”

english_verse: “I am a servant of the living Lord,” Elisha answered, “and I swear that I will not take anything from you.” Naaman kept begging, but Elisha kept refusing.
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha yɛli, “Yawɛ ŋun be ka n jɛmd’ o ŋɔ zuɣu, n ku deei pin’ shɛli a sani.” Ka Naaman daa balim o ni o deem’ li, amaa ka o zaɣisi.

english_verse: Finally Naaman said, “If you won't accept a gift, then please let me take home as much soil as two mules can pull in a wagon. Sir, from now on I will offer sacrifices only to the Lord.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Naaman daa yɛli Ilaisha, “A yi ku deei m pini, dindina, n suhir’ a, nyin’ chɛ ka bɛ tooi taŋkpaɣu ka di saɣi buntaans’ ayi ʒibu ti mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ ka n zaŋ kuli, dama pumpɔŋɔ zaŋ chana, mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ ku lan zaŋ binshɛli nyo buɣim bee m-mali sara ti buɣili kam yaha naɣila Yawɛ ka n ni jɛm.

english_verse: But I pray that the Lord will forgive me when I go into the temple of the god Rimmon and bow down there with the king of Syria.”
translation_verse: Ka dimbɔŋɔ puuni, m mali tahima ni n yi ti doli n naa chaŋ Siria buɣili Rimɔn jɛmbu duu nti damdi di tooni, biɛhiŋ kani, Yawɛ ni chɛ mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ taali.”

english_verse: “Go on home, and don't worry about that,” Elisha replied. Then Naaman left. Elisha Places a Curse on Gehazi After Naaman had gone only a short distance,
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha yɛl’ o, “Kulim’ ni suhudoo.” Naaman ni daa chaŋ, o daa na bi paai shɛli,

english_verse: Gehazi said to himself, “Elisha let that Syrian off too easy. He should have taken Naaman's gift. I swear by the living Lord that I will talk to Naaman myself and get something from him.”
translation_verse: ka Naawuni nira Ilaisha sɔŋda Gɛhaazi yɛl’ o suhu ni, “N dana fa Naaman ŋun nyɛ Siria nir’ ŋɔ bahi, o ni zaɣis’ o ni ʒi pin’ shɛŋa na nti ti o la zuɣu. Yawɛ ŋun be ŋɔ zuɣu, n ni kar’ o naba ti deei shɛli o sani.”

english_verse: So he hurried after Naaman. When Naaman saw Gehazi running after him, he got out of his chariot to meet him. Naaman asked, “Is everything all right?”
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu ka Gɛhaazi daa shiri yiɣisi kariti Naaman naba. Ka Naaman daa ti nya ka so zɔri dol’ o nyaaŋa na, ka o sheeg’ o chɛchɛbuŋ zuɣu n-chaŋ ti tuh’ o soli bɔh’ o, “Alaafee?”

english_verse: “Yes,” Gehazi answered. “But my master has sent me to tell you about two young prophets from the hills of Ephraim. They came asking for help, and now Elisha wants to know if you would give them
translation_verse: Ka Gɛhaazi yɛli, “Alaafee. N dana n-tim ma na ni nti yɛl’ a ni nachimbih’ ayi bɛn nyɛ anabinima n-yi Ifriim zoya tiŋ’ ni kana; ni o suhir’ a ni a ti ba anzinfa laɣibaligu tuhili mini binyɛr’ suma ayi din nyɛ chuɣu binyɛra na.”

english_verse: “Sure,” Naaman replied. “But why don't you take twice that amount of silver?” He convinced Gehazi to take it all, then put the silver in two bags. He handed the bags and the clothes to his two servants, and they carried them for Gehazi.
translation_verse: Ka Naaman yɛl’ o, “Chɛ ka n zaŋ anzinfa laɣibaligu tusaayi ti a.” Ka o daa balim o zaŋ anzinfa laɣibaligu tusaayi mini binyɛr’ suma ayi din nyɛ chuɣu binyɛra maa n-niŋ kpalans’ ayi ni lo n-zaŋ ʒil’ o tumtumdiba ayi, ka bɛ zaŋ li ʒi m-be Gɛhaazi tooni.

english_verse: When they reached the hill where Gehazi lived, he took the bags from the servants and placed them in his house, then sent the men away. After they had gone,
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa ti paai zoli maa gbini, ka o deei li bɛ sani n-zaŋ kpɛhi duu; ka chɛbisi ba ka bɛ ŋmaligi labi.

english_verse: Gehazi went in and stood in front of Elisha, who asked, “Gehazi, where have you been?” “Nowhere, sir,” Gehazi answered.
translation_verse: Ka o daa kpe n-chaŋ ti zan’ o dan’ Ilaisha tooni, ka Ilaisha bɔh’ o, “Gɛhaazi, ya polo ka a lee chaŋ?” Ka o garigi yɛl’ o, “Mani ŋun nyɛ a dabili ŋɔ bi chaŋ luɣ’ shɛli.”

english_verse: Elisha asked, “Don't you know that my spirit was there when Naaman got out of his chariot to talk with you? Gehazi, you have no right to accept money or clothes, olive orchards or vineyards, sheep or cattle, or servants.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Ilaisha bɔh’ o, N shia di ka a sani saha shɛli doo la ni di yi o chɛchɛbuŋ’ ni n-kana ti tuh’ a sol’ la? Pumpɔŋɔ nyɛla saha shɛli di ni simdi ni a deeri liɣiri mini binyɛra ni olivi tihi ni tihi puri ni piɛri ni niɣi ni dabidɔbba ni dabipaɣiba?

english_verse: Because of what you've done, Naaman's leprosy will now be on you and your descendants forever!” Suddenly, Gehazi's skin became white with leprosy, and he left.
translation_verse: Dinzuɣu Naaman kɔŋ’ maa ni lu a min’ a bihi zuɣu n-kul maliya sahakam! Ka Gɛhaazi daa ŋmalig’ o sani n-yi ni kɔŋa; ka o niŋgbuna dii paligi laɣilaɣi kaman gumbɔrigu la.

english_verse: One day the prophets said to Elisha, “The place where we meet with you is too small.
translation_verse: Dahin shɛli ka anabinim’ shɛb’ daa ti yɛli Ilaisha, “Nyama, luɣ’ shɛli ti ni be ka a wuhiri ti ŋɔ pɔri pam.

english_verse: Why don't we build a new meeting place near the Jordan River? Each of us could get some wood, then we could build it.” “That's a good idea,” Elisha replied, “get started.”
translation_verse: Chɛ ka ti chaŋ Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili ni, ka ti zaa ti ŋma dari na nti me duri pahi beni.” Ka o garigi yɛli ba, “Chamiya.”

english_verse: “Aren't you going with us?” one of the prophets asked. “Yes, I'll go,” Elisha answered,
translation_verse: Di saha ka bɛ ni yino daa yɛl’ o, “A yi di saɣi n-dol’ ti chaŋ.” Ka o garigi yɛli, “N ni chaŋ.”

english_verse: and he left with them. They went to the Jordan River and began chopping down trees.
translation_verse: Ka o daa pahi bɛ zuɣu ka bɛ chaŋ. Ka bɛ daa paai Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili ni nti gbaai dari maa ŋmabu.

english_verse: “Where did it fall in?” Elisha asked. The prophet pointed to the place, and Elisha cut a stick and threw it into the water at that spot. The ax head floated to the top of the water.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Naawuni nir’ maa daa bɔh’ o, “Ya polo ka di lu?” Ka o wuh’ o di shee, ka Ilaisha ŋmaai daɣu n-zaŋ bahi nimaani n-chɛ ka lɛbiɛlim maa puhi pan’ na.

english_verse: “Now get it,” Elisha told him. And the prophet reached in and grabbed it. Elisha Stops an Invasion of the Syrian Army
translation_verse: Ka o yɛli doo maa, “Yihim’ li,” ka o zaŋ o nuu tim ha yihi li. Bɛ nyaŋ Siria tɔbbihi

english_verse: Time after time, when the king of Syria was at war against the Israelites, he met with his officers and announced, “I've decided where we will set up camp.”
translation_verse: Siria naa daa ti lo tɔbu ni o tuhi Izraɛlnima, ka daa niŋ o sapashinnim’ saawara, yɛli, “Luɣili yaakaza ka n yɛn chaŋ ti dɔni.”

english_verse: Each time, Elisha would send this warning to the king of Israel: “Don't go near there. That's where the Syrian troops have set up camp.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Naawuni nir’ maa daa tim ti yɛli Izraɛl naa, “Miri ka a doli yaakaza polo, dama Sirianim’ yɛn chaŋ ti dɔni la nimaani.”

english_verse: The king of Syria was furious when he found out what was happening. He called in his officers and asked, “Which one of you has been telling the king of Israel our plans?”
translation_verse: Ka yɛlli maa daa muɣisi Siria naa maa pam ka o bol’ o sapashinnim’ na nti bɔhi ba, “Yi ni ŋuni n-lee be Izraɛl naa polo?”

english_verse: “None of us, Your Majesty,” one of them answered. “It's an Israelite named Elisha. He's a prophet, so he can tell his king everything—even what you say in your own room.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ ni yino garigi yɛl’ o, “N dan’ naa, ti ni so bi be o polo. Amaa anabi Ilaisha ŋun be Izraɛl tiŋgbɔŋ ni la n-yɛri Izraɛl naa a ni be a duu tɔɣisiri yɛtɔɣ’ shɛlikam.”

english_verse: “Find out where he is!” the king ordered. “I'll send soldiers to bring him here.” They learned that Elisha was in the town of Dothan and reported it to the king.
translation_verse: Ka o yɛli ba, “Chamiya ti nya o ni be luɣ’ shɛli ka n tim ka bɛ ti gbaag’ o na.” Ka bɛ daa ti yɛl’ o, “O be Dɔtan.”

english_verse: He ordered his best troops to go there with horses and chariots. They marched out during the night and surrounded the town.
translation_verse: Ka o daa tim tɔbbihi pam, ka bɛ zaŋ yuri mini chɛchɛbunsi n-chaŋ yuŋ ti teei gili tiŋ’ maa.

english_verse: When Elisha's servant got up the next morning, he saw that Syrian troops had the town surrounded. “Sir, what are we going to do?” he asked.
translation_verse: Ka biɛɣu daa ti neerina asibaasi, ka Ilaisha sɔŋda yina nti nya ka tɔbbihi mini yuri ni chɛchɛbunsi n-kul teei gili bɛ tiŋ’ maa zaa. Ka Ilaisha sɔŋda maa kuhi yɛli, “Mbaye, n dana! Ka wula ka ti lee yɛn niŋ?”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Elisha answered. “There are more troops on our side than on theirs.”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha garigi yɛl’ o, “Di chɛ ka dabiɛm mal’ a, dama bɛn be ti sani gari bɛn be bɛ sani.”

english_verse: Then he prayed, “Lord, please help him to see.” And the Lord let the servant see that the hill was covered with fiery horses and flaming chariots all around Elisha.
translation_verse: Di saha ka Ilaisha daa suhi Yawɛ yɛli, “Neem’ o nina ka o nya.” Ka Yawɛ daa neei nachimbil’ maa nina ka o lihi nya ka yuri mini buɣim chɛchɛbunsi n-kul pali zoli zuɣu n-teei gili Ilaisha.

english_verse: As the Syrian army came closer, Elisha prayed, “Lord, make those soldiers blind!” And the Lord blinded them with a bright light.
translation_verse: Ka Sirianim’ maa daa kana ni bɛ ti liri Ilaisha, ka Ilaisha suhi Yawɛ yɛli, “N suhir’ a, chɛ ka niriba ŋɔ zom!” Ka o daa chɛ ka bɛ shiri zom kaman Ilaisha ni daa suh’ o yɛli shɛm maa.

english_verse: Elisha told the enemy troops, “You've taken the wrong road and are in the wrong town. Follow me. I'll lead you to the man you're looking for.” Elisha led them straight to the capital city of Samaria.
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha daa yɛli ba, “Pa yi ni chani tin’ shɛli maa soli m-bɔŋɔ; pa yi mi ni chani tin’ shɛli maa m-bɔŋɔ. Doliya ma ka n zaŋ ya tahi yi ni bɔri so maa sani.” Ka o daa zaŋ ba tahi Samaria.

english_verse: When all the soldiers were inside the city, Elisha prayed, “Lord, now let them see again.” The Lord let them see that they were standing in the middle of Samaria.
translation_verse: Bɛ ni daa ti kul kpe Samaria puuni, ka Ilaisha suhi Yawɛ yɛli, “Neem’ niriba ŋɔ nina n-chɛ ka bɛ nya.” Ka Yawɛ daa neei bɛ nina maa, ka bɛ lihi nya ka bɛ bela Samaria puuni.

english_verse: The king of Israel saw them and asked Elisha, “Should I kill them, sir?”
translation_verse: Izraɛl naa ni daa nya ba, o daa bɔhila Ilaisha, “M ba, n kum ba? N kum ba?”

english_verse: “No!” Elisha answered. “You didn't capture these troops in battle, so you have no right to kill them. Instead, give them something to eat and drink and let them return to their leader.”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha garigi yɛl’ o, “Di ku ba. A ni ku a ni zaŋ a takɔb’ min’ a tɔbu n-gbahi shɛb’ leeg’ a daba? Bomi la bindirigu ti ba ka bɛ di ka nyu kom, ka lab’ bɛ naa sani.”

english_verse: The king ordered a huge meal to be prepared for Syria's army, and when they finished eating, he let them go. For a while, the Syrian troops stopped invading Israel's territory. King Benhadad of Syria Attacks Samaria
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛl naa maa daa chɛ ka bɛ duɣi bindira pam ti ba, ka bɛ di ka nyu n-naai, ka o chɛ ka bɛ lab’ kuli bɛ naa sani. Ka Sirianim’ daa bi lan kana ti liri Izraɛlnim’ yaha. Naa Bɛnhadad min’ o tɔbbihi teei gili Samaria

english_verse: Some time later, King Benhadad of Syria called his entire army together, then they marched to Samaria and attacked.
translation_verse: Dimbɔŋɔ nyaaŋa ka Siria Naa Bɛnhadad daa ti zaŋ o tɔbbihi zaa n-chaŋ ti teei gili Samaria.

english_verse: One day as the king of Israel was walking along the top of the city wall, a woman shouted to him, “Please, Your Majesty, help me!”
translation_verse: Ka Izraɛl naa daa ti doli tiŋ’ maa gooni zuɣusaa n-chani garita, ka paɣ’ so kuhi yɛl’ o, “N dan’ naa, sɔŋm’ ma!”

english_verse: “Let the Lord help you!” the king said. “Do you think I have grain or wine to give you?”
translation_verse: Ka naa maa yɛl’ o, “Yawɛ yi bi sɔŋ a, wula ka man’ ni tooi sɔŋ a? M malila chi bee wain?”

english_verse: Then he asked, “What's the matter anyway?” The woman answered, “Another woman and I were so hungry that we agreed to eat our sons. She said if we ate my son one day, we could eat hers the next day.
translation_verse: Ka bɔh’ o, “Bɔ n-lee muɣis’ a?” Ka paɣ’ maa yɛl’ o, “Paɣ’ ŋɔ n-daa yɛli ma, ‘Zaŋm’ a bidibiga ŋɔ ka ti duɣi ŋubi zuŋɔ; ka sa zaŋ m mi bidibiga duɣi ŋubi biɛɣuni.’

english_verse: So yesterday we cooked my son and ate him. But today when I went to her house to eat her son, she had hidden him.”
translation_verse: Ka ti zaŋ m bia duɣi ŋubi n-kaai biɛɣu, ka n yɛl’ o, ‘Zaŋm’ a bidibiga la na ka ti duɣi ŋub’, ka ŋun’ zaŋ o bidibiga maa ti sɔɣi.’ ”

english_verse: The king tore off his clothes in sorrow, and since he was on top of the city wall, the people saw that he was wearing sackcloth underneath.
translation_verse: Naa maa ni daa wum paɣ’ maa yɛtɔɣa maa, ka o darigi toog’ omaŋmaŋ’ binyɛrigu, ka doli gooni maa zuɣu garita. Ka niriba nya o ka o yɛla buɣu ka di be o binyɛrigu tiŋli.

english_verse: He said, “I pray that God will punish me terribly, if Elisha's head is still on his shoulders by this time tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Ka o daa yɛli, “N yi bi ŋma Shafat bia Ilaisha la zuɣu zuŋɔ dabisili ŋɔ, Naawuni ŋun’ niŋm’ ma din gari lala.”

english_verse: Then he sent a messenger to Elisha. Elisha was home at the time, and the important leaders of Israel were meeting with him. Even before the king's messenger arrived, Elisha told the leaders, “That murderer is sending someone to cut off my head. When you see him coming, shut the door and don't let him in. I'm sure the king himself will be right behind him.”
translation_verse: Ka o daa tim ni bɛ ti gbaai Ilaisha na. Di saha maa Ilaisha mini kpeen’ shɛba n-daa ʒi o yiŋa. Ka naa tumo maa daa na bi paana ka Ilaisha yɛli kpamba maa, “Nyamiya, ninvuɣ’ kur’ la ni tim ni bɛ kana ti ŋma n zuɣu shɛm. Nyamiya, Tumo maa yi paana, yin’ yomiya dunoli n-dihi li gbibi ka di chɛliya ka o kpe na. O dan’ napɔn chichiba n-kul vuri dol’ o nyaaŋa ŋɔ na.”

english_verse: Before Elisha finished talking, the messenger came up and said, “The Lord has made all these terrible things happen to us. Why should I think he will help us now?”
translation_verse: O noli daa na bi lu tiŋa, ka naa maa paag’ o sanna ti yɛl’ o, “Ti muɣisigu ŋɔ yila Yawɛ sanna! Ka bɔzuɣu ka n lan yɛn guhi ŋun’ Yawɛ yaha?”

english_verse: Elisha answered, “I have a message for you. The Lord promises that tomorrow here in Samaria, you will be able to buy a large sack of flour or two large sacks of barley for almost nothing.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Ilaisha daa yɛl’ o, “Wummi Yawɛ ni yɛli shɛm. O yɛliya ni biɛɣuni ŋ-ŋɔ tasaha, bɛ sa ni kɔhi zim balli din tibisim nyɛ kilɔgiram ata anzinfa laɣibaligu zaɣ’ yini, ka kɔhi chi kilɔgiram ayɔbu mi anzinfa laɣibaligu zaɣ’ yini Samaria ŋɔ dunɔdal’ ni.”

english_verse: The chief officer there with the king replied, “I don't believe it! Even if the Lord sent a rainstorm, it couldn't produce that much grain by tomorrow.” “You will see it happen, but you won't eat any of the food,” Elisha warned him. The Syrian Army Stops Its Attack
translation_verse: Ka sapashin’ so ŋun daa guli naa maa yɛli Naawuni nir’ maa, “Hal Yawɛ yi yooi zuɣusaa soya bahi gba, lala ku tooi niŋ!” Ka Ilaisha yɛl’ o, “A nini sa ni nya li, amaa ka a nol’ lee ku to li.” Siria tɔbbihi zoya

english_verse: About the same time, four men with leprosy were just outside the gate of Samaria. They said to each other, “Why should we sit here, waiting to die?
translation_verse: Niriba anahi bɛn daa nyɛ kɔnsi daa do Samaria sambani polo dunol’ shee. Ka bɛ daa ti bɔhi taba, “Bɔzuɣu ka ti lee yɛn ʒi kpe hal ti kpi?

english_verse: There's nothing to eat in the city, so we would starve if we went inside. But if we stay out here, we will die for sure. Let's sneak over to the Syrian army camp and surrender. They might kill us, but they might not.”
translation_verse: Ti yi yɛli, ‘Chɛliya ka ti kpe tiŋ’ ŋɔ puuni,’ kum be di ni, ka ti ni kpi; ka ti mi yi ʒi kpe, ti ni kpi. Dinzuɣu chɛliya ka ti chaŋ Sirianim’ sansani ŋɔ ni, bɛ yi ti chɛ ti, ti ni be; ka bɛ yi ti ku ti, ka ti dii kpi.”

english_verse: They said to each other, “This isn't right. Today is a day to celebrate, and we haven't told anyone else what has happened. If we wait until morning, we will be punished. Let's go to the king's palace at once and tell the good news.”
translation_verse: Di saha ka bɛ daa yɛli taba, “Ti bi niŋ din tuhi. Zuŋɔ nyɛla lahiba’ suŋ dabisili. Ka ti yi zaŋ li shini hal ni biɛɣu ti neei, tibidarigibo shɛli ni ti paai ti. Dinzuɣu pumpɔŋɔ chɛliya ka ti chaŋ ti yɛli nayilinima.”

english_verse: They went back to Samaria and shouted up to the guards at the gate, “We've just come from the Syrian army camp, and all the soldiers are gone! The tents are empty, and the horses and donkeys are still tied up. We didn't see or hear anybody.”
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa chaŋ ti boli ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn guli tiŋ’ maa dunɔdali n-yɛli ba, “Ti chaŋla Sirianim’ sansan’ la ni nti bi nya so bee n-wum so damli, amaa ka bɛ tanti suɣa la beni; ka bɛ yuri mini bɛ bunsi gba loya pahi.”

english_verse: The king got out of bed and said to his officers, “I know what those Syrians are doing. They know we're starving, so they're hiding in the fields, hoping we will go out to look for food. When we do, they can capture us and take over our city.”
translation_verse: Ka naa daa yiɣisi yuŋ’ maa n-yɛl’ o kpambaliba, “N ni yɛli ya Sirianim’ maa ni lo ni bɛ niŋ ti shɛm. Bɛ mi ni kum mali ti, dinzuɣu ka bɛ yi bɛ sansani maa ni n-chaŋ ti sɔɣi, ka tɛhira, ‘Bɛ yi yi bɛ tiŋ’ maa ni na, ti ni gbahi ba zaɣ’ nɛma, ka kpe bɛ tiŋ’ maa ni.’ ”

english_verse: One of his officers replied, “We have a few horses left—why don't we let some men take five of them and go to the Syrian camp and see what's happening? We're going to die anyway like those who have already died.”
translation_verse: Ka o kpambaliba maa ni yino yɛl’ o, “Chɛ ka ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ zaŋ yur’ anu bɛn kpalim ŋɔ chaŋ, dama ninvuɣ’ shɛb’ bɛn nyɛ Izraɛlnim’ ninvuɣ’ gbaliŋ bɛn be tiŋ’ ŋɔ puuni gba kul bela barina ni kaman bɛn pun kpi la. Dinzuɣu chɛ ka ti tim ba ka bɛ chaŋ ti nya.”

english_verse: They found two chariots, and the king commanded the men to find out what had happened to the Syrian troops.
translation_verse: Ka bɛ daa pii wɔribariba ayi, ka naa maa tim ba Siria tɔbbihi maa sani ka yɛli ba, “Chamiya ti nya.”

english_verse: The men rode as far as the Jordan River. All along the way they saw clothes and equipment that the Syrians had thrown away as they escaped. Then they went back to the king and told him what they had seen.
translation_verse: Ka niriba maa daa chaŋ ti doli bɛ naba hal ni Jɔɔdɛn Mɔɣili ni n-nya ka Sirianim’ maa situra mini bɛ neen’ shɛŋa bɛ ni zo ka chɛ m-bahi kul dɔndo sol’ ni. Ka tuumba maa daa labina ti yɛli naa.

english_verse: At once the people went to the Syrian camp and carried off what was left. They took so much that a large sack of flour and two large sacks of barley sold for almost nothing, just as the Lord had promised.
translation_verse: Di saha ka niriba daa yi n-chaŋ Sirianim’ sansani maa ni nti ʒe bɛ nɛma. Ka bɛ daa kɔhi zim balli din tibisim nyɛ kilɔgiram ata anzinfa laɣibaligu zaɣ’ yini, ka kɔhi chi din tibisim nyɛ kilɔgiram ayɔbu mi anzinfa laɣibaligu zaɣ’ yini kaman Yawɛ ni daa pun yɛli shɛm la.

english_verse: The king of Israel had put his chief officer in charge of the gate, but he died when the people trampled him as they rushed out of the city.
translation_verse: Naa daa chɛ ka o sapashin’ so ŋun gul’ o la n-ʒe n-guli dunɔdali, ka niriba daa no o dunɔdali maa ni hal ka o ti kpi kaman Naawuni nir’ maa ni daa pun yɛli shɛm saha shɛli naa ni daa ka o sanna la.

english_verse: But the officer refused to believe that even the Lord could do that. So Elisha warned him that he would see it happen, but would not eat any of the food.
translation_verse: sapashini maa daa yɛlila Naawuni nir’ maa, “Hal Yawɛ yi yooi zuɣusaa soya bahi gba, lala ku tooi niŋ!” Ka Naawuni nir’ maa yɛl’ o, “A nini sa ni nya bindirigu maa, amaa ka a noli lee ku to li.”

english_verse: And that's exactly what happened—the officer was trampled to death.
translation_verse: Ka di daa shiri niŋ o lala, dama niriba daa no o dunɔdali maa ni hal ka o ti kpi.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the king was asking Gehazi the servant of Elisha about the amazing things Elisha had been doing.
translation_verse: Di saha naa maa daa tɔɣisirila Gɛhaazi ŋun daa nyɛ Naawuni nir’ maa sɔŋda la yɛtɔɣa n-yɛr’ o, “Yɛlim’ ma Ilaisha ni daa tum tuun’ kar’ shɛŋa zaa yɛla.”

english_verse: While Gehazi was telling him that Elisha had brought a dead boy back to life, the woman and her son arrived. “Here's the boy, Your Majesty,” Gehazi said. “And this is his mother.”
translation_verse: O ni daa yɛri naa maa Ilaisha ni daa neei kpim’ kum ni shɛm saha shɛli maa, ka o ni daa neei paɣ’ so bia kum ni maa kana nti yɛli naa maa ni o labisim’ o yili min’ o tiŋgbani ti o. Ka Gɛhaazi daa yɛli naa maa, “N dana, n-nyɛ paɣ’ maa, Ilaisha ni daa neeg’ o bi’ so kum ni maa mi m-bɔŋɔ.”

english_verse: Some time later Elisha went to the capital city of Damascus to visit King Benhadad of Syria, who was sick. And when Benhadad was told he was there,
translation_verse: Dahin shɛli ka Ilaisha daa ti ka Damaskus na. Di saha maa ka Siria Naa Bɛnhadad daa biɛra. Ka bɛ daa yɛl’ o, “Naawuni nir’ la be yaŋɔ.”

english_verse: Hazael left with forty camel loads of the best things made in Damascus as a gift for Elisha. He found the prophet and said, “Your servant, King Benhadad, wants to know if he will get well.”
translation_verse: Ka Hazaɛl daa bo Damaskus binshɛɣukam n-ʒili laakumnim’ pihinahi chaŋ ni o ti puhi Naawuni nir’ maa. Ka Hazaɛl daa paai ti zani Ilaisha tooni ka yɛl’ o, “A bia Siria Naa Bɛnhadad n-tim ma a sanna ni n ti bɔh’ a nya o ni kpaŋ o barigu ŋɔ ni?”

english_verse: “Tell him he will,” Elisha said to Hazael. “But the Lord has already told me that Benhadad will definitely die.”
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha daa yɛl’ o, “Cham’ ti yɛli naa maa ni biɛhiŋ kani, o ni kpaŋ; amaa Yawɛ lee kahigi wuhi ma ni o ni bahi kpi.”

english_verse: Elisha stared at him until Hazael was embarrassed, then Elisha began crying.
translation_verse: Ka Ilaisha daa mirig’ o nina kpa Hazaɛl n-kul lihir’ o hal ka vi ti gbaag’ o. Ka Ilaisha kumda.

english_verse: “Sir, why are you crying?” Hazael asked. Elisha answered, “Because I know the terrible things you will do to the people of Israel. You will burn down their walled cities and slaughter their young men. You will even crush the heads of their babies and rip open their pregnant women.”
translation_verse: Ka Hazaɛl bɔh’ o, “N dana, bɔzuɣu ka a kumda?” Ka Ilaisha garigi yɛl’ o, “N ni mi a ni ti yɛn niŋ Izraɛlnim’ zaɣ’ biɛ’ shɛli zuɣu n-chɛ ka n kumdi maa. A ni ti nyo bɛ birininim’ buɣim, ka zaŋ takɔbi ku bɛ nachimbihi, ka ŋme n-chɛrisichɛrisi bɛ bibihi, ka karigi bɛ paɣipuhinim’ puya.”

english_verse: “How could I ever do anything like that?” Hazael replied. “I'm only a servant and don't have that kind of power.” “Hazael, the Lord has told me that you will be the next king of Syria.”
translation_verse: Ka Hazaɛl bɔh’ o, “Ya ka a dabili ŋun nyɛ baa ŋɔ yɛn nya yiko n-tum tuun’ karili ŋɔ!” Ka Ilaisha garigi yɛl’ o, “Yawɛ kahigi wuhi ma ni a ni ti leei Siria naa.”

english_verse: But the very next day, Hazael got a thick blanket; he soaked it in water and held it over Benhadad's face until he died. Hazael then became king. King Jehoram of Judah (
translation_verse: Amaa ka biɛɣu daa neei, ka Hazaɛl niŋ kom mahigi bɔdua n-zaŋ pa naa maa ninni hal ka o ti leei Naawuni dini. Ka Hazaɛl daa di nam zan’ o zaani. Juda Naa Jɛhɔram yɛla (

english_verse: So Jehoram and his cavalry marched to Zair, where the Edomite army surrounded him and his commanders. During the night he attacked the Edomites, but he was defeated, and his troops escaped to their homes.
translation_verse: Di saha maa ka Jɛhɔram daa zaŋ o chɛchɛbunsi zaa n-yiɣisi yuŋ chaŋ Zairi, ka o min’ o chɛchɛbunsi sapashinnim’ ti lu Ɛdomnim’ bɛn daa teei gil’ o zuɣu n-niŋ ba buɣim; amaa ka o tɔbbihi daa zo n-kuli.

english_verse: While Jehoram was king, the people of Edom rebelled and chose their own king.
translation_verse: O ʒiɛman’ ni ka Ɛdomnim’ daa zaɣisi ni Judanim’ ku lan su ba; ka daa pii so n-leei bɛmaŋmaŋ’ naa.

english_verse: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat became king of Judah in Joram's fifth year as king of Israel, while Jehoshaphat was still king of Judah.
translation_verse: Izraɛl Naa Jɔram ŋun daa nyɛ Ɛhab bia la ni daa di nam zaŋ chaŋ yuma anu saha, ka Juda Naa Jɛhɔram ŋun daa nyɛ Jɛhɔshafat bia la daa di nam.

english_verse: Jehoram disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He married Ahab's daughter and was as sinful as Ahab's family and the kings of Israel.
translation_verse: O daa dolila Izraɛl nanim’ naba n-tum kaman Ɛhab min’ o daŋ ni daa tum shɛm la, dama o paɣ’ daa nyɛla Ɛhab bipuɣiŋga. O daa tum alahichi Yawɛ sani.

english_verse: But the Lord refused to destroy Judah, because he had promised his servant David that someone from his family would always rule in Judah.
translation_verse: Amaa Yawɛ daa bi yu ni o bahi Judanim’ yoli o dabili Dauda zuɣu, dama o daa pun lo Dauda alikauli ni o ni zaŋ firila ti o min’ o bidibisi.

english_verse: Everything else Jehoram did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
